english: Cassava roots rot when standing water gets trapped around them in flat, heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra rain drain away so the roots can breathe and stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsɔ amɛhe. Amɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ wo bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in weak plants and small yields. Giving each plant proper space lets it grow strong and produce more.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from intense heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering at the root level and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto flowers and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking the juices from fresh leaves, or by viruses they carry. Protecting the plants with pest sprays or neem oil keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai heei lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem fɔ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and can sleep in the dirt for years waiting for rain. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from stealing water and plant food away from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ nugbɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu ni amɛdu niyenii yɛ he ko ni kɛ otsei ni miida lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize go moldy when I store it in bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains still contain hidden water. Storing wet grains inside tight bags creates heat and moisture that breeds mold and attracts insects, so grains must be fully sun-dried until hard before storage.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ mli lolo. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni mli wa mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani akɛto.

english: Why should I plant local crop seeds instead of buying imported seeds from foreign countries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui moŋ fe ni mahe dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Local seed varieties are already used to Ghana's weather, soil, and rain patterns, making them stronger against local dry spells and pests compared to many imported seeds.
ga: Atsake maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ kɛya Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ, shikpɔŋ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ nɔ momo. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai, hɔmɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ he

english: How can I pick the best seeds from my current farm harvest to save for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni mifeɔ amrɔ nɛɛ amli koni mikɛto kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Choose seeds from your healthiest, strongest crops that yielded the best produce, then dry them completely in a shaded area and store them in airtight containers away from insects.
ga: Halamɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni he wa fe fɛɛ ni woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. No sɛɛ lɛ, gĩ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo bɛ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli, ni kooloi akabote mli.

english: Can I grow my soup vegetables like pepper and garden eggs together on the same land with my main crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ shwiili mli aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ he kome kɛ mitso titri lɛ?

english: Yes, planting short-term vegetables alongside main crops makes good use of your land, gives you food and income quickly, and helps shade the soil to keep weeds down.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ahe lɛ haa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Ha niyenii kɛ shika oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ejie jwɛi

english: How do I know if two different crops will grow well side by side without fighting each other?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ baakwɛ̃ yɛ he kome ni amɛwuuuu amɛhe?

english: Crops grow well together when they have different root depths or heights—such as tall corn paired with low-lying beans—so they do not steal sunlight or soil nutrients from one another.
ga: Tsei daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛkwɔlɛ srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ kɛ ŋmãa ni baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuuu hulu la loo niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to plant my seeds in straight lines with set spacing instead of scattering them by hand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu dumɔwui yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nine baadu nii?

english: Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to grow big, while straight lines make weeding and harvesting much easier for you.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Yɛ be mli ni line ni ja haa jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo lɛ.

english: If I plant a new crop on my farm, should I apply fertilizer to it the exact same way I do for my existing crops?
ga: Kɛji midu tsei heei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani Esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ni midu momo lɛ nɔŋŋ awo mli?

english: No, different crops require different amounts and types of nutrients depending on whether they produce leaves, roots, or fruits, as well as their stage of growth.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛ henɔi srɔtoi. Edamɔ tso lɛ baa, shishifãi, loo aduawai, kɛ agbɛnɛ bɔ ni edaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young crop leaves turn yellow and look weak when weeds grow close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ jwɛi bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your young crops need to stay healthy, causing them to turn yellow and stop growing.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ.

english: What causes my tomato and pepper plants to drop their flowers before fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi tomato kɛ pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Flowers usually drop when the plant is stressed by very high heat, uneven watering, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil like calcium during flowering time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium, yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds after the first rain falls in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady and the soil stays wet about a hand's depth down, rather than planting after the very first light rain which can dry up quickly and ruin your seeds.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ aaafee tso kome lolo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ, ni baanyɛ agbi oya ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do some of my vegetables wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil was watered in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ ekomɛi miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi?

english: Hot afternoon sun causes leaves to lose moisture faster than roots can absorb it; covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because full, direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Keeping some shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a cooler environment and moisture needed for young plants to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa koni tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the cobs are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually show that the maize plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives plants their green color and strength, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy and produces larger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛnáa hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje baai lɛ ni eha ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: What is eating the leaves inside the central stem of my young maize plants and leaving tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni eshiɔ bu bibii?

english: This leaf damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the center leaves (whorl) of young maize. Checking your crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can protect the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when it rains continuously for several days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining, cutting off oxygen to the roots and causing fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. without draining out Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ faaa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why is it necessary to place long poles next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso ko masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to reach sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and giving the plant maximum sunlight exposure.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking jieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi folier helai anaa ni oha tsei lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ.

english: Cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and transfer it into the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer nourishes the neighboring maize plants and improves soil fertility for future seasons.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ hewalɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Covering soil with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from taking away nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat or dry soil. Watering regularly during dry spells and applying mulch helps keep moisture steady so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi daa. Fɔfɔi baanyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my tall plantain trees easily fall over during heavy winds before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni kɛlɛ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani kpamɔ baa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that do not anchor deeply into the earth. When heavy bunches grow at the top, strong winds easily tip the tree, so supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents it from breaking.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ shwereɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baaha tsei lɛ agbo oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tso lɛ akumɔ.

english: How do weeds reduce the final yield of my crops if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ jwɛi lɛ tsuuu nii dani be ni ato lɛ shɛɔ hu?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food and light they need to produce strong harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aná niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the big trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and maintaining moist soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hulu lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in the same field make my maize grow better during the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnuts are harvested, that leftover nitrogen feeds the maize crop that follows.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Akɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V' from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: This yellowing pattern is a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves and grow big, healthy ears.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ toi agboi ni wa.

english: Why does my land yield less cassava when I plant it on the exact same farm three times in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava takes specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those specific nutrients and allows soil pests that target cassava to build up in high numbers.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni kwɛɔ ŋmei nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have broad, fast-growing roots that act like thieves, sucking up the fertilizer and water out of the soil before your crop's roots have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni daa oya ni feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the afternoon heat but look fine again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛfeɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They droop on purpose to reduce water loss, then recover overnight as temperatures drop.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ yiŋtoo akɛ ebaaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi No sɛɛ lɛ, ehiɛ ba shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rains stay longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni efɔɔ daa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain leaves water trapped around the roots for too long, the roots suffocate and fungus takes over, causing them to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii ha amɛhe, ni no haa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, heat stress damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. The plant drops the dead flowers to save its remaining energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Heat stress fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni egboi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing maximum sunlight to reach the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia kane tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa ni oha hulu la babaoo ashɛ baai lɛ ahe bɔ ni ooonyɛ

english: Why are tiny caterpillars suddenly gathering inside the hidden funnels of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miibua amɛhe naa trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which target the tight inner whorl of young maize because the leaves are soft, moist, and protected from natural predators and sunlight while they feed.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛmli edɔ, ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui kɛ hulu la he be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: How do I know if a cash crop like cocoa or cashew will produce well on my land before I buy seedlings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mahe dumɔwui?

english: Different cash crops prefer different soil and weather conditions; cocoa needs deep, rich soil with reliable rainfall, while cashew grows better in drier, well-drained soils. Checking soil moisture, depth, and asking local agriculture extension officers before planting helps ensure your land matches the crop's needs.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi srɔtoi. Cocoa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, cashew tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, emlibotemɔ ni oookwɛ ni obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani odu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii anɔ.

english: Why do crops grow very well on one section of my farm but struggle on another section of the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and underground nutrients vary even across small areas of land. Crops in low areas may get too much water, while crops on rocky or sloped areas may suffer from dry or nutrient-poor soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ hei bibii po. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ana nu babaoo tsɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni tɛi loo gɔji yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ana amanehulu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When soil gets soaked with too much water, the roots cannot breathe air and lose their ability to take up nutrients. Heavy rain can also wash away important nutrients like nitrogen from the root area.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ ajie niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my crops fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop due to plant stress caused by long dry spells, extreme heat, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei ahe haomɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kpakpai kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. aloo nibii ni haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during hot afternoons even when there is still water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: On very hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to reduce water loss and protect the plant until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: How does shade affect the growth and fruiting of my cash crops?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibiiwoo he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Young crops need mild shade to prevent their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist, but mature crops generally need more direct sunlight to produce energy for heavy yield and flowering.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo be ni mli tse. Enɛ ji koni baa akashã, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: How does planting space between crops affect my final yield?
ga: Te gbɛ ni kã tsei ateŋ lɛ saa minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and fertilizer while their leaves fight above ground for sunlight, leading to thin stems and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni akpaaa nii babaoo.

english: How do weeds affect the way my main crop feeds and grows?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa bɔ ni miyeɔ nii mihaa kɛ bɔ ni miduɔ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your cash crops, which starves your main crop and lowers your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oshika ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli ni ebaaha nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: What makes my neighbor's farm produce a high harvest while my farm with the same crop gets very little?
ga: Mɛni haa mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: High yields come from a combination of using certified healthy planting materials, keeping weeds away early, applying the right fertilizer at the right time, and managing pests before they multiply.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ oya. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baatsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ dani amɛshwere

english: Why do my crops grow much slower during cloudy or cooler months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji ni atatu loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Crops use sunlight and warmth as energy to turn nutrients into growth. When sunlight is limited and weather is cold, the crop's internal food-making process slows down naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ hulu la lɛ faaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ Niyenii ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow strong. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, they steal water, nutrients, and sunlight from each other. Giving them enough space allows the underground roots to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts or beans returns nitrogen to the soil and keeps it fertile.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmeii aba.

english: Why do weeds in my field cause my crops to produce less yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest common in Ghana. They hide in the leaves and feed on young maize, but applying approved sprays or neem extracts early can control them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmãa bibii. Shi akpɛlɛ neem tsofai loo nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ mra. lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking juices from the leaves and spreading viruses. Managing these insects keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ akwɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under harsh direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains around them keeps the plants cool and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã he lɛ? miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the heat, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from severe heat, uneven watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Regular watering and proper soil food help flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds right after the very first rainy day of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out and kill young sprouts. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady before sowing seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ ni baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tight during the hot dry afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to reduce the leaf area exposed to the sun. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to stop water from evaporating and conserve moisture during hot weather.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho ni eha fɛ̃i ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during the Harmattan to save water and stay alive. The plant is not dead; it goes dormant to protect itself from dry winds and sun until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai yɛ harmattan beaŋ koni ekɛhere nu ni ehi wala mli. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaakã shi ni ekɛbu ehe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing fruit when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When flowers are not fertilized, the plant drops them to save energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ efeee Kɛ́ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the leaves on my bean crop turn yellow after heavy rain floods my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flooded soil pushes out oxygen, preventing root breathing. Without oxygen, roots cannot absorb nitrogen from the ground, causing the leaves to turn yellow from nutrient starvation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. etsĩɔ shishifãi lɛ amumɔ naa Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: High humidity and cool, damp air during heavy rains create ideal conditions for fungi that cause Black Pod disease. Pruning tree branches improves air circulation to keep pods dry.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmei ni kɛ blackpod hela baa lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why is my pepper plant growing tall with big green leaves but no peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Eyɛ baai agboi eŋɔli. Shi chili bɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich fertilizer makes pepper plants put energy into growing leaves and branches instead of flowers. Balancing the fertilizer helps encourage flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛaatsu nii lɛ baaha o-pepper tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo awo baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ amli yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines wither and dry up at the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally dry up when the plant finishes transferring all its energy down into the underground tuber. This signals that the yam tuber is fully grown and ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, plantain suckers compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture. Proper spacing allows roots to spread so the plant can yield larger bunches.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ afee kui wuji.

english: Why do stem borer insects attack my maize crop more during dry weather than rainy days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ stem borers lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Drought stresses maize plants, making them weak and less able to naturally defend against pests. Dry weather also helps insect larvae mature faster and spread easily.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa ŋmãa tsei haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo.

english: Why do free-roaming chickens destroy my newly planted vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ miifite mi aduawai aŋmɔ ni midu ehee lɛ?

english: Chickens scratch topsoil looking for worms and bugs, which unearths seeds and breaks tender seedling roots. Fencing vegetable beds protects fragile young crops until they are mature.
ga: Kooloi baafolɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtao ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii. Enɛ baatsa dumɔwui lɛ ni efo dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Aduawai tsei ni akɛ gbogboi ebɔ he lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛshɛɔ dalɛ he.

english: Why do some rice varieties in Ghana have names like Agra rice based on places?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ gbɛi tamɔ Akara ŋmãa yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Farmers and seed traders often name popular crop varieties after the town, city, or market where the seeds were first bought or successfully grown, making it easy for other farmers to identify proven seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaafoi kɛ dumɔwui ahe jarayelɔi tsɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni ehe gbɛi lɛ yɛ maŋ, maŋtiase, loo jarayeli he ni ahe dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mli loo adu yɛ omanyeyeli mli lɛ gbɛi. Ha okwaafoi krokomɛi ana dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ mlɛo

english: Is Agra rice a good option for me to plant on my farm?
ga: Ani Akara ŋmãa ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Agra rice is a very popular, high-yielding variety in Ghana that sells easily in major markets, but you must ensure your land has adequate water and good soil drainage before planting it.
ga: Akara omɔ ji omɔ henɔ ko ni ehe gbɛi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana. ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei wuji lɛ amli mlɛo Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ koni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná nu ni fa kɛ sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ dani odu nii.

english: Why should I talk to the local elders before planting a new crop in my community?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ onukpai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ agba sane dani madu tsei heei yɛ mikutso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Elders and experienced farmers know the historical weather patterns, soil conditions, and past pest problems in your specific area, helping you choose crops that are proven to succeed locally.
ga: Onukpai kɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ le kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni eho, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai ni eho yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eye omanye yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Where can I find reliable crop seeds that are widely grown across Ghana?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni aduɔ babaoo yɛ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ yɛ?

english: You can get high-quality, certified seeds from registered agricultural input dealers, local extension offices, or approved farmer cooperatives to ensure high germination and healthy yields.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kuu lɛ mli Nɔyaa Nitsumɔhe loo okwaafoi akuu ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ Koni akwɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do certain crop varieties sell much faster in big city markets like Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ahɔ̃ɔ oya kwraa yɛ maji wuji tamɔ Accra jarayeli hei lɛ?

english: City buyers and traders prefer specific crop varieties that cook well, taste good, and store longer without spoiling, which creates high nationwide demand and better prices for farmers growing those varieties.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sumɔɔ niyenii srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni ahoo jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋɔɔ, ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee lɛ. Enɛ haa maŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ biɔ nibii babaoo, ni ehaa okwaafoi ni duɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ hu jara hiɔ.

english: How can I find out which crop variety has the highest buyer demand before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ dani madu amɛ?

english: You can check with local market women, commodity traders, or your district agricultural extension officer to learn which crop varieties consumers are actively buying in nearby markets.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyabi maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei lɛ. Nibii ahe jarayelɔi loo okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ Koni ole tsei srɔtoi ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ heɔ yɛ jarayeli hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant the exact same crop variety anywhere in Ghana and get the same yield?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ Ghana he fɛɛ he ni maná yibiiwoo ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: No, crops behave differently depending on local rainfall, soil quality, and temperature, so a variety that produces heavy yields in one region might perform poorly in another.
ga: Dabi, tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ latsaa he, no hewɔ lɛ tso henɔ ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpokpaa kome nɔ lɛ ekolɛ etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ.

english: Why are there different types of seeds available for the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ kɛha tso kome lɛ?

english: Agricultural scientists develop different varieties so farmers can choose seeds suited to their specific conditions, such as short-season seeds for dry areas or disease-resistant seeds for humid zones.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi efee srɔtoi srɔtoi. Bɔni afee ni okwaafoi ahala dumɔwui ni sa kɛha amɛshihilɛ pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kukuoo kɛha hei ni nu egbi. loo dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛha hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ

english: Most rice varieties grow best in flat areas or low-lying valleys with soil that holds water well, like clay or heavy loam, though specialized upland rice varieties can grow on drier slopes.
ga: Omɔ henɔi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo jɔɔ lɛ mli ni shikpɔŋ ni nu hiɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo sũ ni mli tse. Eyɛ mli akɛ gɔŋji amli ŋmãa henɔi pɔtɛɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ moŋ.

english: What is the difference between direct sowing seeds and planting in a nursery first?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Direct sowing means planting seeds directly into your main farm field, while nursery planting allows you to raise delicate seedlings in a protected small plot before transplanting them to the main field for better survival.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsɔɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. abuɔ he dani aya ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build healthy green leaves. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea can restore their green color and help them grow taller.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when the rainy season gets very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays soaked with water for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away from the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any young cocoa pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani cacao ŋmɔji bibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress from dry spells, or when small sucking insects like capsids attack the flowers. Providing light tree shade and spraying against sucking pests keeps flowers attached so pods can grow.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ nu he haomɔ ni jɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ba amɛnɔ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo fioo ko wo tsei lɛ anɔ ni akɛ sucker pests shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔji lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever a heavy storm blows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ahum wulu ko baatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that can easily be weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes or root rot. Supporting mature plants with wooden bamboo props and building earth mounds around their bases prevents them from uprooting in strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Atsɛɔ nakai feemɔ akɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni eda lɛ asɛɛ, ni afee gɔŋ ko ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why does my maize grow so tall and thin without producing good ears when I plant it close under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo waa akɛ ebɛ toi kpakpai kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Maize needs full, direct sunlight to make the energy required to grow thick stems and full grain ears. Tree shade starves the maize plants of sunlight and causes them to stretch tall and weak as they reach for light.
ga: Abɛi he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ená hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ toi ni eyi obɔ. Tso mli ŋmɔlɔ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ naa, ni ehaa edaraa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ eshɛ la he.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up, stop growing, and look crinkled?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa dalɛ, ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap and spreading plant viruses. Removing severely affected plants and spraying organic insecticidal soap keeps the insect population low.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso lɛ mli helai lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Tsei ni ena hela waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha kooloi ayibɔ akafee bibioo.

english: Why do insects attack and bore holes into my cowpea plants right when they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfoɔ bu yɛ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ amli kɛji amɛbɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers attract pod-boring pests because the soft blossoms and young pods are rich in nutrients for insect larvae. Monitoring your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides right as the first flowers open protects the crop.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ pɛ kɛkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without turning into tomato fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get extremely hot or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist with organic mulch around the plant bases helps cool the soil and protects the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in my barn even when I want to store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔji ni ŋmɔji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miisumɔ ni mahi shi moŋ

english: Yam tubers naturally wake up from dormancy when they feel warm, humid air in storage. Keeping your yam barn well-ventilated, cool, shaded, and dark slows down sprouting and keeps the tubers fresh longer.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni amɛnuɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ nitoohe lɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli jogbaŋŋ, eyɛ fɛ̃i, eyɛ hulutsoo, ni eyɛ duŋ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ fioo ni eye ebua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains turn to powder after just a few months in the storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powda beni mikɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ ehi nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain powdery damage is caused by small insects called grain weevils that lay eggs inside the dry kernels and eat them from the inside out. Drying the maize completely until it is hard and storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates these pests without using dangerous chemicals.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ powder fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa. Atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmãa ŋmei ŋmei. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi mli ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa waa ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ agbɔjɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why does my rice crop turn yellow and stop growing when there is too much sitting water in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: While rice needs water to grow, completely suffocating the roots under deep, stagnant water deprives them of oxygen, causing root rot and yellow leaves. Draining the field briefly allows the roots to breathe and absorb soil nutrients properly.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni nu he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ shishi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ naa lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi be kukuoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall completely over to the ground just before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miigbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Rice plants fall over, known as lodging, when stems become weak from receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer or when planted too close together. Balanced fertilizing builds strong stems capable of holding heavy heads of grain.
ga: Ale ŋmãa tsei ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ hu akɛ shĩai. Beni tso lɛ mli gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni enine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja lɛ haa ŋmeii ni wa ni baanyɛ ahiɛ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii lɛ baa.

english: Why does my harvested rice break into small pieces when I take it to the mill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli bibii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be akɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rice breaks during milling if the grains develop internal cracks while drying too quickly under harsh, direct sunlight. Drying harvested rice gradually in thin layers prevents grain breakage.
ga: Omɔ mli fãa yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli fãa yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Ni agbiɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ni efeɔ ŋmãa bibioo. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ akagbala.

english: Why do some of my harvested rice grains look chalky and white instead of clear and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ ŋmaa lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee faŋŋ ni efee nɔ ni wa?

english: Chalkiness happens when rice plants experience high temperatures or drought while forming their grains. Keeping fields consistently moist during the grain-filling stage creates clear, hard, high-quality rice that buyers prefer.
ga: Alkalinity baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo hɔmɔ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ miifee. Kɛ́ ahiɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmaa fataa he lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa ni mli tse, ni wa, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ biɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why does my local scented rice lose its sweet aroma after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Aromatic rice loses its natural perfume if left unharvested in the hot sun for too long after maturity. Harvesting at the right time and drying carefully preserves both aroma and grain strength.
ga: Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baafite ebɔɔ su lɛ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ahoo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmaa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli, ni agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmaa lɛ he ŋɔɔ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ hiɔ shi.

english: If I save seeds from my current harvest to plant next season, why do I get a smaller yield?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ miwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Seeds saved across multiple seasons lose their genetic purity and vigor, making them vulnerable to local pests and low production. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures uniform growth and a higher harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ bei babaoo lɛ fiteɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli hetsemɔ kɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ haa amɛdaraa daa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do my rice plants grow tall and weak with few grains when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui fioo pɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, seedlings fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce multiple shoots and heavy grain heads.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ dumɔwui ni tsii.

english: Why are some heads of my rice plants completely empty even though the rest of the plant looks green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tsei lɛ ekomɛi efee efolo lɛ? Ani ŋmãa tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Empty grain heads occur when insect pests or birds feed on the soft, milky grains as they form, or when heat damages flowers before pollination. Protecting fields during flowering stops empty grain heads from forming.
ga: Dumɔwui ayitsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi loo okpoi ye dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tamɔ mliki lɛ beni amɛfeɔ lɛ. aloo be mli ni latsaa fiteɔ fɔfɔii dani pollination baa ŋmɔ lɛ he ni abuɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haaa dumɔwui ayitsei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are small brown spots spreading on my rice leaves and causing them to dry up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ? Ani kɛ́ okɛshwã ŋmãa baa nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa baa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya?

english: Brown spots are caused by fungal infections like rice blast, which thrive when soil nutrients are unbalanced or fields are overcrowded. Proper fertilization and planting resistant seed varieties keep leaves healthy.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ rice blight ji nɔ ni kɛ brow spots baa. Ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa loo yɛ ŋmɔji ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ haa baai lɛ feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young crop in the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds germinate aggressively and steal soil nutrients before young crops fully establish. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks gives young plants the sunlight and nutrients needed to outgrow competition.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani dumɔwui lɛ daraa. Klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya fe akaŋshii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for crop growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted manure helps the leaves turn green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary plantain plants to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist while their roots mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ amɛhe be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch plenty of sunlight to make food for the plant. Without stakes, leaves rot on the hot ground and the roots produce very small yams.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. ni shishifãi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Does my rice crop need to sit in deep flooded water all the time to grow well?
ga: Ani esa akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahi nu ni mli kwɔ mli be fɛɛ be dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: While lowland rice enjoys wet conditions, standing water that is too deep can suffocate young plants or rot their stems. Keeping the soil consistently moist with controlled water levels yields better harvests.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ moŋ Shi nu ni damɔ shi ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ loo eha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu ni akudɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences severe heat stress, irregular watering, or pest attacks. Keeping the soil evenly moist and shading plants slightly during extreme heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i po ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning completely black and rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which thrives in excess wetness and humidity. Pruning extra branches allows sunlight and air into the farm, preventing moisture buildup that spreads the rot.
ga: Fungi hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni gbɛɔ hela ni fiteɔ lɛ eshwaa lɛ naa.

english: Twisted or curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant sap. Using approved insect traps or spraying organic extracts like neem oil can stop the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni etsɔ loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ bug zapper ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii loo akɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ wala mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are made by hungry pests like caterpillars feeding on them. Inspecting your plants early and applying safe control measures stops pests from eating away your yield.
ga: Hɔmɔ ni yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli mra. Ni gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaye onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ.

english: If cassava is planted too close, the plants compete for sunlight and nutrients underground. This results in lots of leaves above ground but small, thin cassava roots below.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmei shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Will planting cowpea or beans help improve my poor soil for my next crop?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop harvest is done, the leftover plant material breaks down and enriches the soil naturally for future crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ agbe ŋmaa lɛ naa Tse mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ tsei.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil without enough organic matter, like decayed leaves or manure, cannot hold water for long. Adding compost or covering the ground with dry leaves (mulching) acts like a sponge, keeping moisture near the plant roots for many days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ. Enyɛŋ ekɛ nu ato be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi (mulch) wo mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tso shishifãi lɛ ahe gbii babaoo.

english: Is it better to burn cleared bushes on my land or leave the dead leaves on the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã tsei bibii ni he tse yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo mashi baai ni egboi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving dead leaves to rot naturally on the land is much better than burning. Burning destroys the natural food in the soil, while dead leaves rot into organic fertilizer that keeps the land rich and holds moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi baai lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehi kwraa fe ni oooshã amɛ. Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there is too much heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender stems and leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. They need quick-growing shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as natural umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ tsei bibii kɛ baai ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green leafy growth. Applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer early gives the plants the food they need to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my cassava stems very close together?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa?

english: No, planting too close creates competition. The crops will fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin plants with small tubers. Giving them proper spacing makes each plant grow bigger roots.
ga: Dabi, dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa. Tsei baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná shishifãi wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and attracts pests that love that crop. Rotating with crops like beans or groundnuts puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni egbalaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ nakai nibii lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are small white powdery insects attacking the bottom of my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ji mealybugs yɛŋ lɛ tutuaa mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Those are pests like mealybugs or whiteflies that suck the juice from the leaves, causing them to curl and stunt plant growth. Spraying a mixture of water and neem leaf extract early can wash them off and protect your farm.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa. Nu ni akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu efutu mli lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni efɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he ni ebu he.

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize inside the storage barn so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects like weevils breed rapidly inside grain if the maize is stored with too much moisture. Ensuring your maize is completely dried in the sun before storing it in sealed bags stops these insects from surviving.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii fɔɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa to he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ koni o-abele lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akajo foi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from stress, such as very high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering and keeping the root area cool with mulch helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni akɛ muji woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so poorly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your main crops can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops consume all the nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rain usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which starves the roots of air and washes away essential nitrogen nutrients that give the leaves their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ekɛ nitrogen nibii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and drying out during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress or by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies that spread viruses. Protecting the soil with mulch and spraying organic treatments like neem oil helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ tomato mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava in my field so it gets enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Cassava is best planted at the very start of the main rainy season (around March or April in southern Ghana). This gives the cuttings enough moisture to establish deep roots before dry spells start.
ga: Akɛ cassava duɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee March loo April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ) Enɛ baaha tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the weeds and dry leaves on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful organisms like earthworms in the soil. Clearing the brush and leaving it to rot naturally adds nutrients back into your soil and holds moisture longer.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ brɔshi he ni aha egbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced very small yields, your soil is weak. An extension officer can also help you test the soil texture and color to recommend the right organic or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ hu baanyɛ aye abua bo ni oka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ ehiɛ su lɛ okwɛ koni amɛtsɔɔ bo tsofai ni sa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant beans and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil to nourish the maize, while the maize stalks give climbing beans support to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni kwɔɔ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant plantains next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu kookoo tsei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi kookoo dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil humid while the cocoa trees mature during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is being damaged by Fall Armyworm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji Fall Armyworm lɛ efite mi-abele lɛ?

english: Look inside the central funnel (whorl) of the young maize plants. If you see ragged holes in the leaves and small brownish waste that looks like sawdust, Fall Armyworm is active and needs treatment.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ faa (ring) lɛ mli. Kɛji ona buji ni etse yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Nɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ miitsu nii ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers rot so quickly after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised by farm tools during harvest, exposed to direct sun, or stored in damp rooms. Storing undamaged yams on raised wooden racks in a cool, ventilated barn prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii fite amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potatoes ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ to tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and heavy fruit bunches make them top-heavy. Tiny root worms or stem borers can also weaken the base, so supporting plants with wooden props protects them from wind damage.
ga: Plantain shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii waa. Shishifãi bibii ni shwieɔ shi loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishitoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni akɛ tsei ebɔ he lɛ buɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ akafite amɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or leave tall trees next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui loo mashi tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ yɛ he ko? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains or shade trees act as living umbrellas that keep the soil moist and protect young cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei bibii loo shade tsei ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni hiɛ ka ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize crop turning yellow and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build food. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land make my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi-ŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has a special ability to take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, they leave natural fertilizer behind for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mli bii, ni amɛyɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by very small insects like aphids or thrips that suck the sap from the leaves and spread viruses. Keeping the farm clean and spraying neem water or appropriate insecticides early can prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni aaakwɛ koni ehe atse ni akɛ neem nu loo tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie nɔ mra Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot underground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater stays on the field without draining away, the tubers drown and fungal rot quickly sets in.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli lɛ Tubers lɛ baagboi ni ŋmeii lɛ baagboi oya.

english: Why are my maize plants weak and stunted even though I cleared all the visible weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛgbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jwɛi fɛɛ ni anaa ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Your field might have a subterranean parasitic weed called Striga (witchweed). Its seeds attach directly to the maize roots underground and steal food and water long before the weed even sprouts above ground.
ga: Ekolɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga (witchweed) lɛ yɛ. Edumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu dani jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Yam plants make underground tubers using energy captured by their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves high into the sunlight, exposing them to light while keeping them clean and free from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaai lɛ mɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Ha baai lɛ aná la Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he tseɔ ni helai bɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds in one hole?
