ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to build big, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil is too dry, or when insects damage the blossoms. Mulching around the roots helps cool the soil and hold moisture so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain often wet only the top layer of dry, hot soil. If a long dry spell follows immediately after, the seeds start to germinate but quickly dry out and die before the regular rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baabɔi kwɛ̃mɔ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ aje shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i nɔ.

english: Why do I have to train my yam vines to grow up wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into direct sunlight so they can produce energy to grow large tubers underground. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs for growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep leaves green and improves harvest yields.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji bɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant groundnuts or cowpeas before maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dani wɔdu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas release natural nitrogen into the soil through their roots. Planting them first enriches the ground with free fertilizer for the maize planted in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nɔ ni ŋmãa bɛ mli kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until rains become regular. The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell that dries out newly sprouted seeds before full rainy season begins.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gbiɔ dani nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry plants, called mulching, keeps water from evaporating in hot sun, keeps roots cool, stops weeds from growing, and adds nutrients to soil as it breaks down.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot during wet weather?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads in cool, overly damp environments. Pruning heavy shade branches and removing infected pods helps air flow and stops fungal spread.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ amli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by small whiteflies transmitting a plant virus, or by severe heat stress. Controlling whiteflies early and maintaining regular watering protects plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Early Whitefly Control Ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: How do I know when cassava tubers are ready to dig up from the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava is usually mature when lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, typically 9 to 12 months after planting. You can gently dig up one stem to check if tubers are large enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ tso lɛ shishi blɛoo. Koni akwɛ kɛji yitso lɛ da bɔ ni sa

english: Why does leaving weeds in my farm reduce the size of my harvested crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to nourishment needed for large roots, leaves, and fruits.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha amɛshishifãi, amɛbaai, kɛ amɛyibii wuji lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Akɛtee tso lɛ shishi?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana. They eat the tender leaves and central shoots of maize, but catching them early with recommended treatments or handpicking can save your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Shi kɛji omɔ lɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo nine ni okɛbaakpa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni okɛbu onibii ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Controlling these pests early helps the leaves flatten out and regain normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites, ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ hu ashwã tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa seedlings scorching and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa seedlings until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, awo amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms instead of forming fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress or lack sufficient water. Giving them consistent water at the root level and light shade during the hottest parts of the day helps them hold their flowers and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my maize grow very tall with leafy green stems but produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai shi ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii waa lɛ?

english: This usually happens when soil has too much nitrogen but lacks phosphorus and potassium. Nitrogen makes plants produce leaves and stems, while phosphorus and potassium are needed for strong cobs and grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fa tsɔ shi ebɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potassium. Nitrogen haa tsei woɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my field for the next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mihe ni mikɛbaadu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant nutrients inside the soil through their roots. When the season ends, this natural fertilizer remains in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without proper drainage, creating conditions for fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why are my harvested seed yams starting to sprout in the barn long before the planting season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃mɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams sprout when exposed to warmth and high humidity in storage. Keeping your yam barn shaded, cool, and well-ventilated slows down sprouting so the seeds stay fresh until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes baakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ o-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ fiofio bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni aduɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with strong wooden poles or bamboo stakes gives them the extra support needed during strong winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ewoɔ aduawai babaoo. kɛ muji babaoo baa Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa to tso titri lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ afata he yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Why is my swamp rice turning yellow and stunted in areas where water stays trapped?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits still for too long without moving, it starves the plant roots of oxygen and causes nutrient blockages like iron toxicity. Draining stagnant water periodically allows roots to breathe and absorb nutrients.
ga: Beni nu lɛ etsɛ lolo ni etsiii ehe Nu lɛ baaha tsei shishifãi lɛ aná oxygen. ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ tsiɔ naa, tamɔ dade ni yɔɔ gbeyei Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ ni ajieɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and curling up, while my neighbor's farm looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava mosaic disease is carried by tiny whiteflies that move from plant to plant. Your neighbor's farm might not have been visited by infected flies yet, or they may have planted disease-resistant stem cuttings.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni fãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛbaa. Ekolɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ eyako okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo. Aloo abaanyɛ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi ni helai nyɛŋ amɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot so quickly during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, damp weather. Raindrops splash fungal spores from the soil onto lower pods, so pruning excess shade trees and clearing heavy bush helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo tsei ni haa hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or if they just need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miimɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛkɛ?

english: A disease usually starts on a few scattered plants, showing spots, strange mold, or wilting. A lack of nutrients usually affects whole rows or entire areas of your farm evenly, making all the plants look pale or stunted at the same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛ tsei fioo komɛi ni egbɛ eshwã ni jieɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ pɛ. Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ saa oŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔji akui fɛɛ loo hei fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbɔjɔ yɛ be kome too mli.

english: If I notice one crop in my field is getting sick, why is it necessary for me to destroy it immediately?
ga: Kɛji miyɔse akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpãtã hiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Removing a sick plant early prevents insects, rain drops, and wind from carrying the sickness to the rest of your healthy crops, stopping an outbreak before it spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi kooloi bibii, nu mli ŋmeii, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni amɛkajie helai kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. ni okpa hela lɛ dani egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my maize crop from caterpillars before they eat up all the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe dani amɛye baai lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Checking your farm early and regularly is the best protection. Inspecting the leaf centers of young maize plants allows you to spot fall armyworm eggs or small worms early and treat them with recommended sprays before they cause major damage.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ ji hebuu ni hi fe fɛɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona armyworm ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii ni egbee shi lɛ mra. Ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Can diseases pass into my new crops if I use seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ anɔ? Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsu nii

english: Yes, many crop sicknesses hide inside the seeds of infected plants. Planting certified seeds from trusted agricultural officers ensures your crop starts off strong without carrying old diseases into the new season.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei ahe helai babaoo yɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ helai momoi baaa be hee lɛ mli.

english: Can crop sickness remain hidden in the soil even after I harvest my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po sɛɛ?

english: Yes, many fungal and bacterial diseases survive in the soil for a long time. Rotating your crops—such as planting legumes after corn—starves these soil diseases because the new plant type is not a suitable host for them.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baanyɛ ahi sũ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake, tamɔ ŋmãa ni ooodu yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ shikpɔŋ helai nɛɛ anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei heei jeee shihilɛhei ni sa kɛha tsei nɛɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Giving plants adequate water and light shade during hot spells helps them retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: This is often caused by leaf spot fungi or root damage from soil pests, which block water from moving up the plant stem. Clearing affected leaves and maintaining good field drainage keeps the plantain leaves green longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa mli tsɛŋemɔ hela loo shishifãi ni sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haaa nu aya tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni ena hela lɛ, ni akwɛ koni nu ho jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni plantain baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow high in my farm make my crops get sick more easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi shwere yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela waa lɛ?

english: Overgrown weeds trap moisture around your crops, block sunlight, and harbor harmful pests that carry plant diseases. Keeping your field weeded allows fresh air and sunlight to naturally protect your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ mɔɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe, etsĩɔ hulu la naa, ni ehiɛɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni hiɛ tsei helai. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi wo oŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ hulu la aba koni ebu onibii ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I put fertilizer on the side of my plants instead of directly on the stem or roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo tso lɛ shishi loo eshishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly on stems or roots can burn the crop because the chemicals are very concentrated. Placing it a few inches to the side allows the roots to reach out safely and absorb nutrients gradually as the plant grows.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi loo shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ yɛ tsofai ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo sɛɛgbɛ inchi fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo shweshweeshwe ni amɛje kpo blɛoo. Ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ

english: How can I tell if the fertilizer I am buying at the market is good quality and not fake?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ, shi jeee amale?

english: Good quality fertilizer usually comes in properly sealed bags with clear manufacturer labels, uniform particle sizes, and no hard, wet clumps. Buying directly from registered agricultural dealers reduces the risk of getting adulterated products.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa yɛ kotoku ko ni akɛwo mli, ni mɔ ni fee lɛ he wolo ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɔɔ nɔ. Uniform particle size Ni ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii ni mli efɔ bɛ. Nihɔɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa oshara ni yɔɔ akɛ abaaná nibii ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Fertilizer is getting very expensive; can I mix animal manure with chemical fertilizer to save money?
ga: Fertilizer jara wa waa. Ani obaanyɛ okɛ kooloi ashishifãi afutu tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ koni okɛ shika akafite?

english: Yes, combining well-rotted animal manure with smaller amounts of chemical fertilizer improves soil health, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and lowers your overall input costs while still giving crops the quick boost they need.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofa fioo ko ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ he feɔ fɛo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni okɛ shika fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ data mli lɛ aba shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛnáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ oya.

english: If I store my leftover fertilizer in my house until next season, will it still work on my crops?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ to shĩa lɛ mli kɛyashi be kroko hu? Ani ebaatsu nii lolo eha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, but fertilizer easily absorbs moisture from the air. If stored on damp floors or in open bags, it hardens into solid rocks or turns into liquid, making it very difficult to apply evenly to your crops later.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ loo yɛ kotoku ko ni agbele mli lɛ Ebaafee tɛ ni wa loo ebaatsɔ nu. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ okɛbaatsu nii yɛ onibii amli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize crops turn dark green and grow very tall after I apply fertilizer, but fail to produce big ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni edɔɔ waa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi ekɛ toi wuji baaa?

english: High nitrogen fertilizer makes leaves grow fast and dark green, but crops also need phosphorus and potassium to grow strong roots and large grain ears. Using a balanced fertilizer ensures proper fruit and grain development.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa baai lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. Shi tsei hu he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ dumɔwui agbo toi. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa aduawai kɛ dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though we are getting enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ani wɔmiiná nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil, or the soil is waterlogged from heavy rain, which suffocates the roots and stops them from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ abote mli.

english: When is the best time during the season to feed my crops with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Most crops need a first feeding shortly after germination to help young roots grow, followed by a second feeding when they start growing rapidly or flowering. Applying fertilizer during heavy downpours will wash it away before plants can use it.
ga: Tsei babaoo he miihia amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ niyenii beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛdara. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ niyenii ni ji enyɔ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ lɛ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my cassava plants rot underground when I plant them in soil where water sits for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, well-drained soil to expand and breathe. Standing water starves the roots of air and encourages soil fungi that cause the tubers to rot before harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava tsei koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmu. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa bulb lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa lɛ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do market buyers offer me lower prices for my vegetables even when they are large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa mi-vegetables lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdara moŋ?

english: Market buyers value firmness, uniform size, clean appearance, and long shelf life over size alone. Large produce that is overly soft or damaged during transport spoils quickly and loses market value.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jarayelihe lɛ buɔ tightness akɛ nɔ ko ni jara wa. uniform size Hefɛo ni he tse Ni shihilɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe dalɛ pɛ. Nibii wuji ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ loo efite yɛ be mli ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ baafite oya ni jara ni jara wa baafite.

english: What is the difference between NPK fertilizer and Urea, and how do my crops react to each?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ NPK kɛ urea ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ ni te miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ eko fɛɛ eko he?

english: Urea provides a quick boost of pure nitrogen to make leaves grow fast and green. NPK contains a balanced mixture of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, which supports leaf growth, root strength, and crop yields all together.
ga: Urea kɛ nitrogen krɔŋŋ fataa he oya koni eha baai lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni amɛfee eŋɔli. NPK yɛ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. ni fiɔ baa lɛ dalɛ shishifã hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ ekome

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on my land before putting down my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves. Plantain trees grow very fast and provide natural shade umbrellas to protect the cocoa until it gets older.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui taoɔ hɔɔŋ ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa baanyɛ ashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛhaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen nutrients from the soil or are getting too much standing water. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ ni nitrogen niyenii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ loo amɛná nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I stop my cassava roots from rotting under the dirt when heavy rains begin?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni akpa ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water settles around them. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows rainwater to drain away easily, keeping the tubers safe under the soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ba amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ atsɔ mli oya. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the plant stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended pest control directly into the central funnel of the plant stops them from destroying your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔji akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my tomato plant flowers falling off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat is too strong or when the plants do not get enough steady water. Giving your tomato plants regular water early in the morning helps the flowers turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seed grains very close to each other in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield bigger fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Why do extension officers recommend placing tall wooden sticks for yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ ama shi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and helping the yam tubers below grow much larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa fitemɔ aba ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato tuber lɛ shishi ni edaa babaoo.

english: What makes the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids sucking the sap out of the leaves. Spraying early with safe neem-based sprays or recommended insecticides helps clear the pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Akɛ neem spray loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How does mixing dried poultry manure into my farm soil help my vegetables?
ga: Te kooloi ashishifãi ni egbi ni mikɛfutuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Poultry manure acts as natural food for your soil and holds water like a sponge. It enriches the ground with nutrients, helping vegetable roots grow deeper and healthier without damaging the soil.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my land better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni madu lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas pull good nitrogen food straight from the air and store it in their roots. When the season ends, that food stays in the soil to naturally feed the next crop you plant there.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen nibii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Is it better to buy less fertilizer if prices go up, or should I just reduce the size of my farm?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi akɛ ooohe ŋmɔshi nibii fioo kɛji akɛ jara tee hiɛ? Aloo esa akɛ ajie ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ nɔ?

english: Using too little fertilizer on a large farm starves your crops and leads to poor yields that lose you money. It is usually better to cultivate a smaller plot properly with the right amount of fertilizer so every plant gives its maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ agbo mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akawo mli jogbaŋŋ ni baaha ofite shika. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ koni tso fɛɛ tso aná yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow, and do I need expensive chemical fertilizers to fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni ani ehe miihia ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa awo mli koni akɛsaa?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen. While chemical fertilizers like NPK work quickly, you can also use well-rotted chicken manure or compost, which costs less and improves soil moisture for future seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK tsuɔ nii oya moŋ, shi obaanyɛ okɛ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ hu atsu nii. Enɛ jara waaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why do market women pay me so little for my tomatoes right after harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo ko koni mahe tomato yɛ kpamɔɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When every farmer harvests tomatoes at the same time, the market gets flooded and prices drop. Because fresh tomatoes spoil quickly, farmers are forced to accept low prices before the produce rots.
ga: Kɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kpa tomato yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayeli lɛ baaho ni ejara baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato hee lɛ fiteɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛkpɛlɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ dani amɛdumɔ nii lɛ agbo.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get stressed, usually from extreme heat, lack of water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer. Mulching your soil with dry grass helps retain water and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds around them for a few extra weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Amɛji otsii fioo komɛi krokomɛi.

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors that steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives young plants full access to what they need to grow strong roots quickly.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ, ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa oya.

english: No, planting seeds too close together forces plants to fight for space, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny fruits. Proper spacing lets each plant grow to its full size and produce a larger overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye he ko, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa kɛyashɛɔ egbɛfaŋnɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season to save money?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli koni mikɛ shika ato?

english: Replanting saved hybrid seeds gives you weak plants and much lower yields in the second generation. It is better to buy fresh certified seeds every season to guarantee strong plants and high yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ adumɔ baaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba. Esa akɛ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ daa be mli koni ana tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Can I leave my dried maize on the farm for a few months until market prices go up?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi kɛyashi jara nɔ jara lɛ baaya hiɛ?

english: Leaving dry maize in the field exposes it to rain, field mold, birds, and heavy insect attacks like weevils. It is safer to harvest early, dry the grain properly, and store it in hermetic bags to keep it safe until prices rise.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ, ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii, okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa lɛ. Nikpamɔ mra lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛwo vacuum kotoku mli koni akɛto he jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni jara lɛ baaya ŋwɛi.

english: How do I decide which crop to plant if I am worried about high fertilizer prices?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni esa akɛ madu lɛ ahe kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jara ni wa lɛ miihao mi?

english: You can choose legume crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, or soybeans. Legumes make their own nitrogen in the soil, so they require far less expensive fertilizer while still improving the soil for future crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ ohala ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo soybeans. Legumes feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara waaa kwraa atsu nii yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are long white shoots starting to grow out of my harvested rice while it is inside the storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kakadaŋŋ agboi yɛŋ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpa beni eyɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When harvested rice is bagged before it is fully dried, moisture gets trapped inside the bag. This trapped dampness tricks the rice grains into thinking they have been planted in wet soil, causing them to sprout shoots.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ wo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Moisture baatsi kotoku lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli nɛɛ lakaa ŋmãa lɛ ni esusuɔ akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants have long, sharp needles growing out of the tops of the grains this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those long needles are called awns. Some rice varieties naturally produce awns as a defense mechanism to prevent birds and animals from easily eating the grains directly from the plant.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii kakadaji lɛ akɛ awns. Omɔ henɔi komɛi feɔ awns yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye dumɔwui ni jɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why did my rice produce full, heavy grains last year, but this year most of the husks are empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ lɛ fa babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi afi nɛɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ babaoo etee?

english: Empty grains, often called chaff, usually happen when the crop experiences extreme heat or a dry spell right during the flowering stage, which prevents the flowers from properly forming seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ chaff Bei pii lɛ ebaa kɛji tso lɛ shɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo egbi yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo dumɔwui jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my harvested maize developing white and black powder on the cobs while drying on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: That powder is mold caused by fungal growth. It happens when harvested grains stay damp, lack proper airflow, or sit directly on wet ground during the drying process.
ga: Pauda lɛ ji ŋmei ni jɛɔ ŋmei ni daraa lɛ mli baa. Ebaa beni dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni agbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do small black beetles appear inside my stored beans after a few weeks, even though the beans looked clean when I harvested them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ moŋ.

english: Weevil insects often lay invisible eggs inside bean pods while the crop is still in the field. After harvest, these eggs hatch inside the stored seeds, and the adult beetles eat their way out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. kpamɔ sɛɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ amli. Ni ŋmeii ni eda lɛ baaye amɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow in the middle, starting from the bottom of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing along the center of maize leaves is a common sign of nitrogen deficiency. It means the soil lacks enough nutrients to support healthy green growth, indicating a need for fertilizer or compost.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl tightly inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the amount of leaf surface exposed to the sun to conserve water during the hottest part of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni amɛbu nu he yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their blossoms instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miiwo fɔfɔi moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden changes in watering, such as going from very dry soil to heavy water all at once.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛtee nu babaoo nɔ shikome.

english: Why do my crop stalks grow very tall and slender, but produce very small harvest yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight. They put all their energy into growing tall to reach light rather than developing strong stems and heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara, koni amɛshɛ la he. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ tsohi nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii nɛ tsii.

english: Why are my cassava roots becoming tough and woody instead of cooking soft like usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfee tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahoo amɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee blɛoo tamɔ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody when left unharvested in the ground too long past their maturity, or when the crop experiences severe drought that bakes the surrounding soil hard.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni amɛdara tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ na hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni haa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli waɔ.

english: Why do insects like to hide under the leaves of my fruit trees and destroy the fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛyahi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ ahe baai ashishi ni amɛfite tsei lɛ ayibii lɛ?

english: Leaves provide shade, moisture, and protection for pests against direct sunlight and predators. Insects breed under the safety of dense foliage and easily crawl onto nearby fruits to feed on them.
ga: Baai haa hulutsoo, fɛ̃i kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni eyi obɔ kɛ shweshweeshwe shihilɛ shishi, ni amɛkpãa amɛshwieɔ aduawai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya koni amɛye amɛ.

english: How does managing or clearing excess leaves help protect my crops from insect attacks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni fa fe nine ni mikɛtsuɔ nii loo mijieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Trimming dense leaves reduces the cool, shady hiding spots that insects prefer. It allows sunlight and air to pass through the branches, which discourages insects from settling and laying eggs near your fruit.
ga: Baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ afolɔ haa he ni mli ejɔ, shade ni koolooi sumɔɔ ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe lɛ baa shi. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli. Enɛ baatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaba ni amɛwo ŋmeii yɛ oyibii lɛ ahe.

english: What causes insects to move from the leaves directly onto my growing fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii jɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa mi yibii ni miida lɛ anɔ?

english: As fruits develop, they become soft and rich in sugars and sap. Insects living under nearby leaves move onto the fruit because it offers an easy and nutrient-rich food source.
ga: Beni aduawai lɛ daraa Aduawai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni sugar kɛ mliki babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kplukai ni hiɔ baai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ashishi lɛ fãa kɛyaa aduawai lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ eji niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Where is the best place to pour water when watering my fruit trees?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mawo mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ nu yɛ?

english: Water should always be poured directly onto the soil at the base of the tree where the roots are. Trees absorb water through their root systems underground, not through their leaves or bark.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nu awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsei gbalaa nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ. Jeee baai loo tso lɛ yibii.

english: Do big, fully grown trees still need me to water them during dry periods?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni maná nu lolo yɛ tsei ni eda lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, large trees still require significant amounts of soil moisture to maintain their size and produce fruit. If the ground dries out completely, even a large tree will stop fruiting and can eventually die.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ babaoo he miihia tsei wuji lolo koni amɛhiɛ amɛdalɛ mli ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Tsei wuji po kpaa yibiiwoo ni yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛgboiɔ.

english: Should I spray water on the leaves of my crop or focus only on the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Focus on applying water to the ground around the trunk. Wetting leaves wastes water through evaporation and creates a damp environment where insects and plant diseases thrive.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama nu ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Baai ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu lɛ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai baanyɛ adara yɛ mli

english: How can I tell if the ground around my tree has enough water during dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dig a small hole a few inches into the soil near the tree's base. If the soil feels damp and holds together, there is water available; if it is dry and dusty, the tree needs watering right away.
ga: Tsɔmɔmɔ bu bibioo ko ni kɛlɛ ji inchi fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ edɔ ni ekɛ ehe ebɔ he lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ nu yɛ lolo. Kɛji egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ Esa akɛ awo tso lɛ nɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How does pouring water on the ground help my crop get food to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Water dissolves nutrients present in the soil so the roots can suck them up like a drink. Without soil moisture, a plant cannot absorb food from the ground, no matter how rich the soil is.
ga: Nu shwieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nakai niyenii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni anuɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei hu nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii aha

english: Why is my mango tree not producing good fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Developing fruits require extra water and energy from the tree. When soil moisture is low, the tree goes into survival mode and drops its flowers or yields small, poor-quality fruits to conserve water.
ga: Yibii ni baa lɛ biɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kroko kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: How do I know if a tree has dried out so badly that it should be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko egbo aahu akɛ esa akɛ afo lɛ?

english: If a tree loses all its leaves, its small branches become brittle and snap easily when bent, and there is no moisture left in the surrounding soil, the tree is likely dead and ready to be removed.
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko baai lɛ fɛɛ shwie lɛ, eniji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ oya kɛ́ amɛkumɔ. ni ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa eshwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Ekolɛ tso lɛ hu egbo ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I use the seeds I saved from my previous harvest for planting this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over generations. They often produce weaker crops, smaller yields, and are more vulnerable to pests and diseases compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ewooo yibii babaoo ni amɛhe waaa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do seeds bought from an agro-input shop grow better than the ones I take from my own storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe shwapo mli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ?

english: Shop-bought certified seeds are specially bred, treated, and tested to ensure high germination rates, strong disease resistance, and uniform growth, whereas storehouse seeds lack these protections.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ, atsuɔ he nii, ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo. Helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ hela ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ bɛ hebuu nɛɛ.

english: Is it really necessary to buy new seeds every planting season instead of saving money and using my own?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ahe dumɔwui heei daa be mli ni amɛdaraa? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni bo diɛŋtsɛ oookɛ shika ato ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ atsu nii?

english: Yes, buying fresh certified seeds each season is an investment because the higher yield and stronger plants easily make up for the cost of buying the seed.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ ji shikawoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yibiiwoo ni fa kɛ tsei ni he wa lɛ baanyɛ ajie shika ni akɛheɔ dumɔwui lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why do seeds taken from market grain produce poor crops when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ jara nɔ lɛ wooo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: Grain sold in the market is meant for eating, not planting. It is often damaged, lacks disease treatment, or comes from hybrid varieties that cannot reproduce good crops a second time.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ koni aye, shi jeee ni adu. Bei pii lɛ efiteɔ Tsamɔ ni bɛ loo ejɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my neighbor getting a bigger harvest than me when we have the same soil type and planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo woɔ yibii babaoo fe mi lɛ? Beni wɔyɔɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ kome ni wɔduɔ nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest often come down to seed quality. Neighbors who buy certified seeds from reliable companies usually get higher yields than those who plant saved seeds from previous harvests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ damɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Bei pii lɛ, akutsoŋbii ni heɔ dumɔwui ni awo he hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ nitsumɔhei ni akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ naa yibiiwoo babaoo fe mɛi ni duɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my crops growing unevenly with some plants tall and others very weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ekomɛi daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ekomɛi hu bɛ hewalɛ waa lɛ?

english: Uneven growth often happens when you plant saved seeds from a previous crop, as genetic quality varies from seed to seed. Certified seeds give consistent and uniform plant growth across the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee baa kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, esoro bɔ ni fɔmɔ nii yɔɔ ha lɛ yɛ dumɔwu kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baaha tsei adalɛ afee ekome ni ehi shi daa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to catch diseases more easily than crops grown from company seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni helai baanyɛ amɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli oya fe tsei ni adu kɛjɛ nitsumɔhe dumɔwui amli lɛ?

english: Commercial seed companies treat their seeds with protective coatings and breed them specifically to resist common diseases, whereas saved farm seeds carry over infections from previous seasons.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni feɔ dumɔwui ahe jarayeli lɛ kɛ nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ ahe nii, ni amɛfɔɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What should I do when I notice my crops are not performing well in the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mina akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Whenever you observe strange crop growth or poor field performance, you should immediately contact your local agricultural extension officer to inspect the field and diagnose the root cause.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaana tsei ni miida yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ loo he ko ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ Esa akɛ oya okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ okwaayeli lɛ nɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ekwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okwɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can an extension officer help me when my crops start showing signs of failure?
ga: Te extension agent lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfite lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: An extension officer can identify whether the failure is caused by poor seed quality, soil issues, pests, or diseases, and guide you on the right treatments or better planting materials to use next time.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ana kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii, shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai ahewɔ ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ tsamɔi ni sa loo dumɔ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii be kroko lɛ he.

english: Where can I find reliable, high-quality seeds that are recommended for planting?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ?

english: You can get high-quality certified seeds from registered agro-input dealers, authorized seed companies, or by asking your local agricultural extension officer for approved suppliers.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli nibii ahe jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Dumɔwui ahe nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ hegbɛ Aloo bi mɛi ni kɛ nibii nɛɛ baa lɛ ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ kɛjɛ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ dɛŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that act as umbrellas, shading the cocoa and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa kookoo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It traps moisture in the dirt, keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow while the plant is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea when the soil is moist can help your crops recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea fata he, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same farm field?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can plant maize and cassava together because maize grows fast and is harvested early, leaving plenty of room for the slower-growing cassava to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa afee ekome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Enɛ haa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I rotate my crops instead of planting maize on the same soil every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and builds up pest populations. Alternating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts valuable nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ayibɔ aya hiɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei wo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni jara wa aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Apply fertilizer a few weeks after planting when young roots can absorb it, and always apply it when the soil is damp after rain so the nutrients dissolve into the root zone.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ. Ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ shishifã lɛ he

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes through my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys maize leaves. You can control them by applying approved crop treatments during early mornings or late evenings when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmeii ahe tsei. Obaanyɛ okɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ akudɔ amɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ be mli beni ŋmeii lɛ eje kpo kɛmiiya niyenii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning light green and yellow with a twisted shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsake lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning extra branches lets in sunlight and air movement, which keeps the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Afoɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize grains from insects while in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe yɛ be mli ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Ensure your maize is completely dried before storing it, clean your barn thoroughly, and store the grain in airtight bags or treat it with safe grain protection powder to stop insect attacks.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ o-corn lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛto. Tsumɔ otsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato vacuum kotokui amli Aloo okɛ dumɔwui ahebuu powda ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii ni okɛkpa kooloi ni baatutua bo lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young cassava plants instead of just letting them grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? cassava tso bibioo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ekwɛ ekome

english: Cassava roots need space, water, and soil nutrients to grow big. Weeds act like thief plants that steal food and water from the cassava and block sunlight, causing your cassava to grow weak and produce very small tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ nii, ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa o-cassava lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow and showing tiny holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Holes and yellow leaves are signs that insect pests, like the fall armyworm, are eating your crop, or that your soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen. The insects damage the leaves, making it hard for the plant to feed itself and stay green.
ga: Bu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi tamɔ cutworms miiye oŋmɔshi nibii. Aloo niyenii kpakpai tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koolooi fiteɔ baai lɛ, ni no haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: What is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the soil is moist, but never right before a heavy downpour. Heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away down the hill before the plant roots get a chance to drink it in.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Shi kaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ gɔŋji lɛ anɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees yield fewer pods when I cut down all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees need partial shade to protect them from strong sunshine and hot dry winds. Without shade, heat stresses the trees, dries out the soil quickly, and causes the flowers to drop off before forming cocoa pods.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: How do I know whether to plant seeds saved from my last harvest or buy certified seeds from an extension officer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Aloo hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ sɛɛgbɛtsɔɔmɔ nitsulɔi lɛ adɛŋ.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time and carry diseases from past seasons. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist common diseases, withstand drought better, and produce much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ helai ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo babaoo

english: Why does my harvested maize get dusty and spoiled inside storage bags after just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo sũ ni efiteɔ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rots or gets destroyed by weevils if it is not dried properly before bagging. Moist grain creates a home for tiny insects and mold that eat the inside of the kernel and turn it into dust.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbo loo ŋmeii lɛ efiteɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko lɛ dani akɛwo kotoku mli. Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ feɔ shia kɛhaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii. No yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mligbɛ ni ehaa efeɔ sũ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Very hot weather damages the flower's delicate parts, preventing it from forming fruit. Watering early in the morning and keeping soil covered with grass mulch keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baafite fɔfɔi lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehaaa enyɛŋ ewo yibii Nu ni awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do I need to start my pepper seeds in a small nursery bed instead of planting them straight into the big farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu pepper dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are tiny and fragile when they first sprout. Raising them in a nursery bed lets you easily protect them from hot sun, heavy rains, and bugs until they are strong enough to survive in the open field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo gbekɛbii ashihilɛhei lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ kooloi bibii ahe mlɛo. Kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Groundnuts and beans are special plants that put natural fertilizer back into the earth, which refreshes your land for the next crop without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ baaha okpokpaa lɛ nɔ afee fɛo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is ready for harvesting without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmãa lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Check the age of the crop (usually 9 to 12 months) and look at the leaves; when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the stem gets thick, it is time to dig up one test plant to inspect the tuber size.
ga: Kwɛmɔ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eye (bei pii lɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) ni okwɛ baai lɛ, be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Be eshɛ ni esa akɛ atsa kaa tso ko koni akɛkwɛ bulb lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my corn plants turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your corn lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my maize plants fall over easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots are shallow or when planted too close together, making their stalks thin and weak. Planting at the right depth and giving plants proper spacing allows them to develop strong brace roots that grip the soil firmly.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa kɛ gbɛ ni sa ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn plants stay small and fail to produce big cobs when rains stop early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛwooo ŋmeii wuji kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra lɛ?

english: Corn needs plenty of water especially during flowering and cob formation. When water is scarce, the plant saves energy just to stay alive, which stops cobs from filling up with grains.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia ŋmãa, titri lɛ yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Beni nu faaa lɛ Tsei toɔ hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui ayi ŋmei lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same spot drains the specific nutrients corn needs and allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nutrients like nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha niyenii tamɔ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when planted right after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ adu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The early season rains cause a natural release of nutrients stored in the soil after the dry spell. Planting immediately lets your seedlings drink water and absorb this rich splash of plant food before weeds start taking over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Dumɔ baaye abua odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnu nu ni amɛŋɔ tso niyenii ni egbɛ eshwa nɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dani jwɛi lɛ baaje shishi amɛye nɔ

english: Why do my crops turn pale and stunted when planted in waterlogged areas of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air just like humans do. When soil stays flooded with water, it drowns the roots, stopping them from breathing and taking up nutrients to feed the leaves.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi hu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haa amɛmuɔ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa baai lɛ yeɔ niyenii.

english: Why does my harvested corn get eaten by small insects so quickly inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mi nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects like weevils lay eggs inside dry maize grains, especially if the grains were stored with leftover moisture. Properly drying the corn until grains crack between your teeth and using insect-proof storage bags stops them from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to ni ŋmɔtɔ eshwɛ. Abele ni ooogbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baaje kpo yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ Ni okɛ kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ni kooloi nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafee babaoo.

english: Why is it important to dry my corn thoroughly before taking it to buyers or factories?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbi ŋmãa dani akɛyaha mɛi ni heɔ loo nitsumɔhei lɛ?

english: Wet or damp corn grows harmful mold that can poison humans and animals, making factories reject it. Drying corn properly keeps it safe, extends its storage life, and gets you a better selling price.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ loo efɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ji awui kɛhaa adesai kɛ kooloi baa. Ha nitsumɔhei srɔtoi akpoo ŋmeii ni tamɔ nɛkɛ Abele ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa efeɔ shweshweeshwe. Ha be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Can I use my harvested corn to make other products instead of just selling the raw dry grains?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ kroko yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi ni ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Yes, corn is very versatile. Beyond selling raw grains, you can process corn into animal feed, cornflour, cereal mixes, or sell it to processing factories that make commercial starch and foods, which increases your overall farm income.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa yɛ srɔtoi waa. Kɛfata dumɔwui ni ahoo lɛ ahɔ̃ɔmɔ he lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmãa afee kooloi aniyenii, ŋmãa ashikishaŋ, ŋmãa ni akɛfutu mli, loo ohɔ̃ɔ oha ŋmãa nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ ashikishaŋ kɛ niyenii kɛha jarayeli. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ mli shika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do processing factories prefer specific types of maize for their products?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei ni feɔ nibii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛha amɛnibii lɛ?

english: Different maize varieties have different qualities; some are soft and ideal for local foods like kenkey, while yellow or hard flint varieties have higher starch or oil content preferred by factories for feeds and industrial products.
ga: Abele henɔi srɔtoi yɛ sui srɔtoi. Ekomɛi yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni sa kɛha maŋ lɛ mli niyenii, tamɔ Kenkey gbee lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tɛ ni ji yellow loo hard flint lɛ yɛ starch loo fɔ babaoo fe bɔ ni tso lɛ he hiaa kɛha kooloi aniyenii kɛ nitsumɔhei nibii.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rain season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until you receive a heavy rain that thoroughly wets the soil down deep (about 2 to 3 consecutive rain days) rather than planting after the very first light drizzle, so your seeds do not dry up and die in the soil.
ga: Mɛɛ ni onine ashɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũuɔ jogbaŋŋ (aaafee nugbɔshiimɔ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ), moŋ fe ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ, koni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the young cocoa seedlings on my farm burning up and losing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitso ni amɛbaai miiho lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing plantain plants nearby to act as living umbrellas that protect them from hot sun and retain soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni bu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow from the tip downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛnaa kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient that plants need to build food and stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge stems and leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or foliage growth energy, the plant uses all its strength to build leaves on top instead of storing energy underground to form thick, starchy roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo baa dalɛ hewalɛ babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa baa yɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ starch.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize on the same land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans with maize is very beneficial because beans catch nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while the maize stalk supports the bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my corn leaves and small powder that looks like sawdust inside the plant top?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda bibioo ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that crawls inside the young growing central leaf of the maize plant to feed during the early growth stages.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye niyenii yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato eŋɔli shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering or a shortage of calcium in the soil, which prevents the fruit from building strong skin at its base.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa aduawai lɛ afee hewolo ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay weak and small even after I add fertilizer?
