ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and the applied fertilizer away from your crops before your crop roots have a chance to take them in.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛboteɔ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry bush grass or palm fronds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi loo ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) protects it from the hot sun, keeps moisture in the ground longer, and prevents weeds from easily popping up around your plants.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ ni otsi jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ otso lɛ he lɛ naa mlɛo

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viral sicknesses passed on by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants turning brown and dry during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, crops lose water faster than their roots can absorb it from the soil. This severe heat stress burns the delicate leaf tissue, causing the leaves to dry out and turn brown.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa nɛɛ shãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo.

english: How does extreme afternoon heat affect the overall growth of my crops?
ga: Te shwane mli dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Very high temperatures force crops to spend energy trying to cool down rather than growing. This slows down their development, damages plant tissues, causes flowers to fall off, and reduces your final yield.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ̃. Enɛ baaha dalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. efiteɔ tso mli fãji ni ehaa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni ehaa onaagbee nibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Does intense sunlight hurt all crops, or do tender plants need shade in warm areas?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ awui aloo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: While plants need sunlight to make food, intense direct heat in warm regions can easily scorch tender crops and young seedlings. Providing temporary or partial shade helps them survive the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la he miihia tsei koni amɛfee niyenii moŋ, shi la ni naa wa ni baa tɛ̃ɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei bibii lɛ oya. Kɛ́ aha amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo loo fã ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I water my crops early in the morning rather than during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ nu leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the soil to absorb moisture and cool the roots before intense heat sets in, whereas afternoon watering rapidly evaporates in high heat without helping the plant.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ dani latsaa lɛ yeɔ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ baaho oya yɛ latsaa be mli ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ.

english: How can spreading dry leaves or straw on my soil protect my plants from scorching weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he?

english: Spreading dry material like mulch over the soil acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and protects lower plant roots from heat damage.
ga: Nibii ni egbi tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu shwieɔ shi oya, ni ebuɔ tso shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Can building a enclosed structure or greenhouse get too hot for my crops in a warm area?
ga: Ani tsũ ko ni afo mli loo ŋmɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ maa baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ tsɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, enclosed farm structures trap heat from sunlight like an oven. If the structure is not properly ventilated or designed for high-temperature areas, the trapped heat will scorch and kill the crops inside.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsũi ni aŋã lɛ mɔɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tamɔ flɔnɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ tsũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo afeee lɛ aha hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni emɔmɔ lɛ baashã ni ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ.

english: What kind of shade shelter should I build to keep my young seedlings from burning?
ga: Mɛɛ hulutsoo be esa akɛ mafee koni mi dumɔwui lɛ akashã?

english: A good nursery shelter in hot areas should have a tall roof and breathable material like palm fronds or shade netting. This blocks harsh direct sunlight while allowing hot air to escape and cool air to flow through.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmɔ kpakpa ni yɔɔ hei ni latsaa yɔɔ lɛ aná ŋwɛitsu ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ nibii ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli tamɔ tsei ahe tsei ahe tsei loo shade netting. Enɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ naa, yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli.

english: Why do crops grown inside some farm structures dry out faster than crops outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji komɛi amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: If a farm structure lacks proper airflow, solar energy builds up inside and creates extreme temperatures that rapidly draw all the moisture out of both the soil and the plant foliage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Hulu hewalɛ buaa ehe naa yɛ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo ni naa wa waa baa, ni no gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai amli oya.

english: What happens to my plants if the shelter I build for them does not have enough airflow?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ shĩa ni mima miha amɛ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa?

english: Without proper airflow, trapped heat creates a harsh microclimate inside the shelter that causes heat shock, withered leaves, stunted growth, and crop failure.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli wa baa shĩa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo, baai ni egboɔ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu shwereɔ

english: How does the height and material of a crop shade house affect the temperature inside?
ga: Te ŋwɛi shĩa lɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛ nibii ni akɛfee lɛ saa shĩa lɛ mli latsaa he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Higher roofs allow hot air to rise away from the plants, while breathable roofing materials allow trapped heat to escape, keeping the temperature around your crops significantly cooler.
ga: Kpoji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jeɔ tsei lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni tsũ yiteŋ nibii ni haa mɔ mumɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo. Ha hulutsoo ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain or cassava beside them creates natural shade and traps soil moisture, keeping the young cocoa cool and healthy.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava, yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ baa. Ehaa kookoo lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not carry it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a moderate rain, and then cover the fertilizer with a thin layer of soil. This helps the roots absorb it quickly before heavy rainfall can wash it down the field.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: When rain stays trapped in flat soil, it starves the plant roots of oxygen and invites soil fungi that rot the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Beni nugbɔ lɛ kã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ nine. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants dropping off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant experiences sudden dry spells. Keeping the soil surrounding the roots evenly moist with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ akɛ muji wo shishifãi lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by small sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that spread crop viruses. Spraying the plants early with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap removes these pests and protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi shwieɔ tsei anɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry out on the branch during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod is a common fungus disease that thrives in humid, shady conditions. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and fresh air into the tree canopy helps keep the cocoa pods dry and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji fungal hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees snap or fall over easily once they start growing big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛfee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain roots grow close to the soil surface, making tall plants top-heavy when carrying fruit. Supporting the main stem with strong bamboo or wooden forks prevents strong winds from knocking the tree over before harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsiimɔ babaoo kɛ́ ewo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ shi dani akpa.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my food crops stay stunted and produce smaller yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ miifee mlɛo ni ehaa amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last harvest fail to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their power to sprout if exposed to warmth, moisture, or insect damage during storage. Storing thoroughly dried seeds in airtight containers mixed with dry wood ash protects them until the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo, fɛ̃i loo kooloi fiteɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛ tso sũ ni egbi efutu mli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛyashi shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain or banana next to them provides shade and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my yam plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need sunlight to make food for their underground tubers. Staking holds the leaves up towards the sun, which helps the crop produce larger and healthier yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kpɛtɛ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ sweet potatoes ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants full of holes and covered in small caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu ni ŋmeii bibii ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which eat the tender growing center of maize plants. Catching them early and applying safe, recommended treatments stops them from destroying your harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni adu lɛ bibii lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra ni okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow with strange light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whiteflies or infected planting stems. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties from agricultural officers keeps your farm safe from this virus.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ji ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii bibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe tsɔne Kɛkɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni hela nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ he.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and rotten before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom-end rot, caused when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium, often due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots absorb calcium evenly.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn pale green or yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nutrients, particularly nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and grow. Adding compost or the right fertilizer restores nutrients to the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they leave natural nitrogen behind for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛshiɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ koni amɛkɛtsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop pests to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes or vegetables breaks pest cycles and restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni haa mɔ hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo aduawai tsakeɔ lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is covering the soil around my crops with dry grass helping them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around Miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ jwɛi yeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct sunlight from heating the soil. This keeps moisture in the ground longer and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa, ni ehaaa sũ lɛ mli adɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds when my crop seedlings are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young seedlings have small roots and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil food. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient needed to create chlorophyll and build green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure restores their healthy green color so they can grow big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni akɛfee klorofil ni akɛfee baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa bɔni afee ni amɛkwɛ toi wuji.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm help feed the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into tiny bumps on their roots. When the plant stems and roots rot after harvest, that nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmei, gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛsaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ beni tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles around them because waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babɔle amɛhe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from the hot sun to keep moisture from evaporating too quickly and stops weeds from taking over your garden.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akafo oya tsɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye obɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to build thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines need to climb off the ground so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is sent down to grow a much larger tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ hoɔ. ni atsu amɛ kɛba shi koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni dara kwraa lɛ

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die if there are no plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ aduko dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct scorching sun. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad living shade and keep the air humid, giving cocoa seedlings the protection they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni miida oya lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ náa hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or pest attack. When the plant feels under threat, it drops flowers to preserve its own energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ awo amɛhe gbeyei Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha yibii heei aba lɛ

english: Why does cutting off the extra shoots on my pepper plants help them produce bigger peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning extra branches prevents the crop from wasting energy on growing excess stems and leaves, directing more water and nutrients straight into developing larger, healthier pepper fruits.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛfee pepper aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my crops if I delay weeding until the weeds grow tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji mikɛ jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ shwie shi kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ baatswa shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from crops during their early growth stage. Even if you weed later, the crop may have already been permanently stunted by the early competition.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli. Kɛji akɛ okɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po. Akaŋshii ni baa mra lɛ hu baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii afee shoo daa.

english: Why should I buy registered seeds from the market instead of just planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli lɛ kɛjɛ jara nɔ lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i du duwuhi nɛ a yi wami kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ.

english: Approved seeds from the national variety catalog are specially tested to resist local diseases, survive dry weather, and produce a much higher yield than saved seeds, which lose their strength after a few seasons.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ana he odaseyeli kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi ahe woji amli lɛ akwɛɔ krɛdɛɛ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Ehiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ato ni hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my red, iron-rich soil dry out so fast and get hard like brick after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi shikpɔŋ tsuru ni dade eyi mli obɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya ni ewaa tamɔ brikii beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Soil high in iron and clay bakes quickly under hot sun, causing the surface to form a hard crust that prevents rainwater from sinking in and makes it difficult for crop roots to breathe and spread.
ga: Shikpɔji ni dade kɛ shikpɔŋ sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni wa ni tsiɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekabote mli, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are the leaves on my young rice plants turning yellow when there is standing water in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Even though rice likes moisture, water that stays too deep for too long without moving prevents air from reaching the roots, stopping the plant from taking up food and causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ moŋ Shi nu ni hiɔ shi yɛ mli tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni etsiii ehe lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ niyenii ni eha baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense to protect itself from losing too much water through its foliage when the sun is very bright and the soil is dry.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni ekɛbuɔ ehe koni ekaje nu babaoo kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shiɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ mli dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer causes stress to the plant, making it shed its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ kɛha shishijee wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed new growth at the top, causing lower leaves to fade and yellow.
ga: Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi lɛ ashishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak crops with small yields rather than strong, productive plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami nɛ e woɔ yiblii.

english: Why do crops grow so small and thin when weeds are left around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi eshwɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds act as thieves that steal water, sunlight, and nutrients away from your crops, starving the young plants during their most important growing stage.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. ni ehaa tso bibioo lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ yɛ edalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, restoring fertility for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni aku sɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aba fɔmɔ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and watery when harvested during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, cassava plants focus energy on growing fresh green leaves and absorb extra water into the tubers, which reduces starch content and makes the roots watery.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Yucca tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ, ni amɛjieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli nu.

english: Young cocoa leaves scorch easily when exposed to direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees nearby to protect them from harsh heat until their root system matures.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow starting from the tip down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛyaa amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in a V-shape from the leaf tip inward usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient crops need to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: V-shape ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee kɛyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛhe nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is my cassava plant growing very tall with big green leaves, but the tubers underground are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cassava spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch to swell its roots underneath.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, e ngɔɔ starch kɛ toɔ konɛ e sisifã ɔmɛ nɛ a hwɔɔ ngɛ e sisi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when soil moisture is uneven, during periods of extreme heat, or when tiny pests damage the blossoms before insects can pollinate them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa lɛ mli Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii Fiteɔ fɔfɔii dani kooloi bibii baanyɛ afee amɛ pollen.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the suckers grow around my main plantain stem at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain titri lɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kome too mli

english: When too many suckers grow together, they steal food and water from each other, resulting in smaller bunches for all stems instead of one heavy, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ fee ekome kɛdara tsɔ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo. Mohu ɔ, e ji kuu kake, nɛ e tsii, nɛ e he wa.

english: Yam leaves need to reach up into full sunlight to make energy. If the vines lay on the dark ground, they cannot capture enough light to grow a large tuber.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ wain tso lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ nɔ Enyɛŋ ená la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops wilt and shed leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds suck moisture rapidly out of plant leaves. Shedding leaves is a plant's natural defense to save water and keep its main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which damage the leaves and can spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwa tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young corn leaves with small dark dirt inside the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli buji ni egbɛ eshwa kɛ muji bibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ? yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the corn plant during the day and feeds on the soft leaf tissue.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni amɛye baai bibii amli fãji

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas have natural root bacteria that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground, leaving behind free soil food for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi amli helai ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni akɛdu wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die if I plant them in an open field without any plantains or shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni kookoo tsei loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them provides shade and keeps the soil moist, helping the young cocoa plants survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to chew up the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: These pests are commonly Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize plants, and when the caterpillars hatch, they eat the tender leaves inside the growing center, which can destroy the crop if not controlled quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ebaaye baai bibii yɛ he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ oya.

english: Why does putting too much dry fertilizer right next to my crop stems make the plants wither?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi babaoo fata mitso lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Fertilizers are rich in salts. When concentrated fertilizer touches tender stems or roots directly without enough water, it draws moisture out of the plant instead of feeding it, causing the crop to burn and dry up.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔ ni ŋmei eyi mli obɔ lɛ Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishifãi ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Egbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shãa ni egbiɔ.

english: Yam plants need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the vines off the ground, reducing plant leaves from rotting due to wet soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tso lɛ akagbee shikpɔŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei ahe baai lɛ baa shi koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stems to cut and plant for a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mafolɔ ni madu koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: The best cassava cuttings come from the middle section of mature, healthy stems. The bottom part is often too woody, and the top part is too soft, but the middle part sprouts reliably and produces strong roots.
ga: Cassava tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ jɛɔ tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ fã lɛ ji tso tsɔ. ni ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ Shi teŋgbɛ fã lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi ni wa.

english: What happens if I plant my cassava stem cuttings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei niji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin plants that produce very small and slender cassava roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo, ni no haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa ni amɛhe tseee.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when the soil gets too dry, or when insects do not visit to pollinate them, preventing the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and making the plant look stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. These insects feed on young leaves and can also spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei amli helai ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ hu amɛshwã.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps the root area cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why are some farmers now planting their crops in containers or bags instead of directly into the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii yɛ tsɛnsii loo kotokui amli moŋ fe ni amɛaawo amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Planting crops off the ground protects them from stubborn diseases and pests that live in the soil. It keeps the roots clean and healthy so the crop can produce a good harvest.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni wa kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahe tseɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii aná ŋmaa kpakpa.

english: How do diseases hiding in my soil end up damaging my crops?
ga: Te helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Harmful fungi and bacteria live in old farmland soil and attack plant roots from underground. This stops the crop from taking up water, causing it to wither and die even if you take care of it.
ga: Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei shishifãi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aŋɔ nu. Enɛ haa egbiɔ ni egboɔ kɛji okwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick even after I clear the land and apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni mikɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: Fertilizer cannot protect plants if the soil itself already carries diseases. If the soil is contaminated, root infections will still prevent the crop from using the nutrients you apply.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ abu tsei ahe kɛji akɛ hela emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ momo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ewo muji Shishifãi lɛ amli helai ni baa lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni enyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni okɛwo mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: What does fertigation mean, and how can it help my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji fɔmɔ nii shishi? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Fertigation means mixing plant nutrients directly into your irrigation water pipes. This delivers food and water to the crop's roots at the same time, saving you labor and reducing wasted fertilizer.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafutu nu paipii ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu yaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ be kome too mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ nitsumɔ toɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How does feeding my crops through water pipes save me money compared to scattering fertilizer by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa kɛtsɔ hose nɔ lɛ haa shika baa shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ niji shwieɔ shi lɛ he?

english: When you broadcast fertilizer by hand, heavy rains can wash it away or weeds can steal it. Feeding crops through pipes puts the nutrients right at the roots so every drop is used by your plant.
ga: Beni okɛ onine duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jwɛi baanyɛ aju. Niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ paipii anɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, otsei lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsuɔ nii.

english: How can I make sure my crops get enough water during the long dry season in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: By using pipeline irrigation systems, you can measure and deliver the exact amount of water your crops need every day, keeping them green and productive even when there is no rain.
ga: Kɛtsɔ paipii ni akɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ osusu nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ daa gbi lɛ he ni okɛha. Ehaa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why is it dangerous to just guess how much water and fertilizer to give my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ masusu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Giving plants too little water or food starves them, while giving them too much can drown the roots or burn the crop. Measuring exact amounts gives the plant just what it needs to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu loo niyenii fioo tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli loo eshã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni asusuɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ daa kwraa.

english: Do crops really need different amounts of water and food as they grow?
ga: Ani nu kɛ niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei diɛŋtsɛ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, just like growing children, crops require precise amounts of water and specific nutrients at different stages of their life to grow strong stems and bear heavy fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, tamɔ gbekɛ ni miida lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ nu abɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Can crops actually grow properly without their roots touching normal farmland dirt?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ etaaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ daa lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, plants do not strictly need dirt to grow; they only need support, oxygen, water, and nutrients. As long as you supply food and water directly to the roots, they will grow fast and healthy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ babaoo he ehiaaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa amɛ ji yelikɛbuamɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Shii abɔ ni okɛ niyenii kɛ nu haa shishifãi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛbaadara oya ni amɛbaaná hewalɛ.

english: Will growing my crops off the ground help them produce bigger fruits and higher yields?
ga: Ani mitsei lɛ ni mikɛbaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii wuji ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, because when crops don't have to fight soil-borne sicknesses or search deep in hard dirt for food, they put all their energy into growing bigger leaves and heavier fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awuu ashi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ loo amɛtao niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai wuji kɛ aduawai ni tsii ni amɛduɔ lɛ mli.

english: How many years will it take after I plant a coconut tree before I can start harvesting fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tso sɛɛ lɛ, afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani ebaanyɛ ekpa yibii?

english: Depending on the type you plant, dwarf coconut trees usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while the taller traditional varieties take about 6 to 10 years to produce their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei tsei ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli tsei srɔtoi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛshɛɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaa lɛ he.

english: How long does sugarcane take from the day I plant it until it is ready for cutting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmei heɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni esa akɛ afo lɛ?

english: Sugarcane generally takes between 12 to 18 months to fully mature and become ready for harvest, depending on the weather and the soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shɛ̃ heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani edaa ni efeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ. Edamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: Can I plant sugarcane together in the same field with my coconut trees?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ tamɔ ŋmei tso?

english: It is not ideal to grow sugarcane directly under mature coconut trees because coconut trees develop wide root systems and dense leaves that block light, preventing the sugarcane from getting the sunlight and soil space it needs to thrive.
ga: Sugar cane ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tso ni eda shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni mli ewo wu ni tsiɔ la naa. Tsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekaná hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my small crops dry up when I plant them close to large trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii Minɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ midu yɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Large trees have big, strong root systems that drink up most of the water and nutrients in the ground, leaving very little water for nearby smaller crops to survive.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa ni nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa nu fioo pɛ eshwɛɔ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why is my sugarcane not growing well under the shade of the bigger trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sugarcane lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Sugarcane requires full, bright sunlight all day to make energy and produce sugar; deep shade from larger trees starves the sugarcane and stunts its growth.
ga: Sugarcane he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni eyi obɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli koni enyɛ ená hewalɛ ni ekɛ sugar aba. Tsei wuji ahe hulutsoo ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni etsĩɔ amɛdalɛ naa.

english: If I plant coconut trees among my short-term food crops, will the trees eventually kill off the smaller crops?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei tsei ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Ani tsei lɛ baagbe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ naagbee?

english: Yes, as coconut trees grow larger, their spreading roots take over the soil space and their big leaves shade out the ground, gradually pushing out smaller crops that need sunlight and surface soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ da Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ nɔ. Ni ebaai wuji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa lɛ fiofio.

english: How far under the ground do coconut roots spread, and can they affect other plants nearby?
ga: Te ŋmei shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashɛɔ he tɛŋŋ? Ni ani ebaana tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Coconut roots spread out several meters around the base of the trunk, creating a dense underground network that aggressively pulls water and nutrients away from nearby plants.
ga: Kokoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mitai babaoo kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi tsɔne ko ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ yiwalɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I easily check if my soil has enough water for my crops without buying special equipment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mlɛo ni miheee nibii krɛdɛɛi?

english: You can check by stepping on the soil or squeezing a handful in your palm; if the soil feels damp, holds together, or leaves wetness on your boots, there is moisture available for crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ muji nɔ ni oootsi loo nine ni okɛaawo onine mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he, loo eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ okotokui lɛ anɔ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it a mistake to plant coconut trees too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji tɔmɔ akɛ aaadu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When coconut trees are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same soil water and nutrients, and their crowns block each other's sunlight, leading to poor growth and low fruit yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni tsei lɛ akɔɔblei lɛ haa amɛhe hulu la lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni yibiiwoo hu faaa.

english: What types of crops grow best on parts of my farm that stay wet easily?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu shwieɔ oya lɛ?

english: Crops like sugarcane and rice love naturally moist soil and do very well in water-rich areas, whereas crops that dislike wet roots may rot if planted in the same soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Tsei ni sumɔɔɔ shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Can using the wrong chemical fertilizer damage or kill my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani tsofa ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ afite loo efite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, improper or unapproved chemical fertilizers can burn the tree's root system, damage soil health, and reduce pod production instead of helping the crop grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso mli ni esaaa loo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso shishifãi lɛ. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if a new chemical spray is safe to use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofa hee ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Safe chemical inputs are tested and certified by government extension officers; using unapproved chemical sprays can leave toxic residues on cocoa beans and scorch plant leaves.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ kaa tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ amɛkwɛɔ ni amɛhaa he odaseyeli. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashi tsofai fɔji ni eshwɛ yɛ kookoo yibii kɛ tsei ahe baai ni eshã lɛ anɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix pest chemicals directly with my crop fertilizer before applying it?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baafutu ŋmɔshi nibii amli tɛ̃ɛ dani mikɛtsu nii?

english: No, combining pesticides with fertilizer without guidance can trigger harmful chemical reactions that burn crop roots, lessen fertilizer effectiveness, and damage plant foliage.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii futu mli ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ko ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni shãa tsei shishifãi. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni efiteɔ tsei ahe baai

english: Why do extension officers recommend specific fertilizers instead of cheap chemical mixtures in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe ŋaa yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni jara waaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Recommended fertilizers are scientifically tested to feed cocoa safely, whereas unverified chemical mixtures may contain harsh substances that permanently ruin soil fertility and destroy your crop.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ ekwɛ jeŋ nilee mli koni akɛha kookoo niyenii shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akako amɛ akwɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahi nibii ni mli wa ni fiteɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛya naanɔ, ni efiteɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens if I suddenly change the type of fertilizer I use on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mitsake ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ trukaa?

english: Switching fertilizers without advice can shock your trees if the new product contains chemicals or nutrient levels that burn the roots or disrupt normal crop development.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni oootsake ni ŋaawoo ko bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ ahe afee shoo kɛji tsofai loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shãa shishifãi lɛ loo tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa yɛ nibii heei lɛ amli.

english: Where exactly around my cocoa tree should I place fertilizer so it does not harm the trunk?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo kookoo tso lɛ he koni ekaye tso lɛ shishi lɛ awui?

english: Fertilizer should be applied in a ring under the outer edge of the leaf canopy, far enough from the main trunk so feeder roots absorb nutrients without getting chemically burned.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ baa lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛtsɔ ekɛ tso wulu lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni aha amɛ niyenii lɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsofai ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees need different fertilizer than food crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi fe niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Every crop needs specific nutrient ratios to flower and fruit; cocoa needs higher potassium for pod health, while grain crops need high nitrogen for early growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko ni akɛtoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai ahe. Cocoa he miihia potassium babaoo kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii he hiaa nitrogen babaoo koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow after I applied a new chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa hee ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ efata he lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves after fertilizing usually indicate root burn caused by applying too much chemical fertilizer, putting it too close to the stem, or using an unapproved mixture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni shãa ni tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ kɛbaa. ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛ nibii ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ atsu nii

english: Why do my young cocoa trees still need shade even when I apply fertilizer to help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight, so shade trees act as protection while fertilizer nourishes the roots, allowing the young plant to establish safely.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ hebuu nitsumɔ ko he nii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso bibioo lɛ ni etswaa ehe shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What should I do if my cocoa trees stop producing pods after I apply a new chemical product?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ kpa ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ beni mikɛ tsofa hee ko etsu nii sɛɛ?

english: Stop using the chemical product immediately and ask an agricultural extension officer to inspect your farm to diagnose chemical toxicity and guide your crop's recovery.
ga: Kpaa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni obi okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko ni ekwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ena tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ aha bɔ ni ooofee okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade from taller plants like plantain or shade trees. Direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their roots are deep enough to find groundwater.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ amli aba mli bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛna shikpɔŋ shishi nu.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the middle vein is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong stalks and full ears, so adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps green them up.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toi ni eyi obɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Fertilizers need soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb them. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can concentrate the salts around the roots and burn them, damaging the crop instead of helping it grow.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eshã amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into large mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifeɔ muji agbo dani miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily into large tubers. High mounds also protect the tubers from rotting by letting excess rainwater drain away during heavy downpours.
ga: Sweet potato bulbs lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo ni etsɔ bulbs wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni ehaa amɛhoɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer feeds the nearby maize plants and keeps your field rich for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni otsaaa jɛmɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when the lower leaves yellow and fall off, the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack, and the main stem turns thick and woody.
ga: Yucca jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ tsei

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant gets too much nitrogen, causing it to put energy into leaf growth instead of fruit production.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants crinkling and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, which can spread plant viruses that stunt crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ tsei amli helai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ ashwã

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and stops weeds from sprouting and stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi (mulch) wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Which plantain sucker is best for me to dig up and plant in a new farm?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain sucker ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad stem base—are best. They grow much faster and produce larger, healthier bunches than water suckers, which have broad leaves early on but weak roots.
ga: Sword shoots, ni yɔɔ baai bibii ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ. Amɛdaraa oya kwraa ni amɛwoɔ niji ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni nuɔ nu, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛjɛ shishijee shi shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die so quickly when the rain stops for just two weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa enɛ otsii enyɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need a steady supply of soil moisture to draw nutrients up to their leaves. During short dry spells, hot weather evaporates water from the topsoil rapidly, causing plants to lose water faster than their roots can pull it in.
ga: Tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Enɛ haa tso lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu awo mli.

english: How can I capture and store rainwater on my farm to use when the rains stop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ nugbɔ nu ato miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa?

english: You can dig simple earth ponds lined with plastic sheeting to catch surface runoff, build shallow trenches (sunk beds) near crop roots to trap rainwater, or direct rainwater from shed roofs into storage drums.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa shikpɔŋ nu ŋshɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ plastic ebɔ he lɛ koni okɛ nu ato ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Bɔɔ bui ni mli ekɔɔɔ (saji ni ebote) yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe koni ona nugbɔ nu. Aloo okɛ nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amajeɔ tsɔne ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it true that watering my crops during the middle of a hot afternoon can harm them?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, watering in hot sunshine causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before roots can absorb it, and hot water drops on leaves can stress the plant. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu ni mli edɔ ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Can covering my soil with dry grass or leaves really keep the ground moist during hot weather?
ga: Ani jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, this practice is called mulching. Dry leaves or straw act like a protective blanket over the soil, blocking direct sunlight so the ground stays cool and retains water much longer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ kuntu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni etsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be babaoo.

english: If I expand my farm to a much bigger plot of land, will my harvest automatically double?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shwere kɛtee he ko ni da kwraa lɛ Ani mikpamɔ lɛ baafee shii enyɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Planting a larger field requires significantly more fertilizer, weed control, and labor; if you spread your existing resources too thin over a bigger area, the crop yield per acre often drops.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Dumɔ yɛ hei wuji biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ nitsulɔi babaoo Kɛji ogbɛ nibii fioo ko pɛ oshwã he ko ni da lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa yɛ acre kome mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do insect pests spread much faster when I plant only one crop across a very large field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ ŋmɔ ni da waa mli lɛ?

english: A large field with only one crop provides an endless food source for pests that feed on that specific plant. Without different crops or trees to act as natural barriers, pests can easily move and multiply across the entire farm.
ga: ŋmɔ agbo ko ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji niyenii jɛɛhe ni bɛ naagbee kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei srɔtoi ni baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii bɛ lɛ, Pests baanyɛ afã ni amɛshwere yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli fɛɛ mlɛo.

english: What happens to my farm soil if I clear a large area of land and leave it bare before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie he ko ni da ni mishi jɛmɛ dani midu nii?

english: Bare soil left exposed to heavy rains gets washed away in a process called erosion, taking topsoil nutrients with it. Direct sunlight also bakes bare soil hard, making it difficult for seeds to germinate.
ga: Akɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eshi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ erosion lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ ni ekɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli waa. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui akɛ amɛakwɛ̃

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sunshine gets very intense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔne ko beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which cuts down on moisture loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi.

english: How does heavy pouring rain affect the fertilizer I put in the soil for my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rainfall can wash surface fertilizer away into streams or wash dissolved nutrients deep into the subsoil past the reach of crop roots, a problem known as nutrient leaching.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ faai amli lɛ loo afɔ niyenii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he, kɛho tsei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ ji naagba ko ni ale lɛ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with few leaves when there are many rainy and cloudy days in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ ni ebɛ baai fioo lɛ? Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni atatu ewo mli gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants rely on sunlight to produce energy. When dark clouds block the sun for long periods, crops stretch upward rapidly searching for light, resulting in tall, weak stems that can break easily.
ga: Tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ atatui ni tsuɔ nii yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ ha hulu lɛ mli tse be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ oya koni amɛyatao la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsei lɛ kɛlɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni baanyɛ akumɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the primary nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. Applying compost or a nitrogen-based fertilizer like urea can help restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nitrogen fee tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant groundnuts or beans on my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. Rotating them with nutrient-hungry crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without buying extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsake kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the tender growing points of maize. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or insecticides can protect your harvest before severe damage occurs.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ hei ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ anɔ. Onibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ okɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe dani nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ aba.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides on my crops right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ ahe dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: Rain washes the liquid pesticide off the leaves before the plant or target pests can absorb it. Spraying on a dry morning when rain is not expected gives the chemical enough time to work effectively.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ baai amli dani tso loo kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai lɛ shwie nɔ leebi ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi ni akpaaa gbɛ akɛ ebaanɛ lɛ, ebaaha tsofai lɛ aná be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when planted in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily burn under direct hot sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or banana trees alongside them provides a temporary natural canopy that protects the cocoa until it matures.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana tsei yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ekwɛɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and using grass mulch around the stem keeps the root area cool so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ latsaa mli haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ muji ni bɔleɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ ahe afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and curl during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large plantain leaves lose water very quickly in intense heat. Curling or drooping is the plant's natural way of reducing the leaf area exposed to the sun to conserve moisture until the temperature cools down.
ga: Plantain baai wuji lɛ amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Curling loo drooping ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their special yield strength and resistance in the second generation. Planting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven growth and much lower yields compared to buying fresh certified hybrid seeds each season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ yibiiwoo hewalɛ kroko kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni aŋmala ashwie shi lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa fe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ ni aheɔ daa afi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive root systems adapted to grab water and soil nutrients instantly. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing vital resources from your main crops while they are still young.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ koo mli ni eyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni atsake koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa ni jɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe Ni ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps the leaves grow green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce lots of green leaves but very few peanuts under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnuts need soft soil and calcium to make full pods. If the ground is too hard, the flower stalks cannot push into the soil, and if the soil lacks calcium, empty pods develop. Adding lime or poultry manure softens the soil and provides the nutrients needed for full peanuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli jɔ kɛ calcium he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ayi obɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Fɔfɔi ahe tsei nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko baakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo kooloi ashishifã fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food that travels down into the roots to build big tubers. Lifting the vines on stakes opens up the leaves to sunlight, stops diseases from spreading on the wet ground, and helps produce larger yams.
