ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Etsiɔ hela naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato lɛ ni edaa.

english: Plantain roots do not grow deep into the soil, making the plant top-heavy when heavy fruit bunches form. Supporting the stem with a strong bamboo pole or wooden fork acts as a crutch to keep the tree standing until harvest.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji aduawai akui babaoo eba. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tso loo tso ni akɛfee ŋmei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ tso ni akɛbaatsu nii koni tso lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds fail to sprout when I plant them directly into the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Vegetable seeds are very delicate; if planted too deep, exposed to hot sun, or left without water, they dry out or get eaten by insects. Starting them in a nursery bed with shade and gentle watering lets them sprout safely before you move them to the main field.
ga: Aduawai dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ, ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, loo ashi ni nu bɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi loo kooloi baaye amɛ. Kɛ́ oje amɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nu ni yɔɔ blɛoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying during the hot afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Tomatoes often wilt in wet soil because of bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks the inside of the plant stem so water cannot travel to the leaves. Changing the location of your tomatoes and rotating them with crops like maize helps clear the soil of this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ahewɔ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ aya baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ otsake he ni tomatoi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that feed on the sap and pass viruses to the plant. Spraying with neem leaf extract or safe insecticides controls the insects so new leaves can grow straight.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi lɛ koni baa heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water sits around them for too long or when root-rot fungi in the soil attack them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shishifãi ni egboi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ egbi ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off the stem without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of water, or attacks by insects like mirids. Keeping temporary shade trees like plantains around young cocoa keeps the farm cool and protects the flowers so they can form pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni ha amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ha yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my rice plants growing very tall like grass without making many heads of grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ tsɔ ni amɛwooo dumɔwui babaoo lɛ?

english: Rice plants grow tall and bushy without grain when planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving each plant enough space allows sunlight to reach the stems so they produce strong heads full of rice grains.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni dumɔwui bɛ mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha amɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Ni ahaa tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi Enɛ haa ŋmãa toi lɛ mli wa ni ŋmãa ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunches get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ dara lɛ?

english: Plantain trees do not have deep roots like timber trees; their roots stay close to the topsoil. As the heavy bunch grows, the top weight pulls the stem down unless you prop up the trunk using a strong wooden Y-fork pole.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ tsei. Eshishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ kuu lɛ da lɛ, Maximum weight lɛ baagbala tso lɛ shishi. Ja okɛ Y-shaped fork posts ni akɛ tso ni wa fee lɛ fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my plantain crops turning yellow and dry during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods like the Harmattan, plantain leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink from the soil. Placing a layer of dry leaves or grass around the base of the plant traps moisture in the ground and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ Harmattan lɛ, plantain baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai loo jwɛi ni egboi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When plantains are planted too close, their large leaves block sunlight from each other, and their roots fight for nutrients and water in the soil. Spacing them at least 2 to 3 meters apart gives each plant enough room to produce big bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ hoo lɛ, mitai 2 kɛyashi 3 ni ka tsei ateŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee panicles agboi.

english: Why does my soil become hard and stop producing good crop yields after planting every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais ni ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai akwɛmɔ beni midu nii daa afi lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops continuously removes vital food from the earth without giving it time to replenish. Alternating crops or growing legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil so it stays rich.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ je lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli loo aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain crop taking so long to produce flowers compared to my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ akɛto mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Plantains require rich soil packed with nutrients like potassium and nitrogen to start flowering. Poor soil or weeds competing for soil food will delay the plant from flowering on time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia plantains koni ebɔi fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo jwɛi ni kɛ niyenii miitswa akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná fɔfɔi yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater sits in flat, poorly drained soil for too long. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ ta shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are the tender leaves of my young maize plants full of small chewed holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ashɛreɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center funnel of young maize plants during the day and feeds on the tender leaf tissue.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni kɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baa bibii amli fãji.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and moisture, shielding the young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and lift my yam vines onto tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni makwɛ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that grows large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves into the sun and off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji amli. Staking baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la he ni ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much leaf-building fertilizer in the soil causing the plant to prioritize leaves over fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa baai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ fe aduawai lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants need so much water right when the cobs start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛfee pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: When maize starts forming cobs, it relies heavily on water to transport nutrients into the kernels so they fill up properly. Without enough water at this stage, the grains will remain small, dry, and undeveloped.
ga: Beni ŋmãa lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmeii Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu nɔ waa koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ mli koni ekɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii, ni amɛgbi ni amɛdarako.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn turning yellow before the harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your corn is lacking nitrogen, a key nutrient for plant growth. The crop moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young, growing top leaves, showing that the soil needs extra plant food or fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsei aniyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi.

english: Why should I dry my harvested corn grains thoroughly before processing or grinding them into flour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ dani mikɛtsu nii loo mafolɔ mli ni mikɛfee ashikishaŋ lɛ?

english: Drying maize properly removes excess water that attracts mold and insects. Wet grain produces sticky, poor-quality flour that spoils quickly, while well-dried corn grinds cleanly and makes better food.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ nu ni fa fe nine ni gbalaa ŋmãa kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ kɛyaa. Nibii ni efɔ lɛ feɔ ashikiŋsha ni wa, ni ehiii kwraa ni fiteɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehooɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms eat the soft inside leaves of my young maize plants first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Armyworms target the tender inner funnel of young maize because those fresh leaves are softest and contain the highest amount of water and nutrients, which allows the caterpillars to feed and grow quickly.
ga: Cutworms lɛ kwɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli gbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ baai heei nɛɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ fe fɛɛ, ni nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood the soil for too long, water fills all the air gaps, suffocating the roots and causing harmful fungi to rot them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my crop fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mitsei lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away fertilizer from the topsoil before your crop's roots have time to drink it in. This wastes your money and leaves the plants without the food they need.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Nakai feemɔ baaha ofite shika, ni ebaaha tso lɛ anine ashɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom tips of my tomatoes turn black and soft while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This soft black tip, called blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants don't get a steady supply of water. Irregular watering stops the plant from taking up calcium, causing the bottom of the fruit to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmei diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi calcium ni tso lɛ yɔɔ lɛ naa. ha aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ mli agbala

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield small harvests when I plant seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and resources to build strong stems and produce large crops.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains alongside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my farm reduce my crop yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal essential water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your plants. Keeping the field clear ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa creates shelter and traps soil moisture, keeping the cocoa seedlings safe until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer for my cocoa trees to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your cocoa leaves start turning yellow, or if the trees grow slowly and produce small, weak pods, it usually means the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
ga: Kɛji o-cocoa baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Aloo kɛji tso lɛ miida blɛoo ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ bibii. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off some of the leaves and branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo mi cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ eniji komɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or extra branches so air and sunlight can flow freely through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to send its food energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli oya. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ niyenii hewalɛ amaje koni amɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji.

english: Why do weeds growing around my crops reduce the total harvest I collect?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ha ŋmaa fɛɛ ni mibua naa lɛ ba shi.

english: Weeds compete with your main crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping the ground clean ensures that all fertilizer and water go directly to feeding your crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ehe atse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ yaa onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing far fewer pods than they used to years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmeii babaoo fioo fe afii ni eho lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older than 20 to 30 years, their natural production slows down. You can refresh them by pruning old main branches or by planting new, high-yielding cocoa varieties.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ eye fe afii 20 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi. Obaanyɛ oha amɛhe afee ehee kɛtsɔ niji wuji momoi ni ooofolɔ loo kookoo henɔi heei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally make more flowers than they can support, and only flowers visited by tiny pollinating insects become pods. Ensuring good shade, moist soil, and avoiding harsh chemical sprays helps insects pollinate more flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Ni fɔfɔi pɛ yɔɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Ebatsɔ pod pɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ehiɛ edɔ, ni okpa tsofai ni mli wa lɛ, ebaaye ebua kooloi babaoo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is there a way I can help my cocoa trees produce more pods without just waiting for insects?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maye mabua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo ni mimɛɛɛ ŋmeii?

english: Yes, you can practice hand pollination by gently transferring pollen from one flower to another using small brushes or flower parts, which guarantees more flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ nine mli pollination akase nii kɛtsɔ ekɛ ni oooye blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Okɛ brɔsh bibioo loo fɔfɔi fã ko ajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ baatsɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: Excess water and high humidity cause a fungal disease called Black Pod. Clearing weeds and removing black pods from the farm quickly stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pods baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: How do I tell the exact time a cocoa pod is ready to be picked from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: A cocoa pod is ripe when its skin color changes completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting too early results in flat, bitter beans, while harvesting too late causes seeds to sprout inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji hewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli kwɔ mli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ plantain baai aha kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii fioo komɛi beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering the beans traps heat and starts a fermentation process. This process kills the seed inside so it won't sprout and creates the rich chocolate flavor that buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ, emɔɔ dɔlɛ lɛ ni ebɔi ŋmeii lɛ ahe nitsumɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ekwɛɛɛ ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Can I plant coconut trees and cocoa trees together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛ kakao tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, you can grow them together because tall coconut palms provide helpful overhead shade while cocoa grows underneath, but you must space them far enough apart so their roots do not fight for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome ejaakɛ ŋmeii tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋmɔlɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ be mli ni kokoo lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni oshi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa farm is growing well or falling behind?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo ŋmɔ bibioo lɛ miiya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ loo eefo sɛɛ?

english: A healthy young cocoa farm will show steady stem growth, regular production of fresh green or reddish leaves, and few yellowing leaves during the rainy season.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ tso yibii ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ loo tsuru ni tamɔ amɛhe. Ni baai fioo komɛi yɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted coconut tree to start producing fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yibii?

english: Depending on the variety, dwarf coconut palms can start producing fruits in 3 to 4 years, whereas traditional tall coconut varieties usually take between 6 to 10 years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ bɔ ni amɛji srɔtoi lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɔɔ hiɔ shi yɛ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 teŋ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to know what was previously planted on my land before I put down new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni male nɔ ni tsutsu lɛ adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu kookoo tsei heei lɛ?

english: Previous crops can leave behind hidden soil pests, diseases, or depleted nutrients, so knowing the land's history helps you treat the soil properly before planting fresh seedlings.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu tsutsu lɛ eshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, helai, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni efite. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ he yinɔsane ni ooole lɛ baaye abua bo ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani odu dumɔwui heei.

english: Does young cocoa need full sunlight or do the seedlings prefer shade to grow properly?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei bibii loo dumɔwui lɛ he miihia hulutsoo koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need partial shade to shield their delicate leaves from burning under intense heat, but as they mature into adult trees, they require moderate sunlight to produce high pod yields.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo koni amɛbaa bibii lɛ akashã yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shishi. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa lɛ, hulu la ni fa fioo he miihia amɛ koni amɛná pod yibii babaoo.

english: What does it mean when the leaves on my young cocoa plants start turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the young plant is stressed from a lack of nitrogen in the soil, poor drainage holding too much water around the roots, or too much exposure to direct sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso bibioo lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa nu babaoo hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli tsɔ

english: Why do coconut trees need so much distance between them when I am planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ, ehe hiaa ni amɛteŋ gbɛ babaoo ahi shi lɛ?

english: Coconut trees grow large fronds and extensive root systems that need plenty of open space to capture full sunlight and gather enough water without crowding neighbor plants.
ga: Kokoo tsei yɛ baai wuji kɛ shishifãi babaoo ni biɔ he ko ni agbele babaoo koni amɛná hulu la ni fa ni amɛbua nu ni fa bɔ ni sa naa ni amɛtsiii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anaa.

english: Why are my old family cocoa trees producing fewer cocoa pods than they used to?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei momo lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age past 20 to 25 years, their natural yield naturally declines and they become more susceptible to diseases, meaning old farms need pruning, soil feeding, or gradual replanting.
ga: Beni kookoo tsei lɛ yeɔ afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ baa shi ni helai baanyɛ aba amɛnɔ oya, ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni afo ŋmɔji momoi lɛ amli, aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii loo adu amɛ ekoŋŋ fiofio.

english: How does a long dry season affect my young cocoa trees?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extended dry weather stresses young cocoa plants, causing leaf drop and wilting, which can be prevented by keeping shade trees and applying mulch around the base to keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ haoɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ. Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use the exact same fertilizer for my coconut palms that I use for my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ cacao tsei amli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha ŋmei tsei?

english: While both benefit from soil nutrients, coconut palms require higher levels of potassium and salt minerals compared to cocoa trees, so tailored fertilizer blends give much better results.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛ fɛɛ amɛnáa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he sɛɛ moŋ, Shi ŋmei tsei biɔ potassium kɛ minerals babaoo fe cacao tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa yibii kpakpai babaoo baa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with big leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits in the soil for too long, it pushes air out and washes away nitrogen. Without air and nitrogen, the maize plant cannot make green food for itself and starts turning yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ Abele tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛfee niyenii ni ji ŋmɔŋ amɛha amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the plant suffers from lack of water. Stress from heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant drops the flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when the rainy season is too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Soil that stays soaked for too long suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to grow and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni awo mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgboi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves, or transmitting a virus that distorts normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ eshwaa.

english: Why does my land yield less maize if I plant it in the same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛji midu yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot drains those nutrients completely, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ afite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather when drops of rain sit on the surface of the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ ŋmeii diji lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell when my yams are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams signal maturity when the leaves and vines turn yellow and naturally dry up. This shows that the plant has finished transferring energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ amɛdalɛ kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cowpea farm produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpea plants to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of spending energy to produce flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ he wami kɛ peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop right after the first rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems already adapted to the local soil. They wake up instantly and absorb water and nutrients faster than young crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii.

english: Why do extension officers tell us not to burn bush cleared from our land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ akashã jwɛi ni ajie dani adu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich topsoil organic matter, kills beneficial soil organisms like earthworms, and leaves the ground dry and weak for future planting seasons.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ mli lɛ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops only when the soil is moist or after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so roots can absorb it safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn and damage plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Why do plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ amɛbɔi yibii babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems, so strong winds or heavy fruit weight can push them down unless you prop them up with sturdy wooden poles.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo tso yibii lɛ tsiimɔ baanyɛ atsi amɛ kɛba shi. Ja okɛ tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds early from my field before my crops grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baadara?

english: Weeds grow rapidly and steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from young crops, which stunts their growth if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa kɛji ajieee lɛ mra.

english: Why do my cocoa trees get black pod disease more often when the farm has too much shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni black pod hela lɛ yeɔ cocoa tsei shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess shade traps high humidity and reduces airflow, creating the damp environment that fungal spores need to infect cocoa pods.
ga: Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo ni ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni fungal spores he hiaa koni ekɛ hela awo kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: What causes the leaves of my tomato plants to curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot, dry weather is often caused by tiny whiteflies transmitting viral diseases, combined with heat stress and irregular watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. ni ji mɛi ni kɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ Okɛ nakai nɔ lɛ afata dɔlɛ he haomɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ he.

english: Why does hybrid maize seed bought from the agricultural store yield more than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high vigor and disease resistance in their first generation, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose those traits and yield much less.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nibii krokomɛi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai sui lɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: How do I know when my cassava crop is fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting when lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the ground around the main stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso wulu lɛ miije shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why is correct spacing important when planting yam tubers in mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ he hiaa beni aduɔ sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ?

english: Proper spacing prevents yam roots from competing with each other for water and soil nutrients, allowing every plant to produce large tubers.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi sweet potato shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my coconut trees suddenly turning yellow and dying from the top down when they used to be healthy for years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmei tso lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo kɛjɛ ŋwɛi kɛmiiya shishi be mli ni eyɛ hewalɛ afii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Coconut Lethal Yellowing Disease, a serious infection spread by tiny sap-sucking insects. It causes nuts to drop prematurely, leaves to turn yellow, and eventually kills the tree.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni naa wa ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Ni naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gbo.

english: What causes the leaves of healthy tree crops to drop off completely within just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni haa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kwraa yɛ otsii fioo ko pɛ mli?

english: Sudden leaf loss is usually a plant's response to severe fungal infections, root decay, or extreme water stress, where the tree sheds leaves to try to conserve moisture and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baa ni laajeɔ trukaa lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni naa wa ko he. shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: If one tree on my farm gets sick and dies, will the sickness spread to the other trees nearby?
ga: Kɛji hela mɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko ni egbo Ani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa tsei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, many plant diseases spread to neighboring trees through insects, wind, contaminated rain splashing, or shared farm tools. Removing infected plants quickly helps protect healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ nugbɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ nɔ. loo amɛja okwaayeli he nibii Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why are my old crop trees producing much less fruit now compared to when I planted them decades ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei momo lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As trees age, their root systems become less efficient, and the soil naturally loses vital nutrients over time unless organic manure or appropriate fertilizers are regularly added.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ da Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli daa.

english: Can I plant new coconut seedlings in the exact same spot where my old dead trees were removed?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei tso hee yɛ he ni ajie mi ŋmei tso momo lɛ yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is risky because disease organisms or root pests from the dead tree can remain in the soil and attack the young seedling. It is better to clear the area, treat the soil, or shift the new planting site slightly.
ga: Oshara yɛ ejaakɛ helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo shishifãi ni jɛ tsei ni egboi amli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutua tsei bibii. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi he lɛ, oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ, loo otsi he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ fioo.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning light green or yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen or is sitting in waterlogged soil, both of which prevent the crop from making food properly through its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ebaa lɛ nɔ efee niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crops dry up and die even when I plant them at the same time of year I always do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns have become unpredictable due to changing weather conditions. Planting on fixed traditional dates might no longer align with actual rains, causing young roots to dry out in hot soil.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Kusum date palm ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ diɛŋtsɛ kpaaa gbee dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I protect my young tree crops from dying during the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of young trees with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the root zone cool and stops moisture from evaporating quickly during hot weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the trunks of my mature trees rotting near the ground and causing them to fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso agbo lɛ shishifã lɛ miifite yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eegbee shi lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by stem rot fungi that thrive when wet soil stays piled up against the trunk base for long periods, weakening the wood until the tree collapses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, stem rot fungus ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ ta tso lɛ shishi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Is it safe to grow food crops under my large coconut trees, or will they steal water from each other?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu niyenii yɛ mi-kokoo tso agbo lɛ shishi? Aloo amɛbaaju nu kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Intercropping is safe if you plant shade-tolerant crops like cocoyam or cassava and keep them slightly away from the coconut base so both plants can share light and nutrients without competing.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji akɛ odu tsei ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo tamɔ kookoo loo yucca. Ni okɛto he ko ni kɛ ŋmei shishitoo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ jaa la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ.

english: Cassava plants naturally shed their leaves in dry weather to reduce water loss and stay alive. As long as the stems remain green and healthy, the plant will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi wala mli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni ehe wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Your soil likely has too much nitrogen and lacks phosphorus or potassium. High nitrogen makes plants focus all their energy on green leaves, whereas phosphorus and potassium are needed to grow strong flowers and fruit.
ga: Ekolɛ nitrogen babaoo yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni fɔsfɔs loo potasium bɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium he miihia waa koni fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I see tiny holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ, amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that eats young maize leaves and stalks. Applying recommended treatments early in the morning or late evening targets these caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ anɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What makes my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly into small cups?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Controlling these insects early prevents severe leaf damage and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ ni naa wa kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni mikɛ tsei niji awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking lifts the yam leaves off the hot soil and spreads them out toward the sun. More sunlight on the leaves helps the plant create more energy to grow larger yam tubers underground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Hulu la babaoo ni tsoɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛkwɛ̃ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If too many suckers grow together, they steal water, space, and nutrients from the main stem. Keeping only one main stem and one or two young suckers ensures the plant grows large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo bua amɛhe naa lɛ, amɛbaaju nu, he ko, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri kome pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ adara ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do young cocoa plants turn brown and wither when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and can easily scorch. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa protects them from direct heat until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Soft cocoa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he. Kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering which stops the plant from taking up calcium from the soil. Keeping the soil moisture steady helps prevent the fruits from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be mli baa Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai akafiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so much slower even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that consume water, fertilizer, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni yeɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last harvest rot or get eaten by insects before planting time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite loo ŋmeii ye amɛ dani be shɛ ni esa akɛ adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often spoil if they are not completely dry before storage or if they are exposed to damp air and pests. Storing well-dried seeds in airtight containers or mixing them with protective ash prevents insect infestation and rot.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ fitemɔ kɛji akɛ amɛgbiko kwraa dani akɛto loo kɛji akɛ amɛbote kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo akɛ sũ ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ afutu mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã ni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize curling up and turning yellow during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much moisture when the heat is high or water is low. It is a natural sign that the crop is thirsty and needs water to cool down and feed properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ akafite kɛji latsaa lɛ fa loo nu lɛ faaa. Eji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii ni nu he miihia amɛ koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ ni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If crops lack water, their leaves wilt, droop, and feel dry or crispy. If they get too much water, the leaves turn pale yellow, feel soft or limp, and the roots may rot from a lack of air in the soil.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi, amɛbaagbee shi, ni amɛnu he akɛ amɛgbi loo amɛmiikpã. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Henumɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ Ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the soil stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers to save energy and moisture when they experience water stress. Without enough water, the plant cannot support forming fruits, so it sheds flowers to survive.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji ekɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ aye abua ni aná aduawai. No hewɔ lɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ joɔ foi.

english: If my farm's water supply breaks down for a few days, will my vegetable crops die immediately?
ga: Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fite gbii fioo komɛi Ani mitsei lɛ baagboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Vegetables will not die instantly, but soft leafy crops will start wilting within 2 to 3 days without water. Shading the soil or adding mulch can help keep them alive until water is restored.
ga: Aduawai gbooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Shi tsei bibii lɛ baabɔi shwiemɔ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji nu bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Will my cassava crops survive if we experience a long delay in water supply this season?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tsei lɛ baahi shi kɛji wɔna be kakadaŋŋ ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, cassava is very tough and copes with drought by shedding its leaves to save water. Once water or rain returns, the plant will grow new leaves and continue swelling its roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei wa waa ni ekpeɔ hɔmɔ naa kɛtsɔ ebaa ni eshwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nu loo nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Tso lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ baai heei kɛ shishifãi ni efuu.

english: Can my wilted pepper plants recover once I fix my water supply and start watering them again?
ga: Ani mi-pepper tso ni egbo lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji misaa nu jɛɛhe lɛ ni mibɔi nu hamɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: If the pepper leaves are only drooping, they will bounce back within hours after watering. However, if the stems have completely dried out and turned hard, those parts cannot recover.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper baai lɛ gboi lɛ Baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbi kwraa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Anyɛɛɛ aku sɛɛ afee Nakai fãi lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to give water to my crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu?

english: Early morning is the best time to water crops because the sun is gentle, allowing water to soak deep into the soil for the roots to drink before the heat of the day evaporates it.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu. Ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ mli tseɔ blɛoo Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anu dani gbi lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crop roots stay near the surface instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Roots stay shallow when they receive frequent, light watering because water only wets the top layer of soil. Watering deeply but less frequently encourages roots to grow down deep in search of stored moisture.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ aha amɛ nu fioo shii abɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nu ni oooha lɛ mli kwɔ shi efɔɔɔ baa lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛtao nu ni ato.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow after water flooded my farm for two days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu ewo miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Flooding fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the crop roots. When roots cannot breathe air, they fail to take up plant foods, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu afua mli nu lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. suffocate plant roots Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ Enyɛŋ eŋɔ tso niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: How does putting dry leaves or grass around the base of my crops help them handle dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ naa?

english: Covering the soil around crops with dry leaves or grass acts like a protective blanket. It shields the soil from the burning sun, keeping moisture in the ground for a much longer time.
ga: Mulching around Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers plant plantain on the same land where they are planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ duɔ plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight, helping them survive and grow well in their early stages.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Will planting plantains next to my cocoa seedlings take away all the nutrients and water from the cocoa?
ga: dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ani mi-kokoo tso lɛ baajie niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When spaced correctly, plantains do not harm young cocoa; instead, they shade the soil, keeping it cool and moist, which actually helps the cocoa roots thrive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Plantains lɛ yeee kookoo bibii lɛ awui. Mohu ɔ, e haa zugba ɔ hɛ mi jɔɔ konɛ kɔɔhiɔ ɔ mi nɛ jɔ nɛ e mi mi nɛ jɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant cocoa alone on a clear field or mix it with temporary shade crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too madu kookoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli loo mikɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ afutu mli?

english: Mixing cocoa seedlings with temporary shade crops like plantains is much better because young cocoa naturally grows under forest shade and will suffer if left exposed in an open field.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kookoo bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kooi lɛ ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ekɛ naagbai baakpe kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ faŋŋ

english: What is the best month for me to start planting my crop seedlings in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ nyɔŋ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi akɛ mabɔi tsei dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ Ghana?

english: Starting around March is ideal because it aligns with the arrival of the main rainy season, giving young plants plenty of water to build strong roots.
ga: Abuɔ akɛ ehi akɛ abaaje shishi yɛ March afi lɛ mli ejaakɛ ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa lɛ kpãa gbee. Ha tsei bibii lɛ nu babaoo koni amɛshishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why do extension officers encourage farmers to prepare their land before March?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛsaa amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani March aba lɛ?

english: Preparing land ahead of time ensures you are ready to plant immediately when the first rains arrive in March, giving seedlings the longest possible growing season.
ga: Kɛ́ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ obaafee klalo akɛ obaadu nii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba yɛ March mli pɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daalɛ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: What happens to my young cocoa seedlings if I plant them near the end of the rainy season instead of the start?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee moŋ fe mra?

english: Seedlings planted late in the season won't develop deep roots in time, making them far more likely to dry out and die during the dry Harmattan season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ nyɛŋ atswa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Why is it necessary for me to follow a seasonal timetable for my farming activities?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ be mli gbɛjianɔtoo ko nɔ kɛha mi okwaayeli nitsumɔi lɛ?

english: Farming depends heavily on weather patterns, so following a seasonal schedule helps you plant, weed, and harvest at the exact times when natural rainfall will support your crops best.
ga: Okwaayeli damɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ nɔ waa. No hewɔ lɛ be he gbɛjianɔtoo ni ooonyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua bo ni odu nii, okɛ jwɛi atsu nii ni okpa yɛ bei pɔtɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ baaye abua onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli.

english: Can I plant my young cocoa seedlings directly under full sunlight?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to heat and will easily burn or dry out under full sun, requiring temporary shade trees or plantains during their first few years.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he waa, ni ebaashã loo ebaagbi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi oya. Enɛ biɔ tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: How far apart should I space plantains when planting them to protect my cocoa seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ gbɛ kroko beni miduɔ nii koni mikɛbu mi-kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Proper spacing ensures plantains provide adequate shade for the seedlings without completely blocking sunlight or overcrowding the cocoa plants.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni sa ni etsĩii hulu lɛ naa loo ehiɛɛɛ kookoo tsei lɛ amli babaoo.

english: How does planting plantains alongside cocoa help my family before the cocoa trees start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo tsei ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miweku lɛ dani kookoo tsei lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Plantains yield fruit much faster than cocoa, providing your family with food and a quick source of income to sell in the market while you wait a few years for the cocoa to mature.
ga: Plantains woɔ yibii oya fe kookoo. Enɛ haa oweku lɛ náa niyenii kɛ shika oya ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ afii fioo komɛi dani kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and produce food, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help nourish your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ niyenii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same spot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally restores nitrogen to your soil.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When is the best time during the day for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer during the high heat of midday can scorch the roots and leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi kɛ baai ashã.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying organic solutions like neem oil or soapy water under the leaves helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of forming into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants experience stress from high heat, erratic watering, or a shortage of key nutrients like calcium and phosphorus needed for fruiting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa kɛha yibiiwoo lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under full sunlight. Intercropping them with plantains or shade trees creates a cool shelter that retains soil moisture while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ du tso lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ darako lolo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and stake my yam vines with wood?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mikɛ tso adu sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need tall stakes to lift their leaves into the sunlight. Maximum sunlight helps leaves generate food that travels down into the ground to build bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ tso kakadaŋŋ koni amɛwo amɛtso lɛ nɔ kɛje kpo kɛya hulu lɛ mli. Hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in standing water because waterlogged soil prevents roots from breathing. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain off naturally.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain suckers turning brown and drooping early in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose water rapidly through their broad leaves during dry spells. Spreading dry grass or leaves as mulch around the base of the plant holds moisture in the ground longer.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni akɛ muji awo mli lɛ abɔle he. Tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from last year fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their ability to sprout if stored in damp or warm conditions where moisture and insects ruin the seed germ. Storing fully dried seeds in sealed containers mixed with wood ash keeps them alive longer.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛto he ko ni mli efɔ loo hulutsoo. ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli hela lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi kwraa lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I get my cocoa trees to produce more pods every year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tso lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo daa afi?

english: To increase pod production, your cocoa trees need regular pruning to allow sunlight through, proper soil nutrients from fertilizer, and timely protection against pests and fungal diseases.
ga: Bɔni afee ni pod feemɔ aya hiɛ Ehe miihia ni afo O-cocoa tso lɛ mli daa koni hulu la atsɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ be naa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack enough water or soil nutrients, or when they face heat stress. Proper shade and feeding help the tree retain its flowers so they turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ kpe Shade ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. no hewɔ lɛ ebatsɔ pod ni mli wa

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, overly wet conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming extra tree branches helps air and sunlight dry out the farm to stop the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kpaɔ fitemɔ.

english: Yellow, curled leaves usually mean the tree is missing vital nutrients from the soil, is suffering from water stress during dry months, or is being attacked by sap-sucking insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu he haomɔ he piŋmɔ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuaa amɛ

english: Why is it important for me to prune extra branches off my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches, allowing light and air into the canopy. This prevents fungal diseases and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing big, healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agboi ni amɛhe wa.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs fertilizer to help my crops grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: If your trees show slow growth, produce pale leaves, or yield fewer pods each season even with good rainfall, your soil is running low on essential nutrients that fertilizer can replace.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ daa blɛoo, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii najiaŋ lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle strong sun exposure. They need temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛná he ko ni amɛhi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava together on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that competes aggressively for water and soil nutrients, which can stunt young cocoa. It is better to use plantain or shade trees instead.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii babaoo ni kɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo lɛ agbɔjɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ atsu nii moŋ.

english: Why are small bugs eating the fresh shoots of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye mi-kookoo ŋmɔji heei lɛ?

english: Insects like capsids target soft new growth to suck out sap, which causes the shoots to dry up and die back. Catching them early with appropriate crop protection keeps the tree healthy.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ capsids lɛ kwɛɔ gbekɛbii heei ni dara lɛ anɔ koni amɛnu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsei ahebuu ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does heavy rain during the flowering period affect my crop yield?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess rain can wash away flowers and create damp conditions where fungal diseases spread quickly, reducing the overall number of pods that develop successfully.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔii lɛ ahe ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ aba ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ omanye lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ ba shi.

english: Should I burn the bushes after clearing my land, or is it better to leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo ehi akɛ mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving cleared bushes and weeds to rot naturally into the soil is better than burning them. Burning destroys natural nutrients and earthworms, while letting cleared plant material decay adds valuable organic matter and keeps the soil moist for your crops.
ga: Ehi akɛ oooha tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni he tse lɛ afite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe fe ni oooshã amɛ. Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii. Yɛ be mli ni ohaa tsei lɛ fiteɔ lɛ, ekɛ nibii ni jara wa fataa he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land has good soil for growing tree crops like coconuts or oil palms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo mu tsei?

english: Good soil for tree crops is deep, dark, crumbly, and drains water well without staying flooded for days. If water sits on top of your land for too long or if the ground is very hard and sandy, you may need to improve it with manure or compost before planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ duŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu lɛ eyaaa gbii babaoo. Kɛji nu hi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ. Ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsake shikpɔŋ lɛ dani okɛdu.

english: Can I plant maize and cassava in between my young coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii ateŋ?

english: Yes, planting short-term food crops like maize, cassava, or legumes between young tree rows is a smart practice called intercropping. It allows you to produce food and earn income from the land while waiting for your coconut trees to grow big.
ga: Hɛɛ, be kukuoo mli niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ. Nifeemɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋaa ni atsɛɔ lɛ intercropping yɛ tsei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ. Ehaa onáa niyenii ni onáa shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ni o-coconut tso lɛ adara lɛ.

english: Is it good to plant oil palm trees and coconut trees together on the same farmland?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu mu tsei kɛ ŋmei tsei yɛ he kome yɛ okwaayeli he kome?

english: It is generally not recommended to mix oil palm and coconut trees on the same farm. Both are large tree crops that need a lot of sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, so planting them together causes them to compete and leads to lower fruit yields for both.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔɔ akɛ akɛ mu kɛ ŋmei tsei afutu ŋmɔ kome mli. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ji tsei wuji ni biɔ hulu la babaoo, nu, kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔ akaŋ ni ebaaha yibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: What short-term crops can I grow to make money quickly while waiting for my tree crops to mature?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo manyɛ makwɛ koni maná shika oya yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Vegetables like pepper, garden eggs, and tomatoes, as well as grain crops like maize and beans, mature within 3 to 6 months. Planting these between wide tree spaces gives you regular cash flow while your main tree crops are still growing.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmeii, abɔɔ mli ŋmeii, kɛ tomato, kɛ agbɛnɛ ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii, shwereɔ yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 mli. Tsei nɛɛ ni ooodu yɛ tsei wuji ateŋ lɛ haa onáa shika babaoo yɛ be mli ni otsei titrii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do I need to measure space between my coconut trees instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu bɔ ni ŋmeii tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha lɛ he moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. If coconut trees are planted too close together, their leaves shade each other, making them grow tall and slender with very few, small fruits.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baai lɛ baaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce energy and grow strong. When shaded by big trees, crops stretch upward to reach the light, making their stems thin and fragile, which leads to poor leaf and fruit production.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara waa. Beni yɔɔ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakpã mli koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baa kɛ aduawai ni ehiii.

english: How many years will it take for a coconut tree to start producing fruits after I plant it?
ga: Beni adu sɛɛ Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: It depends on the variety. Traditional tall coconut trees usually take 6 to 10 years to start fruiting, whereas improved dwarf or hybrid varieties can begin producing fruits much faster, usually within 3 to 5 years.
ga: Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, blema ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 10 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi mra kwraa, bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my coconut trees turn yellow during the dry season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Coconut leaves turn yellow during severe dry spells because the tree is short on water and is trying to protect itself. Placing dried grass or coconut husks around the base of the tree helps keep moisture in the soil during the dry months.
ga: Kokoshi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ nu, ni eebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ebu ehe. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei ŋmɔtɔ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Is it safer for me to plant only one type of crop on my farmland or mix different crops?
