ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni akɛfutu mli?

english: Planting a mix of different crops is safer because it protects your income. If a pest, disease, or bad weather damages one crop, or if its market price drops, you will still have other crops to harvest and sell.
ga: Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nibii amli lɛ adumɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ ebuɔ oshika he kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni ehiii fite nibii kome. aloo kɛji jara nɔ jara ba shi Obaaná ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lolo ni obaakpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. It can also happen if the farm is waterlogged, which prevents the roots from breathing and taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in the same field as my maize help the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally feed the soil and make it richer for your crop without buying expensive synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei pɔtɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha efee nii babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmãa ni jara wa ni akɛfee ŋmãa.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into rich soil manure as it breaks down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii kɛji efite.

english: Why are small worms eating holes inside the tops of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the soft growing center of young maize plants. Catching them early with recommended treatments or bio-pesticides prevents them from destroying the center shoot and killing the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ anɔ. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofafeemɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ni amɛkagbe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains cause water to pool in the soil with nowhere to drain. Fungi thrive in this soaked soil and attack the mature roots before you pull them up.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Fuji lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni etutuaa shishifãi ni eda lɛ dani obaanyɛ ogbala amɛ kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant's sap and transmitting plant viruses. Removing affected leaves and spraying organic pest remedies can protect the healthy stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ajie baai ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry out and die when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts like a sun umbrella, giving them the cool shade and soil moisture they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ shade tso. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do all the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from extreme heat or sudden water shortage. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy and water so it can survive the dry spell.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I bury my maize seeds very deep in the dirt when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu?

english: If a maize seed is planted too deep, it wastes all its stored energy trying to push through the heavy soil and dies before reaching the light. Planting about a thumb's depth allows it to sprout fast and strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli tsɔ Ebaafite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ ni egbo dani eshɛ la lɛ he. Dumɔ ni duɔ tamɔ tsitsi wulu lɛ haa ekwɛ̃ɔ oya, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better to water my garden early in the morning instead of in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo mibɔɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ, ani ehi fe no?

english: Watering in the cool morning allows the soil to absorb moisture and feed the roots before the heat arrives. Afternoon sun causes the water to evaporate into the air instantly, leaving your plants thirsty.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ niyenii dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa. Gbi gbɛkɛ hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ha otsei lɛ aye kumai

english: When maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older, lower leaves up to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛfeɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpeas grow strong and green even when I do not apply chemical fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miida waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛdaraaa moŋ lɛ? Ni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ efataaa he?

english: Cowpeas and other beans are special crops that work with friendly bacteria in the soil to trap nitrogen directly from the air and feed themselves, enriching the soil naturally.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Eji tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni kɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛye ehe niyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why are the leaves on my young pepper plants shrinking and twisting up like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifite tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on the sap and carrying leaf-curl viruses. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ chili baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ curling hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do my young maize plants have ragged holes in the center leaves with small dark droppings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the growing point (the whorl) of the plant. They feed on the tender young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei lɛ amli hei ni amɛdaraa (rings) lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle direct, hot sunlight. They need shade trees to keep the air humid and shield them from sun scorch until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ he miihia amɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ahi shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi amɛbaadara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot in the ground if heavy rains last too long before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain floods the soil for days, oxygen gets trapped out, allowing soft-rot fungi to quickly attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hoɔ nu gbii babaoo. Oxygen lɛ efo mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny beneficial midges (insects) to pollinate them, along with steady moisture. High heat, dry winds, or a lack of pollinators cause the unpollinated flowers to dry up and fall.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii biɔ kooloi bibii fioo komɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ koni amɛfee fɔfɔi, kɛfata he lɛ, hulutsoo be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni awoko amɛmli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn soft and black before they finish ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells during fruit growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains right when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni aduawai akui lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Plantain plants do not have deep taproots, and microscopic worms (nematodes) or weevils often weaken their shallow roots under the soil, making the heavy tree collapse under wind or fruit weight.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii bibii haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni no haa tsei ni tsii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ loo aduawai lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ shishi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and go through a natural rest period after harvest. Once that rest period ends, warmer barn temperatures signal to the yam that it is time to grow a new plant using its stored energy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛtsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, ŋmɔ mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ atsu nii kɛdu tsei heei.

english: What do extension officers mean when they talk about the moisture content of my maize?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni extension officials lɛ tsɔɔ kɛ amɛmiiwie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-corn lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Moisture content refers to the amount of water trapped inside a crop grain compared to the solid part of the grain. High moisture means the grain is still wet from the field, while lower moisture means the grain has dried out enough to stay fresh without rotting.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ falɛ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmaa lɛ fã ni wa lɛ he. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli edɔ lolo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmaa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa koni ehi shi ehee ni efiteee.

english: What is the exact moisture percentage I should aim for before storing my harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔtɔ oha mlijaa pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ makwɛ dani mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ ato?

english: You should aim for a moisture level of 14 percent. At 14 percent moisture, the grain is dry enough to prevent mold and insect damage while remaining safe and healthy for consumption or sale.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ̃ hulutsoo be ni ji oha mlijaa 14 nɔ. Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ oha mlijaa 14 lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ baagbi bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyeli loo jarayeli.

english: Why does an extension officer use a small electronic machine on my maize grains after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ tsɔnei bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The machine is a moisture meter, which measures the exact amount of water left inside your grains. It gives an accurate reading so you know whether your crop has safely reached the 14 percent target before you put it into long-term storage.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ji hulutsoo mita. Enɛ susuɔ nu ni eshwɛ yɛ odumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ he. Ehaa nikanemɔi ni ja bɔni afee ni ole kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ oha mlijaa 14 ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he shweshweeshwe dani okɛwo he ko ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I test if my maize is dry enough for storage if I do not have a testing machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto? Kɛji mɔ ko bɛ ni kaa lɛ

english: You can perform a simple bite test or salt test. When you bite a properly dried grain, it should crack sharply without leaving a soft dent, indicating that the internal water level has dropped sufficiently for safe keeping.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmei kaa loo ŋmei kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋmɔ Esa akɛ efo oya ni eshiŋ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ko, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eba shi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Should I shell my maize cobs immediately after harvest or dry them on the cob first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli tsɔi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akpa ŋmãa lɛ loo esa akɛ magbi ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: It is best to dry maize on the cob first. Shelling maize while the grains are still wet and soft can tear or crack the grains, making them vulnerable to mold and insect invasion.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooogbi ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbala loo ekumɔ ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ haa okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii baatutua bo.

english: Can I leave my maize drying in the sun for too long, or is extra dry always better?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashi ŋmãa yɛ hulu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ? Aloo ehi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be akɛ oooshi lɛ ni egbi fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Over-drying can damage your crop. If maize becomes too dry, the grains become brittle and break easily during handling, which reduces your total harvest weight and market value. Aim to dry it to around 14 percent moisture rather than drying it completely bone dry.
ga: Kɛ́ egbi fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi. Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni oha egbi aaafee oha mlijaa 14, moŋ fe ni oooha egbi kwraa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and spoil after keeping it in sacks for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni efite beni akɛto kotokui amli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rots in bags because it was stored while still containing too much water. Moisture traps heat inside the bag and creates a wet environment where fungi and bacteria thrive, causing the grains to spoil rapidly.
ga: Abele lɛ fite yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ejaakɛ akɛto be mli ni nu babaoo yɛ lolo lɛ. Fɛ̃i mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helatsɛmɛi daa yɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: What will happen to my crop if I harvest wet maize during the rainy season and bag it immediately?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmãa ni efɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli ni mikɛwo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Bagging wet maize causes the grains to generate heat, sprout inside the sack, and grow dark toxic molds like aflatoxin. This spoils the grain, making it dangerous to eat and impossible to sell.
ga: Abele ni efɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ haa ŋmaa lɛ mli dɔɔ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kotoku mli Kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbeyei tamɔ aflatoxin feɔ. Enɛ baafite ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ. Eyɛ oshara akɛ ayeɔ, ni anyɛɛɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do weevils attack some of my stored maize sacks while leaving other sacks untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutua mi-abele kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ kotokui krokomɛi ni amɛtaaa he lɛ?

english: Weevils prefer damp grains because soft, moist maize is easier for them to eat and lay eggs in. Grains dried down to the recommended 14 percent moisture level are too hard and dry for weevils to multiply easily.
ga: Weevils sumɔɔ ŋmaa ni mli efɔ ejaakɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeli waaa ni ewoɔ wɔji. Nibii ni agbiɔ kɛyashɛɔ he ni hulutsoo be ni ajieɔ yi akɛ eshɛɔ oha mlijaa 14 lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni egbi tsɔ ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ afɔ́ mlɛo.

english: How long can my maize stay good in storage if I dry it to the proper standard before bagging?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji migbi lɛ kɛyashɛ he ni sa dani mikɛwo kotoku mli?

english: When maize is properly dried to 14 percent moisture and kept in clean, well-ventilated storage or sealed bags, it can remain in excellent condition for 6 to 12 months without spoiling.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli oha mlijaa 14 ni akɛto he ko ni he tse ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote mli loo kotoku ni atsĩ naa Abele baahi shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ mli nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 12 ni efiteee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and brown instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves change color when the plant is stressed by too much direct sunlight, lack of water, or a shortage of soil nutrients like nitrogen. Giving young plants shade and organic fertilizer helps them regain their healthy green color.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kɛji hulu la shɛ tso lɛ nɔ tsɔ, nu bɛ mli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei bibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe shade kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes holes and dark spots on my young cocoa leaves, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Insects like mirids (capsids) or beetles feed on tender cocoa leaves and stems, causing spots and holes. Using recommended plant protection sprays or beneficial insects at the right time stops the damage and allows healthy leaves to grow back.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids (capsids) loo ladybugs yeɔ kookoo baai bibii kɛ amɛshishifãi. ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ bu baa Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ tsei ahe loo tsofai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni efite lɛ akpa ni ebaaha baa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the right time to move my young cocoa seedlings from nursery pots into the main farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ ajie kookoo tsei bibii kɛjɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Seedlings should be transplanted at the start of the major rainy season (around May or June in Ghana) when they are about 4 to 6 months old and have developed a strong stem to handle outdoor conditions.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee mli. (aaafee May loo June yɛ Ghana) beni dumɔwui lɛ eye aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6 ni amɛná ŋmeii ni wa ni baaye abua shihilɛi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use soil from any part of my farm to fill nursery bags for planting cocoa seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli koni mikɛdu kookoo ŋmeii?

english: No, nursery soil should be rich topsoil mixed with decomposed organic matter or compost taken from forest areas. Good topsoil holds moisture while draining excess water, helping roots develop without rotting.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie kɛjɛ hei ni tsei yɔɔ lɛ efutu mli. Shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hu hoɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do I need to plant shade trees like plantains or forest trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Shade trees act like umbrellas, shielding cocoa leaves from heat, reducing soil drying, and creating a cool microclimate for healthy growth.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Buu kookoo baai ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ shi ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ bibioo ni mli ejɔ kɛha dalɛ kpakpa.

english: How can I protect my cocoa plants from drying out during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the plant base with dry leaves or palm fronds (mulching) keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture, while permanent shade trees protect leaves from harsh dry winds.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo palm fronds (mulching) shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni haa egbiɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I cut off some of the leaves and extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo cacao tso lɛ baai kɛ niji ni eshwɛ lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can circulate through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to direct energy into growing pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji anaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ amaje tsɛŋemɔ helai ni miida lɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its power and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ewo muji ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crop leaves look pale, growth slows down significantly, or trees produce fewer pods over time, the soil lacks essential nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost to boost its fertility.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Dalɛ baa shi waa Aloo tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers and small pods before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers and young pods when they suffer from water stress during dry spells or lack sufficient nutrients. The tree sheds extra pods to save enough water and energy to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛji nu he haomɔ kpe amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛmli. Tsei kwɛ̃ɔ pods koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: How many years after planting will my new hybrid cocoa trees start producing fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi-hybrid cocoa tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin flowering and producing pods within 2 to 3 years after transplanting, provided they receive proper shade, water, and weed control.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Esa akɛ amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ jwɛi ni sa.

english: Leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and yield bigger cobs.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ko ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛfeɔ amɛhe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains stay too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rainwater sits around the roots without draining away, it starves them of air and allows rot-causing fungi to multiply in the wet soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ nu bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efooo kɛyaaa Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee nɔ ni baaha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in an open field with no big trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get scorched by direct sunlight and dry out quickly in the sun. Planting them under temporary shade like plantains shields them from hot sun until their roots are deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains lɛ, ehaa amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil dries out completely. When the plant experiences extreme heat or thirst, it sheds flowers to save its strength instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Kɛ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo kumai ye amɛ lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in the stems of my maize plants, causing them to break and fall over?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eje kpo yɛ mi-abele tso lɛ shishi. Ha amɛkumɔ ni amɛgbee shi?

english: Small caterpillars called stem borers hatch from eggs laid by moths and tunnel inside the maize stalk to eat. As they hollow out the stem, the plant loses its support and snaps easily in the wind.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ stem borers lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ ebote tso lɛ shishi lɛ, tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ efooo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa lɛ oya.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly through rain droplets in cool, damp weather. Pruning dense branches lets sunlight and air into the canopy, drying out the pods so the fungus cannot thrive.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ mli yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nibii ni afolɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. ni egbi pods lɛ Fungus nyɛŋ ada.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves. Controlling these tiny pests early stops the leaves from twisting and keeps the plant growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does a plantain stem die after producing only one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo aduawai akuu kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once in its lifetime. Once the main stem produces its bunch, it passes its energy down to the young suckers growing at its base to start the next crop.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ tso titri lɛ fee kuu lɛ Ebaatsu hewalɛ kɛya tsei bibii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛje ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ shishi.

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their fertilized flowers underground so the actual groundnut pods can form and ripen safely hidden beneath the dirt away from sunlight and animals.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ feɔ ni amɛshwereɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi ni hulu kɛ kooloi bɛ he.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while sitting in my barn before I can take them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ beni mita ŋmɔ mli dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that naturally wake up and start growing new shoots after a rest period, especially in warm and light conditions. Storing them in a cool, dark, and well-ventilated barn delays this sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni baate shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ ŋmeii heei yɛ hejɔɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔɔɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect damage, such as whiteflies carrying mosaic virus, or a shortage of key soil nutrients. Checking under the leaves helps identify if small pests are sucking out the plant's juices.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii efite, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ ni hiɛ mosaic hela lɛ. loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli Baai lɛ ashishi kwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji kooloi bibii miinu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ miida diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil lacks moisture. Providing steady watering and slight shade during severe heat helps keep the blossoms attached so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants droop during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves droop in strong afternoon heat to reduce water loss through evaporation. If the leaves stand back up by evening, the plant is simply protecting itself, but if they remain limp, the soil needs additional water.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi gbɛkɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miibu ehe. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ Nu kroko hu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and pale instead of growing tall and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stays short and light green when there is not enough nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build strong stems and leafy green growth, so adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer early on helps them thrive.
ga: Abɛi feɔ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛma tsei ahe tsei ni wa ni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right before they are ready to be picked?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ mli gbalaa dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when there is a sudden heavy watering or rainfall after a period of dry weather. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the skin can stretch, so maintaining consistent soil moisture prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato baatswa kɛ nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hulutsoo be ko sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even after growing for a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ yɛ be mli ni midu amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots stay small if the soil is packed too tightly for the tubers to expand, or if the plants are placed too close together. Spacing plants properly gives each root room and nutrients to grow thick.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafee bibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni akɛto he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa eko fɛɛ eko náa shishifãi babaoo kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and naturally feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger. In return, tall maize stalks provide vertical support for trailing bean vines.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ asɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ nɔ.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows air and sunlight to pass through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛ black pod rot baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I water my vegetable garden during the hottest hours of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Watering under hot noon sun causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots. Additionally, water drops left on leaves can focus sunlight and cause leaf burns, so early morning or late afternoon watering is best.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu babaoo shwieɔ shi dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛfata he lɛ, nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná hulu la lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni eha baai lɛ ashã. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni oooha lɛ leebi loo shwane ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and scorching during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full, direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or banana provides cover and retains moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo banana lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ato ni ehiɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with bushy leaves but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into producing stems and leaves instead of expanding its underground roots. Proper spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage bigger tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ tsei kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, gbɛ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them with tiny green worms inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the leaf funnels to feed on tender growth, but identifying them early allows you to use recommended sprays or traditional neem oil treatments before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Shi kɛ́ oyɔse amɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema ni ji neem fɔ lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This natural process fertilizes the soil and helps neighboring crops like maize grow bigger and healthier.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot at the stem base and fall over right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Standing water around tomato roots encourages fungal diseases like damping-off or stem rot. Growing tomatoes on raised soil mounds helps water drain away easily and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: nu ni ebɔle Tomato shishifãi baanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tso lɛ shishifãi aba. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why is it necessary to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make energy for developing big tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp soil also prevents leaf spot diseases from spreading.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop producing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by dry weather stress. The plant curls its leaves to conserve moisture, which prevents flowers from developing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli Tso lɛ baafolɔ ebaa lɛ mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. ni tsiɔ fɔfɔii anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why should I avoid applying granular fertilizer when my soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to break down so plant roots can safely absorb them. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can scorch plant roots and waste the nutrients because the plant cannot swallow them without moisture.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛgbala bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛji nu bɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots forces the mother plant to share water and food with all of them. Leaving only two or three strong shoots ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural defense mechanism. Maize plants roll their leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing water from evaporating too quickly during severe heat.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Is it okay for me to trim or cut off the bottom leaves of my young coconut tree if they look too wide?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ afolɔ loo afolɔ ŋmei tso bibioo ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni elɛɛ tsɔ?

english: No, you should avoid cutting off any leaves from a young coconut tree. Every leaf captures sunlight that feeds the plant, helping it build strong roots and grow properly during its early stages.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa baa fɛɛ baai ni ooofo lɛ. kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei bibii amli Ba fɛɛ baa nine shɛɔ hulu la ni haa tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli.

english: Will cutting green leaves off my young crops make them grow faster or hurt them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mifo midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ, ebaaha amɛdara oya loo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: Cutting green leaves off young crops usually hurts them because leaves act as food factories. Removing healthy leaves reduces the plant's energy and slows down its overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ afo tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai eŋɔli lɛ, eyeɔ amɛ awui ejaakɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii afeemɔ he. Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ehaa edalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: My crop branches are spreading out very wide into the farm path; can I chop them off?
ga: Mi niji lɛ gbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ babaoo. Ani manyɛ mafo mli?

english: While you can trim overgrown side branches on mature trees to keep pathways open, you must be careful with young crops because cutting off leafy stems reduces their ability to produce food and yield well.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ ofolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ afã niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ koni gbɛ lɛ ahi shi moŋ. Shi esa akɛ okwɛ tsei bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo niyenii ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it so important to leave a young coconut seedling completely untrimmed while it is growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ aaashi ŋmei tsei bibii ni afolɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young coconut seedlings rely on all their fronds to produce the energy needed to establish deep roots and a solid trunk. Cutting fronds early can stunt the tree's development or delay fruit production.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kwraa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Baai ni afoɔ mra Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ dalɛ afee mlɛo loo eha yibii ni ewoɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: If a leaf on my young plant looks slightly bent or wide, should I remove it to keep the farm neat?
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɔle fioo loo elɛɛmɔ Ani Esa akɛ majie amɛ koni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ahi shi fɛfɛo?

english: No, as long as the leaf is green and healthy, it is working to nourish the plant. You should only remove leaves that are dead, dried up, or badly affected by diseases.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Etsuɔ nii hu koni ekɛha tsei niyenii. Esa akɛ ojie baai ni egboi, ni egbi, loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: If I planted my crops too close and the leaves are overlapping, should I cut the overlapping leaves?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi tsɔ ni miyɛ baai ni tsɔɔ amɛhe hu? Ani esa akɛ mafo baai ni feɔ ekome lɛ?

english: It is better not to cut healthy leaves from young plants. In the future, ensure proper planting distance so each crop has enough room to spread wide without needing to be trimmed.
ga: Ehi akɛ ooofolɔ tsei bibii ahe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Wɔsɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni egbɛ eshwa ni ehe ehiaaa ni afolɔ mli.

english: What role do leaves actually play in helping a newly planted fruit tree survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baai tsuɔ yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa aduawai tsei ni adu ehee lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ mli?

english: Leaves convert sunlight, water, and air into energy and nutrients. For a newly planted tree, having many healthy leaves speeds up root establishment and protects the plant's overall health.
ga: Baai tsakeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii. Kɛha tsei ni adu ehee lɛ Baai babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni ebu tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: At what stage in a tree's life is it safe to start pruning its branches and leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ tso shihilɛ mli ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaje eniji kɛ baai lɛ afolɔ shishi?

english: Pruning is generally safe once a tree is fully established and mature. During the seedling and nurturing stage, keeping all green fronds and branches intact is necessary for survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ ŋmɔmɔ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛji tso lɛ eda ni egbɔ. Yɛ dumɔwui adumɔ kɛ amɛtsɔsemɔ be mli lɛ Baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he miihia waa kɛha wala.

english: Does trimming a young plant to make it look short and tidy help it give more yield later?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni amɛfee tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: No, trimming young plants purely for neatness often reduces their potential yield because it takes away energy-producing leaves when the crop needs them the most.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni afolɔ koni amɛfee fɛo lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo lɛ baa shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ejieɔ baai ni haa hewalɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa tso lɛ waa lɛ.

english: What happens if a farm worker accidentally cuts fronds off my small coconut palms?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔ ko tsɔ oshara nɔ efo baa bibioo ko kɛjɛ mikokoo lɛ mli hu?

english: Removing fronds from small coconut palms weakens the plant, makes it more vulnerable to pests and heat stress, and significantly delays the age at which it will start bearing coconuts.
ga: Ajieɔ baai kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli Ebaaha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa amɛnɔ. ni ehaa afii ni ŋmeii baaje shishi amɛba lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ waa.

english: Why do my crops lose so much weight after I harvest and dry them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo beni mikpa ni migbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops retain a lot of water inside while growing in the field. When you dry them after harvest, that water evaporates, which reduces the total weight even though the crop quality remains good.
ga: Tsei hiɛɔ nu babaoo be mli ni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji ogbi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Nu lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsɔne lɛ mli tsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ su lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Why do my harvested grains get destroyed by insects even when I keep them in a dry storage place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miifite dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛto he ko ni egbi po.

english: Insect eggs or tiny pests often attach to the grains while they are still on the field before harvest, and they hatch and multiply inside storage bags if the crop or storage area is not properly treated.
ga: Kplukai bibii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awui Bei pii lɛ Amɛkpɛtɛɔ dumɔwui ahe be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo dani akpaa. Ni amɛbaafɔ ni amɛfɔ yɛ nitoo kotokui amli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ he ni amɛdaraa loo amɛtoɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops give me a good harvest in the major rainy season, but fail during the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eyeee omanye yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: The major rainy season provides continuous and heavy rainfall required for full crop development, whereas the minor season has shorter, unpredictable rains that often leave crops without enough water before they mature.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa, ni yaa nɔ daa ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ ni yeɔ emuu baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ, nugbɔ nɛɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii anaaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa dani amɛnyɛɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers fall off without producing fruit when plants face sudden heat stress, lack of water during flowering, or when there are not enough bees and insects in the farm to pollinate them.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ trukaa. Nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ afee pollination.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and green, but the cobs are very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Shi ani cob lɛ ji bibioo kwraa?

english: Tall green leaves show the soil has nitrogen for leaf growth, but small cobs mean the plant is lacking nutrients like phosphorus and potassium, which are needed to build full, heavy grains.
ga: Baai eŋɔlii ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni baanyɛ aha baai lɛ akwɛ̃. Shi ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium. Enɛ he miihia koni aná dumɔwui ni tsiimɔ yeɔ emuu.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil, or the plant roots are drowning and unable to breathe due to waterlogging in the field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo tsei ashishifãi miiho ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu yɛ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time my cassava or yam is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-cassava loo mi-sweet potato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Root crops like cassava and yam indicate maturity when their upper leaves naturally turn yellow and begin to drop, and the soil around the base of the plant starts cracking.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ dalɛ he okadii akpo kɛji amɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛje shishi amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ.

english: Why is my produce rotting on the farm before I even get the chance to harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miifite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ po nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Crops rot in the field when excessive rainfall saturates the soil or when insect bites pierce the skin of the produce, allowing fungal infections to spread while the crop is still attached to the plant.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi ŋmɔɔ nibii ni adu lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kã tso lɛ he lolo lɛ.

english: Why do some of my seeds sprout quickly while others planted on the same day do not grow at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya shi ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Uneven germination happens when seeds are planted at different depths, when soil moisture is uneven across the farm, or when some seeds were damaged before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo be mli ni dumɔwui komɛi efite dani aduɔ.

english: How does planting my crops too close together affect how much harvest I get?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ saa ŋmaa lɛ falɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and smaller overall yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa plants need soft shade to protect their delicate leaves from direct heat and harsh sunlight. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains, the young seedlings dry out and die before their roots can establish deep in the ground.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulutsoo be ni mli tse koni ebu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛɔ niyenii anɔ tamɔ plantains bɛ lɛ Tso bibioo lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbo dani shishifãi lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen or that the soil is holding too much water around the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed animal manure will help the leaves regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mikpaa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rains leave standing water in poorly drained soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli, ni no haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when pests attack the blossoms. Watering your plants consistently and keeping the soil moist helps flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to lift and stake my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni madu lɛ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to manufacture food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sunlight, boosting tuber growth and preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli. Ehaa tuber lɛ daa ni etsiɔ folier helai anaa.

english: What is eating small holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: Holes in the center of young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm hiding inside the plant's central funnel. Applying recommended pest treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ awo leebi tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the soil, while legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the earth naturally. Planting legumes restores soil fertility for your next planting season.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Legumes ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy winds before the bunches are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when carrying heavy bunches. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo fork prevents wind from snapping the stem or uprooting the tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo panicles ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa loo ŋmei ni akɛfee ŋtayaa fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafo tso lɛ shishi loo ekajie tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, they compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small peppers. Giving each plant proper space allows it to branch out and produce more fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ bafee ekome lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni etse niji ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the heat and keeps the soil cool. Over time, the grass breaks down and adds valuable organic matter to the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la kɛji akɛ edɔ. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Beni be hoɔ lɛ Jwɛi lɛ fãa ni ekɛ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants suffer from sun scorching when exposed to harsh, direct heat without shade. The intense sun causes the plant to lose water through its leaves faster than its young roots can absorb it from the dry soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he amanehulu kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like tubes in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense against intense sun heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to save its internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ he. Tsei haa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small green pods before the pods get the chance to mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani pods lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: This early pod loss, called cherelle wilt, happens when the tree gets stressed by lack of water, poor soil food, or extreme sun heat, forcing the tree to drop extra pods it cannot afford to feed.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mra nɛɛ akɛ cherel ni egboɔ. Ebaa beni tso lɛ miihao yɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ ajie ŋmeii krokomɛi ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of small flowers but very few actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo shi cocoa ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to transfer pollen so pods can form. If the farm is too dry or sprayed with harsh chemicals that kill these insects, the flowers dry up and fall off without making pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni ekɛ pollen yaa koni efee pods. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ efɔ nɔ. Fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why do my mature cocoa pods turn black and rot right when harvest time is near?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei ni eda lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite beni kpamɔ be lɛ ebɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and thick shade. It attacks mature pods when air cannot flow freely through the farm canopy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli wa mli kɛbaa. Etutuaa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling because the soil is out of plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ?

english: Crops show hunger through their leaves; if leaves turn pale yellow starting from the bottom, the soil lacks nitrogen, while purple or dark red leaves usually mean the soil lacks phosphorus.
ga: Tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen. yɛ be mli ni baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tsuru ni mli edɔ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops remain small and yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Rain provides water, but plants also need nutrients from the soil to grow strong. If the soil lacks essential nutrients or is too packed for roots to breathe, rainwater alone will not make the crop thrive.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara hewalɛ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu lɛ, Nugbɔ Nu pɛ haŋ tsei akwɛ̃.

english: Will planting cassava near my young cocoa trees hurt the cocoa's growth?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe lɛ baaná ŋmei lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: Cassava roots grow fast and aggressively steal food and water from the soil, which can starve young cocoa trees. Planting plantains is better because plantains share water better and provide gentle shade.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye kookoo tsei bibii. Plantains ni aduɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛjaraa nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhaa hulutsoo blɛoo.

english: Why are my crops growing very tall and thin, but not producing good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ekɛ yibii kpakpai baaa?

english: When crops get too much shade from large nearby trees, they spend all their energy growing tall to search for light instead of using energy to grow fruit and pods.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náa hulutsoo babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei wuji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ ni etee hiɛ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii kɛtao la lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛdu aduawai kɛ ŋmeii

english: Cutting non-essential branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the lower trunk, reducing diseases and directing the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ helai anɔ ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my rice plants producing very few seeds while my neighbor gets a huge harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: High rice yields depend on using certified seeds, planting at the right depth, managing water properly, and applying nitrogen fertilizer at key growth stages like tillering and panicle initiation.
ga: Omɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ damɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ he ni sa Nu he nitsumɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa tamɔ tillering kɛ panicle feemɔ mli.

english: How can I make sure the rice I harvest tastes good and isn't full of broken grains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ ŋɔɔ ni dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Good grain quality comes from harvesting at the right maturity—when 80% to 85% of grains turn golden yellow—and carefully drying the harvested paddy on clean tarpaulins rather than directly on bare ground.
ga: Omɔ kpakpa jɛɔ ŋmãa ni akpaa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ mli baa. he ni ŋmãa 80% kɛyashi 85% tsɔɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. ni okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ tarpaulin ni he tse nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, receiving too little water, or being damaged by root pests. Applying a balanced fertilizer and maintaining moisture can restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni nu fioo pɛ enine shɛɔ nɔ. aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ efite lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii ni akɛha ehiɛ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to keep my harvested crop from rotting when rain catches it in the field?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ matsi mikpamɔ lɛ naa koni ekafite kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cut crops should never be left lying on wet ground. Stack them on raised wooden racks or tarpaulins and cover them tightly with waterproof plastic sheets to protect them until they can be moved to a dry store.
ga: Esaaa akɛ ashiɔ tsei ni afolɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Okɛ amɛ ato tsei loo tarpaulin shɛlɛf ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ plastic ni nu nyɛɛɛ abote mli lɛ aha he jogbaŋŋ koni ebu he kɛyashi abaanyɛ ajie kɛya shwapo ko ni mli egbi mli.

english: How do I know when my harvested grain is dry enough to store safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛto he ko shweshweeshwe?

english: You can test grain dryness by biting a kernel: if it cracks sharply with a hard snap rather than flattening, it is dry enough (around 12-14% moisture) to store without risk of mold or rot.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooomɔ nɔ: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ gbá yɛ hewalɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmãa lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi bɔ ni sa. (Humidity aaafee 12-14%) ni akɛtoɔ ni oshara ko bɛ he akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baafite.

english: What can I do to stop insects from destroying my stored rice after harvest?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni kooloi akafite ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ensure the grains are completely dry before storage, clean the storage container thoroughly, and store the crop in sealed hermetic bags or clean drums placed off the concrete floor on wooden pallets.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛto. Tsumɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ato kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli loo tsɔnei ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land seem less fertile every time I plant rice on the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaa shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your rice with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and improves its health naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake o-rice lɛ. Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa egbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛnamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does leaving weeds in my field harm my crop before harvest time?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients away from young crop plants. Clearing weeds early in the growing season ensures your crop gets all the strength it needs to produce heavy grains.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui ni tsii aba.

english: How can I protect my crop from birds when the grains start to ripen?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ okpoi ahe kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɔi shweremɔ pɛ?

english: Birds attack when grains are soft and milky. You can scare them away by hanging reflective ribbons, placing scarecrows, or coordinating with nearby farmers to plant and harvest at the same time so birds spread out rather than destroying one field.
ga: Okpoi tutuaa kɛ́ ŋmaa lɛ mli edɔ ni eyɛ mliki. Obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ akabɔ he kɛtsɔ tsɔnei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ, loo okɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ afee ekome koni amɛdu ni amɛkpa nii yɛ be kome mli koni amɛgbɛ okpoi lɛ amɛshwã moŋ fe ni oookpãtã ŋmɔ kome hiɛ.

english: How does joining a local farmer group help me improve my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni mikɛ mihe baawo mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi koni mikpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Farmer groups allow you to learn better farming techniques from peers, buy quality seeds and fertilizers in bulk for cheaper prices, and share tools and storage space to protect your harvests from going to waste.
ga: Okwaafoi akui yeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ okwaayeli he ŋaai ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ onanemɛi adɛŋ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni hi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ jara ni baa shi nɔ. ni okɛ nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ aha koni obu onibii ahe koni ekafite.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide leafy shade to shield the young cocoa until it is strong enough to stand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ehaa baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo be lɛ naa.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and keep its root tubers alive underground. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves again.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha shishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients for planting maize?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ bɛ?

english: If your young maize plants have pale light-green or yellowish leaves instead of dark green ones, or if growth is stunted, your soil is likely low in nitrogen and needs manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ dalɛ lɛ egbɔjɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: What is eating small holes in the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Spraying approved insecticides early in the morning or late evening when they are active helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants twisted and covered in light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this from happening.
ga: Enɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi, ni koolooi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are extremely hot, when the soil is too dry, or when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do I have to support my yam vines with tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight to make food, which helps the tubers under the ground grow much bigger and reduces disease risk from wet soil.
ga: Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ sweet potato mli lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aha kɛha nihoomɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara babaoo ni ebaaha helai ni jɛɔ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium uptake in the plant. Watering your farm regularly keeps soil moisture steady and prevents this rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be kɛ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crop yield so much during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: During the early weeks, young crop roots are weak and compete heavily with fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early allows your crop to build a strong root system.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How can I stop small insects from eating my stored dried corn after harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmãa ni egbi ni ato yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Insects thrive in damp grain. Ensure your corn is thoroughly dried until the kernels crack cleanly, then store it in airtight hermetic bags to suffocate pests without needing dangerous chemicals.
