ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ baagbele amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni ekɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛjɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Rain can wash nutrients away, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but produce tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eshishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or leaf litter but lacks potassium, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves above ground instead of swelling its roots below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo baai amli jwɛi babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines wrap around wooden stakes and try to climb high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ shwieɔ tso ko he ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines climb stakes to reach direct sunlight. The more sunlight the upper leaves capture, the more food the plant produces to build a larger yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Babaoo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ lɛ naa lɛ, tsei lɛ baajie niyenii babaoo kpo koni amɛkɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the fruit bunch grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that spread near the surface rather than going deep. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the tree becomes top-heavy, so supporting it with a strong wooden prop prevents it from falling.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni eeeya shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ tsɔ tsii Tso lɛ baafee tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fĩ esɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsĩ enaa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of leaves but refusing to bring out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ebɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas often produce excess leaves instead of flowers when they get too much water or rich fertilizer. They need a small amount of mild water stress to signal to the plant that it is time to flower.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsina ŋmeii lɛ, amɛwoɔ baai ni fa fe nine yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Nu he haomɔ fioo he miihia amɛ koni ekɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni ebaawo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Heat and moisture stress prevent the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo haomɔ tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkawo yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees dry up and brown at the edges during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, cocoa trees lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull from the dry soil. Planting shade trees nearby shields cocoa from intense sun and keeps soil moist.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it bad for my crop if rainwater sits on my field for three days without draining?
ga: Ani ebaana hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii etɛ ni nu ko bɛ mli?

english: Yes, standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off oxygen. Roots need air to breathe, and prolonged standing water causes root rot, turning leaves yellow and killing the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛmu. Ni nu ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the leaf juices, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling the insects early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Mra Kooloi Akwɛmɔ Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay loose and soft instead of forming a hard, tight ball?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ egbɔjɔɔ ni eyɛ blɛoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbages stay soft when temperatures are too high or water supply is uneven. They need cool weather, consistent watering, and proper feeding so the inner leaves pack tightly together.
ga: Kaabaji feɔ blɛoo kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ he miihia amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa bɔni afee ni emli baai lɛ afee ekome jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to make food, or that the ground is waterlogged and choking the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛfee niyenii Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni shishifãi lɛ miihoso.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, extreme dry soil, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa Aloo be mli ni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant several seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebɛ hewalɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crowded stems fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all of them malnourished and fragile.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dense stems lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves toward sunlight to produce large tubers underground; lifting them off the damp ground also prevents leaves from rotting and catching fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Kɛ́ owó nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in a clear open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight; they need temporary shade plants like plantains to act as natural covers and protect their delicate leaves while their root systems mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni amɛbuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and causing the whole plant to stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the sap and transmitting leaf curl viruses that stunt the plant's development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni haaa tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my cassava roots soft and rotting inside the soil before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when planted in heavy soil that holds onto too much water without proper drainage, causing air to be pushed out and fungal pathogens to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I wait until after my seeds sprout before applying fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds use their own stored energy to germinate and do not have developed roots yet to drink up fertilizer, so putting fertilizer down too early causes rain to wash it away before the plant can use it.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛbɛ shishifãi ni amɛbaada ni amɛkɛtsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lolo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ ashwie nɔ dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to give me a very small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔ titri lɛ yibiiwoo aba lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and aggressively suck up the water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil that your main plants need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe shia tsei ni amɛmuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa otsei titrii lɛ amli koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ mli.

english: Why is it unsafe for me to spray chemical pesticides on my vegetables right before I harvest and sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ anɔ yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ dani makpãtã ni mahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays require a waiting period to naturally break down into harmless compounds; harvesting too soon after spraying leaves toxic residues on the produce that can poison consumers.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ biɔ ni amɛmɛ be dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbala amɛhe amɛwo nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni baanyɛ ahã mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ lɛ aná tsofai fɔji.

english: How do I know if my maize crop is growing properly one month after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔŋ kome sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: About one month after planting, a healthy maize crop should be around knee-high, vibrant green, and developing thick stems. If it looks small or pale at this stage, it likely needs nitrogen fertilizer and weed clearing.
ga: Aaafee nyɔŋ kome yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Esa akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ashɛ aaafee tsitsi nɔ. ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni eyɛ tso ni mli tse Kɛji akɛ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eji bibioo loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni he hiaa.

english: What is the best time for me to plant maize to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa koni maná yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: The best time is at the beginning of the major rainy season when the soil has steady moisture. Planting early ensures seeds germinate quickly and build strong root systems before any dry spells.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛgbiɔ.

english: What is this armyworm pest that destroys maize, and how can I spot it early?
ga: Mɛni ji cutworm kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ okadi mra?

english: Fall Armyworms are destructive caterpillars that feed on maize leaves and cobs. You can spot them early by looking inside the central funnel of young leaves for small holes or sawdust-like droppings.
ga: Fall Armyworms ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii. Obaanyɛ ona amɛ mra. Kwɛmɔ baa bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ koni ona bu bibioo ko. loo ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii

english: How can I protect my young corn farm from pests so they do not destroy my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe? Bɔni afee ni mikafite mihegbɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Inspect your crop regularly at least twice a week, spray appropriate control treatments directly into the plant funnel early in the morning or evening, and clear surrounding weeds where pests hide.
ga: Kwɛmɔ onibii amli daa, kɛ hoo lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Okɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe ewo mli lɛ.

english: Why are pests attacking my corn field while my neighbor's farm seems to remain untouched and peaceful?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he ni efee dioo lɛ?

english: Pests are often attracted to crops that are under stress, weak, or underfed. A well-fertilized, properly spaced, and weed-free field builds stronger plants that resist pest attacks better.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni haoɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, loo niyenii ni falɛ faaa lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Hei ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ha okɛ ohe akabɔ he ni sa. Ni akɛni jwɛi bɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni he wa ni nyɛɔ amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen fertilizer or that excess water around the roots is suffocating the plant, preventing it from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsi niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ naa

english: How can I make sure my maize ears grow big and well-formed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-ŋmãa toi lɛ ada ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: To get well-formed cobs, space your seeds properly during planting so plants do not fight for light, apply NPK and Urea fertilizer at the right times, and keep the field clean from weeds.
ga: Bɔni afee ni oná cob ni hiɛ su kpakpa Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ dumɔ be mli koni tsei lɛ akatswa la he akaŋ. Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ urea awo mli yɛ be ni sa mli. ni oha jɛmɛ he atse kɛjɛ jwɛi ahe

english: Why do my corn plants bend or fall over before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ebɔle loo amɛmiigbee shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall over due to weak stalks, which happen when seeds are planted too close together, soil lacks nutrients, or stem borer insects burrow into the base of the stalk.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbee shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli Aloo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yɛ ni boteɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: How many times do I need to clear weeds from my corn farm after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: You should weed at least twice: first about two to three weeks after planting when young seedlings are small, and second about five to six weeks after planting before the leaves form a dense cover.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii shii enyɔ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ bibii lolo lɛ. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ aaafee otsii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. dani baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Is good rain enough to make my crop yield well, or do I need to do extra work?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai? Aloo esa akɛ matsu nitsumɔ kroko?

english: Rain provides essential water, but a good crop also requires proper land preparation, quality seeds, timely weeding, pest protection, and soil fertilization.
ga: Nugbɔ ji nu jɛɛhe ko ni he hiaa waa. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kpakpa lolo. dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa lɛ Hebuu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are fully matured and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ edara kwraa kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ Ejeɔ kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my yam vines so frequently while they are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli be mli ni amɛmiida lɛ?

english: Weed roots steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from young yam vines, which stops the tubers underground from swelling into large, healthy yams.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ atomo wain tsei bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii agboi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize stalks produce small ears with missing grains on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ toi bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when the maize plant does not get enough water or nutrients during the flowering stage, or when heat and insects damage the soft silk before pollination finishes.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo beni latsaa kɛ kooloi bibii fiteɔ siliki ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani pollination lɛ baa naagbee lɛ.

english: What causes small green caterpillars to eat the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest that hatches from moth eggs laid on young leaves. They feed on the tender central leaf roll and need early control before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui ni akɛwoɔ baai bibii anɔ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni ehe miihia ni akudɔ amɛ mra dani afite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Is it better to plant seeds saved from my previous maize harvest or buy certified seeds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli loo aaahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred to resist local diseases, handle heat, and produce uniform crops. Saved seeds gradually lose their strength each season, leading to lower yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ dɔlɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite Ehewalɛ fiofio yɛ be fɛɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight and dry Harmattan winds. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a cooler environment and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily once the bunch of fruit starts growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that tiny soil worms (nematodes) can easily weaken. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the root stem cannot hold the weight without a wooden prop for support.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. (Nematodes) lɛ baanyɛ agbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Kɛ́ sɛɛfimɔ bɛ lɛ, shishifã lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ etsiimɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my land yield less food every year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ baa shi daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops pull essential nutrients out of the earth every season. Without replacing those nutrients using animal manure, compost, or crop rotation, the soil becomes tired and depleted.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛtsakeee nakai niyenii lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafite.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts fix nitrogen from the air directly into the ground, naturally naturally enriching the soil so the next crop grows strong without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ saa nitrogen lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa waa ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii babaoo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant without growing into any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures become too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks essential minerals like calcium during the blooming period.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom in a V-shape, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or NPK helps the plant green up and produce healthy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V-shape yɔɔ shishi lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them restores natural fertility, helping your next crop grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei nɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ. Ye obua onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofa babaoo he ehiaaa bo.

english: How can I tell if my crops need more water during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Check your crop early in the morning; if the leaves look wilted or curled before the sun gets hot, the plant is stressed for water. You can also dig a few inches into the soil to see if it is completely dry.
ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli leebi. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni baai lɛ egbɔjɔ loo ebɔle amɛhe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi koni amɛnu nu. Obaanyɛ ofo shi inchi fioo komɛi hu koni ona kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains leave water standing in the field, it suffocates the roots, allowing underground rot and fungi to destroy the crop.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ŋmɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and produce food for the tubor underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the wet ground so they get plenty of sun and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛmɔ hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni eha hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they get too stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent watering and mulching around the stem can keep the flowers attached.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hao amɛ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he daa Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my vegetable seeds sprout at different times instead of all together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli moŋ fe ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛbaafee ekome lɛ?

english: Uneven sprouting usually happens when seeds are planted at different depths or if parts of the soil stay drier than others. Planting seeds at a uniform depth ensures they receive equal moisture and germinate together.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shweremɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui yɛ hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome mli egbi lolo fe fãi krokomɛi lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni tamɔ amɛhe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites. These pests feed on the leaves and can spread viruses that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛ baanyɛ amɛ gbɛ muawai ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: What causes black spots on my cocoa pods when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baa?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let in sunlight and harvesting ripe pods quickly helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni abaakpa koni hulu la babaoo aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slower and produce smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds grow close to your crops, they steal the resources your plants need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe Jwɛi nɛɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are tiny green cocoa pods drying up and falling off my trees before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Koni amɛgbi ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani eda lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' which happens when the tree sheds extra pods it cannot feed, or by pests like mirids (capsids) and fungal diseases. Pruning and pest control help the tree keep its pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘Cherelle wilt’ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa, ni baa beni tso ko fiteɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni enyɛŋ eye loo ŋmeii tamɔ mirids (capsids) kɛ fungal helai kɛbaa lɛ Pruning kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell known as a false start. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout and then dry up in the hot soil before the main rainy season fully begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ale lɛ akɛ amale shishijee nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with leafy stems but produce tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or plants are placed too close together, the cassava put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing energy underground in large tubers.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo akɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii wuji amli lɛ, ŋmei duɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ ebaa lɛ mli.

english: Lifting yam vines off the damp ground allows leaves to catch more sunlight and fresh air, which prevents leaf rot diseases and gives the plant energy to form bigger yams.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ sweet potatoes wuji.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Keeping the farm clean and spraying appropriate organic or chemical controls stops them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ baa lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni akɛ tsofai loo tsofai ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baakpa enɛ.

english: This is usually bacterial wilt, a soil disease that clogs the water pipes inside the stem. Even if the ground is wet, water cannot move up to the leaves, causing the plant to collapse.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, bacteria wilt kɛbaa Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ sũ lɛ mli efɔ po lɛ, nu lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɔ kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Beans and groundnuts are special plants that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the roots decay, they leave free food in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ, amɛshiɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ abele.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you put into the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and soft when my farm experiences heavy rain and standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo beni miŋmɔ lɛ mli nugbɔ nɛɔ waa kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes all the air out of the soil. Crop roots need air to breathe and collect nutrients like nitrogen; without oxygen in flooded soil, the roots suffocate and cannot feed the plant, turning leaves yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛkɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ato. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do leaves on my crop wilt and droop in the hot afternoon sun even though the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miigbo ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: During intense midday heat, water leaves the plant leaves through evaporation faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant wilts to save moisture, but it will usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Nu shĩɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe ehiaaa ni tsei lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe jɔɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the young cocoa trees on my farm turning brown and losing leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under strong sunlight and dry winds. They lose water quickly during dry periods unless shade plants, like plantains, are grown next to them to block the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Nu lɛ laajeɔ amɛ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Ja adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi koni ekɛtsi hulu la lɛ naa.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with bushy green leaves, but the tubers underground are tiny when I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ jwɛi ni baai eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi kɛ́ mifo mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and thick leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build big starch tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee ngmɔkɔ nguahi nɛ a ngɛ starch ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb instead of letting the vines spread across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha wain tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need to reach as much sunlight as possible to make food for big underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, keeps them healthy, and prevents wet ground rot.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking elevator lɛ baajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha oná hewalɛ ni otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why are my maize plants shooting out flowers while they are still very short and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni eyɛ kuku waa ni eyɛ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: When a maize plant experiences early heat or water stress, it thinks it is going to die. To survive, it panics and flowers early to produce seeds before it dries out completely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei na dɔlɛ loo nu mli haomɔ mra lɛ, Esusu akɛ eegbo. koni ehi shi Ehe miihia ni atswa lɛ gbeyei ni efɔ fɔfɔi mra koni ekɛ dumɔwui awo mli dani egbi kwraa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start carrying heavy bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi aduawai babaoo womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, the top of the tree becomes too heavy for the shallow roots to hold, especially when wind blows or soil gets wet.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ bafee tsiimɔ Tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baafee tsiimɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ atere. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: This problem, called blossom-end rot, happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the developing fruit. It usually occurs when watering is irregular, like switching between very dry and very wet conditions.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha yibii ni miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ ateŋ tsakemɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tight cups and refusing to grow fresh flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpooɔ fɔfɔi heei lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often a sign of tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking juices from the undersides of young leaves, or a virus spread by those pests. This damages the leaves so the plant stops flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miinu nu kɛjɛ baai bibii lɛ ashishi. loo helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my cassava bushes drop almost all their leaves during dry periods, and does it mean they are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ egbo?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss. The plant is not dead; it goes to sleep to save energy in its tubers and will sprout new leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli akɛ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi koni ekɛba nu ni fiteɔ lɛ shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebaawɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eyitsoŋ. ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and leaves. It can also happen when the soil stays too soaked with water, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma amɛshishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛkaye nii.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops right before a heavy rain or after the rain stops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba loo beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after light rain, or just before mild rain. Heavy downpours right after application will wash the fertilizer away into streams before your crop roots have time to drink it in.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajie kɛya faa lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛnu.

english: How does leaving dead stalks and dry leaves on my field help my soil for the next season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni egboi kɛ tsei ni egboi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Leaving crop remains on the soil acts like a blanket that keeps the ground cool and traps moisture. As the dry leaves rot, they turn into rich natural manure that feeds the soil for your next planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Kɛji baai lɛ gĩ ni amɛgboi Ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This makes the plants grow tall and thin with smaller yields than if they had proper breathing space.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo fe kɛji amɛyɛ he ko ni sa ni amɛkɛmuɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. When the plant feels stressed by heat or drought, it drops its flowers to save its strength and stay alive.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ dɔlɛ loo hɔmɔ miigba amɛnaa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do tiny holes keep appearing on my vegetable leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ anɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Holes in leaves are usually caused by insects like caterpillars, beetles, or grasshoppers eating the plant. Leaves are the plant's food factory, so when pests eat them, the crop cannot grow full fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Baai ji tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. No hewɔ lɛ, beni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ nakai tsei lɛ Nibii ni adu lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii ni fa.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting under the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot under the ground when rainwater settles in the soil for too long without draining away. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How can I check if the dried seeds I stored from last harvest will sprout before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni egbi ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ dani adu?

english: Wrap 10 sample seeds in a moist cloth or paper, place them in a dark spot, and keep the cloth damp for 5 days. If 8 or more seeds grow little shoots, your stored seeds are healthy and good for planting.
ga: Okɛ dumɔwui nɔkwɛmɔnɔ 10 awo mama loo wolo ni mli efɔ mli. Okɛwo he ko ni duŋ yɔɔ. Ni okɛ atade lɛ ato gbii 5 kɛji akɛ dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni okɛto lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface and carry very heavy fruit bunches at the top. To stop them from falling over in strong winds, prop up the heavy stems using strong wooden poles or bamboo forks.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ, ni aduawai akuu ko ni tsii waa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Koni akagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa hewɔ. Fiɔ tso ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ kɛtsɔ tso tso ni wa loo ŋmei fɔk nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow faster during the major rainy season compared to the minor rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa shi fioo lɛ he lɛ?

english: The major rainy season brings longer, more reliable rainfall and high humidity, which allows plant roots to constantly draw water and food from the soil without experiencing periods of dryness.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛnaaa ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them out in an open, sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse kɛ he ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted nearby to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ lɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the plant is mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient they need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps them regain their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I harvesting long, thin roots on my cassava plants instead of big, heavy tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa ŋmei shishifãi kakadaji ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose soil and enough space between stems to expand. If the soil is packed hard or plants are grown too close together, the roots cannot swell into big tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni egbɛ eshwa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashwere ni amɛfee bulbs agboi.

english: Why are there small caterpillars eating holes inside the leaf funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the central leaves of corn plants. Checking your farm regularly and applying recommended sprays early in the plant's growth helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni atsɔɔ akɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ tsu nii mra yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or attacks from small insects like whiteflies. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protecting the plants from pests helps fruits set successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji ni tutuaa lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to spread their leaves high up to catch sunlight for growth. Staking keeps leaves off the wet ground to avoid disease and allows the plant to produce larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tso ji wain tso ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ bɔni afee ni eda. Staking baajie tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni helai akamɔ tso lɛ ni eha tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil and crops?
ga: Te ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When grown near maize, they naturally feed the soil with nutrients that help the maize grow stronger.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, root space, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the water and plant food available in the soil.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná nu kɛ tsei niyenii fɛɛ ni amɛyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: It is best to wait until the ground gets a thorough soaking from two or three good rains. Planting too early after a single light shower can cause seeds to sprout and then dry out if the rain stops for weeks.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo.

english: Leaving too many shoots around one plantain stem forces them all to fight for the same food and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest stem, resulting in much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome he lɛ, ebaanyɛ amɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwu amɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ eshwɛɔ. Nɔ ni ejɛ mli eba ji akɛ, plantain jwɛi lɛ ebatsɔ agbo kwraa.

english: Why are my crops starting to yellow and wilt during a month when it normally rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ nyɔŋ kome ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa daa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weather patterns can shift from year to year, causing unexpected dry spells even during peak rainy months like June. When temperatures rise without rain, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up, leading to wilting and leaf yellowing.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baanyɛ atsake kɛjɛ afi kɛya afi. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni akpaaa gbɛ baa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa tamɔ June lɛ po amli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops flower early and stay small when the weather stays dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi mra ni amɛhiɔ shi bibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops experience heat and severe lack of water, they go into emergency survival mode. They rush to produce flowers and seeds early to reproduce before dying, which leaves the main plant short, stunted, and low-yielding.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii mli edɔ waa ni nu hu faaa lɛ, tso lɛ boteɔ oyaiyeli shihilɛ mli. Amɛhe feɔ oya koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui mra. koni efɔ dani egbo Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ feɔ kuku, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do some crops on my farm stay green during dry periods while others wither quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni ekrokomɛi hu gboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Different crops have different root structures and water requirements. Deep-rooted crops like cassava can pull moisture from deep underground, while shallow-rooted crops like maize rely on topsoil water and dry out much faster when rains fail.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni tso fɛɛ tso yɔɔ shishifã kɛ nu he hiamɔ nii. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ ŋmei, baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ, ni amɛgbiɔ oya kwraa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops if the rain suddenly stops after planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa beni midu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: No, you should wait until steady rains return. Chemical fertilizers require soil moisture to dissolve, and applying them to dry soil concentrates the salts, which can burn and kill crop roots.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba daa. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani etsɔ mli. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei shishifãi

english: How does covering my soil with dry leaves or grass help my crops survive when the rain fails?
ga: Te baa loo jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with plant materials, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It shields the soil from direct sunlight, reducing evaporation so the ground stays moist and cool for much longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni ehaa la ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni edɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my wilting crops will recover when the rain returns or if they are dead?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo lɛ baatsake kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba loo ebaagbo?

english: Check the central stem and inner leaves early in the morning. If the core remains green and flexible, the plant is alive and will bounce back with water; if the stem is dry, brown, and snaps easily, the plant has died.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ kɛ emli baai lɛ leebi. Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tee nɔ efee eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baahi shi ni ekɛ nu lɛ baaku esɛɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ mli egbi, eyɛ asarasu, ni efoɔ oya lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ egbo.

english: It can be risky because the first rain is often a 'false start' followed by days or weeks of hot sun. It is safer to wait until two or three reliable rains have soaked the ground deep enough to sustain young roots.
ga: Oshara baanyɛ aba ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ ni gbii loo otsii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nɛɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua shishifãi bibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize seeds if the rains stop right after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If the soil dries out completely after planting, the seeds may absorb just enough moisture to swell but fail to germinate, or young sprouts will dry up in the topsoil before their roots grow deep.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui baanyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfutu shi ekwɛɛɛ. Aloo tso bibioo lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ mli aba.

english: Why are my cassava plants dropping their leaves during an unexpected hot and dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be baa trukaa lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces moisture loss and protects its underground tubers until the rains come back.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaai lɛ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai ni eshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How long can young crop seedlings survive without rain after they sprout?
ga: Be enyiɛ dumɔwui bibii baanyɛ ahi shi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Most delicate seedlings like maize or vegetables can only survive about 5 to 7 days without moisture before suffering permanent damage, whereas hardier crops like sorghum can endure longer dry spells by slowing down their growth.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai baanyɛ ahi shi aaafee gbii 5 kɛyashi 7 ni nu bɛ mli dani amɛfiteɔ daa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni wa babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, baanyɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛbaa shi lɛ nɔ.

english: What are chicken droppings, and how do they help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni ji tsina ŋmɔtɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chicken droppings (sometimes called 'lisa') are a rich organic fertilizer full of nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus that feed the soil, helping crops grow stronger roots and produce a heavier harvest.
ga: Kooloo ŋmei (bei komɛi lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Lisa’) ji ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni niyenii mli nibii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus eyi mli obɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Can I apply fresh chicken droppings directly to my young crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh chicken manure is usually too concentrated and can burn delicate plant roots. It is best to let it dry out or decompose for a few weeks before mixing it into your crop soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ tsɔ ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha egbi loo egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfutu osũ ni okɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil needs manure like chicken droppings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your crops grow slowly, look pale or yellowish, or produce small fruits despite getting enough rainfall, your soil is likely low on nutrients and needs manure to regain its strength.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Etamɔ nɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the right way to put chicken manure around my plants?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ woɔ tsei ahe?

english: Place the dried manure in a circle a few inches away from the plant stem rather than touching it directly, and cover it lightly with soil so rain can wash the nutrients down to the roots.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi lɛ afee kooloo ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ inchii fioo komɛi. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ehe baabɔ he tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛ sũ aha he fioo Bɔni afee ni nugbɔ anyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Will using chicken droppings keep my soil healthy for future planting seasons?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ bei lɛ?

english: Yes, organic manure builds up the soil's structure and helps it hold moisture over time, keeping the land productive for future seasons unlike raw chemicals that wash away quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei. Ejeee tamɔ tsofai ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni shwieɔ oya.

english: Why is proper plant spacing so important for getting a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kpakpa lɛ?

english: When crops are spaced properly instead of planted too close together, each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water to reach its full size and give a high yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ajie amɛhe kɛjɛ he kroko moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tso fɛɛ tso baaná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ehiɛ ashɛ elɛɛmɔ fɛɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo nɔ.

english: Why should I plant my seeds in straight rows instead of scattering them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni madu amɛ?

english: Planting in neat rows makes it much easier to walk through your field, control weeds, apply manure evenly, and see which plants are growing well.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ aaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, akudɔ jwɛi lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ana tsei ni miida jogbaŋŋ.

english: What are the key steps I need to take right from planting to ensure a good crop yield?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ mafee kɛjɛ dumɔ mli koni maná ŋmaa kpakpa?

english: Getting a good harvest depends on clear land preparation, planting seeds at the right depth and distance, feeding the soil with manure, and keeping weeds away from young plants.
ga: Nikpamɔ kpakpa damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni asaa he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa kɛ jwɛi ni akɛtsiɔ tsei bibii ahe

english: When is the best stage in a crop's growth to feed it with organic manure?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli koni akɛ tsofa ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aha?

english: It is best to work manure into the soil during land preparation or early in the plant's life so it has plenty of food while building its stem and main leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ loo yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli. Koni ekɛ niyenii babaoo aha yɛ be mli ni efeɔ tsei wuji kɛ baai lɛ.

english: Why is it important to regularly walk through and inspect my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔ mli ni makwɛ nibii ni midu lɛ amli daa lɛ?

english: Regularly inspecting your farm allows you to notice pest damage, disease, or nutrient shortages early before they spread and destroy your whole harvest.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa mra. Dani ebaagbɛ eshwa ni efite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hulu lɛ etswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight because their root systems are not yet fully developed. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains beside them creates a canopy that shields the young cocoa leaves from heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ eshɛko amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lolo. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants store energy in their leaves through sunlight to build large underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, allowing maximum leaf exposure to sunlight while keeping the leaves away from soil-borne damp diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hewalɛ toɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ hulu la nɔ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, yɛ be mli ni ehaa baa lɛ hu tsiɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing maize leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or manure supplies the crop with the essential nutrient it needs to produce green leaves and grow sturdy stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my crop seeds very close to each other?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with smaller harvests. Giving crops proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to thrive.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã tsei ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving brown powder inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This pattern is typical of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the leaf funnels of maize to feed on tender leaves. Spotting them early and applying approved treatments directly into the plant funnels protects the growing points.
ga: Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ feɔ, ni ekɛ ehe teeɔ ŋmei baai lɛ amli koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ ona amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo dumɔwu lɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling whiteflies early and maintaining steady watering reduces this stress on the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli Early Whitefly Control Ni nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ baaha nɔnyɛɛ ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains stay on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Prolonged waterlogging suffocates the root system and promotes fungi growth, causing roots to rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant undergoes stress from irregular water supply, extreme heat, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture balanced and adding balanced nutrients prevents blossom drop.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than my main crops right after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild species adapted to survive in local conditions, allowing them to absorb moisture and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli kooloi ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye hɔmɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: When is the best time of day for me to apply crop treatments or spray chemicals on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛtsaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is ideal because temperatures are lower and winds are calm. Spraying during cooler hours prevents treatments from evaporating too quickly or burning crop foliage in the hot sun.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli Ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Kɛ́ afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi la ni hoɔ oya tsɔ loo tso baai ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ naa.

english: This is a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The maize plant is forced to move nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to keep the new top leaves growing, which tells you the soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or compost.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Anyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ koni amɛjie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ ahe koni amɛha ŋwɛi baa heei akwɛ̃. Enɛ tsɔɔ bo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but produce very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when a plant focuses entirely on top growth, the cassava plant directs all its energy into stems and leaves instead of storing food in the underground tubers.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ema bɔ ni ebaadara babaoo lɛ nɔ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa etso kɛ ebaa lɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, which naturally restores soil fertility for nutrient-hungry crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and drop off the tree during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry spells to reduce water loss and save their roots from drying out completely, which is why keeping shade trees on the farm is necessary to protect them from direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ akagbi kwraa. Yɛ yiŋtoo nɛɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akwɛmɔ he miihia waa koni akɛbu cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my hot pepper plants instead of turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat or water stress, as dropping flowers allows the plant to save its energy and survive unfavorable conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛshwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering during fruit formation, which causes the bottom cell walls of the fruit to collapse.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Enɛ haa wala yibii ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa saplings burn easily in direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut down the extra small shoots sprouting around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Allowing too many shoots to grow creates heavy competition for water and nutrients, which steals energy from the main tree and leaves you with much smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii ni naa wa aba kɛha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni juɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli Ni eshiɔ bo kɛ plantain tso bibioo kwraa.

english: Why is it necessary for me to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum direct sunlight to produce food; lifting the vines onto stakes exposes more leaves to the sun, driving energy down to enlarge the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Hewalɛ ni akɛkuɔ shi koni akɛgbala tubers yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my garden egg plants curling upward and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus transmitted by those insects that distorts normal plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ kɛbaa ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ ni sa lɛ nɔ

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the crop lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure around the base helps the plant regain its strength and stay green.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aku esɛɛ eda waa ni ehi shi ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas together with my maize help my soil and crops perform better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, which means they naturally trap nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer, nourishing the maize plants growing alongside them.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ niyenii

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes into the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides deep inside the funnel of young maize leaves to feed. Applying targeted biopesticides or approved sprays early directly into the plant center protects the growing tip from being destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni teɔ shi ewoɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli shɔŋŋ koni eye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves and spreading viruses. Controlling these small pests early using neem water or recommended sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ neem nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees off my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under direct sunlight and high heat. Keeping or planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains protects young cocoa trees from sun stress and retains moisture in the soil until the trees are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ loo adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cocoa tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo be mli. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when heavy winds and rain arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy foliage loaded with heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the heavy fruiting stems with strong bamboo stakes prevents the roots from tearing out of wet soil during high winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni eyi kɛ aduawai ni tsii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa fiɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do I need to prop up my yam vines with tall wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?
