english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate the energy required for large tuber growth. Staking lifts the foliage into the air for sunlight and keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe, ni ehaaa amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water cuts off oxygen to the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get extremely hot, when water supply is uneven, or when soil lacks calcium. Maintaining regular watering and mulching the soil surface keeps root temperatures stable so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli dɔlɛ yaa nɔ daa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and pale even when I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and space away from crop roots. Clearing weeds early prevents them from starving your crops of essential food and moisture needed for strong growth.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ he ko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishifãi ahe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Etsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I get certified seedlings from extension officers instead of just planting seeds from crops I harvested last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ extension officer ko dɛŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ,.

english: Certified seeds and seedlings are carefully selected and treated to resist common pests and diseases, grow faster, and yield far more produce than seeds saved from previous harvests, which naturally lose their strength over time.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi kooloi kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ. amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ

english: Why do nursery seedlings look small when planted, but grow into much stronger trees than seeds sown directly into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ? Shi edaa ni efeɔ tso ni he wa fe dumɔwui ni adũɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Seedlings grown in a nursery get extra care, rich nutrients, and protection during their most vulnerable stage. This allows them to build a strong root foundation before transplanting, helping them survive harsh field conditions better.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko. Niyenii babaoo kɛ hebuu yɛ bei ni yɔɔ oshara fe fɛɛ lɛ amli Ye obua amɛ ni amɛma shishitoo ni wa dani amɛdu. Yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do plantation crops take so many years to start producing fruit after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Long-term plantation crops like oil palm or cocoa spend their first few years growing sturdy trunks and deep root systems. This initial slow period allows the tree to build the strength needed to produce heavy harvests for decades to come.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ oil palm loo cocoa lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ tsei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ shishijee be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ amli.

english: What basic steps do I need to take when starting a fresh crop plantation from scratch?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ mije sũ dumɔ shishi kɛjɛ shishijee?

english: Starting a plantation requires clearing the land properly, spacing your planting holes correctly so crops do not compete for light and water, and protecting young seedlings with shade and weed control in their first few months.
ga: Abɔɔ shishijee biɔ ni ajie jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛjegbɛ nɔ dumɔ bui jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii akatswa la kɛ nu he akaŋ. ni abu tsei bibii ahe kɛ hulutsoo kɛ jwɛi ni akuɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: Is it good practice to plant yams and other food crops between my young plantation trees on the same farm?
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni aduɔ Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting food crops like yam between young tree crops—known as intercropping—is a smart practice. It provides your family with food and income while the main plantation trees are still growing and taking up little space.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ sweet potatoes ni akɛ tsei bibii, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ intercropping lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ ji nifeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋaa. Ye obua oweku lɛ ni amɛná niyenii kɛ shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso titri lɛ miida lolo ni eheɔ he ko fioo pɛ.

english: Will growing yams alongside other crops on the same land ruin the soil nutrients for my main plantation?
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe Ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mi abɔɔ wulu lɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Growing multiple crops uses soil nutrients, but as long as you clear weeds, leave adequate space between plants, and return plant remains or compost to the soil, the land can comfortably feed both yams and young plantation trees.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi be fɛɛ be ni obaajie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni okɛ tsei ni eshwɛ loo ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ yɛ hejɔlɛ mli.

english: Why do yam tubers stay safe underground for a long time without rotting before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbooo dani akumɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers act as natural storage organs designed by the plant to store energy underground. As long as the soil stays well-drained and free from pests, the tuber remains preserved alive in the soil until harvest.
ga: Sweet potato tubers tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni tso lɛ fee koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ. Tubers lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa.

english: What crops can I plant on my farm to get quick food to eat within a few months while waiting for my main crops to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná niyenii oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Short-term food crops like maize, leafy vegetables, cassava, and cowpeas mature quickly within 3 to 6 months, ensuring your household has food while long-term plantation crops are establishing.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 mli, ni ebaaha oshia lɛ ana niyenii yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ miida.

english: How do I know the right month to begin harvesting my crops so they don't spoil in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa akɛ mabɔi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpamɔ? Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops show distinct signs when ready for harvest, such as leaves changing color, stems drying out, or fruit reaching full size. Knowing the maturity timeline of your crop variety helps you harvest right on time before pests or rains cause damage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kɛji amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ, tamɔ baai ni tsakeɔ, tsei ni egbi, loo aduawai ni dalɛ fa. Kɛ́ ole be ni otso srɔtoi lɛ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okpa yɛ be naa dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo nugbɔ abafite.

english: How can I plan my farm schedule so I have food and income throughout the entire year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni maná niyenii kɛ shika afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can mix short-term crops (vegetables and maize), medium-term crops (cassava and yams), and long-term tree crops. This staggering allows you to harvest food and earn money continuously across different months of the year.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ afutu. (aduawai kɛ ŋmãa), ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be teŋgbɛ (cassava kɛ sweet potatoes), kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli (aduawai kɛ ŋmãa). Nɛkɛ naakpɛɛ nii nɛɛ haa oyaa nɔ okpaa niyenii ni onáa shika yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient plants need to grow. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ koolooi a-ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha amɛdalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Beans and cowpeas have special roots that grab nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop finishes growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as a natural fertilizer for the next crop, like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛbaafee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ Shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are all the small flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Migbee shi kɛjɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔko cocoa ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells, lack of nutrients, or attacks by pests like mirids. Maintaining shade trees to retain moisture and feeding the trees helps them keep their flowers to form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛhao kɛjɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ atatu ni haa amɛhe lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ he hulutsoo koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko, ni aha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛ pod lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them top-heavy. Supporting the stems with strong wooden prop poles helps keep them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. make it top heavy Tso ni wa ni akɛfiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ?

english: Yam leaves need full sunlight to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunshine and keeps them off damp soil where diseases spread easily.
ga: Hulu ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice need to stand in shallow water while growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ adamɔ nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water smothers weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice for space and food, while providing the continuous moisture that lowland rice needs to produce full grains.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi ni baanyɛ atswa akaŋ kɛha he ko kɛ niyenii lɛ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ni he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by a disease in the ground that blocks the plant's water tubes. Changing the crop location every season instead of planting tomatoes in the same spot stops this disease from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu paipii lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. He ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aduɔ tomato yɛ he kome. Ebaaye ebua ni hela nɛɛ akabua ehe naa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed in the tender center funnel of young maize plants. Checking fields early and applying appropriate remedies directly into the leaf funnel stops them before they destroy the main growing point.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Kwɛmɔ hei ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mra ni akɛ tsofa ni sa lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsĩ amɛnaa dani amɛfite he titri ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and causing the whole plant to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tso muu lɛ fɛɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck the sap out of young leaves and pass on plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and allows the plant to grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ yaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: I see many millipedes crawling around my cocoa farm; are they eating my crops or helping my soil?
ga: Mina millipedes babaoo ni miiho kɛmiibɔle he. mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ Ani amɛmiiye miŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Millipedes mostly feed on dead leaves and rotting plant matter, which helps turn farm waste into rich natural soil. However, if there are too many of them, they can sometimes bite young crop seedlings, so keep the base of young plants clear.
ga: Millipedes yeɔ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ni egboi lɛ babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ mli jwɛi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Shi, kɛji akɛ eyɛ babaoo Bei komɛi lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛye dumɔwui bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aha tso bibioo lɛ shishi afee faŋŋ.

english: I sprayed pesticide on my farm, but the insects are still alive. Why is the medicine not working?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ efɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi kooloo lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo. Mɛni hewɔ tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ?

english: Chemicals can fail if they are mixed with too much water, applied at the wrong time of day, or if the pests have hard shells that shield them. Using the correct dosage and spraying early in the morning when insects are active gives the best result.
ga: Tsofai baanyɛ afite kɛji akɛ akɛ nu babaoo futu mli, akɛwo mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli, loo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni wa ni buɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ okɛ falɛ ni sa tsu nii ni okɛshwie nɔ leebi be mli ni kooloi bibii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it important to cut off the extra small branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni fata he kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ he miihia.

english: Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach inside the tree canopy. This keeps damp fungal diseases away and forces the tree to spend its energy growing big, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli edɔ naa lɛ naa, ni enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ni mli wa.

english: My cocoa tree produces many flowers, but most drop off before turning into pods. What is causing this?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii babaoo. Shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pods. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop extra flowers they cannot support, but heavy flower drop can mean the tree lacks water or nutrients, or is being attacked by tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids.
ga: Taakɛ eji lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi krɛdɛɛi ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii kpakpai. loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and overgrown farms. Clearing weeds, pruning dense shade leaves, and removing black pods early stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔji ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmeii diji ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Can dirty cutlasses and harvesting tools spread sickness between my cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni akɛfoɔ nibii kɛ nibii ni akɛkpaa nibii ni he tseee lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes. When you cut a diseased tree, fungal germs stick to the blade. If you cut a healthy tree next, the germs enter the fresh wound and infect the healthy plant.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛji ofo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ Fungus baakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛji oya nɔ ofo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ pilamɔi heei amli ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I store my dried cocoa in bags without insects destroying them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ kookoo ni egbi awo kotokui amli ni kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ?

english: Make sure your cocoa beans are thoroughly dried before bagging, and seal them tightly in airtight hermetic storage bags. These bags cut off oxygen, preventing insects from surviving without needing harmful chemical treatments.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku mli. ni akɛwo vacuum kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ. Nɛkɛ kotokui nɛɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Is it safe to leave old cocoa pod husks near my trees as fertilizer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii momo yɛ tsei ahe akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Decomposed husks return valuable nutrients to the soil, but fresh or diseased husks placed close to tree trunks can trap moisture and spread black pod fungus. Always heap them away from the tree bases.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmãa ni afee ehee loo hela emɔ ni akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli ni egbɛ black pod fungus lɛ eshwa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛto he kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do crops in drier areas of the Bono Ahafo region need extra soil cover like dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ Bono Ahafo kpokpaa lɛ nɔ hei ni nu bɛ lɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mli tamɔ baai ni egboi lɛ?

english: Dry soils lose moisture quickly under hot weather. Covering the soil around plants with dry leaves or mulch acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and holding water for crop roots longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If my neighbor's farm has pests, how do I prevent them from crawling onto my farm?
ga: Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pests travel through touching tree branches and high weeds along farm borders. Clear a clean boundary strip along your farm edge and trim touching branches to create an open space pests cannot easily cross.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsɔɔ tsei aniji kɛ jwɛi kakadaji amli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ ahe. Tsɔɔmɔ husui ni he tse yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa. Ni ŋmɔmɔ tsei niji ni taa amɛhe lɛ koni efee hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛŋ afo mli mlɛo.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my oil palm bunches so the nuts do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mu tsei akui lɛ? Koni ŋmeii lɛ akafite

english: Oil palm bunches are ready when a few loose orange fruits fall to the ground on their own. Harvesting when the bunch turns bright orange-red ensures you get the maximum amount of high-quality palm oil.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo beni ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbee shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okpa ŋmei lɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ, ebaaha oná ŋmei fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ babaoo.

english: Why do my oil palm trees produce so much more fruit late in the year, around October to December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ lɛ? Aaafee October kɛyashi December?

english: Oil palm fruit yields depend heavily on the rainfall patterns from several months earlier. Rain received during the primary rainy season helps develop the fruit bunches that ripen toward the final months of the year.
ga: Mu tso yibii ni anáa lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nyɔji komɛi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ nɔ waa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai akui ni shwereɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: How often in a year should I go through my palm farm to harvest ripe bunches?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ afi mli koni mayakpa tsei akui ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Because oil palm bunches ripen at different times, a farm should ideally be harvested every 10 to 14 days so that no fruit is left to over-ripen on the tree.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mu tsei akui lɛ shwereɔ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Esa akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ akpa nii daa gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 koni aduawai babaoo akashwɛ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens to my palm fruit bunches if I leave them unharvested on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-palm aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni mikpaaa lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe bunches on the tree causes the fruits to rot and increases their free fatty acid levels, which ruins the oil quality. It also attracts pests like rodents and beetles that can damage future harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi panicles ni eshɛko yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa free fatty acid ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baafite fɔ lɛ mlihilɛ. Egbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii hu. ni baanyɛ afite nibii ni abaafee wɔsɛɛ lɛ

english: Can having too many heavy fruit bunches at once weaken my oil palm tree for the next season?
ga: Ani aduawai ni tsii babaoo ni miyɔɔ shikome lɛ baaha mi-oil palm tso lɛ agbɔjɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, producing a huge crop takes a lot of energy and nutrients from the tree. If the soil isn't replenished with fertilizer or organic matter, the tree may enter a rest period and produce very little fruit the following year.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ biɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ tsei amli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Tso lɛ baanyɛ abote wɔɔhe be mli ni ewo yibii fioo ko pɛ yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are some of the palm nuts dropping off the bunch before they are fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ mli dani amɛdaraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop is usually caused by intense dry spells, lack of nutrients like potassium in the soil, or poor pollination when the tree was flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ oya baa ji ni amɛgbi waa. Niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo pollination ni ehiii beni tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do harvested palm nuts start to spoil so quickly if I don't process them into oil right away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji mikɛtsuuu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni efeee mu lɛ?

english: Once a bunch is cut from the tree, natural enzymes immediately start breaking down the fat inside the fruit. Warm weather accelerates this process, so nuts should ideally be processed within 48 hours of harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli enzymes lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa fɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu ŋmeii ahe nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does the oil I extract from late-year harvests feel thicker than oil extracted during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fe mu ni mijieɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fruits harvested during drier months carry less water and a higher concentration of pure oil compared to fruits harvested during heavy rains, making the extracted oil denser.
ga: Nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ aduawai ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ amli, ni mu ni atsake mli lɛ fa babaoo yɛ aduawai ni akpaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he. Ehaa mu ni ajieɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some of my palm fruit bunches look full but have many small, empty nuts inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii lɛ ekomɛi tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyi obɔ shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty or undeveloped nuts occur when flowers are not properly pollinated, often due to a low population of pollinating insects like the oil palm weevil or extreme drought during flowering.
ga: Beans ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni edako jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni feɔ pollen, tamɔ oil palm weevil lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How many years after planting should my young oil palm tree start producing fruit bunches?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni mi-oil palm tso lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Improved oil palm varieties typically start flowering and producing their first small bunches between 2 to 3 years after field planting, reaching full production by their fifth year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii bibii. Klɛŋklɛŋ be ni yɔɔ afii 2 kɛ 3 teŋ beni adu nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ. ni ebaada yɛ afi ni ji enumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea will turn the leaves green and help the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and soft while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo beni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads in high humidity and heavy shade during rainy weather. Pruning extra tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow, along with removing infected pods quickly, stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Agbɛnɛ hu Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up with light yellow and green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus carried by tiny whitefly insects. You cannot cure an infected plant, so the best step is to clear affected plants and plant disease-resistant cassava varieties.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii kɛbaa. Onyɛŋ otsa tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and collapse during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, where tiny organisms block water from traveling up inside the stem. You should remove and destroy the affected plants immediately so the infection does not spread through the soil to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. he ni nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yɔɔ lɛ Tsĩɔ nu naa koni ekaya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ojie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures are too high or when the soil goes through sudden dry spells. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass (mulching) helps keep the roots cool and moist so the flowers can turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi trukaa Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) baawo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ afee aduawai.

english: Why is my maize producing flowers when the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ ji kukuji lɛ?

english: Maize flowers early when it faces severe stress from dry weather or poor soil early in its growth. The plant panics and tries to produce seeds before it dies, which can be avoided by planting at the very start of the rains and feeding the soil.
ga: Abɛi baawo fɔfɔi mra kɛji akɛ ekɛ haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii mli lɛ kpe yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Tso lɛ he feɔ gbeyei ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo dumɔwui dani egbo. Abaanyɛ ajie enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shishijee mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii nɔ.

english: Why are my yams rotting underground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when rainwater stays around them in heavy soil for too long, encouraging soil fungi to attack. Planting your yams on high mounds or raised ridges helps water drain away easily and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu bɔle amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ekanyaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni amɛtutua Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni eha yitso lɛ mli egbi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees keep falling over when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily if underground pests like stem weevils or worms eat away their roots, weakening their grip in the dirt. Planting clean, pest-free suckers and supporting heavy fruiting trees with wooden props keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ agbo oya kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ stem weevils loo ŋmeii ŋmɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi Dumɔ tsei ni he tse Ebɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ asɛɛ kɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei lɛ asɛɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Why do small insects turn my stored dry maize into powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsakeɔ mi-abele ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize weevils invade harvested corn, laying eggs inside the grains and eating them from the inside out. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard before storage and using sealed, airtight bags prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Abele ŋmei lɛ tutuaa abele ni akpa lɛ. Amɛwoɔ wɔji yɛ dumɔwui amli ni amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Akɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ ewaa kwraa dani akɛtoɔ Ni akɛ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ atsu nii koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafee babaoo.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds under my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and plant food from the soil that your cocoa trees need to grow strong. Clearing weeds also removes dark, damp hiding places where harmful pests and diseases can multiply.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu jieɔ hei ni efɔ ni edɔ ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui baanyɛ afɔ́ yɛ lɛ.

english: Can tall grass growing under my cocoa trees attract dangerous insects to my crop?
ga: Ani jwɛi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tsei ashishi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, overgrown grass creates a wet and shaded environment that attracts pests like capsids and bugs that feed on young cocoa pods and weaken the trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baa, ni no gbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if I trim off some of the extra branches?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mifo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Trimming or pruning opens up the tree canopy to let sunlight and fresh air reach the stem and pods, which stops black pod disease from spreading and helps bigger cocoa pods grow.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni cocoa pods lɛ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when their tops become overcrowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ eyiteŋ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: When cocoa branches are too thick and crowded, sunlight cannot reach the trunk where flowers grow, preventing those flowers from turning into full cocoa pods.
ga: Beni kookoo niji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ. Hulu la po nyɛŋ ashɛ tsei ni fɔfɔii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ eyiŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Should I weed under my cocoa trees before or after I spray chemicals on them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ dani mikɛ tsofai afɔ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ loo beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should always weed before spraying so the chemical reaches the bark and soil directly rather than getting wasted on grass and weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsofai lɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshɛrɛ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ashwie lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees need chemical spraying even if they look healthy right now?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofai afɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ bianɛ moŋ, shi.

english: Chemical sprays act like preventive medicine that protects young pods from hidden insects and fungal diseases before visible damage occurs.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa ni buɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii ahe helai ahe dani nɔ ko ni anaa lɛ baafite.

english: How does clearing dead leaves and branches help the spraying chemicals work better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Removing dead leaves and trimmed branches ensures that sprays land directly on the trunks and pods where insects and fungi live.
ga: Baai ni egboi kɛ tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baagbee tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ tsei ahe tɛ̃ɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii hiɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to complete farm cleaning quickly within a few days instead of spreading it out over weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbe ŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ naa oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ? moŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ ashwãa otsii babaoo amli.

english: Doing farm tasks quickly prevents pests and diseases from moving from untreated areas of your farm to the parts you have already cleaned.
ga: Kɛ́ otsu nii oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni atsuuu he nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛya hei ni otsumɔ momo lɛ.

english: What basic steps should I follow on my farm before the main cocoa crop season starts?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Before the main season begins, you should clear underbrush, trim dead branches, and inspect your trees so they are clean and healthy enough to support a full harvest.
ga: Dani be titri lɛ baaje shishi Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Ni okwɛ otsei lɛ amli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛhe tse ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha kpamɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do different varieties of cocoa trees produce pods at different times on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei srɔtoi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different cocoa varieties react differently to rain and sunlight, causing some to produce most of their crop in the main season while others bear fruit during minor seasons.
ga: Cocoa henɔi srɔtoi lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa kookoo henɔi komɛi feɔ amɛnibii babaoo yɛ be titri lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants need extra fertilizer when they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he kɛji ebɔi fɔfɔii lɛ?

english: Just like a pregnant animal needs extra food, crop plants need more nutrients when they start flowering and producing seeds or fruits because most of their energy goes into building the yield.
ga: Taakɛ kooloo fɛɛ kooloo ni hiɛ musu he hiaa niyenii kroko lɛ. Niyenii nibii babaoo hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai lɛ. Ejaakɛ amɛ hewalɛ babaoo yaa yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛfeɔ nibii.

english: What happens if I do not feed my pepper plants when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ haaa amɛ niyenii beni amɛbɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: If pepper plants do not get enough nutrients while producing fruit, the peppers will remain small, drop off early, or the plant will become weak because it spent all its stored energy without getting replenished.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni ewoɔ yibii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baakã he afee bibioo, ebaagbee shi oya, loo tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ ejaakɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ fɛɛ etsu nii ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to add fertilizer to my yam crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi sweet potato tsei lɛ amli?

english: The best time is early in the season when the leaves begin growing vigorously, and again when the plants start forming tubers under the ground to ensure maximum energy goes into growing big yams.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be lɛ shishijee be mli ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa waa lɛ. Ni agbɛnɛ hu, kɛ́ tsei lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ana akɛ akɛ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛmɔ mli.

english: Can I mix my leftover corn husks and rotten fruits to make food for my soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ afutu aduawai ni egboi koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ shikpɔŋ niyenii?

english: Yes, mixing and rotting leftover plant material, fruit scraps, and corn husks creates rich compost. Adding this to your soil gives crops natural food that improves their growth and helps the soil retain water.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe nibii, aduawai amli nibii ni efite, kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni akɛfutuɔ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ enɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa amɛdaraa babaoo, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli.

english: Is rice bran or corn waste good to spread around the roots of my vegetables?
ga: Ani ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mishishifãi lɛ fɛɛ amli?

english: Yes, spreading agricultural waste like rice bran or corn husks around the base of plants acts as mulch. It traps moisture in the soil, keeps weeds down, and slowly breaks down into nutrients for your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli mli jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa ni ajaa kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I combine animal manure with crop waste to use on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ kooloi ashishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi afata he koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, mixing animal manure with crop husks and fruit waste creates a balanced organic fertilizer. It enriches the soil structure and slowly feeds your crops throughout the growing season.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloo ŋmei ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii lɛ haa ŋmei ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii fiofio yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are getting enough nutrients from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can monitor their health by checking leaf color and stem thickness. Healthy trees have dark green leaves and strong stems, while pale yellow leaves and thin stems mean the tree lacks nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ ehewalɛ kɛtsɔ baa lɛ su kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ tsei ni mli wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei bibii tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young plantain suckers turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or it is getting too much or too little water. Checking the soil moisture and feeding the soil can help restore green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo eyɛ nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants slow down their growth during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daaa fioo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants slow down their growth during dry periods to conserve energy and survive the heat. Adding organic cover around their roots helps keep the soil moist so they can keep growing.
ga: Cassava tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough food to grow good tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tomato kpakpa akwɛ̃?

english: If your tomato plants grow thick stems and deep green leaves early on, the soil is fertile. If the plants remain small, weak, or pale, the soil lacks food and needs manure or compost added.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ mra lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii. Kɛji tso lɛ ji bibioo, ebɛ hewalɛ, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same piece of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the specific soil nutrients maize relies on and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive and easily get burnt by direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist until the cocoa trees are strong enough.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ nuɔ he waa, ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What happens if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli?

english: When pepper plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with fewer peppers, and makes it easier for plant diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ shwere tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground into the sun and prevents leaves from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akafɔ ni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without growing into fruits when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and dries up the flower pollen. When flowers are not pollinated, the plant drops them to save its limited water and energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ fioo ko he.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to turn soft and rot if heavy rain stays on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the farm, air cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and decay.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: What is eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants overnight and leaving behind small holes?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome ni eshi bu bibii?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot during the day and feeds on the tender leaves at night. Early spraying or applying neem extract helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii gbɛkɛ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛtsu nii mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ

english: Curling yellow leaves on cassava are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow much faster if I clear weeds when the crops are tiny compared to weeding later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kwraa kɛji mijie jwɛi be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lɛ kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni mijie yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight right when young crops need them most. Removing weeds early allows crop roots to spread without any competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi ni aduɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. The plant naturally moves available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting beans or groundnuts in my farm make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants die or are harvested, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil and acts as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei gboi loo akpa amɛ Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral infections spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills all air spaces in the soil with water, the cassava roots cannot breathe. This excessive moisture allows fungi and bacteria to grow rapidly, causing the tubers to decay.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine nɛɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ daa oya. ha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why do the leaves of my crops roll up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihoso yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural protection mechanism. Plants roll their leaves during intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which conserves moisture and prevents drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ baai babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during severe dry periods to reduce water loss through leaf pores. It is a survival strategy to keep the main trunk and branches alive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi waa lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ aba shi. Eji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa yiwalaheremɔ koni akɛha tso lɛ shishi kɛ eniji wuji lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miikwɛ ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when stressed by extreme temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. The plant drops the flowers to save energy when conditions are not right for fruit production.
ga: Tomato baafɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa tsɔ hao lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ ehiii kɛha aduawai afeemɔ.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposes them fully to sunlight so they can feed the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ awo hulu la ni mli kwɔ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs.

english: Why should I remove extra young shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers allows them to steal water and soil nutrients from the main stem. Removing extra suckers leaves only the strongest ones, ensuring the main plant produces large fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni amɛje kpo lɛ, ehaa amɛjuɔ nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ baashi. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the seedlings compete intensely for limited sunlight, air, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall and thin instead of developing thick, sturdy stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa fioo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii ni mli wa ni mli wa.

english: Is fresh cow dung good to put directly on my crops, or will it damage them?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaafite?

english: Fresh cow dung generates too much heat as it decomposes, which can burn plant roots and damage young crops. It is best to let it dry and break down into compost for a few weeks before applying it to your farm.
ga: Tsina ŋmei hee jieɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii bibii Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha egbi ni egbɛ eshwa ni efee ŋmɔshi nibii otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛtsu nii yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow better and stay greener when I put dried animal waste around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi wo amɛhe lɛ?

english: Dried animal waste acts as a natural fertilizer rich in nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. It feeds the beneficial living organisms in the earth and helps the soil hold moisture for root growth.
ga: Nibii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium eyi mli obɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ niyenii, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli koni shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: How long should I wait after gathering cow dung before I can safely use it on my vegetables?
ga: Kɛ́ mibua tsina ŋmei naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani mikɛtsu nii shweshweeshwe yɛ aduawai anɔ?

english: You should leave gathered dung to decompose in a pile for about 1 to 3 months. Once it turns dark, cool, and earthy-smelling without a strong foul odor, it is fully composted and safe for crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni abua naa lɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmei mli nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 3, beni amɛtsɔ duŋ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa bɛ mli lɛ. Ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni ebaafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Can I mix building cement into my farm soil to make the ground firmer for planting?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsumaa simenti afutu shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui?

english: No, cement hardens soil into a solid block, preventing crop roots from spreading and stopping water from draining properly. Healthy plant soil needs to be soft and airy, enriched with manure or compost rather than building materials.
ga: Dabi, simenti haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa ni etsɔɔ blɔkii ni wa. Ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ tso shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli. yɛ tsumaa he nibii najiaŋ

english: How do I know if my soil needs cow dung or compost before I clear my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsina ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: If your soil turns dusty, light in color, dry quickly after rain, or forms hard crusts, it lacks organic matter. Adding cow dung helps rebuild nutrient levels and keeps the soil spongy and moist.
ga: Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ sũ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. loo ŋshɔŋloo ko ni wa baa Tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. Tsina ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can using unwashed animal manure on my crops introduce diseases to my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni afɔɔɔ he ni mikɛaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, improperly handled or raw manure can spread fungal spores, bacteria, and weed seeds to your crop field. Composting manure thoroughly generates natural heat that kills off these crop pathogens before application.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛtsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbɛ fungal spores, bacteria, kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Komposting ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ ni haa nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ gboiɔ dani akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why is it important for me to clean the livestock pen every morning before collecting manure for the crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsumɔ mi kooloi atsu lɛ mli daa leebi dani mabua ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ anaa lɛ?

english: Daily cleaning prevents flies, bad bacteria, and pests from breeding in wet waste. Keeping the manure pile clean ensures you are carrying healthy organic matter to your crops instead of dangerous rot.
ga: Daa gbi he saamɔ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akabote mli. bacteria gbohii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni mli ewo fɔ mli lɛ amli. O-compost pile lɛ ni oookwɛ koni ehe atse lɛ haa ona nɔmimaa akɛ okɛ nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ miiwo onibii amli. Mohu ɔ, e ji fitemi nɛ ngɛ oslaa.

english: Should I pour cow dung directly onto plant leaves or apply it at the base of the plant?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔse tsina ŋmɔtɔ awo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛwo shishigbɛ?

english: Always place manure on the soil around the base or root zone of the plant. Applying heavy manure directly onto tender leaves can cause leaf scorch, mold growth, or rot.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifã he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo baai bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Fungus lɛ daa loo efiteɔ oya

english: Are there new modern ways to process cow dung instead of just carrying it in a wheelbarrow to the crop field?
ga: Ani gbɛi heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ lɛ yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ tsina ŋmei he nii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ shwiili baawo mli kɛkɛ kɛya ŋmɔji amli?

english: Yes, modern practices include turning cow dung into liquid manure tea, mixing it with crop residue for accelerated composting, or using biodigesters to create rich bio-slurry fertilizer alongside clean biogas energy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi lɛ ekomɛi ji tsina ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ awoɔ ŋmei tii mli nu mli. Okɛ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ afutu mli koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Aloo okɛ nɔ ko ni fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afee nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa ni akɛ biogas hewalɛ ni he tse fata he.

english: What is the best way to store gathered cow dung during the rainy season so it doesn't lose its power?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ abua tsina ŋmei naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ni nijiaŋ ejeee wui?

english: If rain washes over an exposed manure pile, essential nutrients like nitrogen wash away into the ground. Covering the heap with a tarpaulin or keeping it under a simple thatch roof preserves its fertilizing power.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ anɔ lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ hu hoɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tarp ha ŋtayaa lɛ he loo okɛto jwɛi ni akɛfee ŋtayaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my weed killer destroy some weeds on my farm but leave others untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, shi eshiɔ ekrokomɛi hu ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Different weed killers are formulated for specific plant types. Some target broadleaf weeds, while others target grasses, meaning a single spray will not burn every variety of weed on your field.
ga: Afee tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko pɔtɛɛ aha tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ. Ekomɛi ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi kɛ amɛhiɛ fɔɔ jwɛi nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, tsofa kome ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shãŋ jwɛi srɔtoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ oyale mli lɛ.

english: What causes certain weeds on my field to stay green even after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni haa jwɛi komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Some weeds have thick, waxy leaf coatings or deep root systems that prevent standard chemical sprays from entering the plant, making them naturally resistant to basic weed killers.
ga: Jwɛi komɛi yɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ wax loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni tsiɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ naa koni ekabote tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyeɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some weeds dry up quickly after spraying while others take a long time to die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi komɛi gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi heɔ be babaoo dani amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Contact weed killers burn the visible leaves immediately upon contact, while systemic chemicals work slowly by absorbing into the plant to destroy the roots from the inside out.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtswaa mɔ he lɛ shãa baai ni anaa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ eshɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii blɛoo. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli ni eeebote mli koni efite shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ emli kɛya kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does spraying weed killer sometimes only burn the top leaves without killing the whole weed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ ni egbeee jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: If a chemical is not strong enough or isn't absorbed into the roots, it only burns the surface leaves, allowing the underground root system to sprout new growth soon after.
ga: Kɛji tsofai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa loo eboteee shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Ebaashã baai lɛ ahiɛ pɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ.

english: Why do broadleaf weeds need a different chemical spray than grass weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ biɔ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi anɔ fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Broadleaf weeds and grasses have different internal structures and leaf surfaces, so specific chemicals like 2,4-D are designed to attack broad leaves without damaging grass-like crops like maize.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ yɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, afee tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko, ni ji 2,4-D lɛ koni etutua baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ ni eyeee tsei ni tamɔ jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ awui.

english: What is 2,4-D chemical, and when should I use it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofa ni ji 2,4-D lɛ ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: 2,4-D is a selective chemical herbicide used specifically to control tough broadleaf weeds without harming grassy crops like maize, millet, or rice.
ga: 2,4-D ji tsofa ko ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii pɔtɛɛ koni akɛkudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai ni mli wa lɛ. ni eyeee jwɛi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa awui

english: Is there one single weed killer that can clear all types of weeds on my farm at once?
ga: Ani tsofa kome pɛ yɛ ni baanyɛ agbe jwɛi srɔtoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shikome?

english: No single chemical effectively destroys every type of weed safely. You often need to mix or use specific treatments depending on whether you are fighting soft grasses or tough broadleaf plants.
ga: Tsofa kome pɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ akpata jwɛi srɔtoi fɛɛ ahiɛ shweshweeshwe. Bei pii lɛ, ehe bahiaa ni okɛ tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi afutu loo okɛtsu nii. Edamɔ kɛji okɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli wa miiwu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I sometimes need to clear paths into the middle of my dense farm before applying chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ ehe hiaa ni mafo gbɛ ko mli kɛya ŋmɔ ko ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ tsofai awo mli lɛ?

english: Thick growth can block spraying nozzles from reaching inner weeds, so physically opening paths ensures the chemical directly hits every targeted plant.
ga: Nɔ ni yaa hiɛ waa lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe, no hewɔ lɛ, gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛ ni agbeleɔ lɛ haa tsofa lɛ tswaa tso fɛɛ tso ni akɛmamɔ ehiɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How do I know which chemical to buy when I have many different kinds of weeds growing together?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni esa akɛ mahe beni miyɛ jwɛi srɔtoi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: You must inspect your field to see if the main problem is broadleaf weeds or grasses; identifying the dominant weed type tells you whether you need a general or selective weed killer.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli koni ona kɛji naagba titri ni yɔɔ mli ji jwɛi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo. Kɛ́ oyɔse jwɛi ni yeɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔɔ bo kɛji akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afɔɔ feemɔ loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ he miihia bo.

english: What should I do if weeds in the center of my farm plot are too thick for my spray to reach?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli eyi tsɔ ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he?

english: You must manually cut a way into the dense areas to apply stronger specialized chemicals directly to the stems and lower leaves of those tough weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ onine afo gbɛ kɛya hei ni mɛi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ koni okɛ tsofai krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo awo nakai jwɛi ni wa lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishi baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and produce big cobs, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage will help the crop recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea tsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant groundnuts together with my maize, will they steal food from the maize plants?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa Ani amɛbaaju niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli?

english: No, groundnuts actually help feed the maize. Groundnuts are legumes, meaning they take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which acts like a natural fertilizer for the maize.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ekɛ ŋmãa yeɔ nii. Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava bushes curling up and showing yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whitefly insects. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by agricultural officers is the best way to prevent this and get a full harvest.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi etsɔɔ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nibii ni anáa lɛ anaa ni akwɛɔ koni aná nibii babaoo.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical pest controls on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You should spray early in the morning or late in the evening. During these cooler times, there is less wind to blow the spray away, the hot sun won't dry it out too fast, and you avoid harming beneficial insects like bees.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ fɛ̃i be ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ mlɛo akɛ ebaatswa spray lɛ kɛya. Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haŋ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ni okpa kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ awuiyeli.

english: Why do weeds reduce my crop yields even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they aggressively pull water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the plant's life gives your crop full access to food and water.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli—amɛkɛ yiwalɛ shwieɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain next to young cocoa creates living umbrellas that provide the shade and moisture the seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa dumɔwui lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: If I bury my maize seeds very deep in the ground, will they grow stronger roots?
ga: Kɛ mifu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani shishifãi lɛ baawa?

english: No, planting seeds too deep uses up all their stored energy before they can push up through the soil into the sunlight. Planting at a shallow depth of about two finger-joints allows seeds to sprout fast and stay healthy.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ dani ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ aaafee niji enyɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if the soil has enough moisture for planting after the early rains begin?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a ball of soil in your hand: if it holds its shape without dripping water and easily crumbles when touched, it is ready. If it breaks apart into dry dust, wait for more rain before planting so your seeds do not dry out.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ oniji amli: kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni efooo ni efoɔ oya kɛji ota he lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo. Kɛji efo mli ni etsɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ Mɛɛ nugbɔ babaoo dani odu. koni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rot before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and adding compost helps the tomato fruits grow healthy.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be, ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otomatoi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams soften and rot quickly after I store them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya ni egboɔ kɛ́ akɛto he lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when they are wounded during harvest or stored in hot, unventilated places. Storing undamaged yams on raised racks in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them cool and prevents decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ epila yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto hei ni edɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ atomo ni efiteko lɛ ato adekai ni awó nɔ yɛ tsũ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ ni ehaaa efite.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize grow better the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground through their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil to nourish the next maize crop naturally.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil runs out of nitrogen, which is the main plant food used to grow big green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring back their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi. ni ji niyenii titri ni jɛɔ tsei ni akɛduɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to sprout if I plant them very deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: A seed only has a small amount of stored energy inside it. If buried too deep, the young shoot exhausts all its energy trying to push through the heavy soil before reaching the sunlight.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ dani amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he.

english: Fall armyworms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the plant during hot days and feed aggressively at night when it is cool, making the damage seem like it happened all at once.
ga: Fall worms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni amɛyeɔ nii waa gbɛkɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Ehaa nɔ ni efite lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eba shikome.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when there is heavy, prolonged rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the field without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing harmful fungi to grow and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji amli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ daa ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without forming any fruit during hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High heat stresses tomato plants and prevents pollen from fertilizing the flowers. The plant naturally sheds these unfertilized blossoms to save its energy until cooler weather returns.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ nɛɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my cocoa trees curl up and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?
