english: Dry Harmattan winds suck water out of leaves faster than the roots can pull moisture from dry soil. The cocoa tree sheds its leaves on purpose to reduce water loss and survive the dry spell.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger in my field than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested maize grains completely in the sun before putting them in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani mikɛwo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Moisture inside harvested grain creates the perfect environment for mold and destructive bugs like weevils to multiply. Sun-drying hardens the grain and protects your harvest from rotting.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii ni ji ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ bii. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ebuɔ onibii ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new ones, showing you it needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛye baai heei. Etsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why should I plow my farm before planting instead of just clearing the weeds and planting directly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu miŋmɔ lɛ he nii dani madu nii? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi jwɛi kɛkɛ ni odu tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Plowing loosens hard soil so crop roots can easily push deep down for food and water. It also buries weeds and allows rainwater to soak into the ground instead of washing your topsoil away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya koni amɛyana niyenii kɛ nu. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes right in the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Those are likely fall armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed on the sweet, tender growing point of maize. If not treated early, they can destroy the main stem and stop the plant from producing cobs.
ga: Ekolɛ amɛji cutworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ ni mli jɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra Ebaanyɛ efite tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ni eha tso lɛ akafee cob.

english: Why gives better yield when I buy certified seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mihe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist local diseases, tolerate drought, and grow uniformly. Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and often yield smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛnyɛŋ amɛye maŋ lɛ mli helai anɔ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ ni edaa be fɛɛ be Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ baa shi kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli ni bei pii lɛ amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and skinny with small fruits when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space. Proper spacing ensures each individual plant gets enough food and light to produce strong stems and big fruits.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji.

english: Why is it bad to plant cassava on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the ground and lets crop-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating crops like cassava with legumes helps replenish nutrients naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ amɛhe, tamɔ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmeii ewo mli lɛ, haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crop yield more when the plants are young compared to when they are full-grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui waa beni amɛdara fe be mli ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young crops need all available sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to build their roots and stems. If weeds compete with them early on, the crop gets stunted and cannot fully recover even if you weed later.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ taoɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ koni amɛfee shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo akaŋshii mli mra lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ehiɛ kpaaa nɔ kwraa kɛji okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie nɔ sɛɛ mli po.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into little rolls during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii lɛ? Yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism pepper plants use to protect themselves from intense heat. Shrinking their leaf surface area stops moisture from evaporating too quickly out of the plant.
ga: Leaf curling ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil and grow mold inside storage bags even when the bags are sealed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ atsĩ kotoku lɛ naa moŋ?

english: If maize is bagged before it is completely dry, trapped moisture creates heat and humidity inside the bag. This creates the perfect environment for mold to grow and storage pests like weevils to multiply.
ga: Kɛji akɛ awo ŋmãa lɛ kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ bii.

english: How can I tell if insects are damaging my crops before I actually see the insects?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite miŋmɔshi nibii dani mana amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Insects often leave early signs like tiny holes in leaves, sticky residue, curled leaf tips, or wilting stems. Regularly turning leaves over to inspect the undersides helps you catch pest invasions early before major damage occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ mra be mli okadii, tamɔ bu bibii yɛ baai amli, nibii ni eshwɛ ni shwieɔ shi, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni ebɔle ehe, loo tsei ni egbo. Kɛ́ otsake baai lɛ daa koni okwɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mra. dani nɔ ko ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli baafite

english: Why didn't the chemical spray kill all the pests on my farm after I sprayed it just once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ shikome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pest treatments often require a follow-up application because sprays usually kill adult insects but leave behind unhatched eggs. Applying a second treatment after the eggs hatch breaks the insect life cycle completely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe tsamɔ biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ fɔɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ agbemɔ shi eshiɔ ŋmeii ni efoko. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ji enyɔ tsu nii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ efɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ wala shihilɛ kwraa.

english: Why are tiny green insects gathering under the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miibua amɛhe naa yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: These are likely aphids, small insects that suck sap from the plant and weaken it. They hide under leaves to shield themselves from direct sun and heavy rain, so applying treatments beneath the leaves is necessary to reach them.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii ji enɛɛmɛi. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ ni ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant drains nutrients from its older leaves to feed the younger top leaves, signaling that your soil needs fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei jieɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if my tomato plants are just thirsty or if they actually need plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kumai miiye mi-tomato tsei lɛ kɛkɛ loo amɛmiitao tsei niyenii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If plants only need water, they wilt during hot afternoon hours but revive by evening. If they lack nutrients, their leaves permanently change color, grow slowly, or produce weak stems even when the soil has adequate moisture.
ga: Kɛji nu pɛ he miihia tso lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. shi abaatee amɛ shi gbɛkɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ faaa lɛ Baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ daa, amɛdaraa blɛoo, loo ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do my yam plants produce big leafy vines but only small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai wuji yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii pɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into leaf growth rather than stem tubers. Yams require balanced nutrients containing phosphorus and potassium to encourage large tuber growth under the ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli yɛ stem bulbs lɛ najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni eha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees scorch and wither under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living shields until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ adamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ naa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ gãimlibi kɛha wala kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flower dropping occurs when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plants helps the flowers stay attached and produce peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa waa ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ahaa tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cassava leaves fall off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry harmattan conditions as a natural survival mechanism to conserve water. Once the rainy season returns, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ harmattan gbimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu he. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I inspect my crops every few days even when the farm looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli daa gbii fioo komɛi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ po lɛ?

english: Regular farm inspections help you spot early signs of trouble like insect eggs, emerging weeds, or nutrient deficiencies before they spread widely. Detecting issues early makes treatment much easier and less expensive.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona naagbai ahe okadii mra, tamɔ kooloi bibii kɛ jwɛi ni miiba lɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa dani egbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he Naagbai ni anaa mra Enɛ haa helatsamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa ni ejara hu waaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily damaged by full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that create living shade to protect the young cocoa plants and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with food that the maize needs to grow big and strong.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa lɛ adara ni ewa lɛ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, saving water inside its stem so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baa koni ekagbi.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that targets young maize. They hide inside the center whorl of the plant where it is soft and moist to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbeɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli he ni amɛyɔɔ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted cassava after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe ŋmei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the local environment with tough root systems. They react immediately to rain to soak up water and nutrients faster than newly planted farm crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Amɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ koni amɛhe nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme hot weather, too much water, or too little water. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ haomɔ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu babaoo, loo nu fioo pɛ kpe amɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: What will happen if I plant my tomato seeds too close to each other in the bed?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu tomato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso nɔ?

english: When tomatoes grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This competition leaves them tall, weak, and thin, leading to poor yields and smaller fruits.
ga: Beni Tomatoi Daa Amɛbɛŋkɛɔ He Tsɔ Tomatoi kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested cocoa beans directly on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Drying cocoa directly on bare dirt allows soil moisture, mold, pests, and dirt to ruin the beans. Raised drying mats keep the beans clean, dry them evenly, and preserve quality for better selling prices.
ga: Cocoa ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmeii, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ muji baa kɔfi yibii lɛ anɔ. Mat ni awo nɔ ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ haa kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe tseɔ. ŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekwɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛha jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ

english: Why should I cover the ground around my yam mounds with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋtayaa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds moisture near the yam roots and prevents heavy rains from washing away topsoil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves often mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant steals remaining food from its oldest, bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ juɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark and filling up with watery liquid inside instead of healthy beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋ ni nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually a sign of Black Pod disease, a fungal infection spread by heavy rain and high humidity. The fungus attacks the pod wall, causing the inside to rot into liquid and destroying the beans.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni hulutsoo be babaoo ba. Fungus tutuaa pod gbogboi lɛ. Enɛ haa emli lɛ fiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nu ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I know if a sick plant on my farm can still be saved or if it is completely ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ abaanyɛ ahere tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yiwala loo akpata ehiɛ kwraa?

english: Check the stem and roots: if the inner stem is still green and roots are firm, the plant can often recover with proper care. If the root system is black, soft, and rotten, the plant is completely ruined and should be removed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ: Kɛji tso lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, tsei baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ yɛ ediŋŋ, bɔdɔɔ, ni egbo lɛ, no lɛ tso lɛ efite kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ.

english: Why do some farmers hang up harvested maize cobs or pods under open sheds after picking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋmãa loo toi ni akpa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa ni agbele naa lɛ shishi beni amɛkpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hanging crops in open, warm areas improves air circulation around them, which dries off remaining moisture, prevents mold growth, and preserves seeds for the next season.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ onibii lɛ fĩ he ko ni mli edɔ ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fungal dalɛ naa ni ekwɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What causes my tomatoes to turn soft and watery inside before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Watery and soft tomatoes often suffer from calcium deficiency or irregular watering, where the plant absorbs too much water at once, causing internal tissue to break down.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni nu yɔɔ mli ni eyɛ blɛoo lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. He ni tso lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ. ni haa fãji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ

english: If a plant in my field dies completely from a disease, should I leave it to rot in the soil?
ga: Kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboi kwraa yɛ hela hewɔ Ani Esa akɛ maha egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: No, completely ruined or diseased plants should be carefully uprooted and destroyed away from the farm. Leaving them in the field allows diseases to spread to healthy surrounding crops.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ajie tsei ni efite loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akpata amɛhiɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft, watery, and spoiled when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo, nu yɔɔ mli ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive soil water deprives cassava roots of oxygen, leading to root rot. Poor drainage causes the tubers to absorb too much water and rot underground.
ga: Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I test if the seeds I saved from last season are still good for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo akɛ adu?

english: You can perform a simple germination test by wrapping 10 seeds in a wet cloth for a few days; if 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and ready for planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni oookɛwo mama ni mli efɔ mli gbii 2-3 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ adu.

english: Why does my watermelon harvest end up watery and tasteless instead of sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ mli nu ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Watermelons become watery and tasteless when given too much nitrogen fertilizer or excess water right before harvest, which dilutes the fruit's natural sugars.
ga: Watermelon lɛ bafeɔ nu ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nu babaoo dani akpa. Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli sugars ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ afee mlɛo.

english: What happens to my crops when rainwater stays standing on my field for several days?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo?

english: Standing water suffocates crop roots by cutting off oxygen, causing leaves to yellow and roots to decay, which eventually destroys the crop if drainage paths are not created.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Enɛ baafite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ naagbee kɛji akɛ afeee gbɛi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess humidity and soggy soil create ideal conditions for fungal leaf spots and root rot, which stress the pepper plant and cause it to drop yellowing leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ haa shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha baa he muji kɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ. Enɛ baaha pepper tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni eha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer around the base of the plant helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii awoɔ he fɛɛ he. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my okra plants grow huge leaves but very little fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra lɛ baai wuji shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes okra to spend all its energy growing big leaves instead of flowering. Switching to balanced nutrients or adding phosphorus helps the plant focus on producing pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha okra lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Niyenii ni ja loo fɔsfɔs ni yaa hiɛ lɛ nɔ tsakemɔ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when heavy rain stays on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater gets trapped and waterlogs the soil, the roots suffocate and rot-causing organisms quickly break them down.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya.

english: Dry Harmattan winds and strong sun pull water out of cocoa leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the dry soil. Young cocoa trees need shade trees planted nearby to shield them from excessive sun and wind.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni adu tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves shred into thin ribbons during strong winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miigba kɛmiitsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli

english: Plantain leaves split naturally along their veins when strong winds blow so that air passes through easily. This prevents the heavy wind from snapping the trunk or pulling the plant out of the ground.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ ji koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akafo tso lɛ shishi loo egbala tso lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering because the plant gets stressed and tries to save energy rather than form new fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei lɛ miihao ni amɛmiitao ni amɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why does my harvested maize crop have missing grains on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when dry weather or high heat damages the maize silk during pollination. If the silks cannot receive pollen, the corresponding kernels fail to form on the cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa fite ŋmãa siliki yɛ pollination be mli. Kɛji akɛ siliki lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná pollen Dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe yeɔ tsakpaa lɛ efeee yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling upward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled, tiny pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids. Controlling these insects early prevents them from spreading leaf-curling viruses to the rest of your farm.
ga: pepper baai bibii Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ hela ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi lɛ.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from around my young crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients directly from your young crops, which stunts their growth and leads to small harvests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa dalɛ aya hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmaa fioo pɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need poles to lift their leaves up toward the sunlight. Staked vines catch more light to produce food, which is then sent underground to grow large, healthy tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Wein tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ la babaoo koni ekɛfee niyenii. Akɛ enɛɛmɛi yaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulb agboi ni he wa.

english: How long does it take for a plantain crop to produce fruit after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains usually take about 9 to 12 months to produce a flower shoot, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully mature and be ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi, ni eheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Is plantain farming profitable enough to support my family if I do not have a government job?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ plantain abɔɔ mli nitsumɔ he bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ miweku lɛ nɔ kɛji mibɛ nɔyeli nitsumɔ?

english: Yes, plantain farming has high market demand in Ghana and provides continuous yields through offshoots, making it a reliable full-time source of income to pay for household expenses and school fees.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain okwaayeli he miihia waa yɛ Ghana ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii anɔ. Enɛ haa anáa be fɛɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shia shika kɛ skul nyɔmɔ.

english: What kind of soil do I need on my land to grow healthy plantains?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ he hiaa mi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni manyɛ makwɛ plantains ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: Plantains grow best in deep, rich, well-drained soil with plenty of organic material, such as compost or decayed leaves, and good moisture retention.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ amɛmli, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni miigboi. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ

english: How do plantain plants reproduce if I cannot buy seeds to plant them?
ga: Te dumɔwui baafee tɛŋŋ amɛfɔ kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe dumɔwui ni mikɛkwɛ amɛ?

english: Plantains do not grow from seeds; instead, they grow from underground stems that produce young shoots called suckers, which can be separated and planted as new trees.
ga: Plantains jɛɛɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛ̃ɔ. Mohu ɔ, e wa kɛ jeɔ tso ko nɛ ngɛ zugba sisi nɛ e woɔ ngma bibihi nɛ a tsɛɛ ke ngma a mi. ni abaanyɛ agbala mli ni adu akɛ tso hee

english: How many young shoots should I allow to grow around one main plantain tree?
ga: Esa akɛ maŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei bibii enyiɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he?

english: It is best to leave only 2 to 3 healthy suckers of different heights around the main plant so they do not steal nutrients from each other, ensuring a steady harvest over time.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsei 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhe kwɔlɛ srɔtoi yɛ tso titri lɛ he koni amɛkaye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afeɔ lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Can I grow plantains alongside other cash crops like cocoa on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains kɛfata shika he nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ kookoo he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, plantains are commonly planted with young cocoa trees because their large leaves provide temporary shade to protect young cocoa plants from harsh sunlight while giving you income.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, akɛ cacao tsei bibii duɔ plantains ejaakɛ amɛbaai wuji lɛ haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko koni ebu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa shika hu.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my plantain plant turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves can turn yellow due to natural aging, lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or diseases like Panama disease, which affects how water moves through the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ, nu ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, loo helai tamɔ Panama hela, ni saa nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantain bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain lɛ?

english: Harvest when the individual plantains look plump and rounded rather than angular, and when the dark dried flowers at the tips easily rub off, while the peel is still green.
ga: Kpamɔ be mli ni plantain fɛɛ plantain feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ egbi lɛ, eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ajieɔ su ni tsuɔ nii yɛ amɛnaa lɛ. be mli ni ŋshɔŋloo lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ

english: How do plantain plants behave during the dry season, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te plantains feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and slow down growth during dry spells; covering the soil around the base with dry leaves or mulch helps keep the moisture in the ground.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni ehaa amɛdalɛ baa shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when there is heavy wind, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Plantains have heavy bunches and shallow roots that make them top-heavy; propping up the fruiting stems with strong wooden poles or bamboo prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ jwɛi ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi aduawai lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Which food crops is the government currently encouraging farmers to plant for quick yields and good market prices?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii nɔyeli ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ woɔ okwaafoi hewalɛ koni amɛdu koni amɛná yibiiwoo oya kɛ jara kpakpa?

english: The government promotes crops like maize, rice, soybeans, tomatoes, and onions under national farming initiatives because they mature fast, support local food security, and have strong, consistent market demand.
ga: Nɔyeli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, soybeans, tomato, kɛ ŋmãa he hewalɛ yɛ National Agriculture Initiative lɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ tsei daa oya Fiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ ni jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yɛ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ aya nɔ akwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell when my okra is ready to harvest so it stays tender enough for cooking soup?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ okra lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni eyɛ blɛoo lolo bɔ ni sa kɛha shwiili?

english: Okra should be harvested while the pods are young, soft, and about finger-length. If you bend the tip of the pod and it snaps off easily, it is fresh and ideal for cooking.
ga: Esa akɛ akpa okra be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni amɛlɛɛmɔ aaafee inchi kome. Kɛ́ otsi pod lɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaaje kpo mlɛo. Ebaafee ehee ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking nutrients from under the leaves. Neem oil or mild insecticidal soaps sprayed on the leaves can clear them up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni afɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my garden egg fruits rot from the bottom while they are still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite kɛmiijɛ shishi be mli ni amɛmiida yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Bottom rot in garden eggs is caused by a shortage of calcium in the plant, which often happens when watering is irregular. Consistent watering helps the plant move calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ashishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso yibii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out small and watery instead of big and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee wuji ni amɛmli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava needs loose, well-drained soil and adequate sunlight to build up starch in its roots. Planting in waterlogged soil or harvesting too early prevents the tubers from developing fully.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse he miihia cassava. Etsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee starch yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ yɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi bulb lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shweremɔ he.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen or the roots are trapped in waterlogged soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it good to plant maize and cowpea together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, planting maize and cowpeas together benefits both crops. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil to feed the maize, while the tall maize stalks provide natural support for cowpea vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ lɛ, yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛfiɔ cowpea wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ.

english: When is the right time of day to apply fertilizer to my crops so it does not burn them?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni shãa akafee?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer early in the morning or late in the afternoon when the weather is cool and the soil is moist. Applying fertilizer under direct, hot sunlight can burn the roots and leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from weevils without using dangerous chemicals?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara tsuuu nii?

english: Make sure the maize is thoroughly dried in the sun until the grains are very hard before storing. Storing the dry grains in airtight hermetic bags starves pests of oxygen and prevents weevil damage naturally.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ hulu lɛ egbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ana kɔɔyɔɔ fioo. ni atsĩ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anaa

english: Why should I plant my maize in neat rows instead of scattering the seeds randomly across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ fɛo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooogbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa lɛ

english: Planting in straight rows makes it much easier to weed, apply fertilizer, and walk through your farm. It also ensures every plant gets equal sunlight and enough room to grow large cobs without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni abaatsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa, ni he ko hu yɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their leaves block sunlight from reaching one another and their roots fight for underground space and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, small tubers instead of large ones.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo moŋ fe agboi.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when I leave weeds to cover the ground around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mishiɔ jwɛi koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping your farm clean of weeds allows your crops to take in all the nourishment they need to grow strong and produce well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off dry and diseased branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji ni egbi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Removing dead or infected branches stops pests and fungal diseases like black pod from spreading to healthy pods, keeping the whole farm clean and protecting your harvest.
ga: Niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli atse ni obu onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They need temporary shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantains to keep them cool and preserve moisture around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young vegetables with dry leaves or grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material keeps the ground cool and slows down water evaporation, helping your young plants stay hydrated and survive hot weather.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa odumɔwui lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that water is drowning the roots. Adding organic manure or proper fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu miiha shishifãi lɛ miiho. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same land alongside my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, growing leguminous crops like beans with maize is helpful because beans trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds and strengthens the maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and rot whenever rainwater stays pooled around their stems for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nu baabua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plant roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water sits around the roots for too long without draining, the roots suffocate and rot, causing the plant to wilt and die.
ga: Pepper tso shishifãi lɛ hia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu bɔle shishifãi ahe be kakadaŋŋ ni nu shwieee lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every year if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land without break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin stems and tiny or empty cobs, yielding less harvest overall than properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dense tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. loo efolo Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and ensures the plant gets enough sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs wuji ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast and turn hard like rock after just two days without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya ni efeɔ shiŋŋ tamɔ tɛsaa lɛ?

english: Soil turns hard and dry quickly when it lacks organic matter like rotted compost, animal manure, or dry leaf mulch. Adding organic material acts like a sponge, helping the ground hold water much longer during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ baanyɛ afee shiŋŋ ni egbi oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfataa he lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted chicken manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaai lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo tsina ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps prevent this.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ enɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I apply strong chemical fertilizer at the exact same time I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Applying chemical fertilizer directly against raw seeds or tender shoots can burn and destroy the delicate young roots. Fertilizer works best when applied a few weeks after germinating or placed in a small trench a few inches away from the plant stem.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɛɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni efite amɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ loo akɛwo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. No ji inchi fioo ko kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when the sun gets very bright in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight when their root systems are small. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava around them creates shade and keeps the air humid, protecting the seedlings.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ faaa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. koni akɛbu dumɔwui lɛ ahe

english: Why do my crops fail to grow if I plant right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ kɛji midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a heat wave or dry period before the real rains begin. If seeds sprout during this dry gap, the tender young roots dry out and die under the hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ateŋ Shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What is causing all these small ragged holes in the leaves and center whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ baai kɛ amɛteŋgbɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant's leaves during the day. Early spraying with appropriate bio-pesticides or neem extract can control them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ baai amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmei ni miida lɛ.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, signaled by the leaves starting to turn yellow and drop off naturally. You can test maturity by carefully digging up just one tuber near the surface to check its size before harvesting the full plant.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Okadii lɛ ji akɛ, baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni edara ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ bulb kome ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ bɔ ni elɛɛmɔ ji dani okpa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and scorch easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade trees to act as living umbrellas, keeping the air moist and soil cool until their root systems grow strong enough to handle full heat.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ amli baawa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ la ni tsoɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main element crops use to build green leaves; when the soil runs out, the plant steals nitrogen from its oldest leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Eji nɔ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwie shi lɛ, tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to scatter dry fertilizer on top of dry soil when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ magbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops cannot eat dry fertilizer directly; plant roots can only drink nutrients dissolved in water, so fertilizer applied on dry land stays useless on top of the ground or burns plant tissues.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu niyenii ni mli ewo nu mli pɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ mli fãji ashã.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava seeds very close together so I can get more food out of my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ? mi nɔ babaoo

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block each other from sunlight, resulting in thin plants and tiny, poor tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulb bibii bibii baa.

english: Why do all the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get stressed by high heat or irregular watering, which causes the stem connecting the flower to dry up and snap off before pollination can happen.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfoɔ dani pollination baa.

english: Why do small armyworms attack the young hidden leaves inside the maize stalk instead of the outer leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ tutuaa baa bibii ni akɛtee ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ moŋ fe baa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ?

english: The center leaves inside the stalk are softest for young caterpillars to chew, and hiding deep inside the plant protects them from heat, heavy rain, and birds.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye. Ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ tee tsei lɛ amli tɔ̃ɔ lɛ, ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my farm than the maize and cassava I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛ hiɛdɔɔ duɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted over thousands of years to survive harsh weather and nutrient-poor soil, allowing them to drink up groundwater and grow long before planted crops catch up.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa kɛ shikpɔji ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛdaraa be kakadaŋŋ dani tsei ni miida lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why does cutting off the extra shoots growing at the bottom of my plantain plant give me bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa mifeɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck water and food away from the main mother plant; cutting them leaves all the soil nutrients for the main plant to build one large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo lɛ, ehaa sũ mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ feɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker if I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop relies on and allows soil diseases and pests that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the hot afternoon sun and open back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli, ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up during hot afternoons to reduce their surface area, helping the plant trap moisture and prevent water from evaporating into the dry air during the hottest hours.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and start curling when there is no rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: When crops do not get enough water, they close their leaf pores to conserve moisture and cannot draw up soil nutrients properly, which causes the leaves to turn yellow and wilt from stress.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Eŋaa baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛjɛɔ haomɔ mli.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives the soil time to absorb the moisture before the sun gets too hot, preventing water from evaporating into the air before the plant roots can drink it.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to survive if I cut down all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛji mifo tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees act as a shield, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can establish strong roots without burning.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji haa hɔnɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa ni ashãaa amɛ.

english: Why does maize grow tall and green on one side of my farm but stay short and yellowish on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi fã kroko lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ?

english: Soil quality is not the same across an entire field; some areas have fewer plant nutrients or hold too much water, causing plants in those spots to starve and stay small compared to plants in richer soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hei komɛi yɛ ni tsei amli niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ nakai hei lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ yɔɔ nii babaoo nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my soil is good enough to plant vegetables without using expensive testing tools?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai ni mikɛ kaa nibii ni jara wa tsuuu nii?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark in color, smells fresh like rain, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture without becoming swampy, and contains living creatures like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ hee tamɔ nugbɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ

english: Will I get more harvest if I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe? Koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Planting too close actually reduces your total harvest because the plants end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small or empty fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei baatswa akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves get white powdery spots and turn sticky during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Powdery spots and stickiness are signs of sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or whiteflies, which multiply rapidly in hot, dry weather and feed on the plant's juices.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo whiteflies lɛ he okadi. Amɛfɔɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni amɛye nu ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ akɛ niyenii

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotten before they even get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering or dry spells during fruit formation.
ga: Shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why is my pepper plant producing plenty of green leaves but dropping all its flowers without making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewooo pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them grow lots of leaves, but they need phosphorus and balanced nutrients to keep their flowers and convert them into fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná baai babaoo. Shi fɔsfɔs kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛkwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsake amɛfee aduawai.

english: Why do some of the seeds I plant fail to come up out of the dirt even after I water the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Seeds may fail to sprout if they were buried too deep for the tiny shoot to reach the surface, if the soil was packed down too hard, or if too much water caused the seed to rot before it could grow.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ kɛha ŋmeii bibii. baakwɛ̃ Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Aloo kɛji nu babaoo ha dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to plant shade crops like plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ madu tso ko ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantain yɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Fast-growing plantains act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow bottom leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and strong, so it starves its older bottom leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ koni eye ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do my elders advise me to plant cowpea or groundnuts before planting maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii dani adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the ground with fertilizer for heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Lifting the vines up on stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which helps the plant store more energy and make larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo toɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee wuji

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Giving cassava too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant spend all its energy building stems and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to grow thick roots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen wo o-cassava lɛ mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ baa si konɛ e ha nɛ shishifã ɔmɛ nɛ a pee tsɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes and dark dirt inside the upper leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Muji ni egbɛ eshwa ni edɔ yɛ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ aŋwɛi baai lɛ amli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing shoot of the maize plant and eats the soft new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing after small insects visit them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ beni kooloi bibii ebasara amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies carry viruses that they pass into the pepper plant when they feed. These viruses stop the leaves from expanding normally and reduce fruit production.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies hiɛɔ helai ni amɛtsɔɔ mli kɛyaa pepper tsei anɔ kɛ amɛyeɔ nii. Nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã bɔ ni sa, ni ehaa aduawai ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: The first rain often creates a hot, humid atmosphere in dry soil, followed by a dry spell. Planting too early can burn fragile seedlings before the rainy season fully settles.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. ni hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba naagbee.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without growing any fruit during very hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures dry out and kill the pollen inside tomato flowers. Without live pollen, the flowers cannot get fertilized to form tomatoes, so the plant drops them.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛji akɛ pollen ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka bɛ lɛ Anyɛɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi awo mli koni efee tomato. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shi lɛ.

english: Why do my garden vegetables wilt in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In intense sun, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can drink from the soil. The leaves temporarily droop to conserve moisture and usually recover when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he, ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, ehaa amɛhe feɔ shoo.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil food. Maize moves available nutrients to its newest upper leaves first, leaving the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Abele tsiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Ha ni shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and weak roots that cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects them from drying out until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni eshɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ he.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops droop and wilt in the afternoon heat even when it rained a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mibɛ amɛ lɛ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose moisture into the air faster than the roots can take up water from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to save water, but usually recover in the evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, baai lɛ fiteɔ nu ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛɔ shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too high or when there is sudden water stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the unproductive flower to preserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ loo kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi ni wooo yibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do the bottoms of my ripening tomatoes turn dark brown and rot during heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom-end rot, happens when irregular water supply prevents the plant from moving calcium to the growing fruit, causing the tissue at the bottom of the tomato to collapse.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ baa kɛji nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ tsi tso lɛ naa koni ekajie calcium kɛya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ tomato lɛ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juices out of young leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ niyenii lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale green and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with crops for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients. When weeds are not cleared early, they steal essential food from your crops, leaving them weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ beni ajieee jwɛi lɛ mra Amɛbaaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ onibii amli. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over when I plant three or four seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ fee ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting too many seeds close together forces the plants to fight each other for root space and sunlight. This causes them to stretch upwards rapidly, resulting in thin, weak stems that break easily in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ hulu la. Ehaa ehiɛɔ shi oya Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli tse ni ebɛ hewalɛ, ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, efoɔ oya.

english: Why do I need to construct stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ma tso kɛha mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to convert sunlight into food energy. Raising the vines on stakes exposes more leaves to light and keeps them off the damp soil, reducing disease exposure and increasing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsake hulu la lɛ ewo niyenii hewalɛ mli. Wein tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ yibii lɛ aná la babaoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni oha yitso lɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and drying up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily in full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby provides a living umbrella that shields the cocoa seedlings and keeps the soil moist until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and getting pale yellow patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This curling and yellowing is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease damages the leaves' ability to capture sunlight, which stops the plant from growing large tubers underground.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ mli. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni baai lɛ yɔɔ ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ akwɛ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are there holes in my maize leaves and small green drops inside the growing tops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? yɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli
