english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest eating the central leaves of your young maize. The green drops are its waste, and if left untreated, the pest will destroy the growing point before corn cobs can form.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ obi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ. Abuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akɛ jwɛi. ni kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Pests fiteɔ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ dani ŋmãa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on this natural nitrogen fertilizer left behind.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does the chemical fertilizer I put on my crops seem to disappear without helping when a heavy rain falls right after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ laaje ni yelikɛbuamɔ ko bɛ he beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy downpours wash away fertilizer from the topsoil before plant roots have time to drink it in. Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is already moist, but not right before heavy rainstorms that carry nutrients away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ afeɔ enɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛya lɛ aba.

english: Why do my yam vines need high wooden poles to climb on if the tubers grow under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the plant using direct sunlight. Lifting the vines off the soil with stakes spreads the leaves out so they catch maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to make huge tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. ni tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo

english: Why do my plantain plants easily blow over and fall to the ground when strong winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over when pests like root nematodes attack their underground roots, or when too many suckers are left growing around one main stem, making the root system too weak to hold the heavy plant balance.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ tutua amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. aloo be mli ni ashi ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. single main trunk Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso ni tsii lɛ afee ekome.

english: Why are the small flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, flat rotten spots on the bottom side as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato aduawai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ tomato lɛ shishi kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium while the fruit is forming. It usually happens when watering is irregular, because roots need steady soil moisture to carry calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni faaa yɛ tso yibii lɛ mli lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛ calcium awo aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my rice fields need to be flooded or kept very wet while the plants are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ nu atsɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli loo edɔ waa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rice roots need consistent water during the flowering stage to keep the pollen active and transport nutrients into the head. Dry soil at flowering causes empty, papery grain heads.
ga: Nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ omɔ shishifãi amli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ koni eha pollen lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya bulb lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afee efolo ni amɛfee tamɔ wolo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for growth. The plant takes whatever nitrogen it has left from its older lower leaves and sends it up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei lɛ heɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli ni amɛtsuɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with big leaves, but the tubers in the ground are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer or soil nutrients without enough potassium, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my corn even when I planted the seeds in clean soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly grab light, water, and food from the soil faster than domestic crops can. Their seeds can also stay dormant in the dirt for years waiting for the right moment to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe oya kɛha la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fe shia tsei. Edumɔwui lɛ hu baanyɛ afee nɔ ni wɔɔ. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni amɛmiimɛ be ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct heat from the sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally feed and enrich the soil for heavy-feeding crops like maize without relying entirely on bought fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ aye niyenii ni amɛha efee shweremɔ kɛha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛkɛ amɛhe efɔɔɔ ŋmãa ni aheɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer right before a very heavy rain comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away off the surface of your farm or pushes it too deep down into the dirt where the crop roots cannot reach it, wasting your money and crop food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe loo ebaatsi kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Efiteɔ shika kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ.

english: Why does covering the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass help them during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks the harsh sunlight from drying out the ground. It keeps moisture locked in the dirt and keeps the crop's roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ muji mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my small green cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they can even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy or humid conditions when moisture stays on the pods for too long.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i lɛ baahi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking extra branches from my cocoa tree give me more pods later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ haa mináa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded branches so air and sunlight can flow through the tree. Sunlight helps flowers form into pods, and better airflow keeps fungal diseases from staying wet on the branches.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni mli ewo wu lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni mli efɔ ni baa tsei aniji anɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upward and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viruses. The virus disturbs the plant's normal growth, causing the leaves to curl and stunt plant development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Virus tsiɔ tsei adalɛ ni sa lɛ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the leaves of my young maize plants, and how does it affect my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the leaves and growing tips of maize. If left untreated, they destroy the plant's leaves, preventing it from converting sunlight into food, which severely reduces your final yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baai kɛ eshishigbɛ. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Ebaakpata tso lɛ baai lɛ ahiɛ. Tsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ niyenii Enɛ baaha onaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key food maize needs to build strong stems and leafy growth. Adding fertilizer like NPK or Urea early in the season feeds the plant and stops the yellowing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛma ŋmãa ni wa kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii ni ekpa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How far apart should I plant my maize seeds, and why does spacing matter?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔtsi wɔhe kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: Planting maize seeds about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between stands ensures each plant gets enough light, water, and soil nutrients without fighting neighboring plants, leading to bigger cobs.
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni aduɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 75 yɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ateŋ kɛ sɛntimitai 40 yɛ ŋtayaai ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu ni ekɛ ŋmei ni da fe no baa

english: Why do my maize plants need so much water when they start showing silks and tassels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa nu babaoo nɛkɛ beni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛjieɔ siliki kɛ ŋmeii akpo lɛ?

english: The silk and tassel stage is when the plant is forming grains on the cob. If maize suffers from dry soil during this flowering period, many grains will not develop, leaving you with empty or partially filled cobs.
ga: Silk kɛ tassel stage lɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ miiwo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa piŋɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli Dumɔwui babaoo shwereŋ. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmei ni nɔ ko bɛ mli loo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do hybrid maize seeds yield more than the seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid corn dumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to combine strong qualities like high yield and drought resistance. Replanting seeds saved from last year loses those combined strengths, resulting in uneven growth and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni akɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo kɛ hɔmɔ ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ nii lɛ afata he. Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaha amɛhewalɛ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ afite. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Is it helpful to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil, acting as natural food for your maize while also covering the ground to prevent weeds and retain soil moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shwiemɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi akabote mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is my young maize growing so slowly even though the rains are good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds growing alongside your maize are stealing the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crop. Clearing weeds during the first month allows young maize roots to grow deep without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ o-ŋma lɛ masɛi lɛ miiju nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: What causes my tall maize plants to fall over during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni haa mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: This is called lodging, which happens when roots are too shallow, plants are overcrowded, or stalks are weakened by pests. Strong winds can easily blow top-heavy plants down if root anchoring is poor.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ abobaahe. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Tsei lɛ eyi tsɔ. aloo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ egbɔjɔ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahewɔ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shwieɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ anɔ oya kɛji shishifãi lɛ fioo pɛ fiɔ tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Insects called grain weevils burrow into dried maize to lay eggs, and their larvae eat the grain from the inside. Properly drying your maize and storing it in airtight bags protects it from these pests.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ shwieɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli koni amɛwo wɔji. Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mligbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo vacuum kotokui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why should I plow or loosen the soil deeply before planting maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mafee lɛ mlibotemɔ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil makes it easy for young maize roots to penetrate deep underground to collect moisture and anchor the plant firmly, leading to faster initial growth and better drought survival.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmãa bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni amɛbua ŋmɔtɔ naa ni amɛfi tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, abele bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting plantain together with young cocoa seedlings on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni akɛ kookoo tsei bibii ewo mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants grow rapidly and produce wide leaves that provide essential shade to delicate young cocoa seedlings, protecting them from harsh sunlight and soil drying out while they establish roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛhaa baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ naa hɔɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi he be mli ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller fruit bunches when planted under dense mature shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Plantains require direct sunlight and heavy soil nutrients to grow large bunches; thick tree canopies block essential light and roots compete for soil moisture, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Plantains he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni tsii koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ jwɛi wuji. Tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ he miihia la ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Will planting plantain alongside cocoa reduce the amount of cocoa my land produces in the long run?
ga: Ani plantains ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ baaha kookoo ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: In the early years, plantain actually helps cocoa survive through shade. However, if plantains are not thinned out once cocoa trees mature, they will compete for soil nutrients and water, reducing overall cocoa yields.
ga: Yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ, plantains yeɔ ebuaa kookoo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ ajieee plantains lɛ bibii be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ, Amɛbaatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, kookoo ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Why do farmers grow plantain alongside cocoa if plantain sells for less money in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ plantain yɛ kookoo masɛi kɛji amɛbaanyɛ amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni waaa nɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa takes three to five years to produce its first harvest. Growing plantain provides immediate food and short-term household income while you wait for the main cocoa crop to mature.
ga: Cocoa heɔ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani eshɛɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ he. Plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ shia shika ni heɔ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni omɛɛɔ cacao tsei titrii lɛ ni amɛdara lɛ.

english: How do large shade trees help protect cocoa farms during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Bɔ ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ buɔ Harmattan kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ he yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ

english: Large shade trees reduce extreme heat stress on cocoa leaves, lower moisture loss from the soil, and act as windbreaks against hot, dry winds that cause leaves to drop.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hulutsoo ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni baa kookoo baai anɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ tsɔne ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black or rot when there are too many plantain trees crowded around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo amɛgboɔ beni plantain tsei babaoo ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Overcrowding creates too much shade and traps moist air around the crops, creating a wet environment that causes fungal diseases like black pod rot to spread rapidly.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa tsɔ ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How does plantain vegetation help keep the soil cool and moist for other nearby crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantain tsei yeɔ ebuaa koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves create a thick ground shade that blocks direct solar heat, and their fleshy stems store large amounts of water that naturally release moisture into the surrounding air and upper soil layer.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ loo lɛ toɔ nu babaoo. ni jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: When is the correct time for me to remove plantain plants from my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ majie dumɔwui kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli?

english: You should start cutting back plantain plants around three to four years after planting, when the cocoa trees develop a full leaf canopy that can shade and protect itself.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ aaafee afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ yɛ be mli ni odu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ fee ŋwɛitsu ni eyi obɔ lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hebuu.

english: Will plantain trees steal the fertilizer I apply to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaju ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, plantains have shallow, aggressive root systems that will quickly absorb fertilizer. You should apply fertilizer directly around the drip line of the cocoa tree rather than broadcasting it between rows.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ehe tɛ̃ɛ. Cocoa tso lɛ drip line lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmɔji ateŋ

english: Why do mature cocoa trees need full sunlight once they are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni hulutsoo be fɛɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ kɛji amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he lɛ?

english: Mature cocoa trees use sunlight to power flower production and pod development. While young trees need shade to survive, adult trees need more sunlight to generate high pod yields.
ga: Cacao tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii koni amɛha fɔfɔii afeemɔ kɛ pod lɛ aya hiɛ. yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni eda lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee pod babaoo.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get holes and turn into dust when I store them in sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli bu ni etsɔɔ sũ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Pests like maize weevils lay eggs inside the grains. When the eggs hatch, the larvae eat the inside of the maize, leaving empty shells and powder. Properly drying the maize until it is hard and using clean, airtight storage prevents these insects from multiplying.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli niyenii. Nɔ ni eshwɛ ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ kɛ powda ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ pɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaawa Ni akɛ he ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ atsu nii koni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafee babaoo.

english: How can I tell if my harvested beans are dry enough to store without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-beans ni mikpa lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛto ni efiteee?

english: You can perform a simple salt or bite test: press a bean with your fingernail or bite it gently. If it leaves a dent, the bean still holds water and will rot in storage; if it is hard and does not dent, it is dry enough for bagging.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee ŋmei loo ŋmei he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛtsɔ onineshi ni ooonyɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ loo ŋmei ni oooye fioo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii ba lɛ, Kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ baahiɛ nu mli lolo ni amɛbaafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ewa ni ebɛ ŋmeii lɛ, no lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ awo kotoku mli.

english: Why do my stored bean grains attract tiny black insects after just a few weeks in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikɛto lɛ gbalaa kooloi diji bibii lɛ? Beni otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ehi kotoku lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ

english: Bean bruchids (weevils) often lay tiny eggs on bean pods while they are still growing in the field. Once you harvest and put the beans in warm storage sacks, those eggs hatch into insects that eat through your stored crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii (ŋmei) fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ beni amɛdaraa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lolo lɛ. Beni okpaa ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ woɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli. Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ onibii ni okɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn moldy and stick together inside the sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe yɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This happens when maize is bagged while it still contains internal moisture, or if the sacks are placed directly on a cold floor. Trapped moisture encourages fungi to grow, causing the grains to heat up, stick together, and rot.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo kotoku mli be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli lolo. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ kotoku lɛ fɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔtɔ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃. Ha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ adɔ waa Kpɛtɛ he ni egbo.

english: Why shouldn't I mix freshly harvested maize with old dry maize in the same bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ futuɔ ŋmãa momo ni egbi yɛ kotoku kome mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize carries high moisture that quickly transfers to the dry maize. Mixing them creates a damp environment inside the sack, causing the entire batch to develop mold and attract grain borers.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni etsɔɔ oya kɛyaa abɛi ni egbi lɛ amli. Nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kuu muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbalaa dumɔwui ni shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for green leaf growth. It often occurs after heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize is planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes thin, weak stalks and produces very small cobs with incomplete rows of grain.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa ni ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Why does planting beans in the same field as maize help my maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans are legumes, which means they take nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into a soil fertilizer. The nearby maize roots feed on this extra nitrogen, making the maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans ji ŋmeii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Ehaa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs have missing grains or gaps on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Gaps on a cob happen when the maize silk does not receive enough pollen during flowering. Dry weather or extreme heat when the silks emerge can dry them out before pollen hits them, leaving empty spots on the cob.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmei siliki lɛ enine shɛɛɛ pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa beni siliki lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ baanyɛ aha siliki lɛ agbi dani pollen lɛ anyɛ atswa siliki lɛ. Enɛ haa he ko ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ko baa yɛ ŋmei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages the bean plant to focus all its energy on producing lush leaves instead of flowers and pods. Excessive shade or over-fertilizing can trigger this behavior.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii. Shade babaoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ ajie subaŋ nɛɛ kpo.

english: Why does my plantain plant die after it produces only one bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gboiɔ beni amɛwo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and bear fruit just once. Once the bunch matures, the main stem naturally dies so that all the plant's food and energy can move down into the subterranean rootstock to feed the young sucker shoots growing around it.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ gboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ anyɛ aya shi kɛya shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã lɛ nɔ koni eyaha ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose water very quickly in hot weather. When water in the soil becomes scarce, the plant rolls its leaves to reduce sun exposure and drops older leaves to save moisture for its core stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ baai momoi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛto ŋmɔtɔ he kɛha shishigbɛ.

english: Why do plantain plants easily fall down when heavy rain and wind blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unlike big trees, plantains do not have deep taproots; they rely on shallow root systems near the topsoil. When the bunch becomes heavy, the high center of gravity makes the plant top-heavy, so strong winds can easily pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless you support the stem with a wooden prop.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ tsei wuji lɛ, plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛdamɔɔ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ anɔ. Beni kuu lɛ jeɔ shishi ehaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ Hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni nɔ kwɔ haa tso lɛ tsiimɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Ejeɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo Ja okɛ tso fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantains take much longer to mature during the cold Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani eshɛɔ yɛ Cold Harmattan lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains rely on warm temperatures to process nutrients and grow. The cold nights and dry, hazy days of the Harmattan slow down the plant's internal metabolism, which delays leaf growth, flowering, and fruit filling.
ga: Plantains kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo be nɔ koni amɛtsu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii ahe nii ni amɛdara. Harmattan gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli kɛ gbii ni mli egbi ni afua yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ, fɔfɔi, kɛ aduawai ni eyiɔ obɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do plantains perform better in forest regions like Asante Akyem than in very dry areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ tamɔ Asante Akyem fe hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants are heavy consumers of water and organic matter. Forest regions offer deep, rich, moist soils and consistent rainfall, which keep the plant's succulent stem hydrated and fully supplied with nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui yeɔ nu kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Koo lɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni mli efɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni enáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do I get smaller bunches when I plant my plantain suckers too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ panicles bibii anɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too closely, their giant leaves block sunlight from each other, and their shallow roots compete heavily for soil nutrients and water. This competition leaves the plant with less energy to build large bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Baai wuji lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tso lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I choose the best suckers from my old plantain stems for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ plantains momoi amli kɛha dumɔ?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—young shoots with narrow, spear-like leaves and a broad base attached to the mother stem. These grow much faster, establish stronger roots, and produce bigger bunches than 'water suckers' that have broad leaves early on.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ he lɛ. Enɛɛmɛi daa oya kwraa. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ofee tsei akui wuji fe ‘tso ni nuɔ nu’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my plantains ripen and spoil so fast after I cut the bunch from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwereɔ ni egboɔ oya beni mifo tso lɛ mli fã ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, the plantain fruit releases a natural ripening gas called ethylene and breathes faster. Leaving harvested plantains under direct sun or in hot enclosures speeds up this gas production, causing them to turn yellow and soften rapidly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni omu oya Kɛ́ ashi plantains ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo yɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ gas nɛɛ afee oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo.

english: How do I know that a plantain bunch on my farm is mature enough for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ plantains ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the individual fingers lose their sharp green corners and become round and plump, and the dried flower tips at the ends of the fruit fall off easily when touched.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo beni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fiteɔ eŋɔli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebafeɔ kokroo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ anaagbee lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji akɛ ata he.

english: Why do traders come from dry countries like Burkina Faso to buy plantains in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi jɛɔ maji ni nu bɛ tamɔ Burkina Faso mli kɛbaa koni amɛbahe plantains yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Burkina Faso has a dry, northern climate that lacks the heavy rainfall and moist forest soil required to grow plantains. Because plantains cannot thrive in their local environment, traders travel to high-production zones in Ghana where the crop grows abundantly year-round.
ga: Burkina Faso yɛ kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ waa, ni koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni he hiaa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, plantains nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, jarayelɔi yaa hei ni afeɔ nibii babaoo yɛ yɛ Ghana lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does the number of days I dry my cocoa beans change depending on the weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbii abɔ ni esa akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi lɛ srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa lɛ?

english: During hot, sunny weather, moisture evaporates quickly and your cocoa beans may dry in around 5 days. However, during cloudy or rainy weather, moisture leaves slowly, so the beans will need 7 days or more to dry completely without spoiling.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni kookoo yibii lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ aaafee gbii enumɔ mli. Shi, yɛ atatu loo nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli lɛ, Moisture lɛ laajeɔ fiofio, no hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ agbi kwraa ni amɛfiteee.

english: How many days should I leave my cocoa beans to ferment before laying them out in the sun?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani anyɛ agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Cocoa beans typically need around 6 days of fermentation wrapped in plantain leaves. This process is crucial because it kills the bean seed, stops germination, and develops the rich brown color and chocolate flavor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cocoa ŋmeii biɔ aaafee gbii 6 dani amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni akɛ plantain baai ewo mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ egbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ, ekpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsokolate he ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa beans are fully dry and ready for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fully dry cocoa beans will crackle or crunch easily when you squeeze them in your hand, have a deep reddish-brown color inside, and sound like dry paper rustling when you turn them on the mat.
ga: Kokoo ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ oniji mimɔ mli lɛ, etseɔ loo efoɔ oya. Eyɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ emli. Ni egbɛɛmɔ tamɔ wolo ni egbi ni miitswa kɛji otsɔ mli yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my cocoa beans if I gather them off the drying mat too early after only 4 or 5 days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie amɛ kɛjɛ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ oya tsɔ yɛ gbii 4 loo 5 pɛ sɛɛ?

english: If you remove cocoa beans while they still contain moisture, mold will grow inside them during storage. Moldy beans taste bad, lose their commercial value, and will be rejected by buyers.
ga: Kɛji ojie kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ, Mold baakwɛ̃ yɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Beans ni mli ewo muji lɛ ŋɔɔ waa. Jarayeli sɛɛnamɔ ni elaaje ni mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baakpoo

english: Why do my neighbor's cocoa beans dry faster than mine even when we harvest on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kookoo yibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔkpa amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Drying speed depends on how thickly the beans are spread on the mat and how often they are turned. Spreading your beans in a thin layer and stirring them frequently helps them dry much faster and more evenly.
ga: Bɔ ni egbiɔ oya lɛ damɔ bɔ ni kɔfi yibii ni aja yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ mli wa ha lɛ nɔ. kɛ bɔ ni afɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ atsakemɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii amli ni okɛmiitswa shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛgbi oya ni amɛfee ekome.

english: Why do I need to stir and turn my cocoa beans regularly while they are drying on the bamboo mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ni matsake kookoo ŋmeii lɛ daa be mli ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ ŋmei nɔ lɛ?

english: Turning the beans several times a day ensures that all sides get equal sunlight and airflow. It prevents the bottom beans from staying damp and stops mold from forming.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ shii abɔ yɛ gbi kome mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ yaa nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔfe yibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii afee.

english: Is it harmful if my cocoa beans stay out on the drying mat for up to 7 days or more?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ hi ŋmeii ni agbiɔ lɛ nɔ gbii 7 loo nɔ ni fe nakai?

english: Taking 7 days to dry is normal when the sunlight is weak. However, leaving beans exposed to moisture or keeping already dry beans out too long can cause them to become brittle, break, or attract pests.
ga: Gbii kpawo ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ́ hulu la lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Shi, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii wo ŋmɔtɔ mli loo akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ to be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha etsɔ ŋmeii, efo, loo egbala ŋmeii kɛba.

english: Why do fresh cocoa beans change color from purple or white to dark brown after a few days on the mat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii heei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ purple loo eyɛŋ kɛyaa brown ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni amɛyeɔ yɛ tsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The color change is a natural chemical reaction caused by proper fermentation followed by sun drying. Heat and air break down the bitter compounds in the fresh bean, turning it brown and sweet-smelling.
ga: Su tsakemɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa. Dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ nibii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii heei amli lɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: What should I do with my cocoa beans on the drying mat when rain suddenly starts falling?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsɔne ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ trukaa?

english: You must immediately cover the beans with a tarpaulin or roll up the drying mat and move them under a shed. Rainwater re-wets the beans, which spoils their quality and promotes mold.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tarpaulin aha ŋmeii lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo okɛ ŋmeii ni akɛgbiɔ nii lɛ abɔ he ni okɛ amɛ aya ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Nugbɔ nu baaha kɔfi yibii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do some cocoa farmers ferment their produce for only 5 days while others wait for 7 days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo okwaafoi komɛi kɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa gbii 5 pɛ, yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi hu mɛɔ gbii 7 lɛ?

english: The duration of fermentation depends on the temperature and the amount of cocoa being fermented. Warmer weather speeds up fermentation to about 5 days, whereas cooler weather or larger heaps can take up to 7 days to ferment properly.
ga: Be ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ damɔ hulutsoo be lɛ kɛ bɔ ni kookoo lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fa ha lɛ nɔ. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya oya aaafee gbii enumɔ, yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo ŋmɔtɔi wuji baanyɛ ahé gbii 7 dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I start planting my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the ground is deeply soaked by two or three steady rains. The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell that can dry out and kill newly planted seeds before they take root.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ agbi dani amɛwo shishifãi lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my young crops if the rain stops for a long time after I plant?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kakadaŋŋ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Without rain, young plants cannot pull up nutrients from the soil. Their growth will slow down, they will wilt under the sun, and if the dry spell lasts too long, the crops will dry up entirely.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, tsei bibii nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛdalɛ baafee mlɛo. Amɛbaagbi yɛ hulu shishi. Ni kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ baagbi.

english: Maize leaves roll up like tubes to hide from the harsh sun and stop water from evaporating quickly. It is the plant's natural defense mechanism to save water when the weather is hot and dry.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ ŋmãa nɔ koni ekɛtee hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmãa oya. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why are my crops turning yellow and drooping even though they were green last week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ? Nakai otsi ni eho lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lolo?

english: When plants do not get enough rain or water, they cannot feed properly. Drooping and yellowing are early signs of extreme thirst, showing that the crop is starving for soil moisture.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ náaa nugbɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ egbee shi ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, eji mra be mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye lɛ waa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can I still grow crops successfully if I do not rely only on the rains?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lolo ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔɔ nugbɔ nɔ?

english: Yes, by using simple irrigation methods—such as fetching water from nearby streams, wells, or using water storage tanks—you can supply water to your crops even when the rains fail.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ, nubu loo nu ŋtayaa mli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okɛ nu aha onibii lɛ kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: How can I collect and save water on my farm to use during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabua nu naa ni mikɛto miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛtsu nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: You can catch rainwater from shed roofs into barrels or dig small earth ponds lined with plastic sheeting to store water for watering your crops when the rain pauses.
ga: Obaanyɛ omɔ nugbɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ mli kɛwoɔ baagi mli loo otsaa sũ bu bibioo ko ni akɛ plastic ŋmɔji ewo mli lɛ mli koni okɛ nu ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafɔ nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly just a day after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ gbi kome pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture very fast because direct sunlight and wind bake the ground. Leaving crop residues or spreading dry grass (mulch) over the soil keeps it shaded and holds water much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shãa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwie shi loo okɛ jwɛi (Mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha nu lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What can I add to my soil so that it retains water better for my crops?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nu lɛ ahi miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Adding well-rotted animal manure or compost enriches the soil and turns it into a sponge that holds onto rainwater longer, giving your crops steady moisture.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmei. ni otsake lɛ ofee lɛ sponji ni baanyɛ ahi nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Which crops can survive better on my farm if the rains are short or unreliable?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo loo anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas have deep roots or naturally low water needs, making them much more likely to survive and produce a harvest in dry conditions.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, nu ni he hiaa lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: How do I know if my crops are getting enough water from the rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your plants have firm, strong stems, deep green leaves, and show steady growth without wilting during the hottest part of the day, they are getting sufficient water.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ yɛ tso lɛ fã ni mli wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyaa nɔ edaa ni egbooo yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ená nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me to cut down my sick cocoa trees instead of just spraying them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mifolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni mawo amɛ tsofa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Certain serious cocoa diseases, like the swollen shoot virus, have no chemical cure. Cutting down infected trees is the only way to stop the disease from spreading to healthy parts of your farm and neighboring cocoa farms.
ga: Kookoo helai komɛi ni naa wa, tamɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ Tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛbaatsa hela nɛɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ okpa hela lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli.

english: Can I put fertilizer on my sick cocoa tree to help it recover from disease?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tsofa awo cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ?

english: Fertilizer helps healthy cocoa trees grow strong and produce pods, but it cannot cure viral diseases. Applying fertilizer to an infected tree will not clear the disease and can be a waste of money.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Shi enyɛŋ etsa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ tsofa woɔ mli lɛ ejieee hela lɛ kɛya, ni ekolɛ ebaabi shika.

english: How does a disease travel from a sick cocoa farm to my healthy cocoa farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ajɛ kookoo ŋmɔ ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya mi kookoo ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli?

english: Diseases spread through tiny insects like mealybugs that carry viruses from infected trees to healthy ones, or through fungal spores carried by wind, rain, and dirty farming tools.
ga: Hela nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɛɔ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni he tseee lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees have a serious disease that cannot be treated?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji kookoo yɛ hela ko ni naa wa ni anyɛɛɛ atsa?

english: Look out for signs like swollen trunks or branches, red veins appearing on young leaves, and abnormally small or deformed cocoa pods that ripen prematurely.
ga: Taomɔ okadii tamɔ tsei akutsei loo tsei niji ni efuu. Line tsuji jeɔ kpo yɛ baai bibii lɛ anɔ. kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni ejaaa loo ni bɛ bɔ ni sa ni haa amɛshwereɔ oya lɛ.

english: If I cut down my old diseased cocoa trees, how long do I have to wait before planting new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo kookoo tso ko ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ ebaahe dani adu kookoo dumɔwui heei?

english: After cutting down diseased trees and removing the infected roots, you should ensure the area is properly cleared and treated before planting new improved seedlings, which can often be done in the next planting season.
ga: Beni ofo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Esa akɛ Okwɛ koni ajie he ni hela lɛ yɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani odu dumɔwui heei ni eba lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ afee enɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa seedlings to start producing pods after replanting?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe mi-cocoa dumɔwui heei lɛ dani amɛje shishi amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ beni amɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa seedlings grow faster than old traditional varieties and typically start producing fruit within two to three years if properly cared for.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ hybrid kookoo dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya fe blema henɔi lɛ. ni bei pii lɛ, ebaaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What kind of help or follow-up can I expect from officers after my diseased cocoa farm is cleared?
ga: Mɛɛ yelikɛbuamɔ loo sɛɛnyiɛmɔ manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ onukpai lɛ adɛŋ beni agbe mi-kookoo ŋmɔ ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Extension officers assist by supplying healthy seedlings, teaching proper planting spacing, and making routine visits to monitor the health and growth of the new crop.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ he ni sa. ni amɛyasara daa koni amɛkwɛ bɔ ni tsei heei lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni buɔ amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it necessary to trim or prune my cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afolɔ loo afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unwanted shoots and dead branches, allowing sunlight and air to pass through the tree canopy. This helps reduce humidity that causes fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ni ataooo kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ. Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote tso lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Removing infected pods quickly prevents it from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or the soil has become too waterlogged. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmeii?

english: These holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the central growing leaf of the maize. Applying recommended control methods or clean ash into the center whorl early can stop them from destroying the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii loo ashwishwɛ ni he tse awo teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli mra. Ebaanyɛ ekpa tsei akpãtãmɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up when I plant them in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the young cocoa plants from sun damage until they grow strong.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ adumɔ. Ebaabu kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛyashi ebaada waa.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet, and cool conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight reach the stems and harvesting ripe pods frequently helps prevent the disease.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long because the soil lacks good drainage. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nu kpakpa ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants producing big leaves but very tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ baai lɛ dara shi eshishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes sweet potatoes to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Using balanced soil nutrients and avoiding excess fresh animal manure helps tubers grow bigger.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa tsu nii ni ajie ŋmeii heei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji ebɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a prop made from bamboo or a branched wooden pole keeps the tree upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. koni ekɛte shi ewo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛ tsei niji yɔɔ mli lɛ fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the flowers dropping off my tomato plants without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get extremely hot or when the plant experiences water stress. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering and mulching helps the plant hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by a root disease like bacterial wilt, which damages the plant's water pipes from underground. Removing affected plants immediately prevents the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ahelai, tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ a-nu paipii lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Bare soil left exposed to direct sunlight loses moisture very fast through evaporation. Covering the soil surface around crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) retains water and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni ashi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baafite ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) baadu lɛ baaha nu ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When plants are crowded together, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil food, which results in weak stalks and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni ŋmaa bibioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to grow deep and expand their tubers easily, and mounds help drain excess rainwater away so the tubers do not rot.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Ni gɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ koni bulb lɛ akafite.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves high to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛtso lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo bulb agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rain and wind come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots close to the surface and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, which makes them top-heavy and easy to pull out when the soil gets soft and wet.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii yɛ nɔ, ni eji mlɛo akɛ abaajie kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni edɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and look dead during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plants curl their leaves to shield themselves from losing too much water during extreme heat, and they usually bounce back once the sun goes down and temperatures cool.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ ehe kɛyaa sɛɛ kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the crop is starving for essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that too much water is sitting around the roots and choking them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo ebɔle ehe. shishifãi ni ekɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi

english: Why do the blossoms on my pepper plants fall off without turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, a sudden dry spell, or when there are not enough insects like bees visiting the field to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and dry on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, cool, and overly shaded conditions, especially when cocoa trees are not pruned.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afolɔɛɛ cacao tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot and smell bad under the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When rain stays in the soil for too long without draining, it deprives the cassava roots of air, causing them to suffocate and rot from underground fungi.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni etsɔɔɔ mli Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii amli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the soil dries out too fast. They need shade crops like plantain planted nearby to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I need to cut away some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which produces a much larger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji plantain tsei lɛ dara kɛbɔle Tso titri kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Tsoi lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha plantain tso ni da ni tsii kwraa aba.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen. Nitrogen is a key plant food, and without enough of it in the soil, the plant moves its remaining food to the young top leaves, causing the bottom leaves to yellow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Ni kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices from under the leaves, or by a disease carried by these insects. Treating the crop for tiny insects early stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni anaaa tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ nuɔ tso mli nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli Kooloi bibii akwɛmɔ Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without forming any tomatoes during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When the weather gets too hot, the pollen inside tomato flowers dries up and dies before it can fertilize the flower. Since no fruit can form without pollination, the plant drops the useless flowers to save its energy.
ga: Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai ko bɛ ni baanyɛ afee kɛji pollination bɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stick cuttings at an angle instead of burying them flat in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at an angle or upright lets the buds at the top sprout quickly into stems above ground, while the buds underground grow deep roots that swell into big cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yucca niji yɛ koŋ nɔ loo amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to catch as much sunlight as possible to make food that travels down to grow big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the air and off the wet ground, which also protects them from rotting.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato wain tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ hiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ hu akafite.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when the field is filled with standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni nu ni damɔ shi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special roots that can breathe underwater, but most weeds cannot. Keeping standing water on the field drowns out weeds that would steal plant food while keeping the soil soft for rice roots.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni baanyɛ amu yɛ nu shishi. Shi jwɛi babaoo nyɛɛɛ. Nu ni damɔ shi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛgbeɔ jwɛi ni baaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ blɛoo kɛha ŋmãa shishifãi

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to a special plant family that takes nitrogen food out of the air and puts it naturally into the soil through their roots. When you harvest groundnuts, that extra food stays in the ground to feed the next crop like maize.
ga: Peanuts fata tsei akuu krɛdɛɛ ko ni jieɔ niyenii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ he. Beni okpaa ŋmei Nakai niyenii kroko lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cabbage on the exact same patch of land where I harvested cabbage last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kaabɛji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa kaabɛji yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot back-to-back leaves soil pests and diseases waiting in the ground to immediately attack the new plants. Rotating with a different crop starves those pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛtutua tso hee lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye hɔmɔ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a clearing with no large trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from intense sun heat and conserving soil moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting at the leaf tips usually show that the maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green leafy growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making ragged holes in my young corn leaves and leaving small greenish droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is typical of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central leaves to feed. Controlling them early by applying approved treatments into the leaf whorls during cool morning or evening hours saves the crop yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye nii lɛ feɔ. nɔkwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Kɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ awo baai lɛ ahe yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Dumɔ be

english: Growing tomatoes continuously in the same spot allows tomato-specific soil pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or legumes breaks the disease cycle and leaves the soil healthier.
ga: Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu tomato yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ Ehaa helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ kpaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before any peppers actually start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme dry heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients. Mulching the soil to keep it cool and moist helps flowers stay on the plant to produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli baa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Mulching koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or dried cocoa pods on the soil surface around my garden crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii ashwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with organic mulch traps moisture in the soil, keeps root zones cool during hot days, slows down weed growth, and eventually breaks down into food for the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni wala yɔɔ mli wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn watery and rot underground during heavy rainfall seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ shishi muji yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when stagnant water starves them of air in heavy, waterlogged soils. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: How does growing groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil better for the next season's crop?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, this trapped nitrogen acts as a free, natural fertilizer for future crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei shishifãi fite Nɛkɛ nitrogen ni akɛwo mli nɛɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I let many shoots grow around one mother plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa bibii nɛkɛ beni mihaa tsei ashishifãi babaoo shwereɔ yɛ fɔlɔ tso kome he lɛ?

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow on one stool forces them to fight for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Pruning to keep only two or three suckers per plant allows the main stem to yield large, heavy bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmei) babaoo shwereɔ yɛ ŋmeii kome nɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛha nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni tso lɛ mli ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi shi lɛ, no baaha tso lɛ niji wuji ni tsii aba tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to tie my tomato plants to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruits off wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and rotting caused by soil contact. It also improves air flow around the plant and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Staking baaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ fitemɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ naa. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. dumɔ ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Can a crop disease spread from my neighbor's farm to my own field?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔ mli?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread easily through wind, rain splashes, shared contaminated farm tools, or insects moving between fields and carrying fungi, bacteria, or viruses from infected crops to healthy ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ. loo kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii, helatsɛmɛi, loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are typical signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from infected plants and transfer it to healthy ones.
