ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa, ni amɛkɛhaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants look fresh in the morning but suddenly wilt and die by afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ehee leebi, shi trukaa lɛ amɛgboiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting is usually caused by soil-borne bacteria or root rot fungi that clog the inside of the plant stem, stopping water from traveling up from the roots during the hot part of the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ trukaa lɛ ji helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu akajɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why should I destroy and burn crops that are infected with strange sicknesses instead of leaving them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpãtã ŋmɔshi nibii ni helai ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ ni mashã amɛ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Removing and burning severely diseased plants destroys the source of the infection, preventing fungi, bacteria, or viruses from multiplying and spreading to your healthy crops or neighboring fields.
ga: Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni ajieɔ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ. Tsi fungi, bacteria loo virus naa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ loo ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are black spots forming on my cocoa pods before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi diji dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection that thrives in conditions with high humidity, excessive shade, and poor airflow around the tree leaves.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɔleɔ tso baai gbohii ahe lɛ

english: What makes the bottom of my tomato fruits turn black and rot while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egbo be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot, known as blossom-end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering during fruit formation.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot inside the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the ground is caused by fungi or bacteria entering the tuber through small wounds, insect cuts, or waterlogged soil that smothers the tuber's breathing.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato sũ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa ji ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ni boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ pilamɔi bibii, ŋmeii ni efolɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do small insects cause my plants to stop growing well?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii baanyɛ aha tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Insects damage crops not only by chewing leaves and roots, but also by sucking vital juices and injecting plant viruses that stunt growth and spoil harvests.
ga: Jeee baai kɛ shishifãi ni amɛyeɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ kooloi fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shi nɔ ni fata he ji nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei amli helai ni haaa ekwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and roll up tightly during growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpãa shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up and turn yellow when the plant is stressed by a lack of nitrogen in the soil, drought conditions, or pests like fall armyworms attacking the growing point.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms ni tutuaa hei ni edaa yɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa.

english: Why does planting the exact same crop on the same land every season make the harvest poorer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ehaa nikpamɔ lɛ mli waa lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases that prefer that specific plant to build up in the soil over time.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii komɛi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Coconut trees need proper distance, usually around 20 feet by 20 feet apart (or 8 to 9 meters). Proper spacing ensures their roots and leaves do not fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing them to yield more fruit.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmei tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee ninetalɔi 20 kɛ ninetalɔi 20 (loo mitai 8 kɛyashi 9) kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ akatswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ha amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How many tree seedlings can I comfortably fit on one acre of land?
ga: Dumɔwui enyiɛ manyɛ madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ?

english: Depending on the crop and spacing method used, an acre can hold between 50 to 70 coconut trees. Planting too many trees close together makes them grow thin and tall with lower fruit yield because of competition.
ga: Edamɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii kɛ gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome baanyɛ akwɛ aaafee ŋmeii tsei 50 kɛyashi 70 nɔ. Tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛwooo yibii fioo yɛ akaŋshii hewɔ.

english: What happens to my trees if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their branches block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for the same water and food in the soil, leading to poor growth and very small harvests.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsoi aniji haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ, ni kpamɔ fioo pɛ hu baa.

english: Why are my coconut trees producing fewer fruits after many years on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni mikɛ afii babaoo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tree crops naturally slow down as they age, especially after 40 to 50 years. As the trees get very old and tall, it becomes harder for nutrients to travel to the top, signaling that it is time to replant with fresh seedlings.
ga: Tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛye afii. Titri lɛ, yɛ afii 40 kɛyashi 50 sɛɛ, beni tso lɛ eda ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Ebaawa waa akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaya ŋwɛi. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui heei.

english: Should I cut down all my old trees at once when replanting my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo tsei momoi lɛ fɛɛ shikome kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔ ko miidu ekoŋŋ?

english: Replanting in sections or stages is often better because it allows you to keep earning money from the remaining old bearing trees while your new young seedlings grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ooodu ekoŋŋ yɛ be kɛ bei amli loo yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ehaa onáa shika kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni odumɔwui heei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Does soil that has grown trees for over 40 years need special preparation before I replant?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni tsei ekwɛ nɔ fe afii 40 nɛ lɛ he miihia ni asaa he krɛdɛɛ dani adu ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, land used for many decades usually loses key nutrients. Adding organic compost or manure and clearing out old diseased roots helps restore soil life before planting new seedlings.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛtsu nii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli wo mli ni ajie shishifãi momo ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha sũ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ dani adu dumɔwui heei.

english: How many years can a coconut tree stay productive on my farm?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ŋmei tso baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy coconut tree can live for up to 60 to 80 years, but its most productive fruiting years are typically between 10 and 45 years before yields naturally begin to drop.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi afii 60 kɛyashi 80, shi bei pii lɛ, afii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fe fɛɛ lɛ ji afii 10 kɛyashi 45 dani adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi.

english: How long will I have to wait for a newly planted coconut seedling to bear fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ koni ŋmei dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ awo yibii?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties can start producing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while tall traditional varieties usually take between 5 to 7 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Kokooi bibii baanyɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kokooi ni kɛlɛ, ni ji blema nɔ lɛ heɔ afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii.

english: What key costs should I plan for before starting to replant my land?
ga: Mɛɛ shika titri esa akɛ mato he gbɛjianɔ dani mabɔi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dumɔ ekoŋŋ?

english: You need to budget for clearing old vegetation, buying high-quality certified seedlings, labor for digging holes and planting, and initial care like weeding and watering during the early months.
ga: Esa akɛ oná shika ni okɛbaajie tsei momoi lɛ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli. Nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo kɛha bu ni atsa kɛ dumɔwui kɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ nyɔŋ lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Can I grow food crops between my young coconut trees while waiting for them to mature?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Yes, during the first 3 to 4 years while the tree canopy is still open, you can grow food crops like cassava, legumes, or maize between the rows to get income and food while keeping weeds under control.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli be mli ni tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli egbele lolo lɛ. Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei. loo ŋmãa ni akɛhaa kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ koni amɛná shika kɛ niyenii yɛ be kome mli kɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ.

english: How do I know if the seeds I buy from the market are good quality for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔ?

english: Good quality certified seeds come in sealed bags with official tags. They are uniform in size, free from diseases or insect holes, and produce a much better harvest than grain saved from a previous crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ baa yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli ni amralo lɛ kadimɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Eyɛ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa ni helai loo kooloi bibii bɛ mli ni eha yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations, leading to smaller yields and higher vulnerability to pests. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle local weather, and grow uniformly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi, ni oshara ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Tsu he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe nii ni oda daa

english: Will my maize crop change if my neighbor plants a different maize variety right next to my land?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa yibiiwoo lɛ baatsake kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ du ŋmãa srɔtoi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, maize pollen travels through the wind. If your neighbor's maize flowers at the same time as yours, cross-pollination will mix the varieties, which can lower the overall quality and purity of your crop.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa pollen lɛ tsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛji okutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmãa lɛ fɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli kɛ onɔ̃ lɛ, cross-pollination baaha ŋmãa srɔtoi afee ekome, ni no baaha ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ afee fɛo kɛ ehe tse.

english: How far away should I plant my crops from my neighbor's field to keep my seeds pure?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni ŋmaa lɛ he atse?

english: To keep your seeds pure from cross-pollination, you need a safe distance buffer—often around 200 meters for crops like maize—or you must time your planting so your crops do not flower at the same time as neighboring fields.
ga: Koni odumɔwui lɛ ahe atse kɛjɛ cross-pollination he. Esa akɛ oná he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe—bei pii lɛ, aaafee mitai 200 kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa—loo ehe miihia ni okɛ be awo odumɔ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni onibii lɛ akawo fɔfɔi yɛ be kome mli kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: What happens if I accidentally mix two different seed varieties together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi enyɔ futu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ oshara mli?

english: Different varieties grow and mature at different speeds. Mixing them causes plants to compete unevenly for sunlight and water, resulting in mixed plant heights, uneven maturity, and lower overall crop yield.
ga: Henɔi srɔtoi daa ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ futu mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tsei ni efutu lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ. Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi

english: Why are my plants flowering at different times even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ bei srɔtoi amli eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: This usually happens when mixed or impure seeds are planted. When you use pure, single-variety seeds, all the plants grow, flower, and mature at the exact same time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni efutu loo dumɔwui ni he tse. Kɛ okɛ dumɔwui krɔŋŋ ni ji srɔtoi kome tsu nii lɛ, Tsei fɛɛ daa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛdaraa yɛ be kome mli.

english: How does planting pure, single-variety seeds make harvesting easier for me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwu kome ni he tse ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kɛhaa mi?

english: When all your plants come from a pure seed type, they mature simultaneously. This allows you to harvest your entire field at once rather than making multiple trips to pick mature crops.
ga: Beni otsei lɛ fɛɛ jɛ dumɔwui krɔŋŋ mli lɛ. Amɛbaafee ekome kɛda. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooya gbɛfaai babaoo koni oyahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni eda lɛ,

english: Why are my cassava plants growing different types of tubers across the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ miikwɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: This happens when planting cuttings from different cassava varieties get mixed together before planting. Using clean, labeled stems of a single variety ensures consistent tuber shape, size, and cooking quality.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni afolɔ kɛjɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi amli lɛ futu mli dani adu. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni he tse, ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo nɔ ni jɛ tso kome mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa amɛhe feɔ fɛo, amɛdalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhooɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ.

english: How can I stop crop diseases from spreading from my neighbor's farm to my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei ahe helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa?

english: You can plant border crops, clean farm tools before moving between fields, and make sure you use disease-free planting material right from the start of the season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei yɛ husu lɛ naa. Tsumɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe dani okɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔji ateŋ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni okɛ dumɔ nii ni hela bɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛjɛ be lɛ shishijee mli.

english: Why is it important to check my crops very early when they are still small seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli mra lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani ehe miihia beni eji dumɔwu bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Checking early allows you to spot off-type plants or early signs of disease before they spread across your field or to neighboring farms, protecting your harvest quality from the beginning.
ga: mra be mli ni anaa Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onaa tsei ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ loo hela he okadii mra dani egbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ loo kɛyaa ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli. Buu okpamɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ shishijee

english: Why are some maize plants on my farm growing very tall while others right next to them stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ daraa waa lɛ? bibioo kwraa

english: When crops grow unevenly in the same field, it usually means soil nutrients are spread unevenly or a seed-borne disease attacked the roots of the smaller plants early on.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mlijaa ejaaa. Aloo, helai ni jɛɔ dumɔwui amli baa lɛ tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi mra.

english: Why does my cassava plant have big lush leaves above ground but very small tubers underground when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni kwɛɔ daa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: When cassava receives too much nitrogen or excess rainfall, the plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the root tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai kɛ tsei eŋɔli ni miida lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crop is sick just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Healthy crop leaves are normally a clear green color; if you notice dark spots, yellow patches, leaf curling, or sudden wilting, those visible signs mean disease or pests are attacking your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ. Kɛji ona he ko ni edɔ, he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo he ko ni egbo trukaa Nakai okadii ni anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miitutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even when there is plenty of moisture in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting during rainy periods is often caused by a soil sickness like bacterial wilt, which enters through the roots and blocks water from moving up inside the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ helai tamɔ bacteria wilt ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ baa. Eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaaa nu aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: If one of my cassava plants develops yellow spots on its leaves, will the sickness spread to the rest of my field?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ eko yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani hela baagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, many plant diseases spread quickly from one sick plant to healthy ones through farm tools, insects like whiteflies, wind, or rain splashing off infected leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and drop off before fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed leaves when they suffer from stress, such as poor root health, lack of plant nutrients like nitrogen, or overwatering.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ. Tso mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up tightly and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or aphids, which feed on the leaves and can pass leaf curl virus to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛ baanyɛ amɛ gbɛ curling hela lɛ amɛshwã tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my bean plants without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off prematurely when plants experience heat stress, extended dry spells, or insect pests that feed on the delicate blossoms before pods can develop.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings look weak and stop producing new leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekpaa baai heei feemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and need shade canopy trees like plantain to protect them from direct sunlight and prevent heat burn.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛbiɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu cacao lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛtsi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: What causes small cocoa pods on my tree to turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Yɛ mi tsei ni feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ?

english: This is black pod disease, a fungal sickness that multiplies quickly in cool, wet conditions and spreads when moisture stays on the pods too long.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji fungal hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ mli. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ hi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big trees act as natural protectors, filtering harsh sunlight and keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can survive and grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli bulɔi. Tsɔɔmɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ koni kookoo bibii anyɛ ahi shi ni amɛdara.

english: Why do my plantain trees always fall over during heavy rains, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Heavy winds easily snap or uproot plantain trees because of their shallow roots and heavy fruit. Planting a line of strong trees along the border of your farm breaks the force of the wind and shields your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa loo ejieɔ dumɔwui lɛ oya yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ hewɔ. Tsei ni wa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baafo kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: How do my crops get food and water from the ground when it has not rained for weeks?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Plants use deep roots like underground pipes to draw hidden moisture and dissolved nutrients from deep inside the soil, while organic matter in the earth acts like a sponge to hold onto water.
ga: Tsei kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, tamɔ paipii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛgbala nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ sponji, ni amɛmɔɔ nu mli.

english: If I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize, won't the beans steal food from the maize?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ani ŋmãa lɛ ejuŋ niyenii kɛjɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, beans actually help feed the maize. Beans capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a free natural fertilizer that helps neighboring maize grow strong.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Beans mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are the earthworms in my soil harmful to my crops or are they helping them?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miifite miŋmɔshi nibii loo amɛmiiye amɛmiibua amɛ?

english: Earthworms are beneficial helpers. They eat dead leaves and dirt, turning them into rich fertilizer, and their digging creates underground tunnels that allow crop roots to breathe and absorb water.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ji yelikɛbuamɔi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai ni egboi kɛ muji. Tsɔmɔmɔ amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Ni amɛbu ni amɛfoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛmɔɔ nu.

english: Why should I cover the soil around the base of my crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Dry leaves act as mulch, which acts like a blanket to trap moisture in the soil so it doesn't dry out in the hot sun. As the leaves break down, they also turn into rich food for your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch, ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ. Kɛ́ baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ Ebafeɔ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why do insects destroy one corner of my crop field while leaving another part untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii efite miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Crops growing in weak soil or without enough water get stressed and emit smells that attract insects. Healthy, well-nourished plants produce natural defenses that make it harder for pests to attack them.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmeii ni gbalaa kooloi. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ni haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai akɛ amɛbaatutua amɛ.

english: Why do you advise me to leave cover crops on my land during the dry season instead of leaving the soil completely bare?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Bare soil gets scorched by the sun, losing all its moisture and beneficial nutrients. Cover crops shade the ground, prevent wind from blowing topsoil away, and keep the earth fertile for the next season.
ga: Hulu lɛ shã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ. Efiteɔ emli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo. Tsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. ni eha je lɛ afee nɔ ni woɔ yibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking branches from my cassava or tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-cassava loo tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Removing extra branches prevents the plant from wasting energy on leaves it doesn't need. This forces the plant to direct its energy into growing larger tubers or bigger fruits.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ tsei ahe tsei ni ataooo lɛ anɔ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya ŋmeii wuji loo aduawai wuji ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from the same plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Planting too close causes crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients. This leaves all the plants small and weak, resulting in a much smaller overall harvest than properly spaced crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tsei lɛ atswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmaa fɛɛ ni abaakpa lɛ baafee bibioo fe tsei ni akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact amount of chemical medicine to spray on my crops when they get sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: Always follow the dosage instructions on the product label or ask an extension officer, because giving too little will not cure the disease, and giving too much can burn and kill your crops.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ tsofa lɛ he wolo lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ loo obi mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ. Ejaakɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ nyɛŋ atsa hela lɛ. Ni kɛ́ akɛ babaoo ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ashã ni egbo.

english: Why are my crops still dying even after I apply pesticide to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Pesticides only kill insect pests, not fungal or bacterial diseases, so applying pesticide to a plant suffering from a disease will not save it from dying.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ gbeɔ kooloi bibii pɛ. Jeee fungal loo bacteria hela ni. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii tsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, etsĩŋ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagboi.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and causing the plant to dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, receiving improper watering, or suffering from a root disease that stops it from absorbing food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli, ni awo lɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Aloo eji shishifa hela ko ni haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii?

english: Why is it important for me to clean my farming tools before moving to a new field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ ahe dani mikɛya ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Cleaning your cutlasses and hoes removes hidden disease germs and fungus, stopping you from spreading infections from a sick farm plot to healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ́ otsumɔ o-dagger kɛ o-shovel lɛ, ebaajie helai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okagbɛ hela kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Should I remove and burn crop plants that show signs of severe sickness?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsɔɔ hela ni naa wa he okadii lɛ ni mashã?

english: Yes, taking out sick plants immediately keeps disease spores and insects from spreading to your healthy crops and destroying the rest of your yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai kɛ kooloi bibii akagbɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli ni efite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why does clearing weeds around my crops help keep them healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Weeds hide pests and plant diseases while stealing water and soil nutrients, making your crops weak and easy targets for illness.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai teeɔ yɛ be kome mli. kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ juu. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni helai baanyɛ amɔ bo oya.

english: How often should I water my crops during the dry season to keep them alive?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi?

english: Crops need consistent and precise watering—ideally early morning or late afternoon—so the soil stays moist enough for roots to drink without drying out or rotting.
ga: Ehe miihia ni afɔ tso lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni afɔ lɛ daa. Titri lɛ, leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu ni amɛgbiŋ loo amɛgbooo.

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually kill them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, over-watering drowns the roots by removing air from the soil, causing the root system to rot so the plant can no longer take up food and water.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni no haaa tso lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu dɔŋŋ.

english: What happens if I delay or skip spraying my farm on the planned days?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tee sɛɛ loo mifo mli yɛ gbi ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Skipping planned farm care allows pests and diseases to multiply rapidly, making it much harder and more expensive to save your crops later.
ga: Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya Enɛ haa ewaa ni ejara wa waa akɛ abaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my young cassava plants are healthy and growing properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida?

english: Healthy cassava plants have firm, bright green leaves, strong stems, and steady new shoots without dark spots, wilting, or insect holes.
ga: Cassava tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ, tsei ni wa, kɛ tsei heei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni he ko ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ bɛ mli. Egbo loo eyɛ kooloi akutsei

english: Why do the prices for my harvested rice drop so low towards the end of the year in December?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ jara baa shi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee yɛ December mli lɛ?

english: Between October and December, large quantities of imported rice flood the market alongside local harvests. This sudden massive supply creates a market glut, forcing crop prices down during December.
ga: Yɛ October kɛ December teŋ lɛ, ŋmãa babaoo ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ miiho kɛmiiya jara nɔ kɛfata maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ ahe. Nɛkɛ nibii babaoo ni baa trukaa nɛɛ haa nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ajara ba shi yɛ December mli.

english: Is January a good month for me to take my produce to the market for sale?
ga: Ani January ji nyɔŋ kpakpa ni mikɛ nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baaya jara nɔ?

english: January is usually the slowest month for sales because consumers spend heavily in December and stay home in January, leading to low demand and poor prices for agricultural produce.
ga: January ji nyɔŋ ni jarayeli yaa hiɛ fioo fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ yeɔ shika babaoo yɛ December mli, ni amɛhiɔ shia yɛ January mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, okwaayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni okwaayeli nibii lɛ ajara hu baa shi.

english: Which time of the year should I aim to harvest my crops to get the highest market prices?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be esa akɛ mafee miyiŋ akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛha jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ?

english: Targeting your harvest for late February or March is ideal because food stocks from the holiday season run low, buyers return to the markets, and demand for fresh produce rises significantly.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni akɛma hiɛ yɛ February loo March naagbee lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ gbijurɔyeli be lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa jara nɔ ni aduawai kɛ aduawai heei ni ataoɔ lɛ etee hiɛ waa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect them from harsh sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or shade trees shields young cocoa, retains soil moisture, and keeps the leaves green and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa kɛ latsaa he. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ tsei bibii loo shia tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving green waste inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishi jwɛi eŋɔli yɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central growing shoot of maize plants. Applying approved treatments early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars emerge will protect your maize.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmei lɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow with light patches and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies and by planting stem cuttings from infected plants. You can prevent it by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by agricultural officers and using clean stem cuttings.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni akwɛɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsei niji ni he tse ni afoɔ lɛ atsu nii

english: How can I tell if my farmland has lost its strength before I plant my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho hewalɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellowish leaves, or produced smaller yields than usual, your soil is low in nutrients. Adding well-rotted animal manure or suitable fertilizers restores nutrients to help crops grow strong.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo yibiiwoo ni baa shi fe bɔ ni sa Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seed yams rot in the soil before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seed yams usually rot due to waterlogged soil, soil fungi, or injuries on the yam piece. Planting on well-drained mounds or ridges and dusting seed yams with wood ash or fungicide before planting protects them from rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hewɔ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, loo sweet potato fãi lɛ ni yeɔ awui lɛ hewɔ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Ni kɛ́ okɛ tso mli sũ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii shwie sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe koni amɛkafite.

english: Is it better to water my pepper plants during the hot afternoon or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli loo leebi?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the hot afternoon causes moisture to evaporate too fast and can heat up wet soil around roots, whereas morning watering lets plants absorb water fully before the sun gets hot.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ adɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani hulu lɛ shɛɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and choosing heat-tolerant seeds helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahalamɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches even when the rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around one parent plantain plant, they compete for food and water, resulting in small bunches. Pruning away extra suckers and leaving only three shoots of different ages per stool produces bigger plantain bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome lɛ he lɛ fa babaoo. Amɛbaatswa niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kui bibii. Afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eshwɛ tsei etɛ pɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi yɛ sɛi kome mli. Ebaaha plantain lɛ aná jwɛi agbo fe no.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop shoots at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have tough, deep root systems adapted to survive dry spells, allowing them to grab early rain nutrients faster than crops. Clearing weeds early in the first three to four weeks prevents them from choking your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa jwɛi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai mra yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekatsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my soil has just enough moisture before I sow my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Soil needs a balanced level of moisture—about a quarter full of water capacity—so seeds can absorb water without suffocating. Squeeze a handful of soil: if it holds shape without dripping water or crumbling instantly, it has enough moisture to start germination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ni sa - aaafee nu ni eyɔɔ lɛ mlijaa ejwɛ mli ekome - bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Mimɔ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nine: Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli ni efooo loo efooo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ni baaha eje shishi ekwɛ̃.

english: What will happen to my crops if I start watering them late in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mibɔi nu shwiemɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ naagbee?

english: If water comes too late, crops suffer permanent shock, stunted growth, or early drop of flowers. Watering early ensures plants build strong root systems capable of absorbing nutrients when they need them most.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ ba sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaana Dumɔwui anɔ hewalɛ daa. dalɛ kpaa loo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to apply fertilizer early in the growth of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa yɛ ŋmãa dalɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early application gives young plants the nutrients needed to build strong stalks and deep roots early on. If you wait until the plant is mature, the fertilizer cannot undo past damage or boost the yield significantly.
ga: Kɛtsu nii kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ mra. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Fertilizers nyɛŋ ajie nɔ ni efite yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ loo eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why did my neighbor get a better harvest than me even though we planted the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe mi eyɛ mli akɛ wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komekomei lɛ?

english: Getting inputs like seeds or fertilizer early in the season allows crops to make full use of the rainy season. Planting even a few weeks late often leads to poor yields due to reduced growing time and water availability.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ haa yibiiwoo baaa yɛ dumɔ be ni baa shi kɛ nu ni yɔɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: If a fellow farmer gives me leftover seeds from their farm, can I plant them directly?
ga: Kɛji minaanyo okwaafonyo ko ha mi dumɔwui ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani manyɛ madu tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Leftover seeds can be planted, but older seeds or seeds stored improperly lose their strength to sprout quickly. Testing a few seeds in damp cloth first shows if they are still healthy enough to give good results.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni egbɔ loo ni akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ lɛ laajeɔ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ hewalɛ oya. Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ aka dumɔwui fioo komɛi okwɛ. klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ koni ana kɛji dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo bɔ ni sa ni baaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings fail to grow while others sprout well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛ̃ee yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need sufficient moisture in the ground and good freshness when planted. Cuttings taken from old stems or left out in the sun too long lose their water content and fail to sprout.
ga: Cassava ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa kɛji adu. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli ŋmeii loo ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or the roots are waterlogged and cannot breathe. Adding compost or fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ ni enyɛɛɛ emu. Kompost loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ, eŋɔli.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Proper spacing allows every individual plant to spread its leaves and produce larger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛɔ ebaa lɛ eshwaa ni ewoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: How can I make my old communal farmland fertile again without moving to new land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi akutso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ momo lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ekoŋŋ ni mifãaa kɛyaaa shikpɔŋ hee nɔ?

english: You can restore soil fertility by adding animal manure, leaving crop residues to rot into the soil, or planting cover crops like beans that naturally add nutrients back into the land.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo dumɔ nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ miiho yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants act like delicate babies that burn under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides shelter and keeps the soil cool so young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ abifabii ni he waaa ni shãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an important plant food needed for growth, or that excess rainwater in the field is suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or beans makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers store starch, and when left in the ground past maturity—especially during heavy rains—fungi and bacteria in the wet soil attack and decay the roots.
ga: Kasava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ. ni kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi eda kwraa Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Fungi kɛ bacteria ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy for growing big tubers underground. Stakes lift the leaves high so they can catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Stakes woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are all the small flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if the tree experiences water stress during dry weather, lacks nutrients, or lacks tiny pollinating insects like midges to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ bɛ, loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why should I cut away the extra small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Removing extra suckers stops them from stealing water and plant food from the main plant, allowing the mother tree to grow a larger and healthier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaaa amɛju nu kɛ tso niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso nyɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering while the fruit is forming.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi tip rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking juices from the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crops with dry grass during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool, stops water from evaporating quickly under the sun, and protects crop roots from heat.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ hulu la shishi. ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal fertilizers, water, and sunlight away from your main crops, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides living shade and holds soil moisture, protecting the delicate young cocoa leaves from burning while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shade ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he beni amɛfeɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running out of essential nutrients like nitrogen. Over time, cocoa trees drain nutrients from the ground to grow, so adding fertilizer or organic compost restores essential plant food to keep leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ ekoŋŋ koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do many small flowers fall off my cocoa trees without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii No hewɔ lɛ amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔi?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands of flowers but can only support a small fraction as full pods. Factors like dry weather, heavy rain, or lack of insect pollinators cause extra flowers to drop off naturally.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ebaanyɛ eye ebua fã bibioo ko pɛ. be mli pɛ ni pods lɛ eyi obɔ. Nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa tree if I want it to produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ nɔ kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or crowded branches so sunlight and air can flow through the canopy. This prevents fungal growth and allows the tree to send its energy directly into growing heavy, healthy cocoa pods instead of extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii ni miida ni tsii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ baai baafata he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus. High humidity and poor drainage allow fungal spores to splash from the soil onto the pods, spreading rapidly if damaged or wet pods are left on the tree.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kɛbaa Fuji ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa fungi spores lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa pods lɛ anɔ. ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ efite loo efɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the stems of some of my cocoa trees swelling up and making the branches stop producing leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei komɛi akutsei lɛ amli fũuɔ ni ehaa eniji lɛ kpaɔ baai lɛ?

english: Swollen stems are a sign of the Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is carried between trees by tiny insects called mealybugs. The virus blocks nutrients from moving inside the tree, causing swelling, leaf loss, and eventually killing the tree.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu lɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus lɛ he okadi, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ mealybugs lɛ woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Virus lɛ tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fuuɔ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni naagbee lɛ efiteɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why does my cocoa farm produce a very large harvest late in the year, but a much smaller harvest a few months later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ? Shi nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, akpa nɔ ni faaa kwraa.

english: Cocoa trees in Ghana follow natural rainfall patterns, creating two harvest periods: a main crop season driven by the heavy rains, and a smaller light crop season during drier weather when fewer flowers develop into full pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ yɛ bɔ ni amɛnuɔ nugbɔ amɛhaa. Enɛ haa kpamɔ bei enyɔ baa: be titri ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ; kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be bibioo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbiɔ waa lɛ. Beni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi fioo komɛi

english: What causes tiny dark spots and dry patches to appear on my young cocoa stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa?

english: These spots are caused by sap-sucking pests called capsids or mirids. They bite soft green stems and feed on plant sap, leaving behind wounds that weaken the branches and reduce the tree's ability to hold pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids lɛ. Amɛyeɔ tso lɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Eshiɔ pilamɔi ni haa tso lɛ nine lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛaamɔ etsitsii lɛ amli lɛ baa shi.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are ripe enough to cut down from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-kookoo lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color completely from green or deep red to bright yellow or orange. Harvesting pods when fully yellow ensures the sweet pulp and seeds inside have fully developed for good weight and quality.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha shwiili kpakpa kɛ kpakpafeemɔ.

english: Why must I cover my freshly harvested cocoa beans with banana leaves for several days instead of putting them directly in the sun to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ banana baai aha kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe gbii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha ehi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Covering wet beans with plantain or banana leaves allows them to ferment. Fermentation removes the sour pulp, develops the rich chocolate flavor, and turns the inside of the beans brown, which is essential for getting a good grade from cocoa buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantains loo banana baai ha ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Fermentation jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa tsokolate ni ŋɔɔ waa baa. ni otsake dumɔwui lɛ amli ni efee ŋmɔtɔ Enɛ he miihia koni anyɛ ana yibɔi kpakpai kɛjɛ mɛi ni heɔ kookoo lɛ adɛŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crop is sick just by looking at the color of its leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ahe su pɛ nɔ?

english: Sick plants often show sudden changes in leaf color, such as turning an unusual dark green, yellowing, or developing patches. Healthy leaves usually maintain a uniform, bright green appearance typical for that specific crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ baai lɛ ahe tsakemɔi trukaa, tamɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ unifɔm, eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ ni ji nakai ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning a strange green color instead of their normal look?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookwɛ bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Unusual color changes in leaves are often a clear sign that a plant disease or virus has infested the crop, disturbing its normal growth process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ahe su ni tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso hela loo hela ko miibote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. ni tsiɔ dalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ naa

english: Is there a chemical spray or medicine I can buy to cure every disease on my crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo tsofai yɛ ni manyɛ mahe koni mikɛtsa hela fɛɛ hela ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: No, there is no single cure for every plant disease. In fact, many crop diseases—especially viral ones—have no approved medicine to cure them once a plant is infected.
ga: Dabi, tsamɔ ko bɛ kɛha tso hela fɛɛ hela. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ Tsei ahe helai babaoo titri lɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa Tsofa ko bɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛtsaa lɛ kɛji tso lɛ he hela lɛ pɛ.

english: What should I do on my farm if a crop disease has no approved medicine to cure it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ tso hela ko bɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛbaatsa lɛ?

english: When there is no chemical cure available, you should immediately uproot and destroy the sick plants to stop the disease from spreading to the healthy crops nearby.
ga: Beni tsofa ko bɛ ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ Esa akɛ otsi tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ashishifãi ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Who is the right person to talk to before I spend money on chemicals for my sick plants?
ga: Namɔ ji mɔ ni sa akɛ mikɛ lɛ agba sane dani mafite shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛha tso ni hela mɔ lɛ?

english: You should always consult an agricultural extension officer or an approved agro-dealer who can correctly identify the disease and advise you on approved treatments or management steps.
ga: Esa akɛ oyakwɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ko loo okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ enɔ ni baanyɛ ayoo hela lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo bo ŋaa yɛ tsamɔi loo gbɛjianɔtoi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Can a plant disease easily jump from one sick plant to other living crops on my field?
ga: Tse helai baanyɛ ajɛ tso kome ni hela mɔ lɛ mli kɛya tsei krokomɛi ni hiɛ ka lɛ anɔ. Yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mlɛo?

english: Yes, plant diseases spread quickly through sap-feeding insects, contaminated tools, farm workers' hands, wind, and rain splash, moving easily from infected plants to neighboring healthy crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ nu lɛ anɔ. nibii ni mli ewo muji Okwaafoi anitsumɔ nitsulɔ niji Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli mlɛo.

english: Why does a plant disease keep affecting new living crops on my farm season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai saa tsei heei ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe daa be lɛ?

english: Disease organisms can survive in the soil, on weeds, or in infected planting materials, allowing the sickness to attack new living crops as soon as they start growing.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ sũ mli, yɛ jwɛi anɔ, loo yɛ dumɔ nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli. Ha hela atutua tsei heei ni hiɛ ka lɛ kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Will my crop recover on its own if I leave a diseased plant in the ground?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa kɛji mishi tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Most crops do not recover on their own once infested with a serious disease. Leaving them in the ground allows the sickness to grow stronger and infect the rest of your farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛŋ aná hewalɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛji hela ni naa wa ba. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ mli awa ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my healthy crops if there is a disease outbreak in my community?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe kɛji hela ko ba mi akutso lɛ mli?

english: You can protect your farm by planting disease-resistant crop varieties, cleaning your boots and farm tools before working, and removing any sick plants as soon as you spot them.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Tsumɔ bɔɔtu kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ahe dani otsu nii. Ni jiemɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ kɛji ona amɛ pɛ.

english: Why do some plant diseases attack many different kinds of crops on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai komɛi tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Certain plant diseases are very aggressive and can infect many types of living plants because they feed on basic plant tissues shared by different crop families.
ga: Tsei ahelai komɛi amli wa waa ni ebaanyɛ emɔ tsei srɔtoi babaoo ni hiɛ ka lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ tsei ahe fãji titrii ni ajaa yɛ tsei awekui srɔtoi ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I check rainfall patterns before choosing what to plant on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa dani mahala nɔ ni madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Studying rainfall patterns helps you choose crops that match the water available in your area, saving you money and effort by preventing crop failure from too little or too much water.
ga: Bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa lɛ he nikasemɔ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ nu ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kpãa gbee. Kɛ shika kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ato kɛtsɔ nu fioo loo nu babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni oootsi naa koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need weather information if I already know my land gets low rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji he hiaa mi lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mile momo akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Weather patterns change from year to year. Updated weather info alerts you to unusual heavy rains or extended dry spells so you can adjust your planting time and protect your crops.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ daa afi. Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni atsake lɛ baabɔ bo kɔkɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ nɔ loo hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ otsake be ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ ni obu onibii ahe.

english: How do I know if a piece of land receives enough rain for a new farming project?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ miinɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔ ni sa kɛha okwaayeli nitsumɔ hee ko?

english: You can look at local weather reports and rainfall records for the area to see the average amount and pattern of rain that falls throughout the growing season.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he amaniɛbɔɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he saji ni aŋmala ashwie shi yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ koni ona nugbɔshiimɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛ bɔ ni enɛɔ ehaa lɛ mlijaa mlijaa.

english: What key weather details should I check before starting a new planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee?

english: You should check the area's overall rainfall patterns, the short-term weather forecast, and when the last rain fell to ensure the soil has the right condition for seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ akwɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Be kukuoo mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu kɛ naagbee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná shihilɛ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How does the day it last rained help me decide when to sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ naagbee nugbɔshiimɔ gbi lɛ ye ebua mi ni mikpɛ miyiŋ yɛ be ni esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ he?

english: The date of the last rain tells you if the soil currently holds enough moisture to nurture seeds so they can germinate and sprout successfully.
ga: Gbi ni naagbee nugbɔ lɛ baaba lɛ baatsɔɔ bo kɛji akɛ amrɔ nɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛje kpo yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: Is it safe to plant my seeds in dry ground before rain falls, or should I wait until after it rains?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ anɛ? Aloo esa akɛ mamɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait for a good rain to fall first. Planting in moist soil ensures your seeds get immediate water to start growing without sitting dry in the hot dirt.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ kpakpa klɛŋklɛŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtara shi ni amɛgbi tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I pick the exact best day to plant my crops after the rain season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala gbi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu tsei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee sɛɛ?

english: You pick the best planting day by monitoring recent rain events; planting shortly after a steady rain guarantees the ground is damp enough for seed growth.
ga: Ohalaa gbi ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaadu nii kɛtsɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ ni onyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui akwɛ̃.

english: If my land is naturally dry, why would heavy rain become a major problem for my farm?
ga: Kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ji naagba wulu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Dry soil often cannot absorb sudden heavy rain quickly. The extra water can flood the field, wash away topsoil, or rot crops that are adapted to dry conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ oya. Nu ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔji amli afua. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi ni atsake amɛ awo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli

english: What happens to seeds in the ground if a very heavy rain falls right after planting?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ?

english: Excessive heavy rain can wash seeds out of the soil, bury them too deep under mud, or trap them in standing water where they suffocate before sprouting.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ muji lɛ shishi tsɔ. Aloo okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo nu ni ekã shi, he ni amɛfoɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow crops on land with low rainfall without worrying about weather changes?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo nɔ ni mihaooo mihe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he?

english: No, even crops that survive with little water can be severely damaged if unexpected heavy rain falls or if a long dry spell strikes at the wrong growing stage.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi yɛ nu fioo pɛ nɔ lɛ po baanyɛ afite waa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ dalɛ be ni ejaaa mli

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I harvest them right after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Harvesting cassava when the ground is soaked can cause the roots to absorb excess water, making them spoil faster and harder to store. It is often better to wait until the soil drains slightly so the tubers are easier to dig up without getting damaged or muddy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei to be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa fe nine. Enɛ haa egboɔ oya, ni ewaa akɛ akɛtoɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fioo koni yitso lɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo ni ekɛ nɔ ko loo sũ baaa.

english: Why do cassava roots rot in the ground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain floods the farm and water cannot drain away, it starves the soil of air. Without air, the cassava tubers suffocate underground and fungal diseases take over, causing the roots to rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli obɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie nu lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ shishi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baye nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why does cassava become so expensive in the market during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei jara wa waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, muddy roads make it difficult for heavy vehicles to access farms to transport crops. Because less cassava reaches the towns and market centers, the limited supply drives up the market price.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ewo muji lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsɔnei wuji akɛ amɛaaya ŋmɔji amli koni amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aya. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei nyɛɛɛ aya maji kɛ jarayeli hei babaoo. Nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ fioo lɛ haa jarayeli jara lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How long do I have to sell my fresh cassava before it spoils after harvesting?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei hee dani efite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Freshly harvested cassava tubers are highly perishable and usually start to turn blue-black or spoil within 2 to 3 days. To prevent heavy losses, you must quickly transport them to the market or process them into products like gari or flour.
ga: Kasava shishifãi ni akpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya. ni bei pii lɛ, ejeɔ shishi etsɔɔ bluu-diŋŋ loo efiteɔ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli. Bɔni afee ni akafite nibii babaoo Esa akɛ okɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ oya loo okɛ amɛ afee nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to plant cassava in Ghana so it gets enough water?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ Ghana koni maná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: The best time to plant cassava is at the onset of the rainy season, around March or April in southern Ghana. Planting early allows the stems to establish strong roots while soil moisture is reliable.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee March loo April yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa shishifãi ni wa yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What type of soil should I choose if I want to grow big cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni okwɛ ŋmei shishifãi wuji Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ esa akɛ mahala?

english: Cassava thrives best in loose, well-drained sandy-loam soil. Soil that is too heavy or rich in clay holds too much water, which restricts root expansion and causes waterlogging.
ga: Cassava kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni tsii tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ baa shi ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi.

english: How do I select healthy cassava stems to plant on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose stem cuttings from healthy, mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Select thick, firm stems with visible buds (nodes) and avoid stems showing signs of pests, diseases, or dryness.
ga: Halamɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ aniji. Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni anaa (nodes). Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo ŋmɔtɔ he okadii akpo lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it important to weed my young cassava farm frequently during the first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli shii abɔ yɛ ŋmei ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cassava plants grow slowly in their first three months and struggle to compete with aggressive weeds. Removing weeds early ensures the cassava gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to form strong tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei bibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkɛ jwɛi ni mli wa lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off, and digging up a sample plant will reveal thick, well-formed tubers.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni tsei ahe nɔkwɛmɔnii ni atsa lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ kpo.

english: Can I grow maize on the same field together with my cassava?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛfata ŋmãa he?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava with maize works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, leaving the slow-growing cassava to take over the field for the rest of the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Akɛni ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli hewɔ lɛ, ha ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow big. It can also happen if the soil is too wet or too dry, preventing the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni miisumɔ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ loo egbi tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce less harvest every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land year after year drains the soil of specific nutrients. The soil becomes tired, so crops cannot grow as well unless you rotate crops or feed the soil with manure or fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ miije shishi egbɔjɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ hu nyɛŋ akwɛ̃. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear field without tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct heat and harsh sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. They need temporary shade crops like plantains to shield them and keep the soil moist while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and dry up so quickly when the Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛji harmattan be lɛ je shishi lɛ?
