english: The Harmattan brings dry winds that pull moisture out of plant leaves much faster than roots can drink water from the soil. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass or leaves helps trap moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi tsuɔ nii ni ekɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds and rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ miinɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that do not go deep into the ground. If planted too shallowly or left without support wooden stakes when bearing heavy fruit bunches, strong winds can easily blow them over.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo ashi ni tso ko bɛ ni fiɔ sɛɛ beni awoɔ aduawai akui wuji lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atsɔ mli oya.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land with my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops like groundnuts and beans have roots that capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This naturally enriches the land and helps neighboring crops like corn grow stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and turn black just a few days after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots start spoiling as soon as they are dug up because air enters cuts made during harvest. To avoid loss, cassava should remain in the soil until you are ready to sell, process, or eat it.
ga: Kɛji atsa cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ pɛ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli ni efoɔ amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. koni akafite lɛ Esa akɛ Cassava ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ, obaatsu he nii, loo oye.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches and water shoots from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ tsei krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots steal water and nutrients that the tree needs to produce cocoa pods. Pruning them helps the tree direct its energy into healthy cocoa pods and improves air movement to stop diseases like black pod.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni ekɛfee kookoo ŋmeii. Tso lɛ mlifomɔ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akɛkpa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant suffers from irregular watering. Stress makes the plant drop flowers to save water and energy rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be hewɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow small and produce poor harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibioo ni amɛwooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than farm crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and water away from them. Leaving weeds on your farm starves your crops, making them weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni nu lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe waa Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can a plant disease move from an infected crop to a healthy one just by using my cutlass?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ajie tso hela ko kɛjɛ tso ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ lɛ mli kɛya tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ mi-dagger lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, when you cut a sick plant, the germs stay in the wet sap on your cutlass blade. If you use the same tool on a healthy plant without cleaning it first, you push the germs directly into the healthy plant's sap.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofo tso ko ni hela mɔ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baakã nu ni efɔ ni yɔɔ otsɔne lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ okɛ dɛŋdade kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii yɛ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ ni otsuuu he klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Obaatsi helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ awo tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How does cassava mosaic disease spread across my whole farm so fast?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni cassava mosaic hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: The disease is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck sap from sick cassava plants and carry the virus to healthy ones. It also spreads when you plant stem cuttings taken from a infected plant.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ haa mɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa hu kɛ́ okɛ niji ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ko ni hela emɔ lɛ mli lɛ du.

english: What causes these small caterpillars to eat my young maize leaves so quickly at night?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ oya gbɛkɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the plant funnel during the hot day to protect themselves and come out at night to feed heavily on the soft, young leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ Fall Armyworms ji enɛɛmɛi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. ni amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛbaye baai bibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by these insects that distorts how the plant grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ hiɛɔ ni fiteɔ bɔ ni tsei daraa amɛhaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it risky to plant my maize right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry heat wave. If you plant too early, the soil dries up again and kills the germinating seeds before the main rainy season truly starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ekoŋŋ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Why should I trim or cut off extra branches from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo majie niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches forces the plant to send its food, water, and energy into making big fruits instead of wasting energy growing useless extra leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ hewalɛ aha koni ewo yibii babaoo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's harvest produce less food than bought hybrid seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid ni ahe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred in a lab for maximum strength in their first generation. When you save and replant those seeds, they lose those special qualities, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni ená hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Nakai dumɔwui lɛ baafite nakai nibii krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is lacking nutrients before my crop starts dying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aje shishi amɛgboi?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, young crops grow slowly, stems remain thin, and leaves look light green or yellow instead of deep green.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops dry up faster during a short drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa be kukuoo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water and nutrients from deep in the soil much faster than your crops can, leaving your crops hungry and thirsty.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Ha hɔmɔ kɛ kumai aye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do the market prices of my crops drop so low immediately after the main harvest starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: During the main harvest, almost every farmer brings their crops to market at the same time, creating a heavy supply. When there is more food in the market than buyers need, prices drop significantly until scarcity returns.
ga: yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ mli Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ okwaafoi fɛɛ kɛ amɛŋmɔshi nibii baa jara nɔ yɛ be kome mli. nibii babaoo ni akɛhaa lɛ feemɔ Beni niyenii babaoo yɛ jara nɔ fe bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ Jara baa shi waa kɛyashi niyenii ni faaa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can I stagger my planting so my crops do not mature all at the same time?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ midumɔ nii lɛ amli bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akakwɛ̃ shikome?

english: By planting your fields in smaller batches a few weeks apart instead of all in one day, your crops will reach maturity at different times. This allows you to harvest continuously and avoid selling everything when market prices are at their lowest.
ga: Kɛtsɔ tsei ni ooodu yɛ kui bibii amli lɛ nɔ Okɛ amɛ abɔ otsii fioo komɛi moŋ fe ni ooodu amɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome mli. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa okpamɔ lɛ nɔ, ni otsiɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni okɛbaajara lɛ he be mli ni jara lɛ baa shi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so quickly while I am waiting for market prices to go up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ miifite oya be mli ni mimɛɔ ni jara nɔ jara aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Crops are living things that continue to breathe and lose water after being harvested. High heat and trapped moisture cause rapid rotting, so proper drying, good airflow, and shade are needed to keep them fresh until prices improve.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ji nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛnuɔ nu kɛji akpa amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ fitemɔ baa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni agbi. kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ kɛ hulutsoo koni ekɛha ŋmɔlɔ ahi shi kɛyashi jara lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Why do major crop markets like Techiman always have produce available even when it is scarce in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jarayeli hei wuji tamɔ Techiman woɔ yibii be fɛɛ be lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ nɔ ko faaa yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Large central markets receive produce from many different regions across the country that have different rainfall patterns and harvest times, allowing new supply to arrive continuously as older supply sells out.
ga: Jarayelihe wulu ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nine shɛɔ nibii ni anáa kɛjɛɔ kpokpai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni amɛyɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi srɔtoi kɛ kpamɔ bei srɔtoi. Enɛ haa nibii heei baa be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nibii momo lɛ eho.

english: How can I keep my crops producing yields during the dry season when food is scarce?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni niyenii faaa lɛ?

english: Plants require consistent moisture and soil cover to produce during dry periods. Using simple irrigation, mulching to trap moisture, and planting drought-resistant seed varieties allows crops to thrive when water is limited.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛwo yibii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Mulching koni akɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ni dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ kɛji nu faaa.

english: Why do early-maturing crop varieties often yield smaller harvests than long-season varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe tsei ni shwereɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Early-maturing plants spend fewer days absorbing sunlight and nutrients from the soil before fruiting. While they give you a smaller total harvest, they allow you to sell early when food is scarce and prices are high.
ga: Tsei ni daa oya lɛ heɔ be fioo dani amɛheɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo moŋ. Shi eyeɔ ebua bo hu ni ohɔ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ niyenii namɔ wa ni ejara hu wa.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth during a dry spell even if they do not die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji tso lɛ gbooo po.

english: Water carries nutrients from the soil throughout the plant. When water is low, the plant enters a survival mode, slowing its growth and delaying maturity until it gets enough moisture again.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa tso lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ nu fioo pɛ eshwɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli. Ehaa edalɛ yaa hiɛ blɛoo ni ehaa edalɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ baaná ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look smaller and softer when I leave them on the farm past their harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni kpamɔɔ be lɛ ho lɛ?

english: Once a crop reaches full maturity, it stops putting energy into growing. Leaving it in the soil too long causes it to lose moisture, dry out, or get damaged by soil pests, reducing its quality and weight.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Ebaakpa hewalɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii koni ekɛda lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afite, ebaaha egbi, loo sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite lɛ. Nɔ ni hi kɛ nɔ ni tsiimɔ baa shi

english: Why do pests attack my crops more heavily when weather conditions become hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ waa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: During hot and dry periods, wild vegetation dries up, forcing insects to move to green farm crops for food and water. Additionally, rain naturally washes away many small pests and insect eggs.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yaa nɔ lɛ Tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ baagbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ kooloi bibii aya ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Nugbɔ hu shwieɔ kooloi bibii babaoo kɛ amɛwuji lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant the exact same crop on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the field. Rotating different crops helps restore soil fertility and keeps pests away.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand into large tubers. Building tall mounds gives the yam room to grow downwards easily without hitting hard ground, while also protecting the tubers from rot caused by excess water.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato tsu lɛ daa shi oya ni etswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ ni nu ni fa fe nine kɛbaa lɛ he.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water collects around them and starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly, keeping the soil moist but not waterlogged.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua amɛhe naa. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmeii yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋmeii anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ shi nu akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for green leaf growth. Applying manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves regain their rich green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ni akɛ ŋmeii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I wait a few weeks after my seeds sprout before putting fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young sprouts have tiny, tender roots that can get burned and damaged if strong fertilizer touches them directly. Waiting a few weeks allows the plant to develop a strong root system that can absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bashɛ tso lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ Otsii fioo komɛi ni ooomɛ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa ni baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time and sprout immediately when rain falls. Because weeds are wild, native plants, they naturally adapt faster to the local soil and draw up water and nutrients quicker than crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ oya. ni eŋɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when exposed to full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have thin leaves and shallow roots that lose water very quickly in direct heat. They require shade from temporary plants like plantains or shade trees to shelter them from sunlight until their root systems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ shɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ amli baawa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. When the plant experiences stress from heat or irregular watering, it sheds its flowers to preserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ tsei na dɔlɛ mli haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ Eshwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until there have been two or three steady rains so the soil becomes deeply wet. Planting right after the very first light rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry out again and kill the newly germinated seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ekoŋŋ ni ebaanyɛ egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three to four months, leaving the space open for the slower-growing cassava to expand later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 3-4 mli, ni ehaa gbɛ haa ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni eshwere yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: What causes small worms to eat the inner leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ amli baai lɛ?

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, which hatch from eggs laid by small moths. The worms crawl into the dark, moist center funnel of the young maize plant where the leaves are softest to feed on them.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fɔɔ lɛ amli. Kplukai lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ duŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli, he ni ayeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build strong leaves and stalks. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plant the food it needs to turn dark green and grow fast.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ wulu ko baanɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away fertilizer off the topsoil before the roots have time to soak it in. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist so the nutrients dissolve slowly near the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo koni niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsɔ fiofio. ni bɛŋkɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by high heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its own energy instead of growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite yɛ aduawai ni ebaakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, and it will bounce back as the air cools in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni ebaaku esɛɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs have missing seeds and empty spaces on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii ni elaaje ni ŋmeii yɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Empty spots on a maize cob happen when pollen from the top flower fails to land on every single silk strand during flowering. Strong dry winds or severe heat can dry out the silk before pollination is complete.
ga: He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ siliki kpãai lɛ fɛɛ ahe yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni mli egbi loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha siliki lɛ agbi dani pollination lɛ agbe naa.

english: Why does cutting off the top tip of my pepper plant make it grow bushier?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afo pepper tso lɛ naa lɛ, ehaa efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: The main growing tip releases a signal that prevents side branches from growing. When you cut or pinch off the top tip, that signal stops, forcing the plant to send its energy into growing side branches and producing more fruit.
ga: Nɔ titri ni yaa hiɛ lɛ jieɔ okadii ni tsiɔ niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara. Kɛ́ ofo loo ofo tso lɛ naagbee lɛ, Nakai okadi lɛ baakpa. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo aya niji ni miida lɛ anɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As these pests suck out the sap, they twist the leaf tissue and can pass diseases that stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Amɛ tsɔɔ baa fãji amli ni amɛ baanyɛ amɛ gbɛ helai ni tsiɔ tsei adalɛ naa lɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains flood the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy water sits on the field for days, oxygen is cut off, causing the roots to drown and making them vulnerable to rot fungi in the wet soil.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nu afua lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ baafo shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ oshara ni ji ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ miitswa ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn under direct, full sunlight. Planting fast-growing food crops like plantains next to cocoa creates a living canopy that provides the gentle shade young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ Cocoa masɛi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa hulutsoo ni mli jɔ ni he hiaa cocoa bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are naturally adapted to grab water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops a fair chance to grow without being starved of light and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mli.

english: How do I know which crop variety is best to plant in my district this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akwɛ yɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Different regions have specific soil types and rainfall patterns. Agricultural officers conduct regional tests to recommend crop varieties that are bred to resist local pests and produce the highest yield in your specific climate.
ga: Kpokpai srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ kɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ehaa. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi feɔ kpokpaa nɔ kaai koni amɛkɛtsɔɔ tsei srɔtoi ni akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ kunim kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it helpful to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why does planting cassava on the same plot for three years in a row make the tubers smaller each year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii 3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava draws specific nutrients out of the earth. Repeating the same crop year after year empties the soil of those nutrients, causing smaller yields unless you rotate crops or add fertilizer.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, nakai niyenii kpakpai lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants rot at the roots after a few days of heavy flooding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ nu afua ni naa wa ni eho gbii babaoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot breathe. This weakened state allows soil fungi to easily attack and rot the roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Nɛkɛ shihilɛ ni egbɔjɔ nɛɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baatutua ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ fite.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and curl up when dry spells begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl to reduce their surface area and save moisture, while yellowing happens because dry soil prevents the roots from absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛba hiɛ shi ni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ.

english: Why do my seedlings grow tall and weak instead of strong when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ hewalɛ najiaŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for limited sunlight, stretching upward as fast as possible to reach the light, which leaves them thin and easily broken.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa. Kɛtsɔ ŋwɛi ni oootsɔ oya bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni omɔ kane lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam plants produce small tubers when they are grown in the shade of large trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy through photosynthesis, which gets stored underground as big tubers. Shade limits this energy production, resulting in smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi akɛ ŋmeii wuji Shade tsiɔ hewalɛ ni anáa nɛɛ naa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the stem before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by sudden extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil, which stops proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa pollination ni sa lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do some of my maize seeds fail to sprout even after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep for oxygen to reach them, if the soil surface is too packed hard, or if underground insects eat the seed core.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli fã lɛ.

english: Why do my okro plants flower very early when the weather becomes extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra tso lɛ fɔɔ oya be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat signals to the okro plant that its environment is becoming harsh, triggering it to flower quickly so it can make seeds and reproduce before the weather damages it.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsɔɔ gumbo lɛ akɛ shihilɛ ni eyɔɔ mli lɛ miifee nɔ ni mli wa. Ehaa fɔfɔii shwereɔ oya No hewɔ lɛ abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui ni afɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ dani kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants look small and yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves mean the soil has lost its nutrients, which are the plant's energy source. Rain provides water, but plants also need food in the soil to grow big and green. Adding compost or fertilizer restores this lost soil energy.
ga: Baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, ni ji tso lɛ hewalɛ jɛɛhe lɛ elaaje shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi tsei hu he miihia niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I prevent goats and farm animals from eating my young cassava plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Free-roaming animals prefer tender green leaves. Planting live fences around your field, like thorny bushes or Jatropha plants, creates a natural barrier that keeps goats out without needing expensive fencing.
ga: Koolooi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Aduɔ ŋmɔji ahe tsei ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ ŋmeii loo jatropha tsei. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa tooi akabote mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni atswa ŋtayaa ni jara wa.

english: Why do insects suddenly appear in large numbers as soon as my crops start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo baa trukaa kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Flowers and young buds attract pests quickly because they are sweet and full of nutrients. Pests multiply fast at this stage, so checking your farm every few days helps you spot them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai oya ejaakɛ amɛmli ŋɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Gbii fioo komɛi baaha ona amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil until the soil becomes exhausted. Rotating maize with beans or groundnuts helps restore energy and balance back into the land.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ kɛ jɛkɛmɔ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good to plant groundnuts and cassava together in the same farm plot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the cassava plants. Planting them together protects the soil and gives you two different crops from one piece of land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmei tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive in direct sunlight because intense heat drains their moisture. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby protects young cocoa plants like an umbrella until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni naa wa lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he tamɔ hulutsoo kɛyashi tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil and react instantly to sunlight and water. Because weeds naturally grow faster than cultivated crops, clearing land prompts them to emerge quickly and steal soil energy from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji hulu la kɛ nu ba amɛnɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni oootsi lɛ baaha jwɛi aba oya ni ebaaju shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, will I harvest more food?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil energy. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow big cobs, tubers, or fruits.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji, ŋmeii, loo aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits in heavy soil for too long, it cuts off air to the plant roots and causes fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ekɛduɔ shishifãi ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani midu pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, such as sudden hot weather or uneven watering. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass or leaves keeps the roots cool and moist, stopping flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛmiifee nɔ ko, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Tsi fɔfɔii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi

english: How deep into the soil do rice roots actually grow?
ga: Te ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rice roots are quite shallow compared to many other crops. They generally grow only up to about 30 centimeters (around 1 foot) deep into the ground.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi ahe. Bei pii lɛ amɛ daa aaafee sɛntimitai 30 pɛ (aaafee nane kome) kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why is the topsoil so important for my rice crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Because rice roots are shallow and only reach about 30 centimeters deep, the plant can only feed on the nutrients available in the top layer of soil (topsoil).
ga: Akɛni ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛmli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 30 pɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ aye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (topsoil) lɛ pɛ.

english: Can my rice plants reach nutrients that sink deep underground after heavy rains?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ baanyɛ ana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: No, rice roots cannot go very deep into the ground. If nutrients wash down past the top 30 centimeters of soil, the rice plant will not be able to reach or use them.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa shishifãi nyɛŋ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe sɛntimita 30 lɛ, ŋmãa tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he loo amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Do all crops take their food from the same depth in the ground?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kome mli?

english: No, crops have different root depths. Shallow-rooted crops like rice only draw food from the top layer of soil, while deeper-rooted crops can reach nutrients further underground.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ srɔtoi. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my rice crop dry out faster than crops with deep roots when rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni shishifãi ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ?

english: Rice roots only stay in the top 30 centimeters of the soil. Since the surface layer of soil dries out first during dry spells, shallow-rooted crops lose access to water quickly.
ga: Omɔ shishifãi lɛ nɔ kwɔ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛntimita 30 pɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɛ́ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛná nu oya.

english: Where should I place fertilizer when feeding crops with shallow roots like rice?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ mikɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ miiha niyenii?

english: You should apply fertilizer in the topsoil layer near the surface because shallow roots only stay in the top 30 centimeters of soil and cannot absorb fertilizer buried too deep.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛntimitai 30 pɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afu amɛ tsɔ lɛ.

english: What happens if I apply too much fertilizer to my rice field at one time?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmɔ mli yɛ be kome mli?

english: Applying too much at once is wasteful because shallow roots can only absorb a limited amount of nutrients from the topsoil at a time, and the excess will wash away or damage the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ babaoo wo mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ, eji shikafitemɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii fioo ko pɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ni nɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ baaho loo ebaafite tso lɛ.

english: Why is it better to split fertilizer applications for shallow-rooted crops rather than putting it all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ amli srɔtoi baatsu nii moŋ fe ni akɛbaatsu nii shikome lɛ?

english: Since shallow roots only feed from the top layer of soil, applying fertilizer in smaller split doses gives the crop time to take up the nutrients before they wash beyond the 30-centimeter root zone.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ niyenii mli nibii dani ahoɔ amɛhe kɛhoɔ shishifãi ni ji sɛntimita 30 lɛ he.

english: How do I know if the manure or fertilizer I applied is actually helping my rice?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: If applied properly in the topsoil where the shallow 30-centimeter roots live, the plant will easily absorb the nutrients, leading to healthier green leaves and better growth.
ga: Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛlɛ ji sɛntimitai 30 lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ŋmɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does soil depth matter when choosing a farm plot for growing rice?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ he hiaa yɛ ŋmãa shikpɔji ni ahalaa lɛ mli?

english: Rice only needs good, fertile soil in the top 30 centimeters because its roots do not go deep, making rich topsoil much more important than very deep soil layers for rice.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baa nii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi sɛntimitai 30 lɛ pɛ he miihia ŋmãa. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ he hiaa fe shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ kɛha ŋmãa.

english: Why do I need to spray crop medicine under the leaves instead of just on top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afɔse ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ ŋwɛigbɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Many farm pests and fungal diseases hide on the cooler underside of leaves or at the base of the plant. Applying medicine underneath targets where the pests actually live and prevents rain from easily washing the treatment away.
ga: Okwaafoi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ashishi loo yɛ tsei ashishi ni mli ejɔ lɛ anɔ. Tsofa ni akɛwoɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ shishi ni atsĩɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ tsofa lɛ oya

english: Why do some insects only attack the bottom part of my crop stems near the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi komɛi tutuaa tsei ashishigbɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: The base of the plant stem stays shaded, cool, and moist compared to the top leaves. This creates a comfortable environment for soil pests to feed without drying out in the hot Ghanaian sun.
ga: Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yɛ hulutsoo, edɔ, ni edɔ kɛ akɛto ŋwɛi baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nii ni amɛgbiŋ yɛ Ghana hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why didn't my crop medicine work even though I sprayed the whole field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔshi tsofai lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ? Ani afɔse ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Pesticides often fail if they were mixed using metal tools that neutralised the chemical, applied in hot mid-day sun, or sprayed on top of leaves while pests were hiding underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ dade nibii ni haa tsofai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ futu mli. Okɛwo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Aloo shwiemɔ baai lɛ anɔ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi.

english: Is it bad if I stir my liquid crop chemical with an iron rod or metal knife?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji akɛ mikɛ dade tso loo dade ŋmei shwie tso mli tsofai ni ji nu lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, iron and other metals chemically react with many crop medicines. Touching or stirring the medicine with metal neutralises its active ingredients, causing it to lose its power to protect your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, dade kɛ dade krokomɛi Ekɛ tsofai babaoo ni jɛ tsei amli lɛ feɔ ekome. Kɛ́ okɛ dade ta tsofa lɛ he loo okɛfutu lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni okɛbuɔ onibii ahe lɛ laajeɔ.

english: What is the best type of tool to use when mixing pest medicine for my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui miifutu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Always use plastic buckets and clean wooden or plastic stirrers. Non-metallic materials do not react with chemicals, ensuring your medicine keeps its full strength.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ plastic baagi kɛ tso loo plastic ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni he tse atsu nii. Nibii ni jeee dade kɛ tsofai efeŋ nɔ ko. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ oná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofa lɛ baaya nɔ ahi ehewalɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Can I use an iron bucket to hold my chemical spray liquid?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ dade tsɔji ato mi tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, metal buckets can corrode and chemically weaken your crop medicine. Rust particles from the metal can also break off and clog your knapsack sprayer nozzle.
ga: Dabi, dade tsɔji baanyɛ afite ni eha oŋmɔshi tsofa lɛ agbɔjɔ. Rust nibii ni jɛ dade mli lɛ hu baanyɛ atse ni amɛtsi osɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli spray nozzle lɛ naa.

english: Why does my crop medicine lose its power if I leave the container unsealed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmɔshi tsofa lɛ he waaa kɛji mishi tsɛnsi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Air, moisture, and heat break down the chemical compounds in crop medicines over time. Keeping containers tightly closed protects the medicine's strength until you are ready to use it.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ, hulutsoo, kɛ dɔlɛ fiteɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe tsofai amli lɛ yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsɛnsi lɛ ŋmɛ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu tsofa lɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do the roots at the base of my crops rot even when the leaves look green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ shishi lɛ miifite lɛ? Ani baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli lolo?

english: Water and humidity tend to build up right around the base of the stem, encouraging soil fungi to attack the roots. Applying treatment directly to the base helps protect the hidden root zone.
ga: Nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɔɔ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi, ni ewoɔ sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo shishitoo lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shishifã ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds right around the stem base of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds clustered near the plant base trap extra moisture and create a dark shelter for pests to multiply, while also stealing nutrients directly from your crop's root area.
ga: Jwɛi ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo ni amɛfeɔ he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ koni amɛfɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ hu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How close to the plant base should I apply fertilizer or soil medicine?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ mli nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tɛŋŋ?

english: Apply treatments in a small circle around the base where the roots spread out, but avoid letting raw chemicals touch the main stem directly so you do not burn the plant.
ga: Kɛ kooyigbɛ bibii atsu nii ni okɛmiibɔle shishigbɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he. Shi kaahã tsofai ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. koni akashã tso lɛ

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my farmland makes the next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special crops that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This acts like a natural fertilizer for whatever crop you plant in that soil next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama ŋmɔtɔ ko masɛi koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are vines that need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp soil to catch maximum sunlight and protects the leaves from rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo, ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my growing maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help them recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a viral sickness spread by these insects. Sprinkling soapy water or using appropriate organic sprays can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Nu ni akɛ samla shwieɔ nɔ loo akɛ tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the heat becomes too high or when the plant experiences water stress during flowering. Regular watering during hot afternoons helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I wait for two or three good rains before planting my maize seeds instead of planting after the very first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ kpakpa? shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ dani adu ŋmãa Dumɔwui Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ

english: The first rain of the season can be a 'false rain' followed by a long dry spell. Waiting for consistent rains ensures the soil stays moist enough for seeds to germinate and survive without drying up.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee ‘amale nugbɔ’ ni hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the lower branches from my healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so air and sunlight can pass through freely. This prevents moisture buildup that causes black pod disease and encourages the tree to send energy to fruiting.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli oya. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛfite hewalɛ kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the entire plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava shows it is ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and fall off naturally, and cracks appear in the soil around the base of the stem where the roots are expanding.
ga: Akɛɛ Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi he ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ yɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it good to cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating soil water, keeps the root area cool, and blocks weeds from stealing nutrients from your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Etsiɔ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do my crop roots rot and turn yellow when too much rainwater sits on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water stays on the soil for too long, it pushes out all the air, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool, stops heat from drying out water in the ground, and protects topsoil from being washed away by heavy rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi haa Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa dɔlɛ baa shi koni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akagbi. ni ebuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Is there any medicine or chemical spray I can put in floodwater to save crops that are submerged?
ga: Ani tsofai loo tsofai komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ mikɛwo nu afua mli koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ?

english: There is no chemical medicine that can undo water damage. Once crops are submerged and suffocate from too much water, the only fix is to drain the water away from the field as fast as possible.
ga: Tsofai komɛi bɛ ni baanyɛ asaa nu ni efite lɛ. Kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ Nɔ pɛ ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii ji ni ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya bɔ ni aaanyɛ.

english: Why do dark spots and rot appear on my crop leaves every time it rains continuously for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Constant rain creates high moisture and wet leaves, which are perfect conditions for fungal diseases to grow and spread quickly across your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ baai ni efɔ baa. Enɛɛmɛi ji shihilɛi ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ onibii fɛɛ amli.

english: What major problems should I expect my crops to face during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ naagbai wuji esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛbaakpe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: During heavy rains, crops often suffer from waterlogged roots, soil erosion that washes away plant nutrients, and an increase in leaf fungal diseases due to constant wetness.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ amanehulu. Shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi, ni haa tsei amli niyenii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my crops wilt so quickly during the dry season even when I give them a little water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: In the dry season, high heat and dry air pull moisture out of plant leaves faster than small amounts of surface water can reach the deep roots.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni nu bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ ahe.

english: How can I prepare my land to help my crops survive the transition from the rainy season to the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ tsakemɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛyaa hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli?

english: Adding organic compost and building good soil structure during the rainy season allows the soil to trap deep moisture, which keeps plants alive longer when rains stop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he ni afee shikpɔŋ kpakpa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: How can I prevent heavy rain from collecting around my crops and ruining my harvest?
ga: Matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabua ehe naa yɛ mihe. Te ebaafee tɛŋŋ efite miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwo lɛ?

english: Digging shallow drainage channels around your fields and planting crops on raised soil beds allows heavy rainwater to flow safely off your farm instead of standing around crop roots.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni oootsi Oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ akashɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɔle tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my vegetables during the hot dry season?
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ aduawai anɔ nu?

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening gives plants time to absorb moisture into their roots before the strong sun causes the water to evaporate.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ náa be ni ekɛŋɔ nu kɛboteɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli dani hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ.

english: Can I harvest and store crop fruits that were soaked in floodwater before picking?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa tsei ni akɛwo nu mli dani mikɛto lɛ aduawai ni mikɛto?

english: Crops harvested from flooded fields spoil very quickly because excess water weakens their skin and invites rot, so they should be consumed immediately or dried right away.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ oya waa ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa hewolo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efiteɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aye amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo agbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains on the same farm where I am planting my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei bibii yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive the harsh sun during their first few years. Plantain trees grow very quickly and provide big leaves that shield the young cocoa plants while also giving you food to harvest early on.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hɔnɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii ni obaakpa mra.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting cocoa before I can harvest my first pods?
ga: Kɛ́ odu kookoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani onyɛ okpa oklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: With improved cocoa varieties available today, you can expect your trees to start bearing pods in about two to three years, whereas older traditional varieties usually take around four to five years.
ga: Kɛtsɔ cocoa henɔi ni atsake lɛ ni yɔɔ amrɔ nɛɛ nɔ lɛ Obaanyɛ okpa gbɛ akɛ otso lɛ baaje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ daa lɛ, bei pii lɛ eheɔ aaafee afii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ.

english: How can I tell if the piece of land I have is good enough for crop farming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ fa kɛha okwaayeli?

english: Good agricultural soil is typically dark brown or black, crumbles easily in your hand, and drains water well so it does not stay flooded for long periods after heavy rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ, efiteɔ oya yɛ nine mli, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɛɛɛ nu afua mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together just to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with smaller yields instead of producing healthy harvests.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ najiaŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same plot without ruining the harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to spread out later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every time I plant the exact same crop on the same land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack that specific plant to build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate that your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need for strong growth, or that the ground is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Weeds are natural wild plants built to survive tough conditions, so they quickly absorb sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than your planted crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme hot weather, inconsistent watering, or a lack of insects like bees to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yashɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baahã fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination lɛ ni bɛ

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my farm so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni jwɛi akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist right after a light rain, and gently mix it into the soil near the roots so it isn't washed away by heavy rainfall or dried out by sunlight.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ, ni okɛfutu shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli blɛoo koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo hulu la akashwie nɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip and moving down the middle mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early in the plant's life helps bring back the healthy green color and supports fast growth.
ga: Kaadii ni ji yellow lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ naagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eku esɛɛ efee eŋɔli ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eda oya.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even when I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same piece of land continuously drains the soil's natural nutrients. Rotating your main crop with legumes like beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts helps restore essential nutrients naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, tsina ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: The Harmattan brings harsh, dry winds and high temperatures that dry out young plants quickly. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates shade and keeps moisture in the soil to help them survive.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni mli egbi baa. kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ni haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba ni ehiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers heat stress or lacks consistent water during hot weather. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering regularly keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers stay on to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ naa piŋmɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ mli loo nu bɛ amɛnɔ daa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi shwie nɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes inside the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that feeds inside the central growing part of maize. Checking your farm early and applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides into the central leaf funnel helps stop them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa fãi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or infected stem cuttings. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties provided by local extension services.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu kɛtsɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmei nitsumɔhei ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will planting my crops closer together give me a bigger harvest from my field?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in smaller, weaker crops. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to develop fully and produce a higher yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young crops have weak roots and cannot easily compete with fast-growing weeds for food, water, and light. Clearing weeds early ensures all the soil's nutrients go directly to your young plants.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii, nu, kɛ la he mlɛo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii fɛɛ yaa otsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied to moist soil while the crop is actively growing. Applying fertilizer during heavy rain causes it to wash away, while applying it during severe drought can burn the plant roots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso shishifãi ashã.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting soon after I store them in my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi fitemɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛto mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised during harvest or kept in hot, unventilated spaces. Handling yams gently and storing them off the ground in a cool, airy yam barn prevents heat buildup and decay.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato tsu nii blɛoo ni okɛto shikpɔŋ yɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo akafee nɔ ko ni efite.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up while the plant is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new growth at the top, showing that your soil needs more nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo he miihia oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why did my crop leaves turn brown and dry up after I put fertilizer right next to the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii efata he yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is full of strong salts that suck moisture out of the plant roots and stems when placed too close. Leaving a small space between the stem and the fertilizer prevents this burning effect.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ. ja gbɛ bibioo ko ni kã tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ koni akashã

english: How can I tell if my crops are actually absorbing the fertilizer I apply instead of it being wasted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ moŋ fe ni mafite lɛ?

english: When crops take in fertilizer properly, you will see new leaves turning dark green and firm within a few days, and stems becoming thicker, showing that the plants are using the nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ awo tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ Obaana baa heei lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee shiŋŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsɔɔ akɛ tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry weather as a survival trick to save water. Once the rains return, the plant quickly sprouts new green leaves from its stems.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ. Taakɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ kɛha wala koni akɛhere nu yiwala. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli oya kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tight during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps the plant hold onto its water until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper plants often shed flowers when the weather is too hot or dry, or if they have too much water, because the plant becomes stressed and conserves energy rather than making fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji nu fa babaoo Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow much better when I plant them in a field where I previously grew groundnuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsutsu lɛ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans work with beneficial tiny organisms in the soil to fix nitrogen from the air into the dirt, leaving natural food behind for the next crop you plant.
ga: Peanuts kɛ nuts kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ekɛsaa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Shi adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on as many leaves as possible to make energy. Climbing up stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum light, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Tso lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ haa baai lɛ naa la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ daraa lɛ

english: Why does my maize grow thin and tall with very small cobs when weeds are around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli tse ni ekɛlɛ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni jwɛi ebɔle he lɛ

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight from your crop. The maize stretches tall to reach for light, using up energy that it should have used to build big, healthy cobs.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni eshɛ la lɛ he. Ekɛ hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛfee ŋmei agbo ni mli wa tsuɔ nii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the leaves and branches become too thick and crowded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɛ be mli ni baai kɛ eniji lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowded branches block sunlight from reaching the inner stem and trap moist air, which causes flowers to rot and diseases to spread, resulting in fewer cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ mligbɛ ni emɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the crop so it can make healthy food for itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha niyenii lɛ afee niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What do soil additives actually do to help my crops grow better during dry seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni akɛfataa sũ he lɛ tsuɔ koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Soil additives act like sponges and vitamins mixed into the dirt; they help the soil hold water longer and make it easier for plant roots to absorb food, keeping crops healthy even when rainfall is low.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ekɛ vitamini futuɔ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhe wa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?
