english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops end up competing with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough food to grow large, healthy produce.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant plantain trees alongside my young cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct heat. Fast-growing plantains provide broad shade leaves that act as living umbrellas, keeping the ground cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and droop in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a crop's natural defense against extreme heat. The plant folds its leaves to reduce surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve water so it does not dry out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in dark, wet conditions. Clearing thick weeds and trimming lower branches lets air and sunlight flow through, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la tsɔɔ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do fall armyworms manage to destroy my maize crop so fast?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fall armyworm lɛ nyɛ efite mi-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Adult moths lay hundreds of eggs on crop leaves at night. Once hatched, the caterpillars quickly crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on tender growing tissues, which stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Kplukai ni eda lɛ fɔɔ amɛwuji ohai abɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ gbɛkɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ fɔ lɛ ŋmei lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) koni amɛye fãji ni miida blɛoo lɛ. Enɛ haaa tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by high temperatures, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil evenly damp and encouraging insects helps the flowers successfully set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ be fɛɛ be loo fɔfɔi ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni eha kooloi bibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or get moldy so quickly after I put it in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ loo ehiɛɔ oya beni mikɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots when it is bagged while still containing internal moisture. Thoroughly drying the harvested grains in the sun before storage prevents mold spores and insects from surviving inside the bags.
ga: Abɛi baagbo kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo. Kɛ́ ogbala dumɔwui ni okpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu mli dani okɛto lɛ, no haaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii akaje kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why do improved hybrid seeds produce more bags of grain than seeds saved from last year's harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui kotokui babaoo fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ afi ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Improved seeds are carefully bred to resist local diseases, tolerate drought better, and use soil nutrients more efficiently, whereas saved seeds lose vigor over time and yield less harvest.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ kwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Hɔmɔ he tsuishitoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when I do not apply store-bought fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which helps plants build green leaves and grow strong. When there is not enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant moves its remaining nutrients from its older lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-abele lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Can fresh chicken manure burn my crops if I put it directly around the roots?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hee baanyɛ ashã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmei wo shishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, fresh chicken manure is very strong and contains high amounts of nitrogen and natural salts. When applied directly without aging, it creates a harsh environment that pulls water out of the plant roots, causing the roots and lower leaves to scorch or burn.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ ni efiteee Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli wa ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ baa. Eshãa loo eshãa shishifãi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: How does putting dried plant leaves around the bases of my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni egbi ni mikɛfataa mitsei lɛ ashishi he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves—known as mulching—acts like a protective blanket. It shields the soil from direct sunshine, keeps the ground cool, and stops soil water from evaporating into the air so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do crop seeds saved from last year's bought harvest produce weaker plants than the original seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni jɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli kpamɔ ni ahe lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ nii oya fe shishijee dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Many modern seeds sold in stores are hybrids created by crossing two specific parent plants for one high-yield generation. Seeds saved from those hybrid crops lose that combined strength, causing the next generation of crops to grow unevenly and produce smaller yields.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee kɛtsɔ fɔlɔi tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛná yinɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni amɛbaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Will allowing free-range chickens to walk through my vegetable field hurt my growing plants?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mahã kooloi ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ ayashara shi yɛ mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye mitsei ni miida lɛ awui?

english: Chickens can help your crops by eating damaging beetles and caterpillars, but they can also cause harm. If seedlings are young and tender, chickens may scratch up delicate roots or eat the fresh leaves, so it is best to let them in only after your crops are bigger and stronger.
ga: Kooloi baanyɛ aye abua onibii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi ebaanyɛ ekɛ awui hu aba. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, Kooloi baanyɛ atsɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ loo amɛye baai heei lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi amɛ pɛ kɛji otso lɛ eda ni ehe wa.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly when tiny insects land on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like aphids or thrips suck out the sap that gives leaves their strength and often spread plant viruses. The pepper leaves curl up as a stress response to the physical damage and liquid loss, which slows down the plant's ability to make food.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ aphids loo thrips Amɛmuɔ nu ni woɔ baai lɛ hewalɛ ni bei pii lɛ amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ amɛshwãa. Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ nɔnyɛɛ, gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ hetoo mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do cassava leaves grow very dark green and bushy after I spread poultry droppings in the garden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔji beni mikɛ kooloi afɔfɔi eshwie abɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Poultry droppings are rich in nitrogen, which is the main fuel plants use to build chlorophyll and green leaf tissue. When your cassava plant drinks up this nitrogen, it responds by producing dark green, bushy foliage and growing stems quickly.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ kooloi ashishifã mli. Eji tsofa titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ klorofil kɛ baa eŋɔli fãji. Kɛji o-cassava tsei lɛ nu nitrogen nɛɛ Ebaaha hetoo kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni daa oya lɛ ni ebaajie lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land yield much healthier crops after I let the field rest unused for two seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ beni miha ŋmɔji lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni mikɛtsuuu nii bei enyɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When land rests—a process called fallowing—wild vegetation grows back, naturally trapping rainwater and decomposing into organic matter. This restores nutrients to the soil, breaks pest and disease cycles, and gives the earth time to rebuild its strength naturally.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe - nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ defoliation - koo mli tsei daa ekoŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ buaa ehe naa kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akumɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ mli ni aha je lɛ be ni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow much stronger when planted on land where groundnuts grew previously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa waa waa kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ aduɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the groundnuts are harvested, that trapped nitrogen remains behind in the earth, giving the next maize crop a natural boost.
ga: Muawai ni ji naanyobɔɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmeii Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do wild weeds sprout much faster than my cassava cuttings after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to survive in the dirt for years waiting for water, so they sprout immediately to grab sunlight and soil nutrients. Cassava cuttings take longer because the stem must first spend energy growing new root systems before it can shoot leaves above ground.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo, ni amɛmɛ nu. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kasava ni afoɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo ejaakɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo shishifãi heei dani enyɛ ewo baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my cocoa farm producing fewer pods now than it did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Over many years of farming, crops continually absorb the natural goodness and nutrients from the earth. Without replacing those nutrients, the soil becomes tired and weak, leading to lower harvests.
ga: Yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, Nibii ni Aduɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli sɛɛnamɔi kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji tsakemɔ ko bako nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nijiaŋ jeɔ wui ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: How do I know if the land on my farm has lost its natural strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehiɛ ebɔi hewalɛ?

english: When farmland loses its nutrients, you will notice signs such as slow crop growth, yellowing leaves, smaller cocoa pods, and a steady decline in your total yield each season.
ga: Kɛji okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fite lɛ Obaana okadii tamɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, kɛ kookoo ŋmeii bibii. Ni nibii fɛɛ ni ofeɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why does farmland lose its richness even if I do not change how I farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli hei lɛ miifite amɛ nii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsakeee mi okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Every time you harvest cocoa pods, you are removing nutrients that the tree pulled from the ground. Over time, continuous harvesting empties the soil's natural food reserve.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ Ojieɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ gbalaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Nikpamɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What exactly does fertilizer do when I put it on my land?
ga: Mɛni tuuntu ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ kɛ mikɛwo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer acts as food for the soil. It replaces the essential nutrients that crops have used up over time, giving the land back its strength to support healthy growth.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ aku esɛɛ eba shi waa koni eye ebua dalɛ kpakpa.

english: Can my cocoa trees produce a good harvest without adding any fertilizer?
ga: Ani mi-kookoo tso lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii kpakpai kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko bɛ mli?

english: While cocoa trees can survive without fertilizer, worn-out soil cannot provide enough food for a heavy crop, resulting in smaller pods and lower yield compared to well-nourished soil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei baanyɛ ahi shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehiaaa amɛ moŋ, shi shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aha niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni niyenii kpakpa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Is fertilizer just medicine for sick crops, or do healthy cocoa trees need it too?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ji tsofa kɛkɛ aloo kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Fertilizer is regular food rather than just medicine. Even healthy trees need continuous feeding from nutrient-rich soil to keep producing large, healthy cocoa pods every season.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji niyenii ni ayeɔ daa moŋ fe tsofa kɛkɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po he miihia niyenii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How does the fertilizer I put on the ground actually reach and help my cocoa trees?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shɛɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ?

english: Rainfall dissolves the fertilizer into the earth, where the cocoa tree's roots drink it up and send those essential nutrients up into the trunk, leaves, and pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Cacao tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishi, ebaa, kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Will using fertilizer ruin my land if I apply it every year?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli daa afi lɛ, ani ebaafite shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: When applied in the correct recommended amounts, fertilizer does not ruin the land; instead, it safely replaces what the crop takes away, keeping the soil fertile for future years.
ga: Kɛji akɛ aŋɔ yɛ falɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Ŋmei lɛ fiteŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Shi ebaaye nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyaa lɛ najiaŋ shweshweeshwe. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ afii babaoo ni baaba lɛ.

english: Why do agriculture officers place so much focus on teaching us about soil food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he tsɔɔmɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ?

english: Extension officers focus on soil nutrition because proper feeding of the land is the most direct way to increase crop production and secure better income for farming families.
ga: Extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpa nɔ. Enɛ ji akɛ, niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ji gbɛ ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni ehaa shika ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa okwaayeli wekui anɔ.

english: Does putting fertilizer on my land guarantee an immediate big harvest?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa anáa ŋmaa babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer supplies the necessary soil nutrients, but getting a maximum harvest also depends on good rain, proper weed control, pruning, and protecting trees from pests.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Shi nikpamɔ babaoo lɛ hu damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kpakpa nɔ. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ ni sa ni afoɔ kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as natural sunshades and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or viruses they carry, which drain the plant's energy and stunt its growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛhiɛɔ lɛ Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do bugs and caterpillars attack my farm much more during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in warm, humid weather because high moisture helps their eggs hatch quickly, and the abundance of fresh green leaves gives them plenty of food.
ga: Koolooi yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya. Ni baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa amɛnáa niyenii babaoo.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow before it even starts producing corn ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ebɔi toi feemɔ po lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly due to a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves, or because waterlogged soil is choking the roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ titri lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Aloo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ.

english: What does animal manure actually do to help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni kooloi ashishifã yeɔ ebuaa yɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ? Koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and improves its structure, allowing the ground to hold water longer so plant roots can continuously absorb food and moisture.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã haa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough space on the farm for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji he ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Weeds compete continuously underground and above ground; their fast-growing roots steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your main crops, leaving them weak and small.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ fɛɛ. Shishifãi ni daa oya lɛ juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ni jɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ Ha tso lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni efee bibioo.

english: If I plant my seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, space, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants that produce much smaller overall yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni wooo yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Too many suckers around one plantain stem share the same food and water source, causing all of them to produce tiny bunches. Removing extra suckers lets the main stem grow large, heavy fruits.
ga: Ayɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ ni ebɔle he. Plantain kome ni kɛ niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe kome tsuɔ nii. Ha amɛ fɛɛ amɛfee kuu bibioo ko. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting inside the soil before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when soil stays overly wet for long periods without proper drainage, or when fungal diseases infect the stem cuttings used to plant the crop.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko gbɛ eshwa tsei niji ni akɛduɔ tsei lɛ anɔ

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, so why do they keep dropping off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ egbeeɔ shi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no bees and beneficial insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he fɛɛ he. Ha wɔfee fɔfɔii lɛ pollen.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries up soil moisture quickly. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool canopy that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Enɛ haa shade ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la.

english: Why should I leave wide spaces between my maize seeds instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni da yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: Planting seeds too close together causes the maize plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stems and small cobs. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough nourishment to grow strong and produce large ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ toi wuji aba.

english: How deep into the soil should I plant my maize seeds during the planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep into the soil. Planting too shallow allows birds to eat the seeds or heat to dry them out, while planting too deep makes it difficult for the seedling to push through the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi lɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛkɛ dɔlɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛgbi dumɔwui lɛ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ mli tsɔ lɛ baaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that the ground is waterlogged, which stops the roots from taking up nutrients. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains the soil of specific nutrients like nitrogen and encourages crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ewoɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during the hottest part of the day as a natural reaction to reduce water loss caused by excessive heat and direct sunlight. If they uncurl in the evening when temperatures drop, the plant is simply protecting itself.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni baaha nu ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ aba shi. Kɛji amɛjie amɛhe gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ Tso lɛ miibu ehe kɛkɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady soil moisture and adequate shade during high heat helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be ni ená hulutsoo ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively consume the water, fertilizer, and light in the field. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing essential resources away from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛyeɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la waa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: What causes small holes to appear in my tomato leaves and fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi tomato lɛ baai kɛ aduawai anɔ

english: Holes in tomato leaves and fruits are caused by insect pests, such as caterpillars or fruit borers, feeding on the plant tissue. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and using appropriate organic or chemical controls stops pest damage.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ tomato baai kɛ aduawai amli lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii loo aduawai amli ŋmeii. ni yeɔ tsei ahe fãji Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ nibii ni sa ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ akpa.

english: Cassava is typically ready for harvest when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the stem starts to crack as the underground tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni he ni ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide the young cocoa trees with shade and soil moisture needed to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the roots are waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like Urea will help the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ye bu bibioo ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the shoot of the corn plant. Spraying approved insecticides or applying neem extract early in the morning or evening helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ loo okɛ neem mli nu tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Which direction should I point the buds when planting cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ?

english: The small growth buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. If you plant them facing down, the stem will grow weak and produce fewer tubers because it wastes energy turning itself around underground.
ga: Esa akɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ohiɛ shi lɛ Tso lɛ yitsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs fioo ejaakɛ amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand easily underground. Making mounds gives the yam tubers enough space to grow big and prevents heavy rain from waterlogging the roots and causing rot.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi oya. Gɔŋ ko ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When grown with or after maize, they naturally feed the soil and make your maize grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa loo yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ Amɛbaaye nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni oha o-abele lɛ ada waa ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuuu nii

english: Leaf curl is often caused by tiny whiteflies transmitting a virus or by extreme heat and underwatering. Protecting young plants with nets and spraying organic insecticides like neem oil keeps whiteflies away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa loo kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu shishi ni mɔ ko yɔɔ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi abu tsei bibii ahe ni akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi tamɔ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii yɛji akabote mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating in the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing and taking nutrients away from your pepper plants.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ akatsɔ la yɛ hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do small green mangoes fall off my tree before they grow big and sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mangoes drop early when the tree does not get enough water during hot weather or when fruit flies lay eggs in the young fruit. Watering the base during dry spells and using fruit fly traps stops fruit drop.
ga: Mango shwieɔ baai lɛ mra kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa loo kɛ́ aduawai amli ŋmeii wo amɛwui yɛ aduawai bibii amli. Nu ni oooha shishitoo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akɛtswaa aduawai lɛ ahe tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ ahe tsei lɛ akpa.

english: Is it better for me to water my crop in the early morning or in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the water soaks deep into the roots without drying up quickly in the sun, giving plants moisture to stay strong through the afternoon heat.
ga: Nu ni oooha lɛ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ baabote shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni hulu lɛ egbiŋ oya. Ha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ shwane lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I use the same machine to harvest both my rice and my corn fields?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ akpa ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji fɛɛ?

english: Yes, a combine harvester can harvest different crops like rice and corn, but you must change the front section of the machine (the header) because corn stalks are much thicker and taller than rice plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Shi esa akɛ otsake tsɔne lɛ hiɛ (yitso) ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli tsei babaoo ni amɛkwɔ fe ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Why does a harvesting machine need different parts attached to it for different crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ fãi srɔtoi awo nikpamɔ nibii amli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Crops grow differently in height, thickness, and grain arrangement. Attachments called headers are specifically designed to cut, pick, or strip a particular type of crop without crushing the harvest.
ga: Tsei daa yɛ ŋwɛi ŋwɛi, ŋwɛi ŋwɛi, kɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo srɔtoi amli. Afee nɔ ko ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ yitso lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛfo, ajie, loo ajie ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko ni akumɔɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my corn is mature enough to be harvested with a machine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔne akpa?

english: Corn is ready for machine harvest when the outer husks and leaves turn completely brown and dry, and the kernels are hard enough that pressing them with your fingernail leaves no dent.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ anyɛ nɔ koni amɛkafee ŋmeii.

english: What will happen to my crop if I harvest it with a heavy machine while the stalks are still green?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ mikɛ tsɔnei ni tsii ŋmɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ eyɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ?

english: Green stalks contain too much moisture and flexibility, which can cause them to tangle and clog the machine, while also crushing wet grains instead of cleanly separating them.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ elasticity. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɔnei lɛ afee basabasa ni amɛtsi amɛhe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbala mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to my maize if I leave it on the farm too long after it has dried?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji mishi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni egbi sɛɛ?

english: Leaving dry maize in the field for too long makes it vulnerable to attack by insects like weevils, damage from birds, rot from unexpected rain, and falling over in high winds.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni egbi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ atutua lɛ oya. Okpoi ni fiteɔ Nibii ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ mli ni egbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ mli

english: Why do my corn plants need to be planted in straight, even rows if I want to use a machine for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmãa mli kɛji miisumɔ ni mikɛ tsɔne akpa amɛ?

english: Straight, evenly spaced rows ensure that heavy harvesting machinery can drive through the field along the crop lines without running over and crushing the plants.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi ni ja ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa anyɛɔ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni akɛkpaa nibii ni tsii lɛ amli yɛ dumɔwui agbɛjianɔtoi lɛ anɔ ni amɛjooo foi kɛhooo tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛkumɔɔɔ amɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn plants fall over before harvest time while others stay upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hiɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Corn plants fall over due to weak root support, shallow soil, heavy winds, or pests damaging the inside of the stalk, which makes machine harvesting difficult.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ekɔɔɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: Do I need to clear weeds from between my crops before bringing a harvesting machine into the field?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akpamɔ tsɔne lɛ aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, thick weeds can wrap around moving mechanical parts, cause machine blockages, and pollute your harvested grain with weed seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni mli tse baanyɛ abɔle tsɔnei ahe nibii ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ ahe. ni haa tsɔne lɛ tsiɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi dumɔwui woɔ okpamɔ lɛ mli muji.

english: How does rainy weather right before harvest time affect my fully grown grain crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ baaná miŋmaa ni eda lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Rain on fully mature, dry crops causes the grains to re-absorb water, increasing the risk of mold growth, rot, and premature sprouting while still on the stalk.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ tsei ni edara ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu ekoŋŋ. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yaa hiɛ. fitemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested grain crack or shatter into tiny pieces during mechanical harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ miigba loo amɛmiigbɛ bibii bibii lɛ? Yɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ mli?

english: Grains crack during harvest if they become extremely dry and brittle under harsh sun, or if the machine is running at a speed that is too aggressive for the crop's condition.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa baagbala yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli kɛji akɛ egbi waa ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɔne lɛ miitsu nii oya fe bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are growing properly underground before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: You can tell tubers are expanding well when the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack and bulge outward. Strong green stems and vibrant leaves above ground also indicate healthy root development below.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ bulb lɛ miigbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ je shishi egbɛ eshwa ni efo kɛmiiya kponɔgbɛ. Tso lɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ wala mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu tsɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm is rich enough to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture well, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or decaying organic matter. Hard, pale, or sandy soil that drains water instantly usually needs compost or manure added.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nibii ni fiteɔ, shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni ehiɛ su, loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ, ni bei pii lɛ ehe bahiaa ni akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei afata he lɛ yɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to add extra fertilizer to my maize farm so I get a big yield?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi awo mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni maná yibii babaoo?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about two weeks after planting when seedlings emerge to help roots grow. Apply a second round, called top-dressing, when the maize reaches knee height just before flowering to boost ear growth.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ fã lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ eje kpo lɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. Akɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ top dressing lɛ tsuɔ nii. Beni ŋmãa shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi koni eha toi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and yellow even though I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Stunted, yellowing maize is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure will help the leaves turn dark green and push the plant to grow taller.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ tso lɛ aya ŋwɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain next to young cocoa creates a canopy that protects them and retains moisture until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How close together should I plant my plantain suckers so they do not fight each other for nutrients?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tɛŋŋ koni amɛkaye niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted about 3 meters apart. Planting them too close causes their large leaves to block sunlight from each other and forces their roots to compete for water and nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ aaafee mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai wuji lɛ atsĩ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe. kɛ shishifãi lɛ ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Premature leaf drop in cocoa is often caused by insect pests like mirids (capsids) sucking sap from the branches, or by root damage during prolonged dry spells. Inspecting underneath the leaves for insects can confirm the cause.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ aniji amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. aloo kɛjɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akwɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ema nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa lɛ nɔ mi.

english: What causes holes in the main stems of my cassava plants and how does it affect my farm?
ga: Mɛni ha bu ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ ba? Ni te enáa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in stems are caused by stem borer insects that tunnel inside the plant, weakening it so it breaks easily in high winds. Using clean, pest-free stems for propagation prevents this issue in new plantings.
ga: Kplukai ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli ni shwieɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ no hewɔ lɛ efoɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni he tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛha shweremɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa yɛ dumɔwui heei amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when the plant lacks phosphorus. Consistent morning watering and proper feeding help flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa leebi kɛ niyenii ni sa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Does leaving weeds on my farm harm my crops if the crop is already taller than the weeds?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni mijieɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui kɛji tsei lɛ kɛlɛ fe jwɛi lɛ momo?

english: Yes, weeds hidden underneath your crop canopy still steal water, fertilizer, and nutrients from the soil root zone, which reduces your crop's final yield even if the crop is taller.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tsei ashishi lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmei, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lolo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ kɛlɛ moŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to cover them, the intense sun burns their leaves and quickly dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni tsoɔ babaoo lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall with large green leaves but give me small, empty ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ehaa mi abele toi ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like phosphorus and potassium, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems rather than developing full, heavy seeds or fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium he lɛ, Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛha baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ada. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ wuhi aloo yiblii nɛ a he wami ɔ suɔ.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and rotting before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. When tree branches are too thick and don't allow sunlight and air to pass through, water stays on the pods and spreads the infection.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ aniji lɛ egbɔ tsɔ ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Nu baanyɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni egbɛ hela eshwa.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are drooping because of afternoon heat or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane mli latsaa lɛ hewɔ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Heat wilting usually happens during the hottest hours of the afternoon, and the plant bounces back by cool evening or morning. If the plant stays droopy and soft even early in the morning, it is likely suffering from a bacterial or fungal disease in its roots or stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, latsaa ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ baa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni latsaa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Ni tsei lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba yɛ gbɛkɛ loo leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli. Kɛji tso lɛ egbo lolo ni eyɛ blɛoo leebi po Etamɔ nɔ ni bacteria loo fungal hela ko yɛ shishifãi loo eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cassava sticks very close together so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-cassavas lɛ duɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa koni maná he ko babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need space under the soil to expand into big tubers. Planting them too close makes the plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in tall thin plants with small, thin roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ kwɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu yɛ bibii.

english: Why does my piece of land yield fewer crops every year even though I plant the exact same crop using the same methods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ gbɛi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ tsei lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to replenish. It also lets pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop build up in the ground over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ. Ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do flowers keep falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant feels stressed, such as during extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or overwatering. It also happens if insects like bees are not around to transfer pollen between flowers so the fruit can start growing.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli, tamɔ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi trukaa, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ fe nine. Ebaa lɛ hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛŋkɛɛɛ koni amɛjie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ koni aduawai aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly and aggressively compared to the food crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa waa kɛ akɛto niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have evolved over centuries to be extremely tough. They are faster at drinking water and taking nutrients from the soil than farm crops, which have been selected over time to produce food rather than fight off competitors.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli ni efee tsei ni wa waa. Amɛhe feɔ oya yɛ nu ni amɛnuɔ lɛ mli ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fe okwaayeli mli nibii, ni ahala amɛ be kakadaŋŋ koni amɛha niyenii aba moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ akaŋshilɔi lɛ baawu.

english: Can I save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum strength in their first generation. If you save and plant those seeds for a second season, the offspring lose those special traits, producing uneven plants and a much lower harvest.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ to ni odu kɛha be ni ji enyɔ lɛ. Seshibii lɛ baafite nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome kɛ ŋmaa bibioo kwraa.

english: Why should I cut off green branches or shoots from my crops when they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji loo tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ?

english: Removing unnecessary or extra branches (pruning) redirects the plant's food and water straight into growing larger fruits rather than maintaining excess leaves. It also opens up space for air and sunlight to pass through, keeping the plant dry and disease-free.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi. (Pruning) lɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ gbɛ kɛyaa tso yibii wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, moo ngɔ baai nɛ piɛɛ he ɔ kɛ to he. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hu tsɔɔ mli. Ha tso lɛ agbi ni helai akabote mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and burning up in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiishã yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, protecting the seedlings from hot sunlight and keeping the soil moist while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli wa lɛ

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying poultry manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the base helps the plant regain its dark green color and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle lɛ he lɛ atsu nii Shishitoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná su ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmei ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the rainy season becomes very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped around them for too long because the soil cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ amɛhe. Etsɛ tsɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: What is causing ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars, like the Fall Armyworm, hiding inside the plant funnel. Catching them early by inspecting the field weekly and applying recommended bio-pesticides or organic extracts will stop them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛmɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ he ni okwɛɔ jɛmɛ daa otsi ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, obaaye obua ni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and small cobs. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and food to produce larger, heavier yields.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce less food even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight intended for your crops. Removing weeds early in the growing season ensures all applied nutrients go directly to feeding your crop instead of unwanted weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ yaa niyenii ni akɛhaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without growing into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ anɔkwa tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants face heat stress or irregular watering. Providing steady water at the roots and placing dry grass around the plant base keeps the soil cool, helping flowers turn into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ehe lɛ. Tsei ashishi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni etsɔɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids sucking sap from under the leaves, which can also spread plant viruses. Controlling these small pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu Mra be mli ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during dry spells?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops—known as mulching—acts as a protective layer that keeps the sun from drying out the ground. It locks moisture in the soil longer so plant roots stay hydrated between rains.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ he ni mikpa ŋmã yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it naturally into the dirt. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize restores fertility to your soil for the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or is getting drowned by too much water. Nitrogen is the essential plant food that keeps leaves green so the crop can grow full, healthy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo eefo nu mli. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ toi ni eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: If your young cocoa leaves look burnt, dry up at the edges, or fall off early, the trees are receiving direct heat from the sun and need shade plants like plantains or nurse trees to protect them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa baai bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã, egbi yɛ eshishigbɛ, loo egbee shi oya lɛ, no lɛ hulu ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ miipiŋ tso lɛ. ni ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tendrils koni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain plants drooping and snapping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkuɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally fold down and droop during hot, dry weather as a self-defense mechanism to reduce water loss and protect the main stem until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebuɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very bushy with heavy leaves, but the tubers in the ground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni ehiɛ baai ni tsii waa lɛ? Shi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of storing starch into large tubers below the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso nguahi a mi ngɛ zugba sisi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas in my field make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, naturally restoring nutrients that heavy-feeding crops like maize take away.
ga: Cowpea tsei ji ŋmeii ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni kooloi ni tsii yeɔ niyenii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my pepper plants before any peppers grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ dani ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil required to support fruit formation.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii lɛ mli lɛ miipiŋ amɛ.

english: Why do my tomatoes develop dark, rotten patches on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo yɛ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, often due to irregular watering or dry weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ daa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my yams under the ground are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams indicate harvest readiness above ground when their vines and leaves turn yellow and dry up completely, showing that the plant has finished sending energy into the underground tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ asaa he kɛha kpamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni wain tsei kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my crops grow slower and yield less?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiiwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitor plants that steal fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your main crops, leaving them undernourished and weak.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Enɛ haa amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why do I need to cut back shade trees as my cocoa plantation grows older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ miigbɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need heavy shade to survive heat, but mature cocoa trees require higher amounts of sunlight to flower heavily and produce maximum pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ni mli wa koni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa be lɛ mli. Shi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: If I manage to get a piece of land that was previously damaged by informal mining, how will I know if crops can grow on it?
ga: Kɛji manyɛ mana shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ, Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Soil damaged by mining often contains toxic chemicals, heavy metals, or extreme acidity, which prevents seeds from sprouting and turns crop leaves yellow. Before planting, the soil needs testing, heavy organic matter like compost added, and proper land restoration to bring back vital plant nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei, dade ni tsii, loo acidity ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru tsaa fiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dani abaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni aka shikpɔŋ lɛ akwɛ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii koni akɛha tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and pale even though rain is falling on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food crop plants need to stay healthy and green. Overused or washed-out soil loses these nutrients, so adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu shwieɔ nɔ fe nine loo nu shwieɔ nɔ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers deform when planted in hard, rocky, or compacted soil that prevents underground expansion. Building high, loose soil mounds allows yam roots to stretch down easily and form big, straight tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ koni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ shishi shweremɔ naa. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni afee lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: I want to start farming to earn income quickly, so which crops grow fast and can be harvested in a few months?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi okwaayeli koni maná shika oya. Mɛɛ tsei daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli?

english: Vegetables like tomatoes, peppers, and okra, as well as legumes like cowpeas, mature quickly within 2 to 4 months. They provide much faster financial returns compared to long-term tree crops like cocoa or oil palm.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ tomato, pepper, kɛ okra Legumes, ni cowpeas fata he lɛ, shwereɔ oya yɛ nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa shika helɛtemɔ baa oya kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli tamɔ cocoa loo oil palm lɛ he.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa seedling to start producing fruit pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ aduawai ŋmɔji ahe shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa trees take about 3 to 5 years to start fruiting, but modern hybrid cocoa varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years if given proper shade, water, and protection from pests.
ga: Kusum mli cacao tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids lɛ baanyɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo, nu kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahebuu ni sa.

english: Wild weeds have deep root systems and dormant seeds already stored in the soil that naturally adapt to harsh conditions, whereas cultivated crops require time, soft soil, and tender care to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ nitsumɔ. Ha ehi shikpɔŋ ni shihilɛi ni mli wawai nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei ni miida lɛ heɔ be lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ kwɛmɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa

english: Since farm land is hard to secure, can I plant cassava and maize together on the same small patch?
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ wa. Mibaanyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Ani ebaanyɛ efee nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, growing cassava and maize together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested within 3 to 4 months, leaving the field open for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɛɔ koni ŋmãa ni daa blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops on my small plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni makwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close together makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin stems and small yields rather than a healthy harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi. Yɛ kpamɔ kpakpa najiaŋ lɛ

english: Why do my young crops wilt and drop leaves during short spells without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaa fiteɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young plants have shallow root systems that cannot reach deeper groundwater during hot dry spells. Placing dried grass or leaves around the stem base as mulch traps moisture in the dirt and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo Mulching he yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: What causes small holes in my vegetable leaves, and will it stop the plant from bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-vegetable baai lɛ anɔ Ni ani ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by insect pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the plant. If too many leaves are damaged, the plant cannot absorb enough sunlight to produce food, leading to poor fruit development.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ efite tsɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, aduawai lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing so slowly this season compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize plants often slow down their growth when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or when rains are irregular. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer early in the season helps boost their growth speed and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa daamɔ baa shi kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛya oya ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why are my yam vines slowing down their growth even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need proper support, such as sturdy stakes, to climb toward sunlight. Without tall stakes, the plant leaves cannot capture enough light energy, which slows down the vine's growth and reduces tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ ni sa, tamɔ tso ni wa. koni ekwɔ koni ená hulu la Kɛji osharai ni mli wa bɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ la hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baaha wain tso lɛ ada blɛoo ni ebaaha bulb lɛ dalɛ aba shi.

english: Which crops can I pair with my cassava to get better results from my land?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ mikɛ ŋmei afata he koni maná yibii kpakpai kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts alongside cassava works as a great match. Legumes naturally fix nitrogen into the soil, which feeds the cassava while maximizing your land's output.
ga: Nibii ni akɛduɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmei woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Legumes lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ aye nii, ni ebaaha yibiiwoo ni jɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Can I plant cassava close to my young cocoa trees, or will they affect each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cassava yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe? Aloo ani ebaaná amɛhe nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava roots draw heavy amounts of water and nutrients from the soil very quickly. Planting it too close to young cocoa creates harsh competition that will slow down your cocoa trees' growth.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jieɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ cacao tsei tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa ni haa cacao tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that your cocoa trees are receiving too much direct sunlight without shade, or that the soil is low in nutrients like potassium. Providing shade trees and organic fertilizer helps restore leaf health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be ko bɛ he. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ potassium ni faaa. Shade kɛ organic fertilizer yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the afternoon heat even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: In high heat, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the wet soil. Covering the base of your plants with dry grass mulch keeps the soil cool and protects the root system.
ga: kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to leave specific distances between my plantain suckers when setting up my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-plantain tsei lɛ abɔ he beni miisaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plantain tree receives enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients without competing with its neighbors. Good spacing prevents stunt growth and leads to larger, healthier bunches.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ yeee akaŋ. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ naa. ni ekɛ kuu ko ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: How do I set up nursery shade to prevent my vegetable seedlings from getting scorched?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ shade screens awo mli koni tsofa-kɛ-ŋma dumɔwui lɛ akashã?

english: Building a simple overhead frame covered with palm fronds allows filtered light to reach young seedlings while protecting them from harsh midday sun and heavy rain drops that can damage delicate stems.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ tsei ahe tsei ehà nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa la ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ shɛɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baanyɛ afite tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my land is a good fit for growing tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha tomato ŋmɔ?

english: Tomatoes thrive in loose, well-drained soil that does not trap standing water after heavy rain. If water stays pooled on your field for days, tomato roots will rot and plant growth will stop.
ga: Tomato kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo Tomato shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baakpa.

english: Why does my soil lose its ability to produce good crop yields after a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot repeatedly strips the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating your crops with beans or cover crops helps rebuild soil structure and restores natural fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from lack of water when there is no rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miipiŋ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: When crops don't get enough water, their leaves start to droop or wilt, turn dull green or yellow, and feel warm to the touch. If the top few inches of soil are dry and crumble into dust, your plants are stressed and need water.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛgbee shi loo amɛbaagboi. Etsakeɔ efeɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni haa mɔ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ ata he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ inchi fioo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli egbi ni eyɛ sũ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miihao ni nu he miihia lɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my farm so the water doesn't dry up quickly?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu koni ekagbi oya?
