english: The best time to water your crops is early in the morning before the sun gets hot, or late in the afternoon. Watering during these cooler times ensures the soil absorbs the moisture instead of losing it to heat and evaporation.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu ji leebi dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ loo shwane. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni baa shi kɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: What simple method can I use to water my crops when the rains stop completely?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ashwieɔ tsei anɔ nu beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa kwraa lɛ?

english: You can use manual watering cans or set up simple drip irrigation using perforated plastic pipes or recycled bottles buried near the plant bases to drop water directly onto the roots without wasting it.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii loo nu ni hoɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii. Kɛ plastic paipi ni mli ewo muji loo tɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ ni afu yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nu afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko akafite.

english: How do I check if the soil beneath the surface still has water for my plant roots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lolo kɛha mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ?

english: Push a dry wooden stick or your finger about three inches deep into the soil near your plant. If the stick comes out clean and dry, the soil needs water; if it comes out with moist, cool soil sticking to it, there is still enough water underground.
ga: Tsɔ tso ni egbi loo onine mli aaafee inchi etɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ otso lɛ mli. Kɛji niji lɛ ahe tse ni amɛgbi Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ eje kpo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ, no lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day as a survival trick to hide their surface from the strong sun, which stops them from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛtee ŋwɛigbɛ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fiteɔ fe nine yɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dry grass help them stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the dirt. It blocks direct sunlight, keeps the ground cool, and traps moisture in the soil for a much longer time.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ akabote mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ

english: Why do my young crops burn easily under strong sunlight even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi kɛ́ miha amɛ nu po lɛ?

english: Young crop leaves are thin and delicate. Strong sunlight can scorch them faster than their small roots can drink up water, which is why providing partial shade during their early growth stage helps them survive.
ga: Baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ oya fe shishifãi bibii. Eji nɔ ko ni anuɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni hulutsoo be ni amɛdaraa lɛ fã ko yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi lɛ.

english: Which food crops can survive better on my farm if the rains fail for a long time?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii baahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and cowpeas are naturally hardy. They have deep roots or specialized leaves that allow them to draw moisture from deep in the soil and store water during dry periods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ji nibii ni wa waa kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo baai krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How does clear weeding around my crops help them survive dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the tiny bit of water and nutrients available in dry soil away from your crops. Clearing weeds leaves all the ground moisture available for your plants to drink.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni anuɔ.

english: How can my family members help me manage the farm best when we are preparing for a dry season?
ga: Te miweku lɛ mli bii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni wɔsaa wɔhe kɛha hɔmɔ be lɛ?

english: Family members can help with light, crucial tasks such as applying dry grass mulch around plant bases, hand-watering vulnerable crops, and clearing weeds early so the crops do not struggle for water.
ga: Weku lɛ mli bii baanyɛ aye abua kɛ nitsumɔi bibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi kɛ nine ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni waaa lɛ anɔ nu. kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye nu he akaŋ.

english: Why should I trim or cut off old leaves and branches from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo loo mafolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji momoi ni jɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Removing old or overgrown foliage, often called pruning, allows sunlight and air to flow through the plant while directing energy toward growing healthy new stems and fruit.
ga: Baai ni egbɔ loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii, ni haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli. kɛ hewalɛ ni akɛhaa koni tsei ahe tsei kɛ aduawai heei ni wa lɛ adalɛ

english: Is there a specific time of year when I should prune my crops?
ga: Ani be ko yɛ afi lɛ mli ni esa akɛ mafolɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli?

english: Pruning is best done before the major rainy season or right after harvest, so the plant can heal quickly and use the upcoming rains to produce fresh, strong growth.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaakpa tsei lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba loo yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. koni tso lɛ aná hewalɛ oya Ni ekɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee dalɛ hee ni mli wa.

english: How does cutting off sickly branches help the rest of my crop stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei niji ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Removing diseased leaves and branches stops infections and pests from spreading to healthy stems, saving the plant energy that it can use to stay alive and yield fruit.
ga: Baai kɛ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Ehaa hewalɛ ni tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes the flowers on my crops to drop off before they turn into fruit?
ga: Mɛni haa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii?

english: Flowers fall off without fruiting when plants suffer from drought, poor soil nutrients, or high heat, which prevents them from having enough energy to support fruit formation.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ na hɔmɔ. Niyenii nibii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo edɔ waa Enɛ haa tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ ebuaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why are my crop plants growing very tall and bushy but failing to produce fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: When crops have too many excess stems and leaves, they use up all their food and nutrients on growing foliage instead of setting flowers and bearing fruit.
ga: Beni tso ko yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai babaoo tsɔ lɛ Tsei yeɔ amɛ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell when my crop plant is ready to start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ ni ebaawo yibii?

english: A crop preparing to yield fruit shows signs like stem thickening, flower development, and healthy green leaves, indicating it has stored enough food to support fruit growth.
ga: Tsei ni miisaa amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii lɛ baajie okadii tamɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa kɛ fɔfɔi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ akpo. kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yeɔ emuu Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ato niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why should I remove extra shoots or suckers growing at the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Thinning out extra shoots prevents weak side-growth from stealing water and nutrients away from the main fruiting stem.
ga: Kɛ́ afee ŋmeii bibii lɛ bibii lɛ, no tsiɔ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anaa koni ekaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso yibii titri lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my harvest if I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and root space, leading to thin, weak plants that produce much smaller harvests.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo kwraa lɛ baa.

english: How do I choose which shoots to remove when thinning my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala suckers ni majie beni mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miifee bibioo lɛ?

english: You should remove the smallest, weakest, or damaged shoots, leaving only the healthiest and strongest stems to receive all the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii bibii fe fɛɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ, loo ni efite lɛ. Tsoi ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ nine shɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits compared to farms where regular pruning and thinning are done?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni akwɛɔ nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Proper crop care like pruning extra branches and thinning excess shoots allows maximum sunlight and soil nutrients to reach the remaining fruits, making them grow bigger and heavier.
ga: Nibii ni adu lɛ akwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afee lɛ bibioo Enɛ baaha hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛtsiiɔ.

english: Is it okay if I start my farm with just a few seeds on a small piece of land?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba mli kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui fioo ko pɛ je ŋmɔ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ?

english: Yes, starting small allows you to learn how your crops behave and manage weeds and pests effectively without getting overwhelmed. As your crops mature and yield a harvest, you can save seeds and profit to expand your land gradually over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ obɔi nibii bibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa, ni okwɛɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ ohe wooo mli. Beni onibii lɛ shwere ni amɛwo yibii Obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui kɛ sɛɛnamɔi anaa koni okɛgbala oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my maize crops take several months to produce corn instead of growing overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaadu lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Crops need time to establish strong roots, leaves, and stems before they have enough energy to produce food. Just like a child must grow before doing heavy work, a plant must go through natural growth stages before it can bear mature grain.
ga: Tsei taoɔ be ni amɛtswa shishifãi, baai, kɛ tsei ni mli wa dani amɛna hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Taakɛ esa akɛ gbekɛ ko ada dani enyɛ etsu nii waa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Esa akɛ tso lɛ atsɔ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ be ko mli dani enyɛ ená dumɔwui ni edara.

english: Why do my cassava plants shed their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods as a natural protection trick to prevent water loss through heat. The plant goes into a quiet state to stay alive underground until the rains return to trigger fresh leaf growth.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nu ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli lɛ he. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli koni ehi shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Will my crops survive if rain does not fall immediately after I put seeds in the soil?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shi kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds can rest safely in dry soil for a short period, but they need moisture to wake up and germinate. If the dry spell lasts too long, the seed may lose its vitality or get eaten by pests, which is why planting right at the start of the rainy season is best.
ga: Dumɔwui baanyɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kukuoo ko. Shi ehe miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ dani enyɛ ete shi ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ baanyɛ afite loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ baaye amɛ. Nɔ ni haa ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings dying when I plant them in an open field under full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight, much like human babies. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted next to them to block excess sun and keep the surrounding air cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ shãa oya. Tamɔ adesa abifao pɛpɛɛpɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni hulu la akashɛ fe nine ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn yellow and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii miifee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiida blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds take over your field, your crops starve, causing their leaves to turn pale yellow and their growth to stunt.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi ha nyɛŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye nyɛŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough goodness to feed my crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds water well, and contains living creatures like earthworms. Crops planted in rich soil show deep green leaves and thick stems.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ oya yɛ onine mli, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ mli. Tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse.

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my plants immediately after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Sprouting seedlings have tiny, tender roots that can easily get burned and killed by strong fertilizers. It is best to wait a few weeks until the roots are stronger and capable of absorbing the plant food safely.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa baanyɛ ashã ni agbe amɛ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii shweshweeshwe.

english: Flowers can fall off if the weather is extremely hot, if the plant lacks water, or if insects like bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Giving the plants steady water and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ he, loo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa koni amɛbawo lɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my pepper plants spend weeks growing big leaves before showing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo dani ewoɔ baai wuji dani ejieɔ e-pepper lɛ kpo lɛ?

english: A pepper plant must build a strong foliage system first because leaves act like solar panels that make food for the plant. Once it has enough leaves to generate food energy, it naturally shifts into making flowers and peppers.
ga: Esa akɛ pepper tsei lɛ afee baa gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ ejaakɛ baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni haa tso lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Kɛji akɛ baai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee hewalɛ kɛjɛ niyenii mli lɛ yɛ lɛ Ebaatsake yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ nɔ.

english: How do I know if the seed bag I bought has official approval to give me a good crop yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui kotokui ni miheɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni maŋ lɛ ekpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Certified seeds carry an official tag or rubber stamp from crop inspectors. This mark shows that the seeds were properly tested in a lab for high germination rates and freedom from diseases before being approved for sale.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ baaná okadi loo stamp kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛlɔ dɛŋ. Okadi nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aka dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ laboratori mli koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo, ni hela bɛ amɛhe dani akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I buy fresh foundation seeds instead of re-planting seeds saved from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe shishitoo dumɔwui heei yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu ehee ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over time, leading to weaker plants and lower yields. Fresh foundation seeds are specially bred for maximum strength, disease resistance, and higher production.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni gbɔjɔɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi. Akwɛɔ shishitoo dumɔwui heei lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my seedlings in the cool early morning or late evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu nii leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hot midday sun causes young plants to lose water rapidly through their leaves and wilt. Planting in the cooler morning or evening gives roots time to settle into the moist soil without high heat stress.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni hulutsoo ni naa wa waa bɛ mli.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them right after the very first light rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ? Klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: A single light rain only wet the surface soil, which quickly dries out under hot weather. Seeds require steady soil moisture over several days to swell up and germinate properly.
ga: Nugbɔ fioo ko pɛ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni baagbi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa gbii babaoo koni amɛfuu ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain crops produce small shoots around their base, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ni esa akɛ majie amɛ?

english: Those shoots are suckers that grow naturally from the main root. Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal food and water from the main plant, so keeping only one or two strong ones ensures big fruit bunches.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifã titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi suckers babaoo ni amɛgbele lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tso yibii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha aduawai babaoo aba.

english: Why do my groundnut plants bend their flower stems down and push them into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miikumɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛmiiwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts bloom above ground, but the actual nuts mature underground. After the flower is fertilized, the stem naturally grows downward into the soil so the pod can develop safely hidden in the earth.
ga: Peanuts fɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi anɔkwa nuts daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni awo fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔ sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ ehe diɛŋtsɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara shweshweeshwe ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my rice plant split into multiple stems when I only planted a single seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ mli gbalaa ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo mli beni miduɔ dumɔwu kome pɛ lɛ?

english: This natural branching process is called tillering. The main stem produces side shoots at soil level, allowing a single seed to form multiple grain-bearing heads and produce a much higher yield.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niji ahe gbɛjianɔtoo nɛɛ akɛ tillering. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwu kome náa dumɔwui ayitsei babaoo ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural self-defense against extreme heat. By rolling up, the leaf shrinks its exposed surface area to conserve water and trap moisture inside.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. beni shwieɔ shi lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo efo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves in dry weather to stop losing water through leaf pores. The plant sleeps underground to stay alive and will quickly sprout new green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu egbi lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ akpa. Tsei kã shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛhi shi. ni ebaakwɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli oya kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods shrivel and turn black when the cold Harmattan wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ tswa lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan air rapidly sucks moisture out of the tree. To protect its main trunk and survive the drought, the cocoa tree intentionally sacrifices its youngest pods.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli oya. Koni abu tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he ni ehi wala mli yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Kɛkɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔ hiɛ ekɛ etsitsi bibioo fe fɛɛ lɛ sha afɔle.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen or the field has too much standing water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting under the soil before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil without good drainage. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the flowers falling off my cocoa trees without turning into young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree suffers from dry soil, extreme heat, or damage from tiny sap-sucking insects like mirids. Keeping temporary shade trees and watering during dry spells helps the flowers stay on and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen lɛ fite tso lɛ. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ nu ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my young corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni tɔmɔ yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ bu yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋ lɛ yeli he?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the funnel of the plant. Applying clean sand, neem seed extract, or approved pesticides into the leaf funnel early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ ŋã ni he tse Neem dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tsu nii Aloo, kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ wo baai lɛ agbɛi lɛ anɔ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why is my main plantain tree taking so long to bear a cluster of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwu titri lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: When too many young sucker shoots grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food and water from it. Removing extra shoots so that only two or three remain gives the main tree enough energy to produce big fruit quickly.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii babaoo dara yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water from moving up inside the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava and using disease-resistant tomato varieties prevents this from spreading.
ga: Muawai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Ni kɛ akɛ tomato henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller yields if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji mijieee amɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water that your crops need to build healthy stems and fruits. Weeding your farm during the first four to six weeks gives your crops the best chance to produce a full harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ amɛyibii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie oŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkpa nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it necessary for me to place tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make maximum food, which flows down to build much larger and heavier tubers under the ground.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ yitso ni da ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying the plants with soapy water or natural neem oil gets rid of the insects and protects new leaves.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi bibii ni ebu baai heei ahe.

english: How does planting groundnuts between my maize rows help my soil stay rich?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When groundnut roots decay, they release this natural plant food into the soil, feeding the nearby maize plants without extra fertilizer costs.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fite Ejieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tso niyenii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ niyenii ni okɛ ŋmãa kroko fataaa he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow from the tip down to the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛyashi amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves, especially starting from the bottom of the plant, usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs plenty of nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the green color.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting groundnuts or beans on my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on this stored natural fertilizer and grows much better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni ato lɛ ni ebaada jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa trees have thin, delicate leaves that dry out quickly under harsh sun and hot winds. They need temporary shade trees like plantains or cassava planted next to them to block direct sunlight and hold moisture in the air until the cocoa roots grow deeper.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni akɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their blossoms without forming any fruit when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high during the day or night, tomato flowers become stressed and the pollen dies before it can fertilize the plant. Without fertilization, the plant drops the flowers to save its energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ shwane loo gbɛkɛ mli lɛ Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ haoɔ ni pollen lɛ gboɔ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo tso lɛ fɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, aphids, or whiteflies. As these insects feed on the plant sap, they spread viruses that cause the leaves to wrinkle, curl, and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids loo whiteflies lɛ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ye tso mli nu lɛ Amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ kpakpa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why are my cassava roots turning soft and rotting in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and cannot drain properly after heavy rains. The standing water starves the roots of oxygen and allows soil fungi to invade and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni enyɛɛɛ efo jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ abote mli ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do I need to put tall wood stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make energy through their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground where they get maximum sunlight and airflow, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ he ni amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo yɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right when the fruit bunches start getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make the top of the plant very heavy. Pests like root nematodes or stem borers can also weaken the roots, causing the tree to collapse under wind or its own weight if it is not supported with a wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ haa tsei lɛ ayiteŋ tsii waa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hewalɛ loo lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi kɛji akɛ tso ko ni fiɔ esɛɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and loose instead of growing into hard, round balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ hiɔ shi bibioo ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ bɔɔlu kokroo ni wa lɛ?

english: When cabbages are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Without enough space and food, the plant cannot build the thick layer of leaves needed to form a tight, heavy head.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kaabii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Kaabaji shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ afee baai ni mli tse. ni he hiaa koni eha yitso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii

english: Why does my oil palm tree stop producing fresh fruit bunches when we go months without rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ kpaɔ aduawai heei ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ be mli ni wɔnáaa nugbɔ nyɔji babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Oil palms require continuous water to produce flowers and develop heavy fruit. During dry spells, the palm enters a survival mode where it delays flowering and reduces fruit growth to conserve its remaining water.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii ni tsii. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Tso lɛ yaa wala shihilɛ mli, ni no haa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the middle instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. This happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or washed away by heavy rains, requiring well-timed fertilizer or compost application.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ biɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does putting dry grass and fallen leaves around the base of my crops help them handle hot weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkpeɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ naa amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves is called mulching. It acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and slows down weed growth.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo

english: Why do my vegetables dry out so quickly even after I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ leebi po lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter cannot hold onto water easily, causing moisture to sink deep or evaporate quickly. Adding decomposed manure or compost helps the soil act like a sponge to store water longer for your crop roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu mli mlɛo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shɔŋŋ loo efoɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji, ni ehaa nu hiɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the small buds face when I am planting cassava stem cuttings in my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akpee naa beni amɛduɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The buds on the cassava stem must point upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new shoots to grow downward first before turning up, which wastes the plant's energy and reduces root yield.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni shishifãi ni baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce large tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛwo bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily whenever they start bearing heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni ebaabɔi aduawai akui womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and pests like root nematodes or stem borers can weaken their grip in the soil. Without propping the trees up with strong bamboo or wooden forks, the heavy weight of the fruit bunch easily pulls the tree down in high winds.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers. Ebaanyɛ eha sũ lɛ mli nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ afee mlɛo. Yibii akui ni tsii baanyɛ agbala tso ko shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ, ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmei loo fɔk ni akɛfiɔ amɛsɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat small holes inside the young leaves of my maize?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ buji bibii? Mi ŋmãa lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the center whorl of young maize plants. Early detection and applying approved treatments or neem extracts directly into the plant whorl helps stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa enɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up, turning hard, and stopping the fruits from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛhe wa ni amɛtsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by severe heat stress. Controlling whiteflies early and providing consistent moisture can help protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Early Whitefly Control Ni hulutsoo be ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why are my cocoa tree flowers dropping off off the trunk before they can turn into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi dani amɛtsɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if there are not enough beneficial insects like midges to pollinate them, or if the tree is experiencing water stress and nutrient shortages, causing it to discard flowers it cannot support.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ nu he haomɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛŋ ahi shi ni esa akɛ ashɛrɛ amɛ ashwie.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism when air temperatures get too high because extreme heat prevents proper pollination. Providing light shade or adequate soil moisture helps the plant retain its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa, ejaakɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growth at the top, which means your crop needs additional organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer to develop properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ organic loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata otsei lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants curl their leaves on hot afternoons to minimize the surface area exposed to the sun and conserve water. If the leaves uncurl in the evening when it cools down, the crop is managing stress normally, but if they stay curled in the morning, the soil is critically dry.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ beni edɔ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nɔnyɛɛ he nii bɔ ni sa. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi leebi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi waa.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my young corn leaves and ragged damage inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ nɔ ni efite ni elaaje yɛ baa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ

english: This pattern of damage is typical of Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on soft young leaf tissue. Checking your field early in the morning and applying safe bio-pesticides or neem leaf extract directly into the central leaf funnel helps stop them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe fãji lɛ feɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem baa mli nu lɛ wo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Does my rice field always need to stay flooded with water for the crop to grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni tsei akwɛ̃?

english: Not all rice requires standing water. Lowland rice thrives in flooded swampy fields, but upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry land using rain water just like corn, as long as the soil remains naturally moist.
ga: Omɔ henɔi komɛi biɔ nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Omɔ folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Shi atsɔse ŋmãa henɔi ni kɛlɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtsɔ nugbɔ nu tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I scatter my rice seeds too closely together when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Sowing rice seeds too tightly causes the young plants to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper line planting gives each plant space to branch out and produce strong stems with heavy grain heads.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Dumɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekɛ niji feɔ niji ni wa, ni dumɔwui tsii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 percent of the grains on the stalks turn a clear golden yellow while the lower stems are still slightly green. Harvesting too late causes dry grains to shatter and fall onto the soil before you can gather them.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ aaafee oha mlijaa 80 etsɔ shika tsuru ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ tso lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ fioo. Nikpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ, amɛgbalaɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani obaanyɛ obua amɛnaa.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough to feed my crops well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture well without turning into hard crusts. If your soil is pale, hard, or dries out too quickly, adding decomposed crop stalks or animal manure will rebuild its strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya Ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse, ewa, loo egbi oya tsɔ Tsei ahe tsei ni egboi loo kooloi afɔfɔi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaha ehewalɛ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans before my corn make the corn yield better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo ŋmei dani adu ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. When you plant corn in that same spot afterward, the corn feeds on the natural fertility left behind by the previous crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni fiɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ ŋmãa yeɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii babaoo ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni eho lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I stored from last season fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Stored seeds lose their power to germinate if they were not completely dry when stored or were attacked by seed insects like weevils. Storing clean, fully dried seeds in airtight containers keeps them fresh and alive for planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbiko kwraa beni akɛto loo dumɔwui amli kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii tutuaa amɛ. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi kwraa lɛ ni akɛaawo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ehee ni amɛhe wa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it doesn't wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkaho?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when crops are actively growing—usually a few weeks after sprouting and right before flowering. Avoid applying fertilizer just before heavy downpours, which can wash the nutrients down into streams instead of feeding the roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miida waa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ anɛ waa. Enɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ awo faai amli moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains spoil so fast when I store them while they are still a bit wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Wet grains create heat and moisture trapped inside bags, which allows mold and fungi to grow rapidly. Grains must be completely dried in the sun before bagging to keep them safe for long periods.
ga: Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i baa ni ŋmɛɔ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ daa oya. Esa akɛ agbi ŋmaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛwo kotoku mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to store my harvested yams inside a shaded room instead of leaving them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ baato tsu ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ

english: Leaving yams outside exposes them to hot sun and unexpected rain, which damages their skin and causes rapid rotting. Storing them inside keeps them cool, dry, and protected from bad weather.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ ehiɛ ni ehaa efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa edɔɔ, egbiɔ, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe.

english: Why do dried cocoa beans turn moldy if rain touches them while they are waiting to be bagged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo yibii ni egbi lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni akɛwo tsɔne mli lɛ?

english: Dry cocoa beans act like sponges and soak up moisture very quickly. Once water touches them, dormant mold spores wake up and destroy the beans, so they must always be kept under cover.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni eŋɔɔ nu oya waa. Kɛ nu kɛ fungal spores ni ewɔ lɛ kpe lɛ, ebaate shi ni efite ŋmeii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aŋmɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I keep my grain sacks elevated on wooden pallets instead of leaving the base of the sacks directly on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo dumɔwui kotokui anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi kotoku lɛ shishitoo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ

english: Cold floors pass damp moisture into the bottom of the bags. Wooden pallets keep the base off the ground so air can circulate, preventing water damage and mold at the bottom.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa nu ni mli efɔ baa kotoku lɛ shishi. Tsoi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haaa shishitoo lɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ nu ni fiteɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ naa.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if rain water sits on their leaves for a long time without drying?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ta baai lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni egbiko?

english: Water trapped on leaves creates the perfect environment for fungal diseases like blight to attack the plant. Good spacing between plants helps air blow through and dry the leaves faster after rain.
ga: Nu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ baai ahe lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight ni baatutua tsei lɛ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava chips turn dark or spoil when rain falls on them while drying on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be mli ni egbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When water touches cassava chips while they are drying, it restarts fermentation and attracts dark mold. If rain threatens, the chips must be covered or moved inside immediately.
ga: Beni nu kɛ ŋmei ŋmɔji lɛ kpe be mli ni amɛmiigbi lɛ. Ebaabɔi ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehe baahia ni aha nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ loo ajie kɛya mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Can I wash harvested vegetables with water to clean off dirt before taking them to the market?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu afɔ aduawai ni akpa lɛ ahe koni majie muji kɛjɛ mli dani mikɛya jara nɔ?

english: You can wash off dirt, but you must wipe or air-dry the produce thoroughly before packing. Leaving standing water on produce causes soft rot during transportation to market.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofɔ muji lɛ he. Shi ehe miihia ni otsumɔ loo okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha egbi dani okɛwo tsɔne mli. Nu ni damɔ shi ni ashiɔ yɛ nibii ni adu lɛ anɔ lɛ haa egboɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crop turn yellow when water collects around the base of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess water pooling at the base smothers the roots and cuts off oxygen. When roots cannot breathe, the lower leaves turn yellow and die, eventually causing root rot if the water stays.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni buaa ehe naa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ naagbee kɛji nu eshwɛ.

english: If I see a few diseased cocoa pods on my trees, why should I pluck them off one by one immediately?
ga: Kɛji mina kookoo ŋmeii ayibɔ ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Diseased pods release tiny spores that spread to healthy pods whenever rain splashes or insects crawl on them. Removing affected pods one by one stops the sickness from spreading to the rest of the tree.
ga: Pods ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ spores bibii. No gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ loo ekɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ shi. Ajieɔ pods ni ena naagbai lɛ ekomekomei. Enɛ baatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it better to stop pests when I see just a few on my crop instead of waiting until they cover the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makpa tsɛŋemɔ helai be mli ni minaa ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaamɛ ni amɛha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Insects multiply very quickly once established. Catching and removing a few early prevents a full outbreak, saving your crop before widespread damage occurs.
ga: Kplukai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya kɛji amɛto amɛhe shi pɛ. Mra ni amɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ hela ni baa lɛ naa kwraa. ni oye obua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala dani fitemɔ ni gbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and scorching during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted nearby to protect them from direct heat and hold moisture in the soil while their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves and catch direct sunlight. When the leaves get enough light, they produce the food needed to grow large, healthy yam tubers underground instead of wasting energy spreading on the soil.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ ná la ni fa bɔ ni sa Ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa koni sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite hewalɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: If too many shoots (suckers) grow around one plantain stem, they steal water and nutrients from the main tree. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, which produces a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo yɛ ni miida yɛ plantain tso kome he. Ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso ni hereɔ lɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha plantain ŋmeii ni da ni tsii kwraa aba.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their blossoms before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiwo aduawai dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or having too much nitrogen fertilizer which makes the plant grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛ́ amɛmiihao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ni haa tomato tsei lɛ náa baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips usually means your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives crops their deep green color and helps them grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ŋmɔlɔ ni baa yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hia yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa tsei lɛ su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which can pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally enriches the soil and provides extra food for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ agbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii babaoo.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer away from the root zone into gutters and rivers before the crop can soak it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist so the roots can absorb it properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui kɛ faai amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips that suck sap from the underside of leaves, or viruses spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early prevents leaf damage and stunted growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai lɛ afitemɔ kɛ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot inside the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mifee klalo akɛ makpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when soil stays soaked with water for too long due to poor drainage. Excessive water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungal diseases that rot the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt inside the leaf center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli ewo muji kɛ sũ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the center funnel of the plant. If left untreated, these worms destroy the leaf tissue and reduce crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ faai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: I have a piece of land that has been sitting idle for years; what is a good crop I can plant on it to get started easily?
ga: Miyɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni akɛtsuuu nii afii babaoo nɛ. Mɛni ji tsei kpakpai komɛi ni manyɛ madu koni manyɛ mabɔi nitsumɔ mlɛo?

english: Cassava or maize are ideal choices for newly cleared land. Cassava is tough, tolerates poor soil, and needs minimal care, while maize grows quickly within three to four months, helping you get a fast harvest while you learn how your land behaves.
ga: Cassava loo ŋmãa ji nibii ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ. Kasava wa. Eŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ gbɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmã daa oya yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okpaa nii oya yɛ be mli ni okaseɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ enii ehaa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is their main nutrient for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves water standing in the soil, suffocating the roots so they cannot absorb food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmãa tso lɛ daa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu niyenii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They behave best under shade crops like plantains, which act as living umbrellas to cool the air and keep the soil moist while the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ feɔ lɛ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays around them in heavy or flat soil, creating conditions where fungal diseases thrive. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps surplus rain drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo ebɔle amɛhe. amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed the unpollinated flower.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii Ehaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local weather and soil conditions, allowing them to drink water and absorb nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni amɛduɔ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: What will happen to my maize if I plant the seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete heavily for sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall and thin with weak stems, producing tiny corn cobs instead of full ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa bibii baa. Yɛ baai ni eyi obɔ najiaŋ

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or a virus spread by these insects. The feeding damages the young leaf tissues, causing them to twist and stunt plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Niyenii fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ amli fãji. Ekɛ sɛɛkuu baa ni etsĩɔ tsei adalɛ naa.

english: Why does my land produce fewer tomatoes when I plant them in the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tomatoi fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously allows pests and soil diseases that target that specific crop to build up in the dirt. Rotating tomatoes with legumes like cowpeas starves out tomato pests and restores natural fertility to the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni aduɔ lɛ kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ejie tomato mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and fold during hot afternoons even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants fold or droop their large leaves during intense heat to reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the sun, preventing excessive water loss. They naturally perk back up in the evening when temperatures cool down.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baafolɔ loo amɛbaagbee baai agboi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite fe nine Amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees protect young cocoa leaves from burning and help keep the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full weather.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​hulutsoo be lɛ he nii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. This happens when the soil is worn out or when heavy rains wash away the nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Amɛji tsei ni niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ fite loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does adding animal manure or decomposed leaves to my farm help crops grow better than plain soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ daa lɛ?

english: Manure and compost act like a soft sponge and storehouse for plant food. They improve the soil's ability to hold water during dry spells and slowly feed natural nutrients to crop roots as they grow.
ga: Manɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni yɔɔ blɛoo. kɛ tsei aniyenii ni akɛtoɔ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ, ni amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa tsei shishifãi lɛ fiofio be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why should I plant beans or groundnuts on a plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and leaves the land tired. Legumes like beans and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my corn leaves and dark dirt inside the plant stalk?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei ahe tsei amli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant during the day, eating the tender shoots and leaving behind their waste.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Ye ŋmeii bibii ni oshi jwɛi yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mifolɔ amɛ po lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long. Poor water drainage starves the roots of air and allows fungal diseases in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ atutua bulb lɛ ni amɛfite.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miifɔlɔ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms. Without proper moisture and cool temperatures, the flower falls off before a tomato can form.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ. aloo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ bɛ. Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi dani tomatoi lɛ afee.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tuber through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground into the air and sunlight, preventing rot and allowing the plant to make bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii haa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe tsei kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa bulbs wuji.

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly wet several inches deep after two or three strong rains. Planting after a light shower is risky because the seeds will germinate and quickly dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashɛ inchii babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwu komɛ kɛ je ye ngma kpami nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ yi.

english: Seeds saved from past harvests lose their vigor over time and can carry diseases from the previous crop. Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, handle harsh weather better, and give much higher yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni jɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ aba Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli ni ehaa yibii babaoo baa

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees off the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high temperatures. Leaving shade trees or planting plantains around them protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps retain moisture in the soil during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ he waa. Tsei ni ashiɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to spread their leaves out to catch sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground and away from soil-borne diseases, allowing the plant to photosynthesize better and feed the growing tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso ko ni esa akɛ egbɛ baai lɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ fotosintɛsis tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate that the maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. As the plant grows, it pulls stored nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth when the soil lacks enough food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa Egbala niyenii ni ato kɛjɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei adalɛ hee niyenii be mli ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land year after year, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei lɛ akwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi. Abɛi kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: If I plant tree crops like oil palm that stay in the ground for decades, how does it affect my soil over time?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei tamɔ mu tsei ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ lɛ, Te ebaaná mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Perennial tree crops continuously take nutrients out of the ground to produce leaves and fruit bunches year after year. Without regularly adding organic matter, compost, or fertilizer back into the earth, the soil slowly becomes depleted and hard, leading to smaller yields as the trees age.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be koni amɛwo baai kɛ aduawai akui afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛji akɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he daa lɛ, fiofio lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no baaha yibiiwoo aba shi be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete directly with the main mother plant for food, water, and sunlight. Pruning away the extra suckers and leaving only one strong follower allows the main plant to put all its energy into producing a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting underground without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni amɛfee klalo akɛ akɛbaato shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe ehiaaa ni otsa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Cassava plants show maturity above ground when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the main stem begins to branch out. You can also carefully dig around the base of one sample plant to check if the roots have swollen to a good size.
