ga: Yucca tsei lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni tso lɛ tso titri lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji shishifãi lɛ efu kɛyashɛ he ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off the plant without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to heat stress or lack of water. When temperatures get too high or the plant is thirsty, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy and survive rather than spending resources on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ loo nu ni bɛ hewɔ titri. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kumai miiye tso lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and ground nutrients. When weeds crowd around your crops, the crops stretch tall and thin trying to reach the sunlight while starving for nutrients below.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi bɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo, ni amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot, dry weather to reduce the leaf surface exposed to the sun, helping the plant hold onto water. However, if curling happens alongside yellow spots, it often means tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids are damaging the undersides of the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ be mli, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi koni eba baa lɛ nɔ hulu la shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ emɔɔ nu. Shi, kɛji akɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ba kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ ŋmeii, miifite baai lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains to shield them, the intense heat burns the leaves and dries out the soil moisture that the young roots need to survive.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ ko nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa shishifãi bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant naturally pulls nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to keep the young growth at the top alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni eha tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot when heavy rain leaves standing water on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu taraa miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it pushes out all the air, suffocating the roots and allowing rotting fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when afternoons get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Extreme heat dries out the pollen, so the flower fails to form fruit and drops off.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji shwane lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ wooo yibii ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why are the fresh leaves on my pepper plants curling up and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. The feeding damages the leaf structure as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Niyenii fiteɔ baa lɛ shishitoo be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why does my main plantain stem produce smaller bunches if I leave many suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwere yɛ he lɛ? Mi plantain titri lɛ

english: All suckers connected to the main plantain stem share the same food and water source. Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal nutrients from the main stem, leaving less energy for big fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii fɛɛ ni kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu jɛɛhe kome. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Enɛ haa hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ kɛha aduawai akuu agbo ko.

english: Cowpeas are legumes with special root nodules that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food. When the cowpea plants decay, that extra nitrogen remains in the soil for the maize to feed on.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Beni tsina tso lɛ fiteɔ Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmãa lɛ aye.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start producing sprouts in the barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams have an internal biological clock. After a resting period (dormancy) post-harvest, the tuber naturally wakes up and uses its stored water and nutrients to push out new sprouts for the next season.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ wala mli ŋmɛlɛtswaa ko. yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswaa sɛɛ (ŋmɛlɛtswaa) yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Bulbs lɛ teɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg leaves droop during the hot afternoon but stand upright again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛdamɔ shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: In high heat, leaves lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The plant intentionally wilts to reduce its surface area exposed to the sun and save water, recovering overnight when temperatures cool.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Akɛ yiŋtoo ko shwieɔ tsei anɔ koni hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi ni akɛbu nu he. Ebaatsa ehe nyɔɔŋ kome mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why is dry weather so dangerous for my maize farm right when the tassels and silks appear at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ awui beni ŋmeii kɛ siliki jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: The tasseling stage is when maize reproduces to form seeds on the cob. If the plant lacks water during this brief period, the silks dry out before receiving pollen, resulting in cobs with missing or underdeveloped grains.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuaa ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ ji be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be kukuoo nɛɛ mli lɛ, siliki lɛ baagbi dani enine ashɛ pollen nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni elaaje loo edarako lɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right amount of fertilizer to give my crops so I do not waste my money or hurt the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni okafite shika loo okaye tsei lɛ awui?

english: Crops need specific amounts of fertilizer depending on their age and type. Giving them too little will not help them grow, while giving them too much can burn their roots and damage the crop.
ga: Tsei biɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko. Edamɔ afii kɛ tso lɛ henɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ ha amɛ lɛ, eyeee ebuaaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa. Yɛ be mli ni akɛhaa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What does compound fertilizer like NPK do to my crops when I put it in the soil?
ga: Mɛni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tamɔ NPK lɛ feɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Compound fertilizers give crops a balanced diet. One part helps the leaves grow green and big, another part strengthens the roots and flowers, and the last part helps the plant fight off diseases and produce strong fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii ni sa. Enɛ fã ko yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa. Fã kroko hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ mli waa. Ni naagbee fã lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ helai wuɔ ni ewoɔ yibii ni mli wa.

english: If my fertilizer bag gets wet or loses its strength before I use it, how does that affect my crops?
ga: Kɛji mi ŋmɔshi nibii kotoku lɛ mli fũu loo ehewalɛ sɛɛ fo dani mikɛtsu nii Te ebaaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer that absorbs moisture or gets spoiled loses its nutrients. If you apply weak or damaged fertilizer, your crops will not get the feeding they need, even if you put a full bag on the farm.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafite niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni efite wo mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naaa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ baagi eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli po.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crops when they are very young or when they start flowering?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii beni amɛdarako kwraa loo beni amɛjeɔ fɔmɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Young crops need feeding early to build strong roots and stems, while a second round of fertilizer just before flowering helps them produce bigger grains and heavier fruits.
ga: Ehe miihia ni aha ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii mra. Bɔni afee ni etswa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ wo mli dani ewo fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo dumɔwui wuji kɛ aduawai ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops look very green and tall after I apply fertilizer, but end up giving me very small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛkwɔ waa beni mikɛ amɛ wo amɛmli lɛ? Shi ani ehaa yibii fioo ko pɛ?

english: Fertilizer can sometimes be deceiving by making a plant grow plenty of leaves quickly, while the plant still lacks the right balance of nutrients needed to produce heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ atsu nii kɛtsɔ baai babaoo ni ekɛhaa tso lɛ oya lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei bɛ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni amɛwo aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Why are my crops producing plenty of leaves but no flowers or fruits after I feed them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi loo aduawai ko bɛ mli beni mikɛ niyenii ha lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus only on growing leaves and stems while delaying flowering, making the plant look very healthy on the outside even though it is not ready to yield fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baaha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai kɛ shishifã lɛ pɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Ehaa kponɔgbɛ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa eyɛ mli akɛ efeko klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii lolo moŋ.

english: How can I tell if the fertilizer I put on my crops is actually helping them or causing them stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo ehaa amɛhaoɔ?

english: Healthy growth shows steady green leaves and strong stems. If the leaf tips turn brown, yellow, or start curling shortly after you feed them, it means the plant received too much fertilizer or the wrong type.
ga: Dalɛ kpakpa jieɔ baai eŋɔli ni ma shi shiŋŋ kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni wa kpo. Kɛji baai lɛ ashishigbɛ tsɔ blɔfo, ŋmɔŋ, loo ebɔi ŋmɔlɔ beni okɛ niyenii eha amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my crop leaves still turn yellow even after I have applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant lacks a specific nutrient that your fertilizer did not provide, or heavy rains washed the fertilizer away from the roots before the plant could drink it.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni o-fertilizer lɛ haaa lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ miinɛ waa, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why do my plants look weak during dry weather even though I gave them enough fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve in the soil so the roots can drink it. In dry weather, the fertilizer stays dry in the dirt and cannot feed the plant, and can even burn the roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anu. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni enyɛɛɛ eha tsei lɛ niyenii. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ashã

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops whenever I put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ be fɛɛ be ni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that easily steal water and fertilizer away from your crops. You must clear all weeds before applying fertilizer so your main crops get all the food.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli oya. Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli bɔni afee ni otso titri lɛ aná niyenii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes the nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the juices from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies. Treating these pests early prevents the leaves from shrinking and curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɔjɔ ni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and woody even after waiting a long time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tso yɛ be mli ni mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ po koni akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soft, loose soil to swell up into big tubers. If your farm soil is hard and compacted, or if you plant the stems too close together, the roots cannot expand and will remain thin and tough.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛfu ni amɛfee bulbs agboi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle ehe Aloo kɛji odu tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛbaakã he amɛfee mlɛo ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my yam leaves turning brown and drying up long before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves dry up early when they are attacked by a fungal disease called anthracnose, especially during heavy rains. When the leaves die early, the yam tuber underground stops growing bigger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ tutua amɛ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli Beni baai lɛ shwieɔ oya Shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ.

english: That is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep into the growing center of the maize plant to feed on tender leaves, which can stunt or kill the crop if not controlled quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nakai baa lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Efoɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ajie loo efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akudɔɔɔ oya.

english: Why are the young flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off before making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they are stressed by prolonged hot weather, lack of shade, or attacks from insects like capsids. Providing shade trees and protecting against bugs helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi tamɔ capsids tutua amɛ. Shade kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi ahe yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or prolonged dry spells that prevent the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli loo shihilɛ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep. Tiny worms in the soil called nematodes often eat away the underground roots, weakening the plant's hold on the ground so even light winds can tip it over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ, no hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko po baanyɛ atsɔ ehe.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds after the first rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best not to plant on the very first rain because the ground underneath is still hot and dry. Wait until you get two or three steady rains so the soil stays deep-moist, which keeps seeds from drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli edɔ lolo ni edɔ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fioo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with strong root systems that absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops. Clearing them while they are still tiny prevents them from stealing food from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa ni shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary nutrient plants use to build healthy leaves. Applying compost or a nitrogen-based fertilizer early in the crop's growth restores green color and improves grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛmaa baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ ayibɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops so that it does not go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛkafite?

english: Fertilizer is most effective when applied to moist soil while plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after planting. Applying it to dry soil can burn roots, while applying it right before heavy rain washes the fertilizer away before plants can absorb it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii 2-3 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã. Shi okɛwo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa koni ekɛfɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when excess rainwater sits around them for too long because the roots drown from a lack of oxygen in waterlogged soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away easily, keeping tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Ha oyitso ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning yellow during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from heat and water loss during hot, dry weather. Watering regularly at the base of the plant early in the morning helps maintain steady moisture and reduces leaf stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ nu egbi lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa, ni ehaa baa lɛ nɔ haomɔ baa shi.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by dry weather, pest attacks, or lack of pollination by tiny insects called midges. Maintaining shade trees on your farm keeps the soil moist and creates a cool environment for pollinators to thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi bibii, loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges ni haaa amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Plantain trees fall over easily because they have shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches of fruit. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or Y-shaped branch prevents wind from tipping the tree over before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ loo tso nine ni tamɔ Y fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa tso lɛ shi dani akpa tso lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper seedlings remaining small and refusing to grow taller after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ji bibii waa ni amɛkpooɔ akɛ amɛbaadara babaoo beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants become stunted if their roots are damaged during transplanting or if the soil is too hard for root expansion. Watering the nursery bed before lifting seedlings and loosening the field soil gives roots the freedom to grow.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ lɛ loo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ afɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ nu dani awó dumɔwui lɛ anɔ, ni ajie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa heyeli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting gives crops full access to necessary nutrients and allows them to establish strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa

english: Why do my yam vines dry up early before the yam tubers are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up prematurely when attacked by fungal leaf diseases or extreme drought. Staking yam vines on sturdy poles keeps leaves off the wet ground, reducing humidity around leaves and preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi oya kɛji akɛ fungal leaf hela loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei ni wa anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akajɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when I clear all the shade trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Mi ŋmɔ lɛ momo?

english: Cocoa trees, especially young ones, naturally prefer light shade. Clearing all big trees exposes cocoa plants to direct sunlight and hot winds, causing leaf stress, water loss, leaf yellowing, and premature leaf drop.
ga: Cocoa tsei, titri lɛ gbekɛbii lɛ, sumɔɔ sui ni mli tse yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ ajie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ ashɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ shoo, nu fiteɔ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why should I plant plantains near my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from direct sunshine and heat. Fast-growing plantain plants provide quick temporary shade and keep the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: No, planting maize too close together causes plants to compete heavily for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin stalks with tiny or empty cobs, ultimately lowering your total harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa. loo efolo Enɛ haa yɛ naagbee lɛ, onitsumɔ fɛɛ ni otsuɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the shoots growing around my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi.

english: Too many young shoots (suckers) take food and water away from the main mother stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishi (tso lɛ shishi) babaoo tsɔ baatswa niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ aduawai akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, oxygen is blocked, allowing fungal decay to set in and turn the tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to build big earth mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and well-drained soil to grow deep and wide. Mounds collect topsoil, improve drainage, and make it easier for underground tubers to expand freely.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekwɛ̃ ni egbɛ eshwa. Gɔŋ lɛ buaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa. ehaa nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa amɛhe.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to environmental stress like high heat, severe dry spells, or over-fertilizing with nitrogen, which causes the plant to drop blossoms to conserve energy.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa. aloo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Curled, distorted leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the plant juices, or viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of bushy green leaves but produce very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Adding too much nitrogen fertilizer causes cowpeas to spend all their energy making leaves instead of flowering. Cowpeas naturally produce their own nitrogen, so extra fertilizer harms pod production.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ atsu nii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fata he lɛ, ebaafite podfeemɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slowly even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal the fertilizer, soil moisture, and sunlight before your crops can absorb them, effectively starving your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Sir, why do my young cocoa plants wither and turn brown when the sunny season starts?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops, like plantains or bananas, to block harsh heat, hold soil moisture, and protect them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo banana. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahi shi ni obu he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting at the tip usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even though I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: When you plant the same crop on the same piece of land continuously, it consumes all the specific nutrients in that soil without giving the land time to recover. Rotating your crops or adding organic manure restores soil fertility.
ga: Beni oyaa nɔ oduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛhaaa sũ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Oŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsake loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and air to produce big, healthy yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Sir, why do some farmers plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with their maize?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize while also reducing weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ abele niyenii, yɛ be mli ni ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ hu baa shi.

english: What is making small ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the maize plant. Inspecting fields early and using recommended treatments or neem extracts can protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii loo neem mli nu lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground during heavy rainfall periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them without draining away, starving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away and prevents root decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shi ni efooo. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Officer, why should I cut off some of the extra young shoots growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers forces the mother plantain tree to share its food with all of them, leading to small fruit bunches. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy for a large yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ehe bahia ni dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ aja niyenii yɛ amɛ fɛɛ ateŋ. Ewoɔ aduawai akui bibii. Kɛ́ ahiɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nibii babaoo ni afeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn black and soft before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom end rot, happens when the plant lacks calcium or receives irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots transport calcium evenly to the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ aya aduawai lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the dirt around their crops with dry grass or cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose their leaves during the dry season but still stay alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli shi eyɛ wala mli lolo lɛ?

english: Cassava plants store extra energy in their thick roots just like a food bank. When dry weather forces the plant to shed its leaves, it survives by living off this stored energy until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kroko toɔ eshishifãi ni mli ewo wu lɛ amli tamɔ niyenii atoohe. Beni kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ. Tsei hiɔ shi kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why does a stored seed yam start sprouting in my barn even without soil or water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni ato lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ loo nu bɛ jɛmɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: A seed yam tuber is packed with stored food energy. Even without soil, it uses its internal reserves to push out new growth until it runs out of stored food or gets planted.
ga: Akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ eyi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ amli obɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ bɛ moŋ Shi ekɛ mligbɛ nibii ni ato lɛ hu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ dalɛ hee naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni niyenii ni ato lɛ baaho loo aduɔ.

english: If I prune back my old cocoa trees, how do they grow new leaves without any original leaves left to feed them?
ga: Kɛji mifo kookoo tso momo lɛ No hewɔ lɛ te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kookoo tso ko akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni shishijee baai lɛ eshwɛɛɛ?

english: Trees store reserve energy inside their trunks and roots. When you cut back the top branches, the tree pushes that stored food upward to sprout fresh new leaves.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji ofo niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni ato lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eha baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my tomato plants look so weak and exhausted right after producing a large harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Making fruits uses up almost all of the plant's stored food energy. Once the tomatoes are full-grown, the plant has emptied its internal reserve and needs water and nutrients to recover.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni tso lɛ eto lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ aduawai. Kɛji akɛ tomato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ emli nibii ni ekɛto lɛ ni ehe hiaa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into straws during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl to trap moisture and prevent the plant from losing water. It is a defense reaction to protect its remaining water and energy so it does not dry out and collapse.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaje nu mli. Eji nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Koni ekagbi ni ekagbee shi.

english: How does leaf disease cause my pepper plants to stop growing even when I water them every day?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni folier hela ko atsĩ mi-pepper tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ?

english: Leaves act as the plant's food factory. When disease damages or covers the leaves, the plant can no longer make or store energy, leaving it unable to grow regardless of how much water it receives.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ niyenii nitsumɔhe. Kɛ hela lɛ kpata loo eha baai lɛ ahe lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee loo amɛto hewalɛ dɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa enyɛŋ eda bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni nu ni enine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ fa ha.

english: Why does root-knot disease kill my crops even when the soil has plenty of manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ root knot hela lɛ gbeɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli moŋ?

english: Roots act as the crop's mouth to absorb water and food. When disease damages the roots, the plant cannot swallow the food in the soil, causing it to starve despite being surrounded by nutrients.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ tso lɛ daaŋ ni eŋɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ hela kpata shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ami niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ebɔle amɛhe moŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn pale yellow and remain small when planted in poor soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi bibioo kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ?

english: Plants need soil nutrients to build green leaves and manufacture energy. In poor soil, the plant stays weak and cannot produce or store enough food to grow tall or make big cobs.
ga: Tsei hia niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛha hewalɛ. yɛ shikpɔŋ gbonyo nɔ Tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo loo amɛto niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara loo amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do crops grown under heavy tree shade fail to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsii shishi lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to turn water and soil nutrients into plant food. Under deep shade, the crop cannot make enough food energy to store away for making big grains or fruits.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛtsake nu kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ amɛfee tsei aniyenii. Yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ lɛ shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛto kɛha dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji feemɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce such small and light yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal the water, light, and fertilizer from the soil before your crop can get them. Without enough of these essentials, your crop cannot build up the energy reserves needed to produce a heavy harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aná. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ faaa lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ ama hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛwo nibii babaoo lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: If my land is cleared and burned after a heavy distraction, how soon can I safely plant cassava?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashã yɛ be mli ni ahao mi waa lɛ sɛɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu ŋmei shweshweeshwe?

english: Burning leaves ashes that give a short boost of nutrients, but the intense heat kills beneficial soil organisms and dries out the land. You should wait for the first good rain to cool the soil down and restore moisture before planting your cassava stems.
ga: Sũ lɛ ni ashãa lɛ haa niyenii krokomɛi fataa he yɛ be kukuoo mli. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ kpataa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbiɔ. Esa akɛ omɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ ni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni ekɛ nu aba ekoŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmei tsei adu.

english: Why does my soil become so hard and grow poor crops after I farm on the same plot for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa waa ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu ehiii yɛ be mli ni mikɛ afii babaoo etsu ŋmɔ kome mli nii lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground every season. If you continuously farm without adding manure, compost, or letting the land rest, the soil loses its organic matter and nutrients, causing it to pack tightly like concrete and starve your plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Kɛji otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe lɛ fataaa he lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ekpɛɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit ni ehaa tsei lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow after heavy flooding on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu afua ni naa wa ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns plant roots by blocking air and washing away nitrogen, which is the main nutrient that gives leaves their dark green color. Without air and nitrogen, the leaves turn pale and yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa kɛ nitrogen ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen bɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants drying up and dropping off in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and tender roots that cannot drink water fast enough when direct, strong sunlight hits them. Sunlight causes water to evaporate quickly from the leaves, making them burn and drop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ anu nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mli wa lɛ mli. Hulu la haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. shã ni egbee shi

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruit during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the pollen inside the tomato blossom so it cannot produce seeds. The plant then drops the unfertilized flower to save its water and energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Dɔlɛ kpataa pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ ahiɛ. Ehaa enyɛɛɛ ewo dumɔwui. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. They stretch upward to reach the light instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaná tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I plant plantain suckers alongside my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei adu dumɔwui?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and cool soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava tubers small and watery when I harvest them during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During heavy rains, cassava plants spend their energy absorbing water and growing leaves instead of storing starch in the roots. Harvesting in drier weather yields firmer, starchier tubers.
ga: yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmuɔ nu ni ehaa ebaai lɛ daraa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, Nikpamɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni mli wa, ni starch yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize farm more during short dry spells in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Warm dry weather allows caterpillar eggs to hatch faster and prevents natural fungal diseases that normally kill pests during heavy rains, leading to a sudden surge in armyworms.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii akui ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ oya. ni etsĩɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bei pii lɛ egbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa. Enɛ ha ŋmeii akuu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up completely before the yams are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ kwraa dani efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: The drying up of yam vines is a natural signal that the plant has finished making food in its leaves and has transferred all its stored energy down into the tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso lɛ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe eniyenii he saamɔ naa. ni ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick even after I spray them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yaa nɔ hela mɔɔ amɛ lɛ? Beni mikɛ tsofa wo amɛmli lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: When crops are planted too close together, leaves touch and diseases spread quickly from plant to plant. Also, dense plants prevent chemicals from reaching all parts of the crop, making it difficult to stop sickness once it starts.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ taa amɛhe ni hela gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Tsoi ni fa babaoo lɛ hu tsiɔ tsofai anaa koni amɛkashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ abaakpa hela kɛji eje shishi pɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I pack as many crops as possible into my field?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo ŋmɔ mli bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: No, planting too closely actually lowers your yield. Overcrowded crops struggle for light, water, and soil food, causing them to become weak and produce smaller fruits or grains.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ odu obɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii loo ŋmaa bibii lɛ baa.

english: Why does my farm feel so hot and stuffy inside when the crops grow thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Tightly packed crops block the wind from blowing through your farm. This traps heat and moisture around the plants, creating a humid atmosphere that encourages fungi and rot.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i bɔleɔ tso lɛ he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he hewalɛ baa.

english: Can excessive heat alone make my crops sick, or is it always pests?
ga: Ani dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine pɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela loo eji tsɛŋemɔ hela be fɛɛ be?

english: High heat puts physical stress on plants by forcing them to lose moisture faster than roots can draw it from the soil. This heat stress lowers the plant's natural defenses, making it easy for sickness to enter.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ baa tsei anɔ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛjie ŋmɔtɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu nibii baa shi. Ehaa helai baa mli oya

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from plant stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ tsei ahe haomɔ hewɔ?

english: Stressed crops often wilt during the day, turn yellowish, grow very slowly, or shed their flowers early. Stress usually happens when plants deal with severe heat, lack of water, or overcrowding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni haoɔ lɛ gboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, edaa blɛoo waa loo ewoɔ fɔfɔi oya Bei pii lɛ, haomɔ baa kɛji tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he, nu bɛ, loo amɛyi obɔ kɛ mɛi babaoo.

english: Why does sickness spread faster across my farm during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Strong heat combined with crowded conditions forces plants to use up their energy quickly just to stay alive. Weakened by heat, crowded plants easily pass infections to neighboring plants.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni kɛ shihilɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ fataa he lɛ haa tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ oya koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ. yɛ dɔlɛ ni eba shi lɛ hewɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ tsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves at the bottom of my crowded crops start to rot during the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, air cannot pass through the bottom leaves to dry them after rain. Trapped moisture combined with warm air creates the perfect environment for rot to destroy the leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni eha amɛgbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha baai ni fiteɔ kɛ fitemɔ.

english: How does trimming away some branches help my crops stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei lɛ aniji komɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Pruning extra branches opens up space for breeze and sunlight to reach the inside of the crop. Good airflow lowers heat, dries wet leaves, and keeps sickness from building up.
ga: Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ gbeleɔ gbɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa shi. baai ni efɔ lɛ egbi ni ekɛ hela baaa

english: Does crowding cause disease directly, or does it just make the plants weak?
ga: Ani tso lɛ mli bii ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ hela baa tɛ̃ɛ loo ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Crowding causes stress first by forcing plants to fight for survival. This continuous stress weakens the plant's immunity, making it very easy for airborne germs to cause disease.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu koni amɛhi shi lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni yaa nɔ daa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli hewalɛ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo waa akɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ helai baa.

english: What is the best way to stop diseases from destroying my crops before the season starts?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ akpa helai ni fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani be lɛ aje shishi?

english: The best protection is proper plant spacing during planting. Giving plants room to breathe prevents stress and heat buildup, stopping diseases before they ever start.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni buɔ mɔ he ji dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛmu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ haomɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa shi lɛ naa. Ye obua ni akpa hela dani ebɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually shows that the plant is hungry for nitrogen. Maize moves its remaining nitrogen to the newer top leaves to survive, leaving the old lower leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Abɛi baajie nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans in my field make the soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni baaba yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the leaves and roots decay, they leave behind natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii ni akɛwo tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my yam plants growing very long green vines with many leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ wain tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen or excess water, they spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending energy to build the tubers underneath.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen loo nu babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, e tsuɔ he wami konɛ e kɛ pee zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the hot afternoon sunshine hits them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ tswa amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that lose water faster than they can absorb it in direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cool shelter that keeps them alive until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa he ko ni mli ejɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems keeps the field healthy.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni jɛmɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw water from the soil, causing them to wilt to protect themselves. If they bounce back by evening, it is a normal protective behavior.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ koni ebu ehe. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ lɛ, enɛ ji hebuu subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight underground for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves shade each other from sunshine, resulting in thin stalks with small ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil covered with mulch and keeping plants watered helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I leave thick, overgrown branches inside the tree canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mishi niji ni mli tse ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Dense branches prevent sunlight and air from reaching the main trunk where cocoa flowers bloom, creating dark, humid places where pests and diseases thrive instead of growing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ tso titri lɛ he ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ yɛ lɛ. Ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii kɛ helai shwereɔ yɛ yɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛakwɛ̃ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant seeds saved from last year's maize harvest instead of buying new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, heɔ dumɔwui ehei ni awo he odase.

english: Many commercial seeds are special hybrids bred for high yields, but the seeds harvested from them lose those strong traits in the next generation, producing weaker plants with smaller yields.
ga: Jarayeli dumɔwui babaoo ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops dry up so quickly even when it rains heavily for a short time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain on hard ground causes water to quickly run off the surface instead of sinking in. Without trenches or catchment spots to slow the water down, soil cannot hold enough moisture for plant roots to use later.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefo shi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo hei ni nu yɔɔ ni baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ kɛbaatsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: Can I dig shallow trenches across my farm to help my crops get more water?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafo bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná nu babaoo?

english: Yes, digging shallow trenches along the slope catches rainwater runoff and gives it time to soak deep into the soil, keeping your crops hydrated even during short dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋshɔkei ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ atsamɔ. Yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ, emɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni ehaa be ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po.

english: If my farm is located near a community water catchment area, can I freely draw water from it for my crops?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛ akutso lɛ mli nutoohe ko Ani manyɛ majie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ heyeli mli?

english: Water catchment areas are often protected to keep drinking water clean for the whole community. Using chemicals or over-pumping near these zones can contaminate the supply or violate local water protection laws.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abuɔ hei ni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ lɛ ahe koni akutso muu lɛ fɛɛ aná nu ni mli tse ni anuɔ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli fe nine yɛ hei nɛɛ baanyɛ afite nu ni akɛhaa lɛ loo eku maŋ lɛ mli nu hebuu mlai amli.

english: Will planting crops directly on the edge of a stream make them grow better?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ faai ahe lɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: While the soil near streams stays moist, planting right at the bank exposes your crops to soil erosion during heavy rains and can cause root damage from flooded, waterlogged soil.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ lolo. Nibii ni ooodu yɛ faa lɛ naa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite onibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi afite kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and fall off during long dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: When water is scarce, cassava plants naturally shed leaves to cut down on water loss through evaporation, preserving vital moisture in their roots to survive until the rains return.
ga: Kɛ nu faaa lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu ni he hiaa waa lɛ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baanɛ.

english: Why do my plants look weak and yellow when water sits on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni nu ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water suffocates plant roots by cutting off their air supply. Without air, roots cannot take up food and nutrients from the soil, causing the plant to turn yellow and weaken.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: How does digging and turning over the soil help my crops get water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mifoɔ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa nu?

english: Loosening hard soil creates spaces inside the earth that act like a sponge, allowing rainwater to soak deeper into the root zone instead of washing away valuable topsoil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji baa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeefɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops droop in the hot afternoon sun even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi po.

english: On very hot days, crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than roots can draw it up. Drooping is the plant's way of reducing its surface area exposed to the sun to save water, and it usually recovers by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie. Drooping ji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbaa amɛhe ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense heat and need shade trees to protect them from direct sun, keeping the surrounding air and soil cool and humid while they grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbiɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni oduɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my maize cobs stay small and light when rain stops during the flowering stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Flowering is when maize builds its grains. If the plant lacks water during this specific time, it cannot transport enough food to fill out the cob, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Fɔfɔii ji be mli ni ŋmãa woɔ dumɔwui. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ be ni ato lɛ mli lɛ, Amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: When the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, and when soil nutrients run low, the plant moves what little nitrogen it has to the newer top leaves.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. ni kɛ́ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it better for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my farm before planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Rotating them with heavy-feeding crops like maize naturally restores soil fertility without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ kooloi aniyenii mli ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why are small caterpillars destroying the funnels of my young maize plants early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ agbɛi lɛ leebi lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, an invasive pest whose larvae feed inside the growing tip (whorl) of maize plants. They hide in the leaf folds during the day and feed at night or early morning, making early detection and targeted sprays crucial before they ruin the growing point.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa mɔ nɔ ni eshishifãi lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishifãi (rings) ni miida lɛ amli. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi mli, ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa. Ha ana mra Ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ he hiaa dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in heavy or flat soil for too long without draining away. High moisture creates an ideal environment for soil fungi to attack the tubers, which is why planting cassava on ridges or raised mounds helps drain excess water.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni baatutua ŋmeii lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight or hot winds. Shade trees protect fragile seedlings from sun scorch and maintain soil moisture until the cocoa plants develop deep root systems and a strong canopy.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa baa.

english: If I plant my crops very close to each other, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa babaoo nɔ kɛjɛŋ mishikpɔŋ bibioo lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close forces crops to compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and smaller fruits, whereas proper spacing gives each plant enough space to produce a healthier, higher yield overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them stay alive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil from the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and gradually adds organic matter to the soil as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ekɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he fiofio beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up during the dry, windy Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan be ni nu egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry, windy weather, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the dry ground. Curling leaves is a self-defense reaction to reduce the leaf surface area exposed to the dry air and conserve water.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni Tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Baai ni abɔleɔ he lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ he koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ baa shi lɛ shi ni akɛbu nu he.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is a lack of pollinators like bees. Irregular watering during flowering stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to preserve its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollinating tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa lɛ Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Why does my plantain tree produce a very small bunch when there are many suckers growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be mli ni ŋmeii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Extra suckers growing around the main plantain stem act like extra mouths to feed, stealing food and water from the parent plant. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two strong stems ensures all nutrients go into forming a large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Plantain tso titri lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ko kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni ejuɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai akuu agbo ni tsii.

english: How can I tell if armyworms are attacking my maize field before my crops are ruined?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akpãtã?

english: Look for tiny holes in young leaves or sawdust-like waste inside the center fold of the maize plant. Catching Fall Armyworms early allows you to treat the field with appropriate sprays before they destroy the entire harvest.
ga: Taomɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai bibii amli loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ omɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ mra lɛ, ebaaha okɛ tsofa ni sa atsu ŋmɔ lɛ he nii dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: What causes black pods to appear on my cocoa trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ cacao tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, shaded conditions. Pruning tall shade trees to let in sunlight and removing infected pods early stops the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei kakadaji lɛ koni hulu la aba ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What can I do to protect my young crop seedlings from being destroyed by farm animals?
ga: Mɛni mafee koni mabu mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔ mli kooloi akafite amɛ?

english: Erecting low physical barriers using local materials like bamboo or palm fronds and clearing surrounding bush edges reduces cover for animals and keeps them away from tender seedlings.
ga: Gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni baa shi ni akɛ maŋ lɛ mli nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsei baa tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa dumɔwui bibii aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is struggling from water stress. Applying a balanced fertilizer like NPK or compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ekɛ nu he haomɔ miiwuu. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛbafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their blossoms before any fruit can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop blossoms when they experience extreme heat or dry soil conditions. Keeping soil moist with regular watering and adding mulch around the base keeps the plants cool so fruits can set.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛwoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishitoo ji ni eha tso lɛ mli ajɔ koni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ shi.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting underground even though the leaves look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when excess water collects in heavy soil without good drainage, allowing fungus to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain away safely.
