ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ni fa fe nine bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ adara. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works very well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space for the cassava to mature slowly over the rest of the year.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abele daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ haa ŋmei lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ fiofio. yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli

english: Why is it important to weed my farm field early rather than waiting until crop harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli mra lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e he hia nɛ waa mlɛ kɛ ya si be nɛ e maa su nɛ e maa kpa ngmɔ ní ɔmɛ.

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and vital nutrients from young crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main plants get all the energy they need to grow strong and produce maximum yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops immediately after the first heavy rain instead of before?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe dani eba lɛ?

english: Planting after a heavy rain guarantees that seeds sit in moist soil, which triggers quick germination and strong early root growth without the risk of seeds drying out in dry soil.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ekwɛ̃ oya ni eshishifãi lɛ hu aná hewalɛ. ni ekɛ ehe wooo oshara mli akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to save seeds from my harvested maize to plant for the next season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds, saving them for the next season usually results in weaker plants and much lower yields. It is best to purchase fresh, certified seeds each season for healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛtoɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate roots that easily burn and dry out under direct sunlight. Retaining larger shade trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a cool environment that protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or growing beans and cowpeas on the land helps put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo aduɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why am I advised not to plant maize on the exact same patch of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛɛɛ akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and soil diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with crops like cassava or legumes keeps the soil healthy and breaks pest life cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa. Ewajeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, and standing water suffocates them, allowing soft-rot fungi to destroy the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. ni nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays or neem extracts protects the new leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem spray loo nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaabu baai heei lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating holes inside the central leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing stem of young maize plants to feed. Checking your fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or wood ash inside the plant funnels can help suppress them.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi amli koni amɛye niyenii. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli mra Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tso mli sũ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛtsi amɛnaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Consistent watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni awoɔ daa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akɛ muji woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my plantain stem give small bunches when I let all the young shoots grow around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ daa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mihaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many young shoots grow around a plantain stem, they steal food, light, and water away from the main fruiting stem. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures the main stem gets enough energy to make large bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii dara yɛ tsei babaoo ahe lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops small and weak even when I irrigate them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwieɔ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight directly from your plants' root zones. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth stage leaves all the soil nourishment for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why does my seed yam rot in the ground instead of sprouting after I plant it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seed yams rot if they are planted in hot, dry soil before the rains fully arrive, or if the cut surface of the seed yam was not allowed to heal and dry before planting. Planting cured seed pieces into moist soil prevents soil germs from entering the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ kwraa. aloo kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ gbɛ ni sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ ahe ni afo lɛ atsa ni egbi dani adu. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni atsa lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote bulb lɛ mli.

english: Are there smaller harvesting machines available that a smallholder farmer like me can buy?
ga: Ani ŋmaakpamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko yɛ ni okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi baanyɛ ahe?

english: Yes, there are small motorized reapers and mini-harvesters designed for small-scale farms. They are much cheaper than big combine harvesters, easy to operate, and significantly cut down your harvesting time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ayɛ tsɔnei bibii ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii ni akɛkpaa nii kɛ tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii ni afee aha ŋmɔji bibii. Amɛjara waaa kwraa fe tsɔnei wuji ni akɛkpaa nibii, ni amɛkɛ nitsumɔ waaa, ni amɛbaa okpamɔ be lɛ shi kwraa.

english: Why can't I use a standard combine harvester for crops that need to be uprooted from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nibii ni ehe hiaa ni ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: Combine harvesters are designed to cut crops above the soil surface. Crops like groundnuts or root crops grow underground and require uprooting and sweeping, which standard combine machinery cannot do.
ga: Afee tsɔnei ni akɛkpaa nii ni akɛfataa he lɛ koni amɛfo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni ehe miihia ni ajie amɛ ni ajie amɛ. ni tsɔnei ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nyɛŋ afee.

english: Is it better for me to buy my own small harvesting machine or keep paying for harvesting services?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-kpamɔ tsɔne bibioo lɛ loo maya nɔ mawo ŋmaakpamɔ nitsumɔi lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: If you have the financial means, buying your own small harvester gives you control to harvest right when your crops mature, avoiding delays from commercial machine providers who may arrive late.
ga: Kɛji oyɛ shika Bo diɛŋtsɛ o-harvester bibioo lɛ hemɔ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ ŋmaa lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji onibii lɛ ekwɛ̃. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ sɛɛkuu ni jɛɔ jarayeli tsɔnei ahe nitsulɔi ni baanyɛ aba sɛɛ mli lɛ adɛŋ lɛ he.

english: Can a big combine harvester clear away plant roots and sweep the ground while harvesting my crops?
ga: Ani tsɔne agbo ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛshwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ekpaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: No, combine harvesters only cut standing crop plants at a set height. They do not uproot plants or sweep loose seeds off the ground, so any ground-level gathering must still be done manually.
ga: Dabi, tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ shwieɔ tsei ni damɔ shi yɛ he ko pɔtɛɛ pɛ. Amɛfolɔɔɔ tsei loo amɛshwieee dumɔwui ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ niji atsu shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni abua naa lɛ he nii lolo.

english: How does using a machine for harvesting save me time compared to harvesting by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii lɛ haa be baa shi kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ he?

english: Harvesting machines combine cutting, threshing, and cleaning into one fast operation, allowing you to harvest in hours what would normally take a manual labor team several days to complete.
ga: Nikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashwieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe saamɔ feɔ ekome yɛ oyaiyeli nitsumɔ kome mli. Ehaa okpaa nii yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi amli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ nitsulɔi akuu ko gbii babaoo dani amɛgbeɔ naa.

english: Why is it important for me to reduce the time it takes to harvest my mature crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafo be ni heɔ koni akɛkpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field for too long exposes them to unpredictable rain, bird pests, insect damage, and fungal rot, which quickly reduces seed quality and market value.
ga: Nibii ni eda ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha tsei nɛɛ aná nugbɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ahe sɛɛnamɔ kɛ jarayeli jara aba shi oya.

english: Why do manual harvesting methods require so many farm workers and take so long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ niji tsuɔ nii kɛkpaa nii lɛ biɔ ŋmɔ mli nitsulɔi babaoo ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Manual harvesting involves multiple separate physical tasks—cutting stalks, uprooting remaining plants, bundling, threshing, and sweeping spilled seeds—each requiring dedicated labor.
ga: Nine ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔi srɔtoi babaoo, tamɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni afolɔ, tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ashishifãi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni abua naa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashwieɔ shi, kɛ dumɔwui ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ ashwiemɔ. Nitsumɔ fɛɛ nitsumɔ biɔ nitsumɔ ni akɛ hetuu-kɛhamɔ haa.

english: Why do I still need to gather and sweep up seeds from the ground after harvesting certain crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lolo ni mabua dumɔwui anaa ni mafolɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi lɛ?

english: Certain crops drop their seed pods easily when handled. If the harvester cannot collect low-hanging or fallen pods, manual sweeping is needed to avoid leaving money behind on the soil.
ga: Tsei komɛi shwieɔ dumɔwui ashishi oya kɛji akɛ amɛtsu he nii. Kɛji akɛ nikpalɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi loo ni egbee shi lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ Niji atsu nii koni akashi shika yɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Will using harvesting machinery cause me to lose seeds on the ground during harvest?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ afite yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: Some seed loss can happen if the machine is moving too fast or if the crop shatters easily, but proper machine setup and timing your harvest before seeds become overly dry helps minimize losses.
ga: Dumɔwui komɛi baanyɛ afite kɛji tsɔne lɛ tee oya tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fite oya. Shi tsɔnei ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ agbi tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni nibii ni afiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know if my farm land is suitable for a machine to harvest my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha tsɔne ni akɛkpaa nii?

english: Machines require relatively flat ground free from tree stumps, large rocks, and deep ridges. Cleared fields allow harvesters to move smoothly without damaging cutting blades.
ga: He ko ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ŋmeii, tɛi wuji, kɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ bɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsɔne lɛ. He ni agbele lɛ haa nikpamɔ tsɔne lɛ yaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee ŋmɔji ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops keep getting sick every season even when I clear the land well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Reusing seeds or planting materials from your previous harvest can carry hidden diseases into the new season, repeatedly transferring and recycling the same sickness in your soil.
ga: Dumɔwui loo nibii ni adu kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba be hee lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ helai kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛbaatsu nii shii abɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to save seeds from my current harvest to plant next year?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu afi ni baa lɛ?

english: If your current crop had any disease, saving those seeds will pass the disease directly to your new farm, leading to sick plants and poor yields again.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ yɛ hela ko Nakai dumɔwui lɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ lɛ baaha hela lɛ aya oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei hela mɔ amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I use the healthy-looking crop cuttings from a field that had diseased plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ tsei ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, even parts of a crop that look healthy can carry the disease internally, so planting them will still spread sickness to your next farm.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã emli. No hewɔ lɛ, nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baagbɛ hela ashwã oŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lolo.

english: Why do my crop yields keep getting smaller every year I reuse my own planting materials?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ faaa daa afi ni mikɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ midumɔ nibii tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Continually replanting old stock accumulates and multiplies diseases over time, causing plants to grow weaker and produce less food each season.
ga: Tsei momoi ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ baabua amɛhe naa ni ebaaha helai ayibɔ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ niyenii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: What actually causes disease to spread from one year's crop to the next?
ga: Mɛni haa hela gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni eye afi kome lɛ amli kɛyaa ekroko mli?

english: Disease spreads from season to season mainly through infected seeds and planting stock that carry pathogens from the old farm into the new one.
ga: Hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ be kome mli kɛyaa be kroko mli titri kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui kɛ dumɔwui ni hiɛ hela lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji momo amli kɛyaa ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the best thing I can do before the next planting season to stop crop diseases on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mafee dani ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba koni makpa tsei ahelai ni baa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Stop reusing your old seeds and planting materials, and replace them entirely with clean, disease-free materials for the new season.
ga: Kpaa odumɔwui momo kɛ nibii ni okɛduɔ nii lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ ekoŋŋ. ni akɛ nibii ni he tse ni hela bɛ mli lɛ ato najiaŋ kɛha be hee lɛ.

english: Why does planting fresh seeds prevent disease better than treating sick plants later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui heei ni aduɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ helai atsĩmɔ mli fe helai ni abaatsa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Starting with disease-free seeds prevents infection from the very start, whereas trying to cure a crop planted with diseased seed is difficult, costly, and often unsuccessful.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni hela bɛ mli lɛ je shishi lɛ, ebaatsi hela ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ naa kɛjɛ shishijee. Yɛ be mli ni mɔdɛŋ ni abɔɔ koni ahere tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahere lɛ wa lɛ, Shika babaoo yɛ. ni bei pii lɛ eyeee omanye

english: Where should I go to get clean seeds that will not bring disease to my farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mahe dumɔwui ni he tse ni kɛ hela baaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ?

english: You should visit your local district agriculture office to buy certified seeds and planting materials that are tested and guaranteed free of diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ oya kpokpaa nɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oyahe dumɔwui kɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni ana nɔmimaa akɛ hela bɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do agriculture officers encourage me to buy new seeds instead of using my own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mɛi hewalɛ koni amɛhe dumɔwui heei moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛdumɔwui baatsu nii lɛ?

english: Buying fresh seeds from the agriculture office ensures you break the cycle of disease, leading to healthy plants and a much bigger harvest that covers the cost of the seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui heei ni ooohe kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ haa onyɛɔ ofoɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa babaoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ ahe nyɔmɔwoo lɛ baa.

english: How are seeds from the agriculture office different from the ones I save from my harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Seeds from the agriculture office are specially produced under clean conditions to be free of disease and are selected to give strong growth and higher yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli tse ni helai bɛ mli lɛ amli krɛdɛɛ, ni ahalaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa leaves curl and turn yellow when they get too much direct sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them protects the tender cocoa plants while they grow.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ babaoo shɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ebuɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves and stunted growth usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps the leaves grow green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water and lacks proper drainage, especially during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the light and keeps them off the hot ground where diseases can easily spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ la lɛ hiɛ, ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and dense shade. Pruning surplus tree branches and removing infected pods improves airflow and reduces humidity, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over easily before the fruit bunches are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and carry heavy bunches, making them vulnerable to strong winds. Supporting the main stem with wooden props or bamboo poles prevents the trees from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ loo eshishijee.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize harvest produce smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid maize lose their vigor in the second generation, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields. Buying certified hybrid seeds each season guarantees strong, high-yielding crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baafite hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: How can I keep my soil moist during the dry season so my vegetables do not dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni mi-aduawai lɛ akagbi?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops sunlight from evaporating soil moisture and keeps the crop roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni ekpa hulu la ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller harvests even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, soil nutrients, and space. Clearing weeds early in the crop's growth period ensures your plants get all the nourishment they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu. Shikpɔŋ kɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be mli lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and improves the growth of neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛjieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient it needs to grow green and strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the soil too waterlogged for the roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni ehe wa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amu.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot and dry, or if the plant does not get steady water. It can also happen if you give the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes it focus on growing big green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha otsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves stay wide open instead of forming a tight, hard ball in the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ miigbele amɛhe waa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee bɔɔlu ni mli wa ni mli wa yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads stay soft and loose if the weather is too hot, if they do not get enough direct sunlight, or if watering is uneven. Cabbages need steady water, plenty of sun, and cooler temperatures to force their inner leaves to wrap tightly into a head.
ga: Kaaba yitsei lɛ baafee blɛoo ni amɛbaagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Aloo kɛji akɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ daa lɛ, Cabbage he miihia nu daa. Hulu la lɛ kpɛɔ kɛtsɔɔ mli. kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ koni enyɛ emli baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbɔle bulb lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, twisted, and bent instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji kukuji, ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft earth to push down easily as they grow. If the soil is hard, clay-heavy, or full of stones, the tuber cannot expand downwards smoothly and ends up bent or stunted, which is why making soft, high mounds or ridges helps them grow long.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes koni amɛnyɛ amɛtsi amɛhe oya beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni tsii loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Tubers nyɛɛɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya shi mlɛo ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe. Enɛ hewɔ ni gɔji loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Maize feeds heavily on the soil and pulls out nutrients, leaving the land tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts actually fix nitrogen from the air back into the soil through their roots, restoring natural fertility for your next crop without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii babaoo ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the tree before they are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: This blackening is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, wet conditions during the rainy season. Pruning extra branches to let in air and sunlight, and picking off infected pods early, helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Afolɔ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from young shoots, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and stops the plant from becoming stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔmɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds around my crops when the plants are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, weak roots and need every drop of water, light, and soil nutrients they can get. Weeds grow much faster and will steal these vital resources from your young plants, choking them before they have a chance to grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ. Ni nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná lɛ fɛɛ he miihia amɛ. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa. ni ebaaju nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli. ni otsi amɛnaa dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so the roots don't go bad under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akagbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 8 and 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging up one root near the stem to see if it has developed thick, starchy flesh.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ ŋmei lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ shishifã kome ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni ona kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the broad leaves on my plantain suckers splitting up into thin strips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi banana tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ mli gbalaa kɛmiiya fãi bibii amli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves naturally split along their veins when strong winds blow against them, which stops the big leaves from snapping the whole stem. As long as the leaves remain green and healthy, this splitting is completely normal and helps the plant withstand windy days.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ baagbala amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni baa agboi lɛ akagbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baahi shi akɛ eŋɔli ni amɛhe yɔɔ hewalɛ Nɛkɛ mligbalamɔ nɛɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enyɛɔ edamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ gbii lɛ anaa.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava sticks in the farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting cassava sticks about one meter apart gives the roots enough room under the soil to expand into big tubers without competing with neighboring plants for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ abɔi akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Is it better to plant my yam tubers on flat ground or on raised mounds?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu sweet potato ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ loo yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ?

english: Planting yams on raised mounds softens the soil, allowing the tubers to grow deep and straight while preventing rain water from waterlogging the roots and causing rot.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo. Ehaa yitso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni efeɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, nugbɔ nu ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ akafee ekome yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: What causes black spots on my cocoa pods, and how can I stop them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Black spots are caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shady conditions. Pruning shade trees to let in sunlight and removing infected pods quickly stops it from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ebaakpa gbɛfaŋnɔ oya.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the heart of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which feed on young maize leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract inside the whorl of the leaf protects your crop.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ yi lɛ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the plant sap. Spraying with organic insecticidal soap keeps these insects away and lets the leaves grow flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaha kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellow maize leaves are a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and crop strength.
ga: Abɛi baa ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ su eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Regular, consistent watering at the base of the plant helps flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa, daa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why does my plantain bunch stay small and dry up before it ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛgbi dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: Small, dry bunches happen when the plantain lacks water during flowering or has damaged roots from pests. Keeping mulch around the base holds soil moisture to help the bunch swell.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoi bibii ni egbi lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ plantains lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ loo amɛshishifãi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ. Mulch ni ebɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli koni eye ebua ŋmɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: How do I know the exact time my sweet potatoes are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up, around 3 to 4 months after planting. Digging up one test mound will show if the tubers are large enough.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔi gbimɔ, aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kaa gɔŋ ko ni akumɔ lɛ baatsɔɔ kɛji yitso lɛ da bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cover my farm soil with dry leaves instead of burning them after clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter acts like a protective blanket. It stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, prevents heavy rains from washing away topsoil, and slowly breaks down into natural food for your crops.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efite fiofio ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha onibii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi?

english: Legumes like beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize, helping it grow stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa o-corn lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛkɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and gives specific pests and crop diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai komɛi náa shia ni amɛfɔɔ daa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I remove all the big trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and intense heat. Leaving some tall shade trees provides shelter, keeps the air humid, and protects the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Haa hulutsoo kɛha wɔɔhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen in the soil or that too much standing water around the roots is preventing the plant from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo nu yɛ lolo ni ebɔle tso lɛ he Shishifãi babaoo tsɔ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience extreme stress, such as very high temperatures, inconsistent watering, or a sudden lack of essential plant nutrients.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ trukaa

english: Why do I need to leave a specific amount of space between my crop plants instead of scattering them closely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, soil water, and food, which leaves all of them weak and results in much smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu amɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why do I need to cut cassava stems into specific lengths with several nodes before burying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛyashɛ he ko ni nodes babaoo yɔɔ mli dani madu amɛ lɛ?

english: Each node on a cassava stem contains dormant buds. You need enough nodes underground to sprout strong roots and enough nodes above ground to shoot leaves for proper growth.
ga: Node fɛɛ node ni yɔɔ cassava tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni ehiɛ edɔ. Ohe miihia ni oná shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai akwɛ̃ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do small worms burrow into the very center leaves of my maize plants during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: These are typically Fall Armyworms, which prefer to hide and feed inside the soft, tender inner leaves (the funnel) where they are protected from heat and weather while eating the plant's newest growth.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ mligbɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli (channels) he ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ shweremɔ hee lɛ.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it; if applied to dry soil, the concentrated chemicals can sit around the roots and burn them as temperatures rise.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni amɛshã be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How many years will it take for my new coconut trees to start producing fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit in 3 to 4 years, while the traditional tall varieties take about 6 to 8 years. Proper watering and good manure can help them fruit sooner.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ heɔ afii 6 kɛyashi 8. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii oya.

english: Can coconut trees grow well on high hilly land, or do they only grow near the beach?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni gɔji yɔɔ lɛ loo ŋshɔnaa pɛ akwɛɔ amɛ?

english: While coconuts are famous along the beach, they can grow very well on inland high ground as long as the soil is deep, drains water easily, and receives plenty of rainfall and sunshine.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii ehe gbɛi yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa moŋ, Shi ebaanyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ Easy drainage ni onine ashɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ

english: Which coconut variety is best for me if I want to harvest early and sell sweet coconut water?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mi kɛji miisumɔ ni makpa oya ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei nu ni ŋɔɔ?

english: Dwarf coconut varieties are best for fresh water sales because they produce sweet water early in 3 to 4 years and stay short, making the fruits much easier and safer to harvest.
ga: Dwarf coconut henɔi lɛ ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha nu kpakpa mli jarayeli ejaakɛ amɛhaa ŋmeii baa oya yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni anáaa amɛ fioo. Enɛ haa aduawai akpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni ehiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my young coconut fruits dropping off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokooi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Small coconuts usually drop early because the tree lacks water or key nutrients like potassium, or during periods of sudden heat. Giving the tree extra water and compost during dry spells helps prevent fruit drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ejaakɛ nu loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ tso lɛ mli, loo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akagbee shi.

english: What is making the leaves of my young coconut seedlings turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi ŋmei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the plant lacks nutrients like nitrogen or potassium, or that water is sitting around the roots without draining. Adding well-rotted animal manure usually fixes this.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. Aloo nu ko ebɔle he. shishifãi ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛfataa he lɛ saa naagba nɛɛ he.

english: How can I protect my young coconut trees from beetles that bore big holes into the stems?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmei tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ bulɛi wuji kɛboteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ahe?

english: Rhinoceros beetles are attracted to rotting wood and compost piles near farms. Keeping the surroundings clean of decaying palm stumps and placing sand or wood ash in the leaf bases discourages beetles from attacking.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔji lɛ gbalaa rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ aha shihilɛhe lɛ he tse kɛjɛ tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe, ni akɛ ŋã loo tso sũ fata baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua amɛ.

english: Do my coconut trees need extra water during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Ani nu babaoo he miihia mi ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ harmattan be ni nu lɛ egbi lɛ mli?

english: Yes, young coconut trees need regular watering during dry spells to keep growing. Even mature trees yield much heavier fruits with more milk if they get adequate water during dry periods.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni afɔ akokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara. Tsei ni eda lɛ po woɔ yibii ni tsii babaoo kɛ nu babaoo kɛji amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut seedlings when planting them on my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo ŋmei dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Space tall coconut trees about 8 to 9 meters apart, and dwarf trees about 6 to 7 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight and root space to grow full branches.
ga: Space ŋmei tsei ni kɛlɛ aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 9 kɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 6 kɛyashi 7. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa hulu la kɛ shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛgbala eniji lɛ amli kwraa.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my coconut trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can grow food crops like cassava, maize, or legumes between young coconut trees for the first 3 to 4 years. This helps you earn income from the land while waiting for the coconuts to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. ŋmei tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ mli, ni enɛ haa onáa shika kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I use water from a tilapia pond to water my coconut trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ tilapia nubu lɛ mli lɛ aha mi ŋmei tsei lɛ nu?

english: Yes, fish pond water is excellent for crops. The waste from tilapia naturally enriches the water with organic nitrogen and phosphorus, acting as a rich natural liquid fertilizer for your coconut trees.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, loo ŋshɔ mli nu lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. Tilapia jwɛi lɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ji nitrogen kɛ phosphorus fataa nu lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nu ni fa babaoo kɛha o-coconut tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for vegetative growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away or clog the roots with water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer like Urea helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii loo eha shishifãi lɛ tsi amɛhe kɛya. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ni yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my land next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Groundnuts are legumes, which naturally fix nitrogen back into the soil, making the land richer and healthier for future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ babaoo. Peanuts ji ŋmãa ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my crop seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil receives steady rain for several days in a row so that moisture penetrates deep into the ground, rather than planting after the very first isolated rainfall, which can dry out and kill new seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Mohu ɔ, du ngɛ kekleekle nugbɔ nɛ nɛ ngɛ he ko ɔ se. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Removing heavily infected plants and spraying with neem oil or approved pesticides can stop the spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ashwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves develop dark brown spots and dry up before the fruit matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ anɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani yibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by a airborne fungal disease known as Black Sigatoka, which thrives in warm, humid weather. Pruning away damaged leaves and ensuring good spacing between plants improves airflow and reduces humidity around the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Sigatoka, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are tiny insects making holes in my cowpea pods while they are still growing on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii feɔ bu yɛ mi-cowpea ŋmeii lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea pods attract pod borers and sap-sucking bugs during the flowering and podding stages. Spraying organic or recommended treatments right when the plant starts flowering prevents these insects from laying eggs and ruining the seeds.
ga: Bush bean pods lɛ gbalaa pod borers kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ pod be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni tsei lɛ je fɔfɔi lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akawo ŋmeii ni amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil for too long, starving the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomatoes start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from stress, such as extremely high heat, prolonged dry soil, or lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulching around the roots helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa waa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why is my yam crop growing long green vines with many leaves, but the tuber underground stays very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ wain tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: Giving yams too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its energy into growing top leaves instead of expanding the tuber below. Yams need balanced feeding and soft, uncompacted soil to build big tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen wo ŋmeii amli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ajieee nɔ ko awo mli lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Staking keeps tomato leaves and fruit off the wet soil, which prevents soil-borne fungal diseases, protects the fruit from rotting, and gives the plant better access to sunlight for bigger harvests.
ga: Staking baatsi tomato baai kɛ aduawai anaa koni amɛkashwɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa. Ebuɔ aduawai ahe koni amɛkafite. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a major food for plants. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow strong cobs.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abele bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas have tiny helpers in their roots that catch nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When the plant finishes growing, that stored food remains in the soil to help the next crop grow better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ fioo. yɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbe ekwɛmɔ naa Nakai niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same patch of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls a lot of food out of the ground. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot completely empties the soil of nutrients and lets soil diseases build up, leading to smaller yields each year.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afeɔ lɛ fioo daa afi.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and cool air they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Should I start planting my seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains are regular. The first rain is often followed by a long dry stretch, which can dry out your newly sprouted seeds and destroy your crop before it takes root.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ agbi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani amɛwo shishifãi.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, producing small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe tsɔi ni amɛgbɔjɔ. ni kɛ cob bibioo loo efolo baa

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct heat. It keeps the moisture in the ground for a longer time and prevents weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wood off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atswa mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to reach up to catch direct sunlight so they can feed the tuber growing underground. Keeping the leaves off the damp ground also prevents them from rotting and spreading diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa amɛgboi ni helai akagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before growing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather is extremely hot or when the water in the soil goes up and down drastically. Keeping the watering consistent and providing light shade helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ?

english: Ragged holes inside the center funnel of young maize are usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the leaves during the day, so checking early in the morning helps you spot them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ amɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to firmly press down the soil around my fresh nursery beds when preparing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mamɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ahe lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ beni miisaa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pressing down the soil creates a stable structure that prevents erosion and holds the nursery bed together, making sure young roots have a secure base to establish themselves.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni anyɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa, ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli saatso lɛ feɔ ekome. Enɛ baaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdamɔ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I hurry through the land preparation process before putting my seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ofeee oya ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Soil and organic matter need time to settle and react properly; rushing land preparation can leave dry air pockets or hard clumps that stop seeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia be dani amɛhi shi ni amɛfee nɔ ko jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he oya lɛ baanyɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni egbi loo ŋmeii ni wa ni tsiɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ aba.

english: Why is it recommended to leave my prepared soil beds to sit for a few days before I begin planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi dani aje dumɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Letting prepared soil rest allows moisture to spread evenly throughout the bed and gives the earth time to stabilize so fragile young roots do not get stressed.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa saatso lɛ nɔ fɛɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaa shi shiŋŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ akahao.

english: Why should I pour water heavily on my nursery earth right after I finish setting it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafɔse nu babaoo yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Watering immediately after soil setup activates the earth by breaking up dry dirt particles and providing the deep moisture needed to start the softening process.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ebɔle shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ kɛtsɔ muji ni egbi lɛ mligbalamɔ nɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli kwɔ ni he hiaa koni akɛje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: How long does it usually take for dry, hard soil to become soft after I soak it with water?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wa lɛ feɔ blɛoo beni mikɛwo nu mli sɛɛ?

english: It generally takes about three days for deep water to fully penetrate and break down tough earth, turning hard clods into soft, loose soil ready for roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ aaafee gbii etɛ dani nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni wa lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni asaa he kɛha shishifãi.

english: Can heavy watering really soften land that has become too hard and packed down?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, soaking hard ground causes the tightly packed soil particles to absorb moisture and expand, which relaxes and loosens the earth over a few days.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efee ais lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli.

english: Is it better to soak my prepared bed deeply once or just sprinkle a little water on the surface every few hours?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ saatso ni asaa he lɛ awo nu mli jogbaŋŋ shikome loo oookɛ nu fioo ko afɔ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ nɔ kɛkɛ? ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ komɛi?

english: A deep soak allows water to travel far beneath the surface, loosening the lower soil layers over time rather than just wetting the top dry crust.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli shɔŋŋ lɛ haa nu lɛ yaa shishi shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli shwieɔ shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha ŋshɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi lɛ, ŋshɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: What does it mean when extension officers say my seedling's roots need to 'make contact' with the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ kɛ́ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ esa akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ‘ata’ shikpɔŋ lɛ he?

english: Making contact means the plant's fine feeder roots are directly touching moist, soft earth without empty spaces, allowing the crop to drink water and absorb nutrients right away.
ga: Nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nuɔ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my nursery bed soil is soft enough for delicate crop roots to spread out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi-nsɛri lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbɛ ashwã?

english: After a few days of watering, the top soil will feel crumbly and open when touched, showing that the ground has loosened enough for roots to penetrate easily.
ga: Yɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni akɛ nu fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baanu he akɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebaagbele kɛha mɔ ni taa he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi baanyɛ abote mli mlɛo.

english: Why do my transplanted seedlings wither if the surrounding ground is too hard when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ gboɔ kɛji akɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli wa tsɔ beni midu lɛ?

english: Hard ground acts like a wall, preventing tiny crop roots from growing outward to reach moisture, which leaves the plant stressed and unable to feed itself.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo. Etsiɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Eda kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ koni enine ashɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii amɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do people tell me to plant plantains on the same land where I am planting my new cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ midu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ kookoo tsei heei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide temporary shade, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and moist until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Ha cacao tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant the seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin stems and smaller overall yields compared to properly spaced crops.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ faaa kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni sa lɛ ahe.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that excessive water in the soil is drowning the roots and stopping them from feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛkpaa niyenii yeli.

english: Why does my cassava grow huge foliage above the ground but only tiny tubers beneath the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its energy into growing big leaves instead of tubers when the soil has too much nitrogen manure but lacks potassium, which is the specific food crops need to build underground roots.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii krɛdɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ cacao ŋmeii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by hot, dry weather, when they lack adequate soil nutrients, or when tiny pests like mirids bite the delicate blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni nu egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ myrids lɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my ripening tomatoes crack and split open while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi ni miikwɛ lɛ miigba ni amɛmiijara be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when a sudden heavy rain follows a long dry period. The plant drinks up water quickly, making the inside of the fruit expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tsei nuɔ nu oya. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to apply chemical fertilizer when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need moisture to dissolve so plant roots can safely absorb them. Placing dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and damage the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Why am I seeing tiny ragged holes and what looks like sawdust in the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ, ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf funnel of the maize plant to eat fresh leaves and leaves behind its waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ baai amli koni amɛye baai heei ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does a purple-flowered weed keep growing right next to my maize plants and causing them to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: That weed is called Striga (or witchweed). Its roots attach directly to the maize roots underneath the soil to steal water and food, which stunts the growth of the maize.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi lɛ akɛ Striga (loo abɛi jwɛi). Eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I trim off the lowest leaves of my pepper plants that touch the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Removing bottom leaves prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from splashing onto the plant during heavy rains and improves air circulation around the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when the plants grow too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil like nitrogen. Yellow leaves mean the plants are starving because there are too many roots competing in one small space.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen he akaŋ. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi babaoo yɛ ni miitswa akaŋ kɛha he bibioo kome.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants roll up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling in cassava is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading cassava mosaic virus, or by extreme heat and lack of water. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss and protect itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ cassava hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why does planting cowpea or groundnut on my land make my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have small bumps on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer for whichever crop you plant there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato kɛji edɔ waa lɛ?

english: When daytime temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes sticky or dry and cannot fertilize the flowers. The plant drops the unfertilized flowers to save its energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ Tomato pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbiɔ. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔii awo fɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔfɔi bɛ mli lɛ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam crop produce small tubers if I do not clear weeds early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ hiɛ bulbs bibii kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwieee nɔ oya?

english: Yam tubers form in the soil by storing energy made by the vines above ground. If weeds shade the vines or steal water and soil nutrients early on, the yam vine cannot produce enough energy to feed a large tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ wain tsei amli ni amɛtoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji jwɛi ha wain tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ loo amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra lɛ, Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ajie hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji lɛ aye abua.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots rot and the whole plant die when water stands on my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe just like humans do. When water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing them to drown and rot, which kills the whole plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tsei shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni haa efoɔ nu mli ni egboɔ. ni haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gboɔ lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees burn and dry up when there are no bigger trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji bɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive and soft. Strong direct sunshine dries them out faster than their young roots can pull water from the soil, causing the leaves to burn and drop off.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ he waa ni amɛhe yɛ blɛoo. Hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha amɛgbi oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why does stored maize start to produce heat and spoil inside the sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ jeɔ shishi edɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: If maize grains are bagged before they are fully dry, the remaining moisture allows tiny insects and fungi to breathe and multiply fast. Their breathing produces heat and moisture, causing the grain to rot.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmãa wo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni eshwɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii akabote mli. Ebaanyɛ emu ni efɔ oya Mumɔ haa dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo baa. haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ

english: Why should I apply fertilizer to my crops when the soil is wet instead of when it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi lɛ?

english: Crops cannot eat dry fertilizer granules directly with their roots. The fertilizer must first dissolve in soil moisture so the root hairs can drink it up along with the water.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi. Esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu kɛfata nu lɛ he.

english: Why do plantain suckers taken from diseased farms grow slowly and produce small bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni helai yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛfeɔ kui bibii lɛ?

english: Diseased suckers carry hidden pests like microscopic worms (nematodes) or viruses inside their roots and stems. Planting them moves the infection to your new field, preventing the plant from building strong roots.
ga: Suckers ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ hiɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii bibii (nematodes) loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ shishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Amɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha hela lɛ afã kɛya he hee ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee shishifãi ni wa.
