english: Is using a tractor to plow the top of my land enough before planting pawpaw?
ga: Ani akɛ trakta baatsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu paw paws lɛ fa bɔ ni sa?

english: No, just plowing the surface layer with a tractor is not enough for pawpaws. Pawpaw trees need deep soil preparation so their roots can grow down deep into the earth; surface-only tilling leaves the ground underneath too hard for proper root growth.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋshɔ lɛ ni akɛ trakta baatsu nii kɛkɛ lɛ faaa kɛha tsitsii. Pawpaw tsei lɛ he miihia ni asaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ ni oootsu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pawpaw trees not growing well even though I plowed my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi papaya tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Namɔ huɔ ŋmɔji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plowing only the soil surface does not loosen the deeper ground where crop roots need to spread. If the lower soil is hard, your pawpaw cannot establish deep roots to feed properly, leading to poor plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haaa hei ni mli kwɔ ni ehe hiaa ni tsei shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ afee mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ wa Onaji nyɛŋ afee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ koni amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei lɛ adalɛ ni ehiii.

english: How does proper land preparation help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper land preparation loosens the soil deeply, allowing roots to spread easily, absorb nutrients, and create a strong foundation that supports healthy plant growth throughout the season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo. shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ shishitoo ni wa ni fiɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni daraa yɛ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: What is the best way to prepare my soil before putting pawpaw seedlings in the ground?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ papaya dumɔwui?

english: Beyond clearing and tilling the surface, you need to loosen the soil deeply by digging proper planting holes. This ensures the taproot can penetrate deep into the earth rather than staying trapped near the surface.
ga: Kɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oootsu he nii lɛ he lɛ, Ehe miihia ni Ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lolo kɛtsɔ dumɔ bu ni sa ni oootsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ nyɛɔ eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsi ehe kɛjɛ nu lɛ hiɛ lɛ he

english: Why does shallow surface tilling cause problems for long-term tree crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛ naagbai ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Shallow tilling only softens the top few inches of soil. Tree crops need deep root systems, and if they hit hard soil just below the surface, their growth becomes stunted and fragile.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ inchi fioo pɛ afee blɛoo. Tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ he miihia shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. ni kɛji etswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, Dalɛ baafee nɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why does a strong wind keep knocking down my pawpaw trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ yaa nɔ etswaa mi-pawpaw tso lɛ shi lɛ?

english: When pawpaw land is only prepared on the surface, the roots stay shallow instead of going deep into the earth. Without deep roots to anchor the tree, a strong wind can easily push the entire plant over.
ga: Beni asaa pawpaw shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ mli ekwɔɔɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi ni mli kwɔ bɛ ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ tso lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ akumɔ tsei muu fɛɛ oya.

english: How can I protect my crops from falling over during heavy wind storms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa waa mli?

english: The best protection against wind is deep soil preparation before planting. Deeply loosened soil allows roots to anchor firmly into the ground, acting like sturdy pegs that keep the plant standing during high winds.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he ji shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni asaa he dani aduɔ nii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli etse waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni wa ni yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edamɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: What causes fruit trees like pawpaws to have weak root anchorage?
ga: Mɛni haa aduawai tsei tamɔ paw paws lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kpaa gbee?

english: Weak root anchorage happens when the soil beneath the surface is too hard for roots to penetrate. This usually occurs when farmers rely only on light surface tilling before planting.
ga: Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ abote mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ okwaafoi kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ anɔ dani amɛduɔ nii.

english: Can the way I prepare my land affect how well my crops survive bad weather?
ga: Ani bɔ ni masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mihaa lɛ baaná kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli?

english: Yes, thorough and deep soil preparation gives plants deep, strong roots that make them resilient against harsh winds and heavy storms, whereas poorly prepared land leaves plants vulnerable to falling.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ooosaa jogbaŋŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ ahum ni naa wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni asaaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ woɔ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite.

english: Why do some pawpaw farms suffer heavy wind damage while neighboring farms stay upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fiteɔ paw paw ŋmɔji komɛi yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Farms where soil was properly prepared deep down allow trees to form deep, solid root systems that withstand wind, while farms with only surface-tilled soil end up with shallow roots that easily get uprooted.
ga: Okwaafoi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli woɔ wu jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni baanyɛ adamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔji ni shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ pɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni ajieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi amli oya.

english: Why are so many of my fellow farmers in Ghana planting 'highway' corn these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minanemɛi okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miidu ‘highway’ ŋmãa yɛ nɛkɛ gbii nɛɛ amli lɛ?

english: Highway' corn is a popular local name for improved hybrid maize varieties. Farmers are switching to it because it grows strong, adapts well, and produces significantly more bags of corn than older traditional varieties.
ga: Highway’ ŋmãa ji maŋ lɛ mli gbɛi ni ehe gbɛi waa kɛha ŋmãa srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Okwaafoi miitsake kɛmiiya nɛkɛ ŋmãa nɛɛ nɔ ejaakɛ edaa waa, ekɛ ehe woɔ shihilɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmãa kotokui babaoo kwraa fe blema ŋmãa henɔi ni etsɛ waa lɛ.

english: What is the difference between traditional local corn seeds and these new improved seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ akutsoŋbii akusum mli ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ nɛɛ ateŋ?

english: Traditional seeds come from single local crop lines, whereas new improved varieties like hybrids are created by combining two different strong plant types, resulting in crops that yield much higher harvests.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui lɛ jɛ maŋ lɛ mli tso henɔ kome mli. Yɛ be mli ni afeɔ tsei srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ tsei ni akɛfee tsofai sɔrɔtoi, kɛtsɔ tsei henɔi enyɔ ni wa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Are hybrid corn varieties actually proven to work well for farmers here in Ghana?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ eha okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ?

english: Yes, many farmers across Ghana bear witness to the success of hybrid corn, experiencing much stronger plant growth and harvest yields compared to traditional seeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana fɛɛ lɛ miiye omanye ni ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ omanye lɛ he odase. Amɛnaa tsei adalɛ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni mli wa waa kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ahe.

english: What does it mean when an extension officer tells me a corn seed is a 'hybrid'?
ga: Kɛji extension nitsulɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ji ‘hybrid’ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: A hybrid corn seed is created by taking two different types of corn plants and combining them so that their offspring inherits the best qualities of both parents.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa koni seshibii lɛ aná fɔlɔi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ asui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the offspring of two combined crop varieties grow stronger than their original parents?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli bii lɛ daraa waa fe shishijee fɔlɔi lɛ?

english: When you cross two distinct plant varieties, the resulting seed gets a natural boost in vigor, making the new plant tougher, healthier, and stronger than either of the two parent plants alone.
ga: Beni ofɔɔ tsei srɔtoi enyɔ. Dumɔwui ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baaya hiɛ yɛ hewalɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tso hee lɛ mli waa, ehiɛɔ hewalɛ, ni eyɛ hewalɛ fe fɔlɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: How does combining two different types of corn actually work to improve the seed?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmãa henɔi enyɔ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Combining two different corn varieties merges their unique strengths into one seed, creating a new generation of corn that grows better and resists environmental stresses more effectively.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa henɔi srɔtoi enyɔ fata he lɛ, ehaa amɛhewalɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto lɛ feɔ ŋmãa kome. Enɛ haa ŋmãa yinɔ hee ko ni daa jogbaŋŋ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ shihilɛ mli haomɔi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: How do hybrid corn seeds get the strength to produce such big crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa wuji tamɔ nɛkɛ?

english: The strength of hybrid corn comes from genetic diversity. Mixing two different parent plants creates offspring with enhanced growth traits and higher productivity.
ga: Nɔ ni fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ jɛɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ srɔto ha lɛ mli. Fɔlɔ tsei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ ni afoɔ mli lɛ haa seshibii ni yɔɔ dalɛ sui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Can changing the type of corn seed I plant really help me harvest up to 10 bags of maize?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ henɔ ni mitsakeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi diɛŋtsɛ ni makpa ŋmãa kotokui 10?

english: Yes, high-yielding hybrid varieties are specifically bred for heavy production, and under good conditions, farmers can harvest around 10 bags of corn from their plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɔseɔ ŋmeii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha nibii ni tsii ni afeɔ lɛ. ni yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli lɛ Okwaafoi lɛ nyɛ amɛkpa ŋmãa aaafee kotokui 10 kɛjɛ amɛŋmɔji amli.

english: Why does 'highway' corn yield so many more bags than my traditional local corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ‘gbɛjegbɛ nɔ’ ŋmãa lɛ woɔ baagi babaoo fe mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ?

english: Highway' corn is a hybrid that benefits from combined parent traits, allowing each plant to grow larger, produce fuller cobs, and yield far more bags per acre than local seeds.
ga: Highway’ ŋmãa ji ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni náa fɔlɔi asui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ he sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa. Ha cob ni eyi obɔ babaoo ni ofee kotokui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli fe maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui.

english: If I want a stronger crop that produces a higher harvest this season, should I buy hybrid seeds?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miitao ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli hu? Ani esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he?

english: Yes, choosing hybrid seeds is one of the most effective ways to boost your harvest because the plants grow stronger than traditional varieties and yield many more bags of corn.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ni ooohala lɛ ji gbɛi ni mɔɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni oootsɔ nɔ oha okpamɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ ateŋ ekome. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ waa fe shishijee tso lɛ, ni amɛbaawo ŋmãa kotokui babaoo.

english: Why is it becoming so hard for me to find fresh wild grass for my animals during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa mi akɛ mana koo mli jwɛi hee maha mikooloi lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, wild grass stops growing and dries up quickly due to lack of rainfall. Relying only on wild grass is risky, which is why planting drought-resistant fodder crops like elephant grass or saving dried crop residues helps keep your animals fed year-round.
ga: yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni egbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Koo mli jwɛi pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yɛ oshara. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi ni ooodu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ lɛ ni oookɛto lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni oha okooloi lɛ aná niyenii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Is it okay for me to cut fresh grass on someone else's bush land to feed my livestock?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ mafo sũ yɛ mɔ kroko ŋmɔ mli koni mikɛha mikooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: You should always ask for permission from the land owner first. Cutting grass or harvesting vegetation on another person's farm without permission can cause serious land disputes, misunderstandings, and community conflicts.
ga: Bi shikpɔŋtsɛ lɛ gbɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ mɔ kroko ŋmɔ mli tsei ni afo loo akpa ni ahaaa lɛ gbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shikpɔŋ he béi ni mli wa aba. shishinumɔ ni ejaaa kɛ béi ni yɔɔ akutso lɛ mli

english: Can I grow my own grass pasture on a small plot instead of walking far to look for wild grass?
ga: Dumɔ bo diɛŋtsɛ ojwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shɔŋŋ koni oyatao koo mli jwɛi komɛi?

english: Yes, planting dedicated fodder crops like Napier grass or Stylosanthes on your own land saves you time and guarantees a safe, reliable food source for your animals without trespassing on anyone else's property.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛi tamɔ Napier jwɛi loo Stylosanthes ni ooodu yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baaha okɛ be akafite ni ebaaha oná niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha okooloi lɛ ni okɛ ohe wooo mɛi krokomɛi anibii amli.

english: Why do land owners get angry when I clear wild grass near their crop boundaries?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi lɛ amli fu beni mijie koo mli jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Land owners protect grass and plants near their farm borders because wild vegetation helps prevent soil erosion, keeps moisture in the soil, and marks property boundaries. They may also be saving that grass for their own use.
ga: Shikpɔŋtsɛmɛi buɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛŋmɔ lɛ husui lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okadi shikpɔŋ lɛ husui Amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ jwɛi lɛ hu nɔ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitsumɔ.

english: What is this commercial animal feed called 'mash', and how does it help my animals grow?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ jarayeli niyenii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘mash’ nɛɛ ni te eyeɔ ebuaa mikooloi lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Mash is a prepared feed made by grinding grains like maize, soybeans, and rice bran together with added vitamins and minerals. Unlike plain wild grass, it gives your animals a concentrated mix of protein and energy so they build weight much faster.
ga: Atomɔ ni ashã ji niyenii ni ahoɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmaa tamɔ abele, soybeans, kɛ bran ni akɛ vitamini kɛ mineral fataa he lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ koo mli jwɛi folo lɛ, ehaa okooloi lɛ náa protein kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni efutu. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ shwiili oya.

english: Is natural wild grass enough to keep my livestock healthy, or do I need to give them prepared feeds?
ga: Ani koo mli jwɛi ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha mikooloi lɛ aná hewalɛ? Aloo esa akɛ maha amɛ niyenii ni asaa?

english: Wild grass provides fiber, but it often lacks essential proteins and minerals, especially when it dries out. Feeding your animals prepared feed mixes alongside grass gives them the full nutrition they need to stay healthy and grow bigger.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi haa fiber. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛbɛ protein kɛ mineral ni he hiaa waa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ha okooloi lɛ niyenii ni asaa he lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Can I use leftover crop waste like cassava peels or maize husks to feed my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ŋmãa aha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, crop residues like dried maize stalks, cassava peels, and groundnut vines make good supplementary animal feed, especially when fresh green grass is hard to find in the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni eshwɛ tamɔ ŋmãa ni egbi. cassava peel Kɛ ŋmei wain tsei ji niyenii kpakpa. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ewa akɛ aaana jwɛi ŋmɔŋ hee yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How can I store fresh green crops or grass so that my animals have food during dry periods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo sũ ato koni maha mikooloi lɛ niyenii yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You can preserve green fodder by drying it in the sun to make hay or by packing chopped green crops tightly in sealed bags to make silage. This prevents the feed from spoiling and ensures your animals have food during feed shortages.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ niyenii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ato he kɛtsɔ hulu ni oooha egbi koni okɛtsu nii akɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei eŋɔli ni afolɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ koni akɛfee silage lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha niyenii lɛ akafite, ni ebaaha okooloi lɛ aná niyenii yɛ be mli ni niyenii faaa lɛ.

english: Which fast-growing crops can I plant specifically to produce high-nutrient food for my livestock?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu pɔtɛɛ koni maná niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mikooloi lɛ?

english: Leguminous crops like cowpeas, groundnuts, and fast-growing forage grasses produce rich foliage quickly. The leaves of these crops contain high levels of protein that help your animals grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas, peanuts, kɛ niyenii jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ woɔ baai babaoo oya. Protein babaoo yɛ tsei nɛɛ baai amli ni yeɔ ebuaa okooloo lɛ ni edara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my animals grow faster when I give them grain-based feed mixes instead of just grazing in the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikooloi lɛ daraa oya kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmaa ni akɛfutu nii ha amɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooye kooloi yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛkɛ?

english: Grazing animals spend a lot of energy walking around to find enough wild grass. Grain-based feeds deliver concentrated protein and energy directly to the animal in small meals, allowing them to gain weight faster without burning off energy.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛyaa he fɛɛ he. Bɔni afee ni ana koo mli jwɛi ni fa bɔ ni sa Niyenii ni akɛ ŋmãa fee lɛ kɛ protein ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ hewalɛ haa kooloi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ niyenii bibii amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni amɛhe wa oya ni amɛshãaa hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller trees like plantains or forest trees to protect them from hot direct sunlight and harsh winds. Without shade, the tender leaves dry out and the plant dies before its roots can establish properly.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantain loo koo mli tsei adɛŋ. Bɔni afee ni abu kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, baai bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni tso lɛ gboɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow and droop after heavy rains stay on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Tomato roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the field for too long, it drowns the roots, preventing them from absorbing nutrients and leading to yellowing leaves and wilting.
ga: Tomato shishifãi lɛ hia kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight for the same limited water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Giving each plant enough space allows it to feed properly and grow full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni falɛ ni fa fioo pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. Kɛ́ oha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni eye nii jogbaŋŋ ni eda kɛyashɛ ŋmei ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same plot where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them alongside or after maize naturally enriches the soil so your maize grows greener and stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa masɛi loo esɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of plant food in the soil. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy when conditions are not right for fruit production.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. aloo niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei amli ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he beni shihilɛi lɛ ehiii kɛha yibiiwoo.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the roots. Balanced soil nutrients ensure energy goes down into the cassava roots.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ boteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Curled and yellowing leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Affected plants cannot make food efficiently, leading to poor root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see sticky honeydew and black soot on my cocoa pods and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii diji yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: The sticky substance is left behind by mealybugs and aphids feeding on the plant sap. A black mold then grows on this sugary waste, blocking sunlight from reaching the leaves and weakening the tree.
ga: Nɛkɛ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi nɛɛ ji nɔ ni mealybugs kɛ aphids ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ shiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe. ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ

english: Why should I remove the extra shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Cutting them back to leave only one or two strong stems ensures the mother plant has enough strength to bear heavy bunches.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo mli koni ashi tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ he wa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ etere fɔfɔi ni tsii lɛ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the plant has finished transferring its energy down into the root tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops stop producing as many fruits after a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Just like humans, plants naturally grow old and lose their strength over time. After several years of producing fruit, the plant's internal systems wear down, making it hard for it to take in food and produce high yields like it used to.
ga: tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Tsei lɛ daa ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Beni ewo yibii afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ amli gbɛjianɔtoi lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaye niyenii ni aná yibii babaoo tamɔ tsutsu lɛ.

english: Is it normal for a crop's harvest to drop significantly around five or six years after planting?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi waa yɛ afii enumɔ loo enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Yes, for many medium-term crops, five to six years is the peak period for high yields. After this point, the plant's natural energy starts to drop, and overall production will naturally begin to fall.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛha tsei babaoo ni yeɔ be teŋgbɛ. Afii enumɔ kɛyashi enumɔ ji be ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa. Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ Tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ baaje shishi eba shi. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ baaje shishi eba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some of my crops grow so fast at the beginning but get weak later in life?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa oya waa yɛ shishijee mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: In their early years, crops put most of their food and energy into growing strong stems and leaves. After spending years producing heavy harvests, their internal root systems wear out, causing their overall growth energy to decrease.
ga: Yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ tsei kɛ baai ni wa. Yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛfee nibii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ Amɛmli shishifãi lɛ hu fiteɔ. Enɛ haa dalɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How does the age of a crop affect its ability to fight off pests and diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ afii ni ŋmɔshi nibii eye lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛwuɔ eshiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai lɛ ahe?

english: Young crops have plenty of energy to protect themselves and heal from damage, whereas older crops with declining energy become weak and easily get attacked by diseases and insect pests.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛi babaoo ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe he ni amɛtsaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei bibii ni hewalɛ eba shi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ oya.

english: How do I know when it is time to cut down my old crops and plant new ones?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mafo ŋmɔshi nibii momoi amli ni madu eheei?

english: When you notice that adding fertilizer and caring for your plants no longer gives you a good harvest, and the crop is several years old, its strong life stage is over and it is time to replace it.
ga: Beni oyɔseɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ otsei lɛ amli kɛ amɛkwɛmɔ kɛ yibii kpakpai baaa dɔŋŋ lɛ. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi afii babaoo. No mli lɛ, eshihilɛ be ni mli wa lɛ eba naagbee. Ni be eshɛ ni esa akɛ atsake.

english: Why can't I just keep putting more fertilizer on old plants to make them act young again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makɛ tsofa awo tsei ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛfee tamɔ oblahii kɛ oblayei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides food, but old plants lose their ability to absorb and use that food properly. Investing in new, young seedlings brings far better results than spending money feeding aging crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii, shi tsei ni edara lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni amɛkɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ shika wo dumɔwui heei amli lɛ, ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba fe shika ni ooofite yɛ tsei ni egbɔ ni aduɔ lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I delay replacing my old crops when their harvest starts dropping?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momoi lɛ tsake be mli ni kpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi ebaa shi lɛ?

english: If you delay, you will waste time and money caring for plants that yield very little. Replacing old crops quickly ensures your farm keeps producing plenty of food without long periods of low harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ atsɛ sɛɛ lɛ, be kɛ shika baafite yɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ mli. Nibii ni adu momo lɛ ni oootsake oya lɛ haa oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni okpa yɛ bei ni baa shi mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I wait for my old crops to die completely before I start raising new seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ agbo kwraa dani mabɔi dumɔwui heei adumɔ?

english: No, you should prepare your new seedlings early while the old crops are coming to the end of their peak years. That way, the new plants are ready to take over as soon as the old ones lose their vigor.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ osaa odumɔwui heei lɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ miiba afi ni shweremɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ naagbee. Nakai lɛ, tso hee ko feɔ klalo akɛ ebaaye nɔ kɛji tso momo lɛ sɛɛ fo pɛ.

english: Is it better to clear my entire farm at once to replant, or replace the old crops gradually?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaajie ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ shikome koni adu tsei heei loo akɛ tsei momo awo najiaŋ fiofio?

english: Replacing old crops step-by-step or in sections is usually better, as it allows you to keep harvesting from remaining crops while the new seedlings grow, preventing a sudden loss of income.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momoi lɛ tsake yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli loo yɛ fãi amli lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ, ejaakɛ ehaa oyaa nɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui heei kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shika ni baafite trukaa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce smaller tubers when left in the soil for too many seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be babaoo tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants stay in the ground past their best stage, they stop storing extra food in the tubers and begin spending energy just to keep the main stem alive, leading to woody or smaller harvests.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtekeɔ he ni sa jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Ekpaa niyenii krokomɛi ni ekɛtoɔ eyitso lɛ mli lɛ. ni ebɔi hewalɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛkwɛ tsɔne wulu lɛ pɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa anáa tso loo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and die during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and short roots that cannot handle full, direct sunlight or dry soil. Providing shade plants like plantains or shade trees protects them from scorching sun and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Flower drop happens when the tree is stressed by lack of water, poor soil nutrients, or damage from insects like mirids (capsids). Ensuring proper soil moisture and pest control helps the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nu ni bɛ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo nibii ni kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) lɛ fiteɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my maize plants turn yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani tso lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient maize needs to grow strong. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores green leaf growth and bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmãa ni he hiaa ni eda waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo nitrogen ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa ni ji baai eŋɔli kɛ ŋmãa wuji lɛ adara ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good to plant cowpeas or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds the maize growing next to it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eha ŋmãa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining, it smothers the roots and allows fungal diseases to rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha ŋmeii ahe helai aba.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines instead of letting them crawl on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ woɔ tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã ekplekeshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the hot ground and puts them high up where they can capture maximum sunlight to feed the growing tubers, while also reducing fungal diseases from damp soil.
ga: Staking jieɔ sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa he ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni ebaanyɛ emɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ekɛha bulbs ni miida lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I cut away the extra suckers growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie Plantain shishitoo lɛ

english: Too many suckers compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to grow a large plantain bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛduɔ plantains wuji.

english: Plantains have shallow roots and get very top-heavy when carrying heavy bunches. Supporting the main stem with bamboo or wooden props holds the plant steady against strong winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ awó ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo tsei ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why do weeds lower the crop yield of my farm even if I planted good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, space, soil nutrients, and water away from your crops, leaving the crops weak and unable to yield full cobs, pods, or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ nu ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ onibii amli Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and stop growing green during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔɔ eŋɔli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses, or by extreme heat causing the plant to curl its leaves to conserve water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu nu he lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn weak and grow slowly if I leave them on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds act like uninvited guests at a meal—they steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight directly from your crops, leaving your plants starved and unable to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni afɔ̃ko amɛ nine yɛ niyeli lɛ shishi. Amɛjuɔ nu. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ onibii anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to clear weeds on my farm before they damage my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani efite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should weed when the wild plants are still small and before they flower, usually when they reach knee-high or start blocking light from your young crops, so they don't steal nutrients during critical growth stages.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii beni koo mli tsei lɛ darako kɛ dani amɛbaawo fɔfɔi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ eshɛ otsitsi nɔ loo ebɔi la ni jɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ ji koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Does cutting weed tops at soil level hurt my crops less than digging out the weed roots?
ga: Ani jwɛi lɛ ayitsei ni afoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui fioo fe shishifãi lɛ ni aaakumɔ?

english: Digging out weed roots is better for your crops because simply cutting the tops leaves the roots alive to quickly shoot up again and continue competing with your crops for nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi shishifãi ni oootsi lɛ hi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ́ ofo ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ kɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ wala koni amɛdara ekoŋŋ oya ni amɛkɛ otso lɛ abɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow when the surrounding bush grows too thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli eyi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crops turn yellow when they are starved of sunlight; a thick surrounding bush blocks the light your crop leaves need to make food and stay healthy green.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji hulu la bɛ. Tsoi bibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ la ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli lɛ naa.

english: Why is clearing and properly clearing my land so important before I put seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa waa akɛ mafolɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mafolɔ mli dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Proper land clearing removes weed seed reserves and dangerous pests hidden in the bush, giving your young crop seeds a clean, safe environment with enough open sunlight to sprout evenly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara ni yɔɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa o-fruit dumɔwui bibii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without yielding much when I plant them too close together during field setup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe efee mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo lɛ? Beni midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ beni misaa he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight and end up growing tall and skinny trying to reach the light instead of spending energy to produce heavy fruits.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la he ni amɛgbeɔ naa ni amɛfeɔ shwiili kɛ shwiili, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ la lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cocoa pods tell you they are ripe through color changes: green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn bright orange.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ekwɛ̃ yɛ su ni tsakeɔ lɛ hewɔ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: What will happen to my cocoa crops if I leave ripe pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to sprout or rot, and it attracts diseases like black pod that can spread to the rest of your healthy cocoa trees.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Ni egbalaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: How often should I go through my farm to harvest ripe cocoa pods during the main season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be titri lɛ mli?

english: During the main harvest season, you should harvest every two to three weeks to gather pods at peak ripeness and prevent disease from building up on mature pods.
ga: yɛ kpamɔ be titri lɛ mli Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii Enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ koni obua ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe fɛɛ lɛ anaa. ni atsĩ helai anaa yɛ ŋmeii ni eda kwraa lɛ anɔ

english: Why does clearing weeds around young cocoa trees help them grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Kookoo tsei bibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Young cocoa trees have shallow root systems that easily get overwhelmed by aggressive grass roots; clearing weeds keeps the topsoil free so the cocoa roots can take up all the fertilizer and rainwater.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni jwɛi shishifãi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli tseee. No hewɔ lɛ, kookoo shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nugbɔ nu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Is it good to keep big forest trees on my farm while growing crops under them?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mahã koo mli tso agbo ko ahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛfata tsei ni miida yɛ eshishi lɛ ahe?

english: Certain forest trees protect crops like cocoa by providing shade and dropping leaves that enrich the soil. However, if there are too many trees, they block essential sunlight and compete with your crops for water and plant nutrients.
ga: Tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ kooi amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛtsɔ hulutsoo kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi, kɛji tsei babaoo yɛ lɛ, Tsei tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa lɛ naa ni amɛkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei lɛ amli niyenii.

english: Why do my crops growing near the forest boundary grow slower than the ones in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni midu yɛ kooi husui ahe lɛ daa blɛoo fe nɔ ni midu yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Large forest trees have broad branch canopies that block sunlight and wide root systems underground that steal water and nutrients away from smaller crops growing close to them.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ kooi wuji amli lɛ yɛ niji ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa, kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to protect them, heat scorches the leaves and causes the young plant to dry out quickly.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni akɛbuɔ he lɛ, latsaa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers rely on tiny insects like midges for pollination. If the weather is too dry or if chemical sprays drive away these insects, the flowers will wither and fall off without forming pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anɔ kɛha pollination. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ, Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii.

english: Why am I getting huge green leaves on my cassava plants but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy in roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ tsei kakadaji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds before planting my yam seed pieces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabu shikpɔŋ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil so yam tubers can expand easily without hitting hard ground. It also improves drainage so the young roots do not rot in standing water.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ hu bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ akafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over before the fruit bunches are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai akutsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches. Strong winds or loose soil can easily tip them over unless they are planted deep enough and supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mlɛo. Ja adu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni akɛ tsei fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the soil moisture changes drastically, preventing the plant from absorbing enough calcium to build strong fruit walls.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛma aduawai gbogboi ni wa.

english: Rolling leaves is a protective reaction. When maize experiences severe heat or dry soil, it rolls its leaves to reduce water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ mɔ he. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Ebaafolɔ ebaa lɛ koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks key nutrients like nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains can wash nutrients deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea helps the leaves turn green so the plant can make food and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei baanyɛ afee niyenii ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my maize so the grains do not spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbooo?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and a tiny black spot appears at the base of the kernels on the cob, showing that the plant has finished sending nutrients to the grain.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Ni ŋmeii bibii diji yɛ jɛmɛ. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ shishi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa dumɔwui lɛ egbe naa.

english: Why do my maize plants fall over easily whenever a strong wind blows across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over when their roots cannot grip the soil deep enough, which happens if seeds are planted too shallowly or if the soil is too hard. Piling soil around the stem base during weeding gives the roots extra support.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa. Enɛ baa mli kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni atoɔ he kɛbɔleɔ Tso lɛ shishi yɛ jwɛi shwiemɔ be mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ kroko.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall in one section of my farm but stay short and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miiya hiɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ kuku lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil quality changes across different parts of the same land. The short plants are likely in spots with poor nutrients, hard soil that stops root growth, or areas where water collects and chokes the roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su tsakeɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi. shikpɔŋ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ Bei pii lɛ tsei kukuji yɛ hei ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa loo hei ni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I check if my land has enough water for my crops without guessing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni masusu he?

english: You can check by digging six inches into the ground and squeezing a handful of soil; if it forms a soft ball without dripping water, it is right, but using modern soil moisture monitoring tools can tell you the exact water needs instantly.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni oootsi inchii enumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ko ni oootswa shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu shwieee shi lɛ, abuɔ lɛ akɛ eja. Shi kɛ okɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni akɛsusuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ bo nu pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my maize from growing properly?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ mi-abele lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than maize and aggressively drink the water and eat the soil nutrients meant for your crops, while also blocking sunlight from reaching the maize leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni ekɛ hiɛdɔɔ nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ amli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la hu naa koni ekashɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ahe.

english: What is eating small holes into my maize leaves and how does it hurt my harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? kɛtee mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli Ni te enáa mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. Damaged leaves cannot absorb sunlight properly, which starves the plant and leads to smaller cobs or no grains at all.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa mli lɛ baa. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii loo dumɔwui bɛ kwraa.

english: Why do the tips of my maize cobs remain empty without grains forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ naa lɛ efee efolo lolo ni dumɔwui ko bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Empty cob tips happen when the maize plant does not get enough water or fertilizer during the flowering stage, or when high heat prevents the silks from being fertilized properly.
ga: Cob ends ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo ŋmãa ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo be mli ni latsaa lɛ haa siliki ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛwo fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can using machine technology on my farm help me grow better maize?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔnei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Farm monitoring technology helps you track soil health, moisture, and crop conditions early so you can fix problems with water or nutrients before your plants suffer.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ tɛknɔlɔji haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ hewalɛnamɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ osaa nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he naagbai dani otsei lɛ apiŋ.

english: Can a farmer with physical challenges use modern farm machinery to manage a maize field?
ga: Ani okwaafoi ni bɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli tsɔnei atsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, modern farm technologies and light machinery reduce the need for heavy manual labor like land clearing and digging, allowing farmers with physical limitations to comfortably monitor and manage their crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaalee kɛ tsɔnei ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ eha nitsumɔi ni tsii ni akɛ niji tsuɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsaa lɛ eba shi. Ehaa okwaafoi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ kwɛɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize stalks usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the roots are sitting in flooded soil, which stops the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. loo shishifãi ni eta shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant cowpeas between my rows of maize, will it help my crops grow better?
ga: Kɛ midu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, which naturally feeds the maize and improves soil fertility without needing as much synthetic fertilizer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yaa hiɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa babaoo atsu nii.

english: What causes the leaves of my young corn plants to look like tiny holes were shot through them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni atswa bu bibii kɛtsɔ mli?

english: Tiny holes in corn leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnels of the plant early in the morning and feed on the fresh leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow short and yield very small harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and underground nutrients directly from your crop roots, effectively starving your crops while they are trying to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in a field with no tall trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and dry out quickly under direct sunlight; they require shade crops like plantains or bananas to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I not plant my seed yams very close to each other in the mounds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting seed yams too close together forces the vines to fight for sunlight and soil space, which produces many tiny, thin tubers instead of large, heavy yams.
ga: Kɛ́ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha wain tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo babaoo baa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off without fruiting when the air becomes too hot, when the soil receives too little water, or when there is a lack of phosphorus in the soil to support fruit growth.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu fioo pɛ sũ lɛ náa loo kɛ́ sũ lɛ bɛ fɔsfɔs ni baaha aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are mature enough to harvest so they don't rot underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and visible cracks start appearing in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ shishi ejieɔ amɛhe kpo yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my crops with dry grass during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi woɔ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root area cool, and prevents the sun from baking and drying out your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashã oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni eha egbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl and droop as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant save water when transpiration rates are high.
ga: Curls ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛji nu ni hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ fa babaoo.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain after a long dry spell is often followed by hot, dry days that can dry up the soil and scorch young seeds before the main rainy season truly settles in. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures seeds have enough constant water to grow.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã dumɔwui lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baa daa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Look closely at the tiny raised bumps or buds on the stem where old leaves were attached. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so that new leaves grow upward easily while healthy roots develop below.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Yɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni baai momoi ekpɛtɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya ŋwɛi mlɛo yɛ be mli ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and burn easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Keeping large shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides a living umbrella that shelters young cocoa from extreme heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei wuji akwɛmɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni bu cocoa tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I place fertilizer right next to the main stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ masɛi?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's soft skin and damage sensitive roots. It is best to place fertilizer a few inches away in a circle around the plant where the feeding roots can reach it safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 yɛ kooyigbɛ ni ebɔle tso lɛ he yɛ he ni ebaafee shweshweeshwe kɛha shishifãi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ ni amɛshɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and build strong stalks. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni amɛma tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from sudden heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting shade crops or flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps the plant retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ mli dɔlɛ trukaa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu tsei loo fɔfɔi ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ekɛgbala ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes during hot afternoons is often a defense mechanism to reduce water loss through the leaves. If the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, the plant is managing heat, but if they stay curled, it may mean tiny insects like whiteflies are feeding on them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni ajieɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikwɛ hulutsoo lɛ nɔ, shi kɛji baai lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ, ekolɛ etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji miiye amɛ.

english: Will planting cowpeas in the same field as my maize take away food from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ baajie niyenii kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: No, cowpeas actually help feed the maize. Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and converts it into natural plant food in the soil, benefiting neighboring crops like maize.
ga: Dabi, tsina ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa ŋmãa niyenii. Cowpeas ji legume weku lɛ mlinyo, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce energy. Lifting vines on stakes prevents rot on wet ground and helps the plant grow larger tubers underneath.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ bulbs wuji yɛ amɛshishi.

english: What is causing the rolled-up center leaves of my young maize to look chewed with green sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai ni abɔle lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni eŋɔli yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the soft growing center of young maize to feed. Applying targeted organic pest remedies or approved sprays into the leaf center early in the morning helps protect the growing crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida blɛoo lɛ ateŋ koni amɛye nii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when the sun gets very bright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living canopy that provides shade and keeps the moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni haa shade ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kɛha wala lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very thin even when the stems look tall and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ waa eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛlɛ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Tall stems mean the plant has plenty of nitrogen, but building thick cassava tubers requires potassium and loose, well-aerated soil so the roots have room to expand.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa. Shi bɔni afee ni afee cassava shishifãi ni mli tse lɛ biɔ potassium kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Koni eha shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of green leaves but refusing to produce pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas generate their own nitrogen. If you add too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant focuses all its energy on leaf growth instead of developing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Tsinai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen. Kɛji okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai lɛ adalɛ he nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crop turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen early in its life to stay green and grow large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmã kɛjɛ egbekɛbiiashi koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ toi wuji.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. Mulching around the base of the crop helps trap moisture in the soil longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which feed on plant juices and spread viral diseases to the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: Yam rot happens when heavy rainfall causes water to sit around the roots in poorly drained soil, allowing fungi and bacteria in the mud to attack the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato rot lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems. If tiny soil pests like nematodes or root borers damage those roots, the plant loses its anchor and collapses under heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fite nakai shishifãi lɛ. Tso lɛ laajeɔ eŋmei lɛ ni egbee shi yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, dry spells, or irregular watering, which forces the plant to shed flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Cabbages split when they get a sudden surge of heavy rain or watering after a dry spell, causing the inside of the head to swell faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabaji baatswa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa loo kɛji akɛ nu shwie nɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ fũuɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off some of the old branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji momo ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach all parts of the plant. It removes dead or diseased wood and encourages the tree to produce fresh new branches that can bear more pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ hei fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei ni egboi loo hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekwɛ̃ niji heei ni baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Flowers usually fall off when the plant suffers from environmental stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he amanehulu. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: When is the best time of the year for me to start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: In Ghana, planting is best done at the beginning of the major rainy season, usually around April or May, so that seeds get consistent moisture to sprout and establish strong root systems.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, aduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April loo May mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why should I leave space between my plants instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without competing with its neighbors. It also improves airflow, which keeps fungal diseases from spreading easily.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ akutsoŋbii akaŋ Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ hu yaa hiɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has enough nutrients to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Healthy soil is typically dark, soft, retains moisture well, and contains living organisms like earthworms. If your soil is hard, light in color, or crops grow slowly with pale leaves, it needs compost or organic manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli edɔ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo ni amɛhe baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli atsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant cassava on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and healthier.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi aba. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged, which prevents roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii.

english: How can I tell if small insects are damaging my crops before it becomes a big problem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kooloo bibioo ko miifite miŋmɔshi nibii dani ebatsɔ naagba wulu?

english: Regularly check the underside of leaves and young shoots for tiny holes, curling leaves, sticky liquid, or discolored spots. Catching these early signs allows you to treat pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishi daa kɛji buji bibii, baai ni ebɔle amɛhe, nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ mli. loo color change point Mra be mli okadii nɛɛ ni ooomɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsaa tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does clearing weeds from my farm help my cassava grow bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava lɛ ni ekwɛɔ yitsei wuji?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cassava for water, light, and soil nutrients. Removing weeds regularly leaves all the nutrients available for the cassava roots to swell and grow large.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli daa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: How can covering the soil around my plants with dry grass help them during hot days?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ehà shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Te mi tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around your crops, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation, and prevents soil erosion during heavy downpours.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni ooogbɛ oshwã oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni etsi shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during the dry season usually mean the cocoa tree is stressed from too much direct sunlight and a lack of soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving permanent shade trees helps protect young cocoa trees from burning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni bɛ lɛ miihao kookoo tso lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa ni ashiɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Why is it important for me to plant shade trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and hot winds, reduce water evaporation from the soil, and drop leaves that rot and turn into natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ha nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni eshiɔ baai ni egboi yɛ sɛɛ ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: What is the main reason extension officers tell us to prune our cocoa trees regularly?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo titri hewɔ ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo tsei daa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so air and light can circulate through the tree. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji anaa ni ewoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How often should I clear weeds around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ shishi jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weeds should be cleared three to four times a year, especially during the rainy season. Clearing weeds keeps them from stealing nutrients, water, and sunlight from your cocoa trees.
