ga: Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ shii 3-4 yɛ afi mli, titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ o-cocoa tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny insects called midges, or if the tree is stressed by drought or poor nutrients. Maintaining soil moisture and avoiding harsh chemical sprays during flowering helps midges survive and pollinate your trees.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. aloo kɛji akɛ hɔmɔ loo niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dwarf lɛ ni ehiɔ shi ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ woɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn shriveled and black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii So mine lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which is a natural way the cocoa tree thins out pods it cannot afford to feed. However, if it happens to almost all pods, it may be caused by black pod disease or insect damage from capsid bugs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji ‘cherelle wilt’, ni ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ejieɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aha amɛ niyenii lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ enɛ ba nɔ ni miihe ashɛ pods fɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ekolɛ black pod hela loo capsid ni kooloi fiteɔ lɛ hewɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, overly wet conditions with poor air movement. You can control it by removing infected pods immediately and pruning excess tree branches to improve air flow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe fe nine, shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pods are ready to harvest when their skin changes color completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from red to orange-yellow. Harvesting pods while they are still green reduces the quality and yield of your cocoa beans.
ga: Pods lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa beni amɛhiɛ su etsake kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru mli kɛtee yellow-orange Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ, ebaaha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it necessary to ferment my cocoa beans under banana leaves after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ afee cocoa ŋmeii yɛ banana baai ashishi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fermentation is what creates the rich chocolate flavor and dark brown color in cocoa beans. It also stops the seeds from germinating and helps the beans dry properly so they reach export quality.
ga: Nɔ ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ waa yɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ hu shwereɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛya maŋsɛɛ.

english: How does registering with the Ghana Cocoa Board benefit a small-scale farmer like me?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi ni kɛ ehe woɔ Ghana Cocoa Board lɛ mli lɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ?

english: The Cocoa Board helps smallholder farmers by providing access to approved high-quality seeds, mass spraying programs against pests, subsidized fertilizers, and extension services that teach modern farming techniques to boost yields.
ga: Cocoa Board lɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi bibii kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni ehaa amɛnáa lɛ nɔ. Nitsumɔ ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo Akɛ shika yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nitsumɔi ni akɛyaa hiɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi koni nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the correct amount of chemical to mix in my knapsack sprayer so I do not burn my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai abɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛfutu mi-baagi mli tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli? Bɔni afee ni mikashã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Most small chemical sachets are measured to be mixed into one standard 15-liter knapsack sprayer full of clean water. Using too much chemical can burn leaves and damage crops, while using too little will not kill the pests.
ga: Asusuɔ tsofai kotokui bibii babaoo ahe koni akɛfutu tsɔne kome ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛ ni tsiimɔ ji lita 15 ni nu ni mli tse eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ nɔ ko fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend spraying my farm more than once in a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔse miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa fe shikome yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: A single round of spraying usually kills only adult insects, but insect eggs left on the crop leaves will hatch later. Doing a second or third round of spraying destroys the new pests before they can reproduce and damage crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shikome pɛ lɛ baagbe kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ pɛ. Shi kooloi bibii ni ashi yɛ tsei ahe baa lɛ baafɔ sɛɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ji enyɔ loo etɛ lɛ baafite tsɛŋemɔ helai heei dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfɔ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens if rain falls right after I spray medicine on my crops?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikɛ nu shwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Rain washes the chemical off crop leaves before the plant or insects can absorb it, which wastes the medicine and leaves your crops unprotected against pests and diseases.
ga: Nugbɔ shwieɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli lɛ ahe dani tsei loo kooloi bibii baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ tsofa ni ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that lose water quickly under direct hot sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the seedlings from heat stress while they grow stronger roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantain ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: What will happen to my maize crops if I plant the seeds too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their leaves block each other from sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients and water in the soil, resulting in thin, weak plants with smaller ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination inside the blossoms, causing the flowers to drop off before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are being eaten by insects or damaged by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi eye mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo tso hela ko efite?

english: Insects usually leave physical holes or chewed edges on leaves, whereas diseases often cause leaf discoloration, yellowing, dark spots, or wilting without actual bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ bu loo baai ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ahe. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛgboɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ diɛŋtsɛ ko bɛ he.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I use weedicide to clear them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ gbe jwɛi lɛ moŋ.

english: Weed seeds hidden underground can sprout after rain even if top weeds are dead, or the chemical used only burnt the top leaves without killing the deep root system of the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ, kɛji jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ gbo po. loo tsofai ni akɛshãa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ ni efiteee jwɛi lɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or shade, the crop puts all its food and energy into growing tall stems and bushy leaves instead of storing nutrients in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo shade babaoo lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ amɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛduɔ yɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaato niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why does my soil produce lower yields now compared to when I first started farming this piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto be mli ni mibɔi shikpɔŋ nɛɛ nɔ okwaayeli klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ he lɛ?

english: Every crop harvest removes essential food and nutrients from the earth, so continuous planting without adding fertilizer, manure, or letting the land rest leaves the soil tired and hungry.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yaa nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, loo ashiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is an important plant food in the soil, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and weaker every year even though I plant on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee bibii ni migbɔjɔ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil over time. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil's natural strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ baajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and dark brown dust inside the shoots?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths and eat the plant from the inside. Applying recommended organic remedies or targeted insecticides into the center funnel of the plant early in the season stops the damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛfoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli lɛ. Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli tsuɔ he nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ akpa.

english: Why are the green pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in overly wet and dark conditions. Pruning excess branches to let sunlight in and removing infected pods immediately helps stop the disease from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ tsɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ oya lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Spraying natural neem leaf extract or targeted pest controls protects the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem baa mli nu loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers, but the flowers drop off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, prolonged drought, or heavy insect attack on the blooms. Giving the plants consistent water and light shade during extremely hot afternoons helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo kooloi komɛi yɛ ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ waa. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Does the depth at which I bury my crop seeds when planting affect how they grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mifuɔ midumɔwui lɛ mli kwɔ ha beni miduɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Yes, planting seeds too deep uses up all their energy before they can sprout through the soil surface, while planting too shallow leaves them exposed to birds and hot sun. A good rule is to plant seeds at a depth equal to two or three times their size.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha okpoi kɛ hulu lɛ aná dumɔwui lɛ. Mla kpakpa ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my actual crops after the rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil before your cultivated crops can get established. Clearing weeds early within the first few weeks after planting gives your young crops a head start to outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani onibii lɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ enɛ baaye abua ni odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi amɛdara fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni akpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them in heavy soil during rainy periods without proper drainage. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu tsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil with free plant food. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants and keeps the soil rich for future seasons.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei aniyenii ni aheee nɔ ko Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmãa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for healthy green leaves. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure near the base of the plant will help it recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets soil-borne pests and diseases build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts refills nitrogen in the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni akɛ nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or mites sucking leaf sap, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these tiny pests early prevents the damage from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Enɛɛmɛi kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaye abua ni nɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my cowpea pods have tiny holes and missing seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni dumɔwui bɛ mli

english: Tiny holes in cowpea pods are made by pod borer caterpillars that eat the seeds inside while the pod is forming. Spraying safe, recommended pest treatments when flowering begins helps protect the pods.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ cowpea ŋmeii amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ amli. Tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up before the tubers under the ground are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miiho dani ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines often dry up early due to a fungal disease called anthracnose or prolonged dry spells. Planting disease-resistant yam varieties and keeping the soil moist helps keep the vines healthy until harvest time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Sweet potato henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni wain tsei lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when water supply is irregular. Keeping soil consistently moist and planting shade crops nearby during high heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because excess water starves roots of oxygen and promotes fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering my vegetable soil with dry grass help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Te jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ aduawai amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket. It shades the soil, keeps it cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ

english: Why is it important to remove weeds while my young crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ be mli ni midumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and need full light, water, and soil nutrients. Weeds grow very fast and steal these essential elements, so clearing weeds early gives your main crop a strong start.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛtaoɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to grow big after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛdaraa beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers require rich, soft soil with lots of organic material. If planted in hard or poor soil without compost or manure, root growth remains slow and plant development stalls.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ adalɛ baakã he ahi shi blɛoo ni tsei lɛ adalɛ baafee mlɛo.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the necessary shade and soil moisture young cocoa seedlings need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction become pods. The tree drops surplus flowers if it lacks sufficient water, nutrients, or natural pollinators like midges to support full pod development.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, shi fã bibioo ko pɛ bafeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Tsei baajie fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine kɛji amɛbɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa fɔfɔi baa tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ebuaa pod lɛ shweremɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: What happens if I delay harvesting ripe yellow cocoa pods and leave them on the tree?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ be shwie kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ ni mishi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to start germinating or rotting. It reduces bean quality and attracts pests like squirrels as well as fungal infections that can spoil the harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahe baa shi ni egbalaa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, kɛ agbɛnɛ ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet environments with dense shade. Keeping the farm cleared and air circulating helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why does the price I receive for my cocoa beans change from season to season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ jara srɔtoɔ yɛ be ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Cocoa prices are influenced by global market demand, total harvests in major producing countries, and minimum farmgate rates set by government bodies like COCOBOD to protect local farmers from extreme price drops.
ga: Jeŋ jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ náa kookoo jara nɔ hewalɛ. Nibii fɛɛ ni akpaa yɛ maji wuji ni feɔ nii lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔ shinaa naa nyɔmɔwoo ni baa shi fe fɛɛ ni nɔyeli nitsumɔhei tamɔ COCOBOD eto koni akɛbu maŋ lɛ mli okwaafoi ahe kɛjɛ jara ni baa shi waa lɛ he.

english: Will cutting off unnecessary branches from my mature cocoa tree hurt pod growth?
ga: Ani niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ baaná pod lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, pruning helps the tree. Removing dead or excess branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the trunk, preventing fungal diseases and directing the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ. Niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why must I cover my harvested wet cocoa beans under plantain leaves for days before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo yibii ni efɔ ni akpa lɛ haa plantain baai ashishi gbii babaoo dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Covering wet beans triggers fermentation, which stops seed germination, removes bitterness, and creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color required by buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm needs fertilizer to produce more pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: If leaves turn yellowish, tree growth slows down, or pods stay very small despite proper rain, the soil is likely depleted of key nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi Aloo ŋmeii lɛ bibii waa kɛ nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa po. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium lɛ sumɔɔ ni efite.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves dry up and shed during the dry Harmattan period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds strip moisture from leaves quickly. The cocoa tree sheds its leaves as a natural defense mechanism to conserve internal water and survive until the rains return.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni amɛkɛbuɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ he ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Is it bad to use a sharp cutlass to break open my harvested cocoa pods?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ akɛ kakla ni naa wa baafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ?

english: Yes, using a sharp cutlass can easily cut into the wet cocoa beans inside. Damaged beans rot faster during fermentation, lower overall bean quality, and reduce market value. A wooden club is safer.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ akɛ tsɔne ni mli wa tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ efo kookoo ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ amli lɛ mlɛo. Beans ni efite lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ashɛreɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ baa shi. ni ebaa jarayeli jara shi Golf shwɛmɔhei lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen nutrients or getting choked by too much standing water. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves produce chlorophyll and turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen niyenii loo eyɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee chlorophyll ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, too little water, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Giving the crop consistent water and feeding the soil helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. nu fioo tsɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu daa, ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I avoid planting cassava on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ he?

english: Planting cassava repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests accumulate. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield less when I sow seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong and yield a full harvest.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: What does adding animal manure actually do to help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients and acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto moisture during dry spells so crop roots can easily feed and grow.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ ana niyenii ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under full sunlight. Larger shade trees or fast-growing nurse plants like plantains act as umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from scorching heat until they grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves towards the sun to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight, which sends energy down to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee yitso agbo ni tsii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops even when there is plenty of land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ miyɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the water, fertilizer, and sunlight meant for your crops right at the root level, starving your main plants and reducing the final amount of food you can harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ anɔ ni oha naagbee niyenii ni obaanyɛ okpa lɛ aba shi.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves of my young maize early in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ baa? Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which crawl into the center of the plant to feed on fresh foliage before the crop can mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye baai heei lɛ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai amli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my planted seeds rot in the dirt before they can sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Seeds rot when the soil stays too wet and cold, or when planted right before a light rain that stops completely, causing the seed to absorb moisture, swell, and rot without enough continuous water to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo kɛ́ adu dani nugbɔ fioo ko nɛ lɛ, ekpaa kwraa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbalaa nu, amɛfuuɔ, ni amɛgboɔ ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build green leaves. Adding animal manure or the right fertilizer early in the season gives the crop the strength to grow dark green and produce large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛwo toi wuji.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every time I plant maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same food out of the soil until the ground is exhausted. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the dirt for the next crop.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light green and yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from leaf tips is usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will give the crop the nourishment it needs to turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my cocoa leaves burning and turning yellow during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves burn easily under direct sunlight because they need protection from extreme heat. Planting shade trees or plantains nearby creates a natural shield that keeps the cocoa cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, esa akɛ abu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko baa ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking juices from the leaves and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my crops catch fungal diseases faster when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, air cannot flow freely between them, trapping moist air around the leaves. Moisture allows fungal diseases to breed and spread rapidly from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔ he babaoo lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ oya. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni ebɔleɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ.

english: Why does spreading dry grass over my garden soil keep my crops from drying out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ agbi lɛ?

english: Spreading dry leaves or grass on top of the soil (mulching) blocks direct sunlight, stopping water from evaporating quickly so the soil stays cool and moist for your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbi loo jwɛi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in the soil for too long, suffocating the roots. Digging proper drainage channels helps excess rain flow away so the soil stays moist without becoming waterlogged.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Nu ni hoɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsa lɛ baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ni nu akabote mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the ground, feeding neighboring plants without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛtsɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants experience extreme heat stress or lack sufficient water during flowering. Regular watering during hot weather helps flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida kɛbɔle Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishi.

english: Extra shoots around the main plantain stem steal water and soil nutrients away from the mother plant. Cutting off excess shoots leaves maximum energy for the main plant to grow big, heavy bunches.
ga: Extra shoots around Plantain tso titri lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni eha tso titri lɛ ada ni etsɔ kuu agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines on sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ sweet potato wain tsei yɛ miniji lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to produce energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines high into the light while keeping them clear of ground pests and soil dampness.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa la mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: This usually means your soil is low in nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow green and strong. When the plant does not get enough from the soil, it moves what little nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to the new upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni efee hewalɛ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Ejieɔ nɔ ni ji nitrogen fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I put fertilizer on the field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil water to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it in. If you put fertilizer in dry soil under hot sun, the concentrated chemical salts stay near the roots and can actually suck moisture out of the plant, scorching or burning the roots.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ wo hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ. Ebaanyɛ eshã loo eshã shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow so tall with big leaves but only give me small, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when cassava plants are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves to reach light. Because it spends its food making leaves, it leaves very little energy to grow thick tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai ni kwɔlɔ koni enine ashɛ la nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ekɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai. It takes little energy to grow thick bulbs underground.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall stakes to climb instead of just spreading across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers. Lifting the vines up on stakes helps all leaves catch light better and keeps them off the damp soil where fungal diseases can easily rot the stems.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulb agboi ni baakwɛ̃. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ fɛɛ naa la ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni etsĩ enaa koni ekaba yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ Fungal helai baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why do the flowers on my cowpea plants fall off without making pods when the weather stays hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant faces extreme heat and drought stress, it goes into survival mode. It drops its flowers to save water and protect itself from drying out, because making pods takes a lot of energy and moisture that the plant does not have at that moment.
ga: When plants are exposed to extreme heat and drought stress, The tree will go into survival mode. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pods feemɔ biɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo, ni tsei bɛ nakai beaŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither up and die if I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to strong direct sunlight and high heat. Without bigger trees or shade plants like plantains to shelter them, the hot sun burns their tender leaves and dries out their roots faster than they can absorb water.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ bɛ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi oya tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe nu.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking out the sap. Their feeding damages the leaf tissues, making them twist up like cups, and they can also pass plant viruses to your crop.
ga: Leaf curling in peppers is often caused by small insects such as thrips or mites hiding under the leaves and sucking the sap. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. causing them to warp like cups And they can also transmit plant viruses to your crops.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes turn dark brown and rotten before they even get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efiteɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is growing. It often happens when watering is irregular—like alternating between very dry and very wet soil—which stops the plant from taking up calcium smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni ji nɔ ni kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ eyaaa nɔ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni efɔ waa lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's maize harvest give me a poorer yield than the fresh seeds I buy from the extension store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe kɛjɛ shwapo ni akɛyaa ŋmãa mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The seeds you buy are usually hybrids created by crossing two specific parent plants for high yield. When you plant seeds saved from a hybrid harvest, their offspring lose that special combined strength and will produce unequal, smaller cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni oheɔ lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee kɛtsɔ fɔlɔ tsei enyɔ ni akɛfoɔ mli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ Amɛshwiei lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ni abua naa lɛ. ni ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo ni amɛyeee egbɔ lɛ aba

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil with tough shells and strong root systems already adapted to the local environment. As soon as the first rain hits, they wake up quickly to grab the water and soil nutrients before your planted crop seeds even have a chance to sprout.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kã sũ lɛ mli, ni eyɛ ŋmei ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni etsɔ ehe ewo shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Amɛteɔ shi oya koni amɛyamɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Dani dumɔwui ni odu lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ,.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains or cassava next to them creates a protective cover that shelters the tender cocoa leaves from sun damage and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo cassava lɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ kookoo baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he lɛ baa, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to trim off the lower branches of shade trees growing on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aniji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Trimming lower branches lets moderate light and air flow freely through the farm. Good airflow reduces dampness around the cocoa trees, which prevents pod diseases like black pod from spreading.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni yɔɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa shi, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pod helai tamɔ pod diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Weeds are wild, stubborn plants adapted to quickly steal water and nutrients from the soil. Clearing them early ensures your crops get the full benefit of rainwater and plant food without having to fight for resources.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yitsoŋ wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni oootsi ohe mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nugbɔ nu lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdu niyenii ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nibii ni he hiaa lɛ awuu.

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots compete underground for space, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to develop thick, heavy tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ bulbs ni mli wa ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize on the exact same piece of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping maize and cassava works well because maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slower and takes over the space after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya ni esaa ehe kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, edaa blɛoo ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves up toward the sun to feed the plant. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, preventing rot and helping the tubers grow big under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nitrogen they need to turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná nitrogen ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout if I plant them immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often only wets the surface of dry soil. If a hot dry spell follows, the soil dries out quickly and the tender sprouting seeds die before their roots can reach deeper soil water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ hei ni egbi pɛ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ni dumɔwui bibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ gboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nu he yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by fall armyworm caterpillars. These pests hide inside the center of the plant during the day and chew through the leaves as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are some of the small cocoa pods on my trees turning shriveled and black before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ shwieɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Small pods shrivel up due to a condition called cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree has more pods than it can feed, or when sap-sucking insects and pod rot diseases attack the young pods.
ga: Pods bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel’s wilt lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye. aloo beni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛ pod rot tutuaa pod bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Applying compost or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season helps the crop stay green and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season, why does my harvest keep reducing?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops with legumes like groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ mli.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts alongside my primary crop improve my soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their root nodules. As the roots grow and break down, they release this natural fertilizer into the soil for nearby crops to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ shishifãi lɛ dara ni amɛmli gbala Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ kɛtsu nii.

english: Should I put fertilizer in the soil at the exact same time I plant my seeds, or wait until shoots appear?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ loo mamɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii baaje kpo?

english: Seeds carry enough internal food to sprout on their own. It is generally best to apply fertilizer a few weeks after sprouting when the young roots are established enough to absorb the nutrients.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mli koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni shishifãi bibii lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary crops like plantains creates a canopy that protects tender cocoa plants from heat stress and conserves soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves and small powdery droppings inside the center of the plant?
ga: What is causing my corn leaves to be porous and contain tiny particles of excrement? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central leaf funnel of young maize plants, eating the leaves from the inside out before cobs can form.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ dani ŋmei lɛ feɔ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to uneven watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture helps the plant absorb calcium smoothly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground whenever there is heavy rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Flat, compacted soil holds too much standing water, which suffocates cassava roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very small harvests when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each individual plant gets enough energy to build strong stems and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Proper spacing gives each plant enough energy to grow strong, high-yielding stems.

english: Staking raises yam leaves off the damp soil into direct sunlight, allowing the leaves to generate more food for larger tuber growth while reducing exposure to fungal diseases on the ground.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato lɛ baai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo kɛha bulbs wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I test if the seeds stored in my room from last season are still good enough to plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni ato yɛ mitsu lɛ mli kɛjɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: You can perform a quick germination test by placing 10 seeds inside a folded wet cloth for a few days; if 8 or more sprout, your seeds are healthy and strong enough to plant in the farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee oyaiyeli he kaa kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama ni efɔ mli ni afolɔ mli lɛ nɔ gbii fioo komɛi. Kɛji 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ lɛ, no lɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What is Zidol agrochemical used for, and why should I treat my seeds with it before planting?
ga: Mɛni akɛ okwaayeli tsofa ni ji Sidol lɛ tsuɔ nii? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani madu?

english: Zidol is a seed-treatment agrochemical that shields seeds from soil-borne insects and fungal rot, giving the young seedling a clean and protected start to grow strong.
ga: Sidol ji okwaayeli mli tsofa ko ni akɛbuɔ dumɔwui ahe. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ koolooi ni yɔɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei bibii lɛ ahe tseɔ ni abuɔ amɛhe koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my rice seeds fail to sprout when I sow them directly into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate when planted too deep in the soil where oxygen cannot reach them, or when planted too shallow where hot sun dries them out before they establish roots.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ. aloo kɛ́ adu he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ yɛ he ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ ni egbiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baa.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight lines instead of scattering the seeds randomly across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight lines gives every crop equal space, sunlight, and nutrients, while making it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply inputs, and harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei fɛɛ náa he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ ehaa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ojie jwɛi. nibii ni akɛwoɔ nibii afeemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ waaa kwraa

english: Why does lowland rice thrive in flooded fields while my cassava rots under the same conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni tamɔ nɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice stalks have special internal air tubes that pump oxygen down to their roots underwater, whereas cassava roots lack this feature and drown when covered in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ mli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi lɛ. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha amɛhe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops whenever rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants built for extreme survival, allowing them to absorb available groundwater and fertilizer much faster than domestic crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni afee kɛha wala ni yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe shia tsei ahe dumɔwui.

english: Yellow leaves indicate that your plants are hungry for nitrogen—a vital soil nutrient—or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away while choking the roots with water.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe be mli ni ekɛ nu woɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants produce plenty of big green leaves but give me very little yield at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ baai wuji babaoo shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, yibii fioo pɛ ewoɔ lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and heavy leaves instead of developing grains, pods, or fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni tsii. Mohu ɔ, a woɔ dumɔwui, ŋmɔtɔ, loo yibii.

english: Why do dark brown spots appear on my rice leaves and turn the whole field brown before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: These spots are caused by fungal diseases like rice blast, which attack when there is high air humidity, poor soil nutrients, or when infected seeds were planted.
ga: Fungal helai tamɔ rice blight ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ baa. ni tutuaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛji adu dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm crops more heavily during short dry spells than during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni naa wa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes insects off leaves and destroys their eggs, whereas warm dry spells allow pests to multiply rapidly and feed on thirsty crops that are already under heat stress.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kooloi bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ahe ni efiteɔ amɛwuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo oya ni amɛyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kumai yeɔ amɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli momo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or swamps the roots so they cannot feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eye shishifãi lɛ anɔ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛna niyenii.

english: Why is it bad if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil drains specific nutrients like nitrogen and allows crop-specific pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts gives the soil time to rebuild its nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatswa niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees next to my newly planted cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture around the young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to handle sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains grow very quickly and have large leaves that act as umbrellas. Provides shade and retains moisture around light cocoa tree Until it grows strong enough to receive sunlight.

english: Yam leaves need to catch as much sunlight as possible to produce food. When you lift the vines on stakes, the leaves spread out into the light, which fuels the plant to store energy and grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa la lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tsofa ni tsei kɛtoɔ hewalɛ he ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cassava roots rot when soil stays waterlogged for too long without proper drainage. Excessive water suffocates the roots and creates the perfect environment for destructive soil fungus to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Too much water suffocates the roots and creates the perfect environment for fungus in the soil to destroy the tubers.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start sowing my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ?

english: You should not plant after just one isolated rain because the dry earth underneath quickly absorbs the water, leaving your germinating seeds to dry out. It is safer to wait until you receive two or three steady rains within a week so the soil stays moist deep down.
ga: Esaaa akɛ oduɔ nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ gbalaa nu oya. Ha dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ otsi kome mli. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashɛ shishigbɛ

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small dirt patches inside the plant's funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ muji bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They crawl inside the middle whorl of the maize plant to hide, feed on the fresh leaves, and leave behind dark waste matter.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛkpãa kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛyatee amɛhe, amɛyeɔ baai heei, ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to give a small harvest even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your main crop can get to them. If weeds grow unchecked, your crop starves even if you add fresh fertilizer.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani tso titri lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ ni akudɔɔɔ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye bo kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee fata he po.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and drop off without turning into fruit when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the tomato plant and dries out the pollen inside the flowers before bees or wind can pollinate them. Unpollinated flowers cannot produce fruit, so the plant drops them to conserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ mli fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my main crop helps the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the ground and helps neighboring crops grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni jɛɔ sɛɛ mli baa lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during intense heat as a natural survival mechanism to reduce water evaporation and protect the plant from drying out.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ shi ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my corn plants stay thin and produce small ears when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak growth and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo fioo baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and drop leaves if I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ kɛji mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, intense sunlight which can burn the crop and dry out the surrounding soil moisture.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without forming any fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when heat becomes too extreme or when water supply is irregular, causing the plant stress that stops fruit development.
ga: Tomato baagbee shi kɛ́ la lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when heavy rains last longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni afeɔ daa lɛ?

english: Excess water in poorly drained soil suffocates cassava roots by cutting off oxygen, causing anaerobic bacteria and fungi to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, anaerobic bacteria kɛ fungi tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava turn yellow and drop off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the crop is running out of essential soil nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is too dry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ

english: Why do elders say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the field better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, naturally fertilizing the field for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do pepper plant leaves wrinkle and curl upward like small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which damage the leaves and often spread viruses to the crop.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper mli lɛ baa. Enɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ ni bei pii lɛ egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize fields so fast right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ oya nɛkɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ eba lɛ?

english: Pest moths lay eggs on the tender new leaves that sprout after early rains because young corn shoots provide soft, nutritious food for newly hatched caterpillars.
ga: Pest moths woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai heei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmãa bibii lɛ haa ŋmeii ni efɔ ehee lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop black mold inside the storage bags after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ mli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize gets moldy in storage if it is bagged before it is fully dried, as trapped moisture creates the perfect condition for fungi to grow.
ga: Abɛi baaná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli dani egbi kwraa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves roll up to save water during hot, dry weather. When water is scarce, the plant loses energy and cannot draw nutrients from the soil, which causes the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ nu faaa Tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do my young crops wilt in the afternoon sun even when the soil feels slightly wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon heat makes leaves lose water faster than young roots can draw it from the soil. The plant temporarily wilts to conserve energy and reduce water loss until the air cools down.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa baai lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baagbo be kukuoo ko koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ekɛba nu ni efiteɔ lɛ shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce fewer pods when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside bean flowers, preventing proper fertilization. To save its energy, the plant drops these unfertilized flowers instead of trying to form pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa aná fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni akɛ hewalɛ akafite lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ nɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they suffer from high temperatures, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Without enough energy or proper pollination, the plant sheds flowers to protect itself.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baakwɛ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛji hewalɛ ni fa loo pollination ni sa bɛ lɛ, Tsei hu baafite fɔfɔi ni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many flowers at first but very few peppers later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ shishijee mli shi sɛɛ mli lɛ ewoɔ fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Developing flowers requires a lot of the plant's stored energy. If the plant does not get enough water or nutrients after flowering, it lacks the energy to turn every flower into a full pepper.
