ga: Fɔfɔi adalɛ biɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni tso lɛ eto lɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Ebɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaatsɔ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi ni efee chili ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I avoid spraying pesticides when my crops are flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ahe be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Chemical pesticides sprayed during flowering can kill bees and other insects that pollinate your crop. Without these insects to transfer pollen, your flowers will drop off without making fruit.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbe ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi. ni baanyɛ aha otsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ bɛ ni baanyɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, Ofɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛkɛ ni amɛwooo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow thick leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai ni mli tse shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the cassava plant to direct all its energy into leaf growth above ground, leaving little energy to store starch in the underground roots.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha ŋmei tso lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ahi shi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my crops regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. When crops have to compete with weeds, they lose energy, grow slowly, and yield smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni ehe bahia ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ jwɛi abɔ he akaŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi, amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mulching around Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ jwɛi aha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, traps moisture, and stops weeds from growing. This saves the crop's energy and water so it can focus on growing fruit.
ga: Mulching (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu baa shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama aduawai ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads in wet, heavily shaded conditions. Excessive shade and moisture weaken the tree's health, allowing the disease to destroy the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hela lɛ baanyɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is a major food crops need to grow strong. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest top leaves to survive.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up tightly and turn pale during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water when exposed to extreme heat, or because tiny insects like whiteflies have infected the leaves with a plant sickness.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he. Aloo akɛni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛ tsei ahe helai baa baa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do small round holes keep appearing all over my cowpea leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo yɛ mi-cowpea baai lɛ fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by leaf-eating insects like beetles and caterpillars. These insects chew through the leaves to feed, which stops the plant from making food properly through sunlight.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ baa tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii kɛ bu yɛ baai amli. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ŋmɔɔ baai kɛyeɔ niyenii. Enɛ haaa tsei afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their blossoms before producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani ewoɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they get too stressed by very high temperatures or when the air is too dry, which prevents the flowers from setting seeds into actual peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiifee basaa tsɔ kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa waa mli loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Enɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo dumɔwui diɛŋtsɛ akɛ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees dry up their young pods until they turn black and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods turn black and dry up either because of black pod disease caused by heavy rain fungi, or because the tree does not have enough water and food to feed all the pods at once.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ ŋmeii diji hela ni ŋmeii ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛbaa lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hewɔ. Aloo akɛni tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewoji lɛ fɛɛ akwɛ shikome hewɔ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the earth before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil holds too much water for a long time during heavy rains, which chokes the roots and allows water-loving rot fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa hydrophilic rot fungi lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow into strange, split shapes instead of nice long shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ miida ni amɛmiitsɔ srɔtoi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, ni mli eja yɛ srɔtoi kakadaji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yams grow into split or bent shapes when the soil underneath is packed too tight, full of rocks, or when microscopic worms called nematodes attack the growing tuber tips.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. tɛ loo beni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less maize when I plant it on the exact same piece of ground every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmãa fioo beni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil every time and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young cassava plants grow so thin and slow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-cassava tsei lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛmiifee mlɛo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and aggressively steal the sunlight, water, and soil food that your cassava needs to build thick leaves and strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa o-yucca lɛ koni ekwɛ baai ni mli tse kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why didn't the maize seeds I buried in the farm come out of the ground after it rained?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mifuɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to come out if they were buried too deep in the soil, if the soil dried up completely after the first rain, or if ants and soil insects ate the seeds before they could sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui ejeŋ kpo kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii kɛ sũ mli kooloi ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to spray my maize field in stages instead of applying all chemicals at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ mi-ŋma ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ tsofai fɛɛ ashwie nɔ shikome lɛ?

english: Different chemicals target weeds and pests at different stages of growth. Applying an initial chemical protects young maize during its first two critical weeks, while a follow-up chemical targets hardier weeds that emerge later, giving the crop full protection without overloading the soil.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi tsɔɔ jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ amɛdalɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Tsofai ni akɛjeɔ shishi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu abifao ŋmãa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi ni wa ni jeɔ kpo sɛɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ amɛhe kwraa ni amɛwooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine.

english: How long does a weed-control chemical usually stay active in the soil after I spray it on my maize farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fɔɔ shihilɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛshwie mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Most early-stage weed chemicals remain active in the soil for about two weeks. During this window, they prevent fresh weed seeds from germinated, giving your maize sprouts enough time to grow strong before the chemical breaks down.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ jwɛi mli shishijee lɛ ateŋ babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ, ni yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ naa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda waa dani tsofai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it safe for me to keep spraying my maize whenever I spot new weeds growing?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni mana jwɛi heei ni miida?

english: No, over-spraying can burn your crops, ruin soil health, and waste your money. Once you complete the recommended two-step chemical application early in the season, the crop is adequately protected, and further chemical spraying is unnecessary.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ oshika ni efiteɔ Kɛji okɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛi enyɔ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ Abaabu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi ashwie nɔ.

english: Can I mix two different farm chemicals together in my sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ afutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, mixing chemicals without expert advice can damage your maize or weaken the products so they do not work. Certain chemicals are designed to be applied weeks apart in a specific sequence to safely protect the crops.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ afite o-corn lɛ loo eha nɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ agbɔjɔ aahu akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii. Afee tsofai komɛi koni akɛwo otsii babaoo mli yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo pɔtɛɛ ko mli koni akɛbu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens if I miss some spots while spraying chemical on my maize farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mifo otii komɛi amli beni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Uneven application leaves unsprayed pockets where weeds and pests can freely survive. These missed areas allow pests and weeds to quickly multiply and spread across the rest of your healthy farm.
ga: Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ haa kotokui ni akɛshwieee nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shi amɛhaa amɛhe. Nɛkɛ hei ni elaaje nɛɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi shwereɔ oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa oŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds still come back on my farm even after I have sprayed chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: Chemicals only kill active weeds or prevent seeds from growing for a specific time, such as two weeks. If the chemical application was not thorough or if heavy rain washed it away too quickly, hidden weed seeds in the soil will sprout again.
ga: Tsofai gbeɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii loo etsĩɔ dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli, tamɔ otsii enyɔ pɛ. Kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai lɛ wooo mli jogbaŋŋ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho oya tsɔ lɛ, Jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: At what stage of crop growth should I stop applying chemicals to my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli esa akɛ makpa tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Chemical applications should be completed early in the crop's lifecycle once early weeds and pests are cleared. Stopping chemical use early ensures the maize matures naturally and leaves no harmful chemical residue on the final harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai awo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ tso lɛ wala be mli beni ajie jwɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shishijee fãi lɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ. Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ni akpaa mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa yɛ ehe. ni tsofai ni eshwɛ yɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ eko bɛ.

english: Who can I contact if my crops start turning yellow and I do not know which chemical to buy?
ga: Namɔ manyɛ matswa lɛ? Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mileee tsofai ni esa akɛ mahe?

english: You can contact your local agricultural extension officer. Extension officers are available to advise you on the exact pest, disease, or soil problem affecting your crops and can guide you on the right chemical and schedule to use.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyana okwaayeli he nitsulɔ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Extension nitsulɔi yɛ ni amɛbaawo bo ŋaa yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai loo shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai ni saa onibii ahe lɛ he. ni ebaanyɛ ewo bo ŋaa yɛ tsofai kɛ be ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ he.

english: How do I know which specific chemical brand is right for my young maize plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofai ni sa kɛha mi-baby corn tsei lɛ?

english: Different chemicals are designed for specific crops and growth stages. An extension officer can help you select approved, tested products suitable for your local area that will control weeds without harming your young maize.
ga: Afee tsofai srɔtoi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ amɛdalɛ fãi. Wɔ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ohala nibii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ, ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni sa kɛha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni eyeee o-baby corn lɛ awui.

english: What should I do if a chemical fails to work on my farm after I apply it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛtsu nii sɛɛ?

english: If a chemical fails, do not immediately buy a stronger chemical. Call an extension officer to inspect your field to see if the chemical was applied incorrectly, washed away by rain, or if the pests/weeds have developed resistance.
ga: Kɛji tsofai tsuuu nii Kaahe tsofai ni he wa fe no amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Tswaa extension official ko ni ebakwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ koni ena kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai miitsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa Aloo ani tsɛŋemɔ helai/jwɛi nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ?

english: How can I stop farm animals like goats and cows from eating my young cassava plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi tamɔ tooi kɛ tsinai anaa koni amɛkaye mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Farm animals love tender leaves. Planting live fences made of local jatropha plants or quick-growing thorny hedges around your plot creates a natural wall that keeps animals out without costing money for metal wire.
ga: Kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Okɛ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka ni akɛ Jatropha tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fee loo gbogbo ni akɛ ŋmei fee ni dalɛ yaa oya lɛ abɔle oshikpɔŋ lɛ he. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbogbo ko ni haaa kooloi abote mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛfite shika yɛ dade waya he.

english: Why do I see insects falling onto the ground after I spray my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa kooloi bibii ni miigbee shikpɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa eshwie kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: When pest chemical spray touches insects on the branches, it affects their movement, causing them to drop off the leaves down to the ground where they die away from the fruit.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ tsei aniji anɔ lɛ kpe Ebaana amɛ nyiɛmɔ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ he ni amɛbaagboi yɛ yibii lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do tiny bugs hide on the underside of my pepper leaves instead of the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii Aaahi mi-pepper baa lɛ shishi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi ŋwɛi?

english: Insects hide under leaves to shelter from the hot sun and heavy rain while feeding on soft tissue; spraying chemical or neem water under the leaves reaches these hidden pests directly.
ga: Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ashishi koni amɛná he ko kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he yɛ be mli ni amɛyeɔ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Tsofai loo neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ shɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How high up on my maize plants should I aim when applying liquid pest medicine?
ga: Te esa akɛ makwɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ abɔle tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ji nu miitsu nii?

english: You should direct the spray straight into the top leaf funnel where the plant grows from, because destructive pests like armyworms hide deep inside that center pocket rather than on the lower leaves.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ ŋwɛi baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehi shishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Is it safe if liquid fertilizer splashes onto my skin while I am pouring it into the sprayer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baashwie mihewolo nɔ be mli ni mikɛwoɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, farm chemicals can soak through your skin and cause sickness. Always wear protective rubber gloves and wash your body with clean water and soap immediately if any farm liquid splashes on you.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote ohewolo mli ni ekɛ hela aba. Wo rɔbɔt glɔvs ni buɔ mɔ he be fɛɛ be. Ni okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla afɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔ mli nu ko shwie onɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin instead of developing thick stems and heavy cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaana ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight and shoot upward thin and weak, leaving no energy to make thick stems or large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee tsei ni mli tse loo tsei wuji.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather is too hot or when the soil lacks moisture and nutrients during the flowering stage, preventing the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii bɛ mli yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tso lɛ wooo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops leaves or turns yellow to conserve water during dry periods; as long as the roots are established, the plant will shoot fresh green leaves once rain returns.
ga: Cassava baajɛ ebaai lɛ ashwie shi loo ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Be fɛɛ be ni shishifãi lɛ baahi shi lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why does my crop farm dry up so quickly even after a good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast due to direct sunlight. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or cocoa husks keeps the ground shaded and holds moisture in the root zone much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmeii ha onibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii ahi shishifãi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my main crops immediately after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and wake up instantly with the first rain, whereas crop seeds need extra time to break their shell and root, so clearing weeds early gives crops the space to catch up.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛteɔ shi kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui he miihia be kroko koni amɛgbala amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛshɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under harsh, direct sunlight. When they receive too much sun without shade from fast-growing plants like plantains, their leaves burn and turn brown at the edges.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ amɛná hulu la babaoo ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baashã ni amɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ.

english: Why do I see small holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and caterpillars inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. The young caterpillars feed on the growing center of the leaves, creating ragged holes and weakening the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kplukai bibii yeɔ baai ni miida lɛ ateŋ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ bu ni etse lɛ baa ni ehaa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why are white powdery spots appearing on my pepper plant leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛŋ ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a fungal infection that develops in warm, humid weather. It covers the leaves and prevents them from capturing sunlight to make food for the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji powder mli ŋmei. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni baa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ehaa baa lɛ nɔ ni etsĩɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkamɔ hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji ni yaa shɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to produce energy. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes helps the leaves capture maximum sunlight to grow bigger yams underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant multiple maize seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Ha dumɔwui lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli.

english: Seeds planted too close together will compete against each other for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks with small or missing cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo ni bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow much slower even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital nutrients and fertilizers directly from the soil before your main crops can absorb them, effectively starving your crops despite getting enough rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani onibii titrii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why does my farmland produce good harvests for the first two years but smaller yields after that?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli shi ebaa shi yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every harvest removes essential nutrients from the dirt. Without adding organic compost, animal manure, or proper fertilizer back into the soil, the land becomes exhausted over time.
ga: Nikpamɔ fɛɛ kpamɔ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ muji lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa bɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up heavily in the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are receiving too much water during the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-tomato tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Too much water suffocates plant roots by pushing out air from the soil. When this happens, tomato leaves turn pale yellow and droop downwards without feeling dry or crisp.
ga: Nu babaoo haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ enɛ ba lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ni amɛnuuu he akɛ amɛgbi loo amɛhe ejɔ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for green growth. It can also happen when heavy rainfall washes nutrients deep into the soil where roots cannot reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and dying while still small on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in humid, damp conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to flow through your farm, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oookpa ni ojie jwɛi lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes to appear all over the leaves of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni haa bu bibioo lɛ feɔ? Ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Insects like caterpillars or beetles are feeding on the leaves. When leaves get damaged, the plant loses its energy source, making it hard to flower and produce fruit.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii miiye baai lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baafite ehewalɛ jɛɛhe lɛ. Ehaa ewaa akɛ ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there seems to be enough space in my farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji etamɔ nɔ ni he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Even if space looks open, weeds act like extra mouths competing for the same food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ jɛmɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ Shi jwɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ amɛyɛ daaŋ krɛdɛɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa niyenii kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ.

english: Why should I wait to apply fertilizer until after the ground receives rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he kɛyashi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops absorb nutrients through water. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the crop roots or waste the fertilizer because the roots cannot drink dry nutrients.
ga: Tsei tsɔɔ nu mli amɛmɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu niyenii ni egbi lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or missing nutrients. The plant drops flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over so easily when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni haa mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests like nematodes or soft rot from soggy soil. Weakened roots lose their hold in the earth, causing the heavy plant to fall.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo sũ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. ni haa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground if I leave them buried too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji mishi amɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, excessive soil moisture and bacteria begin breaking down the tubers. Harvesting on time prevents water buildup and rot from ruining the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baabɔi ŋmei lɛ mligbalamɔ. Nibii ni akpaa yɛ be naa lɛ haaa nu abua naa ni efite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in the soil for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the wet ground prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant grow larger underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if the ground has enough moisture after the early rains for me to start planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ nugbɔ lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔ shishi?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil from a few inches below the surface. If it holds together in a soft, moist ball without water dripping out, the soil has enough moisture for your seeds to germinate.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ fioo ko kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi inchi fioo komɛi. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe ebɔ he ni efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ ni nu ko hooo kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy leaves. Applying compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK will help the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ebaakwɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli.

english: Is it better for my soil if I burn the dry bush before planting, or should I leave it to rot on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaashã tsei bibii ni egbi dani adu loo ehi akɛ aaaha amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Burning clears the land fast, but it destroys beneficial soil life and burns away good organic matter. Leaving cleared plant material to decompose naturally (mulching) keeps the soil moist, prevents erosion, and creates free natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shãa baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ oya. Shi efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni eshãa nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Tso mli nibii ni ajie lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni efeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why does my land yield less crop every year if I keep planting maize in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil and stops pests from building up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when I cut down all the big trees around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants naturally thrive under partial shade. High direct sunlight and heat stress cocoa trees, causing them to drop flowers and produce fewer pods. Leaving scattered canopy trees keeps the air cool and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Cocoa tsei lɛ naa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni egbɛ eshwã lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rain floods my farm for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for too long, oxygen is blocked, allowing fungal rot to attack the tubers. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Oxygen lɛ baatsi enaa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: If I plant my maize seeds closer together in a row, won't I get a much bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, Ani maná yibii babaoo?

english: Crowding plants forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stalks and small or empty ears. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room and nutrition to grow full, heavy ears.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛtoi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted pepper seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔtɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that quickly steal water, sunlight, and soil food from your delicate seedlings. Clearing weeds early gives your young peppers the best chance to take root and grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ odumɔwui ni waaa lɛ amli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-peppers bibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛwo shishifãi ni amɛdara ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Regular watering and using balanced fertilizer helps the flowers stay on and turn into full fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seed yams at the end of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ oduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee?

english: Yams need continuous soil moisture to develop roots and sprout healthy vines. Planting right before the long dry season sets in causes the seed tubers to dry out and rot in the ground before rainfall returns.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛ shishifãi ni amɛkwɛ̃ wain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ aba lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever strong rain and winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, weak roots and top-heavy fruit stalks. Supporting them with strong wooden props or planting them in groups helps protect them from blowing over during heavy storms.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai tsei ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni wa fi amɛsɛɛ loo okɛ amɛ wo kui amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe koni akashwie amɛ yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure helps the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains too much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water easily. When excess rainwater sits around the roots for too long, it starves them of air and encourages rot-causing fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Enɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee nɔ ni baawo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become extremely hot or when the soil rapidly switches from dry to wet. This stress causes the plant to shed flowers to conserve its own energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli oya. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rainy season fully arrives. Planting too early causes young sprouts to dry up and die when the moisture suddenly stops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu tsei bibii lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ kpa trukaa.

english: How does growing cowpeas together with my maize help my field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the neighboring maize while covering the ground to prevent weed growth.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni ekɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: What is causing the small chewed holes in the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide deep inside the central leaf funnels of young maize plants during the day and feed on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Yams require loose, deep, and soft soil so their tubers can expand downward without hitting hard ground. Mounds also prevent standing water from surrounding the tuber.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsi ehe kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I trim off some of the healthy branches from my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Removing excess foliage allows the plant to direct its energy, food, and water straight into forming bigger and healthier pepper fruits rather than growing more leaves.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ, niyenii, kɛ nu tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe baai krokomɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively absorb water, light, and soil nutrients. When weeds are present, they steal the fertilizer before your crops get a chance to use it.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛmɔɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni jwɛi yɛ Ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in a clearing with direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu la kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the soil dries out too fast. They need temporary shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to shelter them until their canopy develops.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛha amɛhe nɔ ko kɛyashi be mli ni ŋwɛi ŋtayaa ko baaje kpo.

english: Why do dark black spots appear on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain and high humidity create the perfect moist environment for the Black Pod fungal disease to spread. Pruning surrounding branches and clearing weeds allows air to flow through the farm and keep the pods drier.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha blackpod fungal hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni afoɔ Kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ mli ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are holes appearing in the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Holes in maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the plant. Catching them early and applying appropriate natural or chemical controls protects the plant before it is destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ni kɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii loo tsofai ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei ahe dani akpata amɛhiɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and turn small during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants happens when tiny insects like thrips or mites suck the sap from under the leaves, combined with stress from dry soil. Mulching around the base and watering regularly helps the plant recover.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ŋmɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ. kɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ fataa he Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ shishigbɛ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ shi.

english: Why do old farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-abele lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer that feeds nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa niyenii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is running out of nutrients without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori?

english: If your crops start growing very slowly, look pale green instead of dark green, or yield smaller fruits than usual despite getting enough rain, your soil is low on essential nutrients and needs compost or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji onibii je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ blɛoo waa lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo aduawai lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Which way should I push cassava stems into the dirt when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ ofee tɛŋŋ otsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stems should be planted slanting at an angle or buried horizontally with the plant buds pointing upward so roots spread easily and grow into large tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei lɛ ni atsɔ ŋwɛi loo afu amɛ shi ni tso lɛ ŋmei lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei wuji.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak if I don't remove them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, soil moisture, and food; clearing them early ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii, ni ooofɔ amɛhe mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so fast before I can transport them to market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes rot quickly if harvested when fully ripe and soft, or if packed tightly in hot containers without air gaps. Picking them just as they turn slightly reddish-yellow and keeping them cool preserves them longer.
ga: Tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni efee blɛoo. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsɛnsi ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛ́ ajie amɛ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ fioo ni akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from my last maize harvest grow as well as the packaged seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ tamɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ paketi ni mihe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crop varieties lose their yield potential and strength in the second generation, and home-stored seeds can suffer pest damage or moisture decay over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ yibiiwoo kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Ni dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ shia lɛ baanyɛ afite kɛtsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baanyɛ afite yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up when I plant them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. They need partial shade from fast-growing nurse crops like plantain or cassava during their first two years to trap moisture and protect them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient corn needs to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni baai eŋɔli lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvest get smaller every time I plant maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize rapidly drains specific nutrients like nitrogen from the soil every season. Planting it in the same spot continuously exhausts the land and allows corn-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya daa be mli. Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Look closely at the tiny raised buds or nodes along the stem cutting. These buds must point upwards toward the sky like small arrows; planting them upside down makes it very hard for the sprouts and roots to emerge.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nodes lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni woɔ ehe nɔ yɛ tso lɛ fã ni afo lɛ sɛɛ Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ akpɔlɔi bibii. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii kɛ shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso lɛ shishi.

english: Too many suckers fight with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Leaving only one main tree and one or two young suckers ensures the main tree gets enough strength to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain wulu lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ashi tso titri kome kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds and put long bamboo stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni mikɛ ŋmeii kakadaji awo tso nɔ koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight so their leaves can produce food. Raising the leaves off the ground exposes them to sunlight and air, which directs energy downward to grow larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa amɛnɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my groundnut plant bend its yellow flowers down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their pods underground. After the flower is pollinated above ground, it grows a small stem called a peg that naturally burrows into the soil to safely grow the nuts underneath.
ga: Peanut tsei feɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Ebaafee ŋmei bibioo ko. atsɛɔ lɛ pins Enɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛdu ŋmeii yɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to excessive heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollinating insects like bees. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding heavy chemical sprays during flowering allows insects to pollinate the blossoms into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni haa dɔlɛ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Why do I see tiny holes and powdery dirt inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Ni muji ni tamɔ powda lɛ yɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl and eating the tender young leaves. The powdery dirt is their waste; applying an approved insecticide directly into the funnel early will protect the growing point.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii, bibii. Muji ji jwɛi. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu he ni edaa lɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and twisting together into tight bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the tender leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Controlling these sap-sucking insects early with neem oil or targeted sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ ahe nibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akɛ hiɛ fɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Are foreign seed varieties always better than the crop varieties developed here in Ghana?
ga: Ani maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ hi fe tsei srɔtoi ni afee yɛ Ghana biɛ lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Not necessarily. While foreign seeds often promise high yields, locally developed improved varieties are bred specifically to thrive in Ghana's heat and soil, often producing equal or even higher yields while being better suited to local weather.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei pii lɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui woɔ yibii babaoo shi moŋ, shi akwɛɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛshwere yɛ Ghana latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, amɛwoɔ yibii ni tamɔ amɛhe loo nɔ ni fe nakai yɛ be mli ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi.

english: Why do some farmers choose local seed varieties over foreign ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi halaa maŋ lɛ mli dumɔwui srɔtoi fe maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Local varieties developed by agricultural researchers in Ghana are tailored to local growing conditions, meaning they can survive native pests and drought better while delivering very high harvests.
ga: Akɛ akutsoŋbii srɔtoi ni okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ fee lɛ kpãa gbee shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hɔmɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ yibii babaoo waa.

english: Is it safe for me to buy crop seeds that come from overseas?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mahe dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ?

english: Overseas seeds can work, but they are bred for different weather and soil types. Without the right inputs and climate, they may not reach their promised yield, whereas tested local seeds give more reliable results.
ga: Maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ atsu nii. Shi afɔɔ amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni ja ni haa afeɔ nii kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi bɛ lɛ, ekolɛ Dumɔwui lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ nɔ ni awo he shi lɛ he. Yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋ dumɔwui ni aka amɛ akwɛ lɛ haa yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ babaoo baa.

english: How do I measure the yield of my crop to know if my farm is doing well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe koni male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ miiya nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yield is usually measured by calculating the weight of your harvest—such as kilograms or tons—over a specific size of land, like a hectare or acre. This allows you to easily compare how well different seeds perform.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, abuɔ yibiiwoo lɛ he akɔntaa kɛtsɔ onikpamɔ lɛ tsiimɔ, tamɔ kilogram loo tɔn nɔ. yɛ he ko ni dalɛ pɔtɛɛ ko yɔɔ nɔ, tamɔ hectare loo acre Enɛ haa okɛ bɔ ni dumɔwui srɔtoi tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ toɔ he. mlɛo

english: What does it mean when an officer says a crop gives a certain number of tons per hectare?
ga: Mɛni amɛtsɔɔ kɛji onukpai kɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko woɔ yibii tɔni yɛ hectare kome mli?

english: A hectare is a standard measure of land size (about two and a half acres). Tons per hectare simply tells you the total weight of crops you can harvest from that specific area of land.
ga: Hectare ji nɔ ni akɛsusuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ he (aaafee acre enyɔ kɛ fã). Tɔn ni yɔɔ hectare kome mli lɛ tsɔɔ bo ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okpa kɛjɛ nakai he pɔtɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ kɛkɛ.

english: How can I increase the weight of harvest I get from my plot of land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmaa lɛ mli tsiimɔ ni minine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can increase your total harvest by choosing high-yielding, locally adapted seed varieties, spacing your plants properly, and maintaining good soil nutrients throughout the growing season.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni oooha lɛ nɔ. Shi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. ni ekwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai anɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do some imported crops fail to produce a good harvest in Ghanaian soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ wooo yibii kpakpai yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Imported crops are often designed for cooler or different climates. When planted in Ghana, the high heat, intense sun, and local soil conditions can stress the plant and reduce its final output.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli ejɔ loo shihilɛi srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ Ghana lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulu la ni naa wa, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni eha naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: What makes locally developed crop varieties perform so well in our local farms?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni afee yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔji amli?

english: Local research institutes test and select these crops over many seasons in Ghanaian conditions, ensuring their roots and leaves are built to extract nutrients and moisture efficiently from our local soil.
ga: Nibii amlitaomɔ he ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kaa tsei nɛɛ ekwɛɔ ni ehalaa yɛ bei srɔtoi amli yɛ Ghana shihilɛi amli. Enɛ haa anáa tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛbaai koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ wɔmaŋ shikpɔji lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do different seed types of the same crop produce such different amounts of food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome dumɔwui woɔ niyenii babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds carry genetic traits that dictate how they grow. Some seeds are bred to spend energy growing heavy fruit or grain, while others spend more energy growing tall stalks or leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ fɔmɔ sui ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni amɛ daa. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui komɛi koni akɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai loo dumɔwui ni tsii. yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo tsei loo baai ni kɛlɛ.

english: How can I tell if a crop variety will produce a high harvest before I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ ko baawo yibii babaoo dani madu lɛ?

english: You can look for certified seed recommended by extension officers or local research centers, which come with proven harvest records showing how many kilograms or tons they produce per hectare.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni akutsoŋbii loo niiamlitaomɔ hei lɛ jieɔ yi lɛ. Ekɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he wolo ni ama nɔ mi ni tsɔɔ kilogram loo tɔn enyiɛ ni ajie yɛ hectare kome mli lɛ baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Shade trees act as a natural barrier that cools the surrounding air, reduces water loss from the leaves, and protects the tender young plants from sun damage until they are mature enough to handle full exposure.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ shi ni obu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la fɛɛ.

english: Growing maize in the same spot continuously drains the soil of specific nutrients that maize loves to feed on, leading to weaker crops and lower yields over time. It also allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil season after season.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi sumɔɔ ni eyeɔ lɛ daa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ hu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts together with my maize makes the soil better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko miikɛɛ mi akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means they have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so planting groundnuts feeds the soil and helps your maize grow healthier.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, no hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: What is causing the leaves on my young maize plants to have small holes and look chewed up from the center?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baa lɛ baa? Ni ekwɛɔ ni eshɛreɔ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the leaf funnel of young maize plants. Finding them early and applying safe control measures or targeted pesticides protects the growing point of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ baai amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Ni akɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaatsu nii loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before the fruit even ripens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering or dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji blossom end rot, ni baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot and turn watery if I leave them in the soil during heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ, amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboi ni amɛfeɔ nu lɛ?

english: Excess water in heavy rains fills up the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the cassava roots. Without oxygen, the tubers cannot breathe and quickly begin to rot underground.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes exposes their leaves to more sunlight and air, which allows the plant to produce more energy and feed the tuber underground, resulting in larger, healthier yams.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo ashɛ etso lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I choose the best plantain suckers from my old field to plant in my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala plantain tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for 'sword suckers'—these are young shoots with broad bases and thin, sword-like leaves. They grow faster, produce stronger root systems, and yield healthier plantain bunches than suckers with wide, broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’, ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni shishi lɛ mli kwɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ klante. Amɛ daa oya. Bɔɔ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ofee plantain tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to spread chemical fertilizer so it doesn't just wash away when it rains?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, efɔɔɔ ehe?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist but not flooded, ideally right before a light rain or right after heavy rain stops. Spreading fertilizer right before heavy downpours will wash the nutrients away into nearby streams before the roots can drink them in.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu efooo mli. Esa akɛ awo dani nugbɔ anɛ fioo loo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ekpa sɛɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. dani shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ

english: How does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass help my farm during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛhaa he ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil by preventing the hot sun from evaporating water quickly. It keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from taking over your crop area.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa grow very well on one part of my farm but struggle on another part of the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko mli shi ekɛ naagba miikpe yɛ nakai kpokpaa lɛ nɔŋŋ fã kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality is not the same everywhere, even on the same farm. One area may have rich, deep soil with good water retention, while another area may be worn out, rocky, or missing vital plant nutrients needed for cocoa to grow well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su jeee ekome yɛ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli po Ekolɛ kpokpaa ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni he kroko baanyɛ afee he ko ni efite, tɛi loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni kookoo lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is good for planting cocoa before I put my crops in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Good cocoa soil is usually deep, dark in color, crumbly, and able to hold moisture without becoming waterlogged. If the land is very sandy, clayey, or hard, you will need to prepare and nourish the soil first before planting cocoa.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli kwɔ, eyɛ ediŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni enyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋã, shikpɔŋ sũ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa lɛ, ehe baahia ni osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oha lɛ niyenii dani odu kookoo.

english: Why does the soil on my farm get very hot and dry out quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli dɔɔ waa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Bare soil that is exposed directly to the sun loses its moisture quickly through evaporation. Keeping the soil covered with ground plants or fallen leaves shades the dirt, lowers soil temperature, and keeps moisture trapped for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ lasu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ tsei loo baai ni egbee shi lɛ ni oooha nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni eha muji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ aba shi ni oha ŋmɔtɔ ahi onibii amli.

english: What is a cover crop, and how does it help my farm land?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: A cover crop is a special plant grown mainly to protect and enrich the soil rather than for harvest. It spreads across the ground like a carpet to keep the soil moist, stop weeds from growing, and feed nutrients back into the earth.
ga: Cover crops ji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni aduɔ titri koni akɛbu shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eha efee shweremɔ moŋ fe ni akɛbaakpa nii. Egbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: If I plant cover crops, won't they steal water and food from my main crops?
ga: Kɛ midu nɔ ko ni akɛhaa mihe Ani amɛjuŋ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛŋ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli?

english: Special cover crops are chosen because they work together with your main crops. Instead of stealing food, their leaves and roots actually capture nitrogen from the air and add it into the soil, feeding your main crops.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛhaa nɔ ejaakɛ amɛkɛ otsei titrii lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaaju niyenii Amɛbaai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha otsei titrii lɛ niyenii.

english: How do cover crops stop weeds from taking over my cocoa farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ atsĩ jwɛi anaa koni ekaye mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cover crops grow quickly and form a dense layer of leaves over the ground. This layer blocks sunlight from reaching weed seeds underneath, preventing weeds from sprouting and taking over your farm.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If my farm land is tired and no longer producing good crops, what can I do to fix it?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fite ni ewooo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai dɔŋŋ hu? Mɛni ma nyɛ ma pee kɛ ma pee?

english: Tired land needs organic matter and nutrients restored. You can fix poor land by planting nitrogen-rich cover crops, letting special soil-building leaves rot into the ground, or applying natural manure to rebuild the soil's strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ he miihia ni aku sɛɛ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛi awo mli ekoŋŋ. Obaanyɛ osaa hei ni ehiii lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Ha baai krɛdɛɛi ni haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ kɛboteɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii ni okɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do special leaves from plants turn into food for my crops?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe baai krɛdɛɛi bafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When leaves fall or are cut onto the soil, soil bugs and moisture break them down. As these leaves decay, they turn into dark organic matter that releases essential plant food like nitrogen back into the dirt.
ga: Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi loo afo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baafite. Kɛji nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ fite lɛ Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ nibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni jieɔ tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does it take so long for young cocoa plants to start growing strong after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani cacao tsei bibii jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa waa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term tree crop that spends its early period building root systems underground before growing fast above ground. It takes time for young cocoa roots to settle into the soil and begin absorbing nutrients properly.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ko ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ toɔ eshishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani edaa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cocoa shishifãi bibii lɛ he miihia be fioo dani amɛbote sũ lɛ mli ni amɛje niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How long does it take to improve bad soil so that crops can start growing well again?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani anyɛɔ asaa shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ koni tsei anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Improving bad soil is a gradual process that usually takes one or two farming seasons. By using soil-improving leaves and cover crops, you will slowly see the dirt become darker, softer, and richer over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ni aaasaa lɛ ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ fiofio. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ shweremɔ be kome loo enyɔ. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsakemɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, fiofio lɛ obaana akɛ muji lɛ miifee duŋ, efee blɛoo, ni efee nii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and turn yellow when there are no bigger shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from larger trees or plantains because direct heat burns their leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil before their roots are fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing very tall with thin stems but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together or under a very thick shade canopy, they stretch upward searching for sunlight instead of spending energy to produce pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo shishi Yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛtao hulu la.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the main plant for nutrients and water in the soil, which reduces the size and weight of the main plantain bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha plantain tso titri lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii aba shi.

english: Staking holds the leaves up to catch direct sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more food and build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni amɛma ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Does planting cassava stems at a slant work better than planting them straight down into the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant helps tubers grow closer to the surface where the soil is softer, making them easier to harvest while maintaining strong root growth.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ lolo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, causing the plant to move its remaining nutrients up to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize help my maize grow better without extra fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ dani awoɔ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ ŋmei kroko fataaa he lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, creating a natural nutrient supply for the next crop planted in that spot.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai he lɛ baa.
