english: Why do the roots of my crops rot when I plant them in low waterlogged areas during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi fiteɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hei ni nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off air to the roots, causing them to drown, decay, and fail to transport food to the rest of the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aya tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without forming any fruit during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei ni wooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato flowers, preventing proper pollination and forcing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha tomato fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni haoɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. kɛ tsei ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and stopping the crop from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni ehaa tso lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by small pests like aphids or mites feeding on the plant and spreading viruses that stunt overall growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet and humid shade. Pruning unnecessary branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shĩa mli hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Niji ni he ehiaaa ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over during winds when they start carrying heavy fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa beni ebɔi yibii ni tsii womɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can be weakened by soil pests like nematodes or root borers. Using a strong wooden prop or bamboo stake to support the stem carrying the bunch prevents the plant from snapping or uprooting.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ afee amɛ mlɛo. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa tsu nii kɛfi tsei akutsei ni woɔ ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akakumɔ loo eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure near the roots will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is maturing when the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking and the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off naturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miida beni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight to make food. Keeping the leaves lifted off the damp ground also protects them from leaf diseases and encourages bigger tubers to grow underneath.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akɛ sweet potato awo tso nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa kɛha nihoomɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa, ni ehaa bulbs wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and soft before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni eyɛ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually because of irregular soil moisture. Mulching your farm and watering evenly helps the plant absorb calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking into small shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiifee bibii bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is mostly caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from the leaves. Spraying early with organic solutions like neem oil or approved pest controls stops these insects and lets new leaves grow normally.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. Akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔɔ nɔ mra. Ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ kpaa nitsumɔ ni ehaa baai heei kwɛ̃ɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Flower drop is often caused by tiny pests called flower thrips or by giving the soil too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on leaves instead of fruit. Protecting flowers with organic or recommended sprays at early bloom ensures pods develop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɔfɔi thrips. aloo kɛtsɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ anɔ moŋ fe aduawai lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ buɔ he kɛ́ amɛmiifɔlɔ mra lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are there small holes chewed all over my cabbage leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are created by caterpillars like the diamondback moth larva. Checking under the leaves regularly and removing the caterpillars or using natural biopesticides stops them before they ruin the cabbage head.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ kaabeji baai amli lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei ŋmeii amli. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ daa ni ojie ŋmeii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ loo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite kaabe yitso lɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the heavy rain to pass before applying fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ dani mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer right before heavy downpours causes the rainwater to wash the nutrients away before the plant roots can take them in. Applying it when the soil is moist after a moderate rain allows the roots to absorb maximum nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, no haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that scorch easily under intense direct sunlight. They require partial shade from companion crops like plantains or shade trees to retain moisture and survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ nanemɛi tsei tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines are natural climbing plants that need to spread their leaves upward to catch maximum sunlight for tuber growth. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji tsei ni kwɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni bulbs lɛ adara. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a common sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize requires a lot of nitrogen to grow, and when the soil lacks it, the plant pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my pepper seeds too close to each other in the same bed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the same water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to weak, stunted plants with very few peppers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baawuu amɛhe koni amɛná nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in that soil over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any fruit starts growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or sudden dry spells. The plant drops flowers to save its energy and water for basic survival.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil underground if heavy rains stay on the farm for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excess water fills all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing them to rot under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: How does the dry Harmattan wind affect my crops, and how can I protect them?
ga: Te Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Harmattan winds pull moisture out of the leaves and soil very quickly, causing plants to wilt. Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) helps trap moisture in the root zone.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ oya. haa tsei lɛ gboɔ Mulching ni akɛbaabɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) koni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil and weather, allowing them to absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why am I finding small ragged holes in my corn leaves and tiny insects hidden inside the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Kplukai bibii yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ amli. Akɛtee tso lɛ shishi?

english: These holes are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which burrow into the central shoot of young maize plants to feed on the tender leaf tissues before they unfurl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baa bibii lɛ amli fãji lɛ dani amɛje kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa.

english: How long will my coconut trees take to start bearing fruit after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso lɛ baaje yibii womɔ shishi beni midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved hybrid coconut varieties usually start bearing fruit within 3 to 4 years, while traditional local varieties take about 6 to 7 years. Keeping the area around the base clear of weeds and applying proper fertilizer during early growth helps them mature on time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii srɔtoi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7. He ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛ́ jwɛi akafee shishitoo mlai lɛ, ni awo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara yɛ be naa.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing so slowly and not flowering yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ miida blɛoo ni efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lolo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to flower and fruit. Slow growth is often caused by too much direct harsh sunlight, poor soil nutrients, or weed competition, which can be fixed by providing temporary shade crops like plantains and applying fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii. Bei pii lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo ji nɔ ni kɛ dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo baa. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo jwɛi akaŋshii Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaaha lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I plant coconut trees and cocoa trees on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛ kakao tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa and coconut can be grown together in a mixed farm setup. Tall coconut trees provide partial shade that benefits cocoa trees, but you must space the coconuts wide enough so they do not block all light or fight for soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu kookoo kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔji ni akɛfutu mli lɛ amli. Kokoo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be fioo ko, ni enɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei lɛ. Shi ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmei lɛ awo he ko ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa bɔni afee ni ekatsi la lɛ fɛɛ naa loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akashi akaŋ koni ená niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: What distance should I leave between coconut trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe abɔ he tɛŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Coconut trees should generally be planted about 7.5 to 9 meters apart from each other. Proper spacing ensures their wide fronds do not overlap too much, allowing enough air and sunlight for good fruit production.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei aaafee mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 9 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ nɛɛ haa baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ efoŋ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha aduawai kpakpai baa.

english: What causes my coconut leaves to turn yellow and stop producing well?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa nibii kpakpai feemɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves in coconuts are usually a sign of nutrient deficiency—specifically nitrogen or potassium—or waterlogging in the soil. Applying well-rotted manure or balanced fertilizer and ensuring proper drainage usually restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Titri lɛ, nitrogen loo potasium. aloo nu ekã shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akwɛɔ koni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi dani eda lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during rainy seasons. Pruning extra shade tree branches, harvesting regularly, and applying approved fungicides will protect the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni eha hulutsoo babaoo aba daa kpamɔ Ni kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I make sure my cocoa farm stays healthy if I have to leave the village for a few months?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ? Kɛ ehe bahia ni mashi akrowa lɛ mli nyɔji fioo komɛi

english: Before traveling, clear major weeds, mulch around tree bases to keep the soil moist, and hire or assign a trustworthy caretaker to check for pest outbreaks and harvest ripe pods so they do not rot on the trees.
ga: Dani obaafã gbɛ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi titrii lɛ. Gbalamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle tso lɛ shishi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛ loo aha mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai ebote tsei lɛ amli ni amɛkpa tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ koni amɛkafite.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is suitable for planting cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ?

english: Cocoa grows best in deep, fertile, reddish-brown topsoil that retains moisture without becoming waterlogged. If the soil is very sandy, shallow, or rocky, cocoa roots will struggle to thrive.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋã, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo tɛi babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaawa akɛ kookoo shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Should I plant local coconut seeds or get hybrid coconut varieties from the agriculture office?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmei dumɔwui yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ loo mahe ŋmei srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmei kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Hybrid coconut varieties are generally better because they grow shorter, fruit much faster (3–4 years), and yield more nuts per tree compared to traditional local varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni akɛfee ŋmeii lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa kuku. Amɛwoɔ yibii oya kwraa (afii 3-4) ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso kome mli kɛ akɛto maŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ ahe.

english: How should I prepare my cleared bush land before transplanting cocoa seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mi-bush he ni ajie lɛ dani mawo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Clear weeds without burning all field organic matter, leave some medium shade trees, plant temporary shade crops like plantains first, and dig planting holes early so topsoil and compost can settle in them before seedlings arrive.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ ni oshãaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Shi tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fioo. Dumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, klɛŋklɛŋ. ni otsa dumɔ bu mra Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why should I plant cassava and plantain together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii afee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava and plantain together makes good use of space and farm labor. Plantains grow taller to provide shade and produce early, while cassava grows lower and provides a steady food crop underground that you can harvest when needed.
ga: Kasava kɛ plantain ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa akɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ nitsumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Plantains baakwɛ̃ babaoo koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Shi ŋmei lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ fioo ni eji niyenii tso ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni obaanyɛ okpa kɛ ehe miihia.

english: What quick-growing food crops can I plant to feed my family while waiting for my long-term crops to produce?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miweku lɛ niyenii yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ aba?

english: Planting short-duration crops like maize, leafy vegetables, or legumes alongside your main crops provides immediate food and income within three to four months, without disturbing the long-term crops.
ga: Be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele, aduawai ni yɔɔ baai, loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi. Ebaaha niyenii kɛ shika amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. ni egbaaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ anaa

english: Is it better to plant only one type of crop on my farm or mix different food crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo niyenii srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ nii?

english: Mixing crops like plantain, cassava, and legumes protects your farm against total failure if bad weather or pests affect one specific crop, while also keeping the soil healthier.
ga: Nibii tamɔ plantains, cassava, kɛ legumes ni okɛfutuɔ lɛ buɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ kwraa he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ná tso pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ hewalɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves naturally during dry periods to save water and protect their roots. As long as the stems stay green, the plant is still alive and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli lɛ Tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Can I leave my cassava roots in the soil for a long time after they are mature?
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, ani abaanyɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, cassava acts as a living storage bank underground. You can leave the roots in the soil for several months until you are ready to harvest and eat them, though leaving them too long can make them woody.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsuɔ nii akɛ shikatoohe kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Obaanyɛ oshi shishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo kɛyashi obaafee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni oye. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ po lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ afee tsei.

english: How do I ensure my plantain trees grow big bunches of fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mi-plantain lɛ baawo aduawai babaoo?

english: Plantains need moist soil rich in organic matter and proper sunlight. Removing extra shoots (suckers) so that only two or three stalks remain on one plant allows all the strength to go into producing large fruit bunches.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia plantains. Ajieɔ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ahi tso kome nɔ. Ebaaha hewalɛ fɛɛ ni baaha ewo yibii wuji lɛ baaha.

english: Why do small new plantain shoots keep growing around my main plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii heei shwieɔ No hewɔ lɛ edaa yɛ mitso wulu lɛ he

english: Plantain plants produce new shoots called suckers to reproduce naturally. You should cut away the weaker suckers and leave only the strongest one so they don't steal water and nutrients from the main fruiting tree.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ woɔ ŋmeii heei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii koni amɛfɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Esa akɛ ofolɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni oshi tsei ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ bɔni afee ni okaju nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ tso titri ni woɔ yibii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when heavy winds and rain come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Mounding rich soil high around the base of the stem and supporting the fruit stalk with a wooden prop will keep them standing strong.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. cause a lot weight Pile shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ kɛbɔle he Akɛ tsei fiɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ aduawai lɛ ahe. Ebaaha amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for water, soil food, and sunlight. Giving each crop proper spacing ensures strong stems and healthy yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my soil produce better crops after I leave it to rest for a season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai beni miha ejɔɔ ehe be ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest (fallowing) allows wild plants to decay and rebuild nutrients naturally in the ground, making the soil rich and energetic again for your future crop yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ashiɔ koni ekɛjɔɔ ehe (tilling) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa koo mli tsei lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooofee lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young rice plants turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in young rice leaves is usually a sign that the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or that the field is too dry. Nitrogen helps the plant build food and stay green, so adding balanced fertilizer or improving water flow helps them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai bibii ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa wo tso lɛ mli loo aha nu lɛ ho jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my rice crop grow very tall and leafy but produces very few grain heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ dumɔwui ayitsei fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: When rice gets too much nitrogen fertilizer without enough phosphorus and potassium, it puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leaves instead of forming grains. Balanced plant nutrition ensures the crop shifts energy into grain production.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo ŋmã mli ni phosphorus kɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmãa shishifãi kɛ baai ni kɛlɛ moŋ fe ni eeefee dumɔwui. Tso mli niyenii ni ja lɛ haa tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ amɛwoɔ ŋmaa feemɔ mli.

english: Why do birds suddenly start flocking to my rice field just when the stalks look full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi miibɔi amɛhe buamɔ trukaa yɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ani tso lɛ eyi obɔ?

english: During the 'milky stage' of rice development, the young grains are filled with a soft, sweet liquid starch. Birds are attracted to this stage because the grains are easy to eat and highly nutritious before they harden.
ga: Yɛ ‘milk stage’ ni ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ, dumɔwui bibii lɛ eyi kɛ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ ni ŋɔɔ. Bei pii lɛ, okpoi sumɔɔ nɛkɛ shihilɛ nɛɛ ejaakɛ ŋmaa lɛ yeli waaa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli dani ewaa.

english: Why does rice grow better when there is standing water in the field compared to crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ to ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their roots and stems that allow them to transport oxygen under water. Standing water also acts as a natural barrier to prevent weeds from taking over the field.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he ko krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛyaa nu shishi. Nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ.

english: What happens if I sow my rice seeds too close together in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Planting rice seeds too closely causes the individual plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stems that easily fall over during heavy rains and produce smaller grain heads.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso fɛɛ tso nɔ koni ekɛ ehe awo hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do some farmers raise rice seedlings in a small nursery bed before transplanting them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔji bibii amli dani amɛduɔ amɛwoɔ ŋmɔji wuji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Starting rice in a nursery gives young plants a protected environment to grow strong roots before moving them. Transplanting healthy seedlings gives them a head start against weeds in the main field and ensures uniform plant spacing.
ga: Kɛ́ aje ŋmãa tsei ashishi yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ náa he ko ni abuɔ he koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa dani ajie amɛ kɛya he kroko. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa sɛɛnamɔ fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my rice plants after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe mi ŋmã tsei lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weed seeds are naturally hardy and adapted to quickly grab nutrients and water from the soil after rains. Early weeding gives your young rice crop the space and nutrients it needs to establish before weeds choke it out.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha o-rice bibioo lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛto shi dani jwɛi lɛ agbe lɛ.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grain heads turn from green to a golden-yellow color and the lower grains feel hard. Waiting too long causes grains to shatter onto the ground, while harvesting too early leads to broken grains.
ga: Omɔ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli mli kɛtee shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli. ni shishigbɛ dumɔwui lɛ baanu he akɛ amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ. yɛ be mli ni kpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ baaha ŋmaa lɛ akumɔ.

english: Why does my harvested rice spoil or get moldy quickly after I put it into bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ loo efoɔ oya kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested rice retains moisture inside the grain. If the grains are bagged without being thoroughly dried in the sun, the trapped moisture causes mold to grow and heat to build up, spoiling the stored crop.
ga: Omɔ ni akpa ehee lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ abɔle ŋmaa lɛ he ni hulu lɛ egbiko lɛ, Trapped moisture haa ŋmɔtɔ shwereɔ ni dɔlɛ hu baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato lɛ afitemɔ.

english: Why do some local Ghanaian rice varieties take longer to mature than the modern improved seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Ghana ŋmãa henɔi komɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ fe ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Traditional rice varieties are naturally wired to respond to seasonal changes in daylight, taking four to five months to mature. Improved varieties are bred to grow faster—often maturing in three to four months—so farmers can harvest earlier and avoid dry spells.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmãa henɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa waya koni amɛtsu be mli tsakemɔi ahe nii yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Eheɔ nyɔji ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani eshɛɔ. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ koni amɛdara oya—bei pii lɛ, amɛdaraa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli—no hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi lɛ baanyɛ akpa nii mra ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo bei ahe.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔma gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep downwards inside the soil. Making soft, high mounds gives the yam root room to spread easily without hitting hard ground, while also keeping excess rainwater from drowning the crop.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Gɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato shishifã lɛ hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ naa koni ekabote ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why does my farmland produce less corn every year when I plant on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Corn is a heavy feeder that quickly drains nitrogen and nutrients from the earth. Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts the soil; rotating corn with beans or cowpeas helps restore vital nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ji niyenii agbo ko ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ooodu shii abɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔ Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil because they need air to breathe. When water sits around the roots for too long without draining, rot-causing fungi thrive and ruin the harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔɔɔ. Fungi ni fiteɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear away all the big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and shielding young cocoa until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually mean the plant is starving for nitrogen, which gives leaves their green color. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry spell stress. The plant aborts its blossoms to save energy and water until moisture conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ he haomɔ he. Tsei baafo fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛyashi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when they start carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow, fibrous roots that do not reach deep into the soil. As the fruit bunch grows heavy, strong winds easily pull the root system out of the ground unless supported with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni tamɔ fiber ni eyaaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ dara waa Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. ja akɛ tso nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating holes right in the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi-babi corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, an insect pest that hides inside the tight center leaves (whorl) of corn plants to feed on new growth before emerging.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai (rings) ni mli wa lɛ amli koni eye ŋmãa tsei heei ni eda lɛ dani eje kpo.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early prevents the virus from spreading throughout your plot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Ebaatsi helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa okpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa feɔ ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly over a year. Planting them together maximizes field space and provides two harvests from the same plot.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmã daa blɛoo yɛ afi kome mli. Dumɔ ni adu yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ aba kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting early while they are still stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ mra beni miyɔɔ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Yams naturally break dormancy and begin to sprout after a few months depending on heat and light exposure. Storing your harvested yams in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn off the ground helps keep them dormant longer so they stay fresh for market.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 2-3 sɛɛ, ni enɛ damɔ dɔlɛ kɛ la nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ to ŋmeii atsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kponɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ, ni ebaaha amɛfee ehee kɛha jara.

english: Why are the roots of my yam tubers turning soft and rotting underground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Underground yam rot is usually caused by soil fungi and microscopic worms (nematodes) entering wounded tubers, especially in waterlogged soils. Planting on raised mounds or ridges with good drainage and using healthy seed yams prevents rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ baa. (Nematodes) lɛ boteɔ ŋmeii ni epila lɛ amli, titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ akɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ehaaa amɛfite.

english: Why do some of my harvested cassava tubers taste bitter while others from the same farm taste sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi ŋɔɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi komɛi ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally produce bitter compounds when stressed by heat, dry weather, or poor soil nutrients. Different cassava varieties also carry different levels of bitterness, so planting improved sweet varieties and keeping soil rich reduces bitterness.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ jieɔ nibii ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛji akɛ amɛwo dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo niyenii ni ehiii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kasava henɔi srɔtoi Ayɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha ŋmɔlɔ aba shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs heavily to grow. Applying poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growth period will turn the leaves green and restore growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo Kɛji akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmãa loo nitrogen ŋmãa wo mli mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ebaaha amɛdara ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes into the fresh leaves inside the center stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ baa hee ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing tip of the plant. Applying recommended biological or chemical treatments early in the morning when the caterpillars feed will protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii leebi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Can I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant in the next rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid maize will produce weaker plants with lower yields in the next season because hybrid vigor only lasts for one crop cycle. Purchasing fresh certified hybrid seeds each planting season ensures high yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji akɛ, hybrid vigor lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli shikome pɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofa ebɔ he ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging small on the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkã shi bibii lolo lɛ? Yɛ tso ko shishi?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during heavy rains and deep shade. Pruning overhead trees to allow sunlight into the farm and removing infected small pods helps protect healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ afolɔ koni hulu la abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajie ŋmeii bibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and tear apart during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbalaɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves tear and dry out easily because the plant loses water quickly through its large leaves during high winds and drought. Placing thick mulch around the base of the plant traps soil moisture and keeps the plant healthy through dry spells.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbáa ni amɛgbiɔ oya ejaakɛ tso lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai wuji anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Thick mulching Yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ, emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress or lack sufficient water in the soil. Watering your plants regularly and spreading dry grass or leaves around the root base as mulch keeps the roots cool and helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛkɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpe. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ mli daa ni okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi afɔ shishigbɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds develop tiny holes and turn to dust after a few weeks in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ sũ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni akɛto lɛ sɛɛ

english: Cowpea weevils lay tiny eggs on seeds during harvest, and their larvae eat the seeds from the inside out while in storage. Drying your beans thoroughly under the sun and storing them in airtight containers stops the insects from multiplying.
ga: Cowpea ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ kpamɔ be mli Ni amɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo nɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-beans lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akafɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This makes the stalks grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller cobs or no fruit at all.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ feɔ bibioo loo ebɛ hewalɛ ko kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the tall trees from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees like plantains or broadleaf forest trees creates a cool microclimate that protects young cocoa roots and leaves from scorching heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains loo broadleaf bushes lɛ feɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni buɔ shishifãi kɛ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from rotting if transport to the main market is delayed?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ naa koni ekafite kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛmajeɔ jarayelihe wulu lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to heat, direct sunlight, or wet ground. You can keep them fresh longer by building a traditional raised yam barn in the shade with good air circulation to keep the air cool and dry around the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ, hulu la tɛ̃ɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Obaanyɛ oha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛtsɔ kusum naa sweet potato ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tsɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle Tubers lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni egbi.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava roots when I plant cassava on the exact same spot three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome afii etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy-feeds on specific nutrients in the dirt. Planting it continuously on the same land exhausts those soil nutrients, leaving the soil hungry and unable to support large root development unless you rotate crops or fallow the land.
ga: Cassava yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enyɛɛɛ eye ebua shishifãi wuji ni baa lɛ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo otsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look droopy in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to save water and protect themselves when the afternoon heat is too high. As long as the soil has moisture, the leaves will usually bounce back once the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Baai lɛ hu sumɔɔ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba kɛji gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: Why do tiny beetles start eating holes into my stored cowpeas after only a few weeks in the shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ bɔi mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ yeli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni amɛhi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: These beetles, called bruchid weevils, often lay microscopic eggs on the pods while still in the field. To stop them from multiplying and destroying stored beans, dry the seeds thoroughly and store them in airtight containers or hermetic bags.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ bruchid weevils lɛ fɔɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Bɔni afee ni amɛkpa ŋmeii ni ato lɛ babaoo ni amɛfite lɛ Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum bag mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate the blooms. Regular watering and keeping the soil cool with mulch helps the plant hold its flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plants turning yellow at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei ni midu lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips are a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and energy. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the crop regain its healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my newly planted plantain suckers rot in the soil before sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei ni midu ehee lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers can rot if the soil stays waterlogged, if the planting hole lacks proper drainage, or if the original sucker was infected with pests like root nematodes. Planting clean suckers in well-drained soil prevents decay.
ga: Plantain suckers baanyɛ afite kɛji nu tee nɔ ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ dumɔ bu lɛ bɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Aloo kɛji akɛ shishijee sucker lɛ etsɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tamɔ root nematodes. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni he tse yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbo.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tough plants that have adapted to quickly capture water and nutrients from poor soil. They sprout faster than cultivated crops to establish early control over the field, which is why early weed clearing is necessary.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ oya. Amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe tsei ni adu bɔni afee ni anyɛ akudɔ amɛ mra yɛ jɛmɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia

english: How do I know the best time of the year to start planting cocoa on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi kookoo dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa seedlings grow best when planted at the start of the major rainy season, usually between April and June in Ghana, so their roots can establish deep in the ground before the dry season comes.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛ June teŋ yɛ Ghana, no hewɔ lɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishifãi baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɔ̃ɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba.

english: How many years does a new cocoa tree take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, provided they get enough shade, water, and protection from weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ cocoa hybrids ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ jwɛi ahebuu ni sa.

english: Is it fine to plant cocoa trees on a hill, and how do I stop heavy rain from washing away my soil?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni ja akɛ aaadu kookoo tsei yɛ gɔji anɔ? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, cocoa grows well on hills, but rain can wash away topsoil. You can protect your farm by planting along contour lines across the slope and making small soil barriers to trap water and nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gɔji anɔ. Shi nugbɔ baanyɛ ahoo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni ooodu yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. ni amɛma shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛtsii nii bibioo ko Koni amɛmɔmɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: How does farming on a steep slope affect the amount of water my cocoa trees receive?
ga: Te okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ saa nu abɔ ni mi-kokoo tsei lɛ náa lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Rainwater flows quickly down steep slopes instead of soaking into the ground. Digging small ditches or planting cover crops helps slow down the water so the soil absorbs enough for the tree roots.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛyaa ŋshɔ lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ bibioo ko ni aaafo Aloo tsei ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ adumɔ koni eye ebua ni nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do crops grow better in some parts of my land than in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fãi komɛi anɔ fe hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil quality, moisture levels, and sunlight vary across a farm. Lower ground usually holds more moisture and organic matter, while higher or rocky ground dries out faster and has fewer nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, hulutsoo kɛ hulu la lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ shishi sumɔɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves turn brown mainly due to harsh direct sunlight, lack of water during dry spells, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Temporary shade plants can protect them.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ tsɔɔ asasu, titri lɛ yɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ hewɔ. Nu ni bɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pollen, tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ amli baa lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe.

english: Why should I prune my cocoa trees, and when is the best time to do it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kokoo tso lɛ? Ni mɛɛ be esa akɛ ofolɔ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overgrown branches so the tree can send its strength directly into making healthy pods. It is best done just before the main rainy season starts.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni mli wa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofee enɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds from around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, nutrients, and sunlight that your cocoa tree needs to thrive. Clearing them also keeps away insects and diseases that hide in thick grass.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ekɛtsiɔ kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ jwɛi ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ anaa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees need extra fertilizer to thrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni ekwɛ̃?

english: If your cocoa trees have pale yellow leaves, grow very slowly, or produce few flowers, the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen and potassium, showing they need fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, edaa blɛoo waa, loo fɔfɔi fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Etsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize on the same field with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: You can plant food crops together with young cocoa for the first year or two, but keep heavy feeders like cassava at a distance so they do not block sunlight or steal nutrients from the cocoa trees.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo bibii adu niyenii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi loo afii enyɔ lɛ mli. Shi ha tsei ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmei lɛ ahi he ko ni kɛ bo teŋ jɛkɛ koni amɛkatsi hulu lɛ naa loo amɛkaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I use netting over my vegetable farm instead of letting the crops grow freely in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋshɔŋlooi aha mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mahã tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Netting protects delicate crops like tomatoes and peppers from harsh sunlight, heavy rain, and destructive pests. It creates a controlled environment where plants waste less energy surviving weather damage and put more energy into producing high-quality fruit.
ga: Netting yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ pepper he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ fioo koni amɛjo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa foi. ni akɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does growing crops inside an enclosed net structure change how much water my plants need?
ga: Ani tsei ni akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ trellis structure ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ biɔ nu babaoo kɛha mi tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, crops inside enclosed net structures usually lose less water to evaporation because hot winds and direct heat are reduced. This means the soil stays moist longer, so the plants often require less frequent watering than those in open fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋshɔŋlooi ni agbe naa lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ nu fioo ni amɛfiteɔ kɛyaa lasu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei biɔ nu fioo fe tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ.

english: If I build a net enclosure for my crops, will it prevent all crop diseases?
ga: Kɛji mima ŋshɔŋloo ni mikɛbaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ Ani ebaatsi tsei ahe helai fɛɛ anaa?

english: Net structures keep out large insects that carry viruses and protect leaves from heavy rain damage, but they do not stop fungal or soil-borne diseases. You still need good soil management, clean seeds, and proper ventilation inside the enclosure.
ga: Mesh agbo lɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni hiɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite amɛ. Shi amɛkpaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa hu he miihia bo. ŋmaa ni he tse kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ mli

english: Can I just leave my crops to find their own nutrients in the soil, or do I always need to add manure or fertilizer?
ga: Ani manyɛ mashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwie koni mana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he be fɛɛ be?

english: While wild plants spread out and take years to feed themselves, farm crops grow quickly and absorb nutrients fast. On a farm, especially a large one, the natural soil nutrients quickly run out, so you must feed the plants with manure or fertilizer to maintain good growth.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ koo mli tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛheɔ afii babaoo dani amɛyeɔ nii moŋ, shi Okwaafoi aŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii kpakpai oya yɛ ŋmɔji amli, titri lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli. Adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to deeply till and loosen a large piece of land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni atsu shikpɔji wuji ahe nii ni ajie amɛ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Hard soil prevents plant roots from spreading deep down to search for water and nutrients. Loosening the soil allows roots to breathe, grow strong, and hold the plant firmly so it doesn't fall over during strong winds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ. kwɛ̃ waa ni emɔ tso lɛ mli shiŋŋ Bɔni afee ni ekagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli

english: What happens to pest insects when I clear a large field and plant only one crop on a commercial scale?
ga: Mɛni baa tsɛŋemɔ helai anɔ kɛ́ mijie he ko ni da ni midu tso henɔ kome pɛ kɛha jarayeli?

english: Planting a single crop over a large area creates an easy, endless supply of food for specific pests. Insects multiply much faster on large single-crop farms than on small, mixed fields, making pest protection very important.
ga: Tso kome ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni da nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ naagbee baa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi anɔ. Kplukai fɔɔ oya kwraa yɛ ŋmɔji wuji ni aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ amli fe ŋmɔji bibii ni aduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ he hiaa waa.

english: Why do insect pests attack my farm crops so heavily while wild bushes nearby are untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ waa yɛ be mli ni koo mli jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ kã shi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa he lɛ?

english: Farm crops are bred to be soft, sweet, and easy to digest, which makes them very appealing to insects. Wild bushes have developed tough leaves, bitter tastes, or thorns to protect themselves naturally, so crops need the farmer's protection.
ga: Akwɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ koni efee bɔdɔɔ, ehiɛ ŋɔɔ ni enyɛɔ eyeɔ oya, ni no haa kooloi bibii sumɔɔ amɛ waa. Koo mli tsei bibii lɛ ebɔi baai ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛbuɔ amɛhe he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwaafoi abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: If I plant my maize very close together to fit more crops on my land, how will the plants behave?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ he kome koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ hu? Te tsei lɛ baafee amɛnii amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of yielding more, the plants grow tall, weak, and thin, producing very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo babaoo lɛ, Tsei lɛ daraa, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko nɔ ko.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of big green leaves but fail to produce good fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo yibii kpakpai lɛ?

english: Crops produce excess leaves and few fruits when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade. The plant uses all its energy building leaves instead of shifting its strength into flowering and fruiting.
ga: Tsei woɔ baai babaoo ni amɛwoɔ aduawai fioo kɛji amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo. Tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ feɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ baawo fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo mli.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has some water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lolo moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can suck it up from the soil. Wilting is the plant's way of curling up to expose less leaf surface to the sun to save water until the day cools down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Withering ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ efoɔ ehe koni hulu la akashɛ baa lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Koni akɛ nu ato he kɛyashi ebaajɔ

english: How do I know if my oil palm trees are healthy enough for palm oil buyers to take my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni mɛi ni heɔ oil oil lɛ baanyɛ akpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Healthy palm trees have deep green fronds, strong trunks, and produce full, heavy fruit bunches that turn bright orange-red when ripe. Buyers look for uniform tree growth without signs of pest damage or nutrient deficiency, as this indicates high oil yield.
ga: Palm tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni tsɔɔ tsuru-ŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ tsei ni yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be ni nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa lɛ efite. Ejaakɛ enɛ tsɔɔ mu ni fa babaoo ni anáa.

english: What do company inspectors look for when they come to evaluate my crop farm?
ga: Mɛni nitsumɔhe lɛ akɔntaabuu mlikwɛlɔi taoɔ beni amɛkwɛɔ miŋmɔ ni miduɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Inspectors look at farm cleanliness, proper tree spacing, fruit bunch size, and overall tree health. They check whether your crop is free from heavy weed overgrowth and disease so they can estimate how much high-quality harvest your farm will produce.
ga: Mɛi ni baakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baasusu bɔ ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ha lɛ he. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa, aduawai akui lɛ adalɛ, kɛ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ Amɛkwɛɔ kɛji jwɛi kɛ helai ni naa wa bɛ onibii amli. Enɛ ji koni amɛbu nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni oŋmɔ lɛ baaná lɛ ayibɔ he akɔntaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my oil palm trees turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mu tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Lower leaves naturally age and die off as the tree directs its energy toward new leaves and fruit bunches at the top. Pruning away old, dry leaves helps the tree stay clean and allows more sunlight and airflow around the trunk.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egbi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ he tseɔ, ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ ehe. trunk babaoo

english: Why do my young palm trees produce flowers but no fruit bunches grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm bibioo lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi ebɛ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: Young palm trees produce separate male and female flowers. During their early growth stages, trees often produce mostly male flowers or shed unpollinated blooms until the tree matures at around three years old and has enough nutrients to support heavy fruit.
ga: Palm tsei bibii woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Yɛ dalɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ji hii babaoo loo amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa kwraa yɛ aaafee afii 3 mli ni eyɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua aduawai ni tsii.

english: What causes large holes and chewing damage on the leaves of my young palm trees?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ baa?

english: Chewed leaves are usually caused by pests like the rhinoceros beetle or leaf-eating caterpillars. Clearing rotting wood and farm rubbish from your land prevents these insects from breeding near your young crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ baa ŋmɔmɔ baa. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni egboi kɛ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahe.

english: How far apart should I plant my palm trees so they don't crowd each other?
ga: Te esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkabɔle amɛhe?

english: Oil palm trees should be planted about 9 meters apart in a triangular pattern. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, soil nutrients, and water without overlapping fronds that can block light and reduce yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu mu tsei ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9 yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ hulu la nɔ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Baai ni tsɔɔ amɛhe ni baanyɛ atsĩ la naa ni eha yibiiwoo aba shi lɛ bɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava or maize between my palm trees while the palm trees are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop food crops like maize or cassava during the first two to three years of planting palms. Just make sure to keep the food crops at least one meter away from the palm base so they do not compete for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni okɛduɔ o-palm lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ pɛ akɛ kɛ hoo lɛ, okɛ niyenii tsei lɛ akashɛ onine shishi mita kome he. Bɔni afee ni akaye akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he

english: A palm fruit bunch is ready for harvest when five to ten loose fruits naturally fall from the bunch to the ground. The fruits on the bunch will turn a rich orange-red color, showing that the oil content inside is at its highest.
ga: Palm tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni aduawai enumɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋma ni egbee shi lɛ jɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Yibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli wa. Etsɔɔ akɛ mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni eshɛɔ fe fɛɛ.

english: What kind of fertilizer should I give my palm trees to make the fruit bunches bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ akɛwo ŋmei tsei amli koni amɛyibii akui lɛ afee wuji?

english: Palm trees require a balance of Nitrogen for leaf growth and Potassium for fruit development. Applying a specialized palm fertilizer around the root circle once or twice a year during the rainy season helps produce larger, heavier fruit bunches.
ga: Palm tsei biɔ nitrogen ni sa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ kɛ potassium ni sa kɛha aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Ni akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ he lɛ Bɔɔ shishitoo lɛ he shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli koni eye ebua ni ewo yibii ni tsii ni dara.

english: How many years can an oil palm tree continue to produce good fruits?
ga: Afii enyiɛ mu tso baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kpakpai?

english: An oil palm tree can continuously produce profitable fruit bunches for 25 to 30 years. After this point, the trees become too tall to harvest easily, and their fruit yield naturally starts to decline.
ga: Mu tsei baanyɛ aya nɔ awo aduawai ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he afii 25 kɛyashi 30 yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ. Tsei lɛ baafee shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akpa amɛ oya. Ni yibii ni tsei lɛ woɔ lɛ bɔi shibaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are some new cocoa varieties considered better than the older ones in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo henɔi heei komɛi akɛ amɛhi fe henɔi ni etsɛ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: New hybrid cocoa varieties are specifically bred to yield much more pods, mature faster in about 2 to 3 years instead of 5, and withstand local dry seasons and common diseases far better than older traditional trees.
ga: Atsɔse cocoa hee ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba. Ekwɛɔ mra, yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ afii 5 najiaŋ, ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ babaoo fe blema tsei momoi lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa seedlings too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When trees are planted too closely, they compete for food, water, and sunlight, growing tall and weak instead of producing pods. Dense planting also traps humidity, which speeds up the spread of fungal diseases like Black Pod.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii. Dumɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet conditions. Keeping your farm weed-free and trimming low tree branches helps air circulate, which keeps the pods dry and reduces rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ooofee ni jwɛi akafo mli kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it necessary for me to cut off extra shoots and dry branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ tsei krokomɛi kɛ tsei niji ni egbi lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing parts of the tree that steal nutrients. It opens up the tree so sunlight and air can enter, which encourages more flowers to turn into pods and keeps harmful insects away.
ga: Tso lɛ he nibii ni wooo yibii ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ he nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ. Abaagbele tsei lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo hewalɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛfeee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce more flowers than they can feed. However, excessive flower drop happens when the tree lacks sufficient soil nutrients, experiences water stress, or is attacked by small sucking pests like mirids.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Naagbai ni jɛɔ nu mli haomɔ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm needs fertilizer to help my crops grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: If crop leaves turn light green or yellow, trees look stunted, or yields drop significantly compared to previous seasons, your soil is exhausted and needs nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium to regain its strength.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ. loo nibii ni anáa lɛ eba shi kwraa kɛ akɛto bei ni eho lɛ ahe Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia nitrogen, phosphorus, loo potassium koni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds affect the yield of my young cocoa plants?
ga: Te jwɛi lɛ saa mi kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ayibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your farm; they steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's roots. They also hide dangerous pests like snakes and destructive insects that attack young stems.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛkɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara tamɔ onufui kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Can I just take seeds from my own cocoa pods to nurse and plant new land?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji amli ni makwɛ yɛ he ko hee?

english: It is best to buy certified seedlings from official nurseries. Pods from your own farm may carry hidden diseases or cross-pollinate with lower-quality trees, resulting in low yields when planted.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo tsei ni bɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni cross-pollinate lɛ baanyɛ ahi pods ni jɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ́ adu.

english: Does harvesting immature or overripe cocoa pods affect the crop quality?
ga: Ani kookoo ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ loo eshɛ fe nine ni akpaa lɛ baaná ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes. Unripe pods have small beans that will not ferment properly, leading to poor chocolate flavor. Overripe pods may have beans that germinate inside the pod, ruining the cocoa beans before you can dry them.
ga: Hɛɛ. Nibii bibii yɛ ŋmeii ni eshɛko lɛ amli. ni anyɛɛɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsokolate lɛ ŋɔɔ waa. Ekolɛ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Enɛ baafite kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani obaanyɛ ogbi amɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and dry out easily under full sunlight. They need shade from temporary crops like plantain or permanent trees to protect their leaves from sun damage and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ adɛŋ. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitseiaŋ kɛmiiya amɛteŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for strong foliage and healthy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the ground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in soaked soil because excess water prevents oxygen from reaching the roots and encourages fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain water away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ aya hiɛ, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without giving tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato wooo lɛ?
