english: Tomato flowers fall off due to stress from extreme heat, irregular watering, or using too much leaf-growing fertilizer, which stops the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo atsu nii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help my next crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the farm for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to spend time putting tall sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ be ni mikɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up into sunlight so they can make food to build large tubers underground, while keeping leaves off wet soil to reduce disease.
ga: Akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ woɔ tso mli koni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni akɛhoo koni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ koni helai aba shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards tightly and stopping the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on sap beneath the leaves or spreading viral sicknesses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni haa mɔ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ lɛ eshwaa

english: What is eating small holes in the center whorl of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central shoot of young maize and feeds on tender new leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why shouldn't I throw fertilizer on my farm right before a big rain storm starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ wulu ko jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash fertilizer off the field or push it deep into the soil beyond root depth before the plant can drink it in, wasting the input.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest grow weaker plants than certified seeds from the agrodealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ okwaayeli jalɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their yield power in the second generation, leading to mixed plant sizes and smaller yields compared to fresh certified seed.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nibii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ ahe nyɛmɔ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Is heavy rain always good for my crops, or can it cause damage?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii be fɛɛ be loo ebaanyɛ efite nii?

english: While crops need water to grow, too much heavy rain can wash away fertile topsoil, drown root systems, and lead to fungal diseases like black pod in cocoa.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ, Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops seem to suffer even when it rains a lot during the farming season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Heavy downpours can flood the soil so crop roots cannot breathe, compact the earth, and wash away essential nutrients before the roots can absorb them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. Tse shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu. ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ tsuɔ nii dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: How do I know if the rain falling on my farm is enough or too much for my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa loo eshɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe tsɔ?

english: If water settles on the farm surface for days without sinking in or if leaves turn yellow despite plenty of rain, your farm has excess water and needs better drainage.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ kpɛtɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ gbii babaoo ni efoŋ loo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehe miihia ni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing so slowly compared to other crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ akɛto tsei krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a tree crop that puts its early energy into developing strong roots and sturdy stems, so slow early growth is completely normal and healthy.
ga: Cocoa ji jwɛi tso ni kɛ ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ mra lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ená shishifãi ni wa kɛ tsei ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishijee lɛ, dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni sa ni ehaa mɔ he waa.

english: Does slow growth in cocoa plants mean my yield will be poor when harvest time comes?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni daa blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ miyibii lɛ baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: No, slow and steady growth helps cocoa trees build solid branches and deep root systems, which actually leads to healthier pods and better yields over time.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ daa blɛoo ni ehiɛ kã shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni enáa niji ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How many years does a cocoa seedling usually take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwu ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Depending on the variety, hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing fruit in 2 to 3 years, while traditional varieties can take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema cacao henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5, ni enɛ damɔ henɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does too much water in the soil affect the pods on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ saa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive soil moisture creates high humidity around the tree, which encourages fungal infections like black pod disease that cause cocoa pods to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo baa tso lɛ he, ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ black pod hela ni haa cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: What important signs should I look for when I visit an experienced farmer's cocoa farm to see if their crops are healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii titrii esa akɛ matao beni miyasaraa okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ koni mana kɛji amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Look at the leaf color, the amount of shade cover, whether pods are free from dark spots, and how clean the ground under the trees is kept.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ahe su, bɔ ni hulutsoo lɛ fa ha, kɛji ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmeii komɛi ni tsuɔ loo amɛbɛ. Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsumɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ?

english: What simple steps can I take on my farm to reduce damage when the rainy season comes heavily?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ aba shi?

english: Creating proper drainage channels to direct excess water away and keeping ground cover or mulch helps protect the topsoil from washing away during heavy downpours.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ gbɛi ni sa ni afee koni akɛjie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Ni sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli loo sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ baaye abua ni sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ akaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do older farmers always tell me to be patient when growing cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ yaa nɔ amɛkɛɔ mi akɛ mato mitsui shi beni miduɔ kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a long-term investment that takes years to establish, but once mature, a healthy cocoa tree can produce pods consistently for 20 to 30 years.
ga: Cocoa ji shika ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni heɔ afii babaoo dani anyɛɔ amaa. Shi kɛ́ eda kwraa Cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanyɛ awo ŋmeii be fɛɛ be afii 20 kɛyashi 30.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant. It usually happens when watering is uneven—such as letting the soil dry out completely and then flooding it—which stops the plant from taking up calcium.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ nu lɛ be fɛɛ be, tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ahaa egbiɔ kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ, nu shwieɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ calcium.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids, thrips, or whiteflies sucking the plant's juice and spreading plant diseases. Controlling these small pests early with neem water or safe treatments stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii mra kɛtsɔ neem nu loo gbɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea flowers so quickly every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ oya daa be lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce a sweet scent and bright yellow colors that naturally attract flower thrips and pod borers. These insects feed on the flowers to lay their eggs, so monitoring the farm right when flowering starts is key to catching them early.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ he yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no gbalaa fɔfɔi thrips kɛ pod borers kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛwo wɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi lɛ ji nɔ titri ni baaha omɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why do my cocoa trees shed their small flowers without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Ni etsɔko kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, drought, or heavy shade, or when there are not enough tiny insects called midges to pollinate the flowers. Maintaining proper shade and soil moisture helps the flowers set pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo hulutsoo ni naa wa hao amɛ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii yɛ Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midges lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaawo fɔfɔi amli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ aná hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomatoes cracking and splitting open just as they start to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when a dry plant suddenly receives a huge amount of water from heavy rain or overwatering. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa trukaa Tsei ni egbi lɛ naa nu babaoo kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ fe nine lɛ mli. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for a long time, starving the roots of air and allowing soil fungi to attack. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋwɛi shishifãi lɛ ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the bunches of bananas grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ bananai lɛ dara ni amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily snap under heavy weight or high winds, especially if microscopic soil worms called nematodes have damaged the roots. Using wooden poles to prop up stems with heavy fruit prevents them from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ akumɔ oya yɛ tsɔne ni tsii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Tsoi ni akɛfiɔ tsei ni tsii ni aduawai yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make energy that feeds the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into full sunlight, increasing your tuber yield and keeping the leaves safe from ground diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni haa ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ ahi he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Ha tuber feemɔ aya hiɛ ni oha baai lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ahe.

english: Why do my tiny vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die right at the ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai bibii ni ji Mine lɛ gbee shi trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is called 'damping-off', a condition caused by microscopic fungi living in overly wet, crowded nursery beds. Giving seedlings good air circulation, sunlight, and avoiding overwatering keeps the stems strong.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ ‘Damp’, shihilɛ ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni hiɔ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhei ni mli ewo nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli, hulu la, kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their young leaves dry out easily. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides natural shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees grow stronger.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaa bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni eha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves turn green so the plant can grow well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baa lɛ daa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my cassava tubers if I plant the stem cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: If cassava plants are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives the root system enough room in the soil to form large, thick cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛfee ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni mli tse.

english: Pepper flowers often drop when the soil is too dry or during times of extreme sun heat. Keeping the soil regularly watered and using organic mulch around the stem keeps the soil cool, helping the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Okɛ nu awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ organic mulch abɔle he. Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my maize make the soil better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. This acts as natural food for the soil, which helps companion crops like maize grow bigger and stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni fata he, tamɔ ŋmãa, daa ni amɛhe wa ni tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit viruses to the plant while feeding on it. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil spray and removing infected plants prevents the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛyaa tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Early Whitefly Control Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ shwie nɔ ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my dry-season vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo be mli aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, soil loses moisture rapidly to evaporation, causing plant leaves to lose water faster than the roots can pull it up. Covering the soil around plants with dry grass or straw traps soil moisture and protects roots from heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Mulching around Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi ha tsei ahe lɛ, ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he.

english: How can I tell when my sweet potatoes under the ground are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Sweet potatoes show they are ready for harvest when the leaves on the vine begin to yellow and dry up. You can also gently dig out one tuber to test if the skin is firm and the inside is fully developed.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ yitso kome hu ajie blɛoo. Koni akɛka kɛji hewolo lɛ mli wa ni emli lɛ etsɔ hiɛ kwraa.

english: Why does maize grown from seeds saved from last year's hybrid harvest produce smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first planting season. Saving and replanting seeds from a hybrid crop causes the second generation to lose vigor, leading to weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shweremɔ be lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ he waaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop seedlings to stay small and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ miifee bibii ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than crop seedlings, so they steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early in the season gives crop seedlings full access to the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei amli dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛju nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa tsei dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn yellow and dry up when exposed to direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand heavy, direct sunlight because their root systems are still small and delicate. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside them creates a living canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from scorching while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa. Shade tsei tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning pale green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer gives the maize the boost it needs to grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvesting under the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava plants show they are ready when their bottom leaves start to dry out and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. The base of the main stem also swells visibly near the soil line, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Yucca tso tsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso lɛ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ fũuɔ waa yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning dark brown and soft before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium or water while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil consistently watered helps the roots continuously pump calcium into the developing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ calcium kɛyaa tomato ni miida lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by converting sunlight into energy through their leaves. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and air, resulting in larger and healthier yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra shoots sprouting around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to direct its energy into producing large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that sit under the leaves and suck out the plant's sap. Spraying with neem oil or soapy water helps clear these insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe kooloi nɛɛ koni baai heei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, damp conditions. Pruning excess tree branches allows sunshine and airflow into the farm to dry off the pods, making it harder for the fungus to grow.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ ŋmɔtɔ baakwɛ̃.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes straight through the middle of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye bu ko ni yɔɔ mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a pest that burrows into the growing center (funnel) of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying targeted treatments into the funnel kills the pests before they destroy the crop's yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ adalɛ hei (channels) lɛ amli. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ baagbe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients out of the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests to multiply. Alternating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores vital nutrients to the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and turn yellow when I clear all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mijieɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Shade trees act like protective blankets that block excessive heat, conserve soil moisture, and prevent the leaves from scorching.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa baai lɛ shãaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over during strong rains just when the fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli, beni aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that hold onto the soil loosely. As the heavy bunch of fruit grows, the top becomes heavy, so strong winds easily pull the shallow roots out of wet ground unless you support the stem with wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ tsei akui lɛ dara lɛ, amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ tsiimɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ. Okɛ ohe awo hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ amli oya Ja okɛ tso ni akɛfee tsɔne fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less maize every year when I plant maize on the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating your crops gives the soil time to rest and prevents nutrients from being completely used up.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ sɛɛ foɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe, ni ehaaa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell me that planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have special roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen fertilizes the next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso ko gbo lɛ, nitrogen ni ato lɛ haa tso ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ bii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This stress causes them to spend all their energy reaching for sunlight instead of growing thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔnyɛɛ nɛɛ haa amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtaoɔ hulu la. Mohu ɔ, nyɛ hyɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a mi wa.

english: This is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that hides inside the young maize leaves to feed on the tender leaf tissues before the plant fully expands.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli koni eye baa bibii amli fãji dani tso lɛ mli alɛɛ kwraa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits on the land without draining away, the roots suffocate in the mud and encourage fungi that cause the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ muji lɛ mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants grow plenty of leafy vines but end up with small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ wain tsei ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the yam plant to put all its food energy into growing leaves above the ground instead of storing energy in the tuber below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli, moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants dry out fast in the hot season even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ mli daa leebi moŋ?

english: Under strong sunshine, water evaporates from bare soil very quickly before roots can absorb it. Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture longer.
ga: yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of pollination can stress the tomato plant, causing it to shed its flowers to survive rather than spending energy growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo pollination ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ afɔ amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why do I see so many ants crawling all over my cassava leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo ni miiho yɛ mi-cassava baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ants are usually attracted to sweet liquid produced by small sap-sucking insects like mealybugs or aphids hiding under the leaves. Seeing ants on your crop is a sign that you need to check the undersides of the leaves for hidden pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ŋɔɔ ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids ni akɛtee baai lɛ ashishi lɛ feɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. Kɛ́ ona ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ, eji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni ona ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ.

english: Are ants on my cocoa farm dangerous to the cocoa trees?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ kookoo tsei lɛ awui?

english: While ants themselves do not eat cocoa trees, certain types of ants protect and spread mealybugs because they feed on the sweet liquid mealybugs produce. Mealybugs carry the dangerous Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, so controlling ant activity helps prevent disease.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ yeee cacao tsei moŋ, shi ŋmeii komɛi buɔ mealybugs lɛ ahe ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ lɛ. Mealybugs ji mɛi ni kɛ Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akudɔ ŋmeii lɛ anitsumɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai anaa.

english: Can insects living inside the soil damage my yam tubers before I harvest them?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpata mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ dani akpa amɛ?

english: Yes, soil pests such as yam beetles and nematodes live underground and feed directly on growing tubers. They create holes and rough patches on the yam, which reduces its quality and allows rot to set in.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tamɔ sweet potato ŋmeii kɛ nematodes hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba shi ni ekɛ fitemɔ aba.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight like straws during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense sunlight and reduce water loss through evaporation. It is the plant's natural survival mechanism to conserve moisture until temperatures cool down.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he, ni ekɛha nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme afternoon heat, drought stress, or heavy rainfall. The plant sheds flowers to save energy and water so that the main stem and leaves can survive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Akɛni hɔmɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa haa tsei lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi hewɔ lɛ, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛtso lɛ shishifãi titri lɛ kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and die right after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain splashes fungal spores from the wet soil onto the lower leaves of tomato plants. The high moisture and humidity create the ideal conditions for fungal diseases like early blight to grow quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the corn plant moves available nutrients from its older bottom leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: If the soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing thick leafy stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ starch baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow weak and tall when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛyaa shɔŋŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops need direct sunlight to make their food. Under dense tree shade, plants stretch upward toward the light, making them tall, thin, and weak, while the tree roots compete with them for soil nutrients.
ga: Hulu la he miihia aduawai tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii. Yɛ tsei ni mli tse lɛ ashishi Tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ, amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe waaa, yɛ be mli ni tsei shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why does striga weed keep damaging my maize even after I clear all the visible weeds before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi fɛɛ ni anaa dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Striga seeds stay hidden deep inside the soil for years and only sprout when they detect chemical signals from growing maize roots. Once germinated, the weed attaches directly to the maize roots underground to steal water and food.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ afii babaoo. Ekwɛ̃ɔ pɛ kɛji ena tsofafeemɔ he okadii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ni eda lɛ mli. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ ŋmã shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ koni eju nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to use tap water straight from the pipe to water my young vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ hose lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe koni mikɛha mi-aduawai bibii lɛ nu?

english: Tap water often contains chlorine chemical to kill germs, which can harm tender young crop roots and good soil insects. If you leave the pipe water in an open container for a day, the air and sunlight will break down the chlorine, making it safe for your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa ni ji chlorine ni gbeɔ helatsɛmɛi lɛ yɛ nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aye tsei bibii ashishifãi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ awui. Kɛji oshi nu ni jɛ paipii lɛ mli lɛ yɛ tsɛnsi ko ni agbele mli gbi kome. Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la fiteɔ chlorine. Ha efee shweshweeshwe kɛha onibii.

english: I left water in my open farm tank for days and now it has turned green. Is this green water safe for my crops?
ga: Mishi nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋshɔŋlooi atoohe ko ni agbele naa lɛ mli gbii komɛi. Ni agbɛnɛ nu lɛ etsɔ eŋɔli. Ani nu ni ji eŋɔli nɛɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: The green substance is algae growing because sunlight hit the open water. While it will not immediately kill your crops, it shows the water has been standing too long in the sun, which can lower the air quality in the water that roots need.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ tswaa nu ni agbele naa lɛ. Kɛji egbeee onibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ po. Shi etsɔɔ akɛ nu lɛ ehi hulu la lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ he hiaa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow much faster when it rains compared to when I water them with stored pipe water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ? Kɛ akɛto be mli ni mikɛ nu ni jɛ hose ni ato lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ he.

english: Rainwater picks up fresh oxygen directly from the air as it falls, and it is free from treatment chemicals like chlorine. Crop roots love this natural oxygen, which helps them take up plant food faster.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hee ni ji oxygen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni egbeeɔ shi lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ tsofai tamɔ chlorine bɛ mli lɛ, tsei shishifãi sumɔɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛyeɔ tsei aniyenii oya.

english: Should I cover my outdoor water storage tank or leave it open to the sun?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha mi nu ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ nɔ loo mashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: It is best to cover your tank. Leaving it open in the hot sun causes green algae to build up and warms the water too much, which can shock cool plant roots when you water them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ otanki lɛ aaatee. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ abɔle ehe ni ebaaha nu lɛ mli adɔ tsɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha fɛ̃i aba tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli.

english: Why does the water sitting at the bottom of my farm storage drum start to smell bad after a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water needs oxygen from the air to stay fresh. When water sits still for too long, it loses its air, allowing bad bacteria to build up at the bottom which makes it smell foul and unsafe for delicate seedlings.
ga: Nu he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni ehi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ nu tee nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fiteɔ. Enɛ haa helai fɔji buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shishigbɛ. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa ni ebɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though I water the farm every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Just like humans, crop roots need air to breathe. When you put too much water on the land without letting it dry slightly, the water pushes all the air out of the soil, drowning the roots and turning the leaves yellow.
ga: tamɔ adesai nɔŋŋ Tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni okɛ nu babaoo woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ohaaa egbi fioo lɛ. Nu lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. shishifãi lɛ ni shwieɔ nu mli ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: I noticed a green slime layer forming on top of my crop beds after heavy sunshine. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse slime ŋmɔtɔ ko ni miifee yɛ midumɔ saatsoi lɛ anɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: That green layer is algae that forms when wet soil gets direct sunlight for a long time. It means your soil is holding too much standing water and needs to be stirred or drained so air can enter.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni baa kɛji shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ miimɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli. Ni ehe miihia ni atswa lɛ loo ajie kɔɔyɔɔ kpo yɛ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli.

english: My neighbor told me to stir or splash my stored irrigation water before pouring it on my crops. Does this really help?
ga: Mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ato lɛ ashwie loo mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Ani enɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, stirring or splashing water mixes fresh air into it. This adds oxygen to the water, which helps your crop roots breathe easier and absorb soil nutrients more efficiently.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ajieɔ loo ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baafutu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ muɔ mlɛo ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it bad to water my crops with water from a black plastic tank that has been sitting in the hot midday sun?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ plastic baagi diŋ ko ni ta hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli lɛ baafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: Yes, water left in the hot sun becomes very warm. Hot water can burn or shock sensitive crop roots and reduces the amount of healthy oxygen available to the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu ni ashiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ adɔ waa. Nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo etswa tso shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni tsei yɔɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I pour water drawn straight from a deep borehole directly onto my seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafɔse nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ nu bu ko ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ awo dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Deep borehole water often lacks air because it has been trapped underground. It is better to pump it into a container first so air can mix with it before you apply it to your crop roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ ehiɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛwo tsɛnsi mli klɛŋklɛŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ lɛ afutu dani okɛwo otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense sunlight and heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates living umbrellas that shield the delicate leaves and hold soil moisture while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tso bibioo lɛ maa ehe shi lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way I stick cassava stems into the dirt when I am planting?
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, ani ŋmei tsei lɛ baakpã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, you must plant cassava stems with the leaf nodes or buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots struggle to grow upward, leading to weak plants and much lower root yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehe miihia ni odu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ebaa loo eshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaawa akɛ oookwɛ tsei lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Why do I need to build high soil mounds before I plant my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deeply cultivated soil so the tubers can expand easily without pushing against hard ground. Mounding also improves drainage so excess rainwater doesn't collect around the roots and cause them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Pilɛi lɛ hu haa nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akabua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for leaf growth. Applying well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the maize regain its deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ adara lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get stressed by very hot, dry soil or sudden heat waves. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch and regular watering helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo hulutsoo ni baa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu be fɛɛ be, ni akɛ nu woɔ mli daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔ pepper aduawai.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my maize, and how do I save my crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing funnel of maize plants. You can control them by applying recommended pest control products or dropping a pinch of clean sand or wood ash into the plant's central leaves early in the morning.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ. Aloo okɛ ŋã loo tso sũ ni mli tse fioo ko awo tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and overly shady conditions. Pruning extra branches and clearing tall weeds allows sunlight and air to dry the pods and prevent the fungus.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ tsɔ, ni edɔ waa, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ajiemɔ Ha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni etsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that suck sap and spread plant viruses. Protecting the plants with soapy water sprays or neem oil helps keep whiteflies away so the leaves stay flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ shwie nɔ lɛ bu tsei ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ akashɛ amɛhe. Koni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: It is best to water your garden early in the morning before the sun gets hot. Morning watering allows the soil to absorb moisture deeply, whereas mid-day sun causes water to evaporate quickly and can scorch hot leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ obɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi, dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya ni eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: How do I know my groundnuts are ready to harvest without digging up my entire field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can check maturity by pulling up just one or two test plants in your field. If the leaves are turning yellow and the inside of the pod shells has turned a dark brown color, your groundnut crop is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛtsɔ kaa tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni ooogbala yɛ onitsumɔhe nine lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni pod lɛ mli fã lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the young cocoa with shade and moisture until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains wash away nutrients. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea when the soil is moist helps the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and stays there for too long during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants fall off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Mulching around the plants helps keep the soil moisture and temperature steady, allowing flowers to form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same land continuously drains specific nutrients out of the soil and allows maize pests to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ feɔ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upwards and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from the young leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or an appropriate insecticide controls these pests and allows new leaves to expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa. Eyeɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anɔ ni ehaa baai heei daa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight, which allows the plant to produce food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground also protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hu buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Propping up the main stem with a branched wooden pole or bamboo supports the weight of the bunch during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii niji fi tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ kuu lɛ muji lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: How can I tell when my maize cobs are fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn brown and dry, and a tiny black mark appears at the bottom of each grain kernel. Harvesting at this point prevents insects and birds from destroying the grain in the field.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi. Ni okadii diji bibii yɛ jɛmɛ. jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa kooloi kɛ okpoi akafite ŋmaa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping green fruits before they get a chance to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii eŋɔli dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop green fruit when they do not get enough water during dry weather, or when pests like fruit flies attack. Regular watering during dry spells and clearing fallen fruit from under the tree helps reduce fruit drop.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ baashwie amɛyibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ ashwie shi kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa lɛ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ aduawai ni egbee shi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunshine. They need shade from larger trees or plantains when young to keep their leaves from burning and to retain soil moisture around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛhe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda loo plantains amli beni amɛdarako lɛ koni baai lɛ akashã amɛ, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ko he miihia otso lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain farm produce smaller bunches when I leave all the young shoots growing around the main plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: All those extra shoots, or suckers, are competing with the mother plant for food and water in the soil. Pruning extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the mother plant to put its energy into growing big fruit bunches.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi, loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ kɛ tso nyɛ lɛ miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: This is caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease. It spreads rapidly in cold, wet, humid conditions when water droplets splash fungal spores from the soil onto the pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli beni nu mli nui shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Why does putting dried leaves around the base of my plants help them stay healthy during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ baai ni egboi fata mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, protects the soil from drying out in the sun, and turns into rich natural compost over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi haa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ atade, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ muji lɛ mli lɛ. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni hulu lɛ akagbi. ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when the ground stays too wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown, stop growing, and begin to rot from waterlogging.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni no haa amɛdalɛ kpaa. ni ebɔi fitemɔ yɛ nu afua hewɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot during the afternoon, tomato plants get stressed and their pollen dies, causing the blossoms to drop before they can produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni pollen lɛ gboɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do small green caterpillars chew small holes through my maize leaves and hide inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ bu bibii kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are pests called Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize leaves, and when the worms hatch, they eat the softest parts of the plant and tunnel inward to protect themselves from sunlight.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ahe nibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo fe fɛɛ lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to train my yam vines to climb up sticks or trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsɔse mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ tsei aniji loo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need a lot of sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking raises the vines off the shaded ground so the leaves can catch maximum sun to build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking baawó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni efee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest when I plant maize on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Maize sucks out the same nutrients from the soil every single season, making the ground tired and poor. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps put vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shoo ni ehiii kwraa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What does it mean when people say a crop or seed is 'true to type'?
ga: Kɛ mɔ ko kɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo dumɔwui Mɛni ji ‘type-match’ shishi?

english: When a crop is 'true to type', it means the plants will grow up looking and behaving exactly like the original variety you planted, with uniform height, yield, and grain quality without unexpected variations.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ‘ja’ lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ ebaada ni ekwɛ ni efee enii tamɔ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni odu lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, kɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaa, yibiiwoo kɛ dumɔwui ahe su ni yaa nɔ daa ni tsakemɔi ni akpaaa gbɛ bɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the seeds I bought or saved are mixed with other lower-quality varieties?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ loo mikɛtoɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui krokomɛi ni baa shi lɛ efutu mli?

english: You can inspect the seeds before planting to see if they share the same shape, color, and size, or watch the growing plants in the field to see if some look noticeably different in growth or ear structure from the rest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ dumɔwui lɛ dani odu koni ona kɛji amɛhe su, amɛhe su, kɛ amɛdalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Aloo kwɛmɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ koni ona kɛji ekomɛi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa loo amɛtoi lɛ yɔɔ srɔto kwraa yɛ ekrokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: How does planting seeds from a single pure variety benefit my crop yield compared to using mixed seeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni jɛ tso kome ni he tse mli ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi yibiiwoo lɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛfutu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he?

english: Pure seeds grow at the same pace, mature at the exact same time, and respond uniformly to rainfall and fertilizer, giving you a predictable harvest and higher overall yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni he tse lɛ hu daa yɛ oyaiyeli kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli. ni ahoɔ yɛ be kome mli ni ehaa nugbɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni baa daa lɛ hetoo Enɛ haa onáa ŋmaa ni anyɛɔ atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni onáa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni fa babaoo.

english: Can I keep replanting seeds saved from my own maize harvest year after year without losing quality?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa kpamɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ shãaa afɔle?

english: If your crop gets cross-pollinated by neighboring fields or mixed with other types, the seeds stop being 'true to type' and will gradually produce smaller cobs and lower yields in future seasons.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔ ko ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ etsɔ cross-pollination loo ekɛ tso kroko efo mli. Dumɔwui lɛ baatsɔ ais. ‘Eji anɔkwale kɛha henɔi lɛ’ ni fiofio lɛ ebaaha ŋmeii bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I inspect the ears on my maize plants before selecting seeds for the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa toi amli dani mahala dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Inspecting the ears helps you confirm that the crop has developed uniform grains characteristic of that specific variety, ensuring you do not save seeds from cobs that mixed with unwanted lower-quality plants.
ga: Toi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ haa onyɛɔ omaa nɔ mi akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ená nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmaa sui ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Enɛ haa obuaa dumɔwui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ tsei ni ataooo ni ehiii lɛ efutu mli lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize cobs sometimes have grains with different colors on the very same ear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn cob lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi yɛ toi kome mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes pollen carried by the wind from nearby plants; if a different maize variety is nearby, pollen mixes on the cob and creates grains with mixed colors and traits.
ga: Abele naa pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa henɔi krokomɛi yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ Pollen fuses yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ewoɔ dumɔwui ni ji sui kɛ sui ni efutu.

english: What should I do if I notice a few maize plants in my farm growing differently from all the others?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina akɛ ŋmãa tsei fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe tsei krokomɛi lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You should remove or tag those different plants before they flower so their pollen does not mix with your uniform crop and spoil the purity of your harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie loo okɛ okadi awo tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko nɔ. mɛi ni dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Enɛ ji koni akafutu pollen kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni ofite okpamɔ lɛ mli hetsemɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it risky to mix different varieties of maize seeds together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaafutu ŋmãa srɔtoi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Mixing different seed varieties leads to uneven growth, different maturity times, and unwanted cross-pollination that ruins crop uniformity, making harvesting difficult and lowering crop quality.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. be srɔtoi ni shwereɔ kɛ cross-pollination ni ataooo ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ekomefeemɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa nikpamɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baa shi.

english: How can I make sure I do not accidentally plant mixed crop seeds in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni efutu lɛ eduuu miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ oshara mli?

english: Keep seed varieties clearly separated, buy certified seeds from reliable sources, and carefully check the seeds for uniform size and color before putting them into the ground.
ga: Gbalamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ amli faŋŋ. Hemɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ hei ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji amɛdalɛ kɛ amɛhe su yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli dani okɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ.

english: Do buyers pay better prices if my harvested grain comes from a single pure variety?
ga: Ani mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo jara ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ jɛ dumɔwui ni ji purebred kome mli?

english: Yes, grain buyers and food processors pay higher prices for uniform produce because it cooks evenly and produces consistent flour or food products.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni heɔ ŋmaa kɛ mɛi ni feɔ niyenii lɛ woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha nibii ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehooɔ nii pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ batter loo niyenii ni tamɔ ekome baa.

english: If I stop buying chemical fertilizers and switch to organic farming, will my crops still give a big yield?
ga: Kɛji okpa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hemɔ ni otsɔ okwaayeli ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo yibii babaoo lolo?

english: Yes, organic farming uses natural compost and manure which build up soil health over time, allowing your crops to grow well and yield a strong harvest without damaging the soil long-term.
ga: Hɛɛ, organic okwaayeli kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni maa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni mli wa ni eyeee shikpɔŋ lɛ awui yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Is it safe to harvest and eat plantains right after I spray them with farm chemicals?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makpa plantains ni maye amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofai efɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, chemical sprays leave harmful residues on crops that require a specific waiting period before harvesting; using organic methods avoids toxic chemicals on the food you share with family.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shĩɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni biɔ ni amɛmɛ be babaoo dani akpa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛi ni akɛ tsofai fɔji tsu nii yɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ niyenii ni okɛ oweku lɛ yeɔ lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if a fertilizer is chemical or organic?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ji tsofa loo nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli?

english: Chemical fertilizers are usually manufactured powders or granules like NPK and Urea, while organic fertilizers come from natural sources like composted leaves, animal manure, or bio-organic mixes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afeɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ powda loo granular mli, tamɔ NPK kɛ urea, yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii tamɔ baai ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii, loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Does using chemical fertilizers change the taste or shelf life of my harvested plantains?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsakeɔ mi-plantain ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ loo be ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Overusing chemical fertilizers can make crops spoil faster after harvest and alter their taste, whereas organically grown crops tend to stay fresh longer and keep their natural flavor.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ, ni etsake amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsofafeemɔ mli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋɔɔmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is my soil getting hard and dry even though I put chemical fertilizer on my crops every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi nɛkɛ? Namɛi kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii daa be?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the crop directly but do not improve the structure of the ground, whereas organic matter acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold moisture and stay soft.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii tɛ̃ɛ shi ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. yɛ be mli ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehiɔ shi blɛoo.

english: How does organic manure help my crops survive during dry weather?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Organic matter mixed into the soil holds onto underground moisture longer during dry periods, keeping roots cool and hydrated even when rain is scarce.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ bei ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo lɛ po mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves grow very big and leafy, but the fruit bunches stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ baai lɛ? Shi aduawai akuu lɛ ji bibioo lolo.

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen chemical fertilizer makes them grow leaves instead of fruits; balanced organic feeding helps the plant focus energy on producing large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛkwɛ̃ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I protect my farm from pests naturally without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: You can make natural organic pest sprays using water mixed with ground neem leaves or hot pepper, which repels bugs without leaving poisonous chemicals on your food.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛ neem baai ni atswa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ efutu mli lɛ afee adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ. Amɛshwieɔ kooloi bibii ni amɛshiii tsofai fɔji yɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and drop off before the fruits are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can mean a lack of nutrients or poor soil drainage; adding rich organic compost around the base gives the roots steady nutrition to keep leaves green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaabɔle Cone lɛ he lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa be fɛɛ be koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: If I use organic inputs, do I need to apply them as frequently as chemical fertilizers?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛwo mli shii abɔ tamɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: No, organic matter breaks down slowly and continuously releases nutrients into the soil over a longer time, so you often need fewer applications than quick-release chemical fertilizers.
ga: Dabi, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ fiofio. ni ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ atsu nii oya lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do some farmers cover harvested oil palm bunches with sand while waiting for them to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ ŋã haa mu tsei ni akpa lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Covering palm bunches with sand retains natural heat and moisture, which helps the fruits soften and ferment evenly so they can be easily detached from the main bunch for oil extraction.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ha tsei akui lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni ehaa amɛhe feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ kuu titri lɛ mli oya koni akɛjie mu.

english: How do I know when oil palm fruit on the tree is fully ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ mu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm fruit is mature and ready to cut when its outer skin turns bright orange-red, and at least five loose fruits fall naturally to the ground beneath the tree.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ edara ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli tse. Ni kɛ hoo lɛ, mu tso yibii enumɔ baagbee shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does my harvested palm fruit spoil quickly if I leave it standing in the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Once you cut a palm bunch from the tree, the oil inside begins to degrade rapidly due to natural enzymes and heat, which lowers the quality and market value of the oil if not processed within two days.
ga: Kɛji ofo tso lɛ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ Mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli enzymes kɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa mu lɛ kpakpa kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii yɛ gbii enyɔ mli.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava next to my young oil palm trees, or will it harm the palm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ emasɛi? mi tso bibioo lɛ Aloo ebaaye tso lɛ awui loo ebaayeee?

english: You can plant food crops near young palms, but cassava grows tall and heavy, so keeping it at least two meters away prevents it from shading your young palms or taking away crucial soil nutrients.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii tsei yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe. Shi cassava lɛ kɛlɛ ni etsii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ha amɛhi shi kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ahe mitai 2 koni amɛkatsi ŋmei bibii anaa loo amɛkajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my oil palm seedlings when I am planting my farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo oil palm dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Oil palm seedlings should be planted nine meters apart in a triangular pattern so that when the trees grow big fronds, they get enough sunlight without blocking light from neighboring trees.
ga: Esa akɛ adu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ mitai 9 kɛjɛ amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni tamɔ koŋ etɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ baai wuji lɛ, ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni etsĩii la ni jɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: What kind of weeds or plants can harm my oil palm farm if I let them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ jwɛi loo tsei baanyɛ aye mi-palm oil ŋmɔ lɛ awui kɛji miha amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Aggressive weeds like Spear Grass and heavy climbing vines can wrap around young palms, choke their growth, and steal moisture and fertilizers from the palm roots.
