ga: Jwɛi ni he wa tamɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi kɛ wain tsei ni tsii ni kwɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ abɔle tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ahe. etsĩɔ dalɛ naa ni ejuɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli.

english: What type of soil makes oil palm trees grow best and produce heavy fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ haa oil palm tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai ni tsii?

english: Oil palm trees thrive best in deep, well-draining loamy soil that stays moist without turning waterlogged or muddy during heavy rainy seasons.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ekɛ nu loo sũ baaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young oil palm turning yellow, and how can I fix it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsitsi lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the tree is lacking nitrogen or potassium in the soil, which you can fix by applying balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the leaf drip line.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen loo potassium yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛbaabɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ni hoɔ lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: My elders passed down traditional ways of growing palm trees, but how long will a palm tree actually produce fruit for me?
ga: Mi onukpai lɛ ná kusum gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ akɛ gboshinii. Shi mɛɛ be tɛŋ tso baawo yibii eha mi?

english: A well-cared-for oil palm tree starts bearing fruit after three to four years and can continue producing good yields for twenty-five to thirty years before it becomes too tall to harvest.
ga: Mu tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ sɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii kpakpai afii nyɔŋmai enyɔ kɛ enumɔ kɛyashi nyɔŋmai etɛ krokomɛi dani amɛdara tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa.

english: How can I protect my palm farm from pests without using expensive chemicals that ruin the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-palm ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuuu nii?

english: You can plant cover crops like Mucuna, which naturally prevent weeds, keep insect pests away, and add good nitrogen to enrich your soil for free.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ko nɔ, tamɔ Mucuna, ni ji nɔ ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Ha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛ Ni okɛ nitrogen kpakpa afata he koni eha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo yaka.

english: Can spraying the wrong chemicals on my farm crops cause health problems like cancer for the people who eat them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni ejaaa ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi ni yeɔ tsofai nɛɛ aná helai, tamɔ kansa?

english: Yes, using unapproved chemical pesticides or harvesting crops immediately after spraying leaves dangerous toxic residues on food. Always use recommended farm chemicals, wear protective gear, and observe the safety waiting period between spraying and harvesting.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ashwie nɔ lɛ haa tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛɔ yɛ niyenii nɔ. Kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be. Wo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ni okwɛ be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni kã shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crops turning yellow and wilting early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nutrients like nitrogen or is suffering from excess water around the roots. Applying the right fertilizer early and ensuring good soil drainage helps leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo nu ni fa fe nine miiná shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii mra Ni akwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains or mature forest trees protect young cocoa from scorching sun and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei ni eda lɛ baabu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: This happens because the cocoa trees are losing water faster than their roots can drink it from the dry soil. Mulching around the base of the trees with dried leaves keeps the roots cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat my maize leaves as soon as the dry spell begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele baai lɛ ni amɛyeɔ amɛ kɛji hɔmɔ lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: Dry and warm weather causes pests like fall armyworms to hatch and multiply rapidly. Checking your crop leaves regularly and applying safe, approved bio-pesticides at the first sign of damage stops them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ fɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya. Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ baai lɛ amli daa ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ efite lɛ mli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers falling off the plants before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress or a sudden lack of water during flowering. Regular watering during dry weather keeps the plant cool and helps flowers develop into full peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛna dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni faaa trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ daraa kwraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for too long, oxygen cannot reach the cassava roots, causing bacteria and fungi to rot them. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa muawai kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer bags of crops every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ faaa daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii moŋ.

english: Crops remove essential food nutrients from the dirt every time they grow. If you do not replenish the soil with organic compost, manure, or fertilizer, or rotate crops with beans and groundnuts, the soil becomes exhausted.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. loo okɛ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii atsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small, light bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miida ni etsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why does letting weeds grow in my yam farm prevent the yam tubers from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni mikwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haaa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive competitors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your yams. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your yams get all the nutrition required to form large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi ji akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and drying up in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains provides shelter, keeps the soil moist, and protects the young cocoa plants until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa mɔ náa wɔɔhe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and dark green in one part of my farm, but stay short and yellow in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ kuku lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ fã kroko mli.

english: Soil nutrients like nitrogen vary across different spots on a farm. Yellow, stunted maize means that section of soil lacks nutrients, which can be restored using organic compost, animal manure, or balanced fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Yellow dwarf corn tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fãi komɛi bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja atsu nii ni akɛku sɛɛ afee enɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three heavy, steady rains so the soil holds enough deep moisture. Planting too early during unpredictable first rains can cause seeds to dry out and fail to germinate.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same field without harming my crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni eyeee miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, you can plant them together if spaced correctly. Maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, leaving space and nutrients for the slower-growing cassava to mature afterward without fighting for resources.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu amɛ yɛ he kome kɛji akɛ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ja. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii haa ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ koni ekwɛ sɛɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe awo nibii ni he hiaa lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani minine shɛɔ hegbɛ nɔ ni mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater sits in wet soil without draining away. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain off, keeping the roots healthy and dry.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ tsɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and flowers when my field gets flooded after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni pepper tsei lɛ baa kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ eho yɛ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil prevents roots from getting air, causing the plant to suffocate. When roots are stressed by excess water, the plant drops leaves and flowers to conserve energy and survive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe Kɛ́ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ha shishifãi lɛ miihao Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller yields than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give high yields in their first season. Seeds saved from that crop lose those high-performing traits in the next generation, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ baafite nakai sui ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I clear the ground completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant underground for years. When you clear and turn over the soil, you expose buried weed seeds to sunlight and air, causing them to sprout rapidly unless covered with mulch or cover crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ awɔ. shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo Kɛ́ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni otsɔ mli Jwɛi dumɔwui ni afu lɛ lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baa amɛnɔ. Ehaa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya Ja ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why is my tomato crop producing plenty of yellow flowers but failing to grow into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi edaaa ni etsɔɔɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without producing fruit when temperatures get too high or when insects like bees are absent to pollinate them. Excessive nitrogen fertilizer can also cause plants to grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ kɛha pollination lɛ, nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why is my harvested corn turning into dust and getting infested with tiny bugs inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ mli eyi kɛ sũ ni kooloi bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? ni gbaa mɔ naa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli

english: Insects like weevils attack stored corn if the grain is not dried thoroughly in the sun before storage. Drying corn to low moisture levels and storing it in airtight bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating the kernels.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani akɛto. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛye ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: If my farmland is flat, does that automatically mean it is good for growing crops?
ga: Kɛji miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ji ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ ehi kɛha tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Good farmland depends more on how well the soil absorbs and holds moisture than whether the land is flat or on a slope. Soil that allows water to soak in properly without drowning plant roots nourishes crops best.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui kpakpai damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ fe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse loo eyɛ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni haa nu shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ tsei shishifãi shwieee shi lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii ni hi fe fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if the ground on my farm can hold enough water for my crops during dry days?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he ko baanyɛ ato nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: You can test your soil by squeezing a damp handful into a ball; soil that holds together well (often called funtum land) retains water nicely for crop roots, whereas sandy soil that falls apart loses water too fast.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka sũ lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ sũ ni mli edɔ fioo ni oookɛmimɔ bɔɔlu mli lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he jogbaŋŋ (Bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ funtum shikpɔŋ) lɛ hiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa tsei shishifãi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋã shikpɔji ni ekumɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why does water disappear so quickly into the ground when I water my vegetables on sandy land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu laajeɔ oya kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie aduawai anɔ yɛ sũ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has loose, large particles with big gaps, so poured water drains straight through before plant roots have enough time to drink it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni afɔse awo mli lɛ baaho tɛ̃ɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná be ni amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-baby pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) blocks strong sunlight from hitting the earth, stopping water from evaporating so the soil stays moist for your plants much longer.
ga: Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ kɛha tsei lɛ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves after heavy rain often mean the soil is holding too much water around the roots, suffocating them and stopping the plant from taking up food from the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ miihiɛ nu babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: If your soil does not store moisture deeply, the surface soil dries out quickly under strong heat, causing the leaves to lose water faster than roots can pull it up from below.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baagbi oya yɛ la ni naa wa shishi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shishi kɛya ŋwɛi.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak when the ground feels very hard and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ wa waa ni egbi lɛ?

english: Hard, compacted soil makes it impossible for rain to soak in deep, and roots struggle to spread out to find water and nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni edɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nyɛŋ abote mli shɔŋŋ. Ni shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai.

english: How do I choose the right plot of land for vegetables that need a lot of water to grow?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala shikpɔŋ ni akɛduɔ aduawai ni he hiaa nu babaoo lɛ?

english: Look for dark, rich soil that stays damp to the touch after watering, as this soil retains moisture near the shallow roots of vegetable plants better than dry or stony ground.
ga: Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nu ni baahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni oooshɛ he lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai ashishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do farmers make raised mounds or ridges before planting yam or sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi maa gɔji loo ŋmeii dani amɛduɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Mounds loosen the earth so tubers can swell easily while allowing extra rainwater to drain down the sides so the crops do not rot.
ga: Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɔjɔ oya, yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa nugbɔ nu kroko hu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ afãi lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Will my maize crop produce better if I plant the seeds very close together so they can share soil water?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ baawo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛja nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, planting too close forces the crops to compete aggressively for the same water and nutrients, resulting in weak plants with smaller ears of maize.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa toi bibii.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves moving upward usually means your maize is short of nitrogen, an essential plant food. The plant is moving its remaining nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miiya ŋwɛi lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ miitsi nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do groundnut plants bend down and push their flowers into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ fɔfɔi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above the ground, but the actual nuts grow underground. Once the flower is pollinated, the stem grows downward into soft soil so the seed pods can swell and mature safely beneath the ground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ wo pollination lɛ Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baakwɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashwere ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is under stress, often caused by extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of nutrients. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Why should I cut away the small extra suckers growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra shoots suck away water and plant food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the mother plant has enough food to grow a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ shishifã kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the underground tuber. Lifting the vines up on stakes gives leaves maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp ground, which prevents fungal rot.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni etsi ŋmɔtɔ ni baa lɛ naa Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ akafite.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the plants to compete fiercely with one another for light, water, and soil food. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwooo kwraa.

english: Which specific part of a cassava stick is best for me to cut and plant?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mafolɔ ni madu?

english: The middle section of a healthy, mature cassava stem makes the best planting stick. The top tips are too soft and dry out easily, while the very bottom is too woody to sprout roots quickly.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ teŋgbɛ fã ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni edara lɛ feɔ tso ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aduɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naagbee lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni egbiɔ oya. yɛ be mli ni shishigbɛ lɛ ji tsei tsɔ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ adara oya.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. When tree canopies are too dense and retain damp air, rain droplets bounce the fungus spores onto the cocoa pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ewo duŋ, ni efɔ lɛ. Beni tso ko ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛyaa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local environment, making them tough and efficient. They take up water and nutrients from the soil faster than cultivated crop plants.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Ha efee nɔ ni wa ni ehe wa. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ.

english: How can I apply fertilizer to my crops so heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the ground is moist, but not during heavy downpours. Burying or covering the fertilizer lightly with soil near the base of the plant stops rain from washing it off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni bɛŋkɛ shishigbɛ lɛ fu loo okɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so quickly from one cocoa tree to the neighboring ones in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by microscopic fungal spores that easily travel through rain splashes, wind, and crawling insects from an infected pod to healthy trees nearby.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ amli kɛbaa.

english: How do cassava mealybugs manage to move from my neighbor's farm to attack my crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni cassava mealybugs lɛ ajɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ebatutua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Mealybugs are light enough to be carried across farms by the wind, and they also travel on contaminated farm tools, clothes, or infected stem cuttings moved between fields.
ga: Mealybugs lɛ he waaa bɔ ni sa ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ni amɛfãa gbɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni mli ewo muji, atadei loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: If my cocoa trees look strong and healthy, can they still catch the swollen shoot virus?
ga: Kɛji mi-cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ani hela ni efuu lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ ehe lolo?

english: Yes, even healthy trees can get infected because mealybugs carrying the virus feed on them and inject the disease directly into the tree's sap system.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ po baanyɛ aná hela ejaakɛ ŋmeii ni hiɛ hela lɛ yeɔ amɛ ni amɛkɛ hela lɛ woɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: I only see a few fall armyworms on my maize leaves; do I need to spray my whole field immediately?
ga: Mina ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ yɛ mi-corn baai lɛ anɔ. Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa afɔ shia lɛ mli fɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: A very small number of worms might not reduce your harvest, but you must monitor them closely because they multiply rapidly and can destroy a crop in days if the population grows.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ haŋ onibii lɛ aba shi. Shi ehe miihia ni okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛshwereɔ oya, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli kɛji amɛyi fa babaoo.

english: How can I check if my yam plants have root nematodes before it is time to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni ji nematodes dani kpamɔ be lɛ aba?

english: You can look for early warning signs above ground like stunted growth and yellow leaves, or carefully dig up one or two sample roots to check for strange bumps or lesions.
ga: Obaanyɛ otao kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ mra yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ dalɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Aloo okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shishifã lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ kome loo enyɔ he nii koni ona kɛji ŋmeii loo ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ srɔto yɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up tightly during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area, which helps the plant lose less water and survive drought.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu fioo ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when there is too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up air spaces in the soil and suffocates the roots, making it impossible for the plant to absorb essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛhe niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before they turn into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they face heat stress, extreme dry soil, or nutrient shortages as a way to save energy for basic survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo be mli. shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Enɛ ji gbɛ titri ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ hewalɛ toɔ koni anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does striga weed grow attached to the roots of my maize but not my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe shi ekpɛtɛɛɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: Striga seeds lie dormant in the soil and only germinate when they detect specific chemical signals continuously released by the roots of cereal crops like maize and sorghum.
ga: Striga dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji amɛna tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jeɔ kpo be fɛɛ be kɛjɛɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi amli.

english: Bacterial wilt organisms enter the stem from the soil and multiply until they block the water channels inside the plant, causing it to dry up even in wet soil.
ga: Muawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛshwereɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Ha ehi shi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when there are no plantain trees or shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miigboi yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, protecting the delicate seedlings from scorching while keeping the soil moist enough for them to establish strong roots.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni akashã amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow big, or when heavy rain has washed nutrients out of the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee eŋɔli ni amɛdara. aloo beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot inside the soil when it rains continuously for weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excessive rain in poorly drained soil causes waterlogging, which starves the cassava roots of oxygen. This soggy environment allows soil fungi to infect the tubers and cause rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Shihilɛ ni mli efɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or irregular watering, which prevents proper pollination from taking place.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Enɛ haaa amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong wind storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily be weakened by tiny soil pests like nematodes or root weevils, leaving the heavy plant without a firm grip on the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land season after season make my harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ haa mikpamɔ lɛ feɔ bibioo be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season while giving crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans on my farm make the soil better for my next corn crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special nodules on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil, effectively feeding natural fertilizer to the ground for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ anáa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves out in the sun so they can make food; if the leaves stay shaded on the ground, the underground tuber stays small.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo shishi lolo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baafee bibii.

english: Why do my cabbage plants keep growing big open leaves without forming a solid round head in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni agbeleɔ ni efeee yitso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form tight heads when the weather is too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when they are given too much nitrogen fertilizer late in their growth cycle.
ga: Kaabaji yitsoŋ tight kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shɛɔ sɛɛ yɛ dalɛ be lɛ mli.

english: How many weeks after planting my kontomire should I do the first weeding?
ga: Otsii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni midu kontomire lɛ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: You should do your first weeding about 2 to 3 weeks after planting kontomire. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing nutrients, light, and water from your young crop.
ga: Esa akɛ ofee oklɛŋklɛŋ jwɛi shwiemɔ aaafee otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ yɛ be mli ni odu contomire lɛ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Is it better to spray weeds when they are very young with just two leaves or when they grow bigger?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaafɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ beni amɛji bibii waa, ni amɛbaai enyɔ pɛ yɔɔ mli, loo beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: It is best to spray weeds when they are small, around the 2 to 4 leaf stage, because they are soft and absorb the chemical easily. Older, bigger weeds are tougher and require stronger, more expensive chemicals to clear.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ beni amɛji bibii, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee baai 2 kɛyashi 4, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛheɔ tsofai lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni egbɔ ni dara lɛ mli wa ni ebiɔ tsofai ni mli wa ni jara wa koni akɛjie amɛ.

english: Why does the weedkiller I bought kill some weeds on my farm but leave other weeds growing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mihe lɛ gbeɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shi ehaa jwɛi krokomɛi shwereɔ waa lɛ?

english: Different weedkillers target specific weed types. Selective herbicides only kill specific groups, like broadleaf weeds, while leaving grasses untouched. You must identify your main weed type before buying chemicals.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ jwɛi srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ gbeɔ kui pɔtɛɛ komɛi pɛ, tamɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ. ni jwɛi lɛ eshɛko he lolo Esa akɛ otsɔɔ jwɛi titri ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ dani ohé tsofai.

english: How can I spray herbicide on weeds without damaging my food crops growing in the same field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni maye niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ awui?

english: You can use a protective spray hood on your sprayer nozzle to direct the chemical only onto the weeds, or use a selective herbicide formulated specifically not to harm your exact crop type.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ yɛ jwɛi lɛ pɛ anɔ. Aloo okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni afee lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni yeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning soft and limp a few days after I sprayed weedkiller on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves go limp when chemical spray accidentally drifts onto the crop or when the wrong chemical is used. The chemical disrupts the plant's normal water uptake, causing the leaves to lose strength and wither.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ yɛ oshara mli loo kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni ejaaa wo mli. Tsofai tsiɔ nu ni tsei lɛ nuɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ naa. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛgboi.

english: What causes my young kontomire leaves to turn yellow and wither after a few weeks in the ground?
ga: Mɛni haa mibaai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young kontomire leaves wither mainly from excessive direct sunlight, lack of adequate soil moisture, or root damage caused by harsh chemicals applied too close to the stem.
ga: Contomires lɛ ateŋ babaoo baai bibii lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ tsɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he ni ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi tsɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: Will mixing extra weedkiller chemical in my knapsack sprayer make the weeds die faster without harming my soil?
ga: Ani tsofai krokomɛi ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ni mikɛfutuɔ misɛɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baagbe jwɛi lɛ oya ni eyeee mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: No, mixing chemicals stronger than recommended can burn your crop's roots and leave toxic residues in the soil. Always follow the recommended dosage on the chemical bottle for safe results.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni mli wa fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛfutu mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni eshi nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nyiɛmɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be koni ona yibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How long should I wait to plant my crops after spraying weedkiller on a freshly cleared bush?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni madu tsei beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie tsei bibii ni ajie ehee lɛ anɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait about 7 to 14 days after spraying before planting. This gives the herbicide enough time to break down in the soil so it does not attack your new seeds or seedlings.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 yɛ tsofa ni okɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani odu. Enɛ haa tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni egbeee odumɔwui loo odumɔwui heei lɛ.

english: Should I apply weed chemicals before my crops come out of the soil or after they start growing?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni amɛma shi shiŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: Pre-emergence chemicals are applied before crop seedlings emerge to stop weed seeds from germinating, while post-emergence chemicals are sprayed on actively growing weeds after your crop is already up.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni haa tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii dani tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo koni akɛtsi jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ jwɛi ni miida sɛɛ lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni miida lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni otsei lɛ edara sɛɛ.

english: How do I know if the weeds on my farm are grass weeds or broadleaf weeds before I go to the agro-dealer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ji jwɛi jwɛi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo? Dani ebaayakwɛ okwaayeli he jarayelɔ ko

english: Grass weeds have long, narrow leaves with straight parallel veins, while broadleaf weeds have wider, net-veined leaves that often grow in pairs or branching stems.
ga: Jwɛi jwɛi lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji, ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni fãji ni ja, ni kɛ amɛhe kpãa gbee. Shi jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ reticular-veined ni bei pii lɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji enyɔ loo niji amli.

english: How long will it take for my new mango tree to start giving me fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi mango tso hee lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: It depends on the type of seedling you plant. Traditional mango trees grown directly from seeds can take 5 to 7 years to bear fruit, while grafted seedlings that combine two plant parts usually produce fruit much faster, often within 2 to 3 years.
ga: Edamɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Kusum tsei ni akɛduɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 5 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛwo yibii. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni akɛwo tso lɛ mli ni kɛ tso lɛ fãi enyɔ lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ baa oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii 2 kɛyashi 3.

english: I saw some mango seedlings at the nursery that look like two plants joined together, what are they?
ga: Mina mango dumɔwu ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni etamɔ mango tsei enyɔ ni akɛfee ekome. Mɛɛ tso ni?

english: Those are called grafted seedlings, where a branch from a high-yielding mature tree is joined onto a strong young rootstock. This combination helps the tree grow faster, resist soil diseases, and produce sweet fruit much earlier than normal seedlings.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli. ni yɔɔ tso ni eda ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ mli niji ni akɛwo tso ni mli wa ni ji gbekɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ nibii ni akɛfee ekome nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. Enyɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai anaa ni ewoɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ

english: Is it better to plant a mango tree from a seed I saved from a sweet fruit or buy a grafted seedling from a nursery?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsɔ dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ aduawai ni ŋɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ makwɛ mango tso loo mahe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko?

english: It is much better to buy a grafted seedling from a certified nursery. Seeds from fruits you ate take many years to bear fruit and may not taste like the original fruit, whereas grafted seedlings are guaranteed to produce good, marketable fruit in a much shorter time.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui ni jɛɔ aduawai ni oyeɔ lɛ amli lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii, ni ekolɛ amɛhe ejɔɔɔ tamɔ shishijee aduawai lɛ. yɛ be mli ni anáa nɔmimaa akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kwraa.

english: What time of the year is best for me to plant young mango seedlings on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ afi lɛ mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu mango dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant mango seedlings in Ghana is at the beginning of the major rainy season, around April or May. Planting early in the rainy season allows the young roots to establish deeply with plenty of natural soil moisture before the dry season starts.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu mango dumɔwui yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli. Aaafee April loo May Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my young mango tree is ready to start bearing fruit?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni o-mango tso lɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaawo yibii?

english: A mango tree ready for fruiting will develop a thick, sturdy trunk and dense green leaves, and it will begin putting out bright cluster flowers at the ends of its branches, usually during the dry spell between November and January.
ga: Mango tsei ni efee klalo akɛ amɛbaawo yibii lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli tse kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni ebaaje shishi ewo fɔfɔi yɛ kui ni kpɛɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anaagbee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji hɔmɔ be ni yɔɔ November kɛ January teŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my mango tree dropping off before turning into small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mango tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai bibii lɛ?

english: Mango flowers often fall off due to dry weather, strong winds, or pests like thrips and diseases like powdery mildew. Ensuring adequate watering during dry spells and applying proper organic or approved sprays during early flowering helps the tree hold onto its fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ thrips kɛ helai tamɔ powdery mildew hewɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni awo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli, ni akɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔii lɛ fɔɔ mra lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why did my mango tree give me plenty of fruit last year but very few fruits this year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli shi afi nɛɛ amɛwo yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: This is a natural behavior called alternate bearing. When a tree produces a very heavy harvest, it uses up most of its stored energy and nutrient reserves, leaving it too exhausted to form many flowers and fruits in the following year.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ nɔ kroko ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii waa lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii. Shi ni egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai babaoo aba yɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How much space should I leave between my mango trees when I am planting them?
ga: Gbɛ enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi yɛ mi mango tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ?

english: You should leave about 8 to 10 meters of space between each tree. Giving them enough room ensures that branches receive enough sunlight and roots do not fight for nutrients, leading to healthier trees and bigger fruit yields.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10 yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niji lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ ewuuuu kɛha niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or groundnuts between my young mango trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi mango tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, during the first 2 to 3 years when the mango trees are small, you can intercrop with low-growing plants like maize, beans, or groundnuts. This provides you with extra food and income while helping to keep weeds under control around your young trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli lɛ, mango tso lɛ ji bibioo. Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni shwereɔ fioo tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa adu lɛ. Enɛ baaha oná niyenii kɛ shika kroko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ anɔ. o tso bibioo lɛ

english: What causes my mango fruits to get dark spots and rot while hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mango lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ beni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots and rotting are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose or by fruit fly attacks. Pruning the tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow inside the canopy, along with clearing fallen, spoiled fruit from the ground, helps control this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ ŋmeii baa. Niji ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli Kɛfata aduawai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he. baaye abua ni akudɔ naagba nɛɛ.

english: If I use muddy pond water to spray medicine on my crops, will it still work properly?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji tsu nii kɛshwie ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Ani ebaatsu nii lolo bɔ ni sa?

english: No, muddy or dirty water binds to the chemical particles in crop medicine and weakens them, making the spray far less effective against pests and diseases. Always use clear water for mixing plant medicines.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji baakpɛtɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ tso tsofa lɛ mli lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ kooloi kɛ helai agbemɔ mli. Kɛ nu ni mli tse atsu nii be fɛɛ be kɛ́ oofutu tsei ahe tsofai.

english: If I use dirty stream water to irrigate my vegetables, will it make the plants sick?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji wo aduawai anɔ lɛ Ani ebaaha tso lɛ aná hela?

english: Yes, water taken from contaminated streams can carry harmful bacteria and fungi that stick to plant leaves and stems, causing fruit rot and leaf spots. Letting water settle in a tank before light irrigation helps reduce dirty particles.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ faai ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ kɛ baai lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni nu lɛ shwie tanki lɛ mli dani afɔse nu fioo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni muji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize crop turn yellow when rain water stands on my field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the field without draining, soil air is squeezed out and root systems choke. Unable to breathe, the maize roots stop absorbing nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Beni nu yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Abɛi shishifãi kpaɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ hɔmɔ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my corn after a rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-ŋmãa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, native plants adapted to local soil with deep seed reserves. They wake up and drink water instantly, whereas cultivated crops take longer to establish their roots after planting.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji ni dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Amɛte shi ni amɛnu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi baa shi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plant before producing any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani pepper yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get stressed by sudden heat, dry soil, or excessive water. Giving plants steady, moderate water and light shade during hot spells helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu babaoo hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei daa, ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops leaves from making food properly, which reduces the size of cassava tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ahe baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmeii ni ji mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ ahoo jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get dark, flat spots at the bottom while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishigbɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the growing fruit, usually due to irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if yellow leaves on my crop mean the soil is hungry or insects are attacking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akɛ kooloi bibii miitutua amɛ?

english: If soil lacks nutrients, the yellowing usually starts on the oldest lower leaves in a uniform pattern. If insects are attacking, you will see irregular spots, hole damage, webbing, or leaf curling on new leaves.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ jeɔ shishi yɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni yaa nɔ daa nɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii tutua Obaana hei ni yɔɔ srɔto, bu ni efite, tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli, loo baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ yɛ baai heei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow very fast right after I burn bush on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mishã jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning bush releases trapped plant minerals into ash, which quickly feeds the crop like a fast fertilizer. However, burning kills good soil organisms and destroys organic matter, weakening soil health in future seasons.
ga: Tsoi ni ashã lɛ jieɔ mineral kɛjɛɔ tsei ni amɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli akɛ sũ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nii lɛ niyenii oya tamɔ bɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and dying in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to survive, as their leaves burn easily and the soil loses moisture quickly without shade during their early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛhi shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant needs extra nutrients or fertilizer to feed its leafy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi he miihia tso lɛ koni ekɛha ebaai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle whorl of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ye bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ ring lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on the soft center leaves of maize plants and needs early treatment to save the harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai bibii lɛ. ni ehe miihia ni atsa lɛ mra. koni akɛkwɛ nibii ni afee lɛ anɔ

english: How can I tell underground cassava tubers are big enough and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is generally ready between 8 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally dry up and turn yellow, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the dried vegetation on my field when preparing the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashãa tsei ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ asaa ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛha dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter in the soil and kills living micro-organisms that help feed crop roots and retain soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ ni egbeɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei shishifãi yeɔ nii ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Removing excess shoots, called suckers, leaves only one or two strong stalks so all the water and soil nutrients go into growing larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ bɔni afee ni niyenii ni yɔɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ aya plantain jwɛi wulu lɛ mli.

english: Staking allows the yam leaves to spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which provides the energy the plant needs to build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo. Enɛ ji hewalɛ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Should I sow my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until rains become regular, because a single early rain is often followed by a long hot dry spell that can dry out and kill freshly sown seeds.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ kome ni nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, hɔmɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: How do I apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it off my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Place fertilizer a few inches away from the plant stem into a small hole or shallow trench and cover it with soil when the ground is moist.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo bu bibioo ko mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko. loo ŋshɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ sũ aha he kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off due to extreme heat, insufficient soil moisture during flowering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed for fruit formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. aloo niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai afeemɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting shade trees or plantains alongside young cocoa protects them from heat stress until they are strong enough.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ dɔlɛ he haomɔ naa kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds very close to each other to get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and small, poor ears. Giving them proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to produce a good yield.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ he tsɔ lɛ fiteɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii ni ehiii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves and small worms inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii Yɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on young maize leaves and growing points. Spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms are active helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant sap and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays keeps the foliage healthy and flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water settles around them for too long, causing fungal decay. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the soil well-aerated.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu ta shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni ekɛ fungal fitemɔ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ baa.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize crop so it grows strong?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo mi-ŋma lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best practice is to apply NPK fertilizer about 10 to 14 days after planting when roots have formed, followed by a top-dressing of Urea 4 to 6 weeks later when the plant is knee-high.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ ebɔi. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji ŋwɛi atade ni akɛ urea woɔ mli yɛ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato flowers often drop due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of key nutrients like potassium and boron. Maintaining steady moisture in the soil and feeding the plants balanced fertilizers helps fruits set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium kɛ boron ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ama shi shiŋŋ.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves off the damp ground up into the sunlight, which maximizes leaf growth, improves air circulation, and reduces fungal infections from soil contact.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daraa kɛyashɛɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ aba shi

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy and adapted to quickly grab water and soil nutrients before crops can establish themselves. Clearing weeds early prevents them from choking your main crop and stealing vital plant food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii oya ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli oya dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo otsei titrii lɛ amli ni amɛkaju tsei niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same farm?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfata ŋmãa he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas alongside maize improves soil fertility because legumes take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally feeding the maize plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ kɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmãa tsei

english: Is it better to grow only cocoa on my field, or should I mix it with other crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too makwɛ cocoa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mikɛ tsei krokomɛi afutu mli?

english: Growing multiple crops alongside your cocoa trees gives them extra strength and support, creating a healthier farm environment that helps cocoa produce better yields.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei babaoo yɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ kroko. Bɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa kookoo ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How does having different types of plants on my farm make my cocoa trees stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei srɔtoi ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-cacao tsei lɛ mli waa?

english: A farm with a good mixture of crops creates a supportive surrounding environment that protects the cocoa trees and gives them the strength needed to bear plenty of pods.
ga: Okwaafoi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ baa. Enɛ buɔ cacao tso lɛ he ni ehaa enáa hewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Will planting food crops near my cocoa trees steal nutrients away from the cocoa?
ga: Ani niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ kookoo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When done correctly, growing companion crops together actually supports and strengthens the main cocoa crop rather than harming its growth.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Intercropping baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni ewo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ hewalɛ. yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefite edalɛ

english: Why do cocoa trees planted near other plants seem to look healthier than ones growing alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni kookoo tsei ni adu yɛ tsei krokomɛi ahe lɛ yɛ hewalɛ fe kookoo tsei ni adu amɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees thrive in diverse plant environments where surrounding vegetation helps shield them and improves the overall strength of the farm ecosystem.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ tsei srɔtoi babaoo amli. he ni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni abuɔ amɛhe ni eha ŋmɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ ahewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What causes some cocoa trees on a farm to yield a lot of pods while others do not?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni ekrokomɛi hu wooo?

english: A heavy cocoa harvest happens when cocoa trees gain strength from a balanced, supportive farm environment with beneficial surrounding crops.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa kɛji kookoo tsei lɛ ná hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ ni ja ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. hehia

english: How can I tell if my farm environment is supporting my cocoa trees properly?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shihilɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiye abua mi cacao tsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your farm environment is well-balanced with companion crops, your cocoa trees will show high strength and produce an abundant pod yield.
ga: Kɛji shihilɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ja O-cacao tsei lɛ baajie hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ kpo ni amɛbaawo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: What is the best way to keep my cocoa farm producing well year after year?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ awo yibii afi fɛɛ afi?

english: Maintaining a farm that integrates cocoa with other supportive plants provides long-term strength to the trees, helping sustain high yields over time.
ga: Okwaafoi ni kɛ kookoo kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi feɔ ekome lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ. Ebaaha tso lɛ mli awa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli. ni eye ebua ni ahi yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ mli yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ mli.

english: How can growing cocoa improve my family's financial situation?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kookoo dumɔ baanyɛ aha miweku lɛ shika shihilɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Cocoa is a valuable cash crop that, when managed well alongside complementary plants, yields heavily and provides reliable income to support your household.
ga: Cocoa ji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni, kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛfata ŋmɔshi nibii ni awo mli hewalɛ lɛ ahe lɛ, Ebaawo yibii babaoo ni ekɛ shika ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni akɛyeɔ abuaa oshia lɛ baaha.

english: How can I reduce financial stress while waiting for my cocoa trees to produce pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahã shika he haomɔ aba shi yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni cacao tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Planting other crops alongside your cocoa gives you additional harvests and income, reducing financial worries while your main cocoa crop develops strength.
ga: Kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha onibii kɛ shika ni onáa lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa shika he haomɔi baa shi yɛ be mli ni o-cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ naa hewalɛ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend mixed cropping for smallholder farmers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ okwaafoi bibii lɛ ŋaa akɛ amɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Mixing crops strengthens your primary cocoa trees for better harvests while giving you multiple sources of income to secure your financial position.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ o-cacao tsei titrii lɛ koni amɛná kpamɔ kpakpa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onáa shika srɔtoi ni baaha oná shika babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning brown and crisp during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight and hot dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a leafy umbrella that shields the trees and retains soil moisture until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ kookoo bibii ni aduɔ. Ehaa baai ni buɔ tso lɛ he ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ daa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow starting from the middle tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tips in maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green growth, so applying NPK fertilizer or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Does it matter which direction I point cassava stems when pushing them into the ground?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ, ani ebaatsɔɔ mɛɛ gbɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the raised buds or leaf scars pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the shoots and roots grow weak, resulting in a very poor harvest of tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu yucca tsei lɛ ni ŋmeii ni awo nɔ loo baai lɛ ahe okadii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛtee shishi lɛ Tsoi kɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni akpaa lɛ ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do I need to clear land to put tall wooden poles for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔjie shikpɔŋ lɛ koni wɔkɛ tsei kakadaji awo mli koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers based on how much direct sunlight their leaves receive. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground to capture light efficiently and prevents fungal leaf diseases from soil contact.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ bɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni enyɛ emɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Ni tsi fungal leaf hela lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ he.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black rot at the bottom of tomatoes is usually blossom-end rot, caused by irregular watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Maintaining steady soil moisture and adding agricultural lime or compost prevents this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ ni ji diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii ashishi ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: What is eating hole-filled tunnels inside the central funnel of my young maize crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ maye ŋshɔŋloo ko ni bu eyi mli obɔ yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋ gbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on soft central leaves. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or putting clean sand mixed with wood ash into the leaf funnel early can destroy these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ tso sũ efutu mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ amli mra. baanyɛ akpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the green leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which also spread plant viruses. Spraying plants with organic neem oil or soap solutions helps control these insects early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli hu Kɛ akɛ organic neem fɔ loo samla ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra.

english: Why should I cut away the small sucker shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ajie midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: Having too many suckers causes them to steal nutrients, water, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing excess shoots so only two or three remain ensures the main plant produces a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Shikpɔŋhosomɔi babaoo baaha amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eshwɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I wait to weed my farm until the weeds are tall?
