ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mimɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight during their most critical growth stage. Weeding early within the first three to four weeks allows your main crops to establish strong root systems without competition.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ nu he akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la yɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ enɛ baaha onibii titri lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my newly planted young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide the necessary shade and keep the soil moist while your cocoa trees are establishing themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ miida lɛ.

english: How do I know which way to stick my cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem; they should always point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the plant to waste energy trying to grow roots in the wrong direction, leading to poor yields.
ga: Kwɛmɔ hiŋmɛii bibii lɛ loo ŋmeii bibii lɛ. yɛ tso lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Cassava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ shishifãi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ ni ehiii

english: Should I put chemical fertilizer in the soil at the same time I put my maize seeds in the ground?
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli. Ni okɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ loo okɛwooo?

english: It is better to wait about one to two weeks after seeds germinate before applying basal fertilizer. Putting heavy fertilizer directly against fresh seeds can burn them and prevent them from sprouting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii wo dumɔwui heei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ ni eha amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow leaves, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize on the exact same farm land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ babaoo. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why do people spread dry grass around the base of pepper and tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, called mulching, traps moisture in the ground so you water less often, stops weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool during hot afternoons.
ga: Mulch ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ, tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Do I really need to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mato tsei koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yes, staking holds yam leaves up off the ground so they can catch more sunlight and fresh air. This extra sunlight allows the plant to make more food, which results in much bigger yam tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Nɛkɛ hulu la ni fa nɛɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ agboi babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my corn plants getting big ragged holes in them with tiny caterpillar droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ yɛ buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing centers of corn plants. Catching them early and applying organic neem oil mixtures or recommended insecticides inside the leaf funnels saves the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛfutu mli loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist during hot weather helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji dɔlɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds from my farm when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Small crop seedlings cannot compete with aggressive weeds for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the resources they need to build strong stems and roots.
ga: Tsei bibii adumɔwui nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water. Applying a small amount of NPK fertilizer early in the growth stage helps the plant build strong leaves and regain its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko wo tso lɛ mli mra yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava sticks too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of developing big tubers, the plants will grow tall and thin with very small roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ yitso agbo ni eeefee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ Tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛshishifãi bibii waa.

english: When is the best stage for me to apply fertilizer to my pepper crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mikɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ awo mli?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is during early growth when the roots are expanding, and right before the plants start producing flower buds. Applying fertilizer too late when fruits are already big will not improve your yield much.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo mli ji be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ mra. Ni dani tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli sɛɛ tsɔ beni aduawai lɛ dara momo lɛ, no haŋ onibii lɛ aya hiɛ babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by excessive sunlight, dry weather, or insect damage. Planting shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia near young cocoa helps maintain moisture and protects the delicate blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shɛ hulu la ni naa wa he. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo gliricidia ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɛ̃i hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough organic food before planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa dani madu tomato?

english: Healthy soil for tomatoes should crumble easily in your hands and look dark brown or black. If the soil is hard, pale, or sandy, mixing in rotted animal manure or decomposed leaf compost will give your plants the nutrients they need.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tomato lɛ akumɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni efee tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ ŋã lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo baai ashishifãi ni egbo fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea leaves curl in intense afternoon heat as a survival mechanism to reduce leaf surface area. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent excessive water loss until temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli akɛ wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ fe nine lɛ naa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are black spots spreading across the leaves of my yam vines during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves during heavy rains are typically caused by a fungal leaf spot disease called anthracnose. Spacing your crops to allow air movement and removing affected leaves early prevents the fungus from destroying the whole vine.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni haa sweet potato baa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli ni ojie baai ni ena naagbai lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekafite wain tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it necessary for me to clear weeds while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: In their early stages, young crops have small roots and cannot outgrow fast-moving weeds. Clearing weeds early ensures the young crop gets all the available water, sunlight, and soil nutrients without struggling.
ga: Yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye jwɛi ni hoɔ oya lɛ anɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ nine shɛɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbɔɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: Can watering my garden crops too frequently harm their growth?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛhaa mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ shii abɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛdalɛ awui?

english: Yes, excessive watering fills up air spaces in the soil, effectively suffocating the plant roots. Without oxygen, roots begin to rot, causing the plant to turn yellow and wilt even though the soil is wet.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe nine lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ayi obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baabɔi fitemɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are ready to be harvested from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts show maturity when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off naturally. You can confirm by pulling up one plant; if the inside of the pods has dark brown or black vein markings, the groundnuts are ready for harvest.
ga: Peanuts jieɔ dalɛ kpo kɛji baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ tsei lɛ eko ni oootsi kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ loo ediŋŋ Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them directly in an open field without any trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni tsei bɛ he lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green foliage. When nitrogen runs low, the plant moves what little it has to the new upper leaves, causing the bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛji nitrogen faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit while it is developing. It frequently happens when watering is uneven, which prevents the roots from absorbing the calcium present in the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni edaa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaving small caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa? yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the growing center or funnel of the maize plant to feed. Spraying appropriate treatments early in the morning or late in the evening directly into the central shoot helps stop them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ loo gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛyeɔ nii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie he ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa helatsamɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are ready to harvest without digging up the whole root system?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shishifãi lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava plants show maturity when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. The stem near the ground also becomes thicker and woody, usually between 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Tsoi ashishifãi ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni eyɛ tsei. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to build large soil mounds before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ama gɔŋ agbo ko dani adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, deep soil to expand downward without resistance, producing long and smooth tubers. Mounds also improve water drainage around the plant so that heavy rain does not sit at the base and rot the seed.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shi ni nɔ ko nɔ ko tsiii amɛnaa. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu haa nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa akashwie shishigbɛ ni eha dumɔwui lɛ akagbo.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ efeɔ tsɔne yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense mechanism pepper plants use to conserve moisture when it gets hot and dry. By curling their leaves, plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji hebuu gbɛ ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa ehiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni nu lɛ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow slowly even if I cleared the field completely before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ fɛɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and continuously steal essential soil nutrients, water, and sunlight from your plants' roots. Keeping your farm clean during the first 4 to 6 weeks after planting prevents weeds from starving your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpea or groundnuts between my rows of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ mi-corn ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpea and groundnut take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through small nodules on their roots. This enriches the soil naturally, feeding the surrounding maize plants and improving overall yield.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ globules bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ mli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle ohe lɛ niyenii. ni eha nibii ni anáa lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ

english: Why do small insects turn my stored maize grains into powder just a few weeks after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsakeɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ feɔ powda yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni akpaa nii lɛ?

english: These insects are grain weevils, and they multiply quickly if maize is stored before it is completely dry. Sun-drying your maize until the grains are thoroughly hard deprives the insects of the moisture they need to survive and breed.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji dumɔwui amli ŋmeii. Ni amɛshwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmãa lɛ dani egbi kwraa. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ebaaha kooloi bibii lɛ aná nu ni amɛkɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture for the young cocoa seedlings to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots, naturally enriching the ground for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient the plant needs to build strong, green leaves and produce healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl inward during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli ni nu egbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the heat is a defense mechanism where the pepper plant rolls its leaves to slow down water loss through evaporation during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa mli lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he ni pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi fioo kɛtsɔ hulutsoo be mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients, causing it to shed flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Haa amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite

english: Why does my maize grow taller when I clear the weeds early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ daa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with maize for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing them early ensures the maize plant gets all the food it needs to grow tall and produce big cobs.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo ŋmãa wuji.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl into the central funnel of the maize plant and chew through the tender emerging leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii ni miiba lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up the whole field?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni ŋmei eshɛ he ni abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack from expanding tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ, efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to manufacture food for growing heavy tubers under the soil, and staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight and avoid rotting.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni tsii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Ni okɛ ohe awo mli, ni owó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni onine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Why shouldn't I allow too many suckers to grow around one main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ he lɛ? trunk wulu kome

english: Allowing too many suckers forces them to compete with the main plant for food and water, resulting in smaller bunches; leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures bigger plantain yields.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ abɔi niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso bibioo ko Suckers ni yɔɔ hewalɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ eshwɛ koni plantain yibii babaoo aba.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as food for the leaves, or when heavy rains wash away nutrients and drown the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ babaoo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ nitrogen, ni haa baai lɛ niyenii. Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli lɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil richer for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo aha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the crop season ends, those roots decay and release natural fertilizer into the soil.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and short if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ gbɔjɔmɔ ni efeɔ kuku kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, soil water, and nutrients before your crop's roots get a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during hot, dry spells to avoid losing water through transpiration, keeping its underground tubers alive until the rains return.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni egbiɔ koni nu akafite kɛtsɔ nu ni faaa lɛ nɔ. ni oha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop without setting fruit when the plants experience severe heat stress, poor watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ tso lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe. nu ni ehiii loo ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa

english: Why are there ragged holes and white powdery spots on my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ powder yɛŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide in the central funnel of the maize plant during the day and feed on fresh green tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni oye fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ hee

english: Why do I get smaller yields when I plant my seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crowding crops forces their roots and leaves to compete intensely for space, light, and soil moisture, preventing any single plant from growing to its full capacity.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ shishifãi kɛ baai anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha he ko, la, kɛ sũ mli nu. Etsiɔ tso pɔtɛɛ ko naa koni ekadara kɛyashɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I prune the extra shoots or suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine loo ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Extra suckers drain water and energy away from the main mother plant, which reduces the size of the plantain bunch it can produce.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi jieɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa plantain ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ afee lɛ ayibɔ baa shi.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sun, allowing the plant to absorb maximum sunlight to produce energy that gets stored as large underground tubers.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why does cassava start to rot and turn dark inside within just a few days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ ni efeɔ duŋ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava is cut from its stem, exposure to oxygen causes natural chemical changes and decay inside the root since it can no longer defend itself.
ga: Beni afoɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi Oxygen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tsakemɔi kɛ fitemɔ baa shishifãi lɛ amli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu amɛhe dɔŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, which acts as its main food, or when waterlogging prevents the roots from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ titri. aloo be mli ni nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when the dry season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight, which is why they require shade crops like plantains to protect them until they grow stronger.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛná tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains koni amɛbu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa lɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot in wet ground due to fungal diseases that thrive in heavy, poorly drained soil, especially when infected stem cuttings are used during planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested yams develop soft black spots and rot quickly in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly in storage when they get small cuts during harvesting or when stored in a hot, crowded room without cool air circulating around them.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afolɔ mli bibii bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo kɛ́ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mangoes develop dark patches on the skin right as they begin to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango lɛ feɔ okadii diji yɛ ehewolo nɔ kɛji ebɔi ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ?

english: Dark patches on ripening mangoes are caused by a fungal infection called anthracnose, which infects the fruit during rainy weather and shows up as the fruit softens.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mango ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. ni baagbɛ hela lɛ eshwa aduawai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, ni ebaaje kpo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ efee blɛoo.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even when rainfall is good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Continuous planting on the same piece of land without adding organic manure or rotating crops drains the soil of essential plant nutrients, making the land tired.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo atsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ lɛ fitemɔ

english: How can I tell if I have applied too much chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ miitsu nii tsɔ?

english: Too much fertilizer causes the edges of crop leaves to turn brown and look scorched, and it can damage the roots so the plant stops growing.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashishigbɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã. ni ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ tso lɛ kpa dalɛ

english: Why are buyers rejecting my harvested vegetables because of chemical spray residues?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ miikpoo mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Harvesting crops too soon after spraying pesticides leaves dangerous chemical residues on the produce, which makes the crop unsafe for consumers and leads to rejection by export and local buyers.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa mra tsɔ yɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui shwieɔ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha mɛi ni yeɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ kpoomɔ ni jɛɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ kɛ maŋbii ni heɔ nii lɛ adɛŋ baa.

english: Why do my pineapples taste sour even when they look big and yellow on the outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ ŋɔɔ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eda ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kponɔgbɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Pineapples do not get sweeter after they are harvested, so if they are picked too early before their natural sugars develop fully on the stalk, they will remain sour.
ga: Pineapple lɛ baafee nɔ ni ŋɔɔ fe tsutsu lɛ beni akpa lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ ajie lɛ mra tsɔ, dani adebɔɔ mli sugars lɛ baadara lɛ, Pineapple lɛ baaná ŋmɔlɔ lolo.

english: If I use water from a river near a galamsey site to water my vegetables, why are the leaves turning yellow and dying?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ Galamsey lɛ mli lɛ tsu nii kɛwo aduawai anɔ nu. Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Water contaminated by illegal mining often contains heavy metals and toxic chemicals. These poisons block the plant's roots from taking up clean water and good nutrients, which causes the leaves to turn yellow, dry up, and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ nu ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli woɔ mli lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ tsofai fɔji nɛɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ wuɔfɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Can heavy metals from polluted river water actually get inside my cassava or maize crops?
ga: Ani dade ni tsii ni jɛ faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abote mi-cassava loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, crop roots naturally absorb water along with whatever is dissolved in it. If the irrigation water contains heavy metals, the plant will draw those toxins straight into its roots, stems, and fruits, making the harvested food dangerous to eat.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsei shishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ nibii ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ dade ni tsii yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ yaa amɛshishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛyibii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni akpaa lɛ yɛ oshara akɛ aaaye.

english: Will boiling or filtering muddy river water make it safe enough for me to use in my crop nursery?
ga: Ani sũ mli nu ni mikɛshãa loo mikɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baaha efee shweshweeshwe bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ?

english: Boiling or simple cloth filtering removes dirt and bacteria, but it cannot remove chemical pollutants or heavy metals like mercury. Using that water on young crop seedlings will still stunt their growth or kill them.
ga: Atade ni ahoo loo daa ni akɛjieɔ muji kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ. Shi ejieee tsofai ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ loo dade ni tsii tamɔ mercury lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nakai nu lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔwui bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛdaramɔ aya hiɛ lolo loo ebaagbe amɛ.

english: Is underground borehole water always safer for my crops than taking water from a local river?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii fe nu ni jɛɔ faa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii?

english: Borehole water is usually safer because the earth filters out surface dirt. However, if deep mining activities are nearby, heavy metals can sometimes sink into shallow groundwater, so it is best to test the water before using it for large-scale crop farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ejaakɛ sũ lɛ shwieɔ muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Shi, kɛji akɛ shika tsuru ni mli kwɔ yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, Bei komɛi lɛ, dade ni tsii baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aka nu lɛ akwɛ dani akɛtsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why are my crops growing so slowly on land that was previously used for illegal mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ shika tsuru tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil and leaves behind hard, infertile earth contaminated with heavy metals. Crops struggle to grow because the soil lacks necessary nutrients and beneficial organisms, making it hard for roots to spread.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ, ni eshiɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni dade ni tsii ewo mli lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ejaakɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã

english: How can I tell if heavy metals in my soil are the reason my plant growth is stunted?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa mitsei lɛ miigbɔjɔ?

english: You cannot see or smell heavy metals in the soil or plants. The only sure way to know if your crops are suffering from metal toxicity is to collect soil and plant samples and have them tested by an agricultural extension office or laboratory.
ga: Onyɛŋ ona loo onu dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei amli lɛ he. Gbɛ pɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ ole kɛji dade ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ ji ni okɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei ahe saji aba ni oha okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe loo laboratori ko aka amɛ akwɛ.

english: Can adding animal manure help my crops survive in soil that has been affected by nearby mining runoff?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shika tsuru ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ efite lɛ nɔ?

english: Adding plenty of organic manure helps rebuild damaged soil by providing nutrients and binding to some harmful metals, reducing how much poison the crop roots absorb. However, if the soil is severely polluted, manure alone will not make the land safe.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni esaa shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ dade komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofai fɔji ni tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ baa shi. Shi, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji waa lɛ, Manure pɛ nyɛŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomatoes look small and taste bad when I irrigate them with water from local streams near mining areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ bibioo ni ehiii kwraa kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsaa shika tsuru yɛ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Stream water mixed with mining waste interferes with the crop's natural metabolism. Toxic elements prevent the plant from properly developing its fruit, resulting in smaller size, abnormal shapes, and poor flavor.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ faai amli ni akɛ sũ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shika tsuru mli lɛ efutu mli lɛ gbalaa bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkawo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji bibioo ni dalɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli ni ehiii kwraa

english: Why is it risky to grow leafy greens like kontomire near rivers influenced by galamsey?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ contomire yɛ faa ko ni galamsey yɔɔ mli lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Leafy green vegetables naturally absorb liquid rapidly and store high concentrations of heavy metals directly in their broad leaves. Even if the plant looks green and healthy, those leaves can carry dangerous toxins to anyone who eats them.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni amɛhiɛɔ dade ni tsii babaoo yɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ Shi nakai baai lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛya mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops survive near polluted streams while other crops die quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi hiɔ shi yɛ faai ni mli ewo muji lɛ ahe, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi gboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Different crops react differently to soil and water pollution. Deep-rooted or hardy plants might resist the damage for a while, whereas sensitive crops with shallow roots quickly absorb water toxins and collapse.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi feɔ amɛnii yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli mujiwoo he yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ. Tsei ni shishifãi ebɔle amɛhe loo amɛhe wa lɛ baanyɛ ateshi nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ be ko. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ shwieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ nu lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛkuɔ shi oya.

english: How do I know if my crops are dying from lack of rain or if they are just resting in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigboi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ loo mikɛ mihe miijɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Crops curl or droop their leaves in the afternoon heat to reduce water loss, but if their leaves stay dry and limping early in the morning when it is cool, they are suffering from severe water shortage.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ egbi lolo ni amɛgbɔjɔ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tsei lɛ waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plant roll up like narrow pipes when the weather stays dry for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe tamɔ tsɔnei bibii lɛ? Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up during drought to hide their surface area from the hot sun, which stops moisture from evaporating quickly and keeps the plant alive while waiting for rain.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛ amɛhiɛ he lɛ ato hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi be mli ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ lɛ

english: What can I spread on my farm soil to stop the sun from drying out the earth so quickly?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover—known as mulching—blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and traps moisture for your crops to use longer.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ shwieɔ tsei ahe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni onibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is safer to wait until the ground has absorbed steady rain over a few days, because the very first rain is often followed by a dry stretch that can burn up new seedlings.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui heei lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my cassava dropping off when the dry heat starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ bɔi amɛgbimɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves during dry spells to lower its demand for water, allowing the plant to preserve moisture and protect its tubers under the soil.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛba nu he hiamɔ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do wild weeds keep staying green on my farm even when my planted crops are wilting from heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbi kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli po

english: Weeds have deeper and tougher root systems that reach far underground to drink hidden water before your crops' younger roots can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eyashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ koni enu nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ dani tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn yellow when heavy water sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaa shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu eyi miŋmɔji amli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like human beings; when standing water covers the field, it chokes the roots and prevents them from taking up plant food.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Beni nu ni yɔɔ dioo lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Will planting groundnuts between my maize rows cause them to steal water from each other during dry spells?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ abɔi nu he akaŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Groundnuts cover the ground like a carpet to keep the soil shaded and moist, and their roots add useful plant food into the soil that actually helps the maize grow better.
ga: Akpɔlɔi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni edɔ. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ tsei niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni eyeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I pack too many seeds close together to save space on my land?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for the small water and soil food available, leading to thin stalks and very small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii fioo komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do some seed varieties produce good food even when the rain season ends early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi woɔ niyenii kpakpa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee mra moŋ lɛ?

english: Some short-duration seed varieties are bred to grow and produce their yield quickly before the dry weather sets in, making them reliable even with short rain seasons.
ga: Afɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi ni hiɔ shi be kuku koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo yibii oya dani kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ aba. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ mli po.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight without protection. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to act as living umbrellas that keep the air cool and the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ mli kɛji akɛ abuuu amɛhe. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very bushy leaves but yields only tiny cassava tubers beneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ cassava ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi pɛ

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or excessive fertilizer, the cassava plant directs all its energy into growing big green leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly into narrow tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Maize plants roll up their leaves on hot afternoons as a defense mechanism to shield themselves from sunlight and prevent water from evaporating too quickly from their leaves.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same piece of land with my maize without damaging my main crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni mifiteee miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas trap natural nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger without stealing its space.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni eŋɔɔɔ he ko.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off before any small green tomatoes appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tomato bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without forming fruit when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes rapidly from very dry to very wet, causing severe stress to the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tsei anɔ.

english: Why is my farm land giving me lower crop yields now compared to three years ago on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi lɛ baa shi fe afii etɛ ni eho nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing crops continuously on the same soil without resting the land or adding organic manure exhausts the natural nutrients, leaving the soil too weak to support healthy plant growth.
ga: Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛhaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ amɛhe loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why are my cassava leaves showing twisted yellow patterns instead of staying completely green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsake yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ emuu lɛ?

english: Yellow twisted leaves on cassava are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a common virus spread by tiny white insects or by planting infected stem cuttings.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ loo tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my young orange trees drop all their small immature fruits before they get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso bibioo lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young citrus trees drop immature fruit when they lack sufficient water or when the tree is still too young and weak to feed all the fruits it started forming.
ga: Citrus tsei bibii lɛ baashwie amɛyibii ni eshɛko lɛ ashwie shi kɛ́ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ amɛhe. aloo beni tso lɛ ji gbekɛ tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua aduawai fɛɛ ni ebɔi feemɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my planted yam setts take several weeks in the soil before any green shoots start to emerge?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni miduɔ lɛ heɔ otsii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ jeɔ shishi ejɛɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural sleeping period called dormancy after harvest. A yam sett will not sprout until this sleeping phase ends naturally, even if planted in moist soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ hejɔɔmɔ. Sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛŋ kɛyashi nɛkɛ wɔɔhe be nɛɛ baagbe naa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ po

english: Why do my maize plants grow very thin and tall with weak stems when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete fiercely for sunlight, forcing them to stretch upward quickly and tall, resulting in thin, weak stalks that fall easily.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ akpã oya ni amɛkwɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. It can also happen if the soil is too waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye niyenii.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant maize in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients that maize relies on, and it allows pests and soil diseases that target maize to build up and ruin future harvests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni abɛi lɛ damɔ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ baajɛ mli aba. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛfiteɔ wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do I know if I am planting my cassava stem cuttings the right way up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look at the tiny buds or nodes on the stem; they should point upward toward the sky. If you plant the stems upside down, the plant will struggle to sprout and yield very few tubers.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ amɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ baaná naagba yɛ shweremɔ mli ni ebaawo bulbs fioo ko pɛ.

english: Is it better for me to apply fertilizer right before it rains or after it rains?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer right after a light rain when the soil is moist. If you put fertilizer down right before a heavy rain, the water will wash it away before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he dani nugbɔ nɛ waa Nu lɛ baaho dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep wilting and drying up in my open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi yɛ miŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong direct sunlight. They need shade from plants like plantain trees during their first few years to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains amli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crop roots with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil, which is called mulching, keeps the ground cool and stops water from evaporating under the hot sun, helping your plants stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes in the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack young corn leaves and growing points. They hatch from eggs laid by moths and can destroy the crop if not spotted and treated early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ. Amɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji anaaa amɛ ni atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How do weeds cause my crops to grow so small and weak?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔɔ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they steal the sunlight, water, and soil nutrients that your crops need to grow big and strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe awa lɛ.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant transport calcium to the tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nu ni afɔɔɔ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium yaa tomatoi lɛ amli.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from sudden stress, such as extreme heat, lack of water, or giving the plant too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes it grow leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna nɔnyɛɛ trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine. Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if my family land is suitable for planting maize or if the soil is too tired?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miweku lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔ?

english: You can check your land by looking at what weeds grow on it and taking a handful of soil. Dark, rich soil that crumbles easily and holds moisture is good for maize, whereas pale, sandy, or heavily compacted soil means the land needs compost or manure before planting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. ni eŋɔ shikpɔŋ ko Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ nii babaoo ni fiteɔ oya ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmãa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ŋã loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu.

english: Why do my cassava stick cuttings fail to grow when I plant them during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni miduɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings require moist soil to stimulate root growth and sprouting. Without water, the stems dry out quickly and die underground before they have a chance to establish roots.
ga: Yucca tso lɛ shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ koni ewo shishifãi lɛ adalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛnáa hegbɛ amɛtoɔ shishifãi.

english: What happens to my cowpea plants if I plant the seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cowpea seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes them to grow lots of tall leaves instead of forming healthy seed pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu cowpea dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa baai kakadaji babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee dumɔwui akui ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when planted under shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need direct, full sunlight to generate energy for making flowers and fruit. When shaded, the plant wastes all its energy stretching upward to find light, leaving no energy to make tomatoes.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee hewalɛ ni ekɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Beni amɛyɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii beni amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛna la lɛ. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee tomato.

english: What causes the leaves of my young maize plants to turn yellow after a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain can fill up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots. When roots cannot breathe, they stop absorbing nutrients like nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu Ekpaa niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɔmɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Can I plant pepper and garden eggs next to each other on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: It is better to keep them separated because both crops belong to the same plant family and suffer from the same pests, like whiteflies and mites. Planting them together allows insects and diseases to spread quickly from one crop to the other.
ga: Esa akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ ejaakɛ amɛjɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ whiteflies kɛ mites. Tsoi ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa kooloi bibii kɛ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and staying very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects that stunts leaf development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni tsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest yield smaller crops than the fresh seeds I buy from the agricultural dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are often special hybrid varieties bred to be strong and high-yielding. When you save seeds from those plants, the secondary seeds lose those parent traits, leading to smaller and uneven crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayeli dumɔwui ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Kɛji obua dumɔwui anaa kɛjɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli lɛ Dumɔwui ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ amɛfɔlɔ sui lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeee ekome.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the next maize crop grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as natural fertilizer for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa henɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are mature and ready for harvesting without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ shwieee shi?

english: You can tell yam is mature by observing the vines above ground. When the leaves and stems naturally turn yellow, dry out, and die down at the end of the rainy season, it shows the tuber underground has finished growing.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole be ni sweet potato eda kɛtsɔ wain tso ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees prefer partial shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and causes severe water loss. Intercropping them with fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees creates a natural shelter that keeps the young cocoa cool and humid.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ sumɔɔ hulutsoo be fioo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni eha nu lɛ afite waa. Tsei ni akɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ adumɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli he ko ni haa kookoo bɔɔlu lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen, a key food plant roots absorb from the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the leaves regain their dark green color and produce bigger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei shishifãi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eha toi wuji aba.

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvest is done, that trapped food stays in the soil, naturally fertilizing the ground for the next crop you plant, like maize or cassava.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã shi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, and when water sits in the ground for too long, the roots suffocate and rot. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni amɛná kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa. ni kɛ́ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it helpful to cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves—called mulching—acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It holds moisture near the roots so you do not need to water as often, and it keeps weeds from growing.
ga: Mulching kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi Mulching (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with small green worms inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse ehe lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yɛ mli?

english: Those holes are caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that eats the growing heart of the maize plant. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or a mixture of local neem leaf extract early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars before they destroy the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ atsui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem baa ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ futu mli lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and getting crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under the leaves and suck the plant juices. Spraying the plants with soapy water or diluted neem oil gets rid of these small pests so new leaves can grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ shwie tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ koni baai heei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I cut away small plantain shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: When too many small suckers grow around a plantain tree, they steal food and water from the main mother stem. Leaving only two or three strong suckers allows the plant to focus its energy on growing a much larger bunch of plantain.
ga: Be ni tsei bibii daraa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, amɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains babaoo ni ebaadu lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, dry spells, or irregular watering, as the plant tries to save water to stay alive. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting during cooler months ensures the blossoms turn into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miipiŋ amɛ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni odu yɛ nyɔji ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tomatoi lɛ afee fɔfɔi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food for the underground tuber. Staking the vines lifts them off the hot, wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping the yam grow much larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ mli koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewó nɔ kɛjɛ hei ni edɔɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ. Etsiɔ tso helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni dara babaoo.

english: Why do my tomatoes turn out soft and watery instead of firm when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni nu yɔɔ mli moŋ fe ni eeefee shiŋŋ kɛ́ mikpa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes often become watery when the plants receive too much water during fruit ripening or when the soil lacks potassium. Regulating watering as fruits mature helps produce firmer, meatier tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu sɛɛ foɔ tomato mli kɛ́ tso lɛ ná nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ aduawai lɛ loo kɛ́ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ beni aduawai lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tomatoi lɛ ni amɛfee shiŋŋ ni amɛfee loo.

english: How can I reduce the excess water in my tomatoes so traders do not reject them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shi koni jarayelɔi akakpoo amɛ?

english: You can lower fruit water content by cutting back on irrigation a few weeks before harvesting, avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer, and planting tomato varieties bred for firm flesh.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsi nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha otsii fioo komɛi dani akpa lɛ nɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he lɛ he. kɛ tomato henɔi srɔtoi ni aduɔ koni ená ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly before I can sell them in the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes with high water content spoil fast because soft tissues break down easily and attract rot. Harvesting fruit when it is just turning pink and keeping it in a cool, ventilated place helps it last longer.
ga: Tomato ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baafite oya ejaakɛ fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ fiteɔ oya ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okpa aduawai lɛ beni etsɔ pinki ni akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ ni jɛmɛ ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which tomato seed varieties should I buy if I want thick tomatoes that sell well?
ga: Mɛɛ tomato dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe kɛji miitao tomato ni mli edɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Look for improved hybrid varieties that are known for high dry-matter content, such as Roma-type tomatoes or commercial hybrids, which grow thick walls and survive long transport trips.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ale akɛ amɛmli nibii ni egbi babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ Roma tomato loo ŋmeii ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii. ni yɔɔ gbogboi ni mli tse ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ gbɛfaa ni yaa shɔŋŋ lɛ mli

english: Is it possible for me to grow the same firm tomato varieties in Ghana that traders buy from abroad?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ tomato srɔtoi ni jarayelɔi heɔ kɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ Ghana?

english: Yes, Ghanaian farmers can grow high-quality, firm tomatoes by using improved hybrid seeds combined with controlled watering methods like drip irrigation.
ga: Hɛɛ, Ghana okwaafoi baanyɛ adu tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ nu ni akudɔɔ tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ fata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do market women prefer buying imported tomatoes instead of the ones grown locally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei sumɔɔ ni amɛhe tomato ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ moŋ fe tomato ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Traders often prefer imported tomatoes because they are grown under controlled conditions that make them firmer, less watery, and easier to keep fresh during long travel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jarayelɔi sumɔɔ tomatoi ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ ejaakɛ aduɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tomatoi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ, nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni ewaaa akɛ abaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How can a small-scale tomato farmer like me expand into large-scale commercial farming?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni tomato okwaafonyo bibioo ko tamɔ mi lɛ aaatsɔ jarayeli nitsumɔi wuji amli?

english: To scale up, you need reliable water control like drip irrigation, proper land preparation, quality hybrid seeds, and pre-arranged market buyers before planting.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ofee lɛ, ehe miihia ni oná nu nɔkwɛmɔ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saamɔ kpakpa Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ asaa he kɛtsɔ hiɛ dani aduɔ.

english: How do I know if I am giving my tomato crops too much water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mi-tomato tsei lɛ?

english: Signs of overwatering include yellowing leaves, cracked skin on ripening tomatoes, and harvested fruit that feels soft, heavy, and watery.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ ashɛɔ nu fe nine lɛ ahe ji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewolo ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ. Ni aduawai ni akpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ tsii, ni eyɛ nu.

english: Does the type of fertilizer I use make my tomatoes soft and watery?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mi-tomato lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu?

english: Yes, using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes rapid, watery growth. Adding potassium to your soil helps form solid, firm fruit walls.
ga: Hɛɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa nu lɛ daa oya. Potassium ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai gbogboi ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa.

english: What can I do with my harvest if buyers reject my tomatoes for being too soft?
ga: Mɛni mafee kɛ minibii lɛ kɛji mɔ ko ni heɔ mi-tomato lɛ kpoo akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ?

english: If fresh-food buyers reject soft tomatoes, you can process them into tomato paste or puree, dry them, or sell them immediately to local food vendors for quick cooking.
ga: Kɛji niyenii hee helɔi kpoo tomato ni mli jɔ Obaanyɛ okɛfee tomato puree loo puree, ogbi, loo ohɔ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ oha niyenii jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ koni amɛhoo oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the heat of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow roots that easily scorch under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains creates a protective shade canopy that cools the soil and keeps humidity high around the cocoa plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo be babaoo hiɔ cacao tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow starting from the bottom of the stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?
