english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient maize plants need to build healthy green leaves and strong stalks.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and dark dirt inside the centers of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which crawl inside the central funnel of the plant during the hot part of the day to eat soft young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛye tsei lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava cuttings when planting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ ato he ko beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives their underground roots enough room to expand into large tubers without fighting neighboring plants for nutrients and moisture.
ga: Aaafee mita kome ni kã ŋmei tsei ni afo lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to tie my yam vines to tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ makɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akpɛtɛ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to create energy for root growth, and lifting leaves off the damp ground prevents rot and leaf spot diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la koni ekɛfee hewalɛ kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ. Ni baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without fruiting when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture is uneven, which disrupts the natural pollination process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa Enɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli pollination gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that pierce the underside of leaves to suck out sap and spread plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛmu nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛgbɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow around one stool forces them to steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant, leading to smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii kome ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmeii akui bibii.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my cereal crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmaa mli lɛ awo miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied into moist soil during active growth—typically once two weeks after sprouting and again at six weeks—so plant roots absorb it before heavy rains wash it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ miida waa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu yɛ otsii enyɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ lɛ.

english: Why does allowing weeds to grow in my field lower my total crop yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal essential water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop roots, leaving your main crops malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu ni he hiaa, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees drying up and turning brown during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. They need shade trees like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand direct heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the key food crops need to stay green and grow tall. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer to the soil helps restore its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Amɛji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titrii ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and getting yellow spots all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmei ni ŋmei ŋmɔŋ ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. The disease weakens the plant so it cannot produce large, healthy cassava roots.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela lɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ hewɔ lɛ enyɛɛɛ ewo ŋmei shishifãi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crops perform better when I plant groundnuts on the land before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ mli dani midu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you harvest them, that natural plant food stays in the ground to nourish the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. kɛji okpa lɛ Adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my yam tubers rotting in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot under the ground when heavy rain builds up in flat or poorly drained soil. Planting yams on high mounds helps surplus water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ ni naa wa bua shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu sweet potato yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are my plantain suckers producing very small bunches of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When plantain trees are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the dirt. Giving each plant enough space allows it to absorb enough nutrients to produce bigger bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ kuu agbo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of regular watering. High temperatures can dry out the flower pollen, preventing the fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaaa lɛ daa lɛ mli. He ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha pollen lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Why does Striga weed keep attacking my cereal crops even after I clear the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ yaa nɔ etutuaa miŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Striga weed attaches its roots directly to the roots of crops like maize and sorghum under the soil to steal food. Its seeds can sleep in the dirt for years, so rotating crops with cowpeas or soybean helps break its life cycle.
ga: Striga jwɛi lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni eju niyenii. Edumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ cowpea loo soybean tsake ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa amɛwala be lɛ feɔ kuku.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their young fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiwo yibii bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when they experience irregular watering or attacks from sap-sucking pests like thrips. Maintaining steady soil moisture and protecting plants from tiny insects keeps the peppers on the stem.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii kɛji amɛná nu ni ejaaa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips lɛ tutua amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa kɛ tsei ahebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ahe Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why are my harvested onions starting to grow green shoots inside my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onion ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Onions begin to sprout when they are kept in warm or damp air, which tricks the bulb into thinking it is time to start growing again. Storing them in a cool, dry, and well-ventilated space keeps them dormant for longer.
ga: Sabolai jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ loo fɛ̃i yɔɔ. Enɛ baaha sabala lɛ asusu akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛwɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops need fertilizer if my soil already looks dark and rich?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ?

english: Even rich-looking soil loses its key nutrients over time as crops grow and absorb them. Fertilizer replenishes essential elements like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so future crops can grow strong and give heavy yields.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɔ ni baa nii lɛ po laajeɔ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛmɔɔ amɛ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasium baa ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ anyɛ adara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is starving for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and growth energy. Applying the right nitrogen-based fertilizer quickly helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛhe waaa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to put fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied during major growth periods—such as a couple of weeks after planting or when crops start flowering—and when the soil is moist so the roots can easily drink in the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa waa, tamɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni adu tsei lɛ loo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi lɛ. kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my crops hurt them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, using too much fertilizer can burn the plant's roots and leaves, causing them to dry up or produce weak stalks. Always follow recommended application amounts to keep your crops safe.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha egbi loo egbɔjɔ tso lɛ shishi. Nyiɛmɔ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛhaa lɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be koni onibii ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: What actually happens to my crop's roots when I feed the soil with fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baa mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When fertilizer dissolves in moist soil, roots easily absorb its mineral food. This encourages the roots to grow deeper and wider, helping the plant hold firmly in the ground and take in more water.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ mineral nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya. Enɛ baawo shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmli alɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ni amɛmɔɔ nu babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop down during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves droop in extreme heat to save water and protect the plant from drying out. If the soil has good nutrients and moisture, the leaves will naturally bounce back fresh once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Baai lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing fruits when planted very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their leaves block each other's sunlight and their roots fight for nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach light instead of putting energy into making fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe hulu la lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ Amɛsɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛshɛ la he lɛ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛfee aduawai loo dumɔwui.

english: Why do neighboring farms get huge harvests while my crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miiná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Higher harvests come from a combination of good quality seeds, feeding the soil with fertilizer at the right times, proper row spacing, and keeping weeds away so your crops do not have to share their food.
ga: Nikpamɔ ni nɔ kwɔ baa kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛaafee ekome lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa yɛ be ni sa mli Gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ koni ehe ehiaaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aja niyenii.

english: Is animal manure better for my farm than buying bag fertilizer?
ga: Ani kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni aheɔ?

english: Animal manure improves soil structure and holds moisture over a long time, while bag fertilizer gives crops a quick, concentrated boost of nutrients. Using both together often yields the best crop growth.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsu nii ekome lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can women in our local farming group improve our vegetable production?
ga: Te yei ni yɔɔ wɔ maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli kui amli lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛha wɔ aduawai afeemɔ aya hiɛ?

english: Women farmers can double their harvest by using modern row-spacing techniques, applying proper fertilizers at key growth stages, and using improved seed varieties that resist local pests and dry spells.
ga: Yei okwaafoi baanyɛ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee shii enyɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ gbɛi ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baatsu nii yɛ dalɛ bei ni he hiaa amli kɛ dumɔwui ni asaa ni teɔ shi ewoɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong, green leaves. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its color and grow properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ekoŋŋ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land every season, why does my yield keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously draws the same specific nutrients out of the soil every season. Planting it repeatedly exhausts those nutrients and allows soil pests to build up; rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts helps put natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Dumɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer directly touching the stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts. Placing it right against a tender stem will burn the plant's skin and roots; placing it a few inches away in a circle allows the roots to safely spread out and drink the nutrients.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ anɔ lɛ, ebaashã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo yɛ kooyigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shweshweeshwe ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: My cassava plants have huge green bushes on top, so why are the tubers under the ground so thin when I harvest?
ga: Mi yucca tso lɛ yɛ jwɛi agbo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or water, it spends all its energy growing heavy leaves above ground instead of sending food down to build thick root tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ tsei ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before they turn into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ babaoo dani amɛtsɔ cacao ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed to maturity. However, excessive flower drop happens when the air is too dry, when small insects damage the blossoms, or when the soil lacks balanced nutrients.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi kɛyashi amɛdara. Shi kɛlɛ, fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔii loo be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers allows the main plant to put all its energy into growing a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ tso wuji ni tsii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves up into the sunlight and fresh air so they can make food faster, while keeping the leaves off the damp soil prevents fungal rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mli koni amɛhoo oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ kɛ baa helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they drink the plant's sap, the leaves shrink and wrinkle, which stops the pepper plant from growing well.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa pepper tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ada jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossom ends of my green tomatoes turning black and rotten before they can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This problem, known as blossom end rot, happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the developing fruit. It is usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil gets very dry and then suddenly very wet.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni eeeha egbi waa ni efee ŋmɔtɔ waa trukaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my seeds sometimes rot in the dirt when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain often heats up dry soil and creates a hot, humid environment before drying out again. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays consistently moist and cool enough for seeds to sprout safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ dani egbi ekoŋŋ Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni edɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young maize plants seem to grow so slowly in the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the early weeks, maize focuses its energy underground on building a strong root system first; once the roots are established, leaf and stem growth accelerates rapidly.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, Abɛi kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshikpɔŋ shishi hewalɛ nɔ koni etswa shishifã ni mli wa klɛŋklɛŋ. Beni abɔ shishifãi lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do my bean plants bend and stretch sideways instead of standing upright?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ekpã mli kɛtee afã moŋ fe ni eeedamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants naturally lean toward light when shaded by taller crops or trees, stretching their stems to get the sunlight they need to produce food.
ga: Bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi kɛyaa la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji tsei loo tsei kakadaji ewo amɛhe shade. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli ni ekpãa mli koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni he hiaa koni ekɛfee niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upward tightly during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism tomato plants use during extreme heat to reduce leaf surface area and prevent excessive water loss through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Koni akɛba baa lɛ hiɛ shi ni atsĩ nu ni fa fe nine ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen, protecting the main plant by dropping the extra load.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli Koni abu tso titri lɛ he kɛtsɔ jatsu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers wilt and collapse even when the soil is wet from heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efɔ lɛ?

english: Wilting during wet weather usually indicates root rot or pests attacking the underground bulb, which stops the roots from absorbing and sending water up to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ egbo loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa tsei lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu ni amɛtsu nu kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow while the top leaves are bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni mi yucca tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Cassava moves essential nutrients like nitrogen from its older bottom leaves up to feed fresh new top growth whenever soil nutrients or water become scarce.
ga: Cassava tsiɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ loo nu lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves fold up tightly at night or during light rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas fold their leaves during the night and rain to preserve internal moisture, protect leaf tissues from excess surface dampness, and retain heat.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ kɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Ebuɔ baa lɛ he kɛjɛ nu ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. ni ehiɛ dɔlɛ mli

english: What happens to my young cocoa seedlings if I do not clear the weeds around them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Fast-growing weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young cocoa seedlings, leaving the cocoa weak, stunted, and vulnerable to pest attacks.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, egbɔjɔɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua lɛ.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant three maize seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa 3 fee ekome yɛ bu bibioo kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the plants to fight each other for limited soil nutrients and sunlight, resulting in thin stems with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulu la ni faaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and turn brown on the stakes at the end of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: The yellowing and drying of yam vines is the plant's natural sign that it has finished storing energy down in the tuber and is ready for harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Giving the crop consistent water and feeding the soil with the right fertilizer helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni okɛwoɔ onibii amli daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa haa shikpɔŋ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo tomato ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and slowing down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiya hiɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or by a plant virus. Protecting your crops early with proper pest control and soil nutrients keeps the leaves flat and healthy so the plant can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ Abuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe mra Kɛji akɛ akwɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui jogbaŋŋ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my garden eggs coming out small and bitter instead of large and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee agbo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Garden eggs become small and bitter when the plant does not get enough water or soil nutrients during the flowering and fruiting stage. Proper feeding and regular moisture allow the fruits to grow plump and sweet.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Niyenii ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baaha aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young cashew trees taking several years before showing any nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ejieɔ ŋmeii kpo lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally spend their first three to five years building strong roots and branches before producing fruit. Providing the young tree with good fertilizer helps it build that structure faster so it can start yielding nuts sooner.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cashew tsei heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi kɛ amɛniji ni mli wa dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa ha tsei bibii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛma amɛhe oya. ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ oya.

english: Why does my mango tree yield a huge harvest one year, but almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni afeee nɔ ko kwraa?

english: Mango trees often experience 'alternate bearing,' where producing a big crop exhausts all their energy reserves for the following season. Feeding the tree with proper nutrients right after harvest helps it regain energy to produce good yields every year.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei naa ‘tsakemɔ’, he ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato kɛha be ni baa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni sa ha otsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do black spots appear on my mangoes while they are still hanging on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mangoi lɛ feɔ diji yɛ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Black spots on mangoes are typically caused by a fungal infection called anthracnose, which spreads in high humidity and rain. Pruning branches to let sunlight in and using protective treatments keeps the fruit clean and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ mango nɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ hulutsoo ni fa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli koni hulu la abote mli, ni akɛ hebuu atsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso yibii lɛ ahe atse ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the blossoms on my cashew trees dry up and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cashew blossoms dry up when sap-sucking pests attack the flowers or when the tree lacks moisture and soil food. Protecting the flowers during the bloom stage ensures they develop into full cashew nuts.
ga: Cashew fɔfɔii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kɛ́ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutua fɔfɔi lɛ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ cashew ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young oil palm trees turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on oil palm trees usually mean the soil is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen or magnesium. Applying specialized palm fertilizer returns the leaves to a healthy green color so the tree can produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ mu tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo magnesium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa bɔni afee ni tso lɛ awo yibii ni tsii.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of palm nuts is fully ripe for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei tsei lɛ eshɛ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: An oil palm bunch is fully ripe when a few loose orange fruits naturally break off and fall to the ground. This signals that the entire bunch has reached maximum oil content and is ready to harvest.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa kɛ́ citrus yibii lɛ etse. Yibii lɛ ateŋ fioo komɛi gbá yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ mu ni fa fe fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he, ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Can I use the exact same fertilizer on my short-term vegetables as I do on my long-term fruit trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii tamɔ bɔ ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛha tsei ni woɔ yibii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: While general fertilizers feed all plants, quick-growing vegetables need fast-release nutrients for fast leaves and fruit, whereas deep-rooted tree crops like mangoes and palms need specific formulations designed for long-term growth and heavy yields.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ niyenii. Nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ he miihia aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ koni amɛba kɛ amɛyibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ tamɔ mango kɛ ŋmei tsei He miihia fɔmula krɛdɛɛ ko ni afee koni ekwɛ̃ be kakadaŋŋ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when I cut down all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young and mature cocoa trees need partial shade to protect them from excessive sunlight and heat, which scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture they need to thrive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be fioo koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce small, thin bunches when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-banana tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their roots and large leaves fight with each other for space, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil, which prevents the fruit bunches from growing big.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ baai wuji lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baatsi aduawai akui lɛ anaa koni amɛkadara.

english: Why is my maize growing tall with thin stems and pale yellow leaves instead of dark green ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves and thin stems usually mean your soil lacks key food like nitrogen. The plant stretches up to look for light, but without proper soil nutrients, it cannot build strong stems or big cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛna la. Shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Enyɛɛɛ ema tsei ni wa loo tsei wuji.

english: Why does the wild grass on my farm grow much faster than the cowpeas I deliberately planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsina ŋmei ni mito gbɛjianɔ akɛ madu lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to local conditions, so their roots quickly grab water and fertilizer from the soil before your planted crop gets a chance to feed.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ ahe wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ naa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land without them damaging each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested in a few months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes up space only after the maize is cleared.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, shishijee lɛ daa blɛoo, ni kɛ́ ashã ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni eŋɔɔ he ko.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly attack my green corn leaves right after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutua mi ŋmãa baai eŋɔli lɛ trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The fresh, soft leaves that sprout right after the rain are the favorite food for hatching armyworms, and the rain creates warm, humid weather that helps their eggs hatch quickly.
ga: Baai bibii heei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ ji niyenii ni ehe gbɛi waa kɛha helminth ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ amɛmli lɛ. Ni nugbɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛwuji lɛ ni amɛwoɔ oya.

english: Why do the improved cassava varieties recommended by extension officers yield more roots than the traditional seeds my parents used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei henɔ ni atsake lɛ ni ŋmei nitsulɔ lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ wo shishifãi babaoo fe shishijee ŋmei dumɔwui ni mifɔlɔi kɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Improved cassava varieties have been bred to fight off common plant diseases like the mosaic virus and are better at turning soil nutrients directly into thick root tubers.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni akɛwu ashi tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ tamɔ mosaic virus lɛ, ni amɛhe esa jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ tsakemɔ mli amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni mli tse.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without developing any fruits during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause stress to tomato plants, making them drop their flowers to save energy and survive instead of spending energy making fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa tomato shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he ni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing out from the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ

english: Those extra shoots, called chupons, steal water and food from the main trunk and branches where your actual cocoa pods need to grow.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ kɛ tsei niji ni ehe hiaa ni o-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know that my yams are completely ripe and ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams are ready for harvesting when the leaves and vines on top of the soil turn yellow and dry up naturally, showing that the plant has finished storing food in the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛtoɔ eshishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ naa.

english: The very first rain after the dry season is often a false start. If you plant right away, the soil might dry out again for weeks, causing your seeds to germinate and then die from heat and lack of water. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ekoŋŋ otsii babaoo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Maize takes specific nutrients out of the soil every time it grows. If you plant it in the same spot repeatedly, the soil becomes empty of those nutrients, and pests that love maize will build up in that ground. Swapping with crops like beans or groundnuts helps restore the soil.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ebaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe jarayeli Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cover the bare soil around my crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mikɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps root temperatures cool, prevents weeds from growing, and eventually rots into rich food for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha shishifã lɛ mli latsaa lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ Ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, egboɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii babaoo kɛha onibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning light green or yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crops use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help the leaves turn healthy dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but no actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi tomato diɛŋtsɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off without making fruit if the weather gets extremely hot, if the plant does not get enough water, or if there are no insects like bees around to move pollen between the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ he ni amɛbaajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when the sun gets very hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow under larger forest trees in nature. When exposed to full, harsh sunlight without shade trees like plantains or timber trees above them, their broad leaves lose water faster than their roots can pull from the ground, causing them to scorch.
ga: Cocoa tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ koo tsei wuji ashishi yɛ adebɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɛɛ ehe ni tsei tamɔ plantains loo kooyigbɛ loggerheads lɛ bɛ hulutsoo. Baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. kɛ shãa okadii baa

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are naturally shallow, but tiny insects called root weevils or tiny worms in the soil can eat away those roots hidden underground. Without strong roots holding the heavy plant firmly in the dirt, strong winds easily push the tree down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, shi kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ root weevils loo worms lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ hela. Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Shishifãi ni wa ni fiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ ashɛre tsei kɛba shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small and weak even if I water them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growers with aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from your main crops. Even if you water the farm, the weeds will drink it first before your crops get a chance.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii amli lɛ. Kɛji okɛ nu wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baanu dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating small holes inside the center leaf folds of my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ daraaa lɛ? Koni aye bu bibioo ko yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋtayaa lɛ mli?

english: Those caterpillars are called Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize plants, and the hatched worms hide deep inside the central leaf funnel where it is safe and moist, chewing the soft leaves before they unfold.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Amɛwoɔ amɛwui lɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Kɛtsɔ baai bibii lɛ ni oooye dani amɛhe afee fɛ̃i lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my harvested cassava roots soft and watery instead of hard and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become soft or watery if left in waterlogged soil where air cannot reach the roots, causing rot, or if harvested too late after heavy rains when the plant uses up its stored food to grow new leaves.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ loo amɛbaafee nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. putrefy Aloo kɛji akɛ akpa sɛɛ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa sɛɛ beni tsei lɛ efite niyenii ni ato lɛ koni amɛkwɛ baai heei lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build healthy green leaves. This often happens when the soil is worn out or when heavy rains wash away nutrients, showing you need to add compost or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural helpers on their roots that pull food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your maize grow stronger without needing to buy as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ehiɛ wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat the young leaves inside the center of my maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: These are fall armyworms, destructive pests that lay eggs on crop leaves and hatch into caterpillars that hide in the growing tip of the plant. Spraying recommended neem extract or approved pesticides directly into the funnel of the plant early in the morning or late evening will control them.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ ni efɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ni miida lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye enɛɛmɛi anɔ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but soil filled with standing water smothers the roots and lets rot-causing fungi grow quickly. Planting cassava on raised mounds helps extra water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi shikpɔŋ ni nu ni etsi ehe eyi mli obɔ lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa ni eha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ adara oya. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and short roots that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a living canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off wet soil, preventing damp foliage from catching leaf-spot diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Etsiɔ baa ni mli efɔ lɛ naa koni ekaye baa mli ŋmɔtɔ hela.

english: How can I protect my fresh tomato and pepper plants when the rain suddenly stops during a short dry spell?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato kɛ pepper tsei heei lɛ ahe beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku mli lɛ?

english: When rain stops, hot soil dries out fast and damages delicate crop roots. Covering the earth around your plants with dry grass or dead leaves (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the soil and prevents the sun from baking the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, sũ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbiɔ oya ni efiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi shwieɔ tsei ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket, ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaaa hulu la lɛ akashã shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when the days become very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and dries up the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. Providing light shade, keeping soil mulched, and watering early in the morning helps lower heat stress so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee hulutsoo, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ leebi lɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo he haomɔ aba shi. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting multiple seeds in one hole makes the young plants fight each other for water, light, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks with tiny cobs. Plant one or two seeds per hole at the proper spacing so each stalk grows thick and produces large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛfataa he Dumɔwu ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. Dumɔ dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli, ni okɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa awo mli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why do seeds saved from my last maize harvest produce smaller yields than fresh seeds from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds bought from certified stores are special hybrid varieties bred for high yield, but their offspring lose that strength after one season. Replanting saved hybrid seed leads to uneven growth and lower yields, so fresh certified seed gives the best harvest every year.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ shwapoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ ji dumɔwui krɛdɛɛi ni akwɛɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi seshi lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nakai hewalɛ lɛ yɛ be kome sɛɛ. Hybrid dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aaadu ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ afee ekome ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ehee fe fɛɛ ni awo he odase lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ afi fɛɛ afi.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees do not have strong roots yet and cannot handle full direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them protects their leaves from heat and helps the soil retain moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni wa lolo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants and leaving tiny black droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii diji bibii yɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central whorl of the maize plant to feed on fresh leaves. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the plant whorl early in the morning or late evening stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa amɛkpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains turn into fine white powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ etsɔ powda yɛŋ kpakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: This happens because insect pests called grain weevils lay eggs inside the dried grains and feed on the inside. Drying the grains thoroughly, treating them with approved preservation dust, and storing them in airtight bags prevents weevils from multiplying.
ga: Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ seed moth lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ emli nibii lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ jogbaŋŋ Kɛ sũ ni akɛtoɔ niyenii he ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Ni akɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects and by planting stem cuttings taken from infected plants. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties and planting only healthy stems stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii ni adu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ akpa.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during flowering even when the soil has enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks water movement inside the plant stem. Rotating crops with maize or cassava and avoiding planting tomatoes in the same spot every year helps reduce the bacteria in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli lɛ gbɛ. Nibii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa Ni ajieɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ baaye abua ni bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my maize crop grow stronger and greener the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmei lɛ daa waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots. When the groundnut roots decay after harvest, they release this natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ Amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less food if I plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the land tired and depleted. Resting the land or rotating maize with cassava and legumes allows the soil to rebuild its nutrient levels naturally.
ga: Abɛi shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of soil before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo ko dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep and wide under the ground, so they need loose, soft soil to expand easily without hitting hard earth. High mounds also prevent heavy rainwater from pooling around the tubers and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ená shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu babaoo naa koni ekabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my maize seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to plant after the soil has received at least two or three heavy, continuous rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting too early after a single light shower causes seeds to sprout and then dry up if rain stops for a week.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu beni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Why does the pink-flowered striga weed only attach itself to my maize and sorghum plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ striga jwɛi ni fɔfɔii yɔɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ pɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed whose seeds stay dormant in the soil until the roots of cereal crops like maize release specific chemical signals. Planting legumes like cowpeas encourages striga seeds to sprout without giving them a host to feed on, helping clear the weed from your farm.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni edumɔwui lɛ ŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ jieɔ tsofa pɔtɛɛ ko kpo. Legumes tamɔ cowpea ni aduɔ lɛ haa Strica dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni gbɔ lɛ yeee amɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow and curled leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by the agriculture office is the best way to keep your plants healthy and protect your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha otsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni obu onibii ahe.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa trees from dying during the hot Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu cacao tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagboi yɛ Harmattan hulutsoo be mli?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that dry out easily under intense sun and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that blocks the harsh sun and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. Spreading dry grass or mulch around the base of the plants keeps the roots cool and maintains steady soil moisture so the flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ ehe. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the piece of land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil while growing. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally enriching the soil for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni edaa lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops are forced to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each seed proper spacing allows the plant to develop a thick stem and absorb enough food to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, anyɛɔ Dumɔwui anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni eŋɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the hot afternoon even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ nɔ leebi moŋ?

english: In the hot afternoon, heat causes plants to lose water through their leaves faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. This temporary wilting is a natural way for the plant to protect itself, and leaves usually perk back up when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe he. Ni bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves while leaving the neighboring cassava untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ miifite mi-corn tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛshiɔ yucca tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛtaaa amɛhe lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer cereal plants like maize because the tender leaf funnels provide easy food and shelter. Cassava leaves contain natural bitter compounds that prevent armyworms from feeding on them.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ejaakɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Nɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli ni tsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkaye amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii baai amli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra suckers growing at the base of my plantain trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: If too many suckers grow around one plantain tree, they all compete for the mother plant's nutrients, leading to small bunches. Pruning away excess suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, concentrating energy to produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ, dumɔ amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. single plantain tree Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli. kɛyashi ebaatsɔ tso yibii bibii Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni oshi tsei kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tsei agboi ni tsii.

english: Weed seeds are extremely hardy and lie sleeping in the soil waiting for moisture. When the rains start, weeds germinate instantly and grow fast because they are wild plants adapted to survive quickly in local conditions.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛkãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amɛmiimɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni edaa oya ejaakɛ eji koo mli tso ko ni etsake ehe oya koni ehi shi yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shihilɛi amli.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest yield less than new certified seeds from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ amɛji lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced high-yield hybrids designed for strong growth. Seeds collected from a harvest lose those special yield-boosting traits in the next generation, resulting in weaker plants and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni afee koni amɛdara waa. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ sui ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key food plant leaves need to make green color and grow strong. It can also happen when too much water stays around the roots, preventing them from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei ahe koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu babaoo bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛye nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects. Heat stress can also make the leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Heat haomɔ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture changes suddenly from very dry to very wet. When the plant gets stressed by hot weather or bad watering, it drops flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛyaa nɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ loo nu ni esaaa ha tsei lɛ miihao lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are my small mangoes falling off the tree long before they grow big enough to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani abaanyɛ akwɛ amɛ ni aye lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree carries more young fruits than it has water and nutrients to support, so it naturally drops the extra ones. Prolonged dry spells or insect attacks on the stem can also cause young fruit to fall early.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso ko wo yibii bibii babaoo fe nɔ ni yɔɔ kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ enyɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ loo kooloi bibii batutua tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ yibii bibii lɛ agbo oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots start to rot if the soil stays soaked in water for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the ground for days, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing root cells to die and allowing fungal decay to quickly turn the tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi amli wala yibii lɛ gboiɔ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ oya, ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden stakes to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso ha wain tso lɛ koni ekwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves produce food for the tuber using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to send far more energy down to build larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tuber lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsuɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if there are no plantain or shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ plantains loo shade tsei komɛi bɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains provides canopy cover that cools the air and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaha shãa ni mli ejɔ aba ni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize and vegetable crops grow much stronger after I harvest groundnuts from that ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kɛ mi aduawai lɛ dara waa waa beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has the special natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Once harvested, the roots leave behind enriched soil that feeds the next crop you plant there.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni eyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni ekɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akpa lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo po lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive neighbors that steal soil fertilizer, light, and root space directly from your main crops. Even with enough rain, your crops stay small because the weeds are consuming most of the plant food in the ground.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni yɔɔ basabasa ni juɔ shikpɔŋ ŋmei, kane, kɛ shishifãi gbɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee bibioo lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi yeɔ tsei aniyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops give a poor harvest if I plant them late after the early rains have passed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shishijee be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: Early planting allows crops to catch the peak moisture and gentle warmth at the start of the season when soil nutrients are highest. Planting late means your crops run out of steady water during critical growth stages and face higher pest populations.
ga: Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Ehaa tsei lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni mli jɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ bɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ, ni amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kpeɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because their root systems are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain alongside cocoa creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees from heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning black and rotting while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments. Clearing weeds, pruning dense branches to let sunlight in, and harvesting ripe pods promptly help prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni duŋ ewo mli. weeding Nibii ni afolɔ mli waa koni hulu la abote mli. Ni ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when their leaves receive maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to light while preventing leaf diseases caused by ground moisture.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ ná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛtsɔ la ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, ni atsĩɔ tso lɛ helai ni ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naatsii nɔ.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by underground pests like weevils or worms. Applying organic manure to strengthen roots and propping up heavy fruit bunches with wooden forks prevents the trees from toppling.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii ni akɛwo shishifãi lɛ ahe hewalɛ, ni akɛ tso yibii ahe tsɔne ni tsii tsu nii kɛfi amɛsɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves from the bottom up usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost early in the plant's life restores green growth and improves cob size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he yɛ tso lɛ wala shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my maize grow much better when I plant groundnuts on the plot first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize after groundnuts, the maize feeds on this rich, natural fertilizer left behind.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni fa babaoo ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why are there tiny holes appearing in my young maize leaves with small caterpillars inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ mli?
