english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Checking young crop leaves early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts into the plant whorls helps control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tso bibii lɛ ahe baai mra. Ni kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa mli nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ baai lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and shrinking like old paper?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ tamɔ wolo momo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids that suck sap and spread viruses. Keeping the farm free of weeds and spraying organic insecticidal soap keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates unevenly. Mulching the soil with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping flowers set fruit even in hot weather.
ga: Tomatoi shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ po mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize turn pale yellow and dry up even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to make leaves green and grow strong. Rain alone isn't enough if the soil lacks plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Nugbɔ pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker and yield less every time I plant yams in the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Yams are heavy feeders that pull specific nutrients out of the ground. Planting them repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil and lets soil diseases build up; resting the land or planting beans restores the soil's strength.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai aba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up tightly during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much moisture under intense sunlight, acting like a shield until the heat reduces.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ he. Acts as a shield until the heat subsides.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot or the plant doesn't get steady water, which causes stress and prevents the flower from forming fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo tsei lɛ náaa nu daa. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa, ni ehaaa fɔfɔi awo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together or gets too much nitrogen, it spends all its energy growing big foliage on top to compete for light instead of storing energy in the root tubers below.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo nitrogen fa babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli koni ekɛye la he akaŋ moŋ fe ni ekɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even after I buy good quality seed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like unseen enemies in your farm; their aggressive roots steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight faster than your crops can reach them, effectively starving your plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ henyɛlɔi ni anaaa amɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers say planting cowpeas between my maize rows will help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, feeding nearby crops like maize naturally.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so much longer to produce fruit when planted in open, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni mli tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain roots need shade and moist, soft earth to spread quickly; in harsh open sun, the roots struggle to develop, which slows down the whole fruiting process.
ga: Plantain shishifãi biɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya. Yɛ hulu la ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ Esa akɛ shishifãi lɛ abɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara. Enɛ baaha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungus called Black Pod that thrives in dark, damp environments. Trimming extra tree branches lets sunlight and wind in to dry out the farm and stop the rot.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ekpa fitemɔ.

english: Why did many of the vegetable seeds I buried directly into the earth fail to come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai dumɔwui ni mifu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛko lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep for the tiny sprout to reach the surface, or if the surrounding soil dries out completely before the seed wakes up.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ bɔni afee ni tso bibioo ko akwɛ̃. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi kwraa dani dumɔwui lɛ je kpo.

english: How can I keep my vegetables growing during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ adu aduawai yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: You can use an irrigation system to supply water directly to your plants. This ensures your crops keep growing healthily even when it does not rain at all.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nu aha otsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa po.

english: Why are my neighbor's crops still fresh while mine are dying from lack of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiɛ lolo yɛ be mli ni migboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor is likely using irrigation, which allows farmers to water their crops artificially so they do not rely only on rainfall to keep plants alive.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ nu shwieɔ shi tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhaa amɛdumɔ nii lɛ nu. Enɛ ji koni ehe akahia ni amɛkɛ amɛhe afɔ̃ nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ koni amɛha tsei ahi shi.

english: Can I farm all year round in Ghana even if the rains stop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee okwaayeli afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ Ghana kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa po?

english: Yes, by adopting irrigation methods, you supply regular water to your farm continuously so your crop production does not stop when the rainy season ends.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Obaaha nu ni yaa nɔ aya oŋmɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ ekpaŋ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba naagbee.

english: How can I stop pests from spreading diseases across my entire farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ helai amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Preventing pests from entering your crop area keeps diseases from spreading. Controlling the growing area blocks outside insects so infections cannot easily move from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛ́ otsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote nibii ni odu lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ baatsi kooloi ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ anaa. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tso kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ oya.

english: Is there a way to protect my crops from bugs without buying expensive chemical sprays all the time?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be?

english: Yes, by growing crops in a controlled space like a net house, you physically block insects from reaching your plants, reducing the need to keep buying and spraying chemicals.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ hei ni akudɔ lɛ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ. trellis greenhouse Obaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkashɛ otsei lɛ ahe. Ehaa tsofai ni aheɔ ni aya nɔ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crops keep getting attacked by insects even after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ moŋ

english: In an open field, new insects constantly fly in from outside. Creating a barrier or controlled space stops new pests from arriving, so you don't have to keep spraying repeatedly.
ga: Yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ, kooloi heei miijɛ kponɔgbɛ amɛmiiba be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ ofee gbɛtsii nii loo he ko ni akudɔɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai heei akabote mli, no hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ shii abɔ.

english: What does it mean when people talk about growing crops in a 'controlled environment'?
ga: Kɛ gbɔmɛi wie tsei ni aduɔ yɛ Mɛni ji ‘shihilɛ ni akudɔ’ lɛ shishi?

english: A controlled environment is a protected structure, like a greenhouse or net house, where you control water through irrigation and protect plants from pests and bad weather.
ga: Shihilɛ ni akudɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ko ni abuɔ he, tamɔ ŋmɔ loo ŋmɔ mli tsei. he ni obaanyɛ okudɔ nu kɛtsɔ nu ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni obu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbohii ahe.

english: Why are some farmers building net structures over their tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi maa amɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ tsei lɛ?

english: These net structures create a controlled environment that keeps destructive insects away from the tomatoes and prevents diseases from spreading, keeping the crops safe.
ga: Nɛkɛ lattice tsɔnei nɛɛ haa shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ ni haa kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tomato he. ni atsĩ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ shweshweeshwe

english: Will growing my vegetables inside a greenhouse structure really reduce my farm expenses?
ga: Ani aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua diɛŋtsɛ ni eba ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo shi?

english: Yes, because a protected structure prevents pests from invading, meaning you spend far less money buying chemical treatments over the long term.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ nɔ ko ni abuɔ he lɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkabote mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, shika fioo pɛ ofiteɔ yɛ tsofafeemɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How does a greenhouse setup help if the weather becomes unpredictable?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni atoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baafee aha?

english: Inside a controlled environment, your crops are protected from harsh conditions, and you use irrigation to water them, making your harvest safe even if the rain fails completely.
ga: yɛ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔ mli mli Abaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Ni okɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu. Enɛ haa okpamɔ lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa po.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and tender roots that cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a protective umbrella, keeping the soil moist and shielding the seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ cocoa tsei bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni obu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaafee hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods as a natural defence mechanism to save water. Dropping leaves prevents the plant from losing moisture through transpiration, allowing the root tubers under the ground to survive until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekaje ŋmɔtɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa.

english: Why is it bad to plant many maize seeds closely together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ yɔɔ srɔto lɛ? Dumɔwui ni akɛaawo bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the crowded plants compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This competition results in tall, weak stems and tiny cobs instead of big, healthy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ akaŋshii nɛɛ mli baa ji tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli. Yɛ ŋmãa toi agbo ni mli wa najiaŋ

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ duɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, making it richer for the maize plants without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the vital juices out of the leaves. These pests also spread plant viruses that make the leaves wrinkle, twist, and stop the plant from bearing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ hu gbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛ yibiiwoo naa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right next to the stem can burn the plant's skin and roots due to high salt content. Fertilizer should be placed a short distance away in the soil so the roots can reach out and absorb the nutrients safely.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi yɛ ŋmei babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ kuku nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he shweshweeshwe ni amɛŋɔ.

english: When temperatures get too high, tomato pollen becomes dry and inactive, preventing the flowers from fertilizing. Because the flower cannot form a seed, the plant sheds the flower instead of growing a tomato.
ga: When the temperature is too high Tomato pollen will dry up and become inactive. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo dumɔwui. Instead of growing tomatoes, the trees shed their flowers.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so fast when I stack them together on the warm ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that continue to breathe after harvest. Stacking them on warm ground traps heat and moisture, which creates a perfect environment for fungal rot to spread quickly through the crop.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha rot fungus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to local conditions and can sleep safely in dry soil for months. When the first rains fall, weed seeds trigger immediate germination and growth faster than domesticated crop seeds.
ga: Weed seeds are naturally adapted to local conditions. ni ebaanyɛ ewɔ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ nyɔji babaoo. Beni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Jwɛi dumɔwui woɔ shweremɔ kɛ dalɛ he hewalɛ oya fe shia tsei dumɔwui.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, food, and energy from the mother plantain tree. Pruning away weaker suckers ensures all the plant's resources go into making a single, large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ dumɔwu lɛ mli. Niji bibii ni afoɔ lɛ haa akɛ tso lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni akɛfeɔ plantains akuu agbo kome ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight. Without shade from taller plants like plantain or forest trees, the harsh sun scorches their tender leaves, causing them to dry up and die before their roots are fully established.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã ebaai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani shishifãi lɛ tswaa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soaking wet soil lacks air, which seeds need to breathe and sprout. When planted in waterlogged soil, seeds absorb too much water and rot before they can grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui lɛ amu ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu babaoo ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: How do I know the right amount of water to mix with my crop chemical so it doesn't burn my leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nu ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ afutu mli? Bɔni afee ni mibaai lɛ akashã

english: If you use too little water, the chemical solution becomes too strong and burns the crop leaves. You must measure both the water and the chemical accurately using the specified measuring cup or bucket ratio provided by your extension officer before putting it in your sprayer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ nu fioo pɛ tsu nii Tsofai lɛ baafee babaoo tsɔ ni ebaashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ susumɔ kɔɔpoo loo baket ratios ni o-extension nitsulɔi lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ asusu nu kɛ tsofai fɛɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ dani okɛwo tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nu lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I mix two different farm chemicals together in my spraying machine at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai enyɔ futuɔ tsɔne ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ tsofa lɛ mli yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Combining different chemicals without knowing how they react can weaken their power, destroy your crop, or produce dangerous fumes. Unless specifically instructed that they are safe to mix, always apply each product separately.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛto he lɛ fata he ni aleee bɔ ni tsofai nɛɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi. fitemɔ onibii loo okɛ lasu ni yɔɔ oshara aba. ja gbɛtsɔɔmɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehi akɛ aaafutu. Kɛ nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko atsu nii srɔtoi be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plant turning yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tip and moves down the center of the leaf in a V-shape is a clear sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ miiho. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but produce very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ pepper fioo lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen fertilizer, they spend all their energy growing leaves and branches instead of flowers and fruit. Balancing your fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to produce more peppers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei niji yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium to o-fertilizer lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms stay hidden deep inside the central funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fall Armyworms hide in the central funnel (whorl) because the leaves there are soft and easy to eat, and it protects them from sunlight, heavy rain, birds, and direct chemical sprays.
ga: Baai amli ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ (ring) lɛ mli ejaakɛ baai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyeli waaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, okpoi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop yellow spots during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava leaf curling in dry weather is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. These insects multiply quickly in warm, dry conditions and suck the sap from the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ Yucca baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. ni enuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant before turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and protected helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛna haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium ni faaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abu he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam tubers rot underground when water collects around the roots in flat or poorly drained soil. Building high mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and safe from rotting fungi.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, full sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the heat dries out the surrounding soil. Keeping some tall trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby provides essential shade and moisture while the cocoa roots establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ebaai lɛ shãa oya, ni latsaa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ agbi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ Aloo, dumɔwui ni daa oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ aba yɛ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ etswa shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning pale yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves inward usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen, which gives plants their green color. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure to the soil will help the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ anaa ni eyaa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni haa tsei feɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become hard, woody, and watery if I leave them in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, tso kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers reach their best quality around 9 to 12 months after planting. If left in the soil past maturity through rainy and dry seasons, the plant starts feeding on its own stored starch, leaving behind tough fibers and excess water.
ga: Cassava ŋmeii lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ hɔmɔ be mli. Tso lɛ baabɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ e-starch ni ato lɛ yeli. Enɛ haa tsɔji ni wa kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets extremely hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly flooded with water. Watering your crop regularly and mulching the ground around the roots keeps soil conditions steady so flowers can form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi aahu akɛ nu afua baa trukaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛ yaa hiɛ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves and passing on plant viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or targeted sprays helps new leaves grow flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi ni amɛhaa helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ kudɔmɔ mra Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni baai heei lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce the food needed for growing big tubers underground. Vines left trailing on the damp ground get shaded by weeds and are easily attacked by fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ aya hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Wein tsei ni ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, jwɛi shwieɔ amɛhe oya, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the extra small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Krɛdɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: When too many shoots grow from the same root base, they steal water and food from each other, resulting in small plantain bunches. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one strong sucker beside the main stem ensures all the soil nutrients go into making big, heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishifã kome mli Amɛbaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii. Enɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmeii titri lɛ. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee aduawai wuji ni tsii.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help the maize crop I plant in that same soil next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to the legume family, which has special root nodules that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil. When these plants decay after harvest, they leave behind rich, natural nitrogen fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow near my maize make the maize stalks thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa lɛ tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively drink up the soil moisture and nutrients that your maize needs to build thick stalks. When weeds crowd the base of the maize, the crop wastes its energy stretching upward toward the light instead of growing strong roots and sturdy stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛmuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa o-ŋmã lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ. Beni jwɛi lɛ ebɔle ŋmãa lɛ shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ etsɔmɔmɔ kɛmiiya la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisifãhi nɛ a he wa kɛ tsohi nɛ a he wa.

english: Why is it bad to save seeds from my high-yielding hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji hybrid dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baato koni adu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for peak performance only in their very first generation. If you plant seeds saved from that harvest, the second-generation crops will grow unevenly, produce small cobs, and lose the strength and yield of the original parent seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei ayinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. ni ekɛ ŋmei bibioo ko baa ni shishijee dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize needs to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni etswa ŋmãa ni wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves that cannot withstand full sunlight; they need shade from temporary companion crops like plantains to keep them cool and retain moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe yeɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava harvests when I plant it on the same field every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo ŋmei fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the ground without giving the soil time to recover, which weakens the plants and reduces root size over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with big leaves but produce tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eyɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the plant spends all its energy growing leafy branches above ground instead of storing food in the roots below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo amɛniji lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shishigbɛ.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunlight to manufacture food; lifting the leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to catch more light, which feeds energy down to grow bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la babaoo kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa la babaoo. Enɛ baaha hewalɛ awo mli koni eha yitso lɛ agbo.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to sow my seeds after the first rain comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to survive after sprouting; planting after only one light rain is risky because the dry soil underneath will absorb the water quickly and dry out the seed.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Shikome pɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baaŋɔ nu oya ni ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than your crops can take them up, leaving your crops hungry even in fertilized soil.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni otsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ha hɔmɔ aye onibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ po nɔ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hidden in the plant centers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine yɛ bu ko ni akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest that burrows into the growing central leaves of maize plants to feed during warm weather.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni eye niyenii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the internal channels of the stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli loo bacteria mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛi lɛ anaa Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly at the base of my young plant's stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly against a tender stem acts like salt and burns the plant's delicate bark and young roots; placing it a few inches away allows the roots to safely drink the dissolved nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baatsu nii tamɔ ŋoo ni ebaashã tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛto shishifãi lɛ ahe ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni mli ewo muji lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to stay green. The plant automatically pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe nɔ. Tsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt and droop in the afternoon heat, but stand up fresh again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi obaaku osɛɛ kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can drink it up, so the leaves droop to shade themselves from the sun. Overnight, the roots catch up on drinking water, allowing the plant to stand tall again.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Baai lɛ gboɔ koni amɛtsi hulu lɛ naa. Yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nu ni anuɔ lɛ he. Ha tso lɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl inwards tightly when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a tomato plant's defense mechanism to save water. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant shrinks the area exposed to the hot sun and traps moisture underneath the leaf.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni buɔ tomato tsei ahe koni amɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni aaatsɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe lɛ, ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of bushy leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or raw manure, the cassava plant spends all its strength growing big stems and leaves above ground, leaving no energy to build heavy starch roots underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ Kasava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ etsitsi kɛ baai wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eshiii hewalɛ ko kwraa ni ekɛbaafee shishifãi ni tsii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their tiny flowers before they can grow into full cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Bei pii lɛ dani amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally produces thousands of flowers, but it sheds them if it lacks sufficient water or soil nutrients, or if tiny insects like midges are not available in the farm to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi amɛbaagbee shi kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmeii?

english: How do I know that my yams under the soil are mature and ready for harvest without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ ni mikɛ amɛ efoŋ?

english: Yams tell you they are mature through their vines above ground. When the green leaves stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up, it means the plant has finished sending all its nutrient food down into the buried tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes kɛɔ bo akɛ amɛtsɔ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ amɛdara. Kɛji baai eŋɔlii lɛ kpa shweremɔ lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi, ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ etsu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛba shi kɛtee ŋmeii ni afu lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very thin cobs when I plant three or four seeds in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tseee waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the growing stalks fight like people sharing one small plate of food. Their roots compete for the same water and soil nutrients, leaving no plant strong enough to grow a large cob.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, tsei ni miida lɛ tswaa amɛhe tamɔ mɛi ni miija niyenii tsɛnsi bibioo ko. Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni jɛɔ nu lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, no hewɔ lɛ tso ko bɛ ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ ada ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo.

english: Cowpea plants have special bumps on their roots that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the dirt. When the cowpea plant dies, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do young caterpillars always hide deep inside the middle funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant is soft, moist, and hidden from the hot sun and birds. Pests like the Fall Armyworm crawl in there because it offers safe shelter and tender green leaves to eat.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛhiɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ shwereɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ejaakɛ ehaa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni amɛyeɔ nii.

english: Why did the leaf edges of my crops turn dry and brown after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ egbi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain strong mineral salts. If placed too close to the plant stem without enough soil moisture, the fertilizer sucks water directly out of the roots, causing leaf edges to dry up as if scorched by heat.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la eshã amɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my maize crops grow thin and turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-ŋmã lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your maize for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds crowd the field, they starve the maize of essential food, causing the crop leaves to turn yellow and the stems to grow thin and weak.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmãa yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi ebɔle ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Amɛbaaye niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eshishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I leave heavy bush to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi ni mli tse koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe? Kasava shishifã?

english: Heavy bush blocks sunlight from reaching the cassava leaves and chokes root space under the ground. Without enough sunlight and soil room, the plant cannot produce large cassava tubers, resulting in very low harvest yields.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ ŋmei baai lɛ ahe. kɛ niyenii ni yeɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishigbɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ Kɛji hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ tsu ko bɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ ajie shishifãi wuji. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii ni akpaa lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Should I burn all the weeds and bushes after clearing my land for planting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ beni mijie he ni adu nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning cleared bush destroys useful organic matter and beneficial micro-organisms in the topsoil. Allowing the cut leaves and grass to dry and rot back into the soil naturally enriches it with nutrients for your crops.
ga: Brɔshi ni ajie lɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha baai kɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ agbi ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ afata onibii ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce fewer fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When pepper plants are crowded together, their leaves shade each other from the sun and their roots fight for the same food in the soil. This stress causes the plant to drop its flowers instead of forming healthy peppers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ abua pepper tsei anaa yɛ kui amli lɛ Baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ hulu lɛ he. ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops planted under big shade trees grow tall and weak without producing food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be agbo shishi lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo niyenii lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to make the energy required for fruit development. When shaded by tall trees, the crop stretches upward trying to reach the light, making the stem thin and preventing fruit from growing.
ga: Hulu la he miihia tsei tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Beni eyɔɔ tso kakadaŋŋ ko shishi lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɛ eshwa kɛya ŋwɛi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni ebɔɔ koni ekɛ la aha lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ehaaa aduawai akwɛ̃.

english: How does leaving cut grass on top of the soil help my vegetables during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cut grass acts as a protective cover or mulch over the ground. It shades the soil from direct sun heat, keeps the roots cool, and prevents water from evaporating quickly so your crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni afo lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crop field more when it is overgrown with weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ beni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Dense weeds create dark, cool, and humid conditions where insect pests can hide, reproduce, and stay safe from natural predators before moving over to destroy your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa, he ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi, amɛfɔ, ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ahe. dani oshi ni oyafite oŋmɔshi nibii

english: Why is it wasteful to apply fertilizer in a farm field that has not been weeded?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ nii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔji ni afɔko jwɛi lolo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that absorb nutrients much quicker than young crops. If you apply fertilizer without clearing the weeds first, you end up feeding the weeds, making them grow faster and choke your crops.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe tsei bibii. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni ogbeee jwɛi lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, Obaafee jwɛi lɛ niyenii. Ha ekwɛ̃ oya ni efite onibii.

english: Why do my yam plants struggle to grow well in hard soil filled with wild plant roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ miitao ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni koo mli tsei shishifãi eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need loose, workable soil to expand downward easily. Hard soil filled with wild roots physically blocks the yam tuber from expanding and steals water away from the crop.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shi oya. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni koo mli shishifãi eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni ejuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds sprout back up so fast right after I clear my farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried dormant in the soil for long periods. When you clear the bush above, sunlight and air reach the soil surface, triggering those buried seeds to germinate and sprout rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji ojie jwɛi ni yɔɔ Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsirɛ nakai dumɔwui ni afu lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize turn yellow and burn after I spray chemical medicine to clear weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: If agrochemicals are applied in the wrong dosage, at the wrong time of day, or if non-selective weedkiller touches the crop directly, it poisons the plant's leaves, stopping them from making food and causing them to turn yellow or dry up.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ okwaayeli tsofai tsu nii yɛ falɛ ni ejaaa mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli loo kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Ebaafee tsofa ni gbeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kpaɔ ni eha baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛgbiɔ.

english: Will spraying very strong chemical medicine on my cocoa trees harm the leaves while killing pests?
ga: Ani tsofai ni mli wa waa ni akɛshwieɔ kookoo tsei anɔ lɛ baaye baai lɛ awui yɛ be mli ni egbeɔ kooloi bibii lɛ?

english: Yes, using chemicals that are too strong or not approved for cocoa can burn young leaves and flowers, weakening the tree while also killing helpful insects like bees that help your cocoa trees produce pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa tsɔ loo ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ kɛha kookoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi. egbɔjɔɔ tso lɛ Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbeɔ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ.

english: How can cassava disease move from my neighbor's farm into my own crop field?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei helai jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli kɛyaa bo diɛŋtsɛ oshikpɔji anɔ?

english: Cassava diseases spread when tiny insects like whiteflies carry viruses from infected leaves across farm borders, or when farmers share infected stem cuttings and unwashed tools that carry disease-causing germs.
ga: Cassava hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ kɛ hela lɛ baa kɛjɛ baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛfo ŋmɔ husui lɛ amli. Aloo beni okwaafoi jaa tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ nibii ni afɔɔɔ he ni helai ni kɛ hela baa lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the exact same plot every year lead to more sick plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa hela mɔɔ lɛ waa lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and fungal diseases to survive in the dirt and multiply in larger numbers every season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛyi fa babaoo daa be mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow large green leaves but fail to yield any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi enyɛɛɛ ewo pepper lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and branches instead of flowers. Plants need balanced nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to form healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai kɛ eniji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ moŋ fe fɔfɔii. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium he miihia tsei koni amɛwo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my garden egg seedlings drop their flowers before growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛdu aduawai lɛ?

english: Garden egg flowers fall off when the plant experiences sudden shock or stress, such as extreme heat, a lack of regular water, or a shortage of essential plant food in the soil.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na shoofeemɔ loo haomɔ trukaa, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ daa. loo tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during severe afternoon heat as a survival trick to reduce the leaf area exposed to direct sunlight, which keeps the plant from losing too much moisture.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli. Taakɛ yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo ni akɛbaa he ni baai lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo.

english: Why do the roots of my yam plants start to rot when rain sits on the field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Yam roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the soil for too long, it pushes out all the air, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for rot-causing fungi to attack.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa sweet potato shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ atutua amɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant maize seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crowded plants fight over limited water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in tall, thin stems with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dense tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná nu fioo, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni dumɔwui bibii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: How do weeds cause my cowpea crop to grow weak and produce poor yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo?

english: Weeds grow faster than cowpeas and steal away essential moisture, sunlight, and nutrients, while also harboring harmful insects that feed on the cowpea leaves and pods.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsina ŋmeii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔtɔ, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eji he ko ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yeɔ tsina tso lɛ baai kɛ eshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize crops turning yellow and full of small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with holes are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Pests eat the leaves, which stops the maize plant from capturing sunlight and growing strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ buji baa. Kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ yeɔ baai Enɛ haaa hulu la ashɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ daraa waa.

english: No, heavy rain will wash the fertilizer away into streams before your crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not during heavy downpours.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho ŋmɔshi nibii kɛya faai amli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do people advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots, making the land fertile again naturally.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: How do I know which cassava stems are best to cut and plant for a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afo ni adu kɛha ŋmɔ hee?

english: Select stems from healthy, mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old and free from diseases. Use the hard middle section of the stem rather than the soft top or woody bottom for the strongest sprouts.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni hela bɛ amɛhe. Kɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni wa lɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishi ni tso yɔɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni mli wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller roots when I leave weeds to grow around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ mli beni mishiɔ jwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds steal these resources, your crops do not get enough nourishment to grow full-sized roots or tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Beni jwɛi ju nibii nɛɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ enaaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi loo bulbs ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Black Pod is a fungal disease that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Clearing extra tree branches lets in sunlight and air, which dries out the pods and helps stop the fungal disease from spreading.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gĩɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight and soil food. This leaves you with tall, thin, weak stalks that produce tiny cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛwooo ŋmeii kwraa.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and spoil when I put it inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ?

english: Maize spoils in bags if it is not fully dried after harvest. Moisture trapped inside the grains encourages mold and dangerous poisons like aflatoxins to grow, making the crop unsafe to sell or eat.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji egbiko kwraa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ aflatoxin lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ahɔ̃ɔ loo ayeɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsei kakadaji fiɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground allows their leaves to spread out and catch maximum sunlight, which fuels the growth of big tubers underground. Staking also keeps leaves away from soil diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa ebaa lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni enáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. ni ji tsofa ni haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale white or light yellow during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eyɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extremely high heat and intense sun cause heat stress, which breaks down chlorophyll—the green pigment in leaves. Without sufficient shade or soil moisture during hot periods, leaves lose their green color and can turn pale or dry out.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Enɛ haa klorofil, ni ji su eŋɔli ni yɔɔ baai amli lɛ, fiteɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Baai lɛ baaje amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛgbi.

english: Why do some of my pepper seeds take a very long time to crack open and sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, soil temperature, and air to break their outer seed coat. If the soil is too dry or too hard, the shell cannot soften, requiring patience and steady watering until the seed cracks open and sprouts.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. Shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli latsaa ni baaha dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ mli agbala. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo ewa tsɔ lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ efeŋ blɛoo. Ebiɔ tsuishitoo kɛ nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baatswa ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to flip or turn over the topsoil before planting new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ loo matsake shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu tsei heei?

english: Turning over the soil loosens hard earth, buries old plant matter so it can rot into manure, and exposes hidden soil pests to the sun, creating a healthy environment for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oootsɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Fuu tso momo ni eshwɛ lɛ koni amɛgboi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ jeɔ hulu la lɛ shishi. Ehaa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ.

english: How does waiting patiently affect the final color and quality of my pepper crop?
ga: Te tsuishitoo ni akɛmɛɔ lɛ saa mi-pepper lɛ su kɛ naagbee su lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Peppers undergo a natural chemical change as they ripen on the plant, turning from green to red or yellow. Harvesting them too early stops this transformation, while allowing them to mature fully increases their sweetness, nutrient content, and market value.
ga: Chili peppers tsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofa tsakemɔi amli beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee etsuru loo ŋmɔŋ Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ baatsi tsakemɔ nɛɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ha amɛdara koni amɛ ŋmɔlɔ aya hiɛ. Niyenii mli nibii kɛ jarayeli jara

english: What happens to young cocoa trees if they are exposed to direct high heat without shade?
ga: Mɛni baa cacao tsei bibii anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛtee la ni mli edɔ waa mli tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under intense heat and full sun. Shade crops like plantains shield young cocoa plants from heat damage until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ amɛhe lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do white, papery patches appear on my tomatoes when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ woji yɛŋ ni tsɔɔ mi-tomato lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: This is called sunscald, which happens when intense sunlight heats up the fruit directly. The high heat damages the tomato skin, causing it to lose color and turn into a white, dry, leathery spot.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ wo aduawai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ tomato hewolo. Ehaa su lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni efeɔ futafuta, egbiɔ, ni ekpɛtɛɔ he.

english: What happens if I water my crops during the hottest peak of the day?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ nu wo mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Watering under high midday heat causes rapid evaporation before the roots can absorb the moisture, and water drops on leaves can magnify sunlight, causing dark or pale heat spots on the foliage.
ga: Nu ni akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa woɔ mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa hulutsoo baa oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu. Ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo he tsɔi ni tsuɔ loo etsakeɔ su baa baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft or pale inside if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving cassava in hot, wet ground past its maturity period causes the root starch to break down into fiber and water, leading to internal discoloration, loss of firmness, and lower processing quality.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ nɔ ni eho be ni ekɛdaa lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha shishifã lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ agbá ni etsɔ ŋmeii kɛ nu. ni kɛ mligbɛ su tsakemɔ baa lɛ haaa ehiɛ afee shiŋŋ ni ehaa nitsumɔ lɛ mli hilɛ baa shi

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants look bleached white after insects attack them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ futafuta yɛ be mli ni kooloi bibii etutua amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Certain pests, like sap-sucking insects or leaf-miners, scrape off the leaf's green outer layer to feed on plant juices, leaving behind clear or white papery trails across the leaf surface.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui komɛi, tamɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu loo mɛi ni shwieɔ baai Amɛshwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni ji eŋɔli lɛ koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ. Eshiɔ wolo yɛŋ loo ni mli tse he gbɛ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea pods turn dry and pale white when they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔtɔi lɛ egbi ni eyɛ futafuta beni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: As cowpeas reach full maturity, the plant naturally dries out its outer pods to protect the seeds inside. The green pod turns pale white or light brown, signaling that the seeds are fully grown and ready for picking.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ haa kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ gĩɔ koni ebu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe. Pods eŋɔli lɛ tsɔɔ eyɛŋ loo blɔfo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Yam vines produce tubers by catching sunlight through their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can capture maximum sunlight while staying safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I harvest more corn?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani minyɛŋ makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close causes the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni haa tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer usually fixes this.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in extreme heat. It is a natural behavior that helps the plant conserve moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants suddenly wilting and dying even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot. The bacteria or fungi block the plant's internal tubes, preventing water from reaching the leaves even if plenty of water is in the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ baa. Muawai loo ŋmeii tsiɔ tso lɛ mli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Ehaa nu shɛɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Leaf curl in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the plant's juices, or by a virus spread by those insects. Controlling tiny pests protects the new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai heei lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cassava crop produce huge leaves above ground but very small roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baa agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of feeding its underground storage roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa lɛ, Cassava tsei hu kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe shishifãi ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets maize pests and diseases build up in the soil, leading to poorer harvests over time.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmãa helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans help improve my farm's soil for other crops?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Cowpeas and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into soil nutrients. When the plants finish growing, they leave that extra nitrogen behind for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Ebaashi nitrogen ni fa fe nine kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees dry out quickly because the hot sun and dusty dry winds steal moisture faster than their small roots can drink it. Plantains or shade trees planted alongside cocoa act as living umbrellas, providing needed moisture and shelter.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ juɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya fe shishifãi bibii. Abaanyɛ anu tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni adu yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ wɔɔhe ni he hiaa lɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow at the tips while the rest of the farm looks green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ? be mli ni fãi krokomɛi Okwaafoi lɛ feɔ eŋɔli?

english: Yellow leaf tips usually mean your maize plant is starving for nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or compost near the base of the stem helps the leaves turn dark green and strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni etsɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do small green caterpillars keep eating holes in the middle funnel of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛye bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which target young maize leaves. They hide inside the central funnel where moisture collects, so applying recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel early in the morning controls them.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli he ni nu ni mli edɔ buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in soaked soil because waterlogged dirt starves the roots of air and encourages destructive fungus. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain off cleanly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ shishifãi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa hetsemɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines up tall wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛya tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the heavy tuber underground. Staking keeps leaves lifted toward the sun while protecting them from heat and soil-borne diseases on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and making the fruits small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle ehe ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Using safe neem-based sprays early keeps these insects off your peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any tomato fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dryness after watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch around the plant base keeps the soil cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao loo egbi trukaa beni awo lɛ nu sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the bunch of fruits is small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Akɛ aduawai lɛ woɔ yibii fioo lolo?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and thick stems that catch a lot of wind. Supporting the main stem with strong wooden prop-forks prevents rainstorms from pushing the plant over.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse ni mɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekatsi tso lɛ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my crop field when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ midumɔi lɛ anɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it. If applied to dry soil, fertilizer sits undissolved and can burn the crop roots when the weather heats up.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, Fertilizer lɛ shwieee shi ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and weak even if I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and expensive plant food away from your crop roots. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of planting ensures your crops get all the nutrients to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ tso niyenii ni jara wa kɛjɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily in full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them provides natural canopy shade and preserves soil moisture, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and healthy.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli shade aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.
