english: Why is my maize crop turning light yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves and strong growth. Applying animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizers like urea helps restore the dark green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ he miihia kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally takes nitrogen from the air and adds it into the soil. Planting them with maize acts like a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer for your maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ nitrogen mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the middle of my young maize leaves, and how do I fix it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni kɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ baa? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the leaf funnel. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended neem extracts or safe insecticides into the leaf funnel will stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baa ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛwoɔ baai amli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil before it is time to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water collects and stays around the roots in heavy soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away easily, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu babaoo bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady for two to three consecutive weeks rather than planting after the very first rain. Planting too early can cause seeds to dry up and die if the rain stops suddenly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the vines up to catch sunlight and keeps the leaves off damp ground, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ wain tso lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la lɛ he, ni ehaaa baai lɛ ahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Koni akɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plants without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive chemical fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with grass mulch and avoiding over-fertilization helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better to start my pepper seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaaje pepper dumɔwui lɛ shishi yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu amɛ awo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are very small and fragile, making them easy targets for heavy rains and pests in the main field. A nursery bed lets you shelter, water, and protect the young sprouts until they are strong seedlings ready for transplanting.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he oya. Nursery saatsoi lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ he ko haa, okɛ nu haa, ni obuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops, and why must I clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early eliminates this competition so your crops get all the food and space they need to grow heavy yields.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Koni oha onibii lɛ niyenii kɛ he fɛɛ he ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves underneath my maize plants turning yellow while the top ones stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the plant moves nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top. Yellow lower leaves show that your soil is running low on nitrogen and needs fertilizer.
ga: Beni nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha baa bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell what nutrient my crops are missing just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii ni he hiaa mitso lɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Crops show clear warning signs on their leaves when hungry. For instance, yellowing lower leaves signal nitrogen shortage, purple leaves often mean phosphorus deficiency, and burnt leaf edges usually indicate potassium lack.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hɔmɔ miiye amɛ. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, baai ni ashã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium faaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither and die when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense, direct sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out easily. Big trees act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist enough for young cocoa to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa koni cacao tsei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my cassava plants shedding all their leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is cassava's natural way of conserving water when rainfall stops. The stem and roots stay alive underground, and fresh green leaves will sprout as soon as the rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ ŋmei he kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ pɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plants experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much chemical fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and balanced helps the flowers stay on to produce tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ tomato.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of green leaves but very few beans after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally capture their own nitrogen from the air through their roots. Applying excess nitrogen fertilizer makes the crop put all its energy into leaf growth rather than forming flowers and seed pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ tsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ baai ni miida lɛ ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ŋmɔji

english: Leaf curling in pepper is often caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or whiteflies hidden under the leaves, or viruses they transmit. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaf twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Mra be mli ni akudɔɔ kooloi nɛɛ Ebaaye ebua ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsake.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking lifts yam vines toward sunlight so the leaves can make food efficiently, while keeping them off damp ground where fungal leaves rot easily, resulting in bigger tuber yields.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, atsĩɔ enaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii baai lɛ fiteɔ oya lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baafee babaoo.

english: Why do my maize crops grow tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the roots fight underground for water and soil food, while leaves shade each other above ground. Proper spacing allows every plant enough light and food to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ náa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut away the extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie plantain tso lɛ tso lɛ

english: Extra suckers steal water and food away from the main mother plantain tree. Removing most suckers leaves one main stem to focus all energy into producing a heavy, high-quality plantain bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri kome pɛ ni okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu plantains tsei ni tsii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ he nii.

english: Why does my farmland turn into deep mud whenever heavy rains fall, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ muji ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: Flat soil with no channels collects rain water instead of letting it flow away. Making raised earth ridges or digging simple drainage ditches along your field helps water drain off, keeping your plant roots safe from flooding and mud.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛjegbɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu lɛ naa moŋ fe ni eeeha ejo foi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni nɔ kwɔ ni aaafee loo nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋtayaai amli lɛ ni atsa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni nu lɛ ajɛ mli. ni oha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ nu afua kɛ sũ he.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to make raised soil mounds before planting roots like yams or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfee shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani wɔdu shishifãi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Raised mounds keep soil loose so crop tubers can grow large and long. Mounding also lifts roots above standing rainwater during wet months, protecting your crop from rot and mud damage.
ga: Gɔŋ ni awo nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ adara ni efee kakadaŋŋ. Gɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa hu ni ewoɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛyaa nugbɔ nu lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ nyɔji lɛ amli. Buu onibii ahe kɛjɛ fitemɔ kɛ muji ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why should I plant my crops in neat rows instead of scattering seeds everywhere across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo nɔ moŋ fe ni magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Row planting gives every plant its own space, sunlight, and nutrients to grow strong. It also creates walkways that make weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier without stepping on young plants.
ga: Row planting haa tso fɛɛ tso naa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa edara jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa gbɛ ko hu baa ni haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa ni anaaa tsei bibii anɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to put my seeds into the ground when the rainy season approaches?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: Planting too early in dry dirt burns seeds, while planting late during flooding washes them away. The best time is right after the first steady rains when the soil stays moist enough to help seeds sprout quickly.
ga: Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ nu afua be mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ afite. Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo bɔ ni sa ni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and drop off when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked in water for too long, plant roots drown because they cannot breathe. Drowning roots rot underground, which makes the leaves turn yellow and drop off from lack of nourishment.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbo ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do insect pests appear in large numbers on my young crops immediately after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo jeɔ kpo yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Warmth and humidity from early rains cause hidden insect eggs in the soil and surrounding weeds to hatch quickly. Checking leaf undersides early helps you spot pest outbreaks before they destroy tender shoots.
ga: Dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni jɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ mli lɛ haa kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Enɛ baaye abua bo ni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ dani amɛfite tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy and black even after I bring it home from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli ewo muji ni eyɛ ediŋŋ beni mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba shia po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize rots in storage if harvested wet or packed away before drying properly. Trapped moisture creates heat and fungi, so sun-drying grain until it is hard and dry is required before storing.
ga: Abɛi fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ ni efɔ lɛ loo awo mli dani egbi jogbaŋŋ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbi dani akɛto.

english: How can I safely store my harvested beans at home so weevils do not eat them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ mi-nuts ni mikpa lɛ ato shĩa shweshweeshwe koni ŋmeii akaye amɛ?

english: Storing well-dried beans in sealed, airtight bags prevents insects from getting air to survive. Without oxygen, weevils and their eggs die off, keeping your bean harvest clean for months.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛwui lɛ baagboi. Ha o-bean ni okpa lɛ he atse nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I store my bags of harvested crops directly on the mud or concrete floor of my room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-nibii ni mikpa lɛ kotokui lɛ toɔ sũ loo kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Floors draw moisture from the ground into crop bags, causing dampness, rotting, and mold. Storing bags on raised wooden pallets keeps air circulating beneath them and preserves your harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa grow bag lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui to tsei ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kotokui lɛ ashishi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ akafiteɔ.

english: What is the best way to dry my crops after harvest if rain keeps falling unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ? Kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be trukaa?

english: Drying crops on clean raised tarps or plastic sheets allows you to cover or move them quickly when rain starts. Keeping crops off bare ground prevents them from re-absorbing moisture and mud.
ga: Nibii ni adu yɛ tarp loo plastic ni he tse nɔ ni ooogbi lɛ haa onyɛɔ ohaa nɔ loo otsiɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ sũ ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because their leaves burn easily under direct sun, and their roots are too small to drink enough water from hot soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Ni shishifãi lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛnu nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: Why is it important to leave some big trees standing in my farm when clearing land for crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijieɔ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Large shade trees protect crops from harsh sunlight, keep the soil cool and moist during dry seasons, and drop leaves that rot into rich natural fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Tsei wuji haa hɔnɔ ni amɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni ehaa baai ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, dark conditions. Letting more sunlight into the farm and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the wet rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ hulu la babaoo gbɛ ni ebote ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hela ni fiteɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why are the stems of my cocoa trees swelling and the leaves turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fũuɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ feɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Swollen stems and red leaf veins are signs of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Affected trees must be removed so the virus does not spread to healthy neighboring trees.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai lɛ ahe fãji tsuji ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadii. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is a green bush-like plant growing directly out of my cocoa tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni tamɔ jwɛi eŋɔlii miikwɛ̃ kɛmiijɛ mi-kookoo niji lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite that steals water and food directly from your cocoa tree. You must cut it off below its base, or it will slowly weaken and kill the branch.
ga: Tso nɛɛ ji mistletoe. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ ofo lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ fiofio ni ebaafite niji

english: Why should I cut off healthy branches from my cocoa tree if I want more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛji miitao ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches that waste the tree's energy on leaves instead of pods. It also opens up the tree so air and sunlight can flow through, reducing disease.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ŋmeii lɛ. Egbeleɔ tsei lɛ hu koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa shi.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when there are not enough tiny insects (midges) to pollinate them. Keeping mulch on the soil creates a good home for these beneficial insects.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii (teŋgbɛ nibii) ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ náa shia kpakpa.

english: Planting crops too close forces them to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak plants, smaller harvests, and faster spread of diseases.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya

english: Cassava roots grow very aggressively and will steal water and food away from young cocoa trees. It is better to use plantain or cocoyam for temporary shade instead.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ daa oya. ni ebaaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ kookoo tsei bibii amli Esa akɛ akɛ plantains loo kookooi atsu nii akɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo moŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is hungry without taking it to a laboratory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mikɛyaaa laboratori lɛ?

english: You can tell by watching your plant leaves: yellowing leaves usually mean a lack of nitrogen, while pale leaves with weak growth mean the soil is missing key nutrients needed for crop growth.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole kɛtsɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ nɔ: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain leaves act like big umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain baai ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Tomatoes often drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when bees are not around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomatoi shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food that helps crops stay green and produce food for growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii kɛha dalɛ.

english: Covering the ground, also known as mulching, keeps moisture in the soil during dry hot days, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the soil cool for plant roots.
ga: Ale mulching hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔi amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me very small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi kɛ́ akpa lɛ, ewoɔ shishifãi bibii waa lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing top leaves instead of storing food down in the underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo hulutsoo be babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main tree for water and soil nutrients. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to bear a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfite lɛ?

english: Curled or wrinkled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the leaf undersides, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe loo ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo kɛjɛ leaf curl hela ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your crops, effectively starving your plants even if you care for them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji okwɛɔ amɛ po.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young corn leaves and sawdust-like droppings inside the funnels?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center shoot of young corn plants during the day and feeds on the soft leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves green up and gives the plant energy to make large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ organic loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: What benefit does putting cow dung or poultry manure in my field give my crops compared to quick chemical fertilizers?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ tsina loo kooloo ŋmei ni mikɛfataa miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ani akɛto tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii oya lɛ ahe?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil over a long period while helping it hold onto rainwater better, which keeps your plants healthy even during short dry spells.
ga: Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo mli po.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in the exact same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ he kome pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces them to fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil, which results in weak stalks and smaller cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Does it matter which way I push my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, ani okɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ko nɔ?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down makes it difficult for the sprouts to grow upward toward the sun, which delays growth and reduces your overall yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni aduɔ kɛyaa shishi lɛ baaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ baaha shweremɔ aba shi ni ebaaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Tall shade trees act like umbrellas that protect the seedlings from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do small caterpillars destroy my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them naturally?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miifite mi-cabbage baai lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu amɛhe yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Caterpillars hatch from eggs laid by moths to feed on leafy crops. Spraying a simple mixture made from crushed neem leaves or seeds acts as a natural barrier that stops them from eating your plants.
ga: Kplukai fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii fɔɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye tsei ahe baai. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo Akɛ neem baai loo dumɔwui ni atswa lɛ fee, ni etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaye otsei lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn black and rot before they can turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This black rot happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps prevent the fruit from spoiling.
ga: Nɛkɛ black rot hela nɛɛ baa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafite.

english: Why do weeds harm my pepper plants even if I give the crops plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miitutua mi-pepper tsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crop plants and steal the nutrients and light meant for your peppers, leaving your crops weak and unproductive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ ni amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha o-peppers lɛ. Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without producing any pods during hot dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When the sun is too intense and soil water is low, bean plants drop their blossoms to save energy and stay alive until better weather returns.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, ŋmeii tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice for me to plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which puts nitrogen back into the soil, restoring the nutrients that the heavy-feeding maize crop took out.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Koni akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ŋmãa ni ayeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ ejie lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: If I plant fewer seeds across my field, will the remaining crops actually yield bigger harvests?
ga: Kɛ midu dumɔwui fioo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ baawo yibii babaoo diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes. When crops like maize or cassava have more space, their roots can access soil nutrients and water without competing with neighboring plants, which allows individual plants to grow stronger and yield larger produce.
ga: Hɛɛ. Be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ná he ko babaoo. Amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ebɔko akaŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: What happens to my maize plants if I overcrowd them on my plot to try to get more plants?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔ lɛ eyi obɔ kɛteke nɔ koni mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni maná tsei babaoo?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they shade each other from sunlight and fight for nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, tall, and weak, resulting in very small or missing cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe shade ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛhe waaa, amɛkwɔ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛbɛ ŋmeii.

english: If I cut off the top stems of my pepper plants, will that stop leaf growth and help produce more peppers?
ga: Kɛji mifo ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ Ani baai lɛ baakpa shweremɔ ni eye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo aba?

english: Trimming the main top stem stops upward height growth and encourages the plant to spread outward. This produces more side branches, which leads to more flowers and a higher yield of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi tso titri lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ dalɛ kpaa ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni egbɛ eshwa kponɔgbɛ. Enɛ baaha tsei niji babaoo akwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi babaoo kɛ chili babaoo ni afeɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small even though the leafy stems above the ground look bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ ahe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛji ŋmɔji kɛ eŋɔli moŋ?

english: When there is excessive nitrogen in the soil, cassava plants focus all their energy on developing leaves and tall stems above ground instead of storing food in their root tubers below.
ga: Beni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed their leaves during the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival mechanism. Cocoa trees drop leaves in dry conditions to reduce water loss from transpiration, preserving moisture in their stems until the rains return.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Cacao tsei duɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hei ni egbi koni nu ni shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ tso lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil around them is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves and usually recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagbee shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the yellow flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures become too high because extreme heat prevents successful pollination and causes the plant stress, leading it to shed unfertilized blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni afɔɔɔ amɛ fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or beans in my land make my maize grow better in the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When the legume crop finishes, that natural nitrogen remains in the soil to feed nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu legume lɛ agbe naa Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei ni nitrogen he hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain turn yellow once the big bunch of fruit appears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji ŋmeii wuji je kpo lɛ?

english: Once a plantain produces a bunch, it diverts nutrients away from its older lower leaves to feed the developing fruit, causing those lower leaves to turn yellow and die naturally.
ga: Kɛji plantains lɛ je kpo yɛ kui amli Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa nakai baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: If I remove the yellow, spotted leaves from my tomato plants, will it help the plant stay healthy?
ga: Kɛ mijie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, Ani ebaaye ebua ni mi tomato tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes. Removing diseased or yellowing lower leaves prevents fungal spores from spreading to fresh growth and allows the plant to focus its energy on healthy leaves and fruit growth.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ loo amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ, ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal spores lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli, ni ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stems upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds or 'eyes' that point upward. If you plant them upside down, the shoots and roots must bend and fight extra hard to grow in the right direction, resulting in weak plants and very small tubers.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛji okɛ amɛ shwie shi. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ shishifãi lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛwu waa fe tsutsu lɛ bɔni afee ni amɛdara yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni bulb lɛ hu faaa kwraa.

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the young plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks with tiny cobs instead of strong stalks with large, healthy cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Mohu ɔ, o náa tso nɛ mi wa kɛ tso ngua ko nɛ he wa.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—their leaves burn easily in full sunlight. Leaving some big trees or planting plantains provides necessary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa establishes strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tsei wuji loo plantains ni ashiɔ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo lɛ maa shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top, signaling that you need to add manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha tsei heei ni daraa yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop dies, that extra food stays in the soil to feed your next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii gboi lɛ Nakai niyenii kroko lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛye oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to erect long wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, prevents leafy diseases, and allows the plant to send maximum energy down to grow big yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛfee niyenii. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ, ni ehaaa baa helai aba, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, drain water and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plantain tree has enough food to yield heavy, full bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii loo suckers ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii titrii lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni tsii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ aba.

english: Why should I cover the ground around my garden crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground, or mulching, acts like a blanket that stops heat from evaporating soil moisture quickly. It keeps the soil cool during dry spells and prevents weeds from growing near your crops.
ga: Mulching, loo mulching tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme afternoon heat or inconsistent watering. When the plant gets stressed by heat or drought, it drops its flowers to save moisture rather than trying to grow fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni bɛ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kɛji hulutsoo loo hɔmɔ ha tsei hao lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and twisting together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling pests early stops the curling and keeps new leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Early Pest Control Ekpaa ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa baai heei feɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an important food for crops, or it is not getting enough water. Adding manure or the right fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni ehaa yibii kpakpai baa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and look sleepy during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni ewɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can drink it from the ground. The leaves droop temporarily to protect themselves and usually stand back up in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper space lets its roots spread and leaves get enough light to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa eshishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: If my cassava plant grows very tall with lots of leaves, does it mean I will get big tubers underground?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava lɛ da waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ maná yitso agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Not necessarily. When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in the root tubers underground.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do flowers fall off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot dry weather, lack of soil water, or an imbalance of nutrients in the soil during flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei kɛ haomɔi kpe, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa, nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ejaaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts work with friendly organisms in the ground to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil as food for the next crop.
ga: Legumes, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and stop growing so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiikpa shweremɔ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water, soil food, and sunlight away from your crops, essentially starving your crop until you clear the weeds away.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ baaha hɔmɔ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aahu kɛyashi obaajie jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are there holes in my young maize leaves and small worms hiding inside the central shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ bu ni akɛtee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing leaf funnel to eat fresh leaves, which can severely weaken the plant if not managed early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai heei lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why should I cut off extra shoot suckers growing around the base of my plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: Extra suckers drink water and eat soil food that the main plant needs. Removing extra suckers leaves more energy for the main stem to produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi lɛ nuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsei ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do I see holes chewed in my crop leaves during the day, but I cannot find any insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu ni atsɔ mli yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Pests like the fall armyworm hide inside the plant funnels or under the soil during the day to escape heat and predators, coming out only at night to feed on your crops.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ cutworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishi loo shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛjo hulutsoo kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ anaa foi. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ pɛ koni amɛbaye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do armyworms and caterpillars suddenly show up in huge numbers on a farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo eba trukaa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Adult moths fly in at night and lay hundreds of eggs on young plants; when these eggs hatch all at once, thousands of caterpillars appear overnight and begin eating the crops simultaneously.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ foɔ kɛboteɔ mli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ tsei bibii anɔ. Kɛ́ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fee ekome lɛ, ŋmeii akpei abɔ jeɔ kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛjeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeli shishi shikome.

english: Can insect pests fly from my neighbor's farm to destroy my own crops?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afã kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli koni amɛbafite mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, adult pests like moths and beetles can easily fly from neighboring farms at night to search for fresh leaves to feed on and lay eggs.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii ni eda tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afã kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli gbɛkɛ mli oya koni amɛyatao baai heei ni amɛkɛye niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui.

english: Why are my crops failing even though I put in all the hard work to clear and weed my land properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ efiteɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa koni mikɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛjie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Proper clearing removes weeds, but crops also require essential soil nutrients, adequate water, and protection from hidden pests or root diseases to stay healthy and grow.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie jwɛi lɛ. Shi niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo shishifãi helai ahe koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara.

english: How can I tell if my farm is struggling because of poor soil or because of insect pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ miifee basaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahewɔ?

english: Pests usually leave physical marks like chewed leaves, holes, or visible waste, whereas poor soil causes widespread yellowing, thin stems, or slow growth without leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu, loo jwɛi ni anaa. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ babaoo, amɛshishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛbaakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛfiteee baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young crops look strong when they sprout but start dying after a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa beni amɛkwɛ̃ shi amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds use stored energy to sprout, but once that energy runs out, plants depend entirely on root health and soil nutrients, making them vulnerable to hidden stem borers or poor soil quality.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shi kɛ́ hewalɛ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Tsei lɛ damɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ oshara akɛ amɛbaabote tsei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ amli.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray pesticides to catch night pests like armyworms?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ koni mikɛmɔ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ asraafoi a-sraafoi?

english: Spraying in the late evening or early morning is most effective because that is when nocturnal pests come out to feed and direct sunlight won't weaken the chemicals.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, gbɛkɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa tsofai lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Is there a simple local method I can use to stop worms from eating my young maize leaves if I cannot afford chemicals?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni ji maŋ lɛ mli ni manyɛ matsɔ nɔ matsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ? Kɛji minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofai

english: Putting a small handful of clean dry sand or wood ash into the top funnel of young maize plants can scratch and suffocate small worms without harming the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã ni egbi loo tso sũ ni mli tse fioo ko fata ŋmãa tso bibioo ko yiteŋgbɛ ŋã lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋã bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ amɛ agbɔjɔ ni eyeee ŋmãa lɛ awui.

english: What immediate steps should I take when I notice a sudden pest attack starting on one part of my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ mina akɛ trukaa lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miiba miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ?

english: Act immediately by destroying heavily affected plants in that section, hand-picking visible insects early in the morning, and applying recommended treatments before the pests spread to the rest of the field.
ga: Feemɔ nɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni ena naagbai waa yɛ nakai fã lɛ mli lɛ akpãtãmɔ nɔ. Okɛ onine afɔ kooloi bibii fɛɛ ni anaa lɛ anɔ leebi. ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii dani tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ mli.

english: Why do armyworms prefer to attack maize crops rather than other plants on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmãa fe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants have tender, sweet leaves and central funnels that collect moisture, creating a perfect shelter and food source for armyworms to feed and grow quickly.
ga: Abele tsei yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛ funnel ko yɛ teŋgbɛ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Ehaa asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ náa he ko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ nii ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: How long does it take for a new cocoa tree to start giving pods after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties start producing pods within 2 to 3 years with good farm care, whereas older traditional varieties take about 4 to 5 years to start bearing fruit.
ga: Hybrid cocoa henɔi lɛ baabɔi pods feemɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain shoots on my farm at the same time as my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce broad leaves that shade young cocoa seedlings from strong sunlight, protecting them from drying out during their first two years.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ kookoo tsei anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my cocoa seedlings die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings often suffer from transplant shock, taproot damage during planting, or extreme heat when exposed to direct sunlight without enough shade and moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni atsakeɔ amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Taproot lɛ fite yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ. aloo ekɛ ehe woɔ la ni mli edɔ waa mli yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli.

english: How often do I need to clear weeds around my young cocoa trees during the first two years?
ga: Ehe miihia ni mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ. Shii enyiɛ miduɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa trees compete heavily with weeds for soil nutrients and water, so you should weed around their bases every 2 to 3 months during the early years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okɛ jwɛi awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ he daa nyɔji 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during the dry Harmattan season mean the tree is heat-stressed and lacks sufficient moisture and shade to keep its leaves healthy.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni ebɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of expanding tubers below ground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nitrogen bɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves start turning pale green or yellow, starting from the leaf tips and moving inward in a V-shape.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Ejeɔ shishi yɛ baa lɛ naagbee ni eyaa mli yɛ V su mli.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, overly wet, and humid farm conditions with poor air movement.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ waa ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ

english: How does heavy rainfall affect my cocoa flowers during the flowering season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Very heavy rain can wash away pollen or physically knock delicate cocoa flowers off branches before insects have a chance to pollinate them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe loo etswa kookoo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Is it helpful to cut off some of the branches from my growing cocoa trees?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tso ni miida lɛ niji komɛi?

english: Yes, pruning removes dead or weak branches and opens the canopy to sunshine and air, which reduces fungal diseases and helps the tree produce more flowers and pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. ni ogbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is being attacked by pests like Fall Armyworm, which drain nutrients from the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miitutua lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has enough moisture for planting after the first rains?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of soil into a ball; if it holds together without dripping water and breaks apart easily when pressed, it is ready for planting.
ga: Mimɔ shikpɔŋ sũ fioo ko mli ni ofee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he, nu ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ lɛ, no lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leafy stems but small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or planting cassava stems too close together makes the plant spend all its energy growing leaves instead of storing food in the tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I leave space between my cassava plants instead of crowding them together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni mikɛ amɛ baabɔ he?

english: Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients so the roots can expand into big tubers.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ alɛɛ mli ni amɛfee yitso agbo.

english: What causes young cocoa pods on my trees to turn black and dry up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, a fungal attack that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions during the rainy season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when they look green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and get top-heavy when fruiting, so without wooden props or if root-damaging pests are present, strong winds can easily pull them down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ yɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala amɛ kɛba shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Is it bad to put fertilizer directly against the stem of my crop?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, putting fertilizer right on the stem can burn the plant and destroy delicate surface roots. It is best placed a few inches away in a ring or small hole.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛto he ko ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo buji lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. inchi fioo komɛi pɛ

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm even after I cleared them with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miikwɛ̃ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade jie lɛ po?

english: Clearing with a cutlass only removes the top of the weed, leaving the living roots under the dirt ready to shoot up again after rain.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ŋmɔ jwɛi lɛ, jwɛi lɛ yiteŋ pɛ jieɔ. Shishifãi ni hiɛ ka yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lolo, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when bees and wind aren't moving pollen between flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii pollen yɛ fɔfɔi ateŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants drop and wilt during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants lose water quickly through their leaves in afternoon heat, so they temporarily wilt to conserve moisture until the sun cool down.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulu lɛ haa amɛhe jɔɔ.

english: Why do my palm nuts yield less quality oil if I wait too long after harvesting to process them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm ŋmeii lɛ haaa fɔ ni ehiii kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ dani mikɛtsu nii lɛ?

english: Once oil palm fruit is cut from the tree, natural enzymes immediately start breaking down the fresh fats inside into free fatty acids. Processing them quickly preserves the high-quality oil and valuable by-products like glycerin used in skin creams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo mu tso lɛ yibii lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli enzymes lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛgbalaa mu hee ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ fatty acids ni aheee nɔ ko. Kɛ́ atsu he nii oya lɛ, ehaa fɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni jara wa ni jɛɔ mli baa, tamɔ glycerin ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hewolo nɔ tsofai amli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Can I use the waste liquid and ash from my cocoa pod husks after harvest, or is it just trash?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni fiteɔ nii kɛ sũ ni jɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akpaa sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii? Aloo eji jwɛi kɛkɛ?

english: Cocoa pod husks are rich in potassium; when burned to ash and mixed with water, the extract forms the natural lye base used to make traditional soaps and cosmetic creams.
ga: Potassium babaoo yɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ ashã lɛ, etsɔɔ lamulu ni ekɛ nu futuɔ. Nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli lye shishitoo ni akɛfeɔ blema samla kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava spoil so quickly within just two or three days of being dug up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living organs full of water and starch. Once detached from the stem, the root loses its natural defenses, causing rapid chemical breakdown and rotting within a few days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji gbɔmɔtso mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ eyi mli obɔ. Kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsofai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ.

english: Why do buyers prefer cassava that is harvested during the dry season rather than the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmei ni akpaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ?

english: During the dry season, cassava roots absorb less water from the soil, resulting in a higher concentration of starch. This makes the root denser, heavier, and better suited for processing into gari or flour.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Cassava shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu fioo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji starch ni mli edɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛhe tsiimɔ, ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafee gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start growing green shoots even when I store them in a dark barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ewo duŋ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers are living storage stems that go into a temporary resting state. When their internal biological clock detects a change in season, they naturally use their stored water and nutrients to sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji tsei ni hiɛ ka ni boteɔ shihilɛ ni mli wa mli. Kɛji akɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ na be tsakemɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo wain tsei heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do mature coconuts have less liquid inside them compared to young green coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu fioo pɛ yɔɔ ŋmei momo mli kɛ akɛto ŋmei bibioo he lɛ?

english: As a coconut matures on the palm, the tree gradually converts the inner liquid water into solid white coconut meat, which is rich in natural fats and oils.
ga: Kɛji ŋmei ko kwɛ̃ yɛ onine nɔ Tso lɛ baatsake nu ni ji nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fiofio ni etsɔ ŋmei loo yɛŋ ni wa. ni adebɔɔ mli fɔ kɛ fɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do wild shea trees take so many years before they start producing their first fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli shea tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛjeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ awomɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Shea trees invest their early years building an extremely deep taproot system to survive long dry seasons. Only after establishing strong underground roots do they produce oil-rich nuts used for food and cosmetics.
ga: Tonchia kɛ shika wo shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni afee taproot gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni mli kwɔ waa ni baaha ehi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli. Beni ato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni wa ama shi pɛ kɛkɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa mɔ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming fruits when the weather becomes very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni amɛwooo yibii be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes pollen to dry out or become sterile. Without successful pollination, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ loo efeɔ nɔ ni nyɛɛɛ afɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants turn yellow and stop growing during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills air pockets in the soil, suffocating plant roots so they cannot absorb nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green chlorophyll and fuel growth.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashɛɔ he ko ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nitrogen. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee klorofil eŋɔli lɛ kɛ fuel lɛ dalɛ.

english: Why does my stored maize get infested with small insects even though I put clean grain into the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni he tse wo shwapo lɛ mli po?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside the grain kernels while the maize is still in the field. If the harvested grain still contains moisture, those eggs hatch inside the storage bin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui bibii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ, Nakai ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ nutoohe ko mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is short on nitrogen. The plant automatically moves stored nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to nourish the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their crops with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried leaves or grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps the root zone cool in hot weather, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Young cocoa plants sunburn easily under direct sunlight. Planting plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the air moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ hulu lɛ shãa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ Ebaaha hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni eye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs tall stakes to lift its leaves into the sunlight. Better sun exposure helps the plant make more food to grow large, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni shwieɔ shi ni he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaving too many suckers around a plantain tree causes them to compete for nutrients and water, which reduces the size and weight of the main plantain bunch.
ga: Ni aaashi ŋmeii lɛ abɔle Dumɔwui babaoo tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ niyenii kɛ nu he. Enɛ baaha plantain tso titri lɛ dalɛ kɛ etsitsinɔnii aba shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long, especially in heavy clay ground. Excess water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ.

english: What is making ragged holes in the center of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the whorl and eating the tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fall armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii amli ni amɛyeɔ baai ni miida ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water supply is irregular, or flowers are not pollinated properly, preventing fruit from setting.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi lɛ mli lɛ jeee nɔ ni sa. Aloo afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibii lɛ waaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants look droopy in the afternoon sun even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself and usually recovers in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu ehe he, ni bei pii lɛ, ebaagbɔjɔ kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ he?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the maize plants to fight each other for sun, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and very small ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii waa.

english: How do I know when my plantain fruits are ready to be harvested from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the fingers become plump and lose their sharp angles, typically around 3 to 4 months after flowering, even while still green if you plan to transport them long distances.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛniji lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ efo mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ asɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛbaakã he amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ okɛ amɛ aya he ko ni jɛkɛ moŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain trees turning yellow and dying before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually caused by a lack of nutrients like potassium, drought stress, or fungal diseases such as Black Sigatoka. Adding well-rotted manure or compost around the base helps keep leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa tamɔ potassium ni bɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Black Sigatoka, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fataa he Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa.

english: How long should I leave my cassava in the ground before digging it up?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ dani mafo?

english: Most cassava varieties reach full maturity between 9 to 12 months after planting. Leaving them in the ground past 15 to 18 months can cause the roots to become tough, woody, and less marketable.
