ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔji 15 kɛyashi 18 lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ afee nɔ ni wa, ni efee tamɔ tso, ni jara waaa.

english: Why does cassava spoil so quickly after I dig it out of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ ajie ŋmei kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, egboɔ oya lɛ?

english: Cassava roots have high water content and continue to breathe rapidly after harvest, causing internal rot within 2 to 3 days unless stored in cool soil, processed into products like gari, or consumed quickly.
ga: Nu babaoo yɛ cassava shishifãi amli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛmu oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Ehaa mligbɛ fitemɔ baa gbii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli ja akɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ nɔ. Afeɔ lɛ nibii tamɔ gari loo ayeɔ oya.

english: What kind of place or soil is best for planting cocoyam on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ he loo shikpɔŋ nɔ̃ ji nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoyams grow best in loose, rich, moist soils that hold water well without getting completely flooded, and they benefit from light shade beneath tall trees.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni baa nii, ni nu yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu shwieee nɔ kwraa lɛ nɔ. Ni amɛnáa hulutsoo blɛoo ni yɔɔ tsei kakadaji ashishi lɛ he sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoyam plants developing brown spots and rotting prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is often caused by Taro Leaf Blight, a common fungal disease triggered by high humidity and continuous rainfall, which weakens the plant and reduces tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, albino baa mli hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting so that the crop yields well?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛ́ midu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Plant maize seeds in rows about 75 cm apart, leaving 25 to 30 cm between plants within each row. Spacing them properly prevents plants from crowding each other and competing for light and nutrients.
ga: Dumɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa mli ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee 75 cm, ni tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee 25 kɛyashi 30 cm yɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa mli. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baatsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkabɔ amɛhe ni amɛkatswa akaŋ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the funnel of young maize plants; spraying recommended biological or chemical controls at early detection protects your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ afɔse nɔ kɛji ana lɛ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why is it good for my farm soil if I plant maize after harvesting legumes like beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa beni mikpa ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Planting maize after legumes allows the maize to feed on that stored nitrogen, leading to healthier growth and better yields.
ga: Legumes jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii adumɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa abɛi lɛ yeɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ. Ekɛ dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ yibiiwoo ni hi baa.

english: How can I prevent crops like plantain and cassava from getting damaged when taking them to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava naa koni ekafite kɛji mikɛba jara nɔ?

english: Harvest during cool early morning hours, avoid dropping or scratching the produce, and pad transport vehicles with fresh leaves or straw to absorb bumps on rough roads.
ga: Kpamɔ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni oooshwie shi loo oooshwie shi lɛ he. ni okɛ baai loo jwɛi hee aha tsɔnei ni akɛ nibii majeɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛjie ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains to protect their delicate leaves, keep the soil cool, and retain moisture until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛbaai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa kwraa

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛfata kookoo tsei ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Cassava grows heavy, deep roots that compete aggressively with young cocoa trees for nutrients and water in the soil. It is better to use plantains or cocoyams instead, which provide gentle shade without starving the young cocoa.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni tsii, ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ cacao tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ plantain loo kookoo atsu nii moŋ, ni ehaa hulutsoo be blɛoo ni hɔmɔ yeee kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why do so many flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce thousands of flowers, but only a small fraction become pods. Factors like dry weather, lack of insect pollinators, or poor soil nutrients cause the tree to shed excess flowers to save energy for the surviving pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi fã bibioo ko pɛ No sɛɛ lɛ ebafeɔ pod. Nibii tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni pollinators bɛ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka lɛ.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa trees reduce how much harvest I get?
ga: Ani niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha yibiiwoo ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing extra or weak branches lets sunlight reach the tree trunk where pods grow and directs the tree's energy into producing bigger, healthier cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha onibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi he ni ŋmeii lɛ daa lɛ, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cold, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning branches to let air and sunlight inside the farm helps dry out the pods and stops the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aba ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: What causes tiny dark spots and dry patches on my young cocoa stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? Ni hei ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage comes from sap-sucking insects called capsids or mirids. They thrive in overly sunny spots, so maintaining steady shade trees and treating affected areas controls their population.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo mirids lɛ amli. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ he ko ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni okwɛ he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ baakudɔ eyibɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop lacks vital soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the roots are trapped in waterlogged soil. Adding organic manure or proper fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli. Organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil waiting for sunlight and rain to grow. Covering bare soil with organic material or cover crops blocks sunlight, preventing dormant weed seeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe tee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmiimɛ hulu kɛ nugbɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu la naa. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye nɔ.

english: Why must I ferment my cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ woɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani migbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the beans to remove the natural bitterness, develop the rich chocolate flavor, and turn the inside of the bean brown. High-quality, fermented beans attract better market demand and top prices.
ga: Fermentation haa ŋmeii lɛ mli dɔɔ koni ejie amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Feemɔ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ ni okɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Soybeans ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gbalaa jarayeli nibii ni ataoɔ kɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How does drying my cocoa beans properly affect the price I get at the buying depot?
ga: Te mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ni migbiɔ lɛ saa jara ni minine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ he ni miheɔ nii yɛ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Thoroughly sun-drying cocoa beans prevents mold growth and spoils during storage. Buyers pay premium prices for clean, well-dried cocoa that meets international export quality standards.
ga: Cocoa yibii ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ kɛ fitemɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ kookoo ni he tse, ni egbi jogbaŋŋ ni kɛ majimaji ateŋ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he nyɔmɔ ni nɔ kwɔ waa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvesting without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava usually matures between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant starts to swell and crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots inside the yam barn even when I haven't planted them yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ mi-sweet potatoes ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miduuu lɛ kwraa?

english: Yam tubers naturally go into a resting period after harvest. Once warm weather or humidity returns, the tuber senses the change in environment and naturally breaks dormancy to start growing a new plant using the food stored inside itself.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii boteɔ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulutsoo be ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Yitso lɛ nuɔ tsakemɔi ni baa shihilɛ mli lɛ he. Ni efoɔ ebɔɔ su ni eyɔɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛ niyenii ni ato yɛ emli lɛ aje tsei heei akwɛmɔ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain take so long to produce a bunch if I leave all the young shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The main plantain stem shares its food and water with all the shoots growing around it. If you leave too many shoots, the main plant gets starved of nutrients and takes longer to mature. Removing extra shoots leaves energy for the main plant to grow faster and yield bigger bunches.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmeii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ jaa niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Tso titri lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii dani edaa. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eda oya ni ekɛ niji wuji aba.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil still has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo moŋ?

english: During very hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to close its leaf pores and save water, but it usually recovers once the afternoon heat reduces.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛgbala baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛ nu ato he. Shi bei pii lɛ, amɛhe waaa kɛji shwane mli latsaa lɛ ba shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mostly because of extreme sun heat or dry spells. When the weather gets too hot or the soil dries out completely, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa lɛ hewɔ ni tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the tall trees off my land before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like soft infants that cannot stand full direct sunlight or harsh dry winds. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the cocoa leaves from burning and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ abifabii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baabu kookoo baai ahe koni amɛkashã, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow and stay small when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded together, their roots fight for the same food and water in the soil while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition starves the plants of nutrients like nitrogen, making the leaves turn yellow and slowing down growth.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ kɛhaa niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haaa tsei lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo.

english: Why is it harmful to apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can drink them in safely. Applying fertilizer to dry soil traps concentrated chemicals around the roots, which can scorch or burn them and damage the crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa tsofai ni fa babaoo bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni baanyɛ ashã loo ashã ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do people say that planting cowpeas or groundnuts improves my soil for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that suck nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food. When the crop matures and leaves decay, that food stays trapped in the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni shwieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tso niyenii Beni tso lɛ daa ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ Nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why do the center leaves of my young maize plants look shredded with dark powder sitting inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni powda ni tsuɔ diŋ eta ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls into the hidden central funnel of the maize plant to hide during the hot day and chews on the tender growing leaves, leaving behind dark waste that looks like wet sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni shwieɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ehe awo mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni ekɛ blɛoo ŋmɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ Eshiɔ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ.

english: What does it mean when someone tells me to prune my mango tree?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo mi mango tso lɛ?

english: Pruning simply means carefully cutting off specific branches or parts of a tree so it can stay healthy and produce better fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ niji loo fãi ni afoɔ lɛ tsɔɔ. tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off branches from my fruit tree if I want more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mitso lɛ niji kɛji miitao aduawai babaoo?

english: Removing unnecessary or overgrown branches helps the tree direct its strength and nutrients to the remaining flowers, allowing fruits to set and grow properly.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni eda fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa fɔfɔi ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛhe gbɛjianɔ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my mango trees producing flowers, but very few fruits actually form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei yɛ fɔfɔi shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many unnecessary branches, it lacks the energy for proper fruit setting. Cutting off extra branches helps flowers develop into full fruits.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji babaoo ni he ehiaaa Ebaaha hewalɛ ni bɛ ni ekɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can cutting branches on my fruit tree cause diseases to get into the plant?
ga: Ani mitso lɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha hela aba tso lɛ mli?

english: Yes, if the cut edges are left damaged or rough, the open cuts can fester and allow fungal diseases to settle inside the tree.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmei ni afoɔ lɛ efite loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Pilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ baanyɛ atswa ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ aba tso lɛ mli.

english: What will happen if I leave broken or poorly cut branches on my tree?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi tso lɛ niji ni ekumɔ loo ni afolɔ waa lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Rough cut edges can fester and rot, which attracts diseases that weaken the tree and prevent your fruit from setting well.
ga: Eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbo. Enɛ gbalaa helai ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa tso lɛ yibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛbaa enɔ.

english: How does trimming off tree parts help keep my farm free of crop diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai akabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Trimming removes crowded or dying parts, which stops dampness from building up and prevents crop diseases from settling in.
ga: Trimming jieɔ fãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fãi ni egboi lɛ. Enɛ haaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ abua naa, ni ehaa tsei ahe helai hu shwieɔ shi.

english: Will removing parts of a fruit tree kill it or stop it from growing?
ga: Ani tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ mligbalamɔ baagbe lɛ loo ebaakpa edalɛ?

english: No, as long as you do it properly, removing weak or extra branches actually gives the tree more energy to grow strong and set healthy fruit.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ ofee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni fa babaoo lɛ ajiemɔ diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni etsɔ hewalɛ ni ewo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my small fruits fall off the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii bibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruits often fail to set properly if the tree is affected by disease or spending too much energy trying to feed extra, unnecessary branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ kɛji hela ko emɔ tso lɛ nɔ loo akɛ hewalɛ babaoo miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni aha tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ niyenii.

english: How can I prevent my mango tree from getting sick after trimming it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-mango tso lɛ naa koni hela akamɔ mi beni afolɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You must make clean, careful cuts so the edges heal properly without festering, which keeps diseases from entering the fresh cuts.
ga: Esa akɛ ofolɔ pilamɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋwɛigbɛi lɛ atsa jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akabote pilamɔi heei amli.

english: Does cutting branches off my tree actually improve the quality of my harvest?
ga: Ani mitso lɛ niji ni mifoɔ lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, trimming unwanted parts stops the tree from wasting resources, leading to cleaner trees, fewer diseases, and better fruit setting.
ga: Hɛɛ, fãi ni ataooo lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baahere tso lɛ kɛjɛ nibii ni efiteɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tseɔ, helai fioo pɛ baa, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant my seeds too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too close together blocks fresh air from circulating around the plants and prevents roots from getting enough air pockets in the soil, which stunts their growth.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abɔle tso lɛ he, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi dalɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to loosen or dig up the soil before I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo mifoɔ mli dani miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Digging loosens hard soil to trap air inside. Roots need to breathe air just like human beings, and loose soil allows roots to easily spread out and take in oxygen.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni afoɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, ehe miihia ni shishifãi amu kɔɔyɔɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni amɛnáa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa mlɛo.

english: Can crop roots really drown if floodwater stays on my farm for too long?
ga: Ani tsei shishifãi baanyɛ atsɔ nu mli diɛŋtsɛ kɛji nu afua lɛ hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Yes, roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers your field for too long, it pushes out all the air, causing the plant roots to suffocate and rot.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ha oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ baatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my crops start to wilt even when there is plenty of sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi shwiemɔ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Sunlight helps crops grow, but plants need water to carry nutrients through their stems. Without enough soil moisture, hot sunlight dries the plant out faster than it can drink.
ga: Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa. Shi nu he miihia tsei koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ enu.

english: Why do my crops wilt when I give them too much water every single day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ fe nine daa gbi lɛ?

english: Giving crops too much water fills up all the empty spaces in the soil where air is supposed to be. Without air in the soil, the plant roots cannot function properly to drink the water.
ga: Nu ni okɛwoɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ haa he ni esa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ eyiɔ obɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ anu nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do crops get their food from the soil to grow big?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii náa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Crops feed by absorbing dissolved vitamins and minerals from the soil through their roots, which acts as the main food that sustains their leaf and fruit growth.
ga: Tsei yeɔ nii kɛtsɔ vitamini kɛ mineral ni mli edɔ ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii titri ni yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ

english: Yellow leaves mean your crops are starving because the soil lacks essential plant food, such as nitrogen, which is needed to keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye onibii ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔŋ.

english: What does adding animal manure actually do for my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Manure serves as rich food for the soil. As it breaks down, it feeds the crops with essential nutrients while keeping the soil light so it can hold both water and air.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii babaoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ egbee shi lɛ Ebaaha tsei lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ahaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why won't fertilizer work properly if I apply it when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants cannot swallow dry fertilizer. Soil water is needed to dissolve the fertilizer into liquid food so the plant roots can suck it up.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ ami ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia koni akɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni etsɔ niyenii ni mli tse ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: What basic things do my crops need every day to stay alive and yield well?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii daa gbi koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Just like humans need air, water, and food to survive, crops must have fresh air around their leaves and roots, sufficient water in the soil, and proper soil nutrients to sustain life and produce fruits.
ga: Taakɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nu, kɛ niyenii he hiaa adesai koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi wala mli lɛ. Esa akɛ tsei ana kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ amɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ahe, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ni niyenii kpakpai yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni sa kɛha wala kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full sunlight and heavy heat. Without enough shade from nurse crops like plantains, the intense heat causes rapid water loss and burns the tender leaves, leading to leaf drop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ kɛjɛ tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa baanyɛ aha nu lɛ afite oya ni eshã baai bibii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai ni laajeɔ

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy weight at the top. If tiny root pests called nematodes weaken the root system, or if too many suckers are left competing around the main stem, the roots cannot hold the plant upright in wind.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ ni yeɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ amɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants turn purple when they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ? Ni eji nɔ bibioo kwraa lolo?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are a sign of phosphorus deficiency. When the young roots cannot absorb enough phosphorus from the soil, the crop produces a purple pigment as a stress response.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Kɛji shishifãi bibii nyɛɛɛ ajie fɔsfɔs ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa nɔnyɛɛ hetoo.

english: Why do my maize stalks snap and fall over right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma tsei lɛ fãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani akpaa kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over, known as lodging, when stalk borer caterpillars tunnel inside the stems or when the soil lacks potassium to make the stalks thick and sturdy against strong wind.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ shi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ shĩa. Beni stem borer lɛ tswaa tsɔne ko yɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ potassium ni baaha tso lɛ shishi afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nyɛɔ eshiɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter and stay hard after I boil them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ŋɔɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji ahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava produces natural defensive chemicals during extended dry periods or when grown in poor soil. Bitter varieties or drought-stressed crops produce higher levels of these compounds, which make the tubers taste bitter and take much longer to soften when cooked.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa loo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Tsei srɔtoi ni mli edɔ loo tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eheɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ blɛoo kɛji ahoo.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting in the barn before the rain even begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers have a natural biological clock. After a few months of rest post-harvest, warm temperatures and rising humidity signal to the tuber that its dormancy period is over, triggering sprouts even in storage.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa. Beni ajɔɔ ehe nyɔji fioo komɛi yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ lɛ haa bulb lɛ leɔ akɛ be ni ekɛhiɔ shi lɛ efo. Ekanyaa dumɔwui yɛ nitoohe po.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping all their flowers without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their blossoms when day temperatures get too high or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Excessive heat dries out the flower's pollen, preventing pollination so the blossom dies and falls off.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ babaoo baaha pollen lɛ agbi. Tsi pollination naa No sɛɛ lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gboiɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking small and crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking leaf sap, or by leaf curl virus spread by whiteflies. The feeding damage causes the new leaves to grow distorted and stunted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baa mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ leaf curl hela ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni niyenii ni ayeɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ haa baai heei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Is it better to water my cabbage crop early in the morning or in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha cabbage tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning. Watering in the hot afternoon causes much of the water to evaporate before reaching the roots, and leaving wet leaves in hot conditions creates an ideal environment for fungal leaf diseases to spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani eshɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni kɛ́ ashi baai ni efɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha baai helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ baa.

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which works with beneficial soil bacteria to capture nitrogen from the air and store it in root nodules. When the cowpea plants decay after harvest, they release natural nitrogen into the soil to feed the following maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛkɛ sũ mli helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji cowpea tsei lɛ fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ nɛɛ niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow when there is too much direct sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need partial shade because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the topsoil that their young roots need to survive.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fioo, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ, ni shishifãi bibii lɛ he hiaa koni amɛhi shi.

english: What are those tall, straight shoots growing out near the base of my cocoa trees, and should I remove them?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ ni ja ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mikoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ majie loo esaaa akɛ majie?

english: Those straight vertical shoots are called chupons or leaders. Removing most of them is important because they drain nutrients away from the main tree without producing many pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai tsei ni damɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ja lɛ akɛ chupons loo hiɛnyiɛlɔi. Amɛteŋ babaoo ni ajieɔ lɛ he miihia ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli ni amɛfeee ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do shade trees help my crops survive through the long dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli?

english: Shade trees cool down the surrounding air, block harsh heat, and reduce water evaporation from the soil, keeping ground moisture available longer for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do some of my small cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ gboɔ ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani edaa lɛ?

english: This can happen naturally when a tree drops excess pods it cannot feed, but it is often caused by fungal infections like black pod disease when moisture gets trapped on the pods.
ga: Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ tso lɛ shɛrɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ ashwie. Shi bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli, tamɔ black pod hela, ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, kɛ́ nu tsɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce flowers only during specific times of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi pɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees respond to seasonal weather patterns, triggering flowers mainly when rains begin so that developing pods will have enough water to mature properly.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsuɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ ahe nii. Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut overlapping branches inside my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni feɔ ekome yɛ cacao tso ni eda lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning thick foliage lets sunlight and air move through the tree canopy, which dries out excess humidity that causes crop-damaging molds and rot.
ga: Baai ni mli tse ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baa.

english: How can I tell if my soil lacks the right nutrients for my crops to yield well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa ni baaha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Common signs of poor soil nutrients include pale or yellowing leaves, slow stem growth, and trees producing small or very few fruits compared to healthy farms.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli lɛ he ji baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, kɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii bibii loo fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young cocoa trees so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ waa lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and light from young crops, preventing their roots and branches from developing fully.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ la ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli Enɛ haaa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see black ants moving up and down the trunks of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii diji ni miiho kɛmiijɛ mikoo tsei lɛ anɔ kɛmiiya shi lɛ?

english: Black ants are often attracted to sap-sucking insects like mealybugs that secrete sugary liquid, and these sap-sucking insects can spread damaging crop diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs ni jieɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ sugar lɛ. Ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ni fiteɔ mɔ lɛ ashwã.

english: How do I know when an old cocoa tree needs to be replaced with a new seedling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui heei atsake cacao tsei momoi lɛ?

english: When an aging tree consistently yields very few pods despite good weather and soil care, or has a hollow, diseased trunk, it is time to replant it with a fresh seedling.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbɔ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ be fɛɛ be, yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kpakpai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ fɛɛ sɛɛ. aloo amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ Be eshɛɛ ni abaadu dumɔwui heei.

english: Do I really need to spray chemicals on my cocoa trees to keep insects away?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai afɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ koni mikɛshwie kooloi bibii?

english: While healthy cocoa trees can resist mild insect pressure, major pests like mirids (capsids) can cause severe pod and foliage damage unless you use approved spraying routines during peak pest seasons.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ adamɔ kooloi bibii ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ anaa moŋ, shi kooloi wuji tamɔ mirids (capsids) baanyɛ afite pod kɛ baai lɛ waa. Ja okɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: What happens to my cocoa harvest if I decide not to spray pest control chemicals at all?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-kookoo ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ? Ni kɛji mikpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieŋ nɔ kwraa hu?

english: Without proper pest management, insects can multiply rapidly, damaging young shoots and pods, which significantly reduces your overall yield and can lead to long-term tree damage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya. Ekɛ fitemɔ baa ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi waa. Ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei lɛ afite be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time of day to spray my crops to prevent pests from coming back?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaku amɛsɛɛ aba?

english: Spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon is best because insects are most active then, and cooler temperatures prevent the chemicals from evaporating too quickly off the leaves.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane ejaakɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii waa. Ni hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ haaa tsofai lɛ ajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: If my cocoa trees look very strong and healthy, can pests still destroy them?
ga: Kɛji mi-cocoa tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ waa ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ afite cacao tsei lolo?

english: Healthy, well-nourished trees withstand minor insect attacks better than weak ones, but aggressive pests will still target healthy pods if pest populations in the area get too high.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ kooloi bibii ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni egbɔjɔ. Shi kooloi ni yɔɔ gbeyei waa lɛ baatutua pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ lolo kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ayibɔ fa tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa farm is in good enough condition to resist diseases?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli bɔ ni sa ni hela baanyɛ atswa mi?

english: A resilient cocoa farm has deep green leaves, clean pruned foliage, proper shade cover, and well-drained soil, though routine farm inspections are still necessary to spot early signs of pests.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ nii lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa. baai ni afolɔ mli ni he tse Shade ni sa yɛ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Ehe miihia ni akwɛ ŋmɔ mli daa po koni ana mra be mli nibii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai eba.

english: Does keeping my farm weeded help my cocoa trees stay strong against insects?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei lɛ ahe waa yɛ kooloi bibii ahe?

english: Yes, weeding removes alternative food sources and hiding spots for pests, allowing your cocoa trees to use all available soil nutrients to grow strong and better endure minor pest stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii krokomɛi kɛ hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa o-cacao tsei lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa ni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can leaving open water containers on my farm attract unwanted insects to my cocoa?
ga: Ani nu tsɛnsii ni agbele mli ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ agbala kooloi bibii ni ataooo amɛ kɛba mikoo lɛ mli?

english: Yes, open water containers collect rainwater and create ideal breeding grounds for mosquitoes and other farm pests, which can increase pest populations near your crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni agbele naa lɛ buaa nugbɔ nu naa ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi krokomɛi fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Should I cover the water barrels I keep on the farm for mixing my crop sprays?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maha nu ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni mikɛfutu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Always keep water barrels covered to prevent insects from breeding in them, keep out falling leaves and dirt, and stop wild animals or farm pets from drinking contaminated water.
ga: Ha nɔ ni akɛhaa nu lɛ nɔ lɛ ahi nu lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni kooloi akafɔ. Etsiɔ baai kɛ muji naa koni amɛkagbee shi. ni atsĩ koo mli kooloi loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkanu nu ni mli ewo muji.

english: Can just a few insects breeding near standing water really cause big damage to my cocoa pods?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii fioo komɛi ni fɔɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ masɛi lɛ baanyɛ afite mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ waa?

english: Yes, even a couple of insects laying eggs in standing water can quickly produce hundreds of offspring, leading to a sudden pest outbreak that can spread across your cocoa farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi bibii fioo komɛi po ni woɔ wɔji yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afɔ́ bii ohai abɔ oya. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã okokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baa trukaa.

english: How far away from my cocoa trees should I store my water drums and farm equipment?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mibaket kɛ okwaayeli nibii lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ cacao tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Store water drums and tools at the edge of the farm in a cleared, shaded area away from direct contact with cocoa branches to keep breeding insects from jumping directly onto your trees.
ga: Ha nu baagi kɛ nitsumɔ dadei ahi ŋmɔ lɛ naa yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Ekɛ kookoo niji akakpe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haaa kooloi bibii ni fɔɔ bii lɛ atsɔ otsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantains near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sun. Fast-growing plantains produce large leaves that provide living shade, protecting the delicate cocoa plants until they grow strong enough to endure direct heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Buu cacao tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni enyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ naa.

english: Why is it good for me to leave my farm plot to rest for a season instead of planting continuous crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kome moŋ fe ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Continuous planting drains the soil of essential nutrients and weakens its structure. Allowing the land to rest gives the soil time to naturally rebuild organic matter, retain moisture, and restore nutrients needed for healthy future yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa enáa be ni ekɛsaa ehe nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli, ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli yibiiwoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Is it helpful for me to start growing cowpeas alongside my main maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba aha mi akɛ mabɔi tsina ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa titri ni miduɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes your maize. Mixing crops also means that if bad weather or pests affect one crop, you still have the other to harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha o-ŋmãa Nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ná ŋmɔshi nibii kome nɔ hewalɛ lɛ, Oyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome kroko ni obaakpa.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are common signs that tiny insects like whiteflies or aphids are sucking sap from the leaves, or that the soil lacks key nutrients. Treating the pests early prevents the plant from losing its energy.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo aphids miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. aloo etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii titrii Helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe tsamɔ Mra Ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkafite hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with very small cobs when I place the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo, ni ŋmeii lɛ hu feɔ bibii waa lɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. The maize stretches high to find light, using up energy that should have gone into producing big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi shãa ŋwɛi koni ena la. Hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii koni akɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Shedding leaves is a natural survival strategy for cassava to preserve water during dry spells. The plant goes quiet to conserve moisture underground and will sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni ŋmei tsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tso lɛ baafee dioo koni ekɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ he. ni ebaakwɛ baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes in the same spot where I just harvested garden eggs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ he ni mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie abɔɔ lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Tomatoes and garden eggs belong to the same plant family and share the same diseases and pests. Planting them in the exact same soil back-to-back allows pests left behind in the dirt to quickly attack the new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ abɔɔ mli ŋmeii yɛ tsei aweku kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni eshwɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii heei oya.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. When conditions get too hot or dry, the plant drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive instead of nourishing fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ aduawai lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhi wala mli.

english: How do weeds harm my crops even when there is plenty of rain for everything?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa kɛhaa nɔ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Rain provides water, but weeds grow faster than crops and steal the plant food and fertilizer hidden in the soil. They also block sunlight and can harbor pests that spread diseases to your crops.
ga: Nugbɔ haa nu, shi jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛtsiɔ hulu la hu naa ni amɛhaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ashwã onibii amli lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Why do certified maize seeds from the ministry grow better than seeds I save from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni sɔɔmɔ nitsumɔ lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are carefully bred to resist common local diseases and produce uniform, high yields. Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose those special traits in the next generation, leading to smaller yields and uneven growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ni eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when planted in an open sunny field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They require shade from crops like plantain or taller trees to protect their leaves and retain soil moisture while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains loo tsei kakadaji amli koni amɛbu amɛbaai lɛ ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on to produce large tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ koni ekɛ bulbs agboi aba lɛ?

english: Yam plants produce larger tubers when leaves receive maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out, allowing the plant to capture more light and convert it into energy for tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛ́ baai lɛ nine shɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ la babaoo ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ hewalɛ kɛhaa bulbs ni miida.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape from the tip?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the leaf tips on lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. Maize requires adequate nitrogen, especially during early growth, to maintain dark green leaves and produce full ears.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa he miihia ŋmãa. Titri lɛ yɛ shishijee fãi ni shwereɔ lɛ amli Koni ekwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ayitsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make the next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When harvested, they leave this natural fertilizer behind, enriching the soil for nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Be ni esa akɛ akpa Amɛbaashi nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ. Koni ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa nitrogen, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by the Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, which is spread by tiny sap-sucking insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early stops the spread of this damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli Whitefly Kudɔmɔ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ naa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery droppings inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ powda mli yɛ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ teŋgbɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the young plant during the day and feed on the tender new leaf tissue, requiring early detection and control.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni amɛye baa hee ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ Enɛ biɔ ni ana mra ni akudɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots develop dark rot and smell bad before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔ dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Root rot in cassava usually happens when soil remains waterlogged for too long or when soil-borne fungi enter through insect wounds. Plant on ridges or well-drained soil to prevent water buildup.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmei mli lɛ baa kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ ŋmei ni sũ ewo mli lɛ bote kooloo ko pilamɔ mli. Dumɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ koni nu akabua ehe naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without forming any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat stress or sudden water shortages. Keeping soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant retain flowers and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa trukaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi kɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms before the fruits mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that can be weakened further by soil pests like root nematodes or stem borers. Staking plants with strong wooden poles or bamboo props prevents them from tipping over under heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sũ mli kooloi tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ fĩ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbee shi yɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ ashishi.

english: Why can lowland rice grow inside standing water while my maize crop rots and dies in the same condition?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shihilɛ kome mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels in their stems and roots that transport oxygen from the leaves down to the submerged roots. Maize lacks these air passages and suffocates when roots are underwater for long periods.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ hei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ kɛji eshishifãi lɛ yɛ nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the seeds I planted taking so long to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ejeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need a specific balance of moisture, air, and soil warmth to wake up. If the soil is too dry or the seeds are buried too deep, germination slows down or fails completely.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛte shi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, Germination lɛ baafee mlɛo loo ebaafite kwraa.

english: Can I save seeds from this season's harvested corn to plant again next year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Saving seeds from improved or hybrid varieties often results in weaker plants and lower yields the next season because their strong traits don't pass down reliably.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ loo tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ jeee gboshinii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or roots that are drowned by too much water, preventing the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo shishifãi lɛ efo nu mli fe nine. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer right next to the stem of my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitsei bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ he?

english: Fertilizer placed directly against a plant stem can chemically burn the soft outer skin and damage tender roots. It is best applied a few inches away where roots can safely reach it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni efite shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛwo mli aaafee 2-3 inch kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall fills all the tiny air spaces in the soil with water, suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungus to attack the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ haa nu yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning allows the roots to absorb water before the sun warms up, whereas afternoon watering causes quick evaporation and can heat up the leaves.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu lɛ haa edɔɔ amɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha yɛ shwane mli lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya oya ni ebaaha baai lɛ amli adɔ.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete fiercely for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leading to thin stems, weak growth, and smaller harvests.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ mli wa waa Ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii Dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ kpamɔ fioo

english: Why do crops grown under big trees look tall and thin but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ ni amɛhe tse shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Shaded plants stretch upward searching for light, spending all their energy growing tall instead of building strong stems and developing healthy fruit.
ga: Shade tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛyatao la. Okɛ ohewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni okɛda. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tso ɔmɛ nɛ a he wa, nɛ e woɔ yiblii kpakpahi.

english: Extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of insect pollination causes stress, forcing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy for basic survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei ajie fɔfɔii koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why do weeds always grow much faster than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for water and nutrients, allowing them to outpace cultivated crops that need more care to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe awo nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsei ni aduɔ, ni biɔ kwɛmɔ kɛ hiɛdɔɔ babaoo koni amɛshwere lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees burning and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shã ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their foliage is soft. Without shade trees or plantain plants around them to act as living umbrellas, the heat scorches the leaves and causes them to dry out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ yɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo plantains bɛ he ni ebɔle amɛhe ni baatsu nii akɛ umbrella lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha amɛgbi.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in high humidity and wet conditions. Excess water standing on the pods allows the fungal spores to enter and destroy the beans.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have holes in them like something is eating them from the inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ bu tamɔ nɔ ni nɔ ko eye amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant where it is soft and chew through the leaves before they open up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋshɔi lɛ amli he ni amɛyɔɔ loo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when it rains a lot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need soil that drains water quickly. When water sits around the roots for too long, it cuts off their oxygen supply and allows soil fungus to cause wet rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ he miihia cassava shishifãi. Kɛ́ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can capture light and make food. Lifting the leaves off the ground helps the plant produce energy to grow larger tubers under the soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ la ni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over just when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that can easily get weakened by underground pests like root nematodes. When heavy fruit bunches grow, the plant becomes top-heavy and snaps or uproots in light winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ oya. Kɛ aduawai akuu lɛ da lɛ Tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛkuɔ loo amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of specific nutrients like calcium and boron needed for the fruit to set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni bɛ mli, tamɔ calcium kɛ boron, ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by insects that distorts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni fiteɔ tsei adalɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning light green or yellow even though I give them enough water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Pale or yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build healthy, deep green foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni mli wa, eŋɔli diŋŋ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my land make the soil better for my next crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant harvested or ploughed back into the soil, it leaves behind natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa tsei loo aku sɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: How long can a mango tree stay on my farm and keep giving me fruits?
ga: Be enyiɛ mango tso ko baahi miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni eha mi yibii?

english: Mango trees are long-term perennial trees that can live and produce fruits for 30 to 40 years or more if properly pruned and cared for, unlike short-term crops like maize or vegetables that finish within months.
ga: Mango tsei ji tsei ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii afii 30 kɛyashi 40 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji akɛ afolɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ tamɔɔɔ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ni baaho yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I trim off some of the big branches on my old mango tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo tsei niji wuji lɛ? Mi mango tso momo lɛ hu nɔ?

english: Pruning opens up the top of the tree so sunlight and fresh air can reach all sides. This prevents plant diseases and encourages the tree to channel its strength into producing larger, sweeter fruits instead of just growing heavy leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni fata tso lɛ yiteŋ ni agbeleɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ baatsi tsei ahe helai anaa ni ewo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ awo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ baai ni tsii kɛkɛ

english: Why does my cassava stop producing big tubers after I plant it on the same land for five years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ ekpa ŋmeii wuji ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii enumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava draws a lot of nutrients out of the earth every season. Planting it repeatedly on the same plot exhausts the soil fertility, so the crop can no longer find the nourishment it needs to swell its roots.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be, ni kɛ́ adu amɛ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ dɔŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my farm soil if I clear all the plants away and leave the land bare for a long time?
ga: Mɛni baaba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie tsei lɛ fɛɛ ni mishi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Leaving soil completely bare exposes it to harsh sunlight and heavy rains, which wash away the rich topsoil (erosion) and dry out beneficial soil organisms, making it harder for future crops to grow.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba enɔ. Enɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ (erosion) lɛ nɔ ni egbiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa waa kɛhaa tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings scorch and die when I plant them in direct sun without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight. They need partial shade from nurse crops like plantains or forest trees to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni ji nurse tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ mli ajɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: After how many years will my cocoa farm start losing its strength and produce fewer pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ baaje shishi egbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ baawo?

english: Cocoa trees usually reach peak production between 10 and 25 years. After around 25 to 30 years, yield begins to decline due to tree aging and disease buildup, meaning the farm will eventually need replanting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii 10 kɛyashi 25 mli. Yɛ aaafee afii 25 kɛyashi 30 sɛɛ lɛ, yibiiwoo jeɔ shishi ebaa shi yɛ tsei ni eda kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ yɛ naagbee lɛ, ehe baahia ni adu ŋmɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cassava right beneath my large, full-grown mango tree to save space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mango tso ni eda lɛ shishi koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to build up energy and grow root tubers. The heavy foliage of a mature mango tree blocks sunlight and its big roots steal water, leaving the cassava stunted.
ga: Cassava he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni ená hewalɛ ni eshishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Mango tso ni eda lɛ baai ni tsii lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. ni eshishifãi wuji lɛ juɔ nu Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ egbɔjɔ.

english: Which food crops can I safely plant alongside my young cocoa trees during the first few seasons?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ bei fioo lɛ amli?

english: Crops like plantain, cocoyam, and legumes work well because they provide necessary shade, control weed growth, and produce fast food or income while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ plantains Cocoa kɛ legumes tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛhaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa. Kudɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni ofee niyenii ni ayeɔ oya loo oná shika be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my green maize plants turning yellow in the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rains can wash away nitrogen—the main plant food for green growth—deep into the earth beyond root reach, or waterlog the soil so roots cannot breathe and uptake food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa lɛ, kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he. aloo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry weather spells, or pest damage. Keeping soil moist with mulch and controlling insects helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ nii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, strong sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting tall shade trees or shade crops like plantains acts as a natural umbrella, keeping the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa can build a strong root system.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Tsei kakadaji ni haa hulutsoo loo hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibioo lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves on a maize plant usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. The plant takes nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new top growth, showing that your soil needs compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in the soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain off properly, keeping the tubers dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ efo kɛya. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ Kɛ́ aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ha ŋmeii lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Flowers drop when the crop is under stress from high temperatures, lack of water, or attack by tiny insect pests like thrips. Ensuring consistent watering during dry spells and checking under leaves for insects helps the plant keep its flowers and grow fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa ha tsei lɛ miihao, nu faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips tutua amɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni okɛ nu awo mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛɔ fɔfɔi anɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can fit more plants on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks and small maize cobs. Giving plants enough space ensures each plant grows thick stems and full, heavy cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso náa tsitsi ni mli tse kɛ tsitsi ni tsii.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight and airflow to catch light and make food for the roots below. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows sunlight to reach every leaf while keeping the leaves away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la ni amɛfee niyenii amɛha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni akɛ tsei tsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baa fɛɛ baa he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye hela yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on the same land with my maize will help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has special roots that capture natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When maize grows nearby, it feeds on this extra nitrogen, making it greener and healthier naturally.
ga: Peanuts yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni eyɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ŋmãa kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ. Ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants crinkling up and rolling into tight curls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on tomatoes are usually a sign of a disease carried by tiny whiteflies that suck plant juices. Covering young nursery beds with protective nets or removing infected plants early prevents insects from spreading the virus to the rest of your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle tomato he lɛ ji hela ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tsei amli nu lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Kɛ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ aha tsei akwɛmɔhe saatso lɛ nɔ loo ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi kooloo lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ hela lɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Why does the top of my soil turn into a hard crust that splits open when the hot sun shines after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni fãa kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tso beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil gets hard and cracks when it lacks organic matter like dry leaves or manure, and is left completely uncovered in direct heat. Spreading a layer of dry grass or leaves over the soil keeps the ground soft, cool, and able to absorb future rainfall easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egbi loo ŋmeii bɛ mli. ni ashi lɛ ni ekɛ ehe wooo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo, ni edɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ wɔsɛɛ lɛ oya.

english: Why shouldn't I scatter my granular fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ granular fertilizer shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away down the slopes or deep into the soil below where roots cannot reach it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist after a soft rain, so the plant roots can drink it up immediately.
