ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa gɔŋji lɛ amli loo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when I plant them in an open, clear field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse, ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young plants until they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe la babaoo.

english: How far apart should I space my cocoa trees when planting them on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mafo kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Cocoa trees are usually planted about 3 meters by 3 meters apart. Proper spacing ensures that each tree gets enough soil nutrients, sunlight, and root space without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ kookoo tsei aaafee mitai 3 kɛ mitai 3 kɛjɛ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, hulu la kɛ shishifãi ahe ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa tree when it looks healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo niji komɛi amli be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, extra, or diseased branches to allow air and light to circulate through the tree. This helps prevent diseases, controls pests, and encourages the tree to direct its energy into growing pods rather than just leaves.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni fe nine loo hela Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ anaa ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli moŋ fe baai kɛkɛ.

english: Can I grow cassava together on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ he kome ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava is a heavy feeder that competes aggressively for soil water and nutrients, which can stunt the growth of young cocoa trees. It is better to use plantains or cocoyams, which provide gentle shade without stealing as many nutrients.
ga: Cassava ji niyenii ni tsii ni kɛ shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ waa. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ naa Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ plantain loo kookoo ni haa hulutsoo blɛoo ni ojuuu niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo baatsu nii.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads quickly during cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods from the tree and clearing weeds around the base helps keep the farm dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛfee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if they are not pollinated by tiny insects, or if the tree is under stress from dry weather, insect attacks like mirids, or a lack of nutrients in the soil.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ haomɔ mli kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ pollen tutuaa lɛ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer to help my crops grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops have slow growth, pale or yellowish leaves, or produce small and light fruit, it usually means the soil has run out of essential nutrients and needs fertilizer or compost to replenish it.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa blɛoo Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even when there is enough rain for everything to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshinii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the vital soil nutrients, fertilizer, and root space meant for your plants, while also acting as hiding spots for harmful farm pests.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛha otsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii akɛ he ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ teɔ shi amɛwoɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural way of protecting itself during hot, dry weather to reduce water loss from its leaves and prevent the crop from drying out completely.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Enɛ ji koni nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ aba shi, ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi kwraa.

english: Why is it bad to leave mature cocoa pods on the tree after they turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaashi kookoo ŋmeii ni edara lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ beni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long can cause the seeds inside to sprout, lower the quality of the beans, and attract rodents or diseases that can ruin the harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃. Bean lɛ mlihilɛ eba shi. ni egbalaa ŋmeii loo helai ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do cocoa trees manage to survive when the dry season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni cacao tsei ahi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ mli?

english: Cocoa trees adapt to dry periods by slowing down their growth and dropping some leaves. This reduces water loss and helps the main stem and root system stay alive until the rains return.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ hulutsoo be mli kɛtsɔ amɛdalɛ ni amɛhaa amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and fall off during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the soil loses moisture, plants shed their leaves to stop water from evaporating through them. It is a natural self-defense mechanism to keep the plant alive during drought.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ foɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni nu lɛ akatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why does my farm produce far fewer cocoa pods during dry spells compared to the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi fioo kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: Dry weather stresses the tree, forcing it to focus its limited water on staying alive rather than growing fruits. As a result, the tree drops small pods and produces a smaller harvest.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ. Enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛha nu fioo ni amɛyɔɔ kɛha wala lɛ afee nɔ ni he hiaa fe aduawai ni amɛduɔ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni ewoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How can I keep my young crops from drying out and dying during the intense heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi midumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: You can shade young plants with fast-growing crops like plantains and cover the ground around their roots with dry leaves or straw (mulch) to keep the soil cool and retain moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains lɛ awo tsei bibii ahe, ni okɛha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shishifã ni baai ni egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli. (Mulch) koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my cocoa trees help them during dry months?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi-cacao ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry leaves creates a protective layer called mulch. It blocks the direct sun from heating the soil, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the plant roots cool.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: What happens to my cocoa trees if heavy rain suddenly falls after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛfite trukaa? Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ sɛɛ?

english: A sudden rush of rain after drought causes trees to absorb water rapidly, which often triggers fresh flowering and new leaf growth, though rapid expansion can sometimes split developing pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa tsei gbalaa nu oya. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa anáa fɔfɔi heei kɛ baai heei. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei komɛi lɛ, oyaiyeli ni yaa hiɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha pods ni miiya hiɛ lɛ mli agbala moŋ.

english: How does delayed rainfall affect the time my cocoa trees start flowering?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ saa mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cocoa trees rely on rainfall to trigger the flowering process. When rains are late, flowering is delayed, which shifts your entire harvest period later into the year.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ ahe hewalɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Enɛ baatsake okpamɔ be lɛ fɛɛ kɛyashi afi lɛ naagbee gbɛ.

english: Why do cocoa trees flower heavily right after the first major rains break the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The return of rain signals to the tree that there is finally enough water available to nourish growing pods, prompting it to produce flowers to start the reproduction cycle.
ga: Nugbɔ kroko ni nɛɔ lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ akɛ naagbee lɛ, nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii yɛ. Wo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ebɔi fɔfɔi feemɔ koni eje fɔmɔ be lɛ shishi.

english: Why do many of my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into pods during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If the weather is too hot or dry, the tree drops excess flowers because it knows it does not have enough water to support all of them into full pods.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tso lɛ baashɛrɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ ashwie ejaakɛ ele akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ bɛ.

english: Is it safe to plant my crop seeds right after the very first rain of the season falls?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky because the first rain is often followed by a short dry gap. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady so the tender new roots do not dry up in the soil.
ga: Oshara yɛ he ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akagbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with direct sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot withstand direct sunlight. They need partial shade—often provided by temporary crops like plantains—to protect them from scorching heat and retain moisture in the soil until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fioo. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ jɛɔ tsei ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, tamɔ plantains lɛ amli, koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them and look like someone sprinkled brown dust inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ efɔ baai lɛ anɔ?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars chew through young leaves and leave behind waste that looks like fine sawdust. Catching this early is important so you can apply the recommended bio-pesticide or spray before the pest destroys the growing center of the plant.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ shwieɔ baai bibii ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛsɛɛ. Ehe miihia ni omɔ lɛ mra No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ atsu nii dani kooloi lɛ akpãtã he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ hiɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in the shape of a 'V' while the top leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing starting from the tips of lower leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen, a key food plantains and maize need to stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the crop regain its rich green color and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni plantains kɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa su eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Why does burning my farm to clear weeds make my crop yields drop after two or three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ lɛ ni mishãa koni mikɛgbe jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic leaf litter and beneficial tiny organisms in the topsoil that naturally feed your crops. Over time, fire leaves the soil hard, dry, and poor, making it harder for plant roots to find nutrients and hold water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ baai amli jwɛi kɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. Ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ, ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii haa onibii lɛ. Beni be hoɔ lɛ La haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa, ni egbiɔ ni ehiii kwraa, ni ehaa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaana niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛhiɛ nu mli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant uses most and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ baaha sũ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii fe fɛɛ lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but only produce small, skinny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii Eshishigbɛ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded too closely together, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of storing food in the roots. Proper plant spacing and balanced soil nutrients encourage bigger tuber growth.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulbs lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flower drop usually happens when the plant experiences stress, such as extremely high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients during flowering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch can help the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli Kɛ́ akɛ muji ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Watermelons crack when there is a sudden heavy intake of water after a dry spell. The inside of the fruit expands faster than the outer skin can stretch. Giving the crop consistent, even water prevents this sudden expansion.
ga: Watermelons tswaa kɛji nu ko ba trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛhaa daa Nu po tsiii nɛkɛ trukaa shweremɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: How do I keep my plantain trees from falling over during heavy rain and strong winds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi plantain tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, especially when bearing heavy bunches. Removing excess suckers so only two or three stalks remain per mat, along with propping up fruiting trees using sturdy bamboo or wooden poles, prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, titri lɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ni mli edɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ koni ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ ashwɛ yɛ mat kome nɔ, kɛ aduawai tsei ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ. Koni atsĩ shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ naa

english: How do I know if the very first rain of the season is enough for me to plant my seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛdu midumɔwui lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out fresh seeds. It is safer to wait until the soil stays moist for several days in a row or after two to three steady rains before sowing your seeds.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. No baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei agbi. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ loo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo komɛi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the tall trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji lɛ? Fɛɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains around them provides the shade and cool air young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii tamɔ adesai abifabii—amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ akwɛmɔ loo plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Tsei lɛ baaha hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ aha kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my crop plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the earth. It keeps the soil cool, holds water for the roots, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Too nu koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ aná hewalɛ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Leaves usually turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed to grow green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted poultry manure will help them turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: How do groundnut plants help make my soil richer for my next crop of maize?
ga: Te ŋmei tso baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha mi ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have tiny swellings on their roots that catch natural fertilizer from the air and put it into the dirt. When you leave the roots to rot after harvest, they feed the soil for your next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ohaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and turning small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny white insects that suck the plant's juices. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems from the agricultural office prevents this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their leaves and rot after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper roots need air to breathe, and sitting in flooded ground chokes them. Planting peppers on raised dirt mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Ni shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtaraa lɛ haa amɛmuɔ shwieɔ shi. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why does rice grow so well in muddy, standing water while my maize rots in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji mli shi ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special natural air tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen down from the leaves to roots underwater. Maize does not have these air tubes, so its roots quickly drown and rot in flooded soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baa shi kɛyaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Abɛi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei. Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwie shi oya ni amɛgboi yɛ sũ ni nu lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. If the vines crawl on the hot ground, leaves get shaded and diseased, resulting in tiny yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ niyenii. Kɛji wain tsei shwie shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni helai baamɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why is my plantain tree taking so long to grow a fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ aduawai akui lɛ?

english: When too many small shoots grow around the base of a plantain tree, they steal water and plant food from the main mother stem. Cutting off extra shoots leaves enough energy for the main stem to produce a big bunch faster.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ. Ejuɔ nu ni eduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ afee niji wuji oya.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the plant before any fruits grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or sudden changes in soil moisture. Giving your plants steady water at their base and partial shade during very hot afternoons keeps the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakemɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu daa kɛ hulutsoo be fioo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to start my cocoa seeds in a nursery instead of planting them directly on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔi kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very fragile and sensitive to strong sunlight, hot weather, and pests. A nursery provides shade, moisture, and protection so the plants can grow strong roots and healthy leaves before facing the rough conditions in the main field.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa waa, ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ kooloi ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ ahe waa. Greenhouses haa hulutsoo, fɛ̃i, kɛ hebuu bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni wa. dani ekɛ shihilɛi ni esaaa baakpe yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ

english: Why is it necessary for me to provide shade over my cocoa seedlings in the nursery?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo kookoo dumɔwui lɛ shade yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight can scorch young seedling leaves and dry out the soil quickly. Shade keeps the soil moist and creates a cool, humid environment that helps the young plants develop properly.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã dumɔwui lɛ baai bibii lɛ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Shade haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ haa tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa seedlings in the nursery are mature enough to be moved to the main field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ edara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu kɛya shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ?

english: Seedlings are ready for transplanting when they are about 4 to 6 months old, have reached about 30 to 40 centimeters in height, and have developed strong stems with several dark green, mature leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛye aaafee nyɔji 4 kɛyashi 6. Amɛkɛlɛ aaafee sɛntimitai 30 kɛyashi 40 ni amɛyɛ tsei ni wa. Eyɛ baai ni eda ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ babaoo.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa seedlings wither and die right after I transplant them from the nursery to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ekomɛi gboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ he ni akwɛɔ tsei lɛ yɛ lɛ kɛtee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This usually happens due to transplant shock, lack of water, direct exposure to strong sun, or damaged roots during moving. Planting during the steady rainy season and keeping shade around them helps young plants survive the move.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he gbeyeishemɔ, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ hewɔ. loo shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli daa ni ehaa hulutsoo be ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso bibioo lɛ ni ehiɔ shi.

english: What is the difference between planting short cocoa tree varieties and tall varieties on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei kukuji kɛ kakadaji ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Short (or dwarf hybrid) varieties grow low to the ground, begin bearing fruit earlier, and make harvesting easier without long poles. Tall traditional varieties take longer to yield fruit and grow higher, but they are often hardier and survive rough conditions well.
ga: Dwarf hybrid henɔi (loo dwarf hybrids) lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi oya ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo ni tsei kakadaji ahe ehiaaa Kusum mli tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛdaraa. Shi amɛfɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my small, young cocoa trees starting to bear fruit even though they look so short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni Mine lɛ miibɔi yibii womɔ eyɛ mli akɛ etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ kuku moŋ?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties are bred to mature fast and produce pods close to the ground at a young age, allowing farmers to harvest crops earlier without waiting for the tree to grow tall.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai krokomɛi koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi. Enɛ haa okwaafoi nyɛɔ amɛkpaa amɛnibii oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛmɛ ni tsei lɛ adara.

english: Which variety of cocoa should I choose if I want a quicker return on my investment?
ga: Mɛɛ kookoo esa akɛ mahala kɛji miitao ni maná shika ni mikɛwo mli lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo oya?

english: You should choose improved short hybrid varieties. They mature faster, yield pods within 2 to 3 years, and are easier to manage and harvest compared to traditional tall varieties.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ŋmeii sɔrɔtoi kukuji ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛ daa oya. Ewoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, ni ekɛ nitsumɔ kɛ ekpamɔ waaa kɛ akɛto blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahe.

english: How many years do I have to wait after planting before my cocoa trees start producing pods?
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii agbe naa lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani enyɛ ewo ŋmeii?

english: Improved hybrid varieties usually start producing pods in 2 to 3 years, while traditional cocoa varieties generally take about 4 to 5 years to give their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmeii feemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛklɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Once my cocoa trees start bearing fruit, how many years can I keep harvesting from them?
ga: Beni kookoo tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ Afii enyiɛ manyɛ maya nɔ makpa nii?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term crops that can produce pods for 25 to 30 years or more if you prune them regularly, control pests, and maintain soil fertility.
ga: Cacao tsei ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji ofoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe daa ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why is cocoa considered a long-term future investment compared to crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abuɔ kookoo akɛ eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ wɔsɛɛ be mli kɛ akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe lɛ?

english: Maize and vegetables give quick returns within months but must be replanted every season. Cocoa takes a few years to start producing, but once mature, it yields income every year for decades without needing to be replanted.
ga: Abɛi kɛ aduawai woɔ yibii oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Shi esa akɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ daa be. Cocoa heɔ afii fioo dani ebɔi feemɔ. Shi kɛ́ Cocoa eda kwraa lɛ, ebaaná sɛɛnamɔ daa afi afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants flower above the soil, but the peanuts grow underneath the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanuts lɛ miikwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmeii miikwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Groundnut plants produce yellow flowers above the soil, but once fertilized, the flower stems (called pegs) grow downward and push themselves into the dirt. The actual peanut pods develop and mature underground where it is dark and moist.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli lɛ, fɔfɔi tso ko (ni atsɛɔ lɛ peg) lɛ daa kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ ehe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Pod lɛ diɛŋtsɛ daa ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni ji shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to heap loose soil around the stems of my groundnut plants when they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mabua sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ naa kɛbɔle he lɛ? Mi-peanut tso lɛ shishifã lɛ beni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ

english: Moulding soft, loose soil around the base of the plant makes it easier for the flowering pegs to dig into the ground. If the ground is too hard, the pegs cannot penetrate, and the plant will produce far fewer peanut pods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etse ehe lɛ ni aaabɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ a-pin lɛ akɛ ebaafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Pins lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli. Ni tsei lɛ baajie ŋmeii fioo ko kwraa.

english: Why do groundnuts grow much better in loose, sandy soil than in heavy clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã nɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts need light, well-draining soil so the underground pegs can easily grow down and expand into pods. Clay soil gets too hard when dry, preventing pod growth, and retains too much water when wet, causing pods to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa tsɔ kɛ́ egbi. etsĩɔ pod lɛ dalɛ naa ni ehiɛɔ nu babaoo mli kɛji edɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji pod lɛ ni fiteɔ.

english: How does planting peanuts in my field help make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Peanuts are legumes, which means their roots work with friendly soil bacteria to pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the earth. This naturally fertilizes the soil, leaving rich nutrients for crops like maize planted next.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛgbala nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛto sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Amɛshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa ni yaa nɔ aduɔ lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I plant my peanut seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ŋmei dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When planted too close, peanut plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This leads to tall, weak stems with very few leaves and small pods underground, resulting in a lower overall harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu Peanut tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nikpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ ba shi.

english: Can I plant my groundnuts under the shade of big trees on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Groundnuts need direct, full sunlight for most of the day to make energy, bloom properly, and grow pods. Heavy shade from big trees causes the plants to stretch out long and thin without producing many nuts.
ga: Hulu la he miihia ŋmeii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei babaoo mli koni amɛná hewalɛ. Fɔfɔi ni sa kɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara He hulutsoo ni mli wa ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How does too much water during the rainy season affect my peanut crop underground?
ga: Te nu babaoo ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ saa mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excess water prevents air from reaching the roots and pods in the soil. This causes the leaves to turn yellow, roots to drown, and the pods underground to rot before they can mature.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my groundnut plants curling up and showing yellow patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow patterns and curled leaves are usually caused by Groundnut Rosette Virus, which is carried and spread by tiny green insects called aphids. Infected plants stay small and fail to produce full nut pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Groundnut Rosette Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ aphids Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ daraaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know that my groundnuts are fully matured and ready to pull out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-peanuts lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Groundnuts are ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, and when you open a few pods, the inside of the shell wall has turned dark brown or black instead of white.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni kɛ́ ogbele pods komɛi lɛ, ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli gbogbo lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting groundnut seeds that have cracked skins or mold on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmei dumɔwui ni ŋmeii egbɛ eshwa loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ dumɔ he?

english: Damaged or moldy seeds often fail to germinate, and they can carry soil-borne fungal diseases like aflatoxin that kill young seedlings early and spoil the entire farm yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni efite loo etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃. Ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhiɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli tamɔ aflatoxin ni gbeɔ tsei bibii mra lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for green growth, or that heavy rain has logged the soil, preventing the roots from absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress, as extreme heat prevents the flower from pollinating properly.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with many leaves but gives me small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɔ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyitso ji bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing green leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions where air cannot flow freely through the farm.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli oya lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas absorb nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps feed the neighboring maize crop.
ga: Cowpeas shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stick cuttings at an angle instead of straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi yucca tsei lɛ aniji lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mafee nɔ ni ja?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant gives the stem more underground surface area, allowing roots to spread out easily and produce more tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ shishigbɛ aná he ko babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo ni ehaa bulbs babaoo.

english: Why do armyworms destroy my maize leaves mostly at night and early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-abele baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hide deep inside the plant stem or soil during the hot daylight hours to protect themselves, coming out to feed only when temperatures cool down.
ga: Fall armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe he. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛyatao niyenii pɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck sap from the leaves and spread plant viruses that stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ amɛdalɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting in the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: When water settles around yam roots without proper drainage, it starves the roots of air and allows soil fungus and bacteria to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kɛ nu lɛ ŋmɛ Sweet potato shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. ni eha ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the essential nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding organic compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color and boosts plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ekoŋŋ ni ehaa tsei lɛ daraa babaoo.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize on the same field continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas restores nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete against each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and very small corn cobs.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to the local soil, so they absorb water and nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops the head start they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ afee klalo kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains cause water to pool on flat ground, it smothers the roots and promotes fungal rot; planting on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crop roots with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dried plant material, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool under hot sunshine, prevents soil moisture from evaporating quickly, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to fully establish before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ agbe naa dani madu dumɔwui?

english: Planting after only one light rain is risky because a brief dry spell can follow, drying out the topsoil and killing young germinating seeds before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo sɛɛ Be kome pɛ ji oshara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, be kukuoo ko ni baanyɛ agbi lɛ baanyɛ aba, ni no baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upward and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by sudden high temperatures or irregular watering. When the plant feels extreme heat or drought, it sacrifices its flowers to preserve its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ tsei nu latsaa loo hɔmɔ ni naa wa he lɛ Ekɛ fɔfɔi baashã afɔle koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala he.

english: How does storing my dried maize in sealed airtight bags protect it from insects?
ga: Te mi-ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ni mikɛtoɔ kotoku ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ mli lɛ baaha kooloi akabote mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects like maize weevils need oxygen to live and reproduce. Storing properly dried maize in airtight triple-layer bags suffocates existing pests and stops new ones from entering without needing chemical dusts.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ bii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ to vacuum bag ni yɔɔ ŋtayaai etɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ momo lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaatsi ŋmãa heei anaa koni amɛkabote mli ni akɛ tsofa ni ji sũ tsuuu nii.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to feed well and produce big, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii kpakpa kɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young maize crops turn pale yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the soil back its strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the weeds and dry leaves on my land before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashãa jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani aduɔ ŋmei?

english: Burning destroys the natural food in the soil and kills good organisms that keep land healthy. Clearing without burning allows the dry leaves to rot into compost, which holds moisture and feeds your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa baai ni egboi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni amɛhaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the funnel leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai ni tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ anɔ?

english: Holes in the center leaves of young maize are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the shoot. Checking the plants early allows you to treat them before the insects destroy the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsa amɛ dani kooloi bibii afite amɛyitsei ni miida lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding on the leaf juices. Controlling these small insects early prevents leaf damage and stops viruses from spreading.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni akafite baai lɛ ni ekpa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when we get too much rain near harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo ni ebɛŋkɛ nikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, the tubers suffocate and rot from fungal diseases.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ŋmɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Tubers lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaafite kɛjɛ fungal hela mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents the flowers from pollinating properly, causing them to dry up and fall off. Giving them steady water and light shade during hot peaks helps protect the blooms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa ni oooha amɛ hulutsoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my cowpea crop produce plenty of green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cowpeas to put all their energy into making thick leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen naturally, so they need balanced nutrients to focus on fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa baai ni mli tse yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni eye niyenii ni ja koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama yibiiwoo nɔ.

english: Why do some of my yam tubers grow twisted and strange shapes instead of smooth and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers lɛ yɛ naakpɛɛ ni efite lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ja?

english: Yam tubers twist when they hit hard, compacted soil or stones underground as they expand. Tilling the soil deep and making soft, raised mounds allows the yams to grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ shishi tɛi beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ kɛ gɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni sweet potatoes lɛ daa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: If I put double the amount of chemical fertilizer on my maize, will it grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo mli lɛ toi enyɔ lɛ, ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, crops have natural limits to how much plant food they can absorb at once. Applying too much fertilizer burns the roots, stresses the crop, and damages the soil structure, similar to how taking too much medicine harms the human body.
ga: Dabi, tsei yɛ adebɔɔ mli husu ko yɛ bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ. haoɔ tso lɛ ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii Taakɛ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii babaoo lɛ ji lɛ, eyeɔ adesa gbɔmɔtso lɛ awui.

english: Why do the branches on my tomato plants snap and fall to the ground when they carry many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shikpɔŋ be mli ni aduawai babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: A tomato stem can only support a limited weight before it bends or breaks. Using wooden stakes or strings to support the main branches helps the plant hold heavy fruits without breaking under its own weight.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ ahiɛ muji fioo ko pɛ mli dani amɛkoto loo amɛkumɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo kpãai fĩ tso lɛ niji titrii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ aduawai ni tsii ni efoŋ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ etsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very thin and tall without big cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwiili ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, they compete for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil food. Overcrowding strains the plants so none of them get enough strength to produce thick stalks or large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abua amɛhe naa lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo tsei bibii loo tsei wuji.

english: Why does my farm produce smaller crop yields after planting on the same piece of land every year without rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni miduɔ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when crops draw out its natural nutrients season after season. Allowing the land to rest or rotating crops like groundnuts and beans gives the soil time to rebuild its natural strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be mli ni tsei lɛ gbalaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ bei lɛ amli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe loo etsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná be ni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow and burn after I spray chemical weedkiller close to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Chemical weedkillers are strong medicines meant for unwanted weeds, but crops absorb them too. Using high chemical doses or spraying too close stresses the cassava plant and damages its green leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ji tsofai ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa jwɛi ni ataooo. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu baanyɛ aŋɔ. Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni efite baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off the plants during very hot and dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ yɛ otsi ni mli edɔ ni nu bɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil put crops under severe stress. To survive and conserve water, the plant voluntarily drops its flowers because it does not have enough strength or water to feed growing pods.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ haomɔ ni naa wa mli. Bɔni afee ni ehi shi ni ekɛ nu ato he lɛ Tso lɛ baajɛ etsuiŋ ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi ejaakɛ ebɛ hewalɛ loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaaye ebua ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off excess branches from my cocoa tree when more branches look like they could bear more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine yɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ? Akɛni etamɔ nɔ ni tsei niji babaoo baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii babaoo hewɔ lɛ.

english: Carrying too many heavy branches wastes the tree's internal strength and blocks sunlight. Pruning removes useless growth so the tree can direct its energy into growing large, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ niji lɛ wo nibii ni tsii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha emli hewalɛ afite ni eha hulu la lɛ akabote mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ̃ kookoo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots reach a peak age where they hold optimum starch. If left unharvested too long, the plant exhausts its stored energy during dry seasons, making the tubers tough and low quality.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ yɛ wala be ni nɔ kwɔ fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkɛ starch ato jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni akpaaa lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither and die when I pour too much water on them every morning and evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛ nu wo nɔ fe nine daa leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air in the soil to breathe just like humans need air. Excess water drowns the root system and causes root rot, which makes the plant wilt even though the ground is wet.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa tsei shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa adesai lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha amɛgboi. Enɛ haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on cocoa trees that live under heavy forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli tsei ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy shade keeps cocoa trees wet and cool for too long after rain. Over-shaded environments create ideal conditions for fungi to grow, overwhelming the natural defenses of the cocoa tree.
ga: Shade ni mli wa haa cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛhe jɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Shihilɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii adalɛ. ni yeɔ cacao tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ ehe lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the root area will help the plants grow strong and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni bɔleɔ he lɛ tsuɔ nii Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni edaraa waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender roots and leaves that burn quickly under intense sunlight and hot, dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them acts as a living umbrella to protect the young cocoa until it is strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Does it matter which way I plant cassava stem cuttings in the ground?
ga: Ani bɔ ni mikɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mihaa lɛ he hiaa mi?

english: Yes, you must always plant the stem cutting with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stems upside down forces the new roots and shoots to fight against gravity, resulting in weak growth and very poor tuber yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ odu tsei ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ yitso lɛ shishi lɛ, enyɛɔ shishifãi lɛ kɛ ŋmeii heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛwu amɛshi hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tuber yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa baa.

english: Yam leaves need maximum sunshine to produce the energy required to swell the subterranean tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread and spreads them out to catch more sunlight.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ egbɛ eshwa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa koni hulu la babaoo aba amɛnɔ.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant lacks nutrients. Ensuring steady moisture and protecting the soil with mulch helps keep the flowers healthy so they can form tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ Nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũuɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔmɔ tomato.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil as natural plant food. Planting them with maize feeds the soil for free, helps the maize grow better, and gives you two crops to harvest from one field.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Abele ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Can I just plant the maize grains I harvested last season as my seeds for this year?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ akɛ dumɔwui kɛha afi nɛɛ?

english: Using saved grains, especially hybrid varieties, leads to weaker plants and smaller yields in the next harvest. Buying fresh, certified seeds ensures that your crops grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and yield much more grain.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Titri lɛ, nibii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ baaha onibii lɛ ada daa. helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmaa babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and stunted even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your main crops. Even with abundant rain, if weeds remain in the farm, your crops will stay hungry because the weeds absorb the soil nutrients first.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otsei titrii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Kɛji jwɛi tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakã he ahi hɔmɔ ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my crop seeds after the long dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist after two or three strong rains, rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting too early on a light rain can cause seeds to sprout and dry up if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's juices, or by viruses they carry. Spraying a simple organic neem oil mixture early on controls these pests and keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ mli A ni akɛ organic neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii amli lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the bottom going up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves its remaining nutrients to the newest leaves at the top to stay alive.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ baajie niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, causing the plant to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Ha tsei agbo koni akɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry periods to save water. The plant is not dying; it reduces leaf cover to protect its tubers and will sprout fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Tsei lɛ gbooo, ni no haa baai ni akɛhaa amɛhe lɛ baa shi koni ebu ŋmeii lɛ ahe, ni baai heei baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on leaf sap, which can also spread leaf curl viruses. Controlling these pests early helps stop the leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ leaf curl hela lɛ hu ashwã. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaye ebua ni akpa baa lɛ fitemɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves compete heavily for the same water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This lack of resources leads to weaker plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tse lɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni bɛ nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains beside them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast with broad leaves, creating living shade that lowers temperatures and keeps the soil moist for young cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛhaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do tall weeds make my crops grow thin and weak instead of bushy and strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa miŋmɔshinii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa lɛ?

english: When weeds block sunlight, crops stretch rapidly upward to reach light instead of developing thick, sturdy stems. This leaves the plant tall, slender, and prone to falling over easily.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi tsi hulu la lɛ naa lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baajie amɛhe oya kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛha la lɛ abote mli. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ tsohi nɛ a mi wa nɛ a he wa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbee shi oya.

english: Why do my crops grow weaker every season if I plant maize on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like beans restores nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mi-ŋma lɛ mli?

english: Maize needs fertilizer early when it is knee-high (about 3 to 4 weeks after planting) to build strong roots and stems, and again just before flowering when it begins forming the cobs.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ shishijee beni eshɛɔ etsitsi nɔ (aaafee otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ) koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa aba. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu dani ewo fɔfɔi beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting shoots while stored in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ beni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go through a resting period after harvest, but warm temperatures and humidity signal to the yam that it is time to break dormancy and sprout new vines.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ be ni amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ tsɔɔ sweet potatoes akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛfo ŋmɛlɛtswaa ni amɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ wain tsei heei.

english: Why do my crops die when rainwater sits on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboiɔ beni nugbɔ nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water stays in one place without flowing away, it fills all the air spaces in the soil and starves the roots of oxygen, causing them to rot and die.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Beni nu hiɔ he kome ni ejeee kpo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli eyiɔ, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ náa lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Can I grow food on a piece of land that turns into a swamp during the wet season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Most regular crops like maize and cassava will drown in swampy soil, but crops like swamp rice, sugarcane, and cocoyam (kontomire) thrive in flooded or constantly wet ground.
ga: Nibii ni afɔɔ namɔ babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa Akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ mli, shi ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ kookoo (contomire) kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu shwieɔ shi loo nu shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ.

english: Why does water collect in some parts of my farm while other parts dry up very quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ oya waa lɛ?

english: Water gathers in low-lying spots or areas where the soil has a lot of heavy clay that traps water. Higher spots let the water flow downhill and dry out faster under the sun.
ga: Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa nɔ loo hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ babaoo ni hiɛɔ nu yɔɔ lɛ. He ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa gɔŋ lɛ shishi ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: How can I prevent standing water from drowning my crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nu ni ekã shi lɛ naa koni ekafo miŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: You can dig shallow drainage channels across your field to guide standing water away, or plant your crops on raised soil ridges so their roots stay above the water level.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko. ŋmɔji lɛ amli koni ejie nu ni ekã shi lɛ Aloo adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ashɛ nu lɛ he.

english: Why do many farmers make soil mounds before planting cassava and yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei?

english: Mounds lift the crops above wet, soggy ground so the roots don't rot, and they give the soil a soft, deep structure that makes it easier for tubers to grow big.
ga: Gɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛyaa hei ni efɔ, ni efɔ lɛ anɔ koni shishifãi lɛ akafite. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli kwɔ ni haa bulbs lɛ baakwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops on flat ground or on raised soil ridges?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ?

english: If your farm gets flooded easily, raised ridges keep roots dry and safe. If your land is dry and water drains away quickly, planting on flat ground helps the soil retain the little water it gets.
ga: Kɛji nu shwieɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya Gbɛjegbɛi ni awó nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi shweshweeshwe. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya lɛ Dumɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu fioo pɛ.

english: Will planting on raised soil mounds help my crops if my farm is in a very dry area?
ga: Ani dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ waa?

english: No, raised mounds lose water faster than flat ground. In dry areas, mounds can cause your soil to dry out too quickly, making your crops suffer during hot weather.
ga: Dabi, gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ hei ni egbi lɛ Gɔji baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii naa amanehulu yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow when the soil stays muddy for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo muji be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Muddy, waterlogged soil prevents roots from taking up important nutrients like nitrogen from the dirt, which causes the leaves to lose their green color and turn yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa baai lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know if a piece of land will flood before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaho dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Look at the land before the rainy season; low-lying areas, spots with dark sticky clay, or places where water-loving weeds grow are strong signs that the land will flood.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwɛmɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ Loo hei ni jwɛi ni sumɔɔ nu lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baaho.

english: Why do crops planted on high ground dry out faster than crops at the bottom of a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni kwɔ waa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ gɔji ashishi lɛ?

english: Water naturally flows down from high places to low places because of gravity, leaving the soil on high ground dry much faster than the soil at the bottom of a hill.
ga: Nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ kɛyaa hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya kwraa fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing in maize leaves that starts at the tip and moves down the middle usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the green color and supports healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant cowpea together with maize in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea is a legume crop that pulls nitrogen gas from the air and puts it into the soil. Planting it alongside maize helps feed the soil naturally, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first two years.
