ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground exposes them to more sun, helping the plant make more food and build bigger yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ owó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ niyenii babaoo. ni amɛfee yam ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because they cannot breathe without air in the soil spaces. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away and keeps the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why should I pare the bottom outer skin of a plantain sucker before planting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi plantain suckers lɛ ashishi dani madu?

english: Trimming the old root base and outer skin removes hidden banana weevil eggs and microscopic worms. It cleans the plantain sucker so it can grow fresh, healthy new roots without pest damage.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo shishifã momo lɛ shishi kɛ hewolo lɛ kponɔgbɛ lɛ, ebaajie banana ŋmei ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etsumɔ plantain suckers lɛ ahe koni amɛkwɛ shishifãi heei, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ehee ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry conditions. Applying dry grass or mulch around the base of the plant keeps the roots cool and moist so the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi. Kɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium uptake when water supply in the soil goes up and down too quickly. Keeping soil moisture steady with regular, light watering helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he beni nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa ŋwɛi ni ebaa shi oya tsɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nu fioo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ajie calcium kɛya aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning dry even when I water the bed daily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ saatsoi lɛ anɔ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato leaf curling is frequently caused by heat stress or microscopic sucking pests like whiteflies that transmit leaf curl virus. Providing partial shade during the hottest hours and spraying neem oil water helps control the insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ leaf curl virus lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. He ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ fã ko kɛ neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akudɔɔ kooloi bibii.

english: How does spreading dry dry grass over my soil protect my vegetable garden in hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass—known as mulching—acts as a protective coat over the soil. It blocks direct sunlight from drying out soil moisture, keeps root temperature cool, and slowly breaks down into natural soil food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwaa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Etsiɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi. Ehaa shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi fiofio ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: This usually means the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for crop growth. When nitrogen is low, the maize plant moves the remaining nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top leaves, causing the lower ones to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛji nitrogen faaa Abɛi tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut leaves develop dark spots and fall off before the nuts are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: This is caused by a fungal leaf spot disease that thrives in humid weather. The fungus damages the leaf surface, preventing the plant from producing enough food to fill out the pods underground.
ga: Fungal leaf spot hela ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungus fiteɔ baa lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. Extreme heat prevents proper pollination, so the plant sheds the unpollinated blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and stop growing big peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa pepper agboi lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from tender leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Damaged leaves cannot make enough food for the plant to grow large fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Baai ni efite lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha aduawai wuji akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are getting burned by the sun?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ etsɔ hulutsoo be mli?

english: If young cocoa leaves turn brown and dry at the edges, look bleached, or curl downwards, they are getting too much direct sunlight. Young cocoa trees require shade from taller plants like plantains to protect their tender leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ amɛnaagbɛ lɛ Etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ futafuta loo ebɔle shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves higher toward sunlight. Staking keeps the foliage off the damp soil, reducing disease risk and allowing the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to build big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ he. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. ni ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛfee bulb agbo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot if I leave them in wet soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay healthy. Excess standing water fills the soil's air pockets, suffocating the roots and creating ideal conditions for soil rot fungi to attack.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atutua.

english: Why do my seeds fail to sprout when I plant them in warm, dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds require moisture to trigger the germination process inside. Without moisture in the soil, the seed remains dormant or can be heat-damaged before it gets the chance to sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni ekanya amɛmli kwɛ̃mɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Aloo dɔlɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ dani amɛná hegbɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over easily once the bunch of bananas becomes large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be mli ni banana ŋmeii wuji yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the top of the soil rather than deep taproots. As the fruit bunch grows heavier, the plant becomes top-heavy and can easily pull its shallow roots out of the ground if not supported.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu lɛ mli wa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee tsiimɔ ni ebaanyɛ egbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ oooshi shikpɔŋ kɛji akɛ afiii sɛɛ

english: Why do insects attack my cabbage leaves much more during the dry season than in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa cabbage baai yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Warm, dry weather speeds up the lifecycle of many insects, causing them to reproduce faster. Additionally, as wild bushes dry up, pests move directly into watered farm fields where green crops are available.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa kooloi bibii babaoo ashihilɛ yaa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfɔɔ oya. Kɛfata he lɛ, kɛ́ koo lɛ mli tsei lɛ egbi lɛ, Pests yaa ŋmɔji ni nu yɔɔ mli ni tsei eŋɔli yɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why can't I plant my maize on the exact same calendar date every year like my father used to do?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ kalanda kome nɔ daa afi tamɔ Ataa lɛ?

english: Weather patterns naturally change from year to year, meaning the rainy season does not start on a fixed calendar date. Planting should be guided by actual rain onset and weather forecasts for that specific year rather than a set date on the calendar.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ afi kɛyaa afi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ ejeee shishi yɛ kalanda lɛ nɔ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. Esa akɛ dumɔ adamɔ nugbɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni eje shishi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni awie yɛ nakai afi lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Yɛ gbi pɔtɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ kalanda lɛ nɔ lɛ najiaŋ

english: Why did my cassava perform so well last year, but this year the exact same field is struggling to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli, shi afi nɛɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔji nɛɛ nɔŋŋ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Rainfall amounts and temperatures vary from season to season. Even on the same land, shifting seasonal weather means one year might provide ideal rain while the next year brings dry spells that slow crop growth.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ latsaa yɛ srɔtoi yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Yɛ he kome po lɛ, be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afi baanyɛ afee afi ni nugbɔ anɔ yɛ gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, afi ni baa lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be baaba ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ blɛoo.

english: How will I know when it is safe to start planting my seeds if the start of the rainy season keeps changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ? Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee tsakeɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ

english: Rather than guessing, wait until the soil has received at least two steady, deep rains and check seasonal weather forecasts from extension agents to confirm that the real rainy season has started.
ga: yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooosusu he Mɛɛ kɛyashi kɛ hoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ ni yaa nɔ daa. Ni okwɛ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he akɔntaabuu kɛjɛ ohiɛyaa najiaŋdamɔlɔ lɛ dɛŋ koni oma nɔ mi akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eje shishi.

english: What will happen to my seeds if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni baaba midumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: The first rain of the year is often a 'false start' followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. Seeds planted too early will germinate and then dry up and die because the soil lacks long-term moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ ji ‘Apasa shishijee’ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, otsii babaoo ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers when the rain unexpectedly stops for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When rain stops mid-season, plants suffer from moisture stress. Tomatoes drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save water and survival energy until reliable moisture returns.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ kpa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he haomɔ baakpe. Tomato duɔ fɔfɔi akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni wala ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my groundnut crop take longer to mature in some years compared to others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshwereɔ afii komɛi fe ekrokomɛi lɛ?

english: Crops grow based on the weather conditions of that specific season. Cooler temperatures or reduced sunlight and water slow down plant development, stretching out the time it takes to reach harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ anaa. He ni mli ejɔ loo hulu la kɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ adalɛ yaa hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa be ni he hiaa kɛha nikpamɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What should I do if the weather office reports that the rainy season will be shorter than usual this year?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ nitsumɔhe ni kwɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ lɛ bɔ amaniɛ akɛ afi nɛɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ baafee kuku fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ hu?

english: When a short rainy season is expected, switch to fast-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties so your crops can fully mature before the rains end early.
ga: Beni akpaa nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ gbɛ Moŋ lɛ, tsakemɔ kɛya tsei srɔtoi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba naagbee oya.

english: Why do my crops give a smaller harvest in some years even though I apply the exact same amount of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii yɛ afii komɛi amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ woɔ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need consistent soil moisture to dissolve and feed the crop. If seasonal rain is poorly distributed, the plants cannot absorb the nutrients properly, leading to lower yields despite your effort.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii. Kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be mli lɛ mlijaa lɛ ehiii lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii kpakpai jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni obɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my young cocoa seedlings when dry spells happen unexpectedly during the rainy period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni akpaaa gbɛ ba yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the soil around the base of your seedlings with dry leaves or grass (mulching) keeps the soil moist and cool during unpredictable dry gaps in the season.
ga: Ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ.

english: Why should I listen to seasonal weather updates instead of relying on traditional rain signs in my village?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni kɔɔ be mli lɛ atoi moŋ fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ blema nugbɔshiimɔ he okadii anɔ lɛ? yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli

english: Changing climate patterns make traditional signs less reliable today. Seasonal weather forecasts use modern climate data to predict overall rainfall trends months ahead, helping you plan better.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi gbalaa blema okadii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ Beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe adafitswaa kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ bɔ ni nugbɔ baanɛ yɛ nyɔŋ ni baa lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Can cocoa actually grow and produce well in every region of Ghana, even up North?
ga: Abaanyɛ adu kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ. Yɛ kooyigbɛ po?

english: Cocoa prefers warm, humid forest climates with consistent rainfall. While traditionally grown in heavy rainfall zones like the Western North, newer drought-tolerant cocoa varieties and shaded farming methods allow small patches to survive in drier northern areas, though adequate water supply remains a major requirement.
ga: Cocoa sumɔɔ koo mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli edɔɔ, ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Eyɛ mli akɛ blema beaŋ lɛ, aduɔ kookoo yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ, tamɔ yɛ kooyi-anaigbɛ moŋ, shi kookoo henɔi heei ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔji bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpaa ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ji taomɔ nii titri lolo moŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees yellow and scorch after I spray farm chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai efɔ amɛnɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Scorched leaves usually mean chemical burn caused by using the wrong mix ratio, applying unapproved agrochemicals, or spraying during intense afternoon heat. Chemicals should always be applied at recommended doses during cool morning or late afternoon hours.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shã lɛ tsɔɔ tsofa ni shãa ni jɛɔ futumɔ ni ejaaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ mli baa. Okwaayeli tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Esa akɛ akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ atsu nii be fɛɛ be yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli loo shwane mli.

english: Will using continuous chemical weedicides spoil my farmland for future crops?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ baaye miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ awui kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Overusing harsh, non-selective chemical weedicides destroys beneficial soil microbes and damages delicate surface feeder roots. Over time, this hardens the soil and lowers fertility. Mixing manual weeding with selective, approved weedicides protects the long-term health of your land.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni halaaa jwɛi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ kpataa sũ mli nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahiɛ, ni efiteɔ shishifãi ni yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. Beni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli awa ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ okɛ niji shwie jwɛi lɛ kɛ tsofai ni ahala ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛnamɔ he be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does cocoa seem to produce far more pods in the Western North than in other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni afeɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ Kooyi-anaigbɛ fe kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: The Western North region naturally has deep, rich forest soils with high organic matter and high annual rainfall. Farmers in other regions can boost their yields by adding organic compost, maintaining proper tree shade, and using water conservation practices.
ga: Kooyigbɛ anaigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ koo shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni eji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni baa nii. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa afi babaoo. Okwaafoi ni yɔɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ Abaanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Kwɛmɔ hulutsoo ni sa kɛjɛ tsei ahe. ni amɛkɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ nu he lɛ atsu nii

english: How do I know when my old cocoa trees have finished their productive life and need replacement?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cacao tso momo lɛ eshɛ ewala be lɛ naagbee ni ehe miihia ni atsake lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years, pod size shrinks, disease susceptibility increases, and overall yields drop permanently despite feeding and spraying. This indicates the farm 'lifecycle' has ended and requires phased replanting with new hybrid seedlings.
ga: Kɛ́ cacao tsei lɛ eye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ dalɛ baa shi. Helai ni baa mɔ nɔ oya lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni nibii fɛɛ ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛya naanɔ kɛtsɔ niyenii kɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ po nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ ‘wala shihilɛ’ lɛ eba naagbee. Ni yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ ehe miihia ni adu dumɔwui heei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he.

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival reaction to conserve moisture during dry spells. You can protect your farm by planting permanent shade trees like Terminalia and applying organic mulch around the bases of trees to trap moisture in the soil.
ga: Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni wala feɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa, tamɔ Terminalia ni ooodu lɛ nɔ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ni okɛbaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do young green cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal attack triggered by excessive humidity, dense shade, and poor airflow. Pruning unnecessary branches, clearing weeds to let sunlight in, and applying recommended fungicides early in the rainy season prevents this loss.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛbaa. Shade ni mli ewo muji kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eyaaa jogbaŋŋ ni afoɔ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ koni hulu la abote mli Ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ.

english: My cocoa tree has thousands of flowers, so why do almost all of them fall off without producing pods?
ga: Mikoo tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can feed, and only 1 to 5 percent become mature pods due to limited natural pollinators (midges) or plant stress. Protecting beneficial shade and avoiding harsh broad-spectrum insect spraying during peak flowering helps pollinators do their work.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua, ni oha mlijaa 1 kɛyashi 5 pɛ baatsɔ fɔfɔi ni eda pɛŋ yɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔii (teŋgbɛ nibii) loo tsei lɛ ahe haomɔ ni faaa lɛ hewɔ. He ni abuɔ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ he kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi lɛ yaa hiɛ waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa pollinators lɛ ni amɛtsuɔ amɛnitsumɔ lɛ.

english: How long must I wait after spraying my farm before it is safe to harvest cocoa pods?
ga: Kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Every chemical has a mandatory 'pre-harvest interval' (PHI), typically between 2 to 4 weeks depending on the product. Waiting for this full period ensures chemical residues break down completely, keeping your beans safe for buyers and consumers.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi fɛɛ yɛ ‘be ni esa akɛ akpa’ (PHI) ni esa akɛ afee lɛ heɔ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi ejwɛ teŋ, ni enɛ damɔ nibii ni afee lɛ nɔ. Be nɛɛ ni ooomɛ ni egbe naa lɛ baaha tsofa ni eshwɛ lɛ afite kwraa. Ha okɔfi yibii lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe aha mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ.

english: Can I plant new cocoa seedlings directly into the exact spots where diseased old trees were cut down?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo dumɔwui heei yɛ he ni afo tsei momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Planting directly into old spots is risky because disease spores and root pests often stay active in the soil. It is best to clear old roots, treat the ground, add organic soil conditioners, and slightly shift the planting spots before introducing fresh seedlings.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni etsɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ bei pii lɛ helai ni jɛɔ shishifãi amli kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie shishifãi momoi lɛ, aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ, ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ afata he. Ni otsake he ni oduɔ lɛ fioo dani odu dumɔwui heei.

english: I bought a chemical at the local market for my cocoa, but I am not sure if it is the right product. What should I do before applying it to my farm?
ga: Miheɔ tsofai ni akɛfeɔ kookoo yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ. Shi mileee kɛji eji nɔ ni sa loo daabi. Mɛni esa akɛ mafee dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You should show the container to an agricultural extension officer before opening or using it. Unapproved or unsuitable chemicals can damage cocoa leaves, destroy pods, leave harmful chemical residues, or ruin your farm's harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie tsɛnsii atsɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ dani agbele loo akɛtsu nii. Tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ loo esaaa baanyɛ afite kookoo baa, efite ŋmeii lɛ, ni eshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui. loo okpãtã nibii ni aduɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahiɛ

english: Why did the leaves on my cocoa trees burn and turn yellow after I sprayed them with a new chemical?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ tsofa hee ko shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow or scorch when a chemical is too strong, improperly mixed, or not meant for cocoa trees. Using the wrong dosage or product stresses the plant and damages its green leaves, making it harder for the tree to make food.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshãa kɛji tsofa ko ni mli wa tsɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Akɛfutumɔ ni esaaa Ni afeee kɛha cacao tsei hu. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa loo nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná haomɔ ni ebaafite tso lɛ yibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaafee niyenii.

english: Is it safe for me to spray my crops with chemical control products during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ko ni akɛbuɔ nibii ahe lɛ baashwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, spraying in intense afternoon heat causes liquids to evaporate too quickly and can cause chemical burns on hot leaf surfaces. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon when temperatures are cooler.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ nu lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsofa ashã baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ leebi loo shwane mli be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ.

english: Why are the small young pods on my cocoa tree turning black and shriveling up before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tso lɛ tsɔɔ ediŋŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ dani edaa lɛ?

english: Young pods often turn black due to fungal attacks like Black Pod disease, which thrives in excess dampness and shade. Proper pruning to let in sunlight and using the right officer-recommended spray helps prevent this loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii ni tutuaa amɛ, tamɔ black pod hela, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi jogbaŋŋ koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ.

english: Why are there so many ants crawling up and down the trunks of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mikookoo tso lɛ mli kɛmiijɛ ŋwɛi kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Ants are usually attracted to tiny sap-sucking insects like mealybugs living on the tree. The ants protect these pests because they feed on the sweet liquid mealybugs produce, but mealybugs can spread serious plant diseases like Swollen Shoot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs ni hiɔ tsei anɔ lɛ gbalaa amɛ. Akpɔlɔi buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ mealybugs nu ni ŋɔɔ lɛ. Shi mealybugs baanyɛ agbɛ tsei ahe helai ni naa wa tamɔ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping all their flowers without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Trees drop flowers when they suffer from water stress, lack of nutrients, or low populations of pollinating insects like midges. Providing adequate shade and balanced crop food helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Tsei baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji nu mli haomɔ, niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔi tamɔ midges lɛ ayibɔ faaa. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ niyenii ni ja ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up tightly when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism that plants use to survive dry weather. Shrinking leaf exposure reduces moisture evaporation, helping the tree conserve water until rains return.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi. Ye obua tsei lɛ ni amɛbu nu he kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why is my cocoa tree growing very tall with thick green leaves, but fails to produce many pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi pods babaoo bɛ.

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, they focus all their energy on leaf and branch growth instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balanced soil nutrients are required to encourage pod development.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe lɛ, Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ niji ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ he miihia kɛha pod lɛ shweremɔ.

english: Why do the roots of my crops turn soft and rot during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Roots rot when heavy rain sits in poorly drained soil for too long, suffocating the roots by blocking oxygen. Trapped underground moisture encourages soil fungi to attack and decay the root system.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli edɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing the food my crops need to produce a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Crops show nutrient hunger through pale green or purplish leaves, weak stems, slow growth, and low yields. An extension officer can inspect leaf signs or run soil tests to tell you exactly what nutrient is missing.
ga: Tsei jieɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kpo kɛtsɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo purple, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, amɛdalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo, kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ nɔ. Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ baai lɛ amli kɛji okadi ko yɛ he loo amɛfee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa koni amɛtsɔɔ bo nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings withered and die when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are not strong enough yet. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, providing the shade and soil moisture the cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ baai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛfataa cocoa bibii ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber underground. Staking also keeps the foliage off the wet ground, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ baa helai anaa.

english: Plantain plants naturally produce many suckers, but if you allow too many to grow, they steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main tree gets enough strength to grow a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baawo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi kɛji oha eda fe nine lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ eshwɛɔ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller fruits when I plant them very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing crops correctly gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong and yield a full harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential for making green leaves. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or adding well-decayed animal manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni akɛfee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the dirt when the rainy season gets too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe, but standing water fills up air spaces and drowns the roots, leading to decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Shi nu ni damɔ shi lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. lead to decay Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot pulls the same nutrients out of the soil season after season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the dirt. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts returns nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ Abaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efoɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant without ever producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop without fruiting when the plant experiences heat stress or erratic watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and regular watering helps the plant hold onto its blossoms so they can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni ewooo yibii kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii akpɛtɛ he koni etsɔ tomato.

english: Why are tiny worms eating into the central funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the center leaves of young maize to feed on soft growth. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts directly into the leaf funnels protects the growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai amli koni eye ŋmeii bibii ni eda lɛ. Kɛji akɛ amɔmɔ amɛ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Curled pepper leaves are typically caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or aphids that feed on the soft undersides of leaves and spread plant viruses. Checking under the leaves early and spraying with simple insecticidal soap or recommended treatments helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. ni okɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ afɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni akudɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain or cassava provides shelter and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: What happens if I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more seeds into my small farm?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ mikɛ dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli hu? mi nɔ babaoo

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce a healthy harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow and drying up before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient for green leafy growth. Adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer when the maize is young helps keep the leaves healthy and boosts corn production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he beni ŋmei lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewaje baai lɛ ni eha ŋmei lɛ shweremɔ aya hiɛ.

english: How does adding decayed animal manure or compost help my cassava and vegetables grow better?
ga: Te kooloo ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cassava kɛ aduawai lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Animal manure and compost enrich the soil with natural plant food and help the ground hold onto water longer. This improves soil fertility naturally and helps crops grow stronger roots and bigger yields.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the central leaves of my young maize plants during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu yɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys young maize leaf funnels. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or safe controls early in the morning when the insects are active stops them before they ruin the farm.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmei baa bibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ atsu nii leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds from my farm when my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crop plants and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable crops with dry leaves or grass during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, prevents the sun from evaporating water from the soil too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, retains soil moisture, and cuts down on how often you need to water.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akajie nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ aba shi

english: Why do the roots of my pepper plants rot when water stands on my farm for days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu hiɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need air inside the soil to survive. When standing water covers the field for too long, it cuts off air to the roots, causing root rot and killing the plant. Creating small drainage trenches allows excess rainwater to flow away.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ ha ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni efiteɔ tso lɛ. Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nubui bibii amli ni afee lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts alongside or after my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmãa dumɔ masɛi loo yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, working like natural fertilizer. This naturally restores soil fertility for the next season and improves your maize harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Enɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni eha o-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do seeds I save from my previous maize harvest give me a smaller yield than certified seeds bought from registered dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni aŋmala egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to resist diseases, withstand drought, and produce high yields. Saved seeds from past harvests lose these powerful qualities over generations, leading to weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni helai akamɔ amɛ, amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hewalɛ nibii nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why should I bother clearing and tilling my land before planting maize instead of just planting directly into the bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni matsu he nii dani madu ŋmãa moŋ fe ni madu yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing and tilling removes aggressive weeds that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young maize. It also loosens hard soil so crop roots can easily grow deep and absorb fertilizers.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni baa shi ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ hu shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: How will using a small power tiller help my crops grow better than using a normal hand hoe?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mini tiller ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A power tiller breaks up hard soil much deeper and faster than a hoe, mixing air and organic material into the ground. This creates soft, rich soil where roots spread quickly and collect water during dry spells.
ga: Power tiller lɛ gbáa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsuɔ ​​nii oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni baa nii. Shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛhiɛɔ nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: When is the right time for me to till my farm land before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ masaa he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu nii?

english: The best time to till is just before the rains start when the soil is slightly damp. Tilling dry soil damages your tools and creates dust, while tilling overly soaked soil creates hard mud blocks when it dries.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ atsu nii ji dani nugbɔ lɛ aje shishi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni oootsu nii lɛ baafite odɛŋdadei lɛ ni ebaaha sũ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa sũ ni wa baa kɛji egbi.

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the mature plants compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin, weak, and produce very small or empty corn cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei ni eda lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli waa. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: How deep should I put my maize seeds in the soil when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Maize seeds should be planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep, which is roughly the length of your thumb joint. Planting too shallow lets birds eat the seeds or heat dry them out, while planting too deep prevents them from sprouting.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ mli aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5, ni ji aaafee oshishifa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha okpoi lɛ aye dumɔwui lɛ loo amɛkɛ dɔlɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛgbi dumɔwui lɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young corn plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your corn plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will restore the green color and help the crop grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster on my land than the corn I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally adapted to survive tough conditions and consume soil nutrients rapidly. Clearing them early—especially during the first month of your corn's life—is essential so they do not choke your young crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Nibii ni ajieɔ mra Titri lɛ yɛ ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia waa. Enɛ ji koni amɛkafite o-corn tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is getting too little water during the sunny period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu fioo pɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ miiná yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves will roll up tightly like green straws during the hottest part of the day to protect itself from drying out. If this continues long, the leaves will turn brown and growth will stop.
ga: Kɛ́ nu bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi eŋɔli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. Kɛji enɛ tee nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛbaakpa dalɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or beans together in the same field with my corn?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmeii?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas with corn is very helpful. Legumes pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the corn naturally, while also spreading across the ground to stop weeds from growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Legumes gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ ashwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ koni jwɛi akakwɛ̃.

english: Should I burn the old corn stalks after harvest or leave them on the farm?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã ŋmãa tsei momoi beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: It is better to till old corn stalks back into the soil rather than burning them. As the stalks decay, they turn into natural food for the soil, helping it hold moisture and stay fertile for your next crop.
ga: Ehi akɛ oootsu ŋmãa tsei momo lɛ ahe nii ekoŋŋ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni oooshã amɛ. Beni tso lɛ tso lɛ miifite lɛ Amɛbafeɔ adebɔɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa fɔmɔ hiɔ shi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops yield smaller cobs when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together causes overcrowding. The crops end up competing with each other for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, which leaves the plants weak and results in small cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii baa.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain tree instead of letting them all grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ plantain tso mli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: When too many suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal food and water from the main mother plant. Keeping only three stems of different ages ensures bigger plantain bunches and continuous harvesting.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpa tsei 3 pɛ ni eye afii srɔtoi lɛ, ebaaha aná plantains wuji kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when I clear all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight because their roots and leaves are very sensitive. They need shade crops like plantains or forest trees to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ nuɔ la he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo koo mli tsei. koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaakwɛ̃.

english: What happens to my yam crop if I do not put wooden stakes for the vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi sweet potato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ emaaa shi?

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves and capture maximum sunlight. Without stakes, leaves stay shaded on the ground, making less food for the plant and leading to very small tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa niyenii babaoo, ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. The crop moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the new top leaves to survive, leaving the old bottom leaves to starve and turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei anɔ koni amɛhi shi. Ha shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why should I not apply chemical fertilizer to my field right before a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wooo ŋmɔ mli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains create surface runoff that washes the fertilizer off your field into streams before crop roots can drink it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is just moist allows the roots to absorb nutrients safely.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oyale mli kɛyaa faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays wet for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil starves cassava roots of air and creates ideal conditions for fungal diseases to thrive. Excess moisture rots the tubers beneath the soil before they can mature for harvest.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni sa aba koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ. Fɛ̃i babaoo baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbo dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Sucking the plant's juices causes the young leaves to deform and curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei amli lɛ haa baai bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomatoes drop flowers when temperatures get extremely high, when there is too much nitrogen fertilizer, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Without successful pollination, the flower dies and falls off.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛji akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ loo kɛji kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Kɛji pollination bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to look stunted even when I buy high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miikpa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miheɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. If weeds are not cleared early, your plants will be starved and remain short and weak.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mli. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Otsei lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛkumɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: The best time to plant cocoa seedlings in Ghana is at the start of the major rainy season, usually around April to June. This allows the young plants to establish strong roots with plenty of water before the dry season hits.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ Ghana ji nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ April kɛyashi June mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa kɛ nu babaoo dani hulutsoo be lɛ baa.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their leaves are tender and cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. Without shade plants like plantains or shade trees, sunlight burns the leaves, turning them yellow and causing them to dry up and fall off.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ ji bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ dumɔwui bibii loo hulutsoo tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu la baaha baai lɛ ashã. Ha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha baai lɛ agbi ni amɛgbee shi.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my land is good enough for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil holds moisture well without staying waterlogged, is deep enough for roots to go down, and is rich in organic matter. Dark, crumbly topsoil usually shows that the land is suitable for cocoa.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ nu ehiɛɛɛ mli. Emli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ atswa shishifãi. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni etse ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ jɛmɛ ji he ni sa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ.

english: Why are the small flowers on my cocoa trees dropping off instead of turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ani amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off if the tree lacks water, nutrients, or proper pollination by tiny insects called midge flies. High heat and dry winds can also cause natural flower drop as the tree tries to protect itself from stress.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu, niyenii mli hewalɛ loo kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ. Atsɛɔ amɛ midge ŋmeii. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi baanyɛ aha adebɔɔ mli fɔfɔii agbo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ miitao ebu ehe kɛjɛ nɔnyɛɛ he.

english: Black pods are usually caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overly humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in, which helps prevent this fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine mli Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my mature cocoa trees stop producing pods during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ kpaɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry harmattan season, dry winds and lack of rain make the tree conserve water to survive. The tree sheds leaves and temporarily stops producing new flowers and pods until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa tsei nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ nu he koni amɛhi shi. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛkpaa fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei feemɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How many years will it take for my new cocoa trees to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cacao tso hee lɛ aje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years to produce their first yield.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ fɔɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or extra branches so the tree sends its food directly to making big, healthy pods instead of wastefully feeding extra leaves. It also lets sunlight reach the farm and keeps diseases away.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​niyenii tɛ̃ɛ koni efee ŋmeii agboi ni mli wa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaafite baai krokomɛi lɛ, Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni hulu la shɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa helai baaa.

english: Why are some of my cocoa pods growing very small with flat seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraaa ni amɛyɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: Small or flat pods usually mean the flowers were not fully pollinated by insects or the tree did not get enough nutrients while the pod was growing. Nutrient-rich soil and good shade help ensure full pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔi bibii loo fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ efɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kwraa. Aloo tso lɛ náaa niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ hulutsoo kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ obɔ.

english: What simple practices make one cocoa farm produce far more pods than another farm on the same size of land?
ga: Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmɔ kome woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe ŋmɔ kroko ni yɔɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: High yields come from planting high-quality hybrid seeds, controlling pests and weeds early, regular pruning to keep the trees clean, and applying the right fertilizer at the correct time of the year.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo jɛɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ mli. Mra Be mli Nibii ni Yeɔ Tso lɛ kɛ Jwɛi lɛ Ahe Afoɔ tso lɛ daa koni tso lɛ he atse. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know when my cassava is fully mature and ready to be pulled from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male beni mi-yucca lɛ eda kwraa ni efee klalo akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava shows it is ready for harvest when its lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the base of the stem begins to crack open as the tubers expand beneath the surface.
ga: Akɛɛ akɛ, kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ, efee klalo kɛha nikpamɔ. Ashiɔ tsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni tsei lɛ amli shwereɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: What will happen to my yam tubers if I leave them in the soil for too long after the vines have dried?
ga: Mɛni baa mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni wain tsei lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature yam tubers in wet soil for too long after the upper leaves dry up exposes them to soil insects, rot, and loss of starch quality, which reduces their market value.
ga: Ni aaashi sweet potato ŋmeii ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ egbi lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha kooloi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aná amɛ. fitemɔ kɛ ashikishaŋ kpakpa ni baa shi Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves roll up and dry out to protect the plant from losing too much water in high heat. The plant intentionally drops its outer leaves to conserve moisture in its main stem until rainy weather returns.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛgbiɔ koni tso lɛ akafite nu babaoo yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Tso lɛ jwɛŋɔ eshiɔ esɛɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cowpea plants curling up and feeling sticky when I touch them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni minuɔ he akɛ amɛhe ejɔ kɛji mita amɛhe lɛ?

english: Sticky, curled leaves are a sign of tiny pests like aphids feeding on the sap underneath the leaf. They secrete a sugary substance called honeydew, which attracts mold if left untreated.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni wa lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ he okadi. Amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nectar lɛ kpo. Enɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they suffer from heat stress, unpredictable watering, or too much nitrogen in the soil, which forces the plant to focus on leafy growth rather than growing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and green in one part of my field but stay short and yellow in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi fã kroko hu yɛ kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo.

english: Uneven growth usually means the soil nutrients or moisture levels are not uniform across your land. Yellow plants in one section often indicate a lack of nitrogen or poor water drainage in that specific patch of earth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeee ekome yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ he kome ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce very small fruits when I plant them close together in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots compete heavily for the same limited pool of soil nutrients and water, preventing any single plant from getting enough food to grow full-sized fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa tso fɛɛ tso aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my corn stalks fall over easily whenever strong winds blow across my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn stalks blow over when their root systems are shallow, which happens if the soil is too hard for roots to grow deep, or if soil was not mounded around the base of the stems to anchor them firmly.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛyaa kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛya shɔŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ atooo sũ lɛ he kɛbɔle tso lɛ shishi koni emɔ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my freshly harvested cassava roots start to turn dark and rot within just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa ehee lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots do not have a hard natural skin like yams, so once pulled from the ground, internal physiological reactions begin immediately. Any small cuts or bruises accelerate decay within two to three days.
ga: Cassava shishifãi bɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni wa tamɔ ŋmei. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli nifeemɔi jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nibii bibii ni afo loo atswa lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested groundnuts get soft and moldy quickly after I pull them up from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly pulled groundnuts carry high moisture inside their shells. If they are not spread out to dry thoroughly in the sun right after harvest, trapped moisture encourages fungal growth and spoilage.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni ajie ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ amɛmli. Kɛji akɛ agbɛɛɛ ashwã ni agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Trapped moisture woɔ ŋmɔtɔ dalɛ kɛ fitemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my crop turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential food plants need to grow strong green leaves. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the soil, or the soil may simply be tired from continuous farming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ agbɔjɔ kɛjɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest every year if I plant the same crop on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmaa fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Every crop draws specific nutrients out of the soil. When you plant the same crop repeatedly without resting the land or changing crops, it drains those specific nutrients completely, leaving the soil weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okɛ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ duɔ shii abɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo etsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii Nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baaho kwraa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and weak when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward quickly to get light. This rapid upward growth makes their stems thin and weak, so they can easily fall over during strong wind or rain.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe oya koni amɛná la lɛ. Nɛkɛ dalɛ ni yaa oya nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ egbee shi mlɛo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ? Yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Rolling up leaves is the plant's natural shield against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the area exposed to the scorching sun, helping it hold onto moisture and survive the hot day.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli dɔlɛ hebuu. Tsei haa hulutsoo baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some crops take many months to yield while others are ready in just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi heɔ nyɔji babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu feɔ klalo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Different crops are naturally programmed with different lifespans. Leafy vegetables put energy into growing leaves quickly, whereas root or grain crops take longer to store energy in their roots or seeds before they mature.
ga: Adebɔɔ kɛ shihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi eto ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ahe gbɛjianɔ. Aduawai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ haa amɛbaai ni daa oya lɛ hewalɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi loo dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi loo dumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does local rice grow so well in flooded or swampy land where other plants die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni tsei krokomɛi gboiɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems that carry oxygen down from the air into their roots underwater. This allows their roots to breathe and thrive in wet soil that would choke and rot other crops.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ tsɔnei krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ ni mli efɔ ni kulɛ ebaagbe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ nɔ. ni fiteɔ

english: Why do insects and caterpillars suddenly appear on my farm right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi kɛ ŋmeii ba miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pest eggs often hide underground or inside dry stems throughout the dry season. When the rains arrive, the moisture triggers the eggs to hatch right as your young, soft crops start growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi loo tsei ni egbi lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni otsei bibii ni ji bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over generations to survive tough conditions. They take up water, light, and soil nutrients much faster and more aggressively than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛheɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya kɛ hewalɛ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous harvest give me a smaller yield than the certified seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Many commercial seeds are specially bred hybrids designed for a powerful first harvest. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special qualities in the next generation, resulting in uneven growth and lower yields.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni afee kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my harvested grain rot or get eaten by insects when stored inside my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ loo kooloi yeɔ amɛ kɛ́ akɛto shĩa mli lɛ?

english: If harvested grain is not dried completely before storage, internal moisture creates warm, damp conditions that attract insects and encourage mold growth inside your storage bags.
ga: Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i baa. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni ewoɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ onitoo kotokui lɛ amli.

english: How do I know when my oil palm fruit bunches are fully ripe and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-oil palm yibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Oil palm fruits are ready for harvest when a few loose, bright reddish-orange fruits begin to fall naturally to the ground from the bunch.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni oil palm tso yibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ fioo ko jeɔ shishi amɛjɛɔ amɛkuu lɛ mli amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Will using a processing machine extract more oil from my palm nuts compared to pounding them by hand?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baajie fɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mi-palm tso lɛ mli kɛ akɛto nine ni akɛbaatswa lɛ he?

english: Yes, mechanical presses apply much stronger and more consistent pressure than manual pounding, extracting nearly all the oil from the fiber and significantly reducing waste.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔne ni akɛnyɛɔ nii anɔ lɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni mli wa ni yaa nɔ daa tsuɔ nii fe ni akɛ niji nyɛɔ nɔ. Ejieɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ mu fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ tsɔji lɛ amli, ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my palm oil turn sour if I wait several days after harvest before boiling the palm nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-palm fɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔ kɛji mimɛ gbii babaoo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ dani mikɛ palm ŋmeii lɛ shã lɛ?

english: Delaying processing after harvest allows natural enzymes in the fruit to break down the oil fats into free fatty acids, which creates a sour taste and lowers the quality of the oil.
ga: Nibii ni afeɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli enzymes ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ gbálaa fɔ ni yɔɔ fɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni efeɔ fatty acids ni aheee nɔ ko. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ mli ŋɔɔ ni ehaa fɔ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Can I put the leftover palm nut fibers and empty bunches back onto my farm soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmeii ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, spreading processed palm fibers and empty fruit bunches back on your land acts as organic mulch, which retains moisture in the soil, controls weeds, and decays into nutrients like potassium for your plants.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso yibii ni atsu he nii kɛ aduawai akui ni bɛ nɔ ko ni ooogbɛ ashwã oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi, amɛkudɔɔ jwɛi, ni amɛgbalaa amɛfeɔ niyenii tamɔ potassium kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots spoil and turn dark so quickly just two days after digging them up?
