ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ duŋ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni atsa lɛ?

english: Once removed from the ground, cassava roots lose water fast and react with air, triggering a rapid natural chemical process called post-harvest decay.
ga: Kɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ nifeemɔ ko ni yaa oya ni atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ fitemɔ baa.

english: Can I safely plant cassava in the middle of my young oil palm farm without damaging the palms?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei shweshweeshwe yɛ mi-oil palm ŋmɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mifiteee ŋmei tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop cassava during the first two to three years of oil palm growth, as long as you leave enough space around the palm seedlings so they do not fight for sunlight and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ loo etɛ ni oil palm lɛ kwɛɔ lɛ mli. Shii abɔ ni obaashi he ko yɛ he lɛ. palm dumɔwui ni fa bɔ ni sa Koni amɛkaye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Yellowing in a V-shape starting from the tips of older leaves means your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaves and fast growth.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ V su mli ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like mites or thrips, which multiply rapidly during hot weather and damage young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mites loo thrips lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni shwereɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ baai bibii lɛ

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid palm seeds instead of just planting seeds collected from my existing farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe hybrid palm dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ ni miyɔɔ mli momo lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Seeds taken directly from farm trees do not produce identical offspring and often yield less oil, whereas certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred to give higher oil yields and resist disease.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ wooo seshi kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni bei pii lɛ, fɔ fioo pɛ amɛwoɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná mu babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ.

english: Why do my young crops stop growing well when weeds are left close to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ashi jwɛi yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops by stealing the water, fertilizer, and sunlight your plants need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara waa lɛ ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up into tight tubes during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water when the sun gets too hot. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down or rain falls.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ loo nugbɔ baanɛ.

english: If rain is falling heavily on my farm, why are the leaves on my crops still turning yellow?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Too much water fills up the air spaces in the soil, which smothers the roots and prevents them from breathing and taking up nutrients, causing leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Nu babaoo eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu ni ehaaa amɛmu ni amɛye niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow taller and stronger when I clear and break up the hard soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛhe waa kɛji mijie shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mifo mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Breaking up hard soil helps plant roots push deep easily to find food and water, while also allowing rainwater to soak into the ground instead of washing away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ gbɛ ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni eeefo.

english: Why do my cassava yields get smaller every time I plant on the exact same plot of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my pepper plants if I sow the seeds too close to one another?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak stems and very few fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he. aloo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollin lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and crowd out my crops even when I do not water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haaa amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, meaning they can steal water and nutrients from the soil much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya kwraa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my crops more heavily during the dry weather than during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ fe nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dry weather weakens plants because of water stress, making them softer targets for insects that are searching for sap to get moisture.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ nu he haomɔ hewɔ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni kooloi bibii ni taoɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ taoɔ amɛhe blɛoo.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn black and rot when I store it inside bags right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku mli beni mikpa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains hidden moisture. If stored immediately without proper drying, heat builds up inside the bag, creating mold that spoils the grain.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛji akɛ akɛto amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni egbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Dɔlɛ baabua ehe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting and shrinking while sitting in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ beni mita nitoohe lɛ?

english: Yam tubers are alive and use their stored energy to try to grow into new plants, which causes them to lose water, shrink, and sprout if kept in warm places.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ tsei heei. Enɛ haa nu sɛɛ foɔ, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwereɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ amɛ wo hulutsoo be mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is essential for growth. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves turn green and produce larger ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni he hiaa koni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmei toi wuji.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or a lack of water. Keeping the soil damp and protecting young plants from harsh sun helps the flowers stay on and produce peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing them properly gives every plant enough room to grow strong and yield more food.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant groundnuts and maize on the same field at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts alongside maize is very good because groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which feeds the maize and keeps your soil healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi lɛ hi waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa saplings dry up and die under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn easily in strong heat. Planting plantain trees alongside them creates living shade to protect young cocoa from direct sun and preserve soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa hɔɔŋ baa koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water trapped in the soil prevents air from reaching them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsi kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How does covering the soil around my crop roots with dry grass help them during dry periods?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and stopping moisture from evaporating quickly under the hot sun.
ga: Mulching ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: What is eating small holes in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which feed on young maize leaves. Checking your farm early and using recommended ash remedies or crop sprays keeps the pest from destroying your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite oŋmɔji lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark shade. Pruning unnecessary branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees and stop the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shĩa mli hei ni edɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ kɛbaa. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ ni helai kpaa.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water, light, and soil food from your farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops the best chance to grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, la, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu la lɛ fa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are small and their tender leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to them keeps the soil moist and protects them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa ni amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ masɛi lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe waa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn dark green and grow heavy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni eha ŋmei toi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up in flat soil and suffocates the roots. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nu ni ekã shi lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the heavy fruits are growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ eda lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that cannot support the heavy weight of a full bunch during strong winds. Propping up the trunk with a strong wooden Y-stick or bamboo pole gives the tree the support it needs until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni tamɔ Y loo ŋmei tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Pepper flowers fall off when the plant suffers stress from extreme afternoon heat or dry soil. Spreading dry grass around the base as mulch and watering regularly keeps the soil cool so flowers can turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle A shishi kɛtsɔ mulch kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. koni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ afee chili ŋmɔtɔ

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high in the air to catch sunlight to make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and exposed to light, which leads to much larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni amɛhoo nii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akabote hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ, ni la hu akashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii ni dara babaoo baa shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the tender center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Those caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing point of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf funnel destroys them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ hei ni ŋmeii tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu lɛ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ baafite amɛ dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even if I planted high-quality seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, light, and soil nutrients away from your crops like thieves. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks after planting ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce full yields.
ga: Taakɛ julɔi ji lɛ, jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less food after farming on the same spot for three years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ miiwo niyenii fioo yɛ be mli ni mitsu okwaayeli yɛ he kome afii etɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops repeatedly removes natural nutrients from the soil over time. Adding compost, growing legumes like beans to fix soil health, or resting the field restores the fertility your crops need.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Fertilizing Dumɔ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii koni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Aloo, hejɔɔmɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha otsei lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii ni he hiaa bo lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl tightly into rolls during hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during peak heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. Ensuring adequate morning watering near the roots keeps the plant hydrated and reduces heat stress.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ fe nine lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ leebi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná nu ni ebaaha dɔlɛ he haomɔ aba shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize plants turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on the bottom of maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the maize plant moves whatever nutrients it has left from its older bottom leaves up to nourish the younger growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. Kɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Abɛi tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea crops make the soil richer for the maize I plant in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to a family of crops called legumes that have special relationship with good bacteria in the soil. These crops pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural plant food in the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ekɛ bacteria kpakpa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ wekukpaa krɛdɛɛ ko. Tsei nɛɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my crops grow bigger and greener leaves so fast?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔji oya lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer delivers concentrated minerals like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium straight to the crop's roots. Nitrogen acts like high-energy food that allows the crop to produce green leaf material, which helps the plant trap sunlight to make its own energy.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nibii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potasium baa. tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ Nitrogen tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei mɔɔ hulu la koni amɛ fee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon even when the ground isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ egbiko kwraa lolo po?

english: In extreme heat, tomato leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. The plant deliberately wilts to curl its leaves and reduce its surface area exposed to the sun, conserving moisture until the cool evening.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe heat stress, dry spells, or a sudden lack of nutrients. The plant realizes it doesn't have enough water or energy to support growing fruits, so it drops the flowers to save its own life.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hulutsoo be mli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ he. Tso lɛ yɔseɔ akɛ ebɛ nu loo hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, eshi fɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: If goats chew off the leaves of my young cassava plants, will the crop still be able to produce cassava tubers?
ga: Kɛji too ko ŋmɔ mi ŋmei bibii lɛ Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmei shishifãi lolo?

english: Cassava is a tough crop that stores extra energy in its stems and roots. If animals eat the top leaves, the plant will use its stored energy to push out fresh new leaves, but its final yield of tubers will be lower because it wasted time and energy recovering instead of growing roots.
ga: Cassava ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni toɔ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi amli. Kɛji kooloi ye baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛshwieɔ baai heei. Shi naagbee yibiiwoo ni jɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli baa lɛ baa shi ejaakɛ afiteɔ be kɛ hewalɛ yɛ shishifãi ni aaada lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why does my yam vine stop climbing higher when the tip of the stem gets broken or eaten?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ akumɔ tso lɛ naagbeehei lɛ loo aye lɛ?

english: The very tip of a yam vine releases natural growth signals that direct the plant to stretch upward. When that tip is destroyed, the plant temporarily stops climbing and must take time to sprout new side-branches from lower down the stem.
ga: Sweet potato wain tso lɛ naagbee lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli dalɛ he okadii ni kɛɔ tso lɛ akɛ ekɛ ehe abɔ he lɛ tsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ naagbee lɛ fite lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ be kukuoo mli ni ehe baahia ni ekɛ niji heei ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ kɛyashi shishigbɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees wither and die when I plant them in a field where all the large trees have been cleared?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni ajie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally grow under the canopy of large forest trees. Their leaves are delicate and burn easily in full direct sunlight, which dries them out faster than their young roots can absorb ground water.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ashishi. Ebaai lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stay small and weak when weeds are growing close around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛhe waaa beni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants with fast-growing roots that steal drinking water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. When weeds surround your crops, your plants go hungry and thirsty, which stunts their growth.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shishifãi lɛ daa oya ni juɔ nu ni anuɔ, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɔle onibii ahe lɛ, hɔmɔ kɛ kumai baaye otsei lɛ. ni haa dalɛ kpaa

english: Why do my cassava plants produce very thin, small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight each other underground for the same limited space, water, and soil nutrients, preventing any single plant from swelling its roots into large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko ni faaa, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni tso ko akaha eshishifãi lɛ atsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a natural survival trick. By shedding leaves, the plant reduces water loss and conserves its energy in the underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa. Kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ baa shi, ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves burn and dry up when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees to protect them from harsh, direct sunlight. Without shade trees, the hot sun burns their delicate leaves and drains the moisture they need to grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni eda lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha amɛná hulutsoo lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ shãa tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ekɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ hoɔ amɛmli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon even when there is water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: During the hottest part of the day, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can suck it up from the ground. As long as the soil is moist, the plant will usually recover once the evening air cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Tsei hu sumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ kɛ́ gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet weather. Pruning extra tree branches helps sunlight and air dry out the crop, making it harder for the disease to spread.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji krokomɛi ni oookpa lɛ baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tso lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa ewaa waa akɛ hela lɛ baagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are there small holes and chewing marks on my young maize leaves after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni chew marks yɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: Pests like the fall armyworm feed heavily on tender, new maize leaves right after the rains begin. Checking your crops early allows you to catch the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ baaye ŋmãa baai heei blɛoo beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ. Nibii ni adu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ omɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds on my farm grow much faster than my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally better at grabbing water, sunshine, and soil food than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your main crops of essential nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛheɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye amɛ kɛjɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer or manure before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: Tired soil often produces pale or yellowish crops that grow very slowly and give poor yields. If your crops look weak compared to past years, adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer will restore the soil food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni daa blɛoo waa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ baa. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto afi ni eho lɛ he lɛ Kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my plantain sucker stop growing fast during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sucker dumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains are made mostly of water and need continuous moisture to produce new leaves and stems. When water is scarce, the plant pauses its growth to save its reserves until it gets watered again.
ga: Nu ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantains babaoo ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be koni baai kɛ tsei heei akwɛ̃. Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu nu ni ato lɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni abaaha amɛ nu ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes the crops to fight one another for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in tall, weak stalks with very small or empty cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred to resist local diseases, handle hot weather better, and produce uniform, larger harvests compared to seeds saved from previous crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kpeɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa ni da fe dumɔwui ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that create shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Which direction should I plant my cassava stem cuttings in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava stems should be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky, either slanted or straight down. Planting them upside down forces the shoots to waste energy turning right-side up, which delays growth and reduces tuber yield.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei tsei ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi. Abaanyɛ atsɔ mli loo akɛwo shi. Kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛtsei lɛ kwɛɔ ninejurɔgbɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward the sun, which boosts tuber growth and protects leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, and stops weeds from getting sunlight to grow, helping your crops stay hydrated and stress-free.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni hulu la akashɛ amɛnɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni otsei lɛ anáa nu ni amɛhaoɔ amɛhe.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds from my maize farm during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants grow slowly at first and cannot compete with fast-growing weeds for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Weeding early gives the crop a strong head start before the weeds can starve it.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la. Ehaa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛ hɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main element needed for healthy leaf growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the root zone, or soil may simply need manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji nɔ titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my crops when the ground is completely dry during a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need water to absorb fertilizer through their roots. Applying fertilizer in dry soil concentrates salts around the roots, which can scorch or burn the roots and damage the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia tsei koni amɛtsɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei abɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã loo eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite tso lɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping their flowers before forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by extreme drought, sudden heat, or pest attacks like mirids (capsids). Keeping good shade cover and managing insect pests helps the flowers remain on the tree to turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids, hulutsoo kpakpa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi ni ahi tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmeii.

english: Tomato leaf curl is commonly caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil or targeted sprays prevents the virus from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Mra be mli whitefly nɔkwɛmɔ Neem fɔ loo spot spray ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom right before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ yɛ shishi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black rotten spots at the bottom of peppers are usually caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium due to irregular watering. Consistent watering helps the plant transport calcium properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ashishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why can my brother in the south plant crops twice a year, but I can only plant once on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛmi nuu ni yɔɔ Anaigbɛ lɛ duɔ tsei shii enyɔ pɛ yɛ afi mli lɛ? Shi ani manyɛ madu lɛ shikome pɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Different regions in Ghana receive different amounts and patterns of rainfall. Some areas have two distinct rainy seasons each year allowing two harvests, while drier areas only get enough rain for one main growing season per year.
ga: Ghana kpokpai sɔrɔtoi naa nugbɔshiimɔ falɛ srɔtoi kɛ henɔi srɔtoi. Hei komɛi yɛ nugbɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi, ni amɛkpaa yibii enyɔ, yɛ be mli ni hei ni egbi lɛ naa nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be titri kome pɛ yɛ afi mli.

english: What is a water table, and how does it affect my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji nugbɔshiimɔ okpɔlɔ? Ni te enáa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: The water table is the underground level where the soil is fully soaked with water. When the water table is high or close to the surface, crop roots can easily reach water, but if it is low and deep underground, your crops rely entirely on rain falling from the sky.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ ji shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi he ni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ lɛ. Kɛji nu lɛ fa loo ebɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa nu oya. Shi kɛji akɛ eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni eyɛ shishigbɛ ni mli kwɔ lɛ Onibii fɛɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my land stay dry at the start of the rainy season while my neighbor's land gets wet easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: This often depends on how deep the underground water table is under your soil. Lands with a deeper underground water level require the rainy season to progress for a while before enough water collects in the soil for crops to use.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ damɔ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli kwɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ baabi ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aya hiɛ be ko dani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa abua shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Should I plant my crop seeds immediately after the very first rain falls?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is usually better to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain often leaves the dry soil quickly because the underground water level is still low, which can cause young seeds to dry up and die if another rain does not fall soon.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ faaa lolo, ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔ kroko enɛɛɛ mra.

english: Why does my hand-dug farm well dry up during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ ni mikɛ mi nine tsu lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, the underground water table drops deeper into the earth because there is no rain refilling it. As the rainy season progresses and rain soaks into the soil, the water table rises back up and fills your well.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ejaakɛ nugbɔ bɛ ni baaha eyi mli ekoŋŋ. Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nu lɛ baaya ŋwɛi ni eyi o-pond lɛ mli obɔ.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant if my community only gets one rainy season in a year?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji akɛ mi akutso lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: In areas with only one rainy season, it is best to plant strong crops like yam, sorghum, millet, or long-duration maize that can grow steadily and make full use of that single extended period of rainfall.
ga: Yɛ hei ni nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɔɔ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eda be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly in the dry season even when I carry water to pour on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu shwie nɔ moŋ?

english: In the dry season, intense heat evaporates surface water rapidly, and the natural underground water is too deep for crop roots to reach. Pouring a little water on top is often not enough to replace the deep soil moisture crops need to stay cool and strong.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ni adebɔɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli kwɔ tsɔ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, nu fioo ni ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaato shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Esa akɛ tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: How do crop roots search for water under the ground when there is no rain?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛnaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ?

english: As the surface soil dries out, crop roots naturally grow deeper downward toward the underground water table. Crops with deep taproots can survive dry spells longer because they can reach deep water stores that shallow-rooted crops cannot reach.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ eshɛ nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ ni tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ ahe.

english: Why does water gather on top of my field late in the rainy season but not at the beginning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee shi jeee yɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: At the start of the season, the underground water level is low and absorbs rain like a sponge. As the rainy season continues, the underground water table rises to the surface until the soil is completely full, causing extra rain to pool on top of your land.
ga: Yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baa shi ni eŋɔɔ nugbɔ tamɔ sponji. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ tee nɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ baaya ŋwɛi kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi. Eha nugbɔ kroko nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: How can I tell if my farm land is suitable for growing vegetables during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha aduawai adumɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Land suitable for dry-season planting usually has a high underground water table, such as low-lying valley bottoms or land near streams, where soil moisture remains close to the surface long after the rains have stopped.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni fa babaoo, tamɔ shikpɔŋ kplanaa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. loo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ faa ko Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does my farm produce less maize every year even though I plant at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? Adu yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Planting the same crop on the same piece of land every season drains specific nutrients from the soil. Rotating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnut helps restore nitrogen naturally to keep the soil fertile.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen baa ekoŋŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa.

english: Why do some parts of my land produce big crops while other parts on the same plot yield very weak plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei komɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ waa ni akɛhaa?

english: Soil depth and organic matter vary across a single farm. Areas where leaves rot into dark topsoil hold more water and plant food, while eroded or stony areas lack the nourishment crops need to grow well.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. He ni baai lɛ fiteɔ lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni mli edɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii babaoo. yɛ be mli ni hei ni ŋmeii efo loo tɛi yɔɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa ni Tsei lɛ dara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Keeping fast-growing shade plants like plantain nearby protects the tender seedlings from heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ Ebaabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why are my plantain trees leaning toward one side instead of standing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ efo ehe kɛtee he kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni edamɔ shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crops naturally stretch towards sunlight to make their food. If taller trees block sunlight from one direction, the plantain stalk will bend toward the open space where it can catch maximum light.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni akɛtsu nii akɛ niyenii. Kɛji tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsi hulu la ni jɛɔ gbɛ kome pɛ nɔ lɛ naa lɛ, Plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa he ko ni gbɛ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la babaoo yɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of green leaves, but the tubers under the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of swelling its roots. Balanced soil nutrients ensure energy goes into tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ yaa bulbs ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms fall off the plant during very hot weather without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ni efeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the flowers. When pollination fails, the plant drops the flower to conserve water and survive the hot period.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛsɛɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my young mangoes falling off the branch long before they get big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree experiences sudden water shortage, lacks key minerals, or suffers from fruit fly damage. Regular watering during early fruit set and managing pests helps keep fruit on the branch.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tso ko na nu ni faaa trukaa. Minerals ni he hiaa ni bɛ loo aduawai amli ŋmeii efiteɔ Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ aduawai awomɔ mra be mli kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more maize from my plot?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely causes crops to fight over water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stalks and very small cobs, overall reducing your total harvest weight.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa. Enɛ fɛɛ baaha okpamɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ muji lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep roots adapted to quickly grab available water and food from the soil. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the nourishment your crops need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that feed on leaf sap, or by viruses they spread. Controlling these pests with mild neem oil spray stops the damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kudɔ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ kɛ neem mu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ. lɛ baakpa nɔ ni efite lɛ

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants use to build strong green leaves. It can happen when the soil is worn out, when heavy rains wash nutrients away, or when weeds steal the food from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Ebaanyɛ eba kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ fite. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii laajeɔ. Aloo kɛ́ jwɛi ju niyenii kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same piece of land every year give me smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize draws specific nutrients from the soil every season. If you plant it in the same spot repeatedly, it drains those nutrients completely, and soil pests that prefer maize will build up in the ground, causing your yields to drop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛji odu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ baaho kwraa. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ baabua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ ni baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so that plant roots can absorb it. If the soil is completely dry, the concentrated chemicals sit against the roots and can scorch or kill your crop.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa Tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kpɛtɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie cacao tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains provide a canopy of shade and hold moisture in the air, protecting the cocoa plants until they grow old enough to handle direct sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũuɔ. Ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la shɛɔ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crop plants grow very tall and thin when planted under heavy shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa shishi lɛ?

english: Plants naturally reach upward to search for sunlight to make their food. When a plant gets too much shade, it spends all its energy growing tall to find light, making it thin and weak.
ga: Tsei shɛɔ ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛtao hulu la ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. Kɛ tsei ná hulutsoo babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ena la. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers stress, such as intense dry heat or lack of water. When the plant senses it does not have enough water to feed a growing pepper, it sheds its flowers to protect itself.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nu he akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ni baaye abua ŋmɔtɔ ni miida lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ koni ekɛbu ehe.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water and food, and their leaves block light from one another. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough light and soil nutrients to grow fully.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when heavy rains fall for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. Excessive rain fills all the small air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating wet conditions where rot-causing fungi thrive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ baanyɛ ada yɛ mli lɛ aba.

english: Why does clearing all the weeds around my crops make the crops grow faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer directly from your crop. Removing weeds leaves all the food in the soil available exclusively for your crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli pɔtɛɛ kɛha onibii lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: Why does cutting off the lower branches and excess leaves of tomato plants help produce bigger tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ afolɔ tomato tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato lɛ ni edara lɛ?

english: Pruning extra leaves stops the plant from wasting food on parts that do not produce fruit. This redirects the plant's energy directly into growing larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akafite niyenii kɛjɛ fãi ni wooo yibii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to stay green. The plant moves its remaining nitrogen to the top leaves to keep growing, leaving the lower leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii titri ni he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ ekwɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tight when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during hot afternoons as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing too much water to the air. Once the sun goes down or the soil gets water, the leaves usually open back up.
ga: Shi oyitsɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baabu ehe koni nu babaoo akafite kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi loo nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbeleɔ.

english: Why do my bean plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ baai agboi babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Bean plants produce excess leaves when the soil has too much nitrogen. The plant spends all its energy growing foliage instead of focusing on flowering and making seed pods.
ga: Bean tsei woɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ baai. Mohu ɔ, a susuɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ a peeɔ ɔ he.

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning extra branches to let sunlight into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe koni hulu la babaoo abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants growing crumpled and sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Crumpled, sticky leaves mean tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies are hiding underneath and sucking the juice from your plant. Washing the leaves with neem oil or mild soapy water helps get rid of them.
ga: Baai ni wa ni egbɔjɔ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies. Okɛ ohe awo shishi ni okɛ nu ni jɛɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ atsu nii. Akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ kɛ nu afɔ baai lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie nakai baai lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground in the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani mikpa amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot when the soil traps excess water without good drainage. The waterlogged soil starves the tubers of air and allows harmful soil fungi to attack and decay them.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu ni fa fe nine ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni ehaa amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when plants face extreme heat, dry soil, or lack of pollinating insects. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa he, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ faaa lɛ anɔ. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why are my pineapples growing very small and sour instead of big and sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe agbo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Pineapples require specific nutrients like potassium and plenty of sunlight over many months. If planted in poor soil or too close together, they cannot gather enough strength to develop sweet, heavy fruit.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ potassium, kɛ hulu la babaoo he miihia pineapple nyɔji babaoo. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ loo ebɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɛɛ ebua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii ni ŋɔɔ ni tsii.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my crops when the crops are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have short roots and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to food so they establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni amɛnuuu jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ahe tawuu he kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, eyɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature and ready to dig out of the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei lɛ ekwɛ ni esa akɛ atsa shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare stems, and the base of the main stem swells and hardens, typically around 9 to 12 months after planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi, ni amɛshiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ewaa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and dry at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that get scorched under direct, heavy sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near them creates a protective canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ he feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do my plantain leaves fold downward and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves that lose a lot of water in intense heat. The plant folds its leaves downward to reduce sun exposure and save moisture, and it sacrifices older leaves to direct remaining water to the center stem.
ga: Plantains yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni nu babaoo fiteɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni eha hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ. ni ebaasha baai ni egbɔ koni ekɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants stay short and produce very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize requires plenty of food from the soil, especially nitrogen, to grow tall and produce big cobs. If the soil lacks nutrients or if weeds steal the water and fertilizer early on, the crop becomes stunted.
ga: Niyenii nibii babaoo he miihia ŋmã kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmeii wuji Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii loo jwɛi ju nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii mra lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my cassava yield big roots in loose soil but very small roots in hard soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ haa shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ?

english: Cassava roots need space to expand under the ground. Soft, loose soil allows the roots to swell easily, whereas compacted or heavy clay soil squeezes the roots and prevents them from expanding.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ he miihia he ko ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafuu. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo ni tsii lɛ miimɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaaa amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterward, the maize feeds on this natural nitrogen left in the soil and grows much healthier.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ baaye adebɔɔ mli nitrogen ni eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebaaná hewalɛ babaoo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant saves energy by shedding flowers instead of nourishing new peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baakwɛ hewalɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaakwɛ ŋmeii heei anɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling happens when tomato plants try to minimize water loss during high heat, or when tiny pests like whiteflies suck sap from the leaves and spread viruses that distort plant growth.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Aloo beni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ amɛshwãa lɛ amɛshwãa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seeds after the rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady rains so the soil is thoroughly wet beneath the surface. Sowing after just one early rain risks seeds sprouting and drying out if the sun returns.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ nɛ shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ kɛ oshara ba akɛ dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaagbi kɛji hulu lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my food crops right after clearing the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi niyenii tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can sleep in the soil for years waiting for light. Clearing the land exposes them to full sun, allowing native weeds—which are naturally tougher—to sprout faster than cultivated seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛmɛ la. He ni amɛjieɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Ekwɛ̃ɔ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start rotting so quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot rapidly when they are bruised during harvesting, exposed to excessive heat, or stored without ventilation. Keeping intact tubers in a shaded, well-ventilated structure prevents moisture buildup and spoilage.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine loo ni akɛtoɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ bulbs ni bɛ muji lɛ to he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ akabɔle ehe ni efite.

english: How do I decide which crop will give me good returns before I clear my land for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ tsei ni baaha yibii kpakpai lɛ ahe dani majie he ko ni abaadu nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Before clearing land, observe local market prices, demand, and transport access. Short-season crops like pepper or maize bring quick cash flow, while longer-term crops like cocoa or oil palm require upfront investment but provide long-term income.
ga: Dani abaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Gbalamɔ ojwɛŋmɔ kɛya maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli jara, nibii ni ataoɔ, kɛ bɔ ni anáa gbɛfaa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ shito loo abele kɛ shika baa oya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmei fɔ Ebiɔ ni awo shika kɛtsɔ hiɛ shi ehaa shika ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to sow my maize seeds so that the rains do not destroy the harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa koni nugbɔ akafite ŋmãa lɛ?

english: In Ghana, planting at the start of the major rainy season ensures plants get sufficient water while growing, allowing the cobs to mature and dry naturally as the rainfall tapers off.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ dumɔ be mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni egbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers very close together to get more bunches on my plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo ahi saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting suckers too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stems and small, light bunches that fetch lower prices.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ tsei bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa lɛ baa, ni no haa amɛjara baa shi.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect the roots underneath; fresh leaves will sprout quickly once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ahe. Baai heei baakwɛ̃ oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why is my tomato plant growing very tall with many leaves but refusing to produce flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai babaoo shi amɛfɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes tomato plants focus on leaf growth instead of flowering; balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages fruit development.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔii ni amɛbaawo lɛ. Nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa aduawai lɛ daa.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they steal nutrients from my main crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mitsei titrii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Planting cowpeas alongside maize is beneficial because cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, feeding the maize naturally and improving soil health.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha ŋmãa niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to damage my young maize crops mostly in the early morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ fiteɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ babaoo yɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ?

english: Armyworms feed during the cooler hours of early morning and evening to avoid direct sunlight, making morning the best time to inspect and treat your fields.
ga: Kplukai tsuɔ nii waa yɛ gbɛkɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai lɛ amli. ni ji leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ koni hulu la akashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ha leebi afee be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni okɛbaakwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli ni okɛtsu nii.

english: Which crops should I select if my farmlands usually experience short rainy periods?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mahala kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kukuoo mli?

english: Drought-tolerant crops such as sorghum, millet, and sweet potatoes have deep root systems or high water efficiency, making them less vulnerable when rains stop early.
ga: Nibii ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni ŋmãa yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo amɛheɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei nɛɛ nyɛɛɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ mra.

english: How long can I store my harvested fresh cassava roots before they begin to spoil?
ga: Be enyiɛ manyɛ makɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa ehee lɛ ahi shi dani amɛje shishi amɛfite?

english: Fresh cassava roots spoil within two to three days after harvest; processing them quickly into gari or high-quality cassava flour extends their shelf life and increases profit.
ga: Cassava shishifãi heei lɛ baafite yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Nibii ni afeɔ oya ni akɛfeɔ gari loo ŋmei ashikishaŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni ehaa sɛɛnamɔi ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What causes my stored maize to turn into white powder after a few months in the barn?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikɛto lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛhi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weevils and grain borers feed on stored maize from the inside out; drying grains to a safe moisture level and using airtight storage bags prevents insect damage.
ga: Weevils kɛ seed borers yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kɛyashɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ shweshweeshwe, ni akɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi akafite amɛ.

english: How many weeks or months does it usually take from the day I plant maize until I can harvest and sell it?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, otsii loo nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaanyɛ akpa ni ahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Most improved maize varieties in Ghana take between 12 to 16 weeks (90 to 120 days) to fully mature, though you can harvest green maize earlier if you plan to sell fresh cobs for boiling or roasting.
ga: Abele henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ otsii 12 kɛyashi 16 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) dani amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ. Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ okpa ŋmãa ŋmɔŋ mra kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ akɛ obaahɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa heei lɛ koni okɛshã loo okɛshã.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest without digging up all my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ efooo?

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting; you can check readiness by carefully digging around one sample plant to see if the tubers are thick, firm, and full of starch.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ kɛji eyɛ kɛtsɔ he ni ooofee lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei lɛ ahe nɔkwɛmɔnɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji bulb lɛ mli eyi, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni eyi kɛ starch.

english: Why do I need to nurse my tomato seeds in a small nursery bed first instead of planting them straight into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli klɛŋklɛŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato seeds are tiny and delicate, so nursing them protects young seedlings from heavy rains, hot sun, and pests until they grow strong enough to survive being transplanted into the main farm.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, saamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni mli edɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What signs will my crops show me when the soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatsɔɔ mi beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When crops are hungry for nutrients, their leaves usually turn pale green or yellow instead of deep green, and the plants grow very slowly with thin stems.
ga: Beni tsei he hiaa niyenii lɛ Bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. Ni tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa kɛ shishifãi bibii.

english: Pepper leaves curl during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss through evaporation, helping the plant conserve water until temperatures cool down.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do my young garden egg plants look wilted in the morning even when the soil feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo leebi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil often means the plant roots are suffering from fungal rot due to poor drainage or excess water, which prevents the roots from drawing up moisture properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miipiŋ yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela he yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo nu ni fa babaoo hewɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbala nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant plantains or cassava alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains loo cassava yɛ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn under direct sunlight, so fast-growing plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in a single row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?
