english: If maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stalks that produce small or incomplete cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa dumɔwui bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather conditions are too hot, when water supply is irregular, or when there are not enough insect pollinators around to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni ŋmeii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ faaa

english: Why are there suddenly many small holes appearing in the leaves of my cabbage crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii babaoo miije kpo trukaa yɛ mi-cabbage lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by pests like diamondback moth caterpillars that hatch on the underside of the leaves and feed on the leafy tissue.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ diamondback caterpillars ni fɔɔ yɛ baa lɛ shishi ni amɛyeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ.

english: How do chemical sprays stop pests from coming onto my farm?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote miŋmɔ lɛ mli aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Chemical sprays act like a protective shield around your crops. They either repel pests with strong odors or kill harmful insects on contact before they can settle and damage your plants.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ onibii ahe. Amɛshwieɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ loo amɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛji amɛkpe dani amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfiteɔ otsei lɛ.

english: If my neighbor sprays chemicals on their farm, can those chemicals travel across to harm my crops?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ shwie tsofai yɛ amɛŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Ani nakai tsofai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli ni amɛye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, chemical drift can happen when the wind carries light spray droplets onto nearby fields. To prevent this, farmers should avoid spraying on windy days and keep a safe distance from other crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aba kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔi kɛ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tee ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ enɛ naa lɛ Esa akɛ Okwaafoi lɛ akpa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ anɔ. ni okwɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe.

english: How long do pest chemicals stay active in the soil after I spray my field?
ga: Be enyiɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikɛshwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: Different chemicals stay in the soil for different lengths of time. Some break down in a few days with sunlight and rain, while strong ones linger for weeks. Always check the label so you know when it is safe to plant.
ga: Tsofai srɔtoi hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bei srɔtoi. Hulu kɛ nugbɔ fiteɔ kooloi srɔtoi komɛi ahiɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii komɛi ni wa lɛ hiɔ shi otsii babaoo. Kwɛmɔ nɔ ni aŋma yɛ nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be koni ole be ni sa akɛ adu.

english: Will strong pest chemicals burn or kill my young seeds if they touch them directly?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mli wa lɛ baashã loo ebaagbe midumɔwui bibii lɛ kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, applying concentrated chemicals directly onto seeds or young shoots can burn them and stop growth. You must always mix chemicals with the correct amount of water and apply them properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã amɛ ni ekpa amɛdalɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tsofai ni sa lɛ afutu nu mli be fɛɛ be ni okɛwo ohe jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I water my seeds immediately after I finish planting them in the ground?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo midumɔwui lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, watering right after planting softens the seed coat and settles the soil tightly around the seed. This provides the moisture needed for the seed to germinate and start growing roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu lɛ he tsɔne lɛ afee blɛoo, ni ebaaha sũ ni bɔle dumɔwu lɛ he lɛ mli awa. Enɛ baaha nu ni he hia koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛje shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aha.

english: Why do extension officers advise us to space crops neatly instead of planting randomly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa moŋ fe ni aaadu amɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Planting in straight, well-spaced rows ensures every single plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja, ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell if I am giving my young crops too much water or not enough?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo miiha mitsei bibii lɛ loo mihaaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If crops do not get enough water, their leaves wilt and turn dry. If they receive too much water, the leaves turn yellow and the roots rot because soggy soil prevents them from breathing.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ baagbi ni ebaagbi. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa amɛmuɔ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer in the soil at the same time I plant, or wait until after the crop comes up?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be kome too mli ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ loo mamɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: It is usually best to wait until the plant sprouts and forms basic roots before applying main fertilizers. If applied too early, the seed cannot use it and heavy rain might wash the nutrients away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni tso lɛ akwɛ̃ ni efee shishijee shishifãi dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ awo mli. Kɛ akɛtsu nii oya tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know when my crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn pale green or yellow, their stems remain thin, and growth stalls. Healthy, well-nourished plants display dark green, broad leaves.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tso lɛ mli etse lolo. ni dalɛ kpaa Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ.

english: Why should I cover my fertilizer with soil instead of leaving it on top of dry ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sũ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture from the soil to dissolve so root systems can absorb it. Leaving fertilizer uncovered on hot, dry ground causes the sun to destroy its nutrients and rain to wash it away.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni nugbɔ hu nɛɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop their leaves during dry spells to save water and protect themselves from heat. Once the rains return, the plant will grow fresh green leaves and continue developing its roots beneath the soil.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are small worms eating the tender leaves in the center of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets young corn in Ghana. They hide in the central whorl of the plant to feed, but early treatment with recommended organic or chemical sprays can eliminate them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Shi atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii mra. Abaanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shihilɛ mli dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is weak and needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu nii?

english: If your previous crop leaves turned pale green or yellow early, or if stems were thin and yields were small, your soil lacks nutrients. Mixing well-rotted cow or poultry manure into the soil restores its nutrients naturally.
ga: Kɛji tso ni eho lɛ baai lɛ batsɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ oya, loo kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsina loo kooloi ashishifã ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfutu sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves get dark spots and look burnt after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This burning look is caused by fungal diseases like leaf blight, which spread quickly in hot, damp weather when rain splashes soil onto leaves. Spacing plants further apart and trimming lower leaves stops water from sitting on the plant and reduces disease.
ga: Nɛkɛ shãa henumɔ nɛɛ jɛ fungal hela ko, tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ fɛ̃i mli kɛji nugbɔ shwie sũ nɔ baa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni afo shishigbɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu akakpɛtɛ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebaaha helai aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to plant my maize immediately after the first major rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Maize needs consistent moisture during its early weeks to grow strong roots and tall stalks. Planting early allows the crops to use all the rainfall of the major season before the short dry spell sets in.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli be fɛɛ be yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ afee shiŋŋ ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akwɛ Dumɔ kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ be lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔi ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku lɛ baa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of soil moisture. Watering your plants consistently and placing dry grass around their roots helps keep the soil cool so flowers can form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Ha tsei lɛ nu daa ni okɛ jwɛi awo amɛhe. Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he sũ? Akɛ jwɛi loo kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, grass, or cocoa husks acts as a shield against the sun. This practice, called mulching, keeps moisture in the soil longer and prevents weeds from taking over your plot.
ga: Ni akɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi, loo kookoo ŋmɔji shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that get scorched by strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantain alongside young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that protect the tender cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa ni buɔ kookoo ni mli tse lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa waa.

english: How do I know that my yams are ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yams indicate maturity when their green leaves and vines dry up and turn yellow naturally. This shows the plant has finished transferring its energy down into swelling the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ egbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ etee shi ni eha ŋmeii lɛ egbɔjɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops even when water is scarce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu faaa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems that are built to steal small amounts of food and water from the soil quickly. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ama amɛ koni amɛju niyenii kɛ nu fioo komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya fe jwɛi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees need a different kind of fertilizer compared to my maize or vegetable crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi kɛ akɛto mi-ŋmãa loo aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees are long-term woody crops that need specific nutrients like phosphorus and potassium to form healthy pods, whereas short-term crops like maize need high nitrogen for fast leaf growth. Cocoa fertilizer is specially mixed to suit the specific dietary needs of cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium, koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ ŋmãa biɔ nitrogen babaoo koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Akɛ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii futuɔ mli krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni kookoo tso lɛ he hiaa lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Can I use one type of fertilizer for all the different crops on my farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi?

english: While a general fertilizer can help many crops, different plants require different balances of nutrients at various stages of growth. Using specialized crop fertilizers ensures that crops like cocoa get the exact nutrients required for maximum yield.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo moŋ, shi tso fɛɛ tso he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ edalɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Tsei amli ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei tamɔ kookoo lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I know if my crops are starving for nutrients or if they are just dry from lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo amɛmiigbi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Plants lacking water will droop and wilt during the heat of the day but usually recover at night. Plants lacking nutrients will show persistent leaf yellowing, weak stems, or stunted growth even when the soil has adequate moisture.
ga: Tsei ni bɛ nu lɛ baagboi yɛ gbi lɛ mli latsaa be mli. Shi bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ. Tsei ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli lɛ baaná baai ni baafee ŋmɔŋ daa, amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, loo amɛdalɛ ehiii kwraa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa po.

english: Why do some fertilizers make my crop leaves grow very big but produce very few fruits or pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii loo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers high in nitrogen encourage heavy leaf and stem growth. If a plant gets too much nitrogen without enough phosphorus or potassium, it spends all its energy making green leaves instead of developing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ haa baai kɛ tsei lɛ daraa waa. Kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. When the soil runs out of these food elements, the plant cannot make green leaf material, causing leaves to turn pale or yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ ba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli nibii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer in the soil before planting or after the crops have sprouted?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani adu loo beni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ?

english: Applying a base fertilizer at planting gives young seedlings early root strength, while applying top-dressing fertilizer after sprouting gives the growing crop an extra boost when it is actively forming leaves, flowers, or fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni aduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi atadewoo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ewo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa tso ni miida lɛ hewalɛ kroko beni ewoɔ baai, fɔfɔii loo aduawai lɛ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the roots instead of dumping it right against the plant stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni mikɛaawo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Roots are the parts of the plant designed to drink in food and water. Placing fertilizer near the root zone lets the plant absorb nutrients safely, whereas placing concentrated fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant.
ga: Shishifã lɛ ji tso lɛ fã ni afee koni enu niyenii kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ ashã.

english: What happens to my cocoa pods if the tree does not get enough food from the soil?
ga: Mɛni baa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Without enough soil nutrients, cocoa trees will produce smaller pods, drop young pods prematurely, and become weak, making them easy targets for pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Pods bibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: How does using proper fertilizer help my crops survive hard weather or dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mikɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ fɔŋ loo hɔmɔ mli?

english: Balanced plant food helps crops build deep, strong root systems and sturdy branches. Healthy plants with strong roots can reach deeper soil moisture and withstand harsh weather much better than weak plants.
ga: Tso niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa, kɛ niji ni mli wa. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shishifãi lɛ wa lɛ baanyɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli kwɔ lɛ, ni amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time of the year to apply food to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli ni mikɛbaahã mi-cacao tsei lɛ niyenii?

english: The best time to feed cocoa trees is usually at the start of the rainy seasons when the soil is moist. The moisture helps dissolve the fertilizer so the active roots can easily drink in the nutrients to prepare for flowering and pod growth.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aha kookoo tsei niyenii ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni tsuɔ nii lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo yɛ hesaa kɛha fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which direction to stick cassava cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole gbɛ ni esa akɛ okɛ o-cassava lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ oodu?

english: You must check the small nodes where leaves used to grow; those nodes should point upwards toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the roots and leaves will struggle to grow, leading to very weak plants or no crop yield at all.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ nodes bibii lɛ amli. Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nakai nodes lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ shi lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ baaná naagba akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ waa loo amɛwooo nɔ ko kwraa.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and weak when I put many seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mibua dumɔwui babaoo anaa yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you plant too many seeds in one spot, the growing roots fight each other for the small amount of water, sunlight, and food in that specific soil patch. Spacing them out allows each maize plant to feed well and grow thick, strong stalks with large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome Shishifãi ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. He ni akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa yeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa ni ŋmeii wuji yɔɔ mli.

english: Yam vines naturally like to climb high to catch maximum sunlight with their leaves. Keeping the leaves off the damp wet ground prevents leaf diseases and allows the plant to send more energy down to build big tubers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɔ kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo kɛjɛ amɛbaa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ baai ahe helai anaa, ni ehaa tso lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the cool shade and moist air they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings dry out and die shortly after transplanting them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience shock when moved from a shaded nursery directly into hot direct sunshine. Transplanting them late in the afternoon or on a cloudy day gives their weak roots time to adjust to the new soil overnight without losing moisture to the sun.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ ahe feɔ amɛ yaa kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ adu shi yɛ shwane mli loo yɛ gbi ni atatu yɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛ amɛhe aaawo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu la lɛ haaa amɛná ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating out the middle funnel parts of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ fã lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides deep inside the leaf funnel where it is dark and safe to eat the newest leaves. Catching them early with appropriate treatments stops them from destroying the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe teeɔ baai ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ, ni amɛhe yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra kɛ tsamɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by a virus they spread. As the insects suck out the plant sap, the leaf deforms and stops growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ kooloi bibii miinu tso mli nu lɛ Baai lɛ baafite ni amɛbaakpa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow plenty of bright yellow flowers, but the flowers just drop off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when there are no small insects around to shake the pollen inside the flower. Excessive nitrogen fertilizer can also make the plant focus only on growing green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii komɛi bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ. Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ hu baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai eŋɔli ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small sucker shoots growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and nutrients from the main stem. Removing all but two or three healthy suckers ensures the main tree produces a heavy, full bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ, Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa ŋmeii babaoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow even though there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni nu babaoo yɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green. Too much standing water can also drown the roots so they cannot breathe or take up nutrients, causing the leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛsu eŋɔli lɛ mli Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Young cocoa seedlings get scorched easily by the harsh sun. Plantains grow quickly and provide wide shade leaves that shield the young cocoa plants and keep the soil moist during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ehaa hulutsoo baai ni mli kwɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close together in the farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. This causes the plants to grow tall and thin with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing in the middle of maize leaves usually means your soil is low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli ŋmɔŋ tsɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛtsakeɔ kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand easily. If the soil is hard or compacted, the tubers struggle to penetrate downward, causing them to stay small and bend in odd directions.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa loo ebɔle ehe lɛ Ebaawa akɛ yitso lɛ baabote mli. Ha efee bibioo ni obɔle hei srɔtoi.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and showing light green patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties helps prevent this problem.
ga: Baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii. Eji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: What causes black, watery spots on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii diji kɛ nu ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmeii anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ baa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, cool conditions. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets light in and stops moisture from building up around the pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofo tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni la abote mli ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua ehe naa yɛ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from extreme heat or lack of water. Giving your plants steady moisture during hot weather stops the flowers from falling off early.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fũu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite mra.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitswa dani ebatsɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when they absorb too much water very quickly after a long dry period. The skin cannot stretch fast enough to hold the rapid growth, so keeping soil moisture even with regular watering prevents cracking.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛ́ eŋɔ nu babaoo oya beni aŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Hewolo lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ ehe oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛya nɔ eda oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nu haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa po lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ripe enough to dig up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ egbɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafo?

english: Groundnuts are ready to harvest when the leaves turn yellow and begin to dry up, and the inside walls of the pods turn dark brown when you crack them open to check.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔ. Ni pod lɛ mli gbogboi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ ogbele mli koni okwɛ mli.

english: Why are my harvested maize grains rotting even after I put them inside bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Grains rot inside bags if they still contain moisture when packed. Sun-drying the maize thoroughly until the grains are hard and crack cleanly between your teeth stops mold from growing.
ga: Ŋmãa fiteɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛ́ awo mli. Abɛi ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbalaɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture around their shallow roots. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow bigger.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ daa.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I prune the extra branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifo niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ kookoo tso ko nɔ?

english: Pruning removes weak or overcrowded branches so the tree can send its food directly to growing pods. It also lets in air and light, which reduces pests and helps the tree produce more healthy cocoa.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ niyenii amaje tsei niji ni miida lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Eha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la hu tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ kookoo ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers when they are stressed by lack of water, low soil food, or extreme heat. Maintaining soil moisture and keeping shade trees helps the plant retain more flowers to form pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi titri lɛ kɛ́ nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ tso lɛ ni ahiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ haa tso lɛ buaa fɔfɔi babaoo anaa koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads very fast in cool, wet weather. Removing affected pods quickly and trimming branches to let sunlight dry the tree helps stop the rot from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya ni afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la lɛ aha tso lɛ agbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ.

english: Why are small bugs causing the young shoots on my cocoa trees to wither and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: These bugs, commonly called mirids or capsids, suck sap from young shoots and pods, causing leaves to fall and branches to die back. Regular monitoring and applying recommended treatments during peak bug seasons stops the destruction.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ, ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ mirids loo capsids lɛ, nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ. Ehaa baai shwieɔ shi ni niji gboiɔ. Nibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsofafeemɔi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ hela lɛ fa babaoo lɛ baaha hiɛkpatamɔ lɛ akpa.

english: How do I know if my soil needs extra plant food or fertilizer to help my crops grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: If your crop leaves turn pale yellow, grow slowly, or produce smaller fruits than expected, your soil is running low on essential nutrients. Adding compost or proper fertilizer restores the soil food your crops need.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛdara blɛoo, loo amɛwo yibii bibii fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much even when I clear around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Keeping the area around your plant roots clear ensures your crops get all the nutrients they need to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tse shishifãi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How does covering the ground with dry leaves help my crops during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves, called mulching, locks moisture into the soil and keeps plant roots cool. It stops the dry harmattan winds from drying out the earth and breaks down into natural plant food over time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ebaatsi harmatta kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. ni efiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni etsɔɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Yes, planting cassava and maize together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the space open for cassava to grow bigger later without competing for space.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi he ko koni ŋmei lɛ adara babaoo sɛɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ he ko akaŋ.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod is completely ripe and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ makpa?

english: A cocoa pod is ready to harvest when its skin color changes fully from green to yellow, or from red to bright orange. Harvesting at full color ensures the seeds inside have proper quality for processing.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛhewolo lɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo kɛjɛ etsuru kɛtee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Nikpamɔ ni yɔɔ sui fɛɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha nitsumɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight damages their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or cassava next to them provides living shade and keeps the soil moist while the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fiteɔ baai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra shoots and dead branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛniji ni egboi lɛ?

english: Removing dead branches and extra shoots (suckers) stops the tree from wasting food on parts that do not produce cocoa. It also opens up the branches so air and sunlight can pass through, which prevents moisture buildup that causes black pod disease.
ga: Niji ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine (ŋmeii) ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ hei ni kookoo baaa lɛ. Egbeleɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ hu koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni buaa ehe naa ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the tip and moving down the middle in a V-shape usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green again so the plant can form full cobs.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ ni amɛyaa shi kɛyaa teŋgbɛ yɛ V su mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why should I plant legumes like groundnuts or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. When grown alongside maize, they naturally fertilize the soil, helping the maize grow stronger while giving you a second crop from the same field.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaafee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa ŋmãa ni ji enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baa.

english: What causes small holes in my cassava leaves and will it reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmei baai anɔ Ni ani ebaaha mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi?

english: Holes in leaves are caused by insects like grasshoppers or beetles feeding on the plant. Leaves are how the plant produces food, so damaged leaves mean the cassava cannot produce big, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Koolooi tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu yɛ baai lɛ amli. Baai ji bɔ ni tsei feɔ niyenii. Baai ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmei lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep roots that absorb water and nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing food and water from your young crops during critical growth periods.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Planting cassava stems too close makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin and tall with small, thin roots instead of thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ daa mlɛo ni ekwɛɔ, ni eyɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ bulbs ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged by insects, kept in damp storage, or collected from hybrid varieties that do not reproduce well. Storing dried seeds in airtight containers keeps them healthy for the next planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji kooloi fite amɛ. Okɛto he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. aloo ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni wooo jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli Dumɔwui ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before making fruits during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers during high heat and dry conditions to save energy and water. Providing consistent water around the roots and mulching the soil keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Nu ni akɛhaa Shishifãi lɛ ahe daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is suitable for planting yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: Yams need deep, loose, soft soil that drains water easily so the tubers can push deep into the ground without rotting. Heavy clay soil that traps water or shallow rocky ground makes it hard for yam tubers to expand.
ga: Sweet potatoes hia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ oya. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛgbooo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni hiɛɔ nu loo tɛi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Officer, why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or compost gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do you advise me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ owoɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every year drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground, making your yields smaller each time.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ baa shi be fɛɛ be.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my seeds when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until the rain falls heavily enough to soak the soil deep down for two or three days in a row. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry up if the rain stops for a week.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ waa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ awo mli jogbaŋŋ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsi kome.

english: Why do my crops look weak and sickly after very heavy rainfall when plants are supposed to need water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Mɛɛ be nu he hiaa tsei?

english: Excessive rain fills up all the tiny air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots because they cannot breathe. It also washes away good soil nutrients and spreads fungal diseases through muddy water splashes.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ hu, ni egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu ni mli ewo muji ni ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves to suck the plant's juice, or by a virus these insects spread while feeding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi koni amɛnu tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ amli

english: Why do weeds always grow so much faster than my planted crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya be fɛɛ be fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep root systems already adapted to the local soil. They are faster at grabbing water and nutrients than crop seeds, which need more time to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni etsɔ ehe kɛtee he ni eyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ mli oya fe dumɔwui, ni heɔ be babaoo dani amɛtswaa shi lɛ.

english: Why do you recommend that I plant plantains in the field alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ mli lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and get scorched by direct hot sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act like large umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa with shade while keeping the soil cool.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Ekɛ hulutsoo buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of pollination. Keeping the soil moist during hot days helps the plant hold onto its blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo pollination ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn hard and woody if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava plants get older or go through long dry seasons, they convert the soft starch in their tubers into tough, fibrous wood to survive, making the roots hard to cook and eat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ dara loo amɛtsɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, Amɛtsakeɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ mli ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmei koni amɛhi shi. Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaahoo shishifãi lɛ ni aye.

english: What causes my yam tubers to split open or grow into bent shapes underwater?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa loo amɛdaraa yɛ nu shishi?

english: Yams split or grow misshapen when the soil is too hard and stony for the tuber to expand smoothly, or when a long dry period is suddenly followed by heavy soaking rains.
ga: Sweet potatoes mli gbalaa loo efiteɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ tɛi ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ. aloo beni egbi trukaa be kakadaŋŋ Nugbɔ ni naa wa nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, an essential nutrient. As the maize plant grows, it moves available nitrogen to the top leaves to support new growth, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmãa tsei lɛ dara Ekɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ yaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eye ebua dalɛ hee. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I plant them in an open field without tall plants nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to high heat and direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them creates living shade that protects the young leaves from scorching and helps soil retain moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he lɛ baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why does cassava spoil so quickly within a few days after I harvest it from the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once cassava roots are separated from the plant, they react rapidly with oxygen in the air. This triggers a natural decay process called post-harvest physiological deterioration, causing dark discoloration and rotting within two to three days.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmei shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ baa. Enɛ haa ehiɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli.

english: Why are the blossoms dropping off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather becomes too hot or when water supply is inconsistent. High heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to preserve moisture and survival instead of producing fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ kɛ wala he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my harvested seed yams refuse to sprout for several months even if I store them in a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ ekpoo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ nyɔji babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Yams go through a natural rest period known as dormancy right after harvest. This internal biological process prevents the tuber from sprouting during the dry season so it survives until favorable rainy conditions return.
ga: Sweet potatoes yɛ adebɔɔ mli hejɔɔmɔ be ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Nɛkɛ wala yibii ni yɔɔ mli nɛɛ tsiɔ bulb lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ ebaanyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ aba.

english: Heavy rainfall causes surface runoff that washes away the fertilizer before plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is already moist or during light rain ensures the nutrients soak into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii abote shishifã lɛ he.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking sap from young leaves. This feeding damages plant cells as they expand, making the leaves curl and distort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Niyenii nɛɛ fiteɔ tsei amli wala yibii lɛ beni amɛmli shwereɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does my maize yield get smaller every year if I plant it on the exact same piece of land continuously?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil while allowing crop-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas helps replenish soil nitrogen and break pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa sũ mli nitrogen lɛ yaa hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunches grow large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi beni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy stems. As the fruit bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to uproot it unless it is supported with sturdy wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tso ni mli wa. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baajie amɛ. ja akɛ tsei ni mli wa tsu nii

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my newly planted crops as soon as the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu ehee lɛ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to survive in soil for long periods and germinate rapidly with the first rainfall. Because wild weeds are naturally hardier than cultivated crop seedlings, they quickly steal sunlight, water, and nutrients unless cleared early.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, koo mli jwɛi ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ wa fe dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. ja ajie kɛjɛ mli oya.

english: Why is it bad to leave my rice seedlings in the nursery for too long before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaashi ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani ajie amɛ kɛya ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving rice seedlings in the nursery for too long damages their roots during uprooting and stunts their growth in the main field, making it hard for them to recover and yield well.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛduɔ shishi lɛ. kɛ shweremɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaaku sɛɛ aba ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai aba.

english: How do I know the right age to transplant my rice seedlings from the nursery to my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male afii ni sa ni esa akɛ adu kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe lɛ kɛya mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Rice seedlings are best transplanted when they are young, usually between 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting (when they have 3 to 4 leaves). Planting them at this young stage helps them root quickly and grow strong.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui beni amɛji bibii. Bei pii lɛ, yɛ otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ teŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ (be mli ni amɛyɛ baai 3 kɛyashi 4 lɛ), kɛ́ adu amɛ bibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: What happens to my rice crop if I wait up to two months before uprooting and planting it?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mimɛ nyɔji enyɔ dani mijie amɛshishi ni midu?

english: Waiting up to two months makes the seedlings old and woody. When you uproot old plants, you break mature roots, severe shock occurs, and the plants produce very few tillers, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛmɛɛ kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ tsei. Kɛji ojie tsei momo lɛ Shishifãi ni eda lɛ baafo. Yiwalɛ gbee ko ba. ni tso lɛ baawo ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do my rice plants look weak and yellow for a few days right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ gbii fioo komɛi beni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: This is called transplanting shock. When you uproot seedlings, tiny root hairs get damaged, so the plant briefly stops taking up water. Young seedlings recover from this shock much faster than older ones.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ he shoofeemɔ. Kɛ́ ojie dumɔwui lɛ, shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi bibii lɛ fiteɔ, no hewɔ lɛ tso lɛ baanyɛ akpa nu ni eŋɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko. Dumɔwui bibii lɛ he waaa kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ shoofeemɔ nɛɛ mli oya fe tsei bibii.

english: How does moving young rice plants early help them produce more grain?
ga: Tsei bibii ni ajieɔ amɛ mra Te aaafee tɛŋŋ aye abua ŋmãa tsei ni amɛwo dumɔwui babaoo?

english: Young seedlings adapt faster to the field and produce many side branches called tillers. Each healthy tiller develops a head of rice, so more tillers mean a larger yield.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ tsakeɔ ehe oya kɛyaa ŋmɔ mli ni ewoɔ niji babaoo ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Tiller fɛɛ tiller ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa yitsei babaoo, no hewɔ lɛ tillers babaoo tsɔɔ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Is it better to plant rice seeds directly on my land or raise them in a nursery bed first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo madu amɛ yɛ dumɔwui atoohe klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Starting rice in a nursery bed allows you to protect young shoots from pests and weeds, and transplanting the strongest young seedlings gives you a more uniform and productive field than direct seeding.
ga: Kɛ́ obɔi ŋmãa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ jwɛi ahe. Ni dumɔwui bibii ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná he ko ni oduɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni woɔ yibii fe dumɔwui ni ooodu tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Does uprooting rice seedlings hurt them more than just leaving them where they sprouted?
ga: Ani ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ awui fe dumɔwui lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ he ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Uprooting causes mild temporary shock, but moving seedlings from a crowded nursery to open land gives each plant enough space, light, and nutrients to grow much larger than if left un-transplanted.
ga: Shishijee ni ajieɔ lɛ kɛ be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ fioo baa. Shi dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei akwɛmɔhe ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ agbo kwraa fe kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni aduuu lɛ.

english: Can I uproot my rice seedlings today and wait until tomorrow to plant them on my main field?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafo ŋmãa dumɔwui ŋmɛnɛ ni mamɛ kɛyashi wɔ koni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant seedlings on the same day they are uprooted. Leaving uprooted seedlings exposed dries out their roots, causing high mortality and slow establishment.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu dumɔwui yɛ gbi ni ajie amɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi dumɔwui ni ajie lɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa gbele ni fa babaoo kɛ shishitoo ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo baa.

english: How should I prepare my field bed so newly uprooted rice seedlings take root easily?
ga: Te esa akɛ asaa ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe aha tɛŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa tsei heei ni ajie kɛjɛ amɛshishi lɛ anyɛ ajie kɛjɛ amɛshishi oya?

english: Your field should be thoroughly plowed, leveled, and kept muddy or soft. Soft soil allows the delicate roots of young seedlings to anchor quickly without breaking during planting.
ga: Esa akɛ atsu oŋmɔ lɛ he nii, afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni aha efee muji loo efee bɔdɔɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mɔ̃ɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛkuuu yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Does delaying the transplanting of my rice seedlings change when my crop will be ready for harvest?
ga: Ani mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛwoɔ he kroko lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii lɛ baatsake beni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, delaying transplanting slows down the plant's natural growth cycle in the main field, which reduces the crop's growing period and leads to underdeveloped grains at harvest time.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ atsake tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ be lɛ feɔ kuku, ni ehaa dumɔwui ni edako jogbaŋŋ baa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How can I tell if a wild herb growing on my farm is safe for medicinal use or if it is poisonous?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji koo mli tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha tsofafeemɔ loo amɛhe yɛ gbeyei?

english: Not all wild plants are safe for consumption. Safe medicinal plants can be identified by specific physical traits like leaf shape, flower color, and smell. Always confirm with an agricultural extension officer or a trusted community elder before harvesting or using unknown plants.
ga: Koo mli tsei komɛi bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyenii. Abaanyɛ ayɔse tsofa tsei ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛtsɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ su pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ baa su, fɔfɔi su, kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ loo akutsoŋ onukpa ko ni okɛ ohe fɔ̃ɔ enɔ lɛ ama nɔ mi dani okpa tso ko ni aleee loo okɛtsu nii.

english: Is it true that cassava can become poisonous if I harvest and prepare it incorrectly?
ga: Ani ŋmei baanyɛ afee poison diɛŋtsɛ kɛji mikpa ni misaa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ?

english: Yes, raw cassava roots contain natural compounds that can release cyanide. Soaking, fermenting, or thoroughly boiling cassava breaks down these natural toxins, making the food safe and nutritious to eat.
ga: Hɛɛ, adebɔɔ mli nibii ni baanyɛ ajie cyanide yɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni ahoko lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ cassava wo nu mli, afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ashã lɛ, efiteɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai fɔji nɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa niyenii feɔ shweshweeshwe ni ehaa mɔ he waa ni ayeɔ.

english: Can I grow local medicinal herbs in the same field as my maize and cassava crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu maŋ lɛ mli tsofai yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, many traditional herbs like Neem or Moringa can be intercropped with food crops. Certain herbs even act as natural pest deterrents, helping protect your main food crops while providing valuable medicinal harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ adu blema tsofai babaoo tamɔ neem loo moringa ni akɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Tsofai komɛi hu tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Ebuɔ oniyenii ni okɛtsuɔ nii titri lɛ ahe, ni ekɛ tsofai ni jara wa hu haa.

english: Will spraying synthetic pesticides on my food crops make the traditional herbs growing nearby unsafe to use?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛfee nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni mikɛshwieɔ miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baaha blema tsofai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, chemical sprays can drift onto nearby plants and soak into the soil, leaving toxic residues on wild herbs. It is best to leave dedicated herbal areas untreated or use natural, organic pest control methods.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni ashiɔ yɛ koo mli tsofai anɔ lɛ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni atsako amɛhe loo akɛ adebɔɔ mli, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛgbeɔ tsofai fɔji lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why do my local medicinal shrubs lose all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tso ni yɔɔ mimaŋ lɛ mli lɛ baai fɛɛ fite yɛ harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves during the dry season is a natural survival mechanism called dormancy. Plants shed leaves to conserve water and protect themselves from dry winds, and they will sprout fresh leaves once the rainy season begins.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala shihilɛ gbɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dormancy. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he. ni ebaatswa baai heei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli

english: Why do shade trees on my farm help delicate herbal plants survive the heat better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ dɔlɛ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Shade trees reduce soil temperature, block harsh direct sunlight, and drop leaves that decompose into natural mulch. This creates a moist, cool microclimate that allows sensitive plants to thrive.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i baa shi. Tsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ni oha baai ni fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: How can I use local Ghanaian plants to protect my stored grains from insects without using chemical poisons?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ Ghana tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ atsu nii kɛbu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni mikɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei tsuuu nii?

english: Drying and crushing leaves from plants like Neem or mixing hot pepper powder into stored grains acts as a natural insect repellent. The strong natural scent drives pests away without contaminating the food.
ga: Baai ni agbiɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei tamɔ neem mli loo ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ futuɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni gbeɔ kooloi. Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa lɛ shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ niyenii lɛ ni efiteee niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my vegetable plants turn yellow even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil is waterlogged and preventing the roots from breathing. Adding well-rotted manure or organic compost usually helps leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do wild herbal plants grow easily in the forest, but seeds I collect from them fail to sprout on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofafeemɔ tsei ni yɔɔ koo mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ koo lɛ mli mlɛo nɛkɛ? Shi dumɔwui ni mibua naa kɛjɛɔ amɛdɛŋ lɛ kwɛɛɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Wild plant seeds often have tough outer coats that require specific forest conditions to break dormancy. Gently scratching the seed coat or soaking the seeds in clean water overnight before planting helps them germinate easily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koo mli dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ko ni wa ni biɔ koo mli shihilɛi pɔtɛɛ komɛi koni ekɛfo wɔɔhe mli. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ atsu nii blɛoo. Aloo okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome dani odu koni eye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya.

english: How can I make sure the herbs I harvest on my farm stay clean and safe for sale at the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai ni mikpaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe tse ni ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvest herbs when they are fully mature, dry them on clean elevated mats rather than directly on the bare ground to avoid contamination, and store them in clean, dry sacks away from moisture and direct sunlight.
ga: Kpaa tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ kɛji amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Gbimɔ yɛ tsɔne ni awo nɔ ni he tse nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni akafite lɛ. ni okɛto kotoku ni mli tse ni egbi mli. Ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Is there a way I can make crops like plantain or cassava yield faster instead of waiting for 18 months?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maná tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni amɛwo yibii oya moŋ fe ni mamɛ nyɔji 18?

english: Yes, you can shorten the growth period by using improved, early-maturing seed varieties, applying fertilizer at the right stages, and keeping the field free of weeds so the plants grow without stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oha dalɛ be lɛ afee kuku kɛtsɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ, ni shwereɔ mra lɛ ni oookɛtsu nii lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ he ni sa. Ni ha jwɛi akafee he ni yɔɔ lɛ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: How do I know when my plantains are fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni dumɔwui lɛ eshɛ ni abaakpa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the fingers look full and round, the flower at the end of the bunch has dried up, and the upper leaves start turning yellow.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji niji lɛ kwɛ he fɛɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi akuu lɛ naagbee lɛ egbi. ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do other farmers tell me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi Ni amɛkɛɛ mi akɛ madu plantains yɛ mimasɛi Mikoo tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees with shade and keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ekɛ hulutsoo buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is it harmful if I plant my crops too close to one another in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which makes them grow thin and produce smaller harvests.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil. Planting leguminous crops like beans or groundnuts helps trap nitrogen from the air back into the soil, naturally fertilizing your land for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Do my crops need food and fertilizer continuously throughout their entire life in the soil?
ga: Ani niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops need nutrients most urgently during their early growth and flowering stages; feeding them proper manure or fertilizer during these critical times ensures strong roots and heavy fruits.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia tsei oya fe fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa kɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ. Niyenii ni sa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ yɛ nɛkɛ bei ni mli wa nɛɛ amli lɛ haa shishifãi ni wa kɛ yibii ni tsii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away even when my main crops are already bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ da fe jwɛi lɛ momo lɛ?

english: Even small weeds constantly steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients away from your crops underneath the soil, which reduces your final harvest size.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po miiju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be fɛɛ be. Enɛ baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why should I loosen the soil deeply before planting root crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmeii?

english: Loosening the soil allows young plant roots to spread easily, reach deeper water reserves during dry spells, and grow bigger roots or tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo. Nu jɛɛhei ni mli kwɔ ni anyɛɔ ashɛɔ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ kɛ shishifãi loo bulbs lɛ baatsɔ wuji.

english: How often should I water my crops if the rain stops unexpectedly during the growing season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mitsei lɛ nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa trukaa yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: During dry spells, crops need deep watering at least twice a week, especially when they are flowering or forming fruits, to prevent the blossoms and young fruits from dropping off.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu ni mli kwɔ shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ eewo fɔfɔi loo ewo yibii. Koni fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable plants turning yellow and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Yellow, curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insect pests are sucking the juice out of the leaves or that the soil is running low on essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahe okadi. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai amli Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ faaa.

english: Why should I plow my farm before planting my crops instead of just clearing the bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ fe ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ amli kɛkɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard soil so roots can grow deeper, buries weeds so they rot into natural fertilizer, and allows rainwater to sink easily into the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Fu jwɛi lɛ koni amɛgboi akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eha nugbɔ nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo

english: How can I easily tell if my farm soil is good enough to grow healthy crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Healthy farm soil is usually dark in color, holds moisture without becoming swampy, crumbles easily in your hand, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kpakpai amli lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ bɛ mli. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni egboi ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow when it rains continuously for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Excessive rain fills all the air spaces in the soil, drowning the roots. Without oxygen, roots cannot soak up nutrients like nitrogen, causing the leaves to lose their green color.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ. Shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen, ni no haa baa lɛ su eŋɔli baa shi.

english: Why do my cassava leaves droop down and curl during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants curl and droop their leaves during extreme heat to reduce water loss from evaporation, helping the crop save moisture to survive dry weather.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa koni nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers but no fruits develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms fall off without producing fruit when temperatures get extremely high, when plants lack adequate water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa. Beni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei ahe loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same plot of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously depletes the specific soil nutrients that plant relies on and allows pests and soil diseases targeting that crop to build up over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ ni aaaya nɔ akwɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei lɛ damɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi be fɛɛ be. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni tsɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my farm than the actual crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe tsei diɛŋtsɛ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are hardy wild plants naturally adapted to local conditions, allowing them to steal soil nutrients, sunlight, and water much faster than cultivated farm crops.
