ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks fall over or break easily in the wind before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛkuɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani kpamɔɔ be shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Maize stalks fall over if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium, if roots are shallow from hard soil, or if stem borer insects have weakened the inside of the stalk.
ga: Abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso lɛ mli fã lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How do I know the right time when my maize is fully mature for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Maize is fully mature when the leaves dry out, a small black layer forms at the bottom of the grain where it attaches to the cob, and the grain becomes too hard to dent with your fingernail.
ga: Abele lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi. A maa pee nɔ́ diŋŋ bibioo ko. Ebaa yɛ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shishi he ni ekɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ. Ni ŋmaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ akɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔi baatsɔ mli.

english: Why are small insects multiplying inside my house and destroying the maize I stored?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifa yɛ mishia lɛ mli ni amɛmiifite ŋmãa ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like maize weevils lay hidden eggs in the grain while it is still in the field. When you pack the harvested maize inside warm rooms, those eggs hatch into pests that feed on the stored grains.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmei ŋmei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtee ŋmãa lɛ mli be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ to tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nakai ŋmãa lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a main food plants use to stay green and grow. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do caterpillars come out of the soil to eat my crop leaves at night instead of during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛbaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Pests like armyworms hide in the soil during the day to protect themselves from the hot sun and birds. They come out at night when it is cool to feed on leaves safely.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbi mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ kɛ okpoi ahe. Amɛjeɔ kpo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso koni amɛye baai lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily with each other for water and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots room to expand into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In strong heat, leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can pull up from the ground. The plant wilts temporarily to conserve water and usually recovers by evening.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Tsei baagbi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni bei pii lɛ, amɛhe baajɔ amɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before they turn into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat or irregular watering stresses the plant, causing it to drop its flowers as a survival mechanism to save energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why does my farm produce less yield when I plant cassava on the same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows soil pests to multiply. Rotating with beans or groundnuts restores soil richness.
ga: Nibii komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ayi fa babaoo. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest grow weaker crops than certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ tso ko ni nyɛɔ etswaa hela fe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often mix with weaker plants in the field or carry hidden diseases from the last season. Certified seeds are specially selected and treated to resist pests and grow uniformly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ futuɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ loo helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ amli. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the yam crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe sweet potato tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil food quickly before cultivated crops can establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii oya kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn out watery and soft when cooked instead of dry and firm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ ahoo amɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaagbi ni amɛfee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava becomes watery if it is harvested too soon after heavy rains or if the plant received too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the roots to hold excess water instead of packing in starch.
ga: Cassava baatsɔ nu kɛji akɛ akpa mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: How can I tell if my maize is completely mature and ready to be harvested for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa ni akɛya jara nɔ?

english: Maize is mature when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the silk becomes dark, and a black layer forms at the tip of the kernels where they attach to the cob.
ga: Abɛi kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa kɛ́ kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. Siliki lɛ baafee ediŋŋ. Ni ŋmei diŋŋ ko baafee yɛ dumɔwu ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ naa.

english: Why are my yam vines growing very large leaves, but the tubers underground remain small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into leafy top growth instead of sending food down to build heavy, full tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa yɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee yi mi nɛ tsii nɛ e hyi.

english: What causes my harvested cocoa beans to feel light in weight when dried?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo yibii ni mikpa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo waa kɛ́ egbi?

english: Light cocoa beans usually happen if the trees lack water during pod formation or if the pods are harvested before the seeds have fully developed inside.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii ni mli tse lɛ baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni afeɔ ŋmeii lɛ loo akpaa ŋmeii lɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ etsɔ mli kwraa.

english: Why do my sweet potatoes rot quickly after I harvest them from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes rot easily if their skin gets scraped during harvest or if they are stored in hot, unventilated rooms without being cured in the shade first to heal their skin.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ajie hewolo lɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli ni atsako lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ehewolo lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there is a lack of phosphorus in the soil to support fruiting.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha yibiiwoo

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and spoil fast before I can carry them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛwoɔ jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving harvested plantain bunches under direct sunlight or harvesting them when they are already too mature speeds up the natural ripening process and causes quick spoilage.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi plantains ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo akpa amɛ beni amɛdara tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya, ni ebaaha amɛfite oya.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and slowing down fruit growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiiha aduawai lɛ miida fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on leaf sap, which stunts the plant's ability to produce healthy fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei awo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I keep insects from eating my stored cowpeas and making them lose weight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ni maha amɛhe afee shoo?

english: You can protect stored cowpeas by ensuring they are thoroughly dried before sealing them in airtight bags (hermetic bags), which suffocates any insects trying to feed on them.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ nɔmimaa ni ooona akɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ nɔ. (vacuum bag) ni haa kooloi bibii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye lɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why does my cassava taste bitter if I leave it in the ground for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: As cassava stays in the ground past its ideal harvest time—especially during dry spells—the roots accumulate higher levels of natural defense compounds that make them taste bitter.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be ni sa ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ hoɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ buaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ babaoo anaa. ni haa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why is it important for me to sort through my harvested corn and pick out the bad ones before storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahala mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni majie ŋmãa ni ehiii lɛ dani mikɛto?

english: Sorting removes rotten, insect-damaged, or moldy grains that can quickly spread pests and diseases to healthy corn during storage. Removing bad grains keeps your overall harvest safe and fresh for longer.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ dumɔwui ni efite lɛ. Kplukai ni fiteɔ nii loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baanyɛ agbala helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui oya kɛya ŋmãa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Dumɔwui gbohii ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni onibii fɛɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni efeɔ ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is hand-picking damaged maize kernels out of a pan enough, or do I always need to use chemicals?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni efite ni akɛ niji shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ pan lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa? Aloo ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofai atsu nii be fɛɛ be?

english: Hand-picking damaged kernels is a very effective and safe method for small batches because physically removing infested grains stops pests from multiplying. Chemicals are generally only needed for very large harvests or severe infestations.
ga: Nine ni akɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni efite lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha dumɔwui bibii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ ajie dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ afɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsofai he hiaa kɛha ŋmaakpamɔi wuji waa loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa pɛ.

english: Why should I inspect my corn cobs before shelling them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli dani mafolɔ mli?

english: Inspecting cobs before shelling lets you discard rotten or insect-infested cobs early, which prevents bad kernels from mixing into your clean grain during the shelling process.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani okɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni okɛ ŋmeii ni egbo loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashwie mra. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui gbohii kɛ dumɔwui ni he tse akafutu yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I select the best maize kernels from my harvest to save as seed for next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli koni mikɛto akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Look for large, clean, full kernels taken from the middle of healthy cobs. Avoid any kernels with holes, discoloration, or signs of mold, as undamaged seeds produce stronger seedlings.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii wuji ni he tse, ni eyi obɔ ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ateŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bu, amɛhe su, loo ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni bɛ muji lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: I see tiny insects crawling inside my stored corn grains. Where do these pests come from?
ga: Mina kooloo bibioo ko ni miiho yɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli Nɛgbɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ jɛɔ?

english: These pests, commonly called grain weevils, often lay their eggs inside the corn kernels while the crop is still in the field. After harvest, when conditions warm up, the eggs hatch inside the grain and the insects eat their way out.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ Loo ni afɔɔ amɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ seed moth. Bei pii lɛ, awoɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ lɛ Wɔɔji lɛ fɔɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. ni kooloi bibii lɛ yeɔ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested corn kernels have tiny powder-filled holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ani akɛ powda eyi mli obɔ?

english: Tiny holes mean insects have eaten into the kernel from the inside. The fine powder is pest droppings and chewed grain, which shows that insects were active in the cob before or right after harvest.
ga: Buu bibii tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi eye dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Pauda kpakpa lɛ ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ dumɔwui ni ayeɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani akpaa loo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Will insects inside my stored grain die on their own if I leave the corn alone?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ baagboi kɛji mishi ŋmaa lɛ pɛ?

english: No, storage insects will not die on their own; they will reproduce rapidly and destroy the entire batch. You must actively remove infested kernels or treat the stored grain to stop them.
ga: Dabi, shwiili mli ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbooo. Amɛfɔɔ oya ni amɛfiteɔ kuu muu lɛ fɛɛ. Esa akɛ ojie dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ loo otsa dumɔwui ni ato lɛ koni amɛkpa.

english: How can I tell if my maize is dry enough to shell and store safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mafolɔ ni mikɛto shweshweeshwe?

english: Maize is sufficiently dry when the kernels are hard, shiny, and make a sharp metallic sound when dropped into a metal pan, or when your fingernail cannot easily dent the surface.
ga: Abɛi lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ mli wa, amɛkpɛ, ni amɛfeɔ dade ŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ amɛshwie dade tsɛnsi mli. aloo be mli ni ŋmeii nyɛɛɛ atsɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ mlɛo

english: Why does my maize turn dark or go bad after I put it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ mli edɔ loo efite beni mikɛwo nitoo kotoku mli sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize turns dark or spoils when trapped moisture inside the kernels causes mold to grow. Drying your corn thoroughly in the sun before bagging prevents this spoilage.
ga: Abele lɛ feɔ ediŋ loo egboɔ kɛ́ nu ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ ha ŋmei ba. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli dani awo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite.

english: Is it safe for me to leave my harvested corn sitting in open pans in the yard?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi ŋmãa ni akpa yɛ pan ko ni agbele mli yɛ abɔɔ lɛ mli?

english: Leaving corn in open pans exposes it to moisture from damp night air, rain, and attacks from birds, rats, and insects. It is better to dry the corn properly and move it into clean, sealed storage containers.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa yɛ pan ni agbele mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ gbɛkɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ okpoi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii tutuaa lɛ mli baa. Ehi akɛ oooha ŋmãa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni no sɛɛ lɛ okɛya tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. They need shade trees or plantains nearby to block strong sun rays and keep the moisture in the soil, protecting them until they are strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu he kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow instead of staying healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an important food in the soil. Giving the crop nitrogen fertilizer or manure helps restore its green leaf color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen loo ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ ahe su kɛ amɛdalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on the same field with maize helps the maize grow bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmei lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans gather useful food called nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the nearby maize and makes the soil richer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei buaa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ náa adebɔɔ mli niyenii, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my crops so the heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ̃ tsei lɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is slightly moist, but avoid applying it right before a heavy downpour. Place it close to the plant roots and cover it lightly with soil so the nutrients stay put.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni ooowo dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ he. Okɛma tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ sũ fioo aha nɔ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahi mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground when heavy rain lasts for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the ground with water, air cannot reach the roots. Excess water trapped in the soil leads to rot and allows harmful soil fungi to damage the cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu ni fa fe nine ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa sũ lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small shapes and stopping the plant from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe bibii bibii lɛ? Ni atsĩ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from leaves and spreading plant viruses. Treating these insects early keeps leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tso lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe tsamɔ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are small green caterpillars eating hole patterns inside the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the center leaves of young corn. Checking your farm early and using proper pest treatments or neem oil protects the corn leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni teɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo neem fɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmãa baai ahe.

english: Too many suckers growing from one plantain root share the same food and water, leaving the main stem weak. Removing extra suckers leaves only strong stems that produce big, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain shishifã kome mli lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome. ehaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ni woɔ yibii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruit when the heat gets high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause tomato plants stress, making them shed their flowers to save energy. Keeping soil moist and using mulch around the base helps retain fruit production.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my cassava farm make my cassava roots harvest much smaller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm, stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your cassava needs. Keeping the farm clean lets all nutrients go directly into building large cassava roots.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa o-cassava lɛ. Kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi wuji amamɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just scatter my chemical fertilizer across the whole field instead of placing it right by each plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛwo tso fɛɛ tso nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Scattering fertilizer across the open field wastes money because rain washes much of it away and weeds eat the rest before your crops can reach it. Placing a measured amount near the roots ensures only your crops absorb the food directly.
ga: Shika ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔji ni mli tse lɛ amli lɛ heɔ shika ejaakɛ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛyaa ni jwɛi yeɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shɛɔ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni asusu he lɛ ma shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha onibii pɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: If I add double the recommended amount of fertilizer to my crops, will they grow twice as fast?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ toi enyɔ fata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ, Ani ebaada oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shii enyɔ?

english: No, giving too much fertilizer can burn the roots of your crops and pull water out of them. Excess fertilizer damages the plant, turning leaves brown and reducing your total harvest.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni egbala nu kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ baafite tso lɛ. Baai lɛ tsɔɔ asarasu. ni eha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does dried animal manure take longer to work on my crops compared to bag fertilizer from the shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloo ŋmei ni egbi lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani tsei kwɛ̃ɔ fe ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni jɛɔ shwapo mli lɛ?

english: Bag fertilizer dissolves quickly in water for direct plant feeding, while animal manure must first be broken down by tiny living organisms in the soil. Manure works slower, but it improves your soil for a much longer time.
ga: Baagi mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli oya koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ be mli ni esa akɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ akpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tsuɔ nii blɛoo shi ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why can't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can harvest more from my small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ madu mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ makpa babaoo kɛjɛ mikpokpaa bibioo lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they steal sunlight, water, and soil food from each other. This leaves you with tall, thin plants that produce tiny cobs instead of strong plants with large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha oná tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. Mohu ɔ, e ji tso nɛ ngɛ he wami, nɛ e ngɛ ngma ngua nɛ e he wa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have big leaves that act like living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and cool air it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kookoo lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava cuttings straight up, at a slant, or flat in the soil?
ga: Ani ekɔɔɔ he eko kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ du tɛ̃ɛ, mikɛ mihe ebɔ he, loo mikɛ mihe wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant buries enough stem nodes to form deep roots while keeping the top exposed to grow leaves easily, giving you a better root yield and making harvesting easier.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ baafu tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛya shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ haa onáa shishifãi ni hi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are starving for nitrogen. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep down into the ground below where young roots can reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without turning into small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers if they lack sufficient nutrients, don't get enough water, or if there are no tiny pollinating insects around to turn those flowers into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛbɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɛɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ he fɛɛ he ni baaha nakai fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up into tight cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl temporarily in the afternoon sun to prevent the plant from losing too much water. However, if they stay curled with yellow spots all day, it means tiny insects like whiteflies have infected the crop with a virus.
ga: Ha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ shwane mli koni tsei lɛ akafite nu babaoo. Shi, kɛji akɛ amɛbɔle amɛhe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji, eŋɔ hela ewo ŋmɔshi nibii amli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry grass or crop leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tomato tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi loo tso baai yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts like a protective blanket. It blocks the blazing sun from drying out the soil, keeps the root area cool, and prevents heavy rains from washing away your topsoil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I see water drops standing on the edges of my cocoyam leaves early in the morning when it did not rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa nu ŋmɔtɔi ni damɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe leebi be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called guttation. When the soil has plenty of water and the night air is cool, the plant pumps out extra water through tiny holes on its leaves; it shows your crop is absorbing water well, not that it is sick.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ gutting. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Tsei shwieɔ nu kroko kɛtsɔɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ amli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miihe nu jogbaŋŋ. Jeee akɛ hela mɔ lɛ.

english: I noticed a thick, sticky liquid coming out of my cashew tree trunk. Does this mean my tree is diseased?
ga: Miyɔse nu ko ni mli tse ni mli tse ni miijɛ cashew tso lɛ shishi. Ani enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ mitso lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Trees naturally produce sap or gum as a defense mechanism to seal up small wounds or protect themselves from stress and insects. Light sap flow is just the tree healing itself.
ga: Dabi, tsei jieɔ nu loo ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ naa akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ pilamɔi bibii ahe. aloo obu ohe kɛjɛ haomɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe Nu ni hoɔ mlɛo lɛ ji tsamɔ pɛ kɛha tso lɛ.

english: When I cut my cassava stem to plant, a reddish juice comes out. Is this stem spoiled?
ga: Beni afo ŋmei tso lɛ koni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Nu tsuru miije kpo. Ani tso nɛɛ egbo?

english: No, cassava stems naturally contain liquid and latex that can turn dark or reddish when exposed to air. As long as the stem is firm and not rotten or soft inside, it is healthy and good for planting.
ga: Dabi, nu kɛ adebɔɔ mli latex ni baanyɛ atsɔ ediŋŋ loo etsuru kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bote mli lɛ yɛ cassava tsei amli. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ mli wa ni emli lɛ egbooo loo ebɛ blɛoo lɛ. Eyɛ hewalɛ lolo ni ehi kɛha dumɔ.

english: How does my maize plant form corn grains when I do not see big flowers on it like tomato plants?
ga: Te mi ŋmãa lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ etsɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa? Akɛni minaaa fɔfɔii wuji tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Maize reproduces through its tassel at the top and the silks on the cob. The tassel releases tiny pollen grains into the wind, which fall onto the silks; each silk carries that life signal inside the husk to form one grain of corn.
ga: Abɛi fɔɔ bii kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Tassels lɛ jieɔ pollen bibii bibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni amɛgbeeɔ siliki lɛ nɔ. Siliki fɛɛ siliki hiɛɔ wala he okadii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ebafeɔ ŋmei ŋmeii kome.

english: Why do many blossoms fall off my tomato plants without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather gets too hot or when there is no wind or insects to shake the pollen inside the flower. Without pollen moving to the right part inside the flower, fruit cannot form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ eyaaa he ni sa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ, Yibii nyɛŋ afee.

english: How does manure put near the roots reach the leaves and branches high up on my orange tree?
ga: Te baafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ baashɛ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Plants have tiny internal pipes inside their trunks and stems. The roots absorb water and dissolved nutrients from the soil, and the plant pulls them up through these internal tubes to feed the leaves and fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ yɛ tsɔnei bibii. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tso lɛ mli Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni mli ewo muji kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni tsei gbalaa amɛ kɛtsɔɔ nɛkɛ mligbɛ tsɔnei nɛɛ anɔ koni amɛha amɛbaai kɛ amɛyibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How do cassava roots turn into big tubers under the ground where there is no light?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei shishifãi bafeɔ ŋmei wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ni kane bɛ lɛ?

english: The green leaves above ground catch sunlight to make plant food. The plant then sends this food down through internal stems into special storage roots, causing them to swell up into tubers beneath the soil.
ga: Baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la koni ekɛfee niyenii aha tso lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ shishigbɛ tso lɛ mli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli he ni akɛtoɔ yɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfuɔ ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Why do my yam tubers start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when they are kept away from soil and water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miibɔi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ amɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ muji kɛ nu he moŋ?

english: Yam tubers store food and water inside themselves. After a period of rest, internal natural signals tell the tuber it is time to grow, using its own stored water and energy to sprout before touching the soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu toɔ amɛmli. Beni ajɔɔ ehe be fioo sɛɛ lɛ, Adebɔɔ mli okadii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛɛ yitso lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ nɔ lɛ, edaa dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my cassava turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is a natural survival trick. During dry weather, the plant drops its older outer leaves to save water and keep its core stem and underground roots alive until the rains return.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaawoo. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tso lɛ baashi esɛɛ baai momo lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he. ni amɛkwɛ tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop down during the afternoon sun but stand up straight again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Shi te shi jaŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: In the hot sun, leaves lose water faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil, so they limp to protect themselves from heat. Overnight, the roots catch up, refilling the plant so the leaves stand up straight again.
ga: Yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyaa amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he. Yɛ gbɛkɛ kome mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛyiɔ tso lɛ mli bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in the middle of the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmãa be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure around the base helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee baai eŋɔli Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloi ashishifã ni fiteɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni eha eŋɔli su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines produce plenty of bushy leaves, but the yams under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ hiɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji bibioo lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer relative to potassium and phosphorus, the yam plant uses all its energy to grow leaves above ground instead of storing food below ground to develop big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto potassium kɛ phosphorus he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas on their land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ ŋmei yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When the crop is harvested and roots decay, they leave natural fertility in the soil for the next maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ egbo Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and showing pale yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a common sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread between plants by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings prevents this leaf twisting and protects your harvest.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he. Agbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebaatsi baa lɛ naa ni ebu okpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves look like they have small holes and brown powder inside the central growing funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ dalɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's leaf whorl. The brown powder is insect waste, and dropping recommended treatments directly into the funnel early stops them before they ruin the whole stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmeii lɛ. Pauda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji kooloi amli jwɛi. kɛ tsofa ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni shwieɔ mra kɛboteɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. baakpa dani efite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any fruit begins to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani aduawai jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures get too high or when they suffer from irregular watering. Providing steady moisture and light shade during extremely hot days helps the blossoms stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa. Fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɛɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight with the main mother plant for nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight. Removing extra suckers leaves energy for the main plant to produce thick stems and large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear away all the big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie cacao tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Retaining larger shade trees or planting plantains alongside new cocoa shields the tender leaves from direct sun heat and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei heei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are getting too much water or not enough water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiná nu babaoo loo amɛmiiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa?

english: If pepper plants lack water, their leaves droop and curl during the day; if they receive too much water, their leaves turn pale yellow and fall off because the plant roots are drowning in soggy soil.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ pepper tso lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpãa shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kɛji onine shɛ nu babaoo nɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does spreading dry grass on the soil around my cabbage plants keep them fresh during dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni agbɛ jwɛi ni egbi ashwã shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cabbage tso lɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ ehee yɛ otsii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) shields the ground from direct heat. This keeps the soil cool and stops water from evaporating quickly, allowing roots to drink steady moisture even when rain is scarce.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well even when it rains continuously throughout the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekpaa shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be afi muu lɛ fɛɛ moŋ?

english: Too much rain can waterlog the soil, drowning root systems by removing oxygen and washing away essential plant nutrients. Plants need a balance of sunlight, drained soil, and water to grow properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee nu. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ jeɔ kpo ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei hia hulu la, shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, kɛ nu ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers fall off my tomato plants before producing fruit during heavy rain periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall physically knocks blossoms off plants and high air moisture prevents pollen from floating through the air properly, preventing fertilization.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha tsei akumɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa pollen lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni atsĩ fɔmɔ naa

english: Can I plant maize during any month of the year as long as there is rain falling?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔŋ fɛɛ nyɔŋ nɔ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ?

english: Even with continuous water, maize needs adequate sunlight and a dry spell toward the end of its life cycle so the cobs can dry properly without rotting.
ga: Yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Abɛi hu he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ be ni mli egbi yɛ ewala be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ ji koni ŋmei lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee.

english: Why are my vegetable crops growing very tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Crops stretch upward and become weak when they do not receive enough direct sunlight, often caused by heavy tree shade or constant overcast skies.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋwɛi ni ewo atatu be fɛɛ be lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: In extreme heat, plant leaves lose moisture faster through evaporation than root systems can absorb water from the ground, causing temporary afternoon wilting.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tso baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, shwane lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the peak of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during wet periods usually indicate that soil nutrients like nitrogen have been washed deep into the ground beyond the reach of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen lɛ etsɔ sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant at the exact same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific soil nutrients over time; rotating different crops or adding compost helps restore ground fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ aba shi fiofio yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ Loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops seem to grow better when I plant groundnuts together with cassava in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei du yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer for neighboring plants like cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after every rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ fɛɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants with aggressive root systems that are adapted to absorb fresh rainwater and soil nutrients far quicker than domestic crop seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli. Amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nugbɔ nu kpakpa kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe shia tsei ahe dumɔwui.

english: Why do I notice more insects damaging my leafy crops immediately after the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɔseɔ akɛ kooloi bibii babaoo miifite mitsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: The start of rains creates high humidity and warmth, which triggers dormant insect eggs to hatch in large numbers just as plants produce soft fresh leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ jeɔ shishi ekɛ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ni nɔ kwɔ baa. Stimulate dormant kooloi akui Amɛteŋ babaoo fɔ. Tamɔ tsei ni haa baai bibii ni yɔɔ ehee.

english: Why do farmers often add cassava to fields where they are already growing crops like corn, rice, and beans?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ okwaafoi kɛ ŋmãa fataa ŋmɔji ni amɛduɔ nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, kɛ ŋmãa momo lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Cassava is a resilient root crop that can remain in the soil longer than grains and legumes. Adding cassava to your fields ensures you still have food to harvest even after your short-term crops like corn and beans are done.
ga: Cassava ji tso ko ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei fata oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa onáa niyenii ni obaakpa lolo. Enɛ ji yɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni agbe naa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are so many farmers in Northern Ghana planting soybeans alongside corn these days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ miidu soybeans yɛ ŋmãa masɛi amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Soybeans perform exceptionally well in the northern climate and soil when grown alongside corn. They produce abundant harvests, giving farmers both a nutritious food source and a reliable cash crop.
ga: Soybeans tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ titri yɛ kooyigbɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔji anɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi. Amɛwoɔ ŋmaa babaoo. Enɛ haa okwaafoi lɛ naa niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Which staple crops can I grow together on my farm to make sure I have a good variety of food?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii titri manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana niyenii srɔtoi?

english: Combining grains like corn and rice with legumes like beans and groundnuts, and adding root crops like cassava, gives you a well-rounded farm that provides balanced food and spreads out your harvest times.
ga: Nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni akɛaafee ekome Ekɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yaa jogbaŋŋ. Ni kɛ okɛ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei fata he lɛ, ehaa onáa ŋmɔ ni efee ekome kwraa ni haa onáa niyenii ni ja ni ehaa okpamɔ be lɛ feɔ srɔtoi.

english: Why should I include legumes like beans or groundnuts in my crop rotation with corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii awo mi-ŋmei tsakemɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans help enrich the soil while yielding valuable food. Growing them along with heavy feeders like corn keeps your farm productive and yields a diverse harvest.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shweremɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni jara wa baa. Kɛ́ okɛ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi baa.

english: When I plant a small quantity of corn or rice seeds, how much harvest can I expect back?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa fioo ko lɛ Sɛɛnamɔi enyiɛ manyɛ makpa gbɛ?

english: Crops like corn and rice have high multiplication rates. A single seed grows into a plant that produces hundreds of new seeds, meaning your final harvest yield will far exceed the weight of the seeds you originally sowed.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ shweremɔ ni fa babaoo. Dumɔwu kome daa ni etsɔɔ tso ni woɔ dumɔwui heei ohai abɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ naagbee yibiiwoo ni obaaná lɛ baaho dumɔwui ni odu yɛ shishijee mli lɛ amli tsiimɔ kwraa.

english: If I plant soybeans for the first time in northern Ghana, will I get a good return on my seed investment?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ soybeans klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. Ani maná sɛɛnamɔ kpakpa kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui ni mikɛwo mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, soybeans adapt very well to the northern soil and weather. With proper planting practices, the harvest yield you collect will be much greater than the quantity of seed you planted.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, soybeans lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli. Kɛtsɔ dumɔ nifeemɔi ni sa nɔ Yibii ni obaakpa lɛ baafee babaoo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do some crops yield far more than the seeds I put into the ground while others need more seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu biɔ dumɔwui babaoo lɛ?

english: Different crops reproduce differently, but food grains and legumes naturally yield multiple pods or ears per seed. When given good soil and water, each seed expands into a much larger crop harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yɛ fɔmɔ srɔtoi. Shi dumɔwui kɛ ŋmeii feɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ dumɔwu kome mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛ nu nɔ Dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli lɛɛɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da kwraa.

english: Why does the market price of staple crops like corn drop when everyone in my area harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ jara baa shi yɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ kpaa lɛ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When harvests are abundant across many farms, there is a large supply of produce in the market. When the crop becomes easily available everywhere, high prices naturally come down.
ga: Beni ŋmaa babaoo yɛ ŋmɔji babaoo amli No hewɔ lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ jara nɔ. Beni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Jara ni nɔ kwɔ baa shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: If a crop becomes very abundant in my district, will it become cheaper for people to buy?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ Ani ebaafee nɔ ni jara waaa kɛha mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ?

english: Yes, when local supply becomes abundant, crop prices drop in the market. This makes food cheaper for buyers, though farmers may need to store some produce to sell later when prices rise again.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni maŋ lɛ mli nibii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ jara eba shi. Ha niyenii afee mlɛo aha jarayelɔi Eyɛ mli akɛ ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okwaafoi lɛ ato amɛnibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ ekomɛi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ sɛɛ mli beni jara lɛ tee ŋwɛi ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Does harvesting a yield much larger than what I sowed mean I will always make a high profit?
ga: Ani kɛ́ makpa nɔ ni fe nɔ ni miduɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ maná sɛɛnamɔi babaoo be fɛɛ be?

english: A large yield gives you more crop to sell and feed your family, but if every farmer has an abundant harvest at once, market prices per bag will drop, affecting overall profit per unit.
ga: Nikpamɔ babaoo baaha oná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ ni okɛye oweku lɛ. Shi kɛji okwaafonyo fɛɛ okwaafonyo kpa ŋmaa babaoo yɛ be kome mli lɛ Jarayeli jara ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ baa shi. ni saa sɛɛnamɔ fɛɛ ni anáa yɛ unit kome mli lɛ he

english: What makes the Akom cassava variety different from other local crops I can plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa Akhom ŋmei henɔ lɛ feɔ srɔto yɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsei krokomɛi ahe? ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Akom is a fast-maturing cassava variety popular in Ghana that matures in about 6 to 8 months, offering quick yields and good tuber development compared to traditional varieties that take over a year.
ga: Akom ji ŋmei henɔ ko ni daa oya ni ale waa yɛ Ghana. Amɛdaraa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli, ni amɛwoɔ yibii oya ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai. Kɛ akɛto blema tsofai srɔtoi ni heɔ nɔ ni fe afi kome lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some crop varieties mature in 6 months while others take a whole year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji 6 mli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ afi muu fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred with different growth cycles; short-duration varieties are designed to feed heavily and complete their tuber development quickly within 6 to 8 months.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Afee ŋmeii srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ koni amɛye niyenii babaoo ni amɛwo bulbs oya yɛ nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli.

english: How do I know when my 6-month root crops are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shishifãi ni eye nyɔji 6 lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Root crops reaching maturity around 6 to 8 months usually show signs like yellowing of lower leaves, firm underground tubers, and a stop in upward stem growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni daa yɛ aaafee nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 mli lɛ jieɔ okadii tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni wa lɛ akpo. ni tso lɛ tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ

english: What will happen to my yield if I harvest my cassava earlier than 6 months?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa ŋmei mra fe nyɔji 6?

english: Harvesting too early cuts off the plant's feeding period short, leaving you with small, watery tubers that have not fully stored their starch.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ niyenii be lɛ afee kuku. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, obaaná yitsei bibii ni nu yɔɔ mli ni ehiɛko ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to nourish my crop well during its first 6 months in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mahã miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 6 ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first 6 months are the critical feeding stage where the plant absorbs soil nutrients to fuel its vegetative growth and build strong underground tubers.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 6 lɛ ji niyeli be ni he hiaa ni tso lɛ shwieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo tso lɛ dalɛ he hewalɛ ni efee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops grow well within their 8-month cycle?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji 8 mli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied early, usually within the first 1 to 3 months, so the plant has essential food readily available during its main growth spurt.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli mra, bei pii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 1 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli, koni tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ be titri ni edaa lɛ mli.

english: What goes on under the soil during the 6-month growth period of cassava?
ga: Mɛni baa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nyɔji 6 ni ŋmei lɛ daa lɛ mli?

english: During this time, the plant transfers food made in its leaves down to its root system, continuously swelling the roots into thick, starch-filled tubers.
ga: Yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwereɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ amɛfeɔ bulbs ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with big leaves but small roots after 6 months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ? Baai wuji shi shishifãi bibii yɛ nyɔji 6 sɛɛ?

english: An imbalance of nutrients, like having too much nitrogen, makes the plant spend all its food on leafy growth above ground instead of developing tubers below.
ga: Niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa, tamɔ nitrogen babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii

english: Why must I keep weeds away from my young crop during its first few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matsi jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei bibii lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with young plants for soil food, water, and sunlight, which slows down the crop's development during its crucial early months.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ adaramɔ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji ni he hiaa waa lɛ amli.

english: How does loose, well-tilled soil help my 6-to-8-month tuber crops grow better?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni atsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-tubers ni eye nyɔji 6 kɛyashi 8 lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Loose soil allows young feeder roots to easily push outward and swell into large tubers while absorbing maximum food and moisture from the earth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛbaatsi amɛhe kɛya kponɔgbɛ ni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small suckers growing near the bottom of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers or chupons, steal food, water, and energy away from the main trunk. Removing them helps the tree put all its energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers loo chupons lɛ juɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are running out of nitrogen, which is essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer can help keep the leaves green and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei, ŋmei, loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aku sɛɛ aha onibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does leaving weeds in my field reduce the size of my farm produce?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mishiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Weeds steal light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get all the food they need to produce large yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekpa nii babaoo.

english: It is best to plant after the ground receives at least two strong rains that wet the soil deeply, rather than after the very first light shower. This ensures seeds have enough steady moisture to germinate without drying out.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu yɛ be mli ni kɛ hoo lɛ, nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa nu ni tamɔ amɛhe ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why should I construct soil ridges across a slope instead of straight down the hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matswa ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni mafo ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Ridges built across a hill act like small walls that hold back rainwater. This stops heavy downpours from washing away your crops and carrying off your valuable topsoil.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni ama yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogboi bibii ni tsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa. Enɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ oŋmɔshinii lɛ ni ekɛ oshikpɔŋ ni jara wa lɛ yaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and soft if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch as they mature, but if left in the soil past their prime or during heavy rains, the plant starts using up that stored energy to grow new top leaves, leaving the tubers watery.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shi kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe be ni sa loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ baabɔi hewalɛ ni ekɛto lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃. Shi tuber lɛ kɛ nu.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the stems without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants often drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Can dry wood ash from my cooking fire really protect my stored maize seeds from insects?
ga: Ani tso sũ ni egbi ni jɛɔ la ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ abu ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, mixing dry wood ash with your dried seeds creates a dusty barrier that blocks and dehydrates insects like weevils, preventing them from feeding and laying eggs in your stored grain.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli sũ ni egbi ni akɛfutuɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ feɔ sũ gbogbo ko ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii anaa ni ehaa amɛnuɔ nu, ni no haaa amɛye nii ni amɛkawo ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni okɛtoɔ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an important plant food. Adding manure or fertilizer early gives the crop the strength it needs to stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye nitrogen. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Beans and cowpeas pull naturally occurring food from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant dies, that food stays in the soil, making it naturally rich for crops like maize or vegetables planted next.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas gbalaa niyenii ni baa adebɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai yaa nɔ aduɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their roots are soft and shallow. Keeping shade trees or planting plantains around them keeps the soil cool and shelters them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛhe ekɔɔɔ. Shade ni akɛhaa loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa wɔɔhe kɛyashiɔ tso lɛ mli waa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber growing under the ground. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil where they might rot and helps them catch the light they need to produce large yams.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatara shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ yɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. ni ehaa baai lɛ naa la ni he hiaa kɛha sweet potato feemɔ babaoo.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays around them for too long in heavy soil. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rain to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Why is it bad to water my vegetable crops in the middle of the day when the sun is high?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ ooofɔ aduawai anɔ nu yɛ gbi mli be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering in the hot afternoon heat causes most of the water to dry up into the air before the roots can drink it. It can also scorch the leaves; watering early in the morning or late in the evening works best.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ nu lɛ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ fa ko agbi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã hu. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets too hot and dry, or when water supply is uneven. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass helps keep the roots cool and retains water so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛgbi. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ ejaaa Shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi koni ewo yibii.

english: Curling leaves are usually a sign that tiny insects are hiding under the leaves and sucking out the juices. Spraying the undersides of the leaves early with soapy water or neem oil helps remove them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji kooloi bibii ahe okadi. Ekɛ ehe woɔ baai ashishi ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ mli. Ni ooofɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem fɔ baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ejie.

english: Why do I get tiny cobs when I plant my maize seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ kooloo bibioo lɛ? Beni aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other for water, light, and food. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrients to grow large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Plantain roots do not go very deep into the ground, while the top carries heavy bunches of fruit. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole prevents strong winds from pushing the plant over.
ga: Plantain shishifãi eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Yɛ be mli ni yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, aduawai babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa koni ekatswa tso lɛ shi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ baai ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay very small even though the plant has big green leaves above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Nakai ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the plant spends all its energy growing leaves instead of expanding its underground tubers. Using balanced nutrients helps the plant feed the cassava roots properly.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛtsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Niyenii mli nibii ni sa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the plant right before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ miikwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when heavy rains or sudden heavy watering follow a dry period. The skin cannot stretch fast enough to hold the sudden intake of water inside the fruit, causing it to crack.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu ni fa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Trukaa lɛ, hewolo lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ ehe oya bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ ahi shi, ni no haa etswaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry. Without enough water and cool conditions, the plant sheds flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ bɛ lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do the stems of my yam plants start rotting near the soil line during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water surrounding the stem suffocates the roots by blocking air and creates a wet environment where soil fungi thrive, causing the tissue near the base to rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle he lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ naa lɛ nɔ. ni efee shihilɛ ko ni mli efɔ ni sũ mli ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ mli. Enɛ haa fãji ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and cool humidity cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ mli. Esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cabbage plants covered in tiny holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ehà mi-cabbage tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth larva feeding on the tissue. Catching them early with appropriate biological or natural sprays prevents them from destroying the head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback moth larvae, ni yeɔ fãji lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabii baai amli lɛ baa. Amɔmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ biological loo adebɔɔ mli spray ni sa nɔ lɛ ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite yitso lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crop plants to grow thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for light, water, and soil nutrients. Because weeds often grow faster, they steal these vital resources away, leaving your crops hungry and shaded.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No hewɔ lɛ amɛju nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ. Shi oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my cowpea plants curl up and turn sticky during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpɛɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curling, sticky leaves are a clear sign of aphids, which are small insects that suck sap from the plant and secrete a sweet, sticky fluid called honeydew. They multiply rapidly during dry weather.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ekpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ji aphids he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Enɛɛmɛi ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu ni mli ŋɔɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nektar lɛ kpo. Amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa oya yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and burning during the sunny months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and tender roots that dry out quickly in direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas grown next to them to block the harsh heat and trap moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni ekɛtsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow very tall and green in one part of my farm, but stays short and yellowish in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã ko nɔ lɛ? Shi fã kroko lɛ baafee kuku ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo.

english: Different parts of your farm have different levels of nutrients in the soil. Yellowish, short maize usually means that specific part of the field lacks nitrogen, which plants need to build strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ fãi srɔtoi yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ falɛi srɔtoi. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa kuku ni ji yellow lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ he pɔtɛɛ ko. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei akwɛ̃ yɛ ni amɛhe wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: What causes small round holes in my cabbage leaves, and will it destroy my entire harvest?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? yɛ mi-cabbage baa lɛ nɔ Ni ani ebaafite mi-nitsumɔ mli nibii fɛɛ?

english: Small holes in cabbage leaves are caused by insects or caterpillars eating the crop. If left untreated, these pests will eat away the leaves the plant uses to make food, resulting in small heads or completely ruined cabbages.
ga: Kplukai loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kaabɛji baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ yeɔ baai ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛyeɔ nii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso bibioo loo kaabe lɛ fiteɔ kwraa.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become regular. The very first rain is often followed by a long dry spell, which will dry out the topsoil and kill your newly sprouted seeds before their roots grow deep.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni egbeɔ dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to plant cassava alone on my land, or should I plant cowpeas between the rows?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mikome too madu ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ?
