english: Planting cowpeas between cassava rows helps your land because cowpeas pull food from the air into the soil, which feeds the cassava while covering the bare ground to prevent heavy rains from washing your good soil away.
ga: Kɛ́ odu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsina ŋmei gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛbaaye ŋmei lɛ, ni amɛbaaha hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafɔ oshikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very thin cobs when I plant many seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse waa beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water, light, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant its own space allows it to get enough food to produce big, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛhe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I harvested this year to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mikpa afi nɛɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: While you can plant saved seeds, seeds from hybrid crops usually lose their strength in the next generation. They often result in lower yields and weaker plants compared to buying fresh certified seeds each season.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui ni ato moŋ, shi bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he hewalɛ ni aheɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and getting dark spots after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Raindrops splash soil onto the lower leaves, carrying microscopic fungal diseases from the ground up onto the plant. Trimming lower leaves and covering the bare ground around the plant with dry grass helps prevent splash-back disease.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anɔ. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni anaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha hei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ sɛɛkuu naa.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are dying or just surviving during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ miigbo loo eeye harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: Cassava naturally drops its lower leaves during the Harmattan to save water while keeping its main stem alive. As long as the top leaves stay green and healthy, the plant is surviving and will grow new leaves when the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan beaŋ koni ekɛbu nu he yɛ be mli ni ekwɛɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ lolo. Shii abɔ ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Tso lɛ hiɔ shi lolo ni ebaaná baai heei kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops every year even though I plant the exact same crop on it every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi moŋ.

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over again while attracting the same pests. Switching crops every season gives the soil time to rest and rebuild its strength.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ shii abɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛ hu amɛgbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize farm turning yellow before the ears are even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding organic compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant recover its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my land next season instead of planting maize again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli moŋ fe ni madu ŋmei ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly drains nutrients from your soil. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and return it to the ground, restoring soil fertility naturally for your future crops.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha owɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains on the same land as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibioo lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I push my maize seeds too deep into the ground during planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli lɛ?

english: If buried too deep, the seed burns through all its stored energy before the shoot can reach sunlight at the surface, causing the seed to rot or die underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛto lɛ shãa dani ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do I have to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can trap as much sunlight as possible to produce food. Leaving vines on the ground keeps leaves in the shade and wet soil, causing smaller tubers and disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Kɛ́ oshi wain tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ ahi hulutsoo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii kɛ helai baa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before I even harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa amɛ po?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water collects around the roots for too long, allowing soil fungi to attack. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajie kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and making the plant stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miihoso ni eha tso lɛ miikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from under the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce smaller yields even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to build big yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do tiny insects get inside my harvested maize kernels even after I dry them properly?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii boteɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ amli? Kɛji migbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs inside the maize grains while the crop is still standing in the field. When stored, these eggs hatch into pests; using treated storage bags or proper sealing prevents them from destroying your grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii fɔɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ awoɔ ŋmeii amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛto lɛ, nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ baatsɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Kɛ́ okɛ kotokui ni akɛ nibii toɔ mli ni atsa amɛhe lɛ tsu nii loo okɛ amɛ naa jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite oŋmaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to make food and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves recover and feed the growing crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛhiɛ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni amɛha tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam vines produce many big green leaves but leave me with small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the yam plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tuber below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni sweet potato tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose almost all their leaves during the dry harmattan season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ani amɛmiigboi?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival trick to save water. The plant is not dead; once the rains return, it will quickly sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baa shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Baai eŋɔli heei baakwɛ̃ oya ni amɛbaaya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before any fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun, irregular watering, or high temperatures. Keeping the soil evenly moist during hot periods helps the flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ haoɔ amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo ni naa wa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: If I plant my corn seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting too close makes crops compete with each other for light, water, and soil food. This leaves you with weak, thin stalks and tiny cobs, whereas proper spacing produces bigger, healthier cobs and higher total yield.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji aba. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ babaoo aba

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the exact same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Rotating your crops with leguminous plants like beans or groundnuts helps rebuild the soil's natural strength.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if they are just growing in the spaces between the rows?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal water and fertilizer from the soil before your crop's roots can reach them, and they also block sunlight and harbor insect pests.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Amɛ tsiɔ hulu la hu naa ni amɛ haa kooloi awuiyelɔi aboɔhe.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my tomatoes turning black and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often brought on by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist allows the plant to move calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield weaker plants than certified seeds from the agriculture office?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe nɔ ni Bureau of Agriculture lɛ wo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can carry hidden diseases from previous seasons and lose their vigor over time, while certified seeds are specifically treated and bred to resist pests and grow uniformly high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baanyɛ atere helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ bei ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛhewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes spoil so fast when I transport them from my farm to the market in Accra?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee jara nɔ yɛ Accra lɛ?

english: Tomatoes have delicate skin and high water content, making them bruise easily when packed tightly in sacks during long, bumpy journeys. Combined with high heat, bruised tomatoes release gas and moisture that cause the whole batch to rot quickly. Packing them in rigid, ventilated crates helps protect them.
ga: Tomato hewolo lɛ yɛ mlɛo, ni nu babaoo yɛ mli. Tomatoi shwieɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo kotokui ni mli wa mli yɛ gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ ni mli ewo muji mli. Kɛ akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa fata he lɛ, tomato ni egbo lɛ jieɔ gas kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tomatoi akuu muu lɛ fɛɛ baafite oya. Kɛ́ okɛwo adeka ni wa ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe.

english: Why are market buyers choosing corn from other farmers instead of buying mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ halaa ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ moŋ fe minɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers look for corn that is uniformly sized, completely dry, and free from insect damage or mold. If your corn is harvested too early or not dried thoroughly, it loses its bright color and attracts pests, making buyers prefer grains that were dried and stored properly.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ ŋmãa ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe, ni egbi kwraa, ni kooloi loo ŋmãa bɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmãa lɛ mra tsɔ loo egbiko bɔ ni sa lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baafite ehiɛ ni kpɛɔ lɛ ni ebaagbala kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Enɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ dumɔwui ni agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ.

english: What makes farm produce rot so quickly when transported over long distances for export?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaayeli mli nibii fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛtee he ko ni jɛkɛ koni akɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: Once harvested, vegetables continue to breathe and produce internal heat. Without cooling or proper air flow, trapped heat and moisture speed up natural decay, causing fresh produce to spoil before reaching distant export destinations.
ga: Kɛji akpa Aduawai lɛ baaya nɔ amɛmu ni amɛbaafee dɔlɛ yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ lɛ, dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ lɛ baaha nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ aya hiɛ oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai kɛ aduawai heei fiteɔ dani amɛshɛɔ hei ni amɛyaa maŋsɛɛ ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How can I store my harvested corn so it doesn't spoil before I get a good buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ato koni ekafite dani maná mɔ kpakpa ni baahe?

english: To protect harvested corn from mold and insects, shell the cobs and dry the kernels in the sun until they are hard and crack when bitten. Storing the well-dried grain in clean, airtight bags or raised cribs keeps moisture and pests away.
ga: Koni abu ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ahe. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni ogbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbala kɛji akɛ amɛye. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotoku ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni awo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Is it good for my land if I plant tomatoes in the same field alongside my corn?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tomato yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, growing corn and tomatoes together can be very beneficial. Tall corn plants can act as a natural windbreak and provide light shade to protect tender tomato plants from intense sunlight, allowing you to maximize harvests from a single plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Abɛi tsei kakadaji baanyɛ atsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ tsimɔ ni eha hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ onáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How do I decide whether to focus on staple crops like corn or cash crops like tomatoes for the new season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ baama ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa waa tamɔ ŋmãa loo shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato nɔ kɛha be hee lɛ?

english: Corn is a low-risk staple crop that can be stored for months to feed your family or sell when prices rise, while tomatoes are high-value cash crops that bring quick money but spoil fast. Planting a combination of both helps secure your home food supply while generating regular income.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ oshara babaoo ni abaanyɛ akɛto nyɔji babaoo koni akɛha oweku lɛ niyenii loo ahɔ̃ɔ kɛji ejara tee hiɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tomato ji shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa ni haa anáa shika oya shi efiteɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ oshia lɛ ahi shi, ni ebaaha oná shika daa.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller corn harvests when I plant crops continuously on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo kɛ́ miduɔ ŋmãa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Crops pull essential food and nutrients out of the earth every growing season. If you continuously plant without resting the land, adding organic manure, or rotating with leguminous crops like beans, the soil becomes exhausted, leading to weak plants and small yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛji odu nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ Okɛ organic fertilizer afata he loo okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii atsu nii ni okɛtsake shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, ni no baaha tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits crack open on the vine right when they are getting ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ tswaa yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛji amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa pɛ?

english: Tomato fruits crack when there is a sudden change in water availability, such as heavy rain following a dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing it to split. Keeping soil moisture consistent with regular watering helps prevent this.
ga: Tomato yibii lɛ tswaa kɛji nu ni yɔɔ lɛ tsake trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ hɔmɔ be sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. cause disintegration Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why is my corn growing very tall and thin with small cobs when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When corn seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete heavily with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and light to build thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, which occurs when the tomato plant cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Maintaining steady moisture in the root zone allows the plant to move calcium into the developing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium yaa tso yibii ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy crop seeds sealed in plastic bags instead of keeping seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛ plastic kotokui ewo mli lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Seeds prepared and sealed in plastic by certified breeders are protected from moisture, insects, and decay. They give you healthier crops and higher yields compared to farm-saved seeds, which lose vigor over time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni kwɛɔ dumɔwui anɔ lɛ saa ni ekɛ plastic ewo mli. Abaabu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe. ni baafite hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I bought have been mixed with lower quality seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ lɛ kɛ dumɔwui ni baa shi efutu mli?

english: Good seeds look uniform in size, color, and shape. If a bag contains seeds of different sizes, colors, or damaged skins, they may be mixed with older or different varieties that will grow unevenly in your field.
ga: Dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ dalɛ, amɛhe su kɛ amɛhe yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔwui ni dalɛi srɔtoi, amɛhe sui srɔtoi, loo amɛshishifãi ni efite yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ Abaanyɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni etsɛ loo srɔtoi ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he.

english: What causes some of the seeds I planted to fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni haaa dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are dead from age, damaged by high heat during storage, or planted in soil that is either too dry or flooded with water.
ga: Dumɔwu ko nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji egbo yɛ dalɛ ni ebɛ hewɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ efite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. loo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Is it safe for me to order crop seeds from abroad to plant on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mabi dumɔwui kɛjɛ maŋsɛɛ koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli?

english: Importing seeds requires approval from agricultural authorities to ensure they do not bring foreign crop diseases or destructive pests into Ghana that could ruin your farm and neighboring fields.
ga: Esa akɛ okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ akpɛlɛ dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maŋsɛɛ aba lɛ nɔ koni dumɔwui lɛ kɛ maŋsɛɛ tsei ahe helai loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii aba Ghana. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ.

english: Will crop seeds imported from another country grow well in Ghana's weather?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni akɛbaajɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ aba lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ amli?

english: Not always. Foreign seeds are bred for specific climates and may fail to produce good yields if they cannot handle Ghana's high heat, humidity, or local rainfall patterns.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be ji be ni afɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi. ni ekolɛ enyɛŋ ewo yibii kpakpai Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ Ghana dɔlɛ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ gbɛ lɛ,.

english: Why do some plants in my field grow very tall while others right next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ bibii lɛ?

english: This usually happens when mixed or non-uniform seeds are planted, or when soil nutrients and water are distributed unevenly, causing weaker seeds to be outcompeted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni efutu loo ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee. aloo beni niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlijaa ejaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ atswa akaŋ.

english: Why do the young leaves on my newly sprouted crops turn yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mitsei heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young shoots often signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, excess water suffocating the roots, or extreme sun heat stressing the young plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo hulu ni tsoɔ waa, ni kɛ haomɔ baa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ

english: How does heavy rainfall immediately after planting affect my crop seeds?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away seeds, bury them too deep under thick mud, or compact the soil surface, making it difficult for young sprouts to push through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui kɛya. Afu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ muji ni mli edɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ shishi Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei bibii akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli.

english: Why do my crops produce plenty of green leaves but very few fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo shi aduawai loo ŋmaa fioo pɛ miiwo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants put all their energy into leafy growth. Crops need phosphorus and potassium to support flowering and fruit production.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa baai lɛ adalɛ. Tsei he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my stored crop seeds spoil or rot before the next planting season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ fiteɔ loo egboɔ dani shweremɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: High humidity and heat cause moisture to build up inside storage containers, encouraging mold growth and insect damage that kills the seed embryo.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa kɛ dɔlɛ haa fɛ̃i baa nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ daraa.

english: I am starting my first cocoa farm this year; how long will it take before my new trees start producing pods?
ga: Mijeɔ mi klɛŋklɛŋ kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ shishi afi nɛɛ. Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mitso hee lɛ baaje ŋmɔtɔ shishi?

english: Hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing fruits within 2 to 3 years with proper care, whereas older traditional cocoa varieties can take up to 4 or 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni akɛfee tsofai ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 loo 5.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings seem to struggle and dry up when there are no shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni tsei ni haa hulutsoo be bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees because intense sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out the soil moisture needed for their early growth.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ̃ mra lɛ agbi.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different chemicals together when spraying my cocoa farm to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai enyɔ baafutu mli kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa miifɔ kookoo ŋmɔ ko nɔ koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: No, mixing unapproved chemicals can harm the cocoa trees, reduce the effectiveness of the treatment, and leave dangerous residues on your crop that fail safety standards.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akpɛlɛɛɛ nɔ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye cacao tso lɛ awui. ehaa tsofafeemɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi ni eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai lɛ kpãaa gbee lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and curl up during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellow and curling leaves are usually a sign of insect pests like capsids sucking the sap from young leaves, or a lack of essential nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ capsids ni shwieɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ he okadi. loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli

english: How long do I need to wait after spraying chemicals before it is safe to harvest my crop?
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani efee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛbaakpa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: You must wait for the recommended waiting period—usually 2 to 4 weeks depending on the chemical—to ensure the chemical breaks down and leaves no harmful residues on the cocoa beans.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ be ni atsɔɔ akɛ omɛ lɛ (bei pii lɛ otsii 2 kɛyashi 4, ni enɛ damɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ) koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tsofa lɛ fiteɔ ni eshiŋ nɔ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, overly shaded farms during the rainy season.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers without growing into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers but drop up to 95% of them to conserve energy and only feed the number of pods the tree can healthily support.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi ajieɔ enɛ shi kɛyashɛɔ 95% koni akɛto hewalɛ he ni akɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Will cutting off the extra shoots growing at the base of my cocoa tree hurt the plant?
ga: Ani ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye tso lɛ awui?

english: No, cutting off these extra shoots (called chupons or suckers) helps the plant by preventing them from stealing nutrients needed for pod production.
ga: Dabi, nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ (ni atsɛɔ amɛ chupons loo suckers) ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ kɛha pod feemɔ.

english: What causes my harvested cocoa beans to be rejected or graded poorly during inspection?
ga: Mɛni ha akpoo mi-kookoo yibii ni akpa lɛ loo ahaaa mi yibɔ ni ehiii yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans get rejected or downgraded if they are not fermented properly, remain wet, become moldy, or show damage from insects and bad chemicals.
ga: Akpooɔ kookoo ŋmeii loo amɛfiteɔ kɛji akɛ afeee amɛ ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ, amɛmli edɔ lolo, amɛmli ewo muji, loo amɛtsɔɔ nɔ ni kooloi kɛ tsofai gbohii efite amɛ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa beans are fully dried and ready for sale?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ egbi kwraa ni esa akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ?

english: Fully dried cocoa beans make a crackling sound when squeezed in your hand, have a deep brown color inside, and have a moisture level low enough to prevent mold during storage.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi kwraa lɛ feɔ gbee ni tswaa kɛji akɛ okɛ onine mimɔ mli. Mligbɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting drowned in too much water. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to stay green, make energy, and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo ebote nu babaoo mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli, amɛfee hewalɛ, ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the land time to restore its soil food naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why shouldn't I put chemical fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can soak them up safely. Putting fertilizer on bone-dry soil burns and damages the roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wui yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baashã ni egbe shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off without growing into peppers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress pepper plants, forcing them to drop their flowers to save water and energy rather than trying to produce fruits they cannot support.
ga: Pepper tsei ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ ni nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛshɛrɛ fɔfɔi amɛshwie koni amɛkɛhere nu kɛ hewalɛ Moŋ lɛ amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains growing above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ aná tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Taller shade crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, keeping the air cool and conserving soil moisture around the cocoa.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ ni bɔle kookoo lɛ he lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them survive the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni jwɛi shwieɔ shi lɛ No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the ground from direct sun heat, trapping moisture in the earth so plant roots stay cool and hydrated.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni tso shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i

english: Why do cassava plants produce very small tubers if I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava stems are planted too closely, their underground roots fight each other for space, soil food, and water, leaving no plant with enough resources to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná he ko, shikpɔŋ niyenii, kɛ nu, ni no haaa tso ko bɛ ni yɔɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and grow very slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛdaraa blɛoo waa lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal food, water, and sunlight away from your main crops, effectively starving your crops and slowing down their progress.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni ehaa oyaa hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground if heavy rains continue for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ tee nɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When soil stays soaked with water for days, oxygen cannot reach the root zone. This suffocates the cassava roots, causing the tubers to decay and rot underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli gbii babaoo lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling up and turning dry even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is frequently caused by viruses spread by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat stress making the leaves curl up to avoid losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji hela ko ni haa tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out quickly in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them creates a cool cover that protects the young cocoa until its roots grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa shihilɛhe ko ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: It is best to wait until the rain has soaked the soil consistently for a few days rather than planting after the very first shower. Early rains can be deceiving, and seeds will die if the soil dries up right after germination.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii fioo komɛi. Mohu ɔ, mo du lɛ ngɛ kekleekle nu ɔ se. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ baanyɛ alaka mɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ baagboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Yam vines produce the food that grows the big tuber underground using sunlight. Lifting the leaves off the ground with sticks helps them get maximum sunlight and prevents soil diseases from attacking the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ niyenii ni hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akatutua baai lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are starving for nitrogen, which is a major nutrient in the soil. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the leaves turn green and produce bigger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects around them without draining away properly. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. ni enyɛɛɛ ejie lɛ jogbaŋŋ Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the sap out of new growth. Spraying the plants with mild insecticidal soap or neem oil water stops these insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Akɛ samla ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni waaa lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ. Aloo neem fɔ nu lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping flowers without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages flowers to turn into fruits.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni ŋmeii bɛ ni baaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ajie nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ akatsɔ aduawai.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that eats fresh corn leaves from the inside out. Putting neem leaf extract or recommended control powders directly into the leaf center early in the morning kills the pests before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai heei kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo powder ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛyeɔ nɔ lɛ fata tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishifã lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily when a heavy wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots close to the surface and become heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with a strong bamboo or wooden prop prevents the tree from breaking under the weight of the bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ ni amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ kɛji amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni mli wa fi tso lɛ shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ yɛ ŋmei lɛ tsiimɔ shishi.

english: Can putting too much chemical fertilizer on my crops actually destroy them?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, using too much chemical fertilizer or placing it directly against the stem burns the roots and draws moisture out of the crop. Always apply fertilizer in small amounts a short distance away from the plant stem in moist soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsu nii babaoo loo akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ ni ebaagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko awo tso lɛ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or shade trees around them to protect their leaves from burning while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ akashã be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: How many cocoa trees can I safely plant on one acre of land without crowding them?
ga: Cacao tsei enyiɛ manyɛ madu shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre kome nɔ ni mɛi ehiɛɛɛ nɔ tsɔ?

english: A standard acre can hold about 435 cocoa trees when planted at a recommended spacing of 3 meters by 3 meters. Proper spacing ensures each tree gets enough sunlight, air, and soil nutrients to yield well.
ga: Acre ni ji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ aaafee kookoo tsei 435 kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 3 x mitai 3 lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but only a small percentage get pollinated by tiny insects or receive enough water and nutrients to develop into full cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi oha mlijaa fioo ko pɛ ji nɔ ni kooloi bibii shwieɔ amɛmli. Aloo nine ashɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Losing leaves during dry weather is a natural survival mechanism. The cocoa tree reduces water loss through its leaves to stay alive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Baai ni laajeɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Cocoa tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, high-humidity weather. Excess moisture on the pods allows the fungus to spread quickly from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii krokomɛi amli.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree produce bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afoɔ lɛ krokomɛi yeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary or weak branches, allowing the tree to direct its energy, water, and nutrients straight into growing healthy cocoa pods rather than feeding extra foliage.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha baai krokomɛi afata he lɛ

english: Will planting cassava next to my young cocoa trees harm their growth?
ga: Ani yucca ni mikwɛɔ yɛ mi-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ masɛi lɛ baafite edalɛ?

english: Cassava grows thick underground roots that aggressively compete with young cocoa roots for soil nutrients and water, which can stunt the cocoa plant's development.
ga: Cassava yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ cocoa shishifãi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii kpakpai amli lɛ akaŋ. ni baanyɛ atsĩ kookoo tsei lɛ adalɛ naa

english: How long does a newly planted cocoa tree take before it starts producing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years of planting, whereas older traditional varieties often take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ fɔɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 heɔ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees fall over during heavy storms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi gbeeɔ shi yɛ ahum ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees struggle to anchor themselves if the soil is too hard or shallow for taproots to grow deep. Soft, waterlogged soil combined with strong winds easily pushes down trees with weak root structures.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛma amɛhe nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eshɛɛɛ tsɔ ni taproot lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shɔŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ tsei ni shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ashwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ.

english: Why do weeds around the base of my cocoa trees slow down their growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi babaoo ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani mi-cocoa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ miiba shi?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients meant for the cocoa tree, causing the tree to grow slower and produce fewer pods.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha kookoo tso lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ daa blɛoo ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai fioo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is missing nitrogen, or heavy rains washed the nutrients away before roots could reach them. Applying fertilizer at the right growth stage and burying it slightly in the soil helps the plant absorb it better.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be ni sa mli ni edara lɛ, ni afu lɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts together with my cassava in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, which feeds the cassava plants. Planting them together improves soil fertility while giving you two different harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Abɛi mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli, he ni ehaa niyenii kɛhaa ŋmei tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in small, weak plants. Proper spacing allows each plant to spread its leaves and roots, producing much larger yields overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso gbɛɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nitsumɔ babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I just save and plant the maize seeds harvested from my farm last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpa kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose their strength over time, leading to lower yields and weaker plants. Buying fresh certified seeds ensures your crops grow uniformly, resist common local pests, and yield better.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai baa

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are wilting because of heat or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbo yɛ dɔlɛ loo hela hewɔ?

english: Plants wilting from heat will recover in the cooler evening or after watering. If the leaves stay wilted, develop dark spots, or turn yellow even when the soil is wet, the plant has a bacterial or fungal disease.
ga: Tsei ni hulutsoo lɛ mli egboi lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli loo beni awo amɛ nu sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛgboi, amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ bacteria loo fungal mli baa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛdara ni amɛbatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from severe heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps protect the flowers so peppers can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa kpe amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like beans restores soil health and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni amɛsumɔɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii kɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow faster and hurt my crops more when the crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni eyeɔ miŋmɔshinii lɛ awui babaoo beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and leaves, making it hard for them to compete with fast-growing wild weeds for sunlight and water. Clearing weeds during the first month gives your crops the strength to outgrow competing weeds.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi kɛ baai bibii. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛkɛ koo mli jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya lɛ baashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ nu. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, onibii lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛye jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ anɔ kunim.

english: Why do my stored grains get full of insects and spoil so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii eyi miŋmaa ni mikɛto lɛ mli ni efiteɔ oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil when they are bagged before being completely dried in the sun, creating a warm, damp environment insect pests love. Thoroughly drying grains and storing them in sealed, airtight bags prevents insects from multiplying.
ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ kɛ akɛwo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ sumɔɔ waa. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting when the first rain falls?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ aje dumɔ shishi beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛɔ lɛ?

english: Planting after the very first rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry up again if rains pause. It is best to wait until the soil stays consistently moist down to your finger depth for several days before sowing seeds.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ agbi oya ekoŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi oniji ahe gbii komɛi dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides canopy shade and moisture, protecting the young plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yam vines need tall stakes to lift and spread their leaves toward the sunlight. Exposing the foliage to maximum light enables the plant to create more energy, which fuels the growth of larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni amɛkɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛkɛ hulu lɛ akpee. Kɛ́ akɛ la ni fa babaoo ha tso lɛ baai lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji lɛ daa lɛ

english: Should I cut off the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani ajie plantain tsei titrii lɛ?

english: Yes, cutting away extra shoots so that only two or three strong suckers remain prevents overcrowding. This ensures the main plant gets enough water and soil nutrients to produce large, healthy bunches.
ga: Hɛɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi koni akafee nɔ ni fa fe nine. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning is best because roots absorb water before the sun warms the air, reducing moisture loss from evaporation and protecting the plant from thermal stress.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ dani hulu lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ mli baa lɛ baa shi. ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning light green and yellow starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Maize relies heavily on nitrogen to stay dark green and build leaves, so adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishifãi ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nɔ waa koni ehiɛ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli ni ekɛ baai aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the main difference between using animal manure and chemical fertilizer on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer supplies quick nutrients directly to plants, while animal manure improves the soil's structure over time, helping it hold moisture and organic nutrients for future seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii yaa hiɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ bei.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the same exact plot of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing the same crop drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and soil diseases that target maize to accumulate in the field year after year.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi.

english: What are these small caterpillars chewing holes in the center leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ ni miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing funnel of maize plants. Catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the crop's development.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji fallworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei ni daraa lɛ amli. Mra mli ni aaamɔ kɛ ekwɛmɔ Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashweremɔ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting and dying even though the soil around them is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Wilting in wet soil is typically caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial diseases that block the water channels inside the plant stem, preventing water from reaching the upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ mli shwiemɔ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tsiɔ nu gbɛi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell when my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmei shishifã ko da bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready to harvest when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, plant growth slows down, and cracks start appearing in the soil around the base of the stem from swelling tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ fee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tsei adalɛ baa shi. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ amli.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, poor pollination, or a lack of key soil nutrients like boron. Ensuring insects can visit your farm or gently shaking the plants helps pollination, while balanced fertilizing keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. pollination ni ehiii Aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ boron bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ ni kooloi bibii aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli loo okɛ tsei lɛ akpokpo blɛoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa yɛ pollination mli Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛhaa lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe.

english: Why are my young orange fruits falling off the tree before they get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fruit drop happens when the tree is stressed by irregular rainfall, pest attacks, or lack of nutrients. Supplying steady water during dry spells and applying balanced fertilizer helps the tree hold onto its fruit until harvest.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ miigba tsei anaa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ eyibii lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive under full, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides living shade that keeps the plants cool and moist during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ebaaha hulutsoo ni baaye abua ni tso lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt during the middle of the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than roots can suck it up. The plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from drying out, and it will usually stand back up once the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, eteɔ shi kɛ́ hulu lɛ nyɔ shi

english: How can I tell if my maize crop needs extra plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-abele lɛ he miihia tso niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: If maize leaves start turning light green or yellow starting from the leaf tip and moving along the center, the soil lacks nitrogen. Healthy maize plants should have broad, deep-green leaves.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni nyiɛɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Esa akɛ abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ.

english: Is it bad to burn my land before planting my crops?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ mashã mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, burning destroys good insects, burns away helpful organic food in the soil, and dries out the earth. Clearing without burning leaves plant residue that rots into natural food for your crops and keeps the soil moist.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shãa gbeɔ ŋmeii kpakpai. Shãa niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi Clearing ni ashãaa baai ni fiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curled, yellow cassava leaves are usually a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava stems provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Abaanyɛ atsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi kɛhaa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot whenever it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain and darkness create high dampness that causes Black Pod disease, a fungal attack. Pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air into the cocoa farm to dry the pods quickly and prevent the rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ duŋ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa ni ekɛ black pod hela, ni ji ŋmei baa. Afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya ni amɛkafite.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist diseases, grow evenly, and produce heavy yields. Seeds saved from past harvests slowly lose their strength over time and often yield much less.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai. kwɛ̃ɔ daa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Hewalɛ ni baa shi yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ ewoɔ nɔ ni faaa kwraa.

english: Spacing maize about 80 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between plants ensures the roots do not fight over soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to bigger cobs.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmãa ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ teŋ lɛ ji aaafee sɛntimita 80, ni tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji aaafee sɛntimita 40. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkayeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Plantain leaves have large surface areas that lose water quickly in high heat. During dry spells, the plant naturally sheds its lower outer leaves to conserve moisture and protect its main stem until the rains return.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛbu tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ he kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Plantains do not have deep taproots; their root system spreads out shallowly near the topsoil. When the heavy fruit bunch develops, the plant becomes top-heavy, so supporting the stem with a wooden prop or bamboo stick keeps it standing.
ga: Plantains bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Eshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa fioo. ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsɔ Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi shwiili babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ tsei loo ŋmei tsei afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni enyɛ edamɔ shi.

english: Why do baby shoot suckers keep growing around the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbekɛbii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui titri lɛ shishitoo

english: Plantains reproduce naturally by producing baby shoots called suckers from their underground stem. Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal water and nutrients from the mother plant, so you should cut them back to keep only one or two strong stems.
ga: Dumɔwui fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ofo mli koni okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 1-2 pɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce smaller bunches when planted too close to other trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwereɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei krokomɛi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves need full sunlight to make energy for growing large fruit. When plants are crowded, they shade each other out and compete for soil nutrients, which leads to thin, light bunches.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaawo aduawai wuji. Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛhaa amɛhe hulutsoo ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei niji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: What makes some plantain bunches heavier and fuller than others on my farm?
ga: Mɛni haa plantains akui komɛi feɔ mlɛo ni amɛyiɔ obɔ fe ekrokomɛi? yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: Bunch weight depends heavily on how much water and soil nutrients the mother plant gets while flowering. Keeping 6 to 8 healthy green leaves on the plant during the flowering stage ensures heavy, full fruits.
ga: Bunch weight damɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tso nyɛ lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai 6 kɛyashi 8 ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ewo yibii ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do plantains grow much faster after the first heavy rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are made of soft leaf layers that store large amounts of water. Once rain hits the soil, the plant quickly absorbs water and expanding nutrients, allowing it to push out new leaves every few days.
ga: Akɛ baai bibii ni toɔ nu babaoo lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tso lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ woɔ mli. Enɛ haa baai heei jeɔ kpo daa gbii fioo.

english: How does planting plantain trees help protect my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and keeping the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ha kookoo kane lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni oha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can I grow cassava together with my plantains on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu ŋmei kɛ plantains yɛ he kome?

english: Yes, but you must space them carefully. Cassava feeds heavily from the soil and needs sunlight, so planting it too close to plantains will cause both crops to fight for soil food and light.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo mli jogbaŋŋ. Cassavas yeɔ amɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la he miihia amɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ plantain tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei enyɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do I know when my green plantains are mature enough to harvest for market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantains eŋɔli lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa kɛha jara?

english: Look at the sharp ridges along the side of the fruit. When the fruit swells and those sharp edges start to round out, the plantain is fully mature and ready to cut while still green.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ afãi lɛ. Beni aduawai lɛ efu ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Plantains lɛ edara kwraa ni efee klalo akɛ abaakpa be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and soften so fast before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested plantains naturally release an invisible gas that speeds up ripening, especially when stacked in tight, warm spaces. Keeping harvested bunches in a cool, shaded, and well-ventilated area slows down ripening during storage and transport.
ga: Plantains ni akpa lɛ jieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni anaaa lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ato hei ni mli wa ni mli edɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which way to put my cassava stem cutting into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni ooofee ofolɔ o-cassava tso lɛ ni okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings have small buds where leaves sprout. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so the stem can grow smoothly; planting them upside down stops the plant from growing properly.
ga: Cassava tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi koni tso lɛ shishi lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ da ni etsɔ ŋwɛi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekada jogbaŋŋ.

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat stretch. If seeds sprout after one rain and then face days of dry heat, the young sprouts will dry up and die before the main rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛkɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ kpe. Tsobii bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baashɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, or that heavy rain has washed key nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii titrii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tight during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during hot periods as a natural defense to protect themselves from losing water through evaporation.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni baatsi nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do I need to put tall bamboo sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ ama shi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam plants produce bigger tubers when their leaves catch maximum sunlight. Staking lifts the foliage high off the ground so leaves catch light easily and stay away from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji kɛji amɛbaai lɛ shɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛmɔmɔ la oya ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I apply chemical fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔji lɛ amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying it to dry soil traps high concentrations of chemical salts around the roots and burns them.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, emɔɔ tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ni eshãa amɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dirt inside the stem funnel?
