ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji yɛ stem cones lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf funnel of young maize plants to feed on soft new growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baai amli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii ni eda lɛ.

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow small even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa po lɛ?

english: Weeds aggressively steal hidden soil nutrients and root space. Even with ample rain, your crops stay small because weeds are taking the food needed to produce leaves and fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ heɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai kɛ aduawai.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade to protect young cocoa plants while keeping the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow green. It can also happen when too much water around the roots prevents the plant from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii ni akɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nu ebɔle he. Shishifãi babaoo haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What causes my cassava plants to grow very tall with many leaves but yield very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tso lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Leaf curling is the plant's natural defense mechanism against extreme heat and sunlight to prevent water from evaporating out of its leaves too quickly.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ji tso adebɔɔ hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa. Enɛ ji koni nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or when there are no bees and insects around to pollinate the flowers so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii bɛ he fɛɛ he. Koni ekɛ fɔfɔii lɛ awo pollination mli koni aduawai aba.

english: How can I tell if armyworms have invaded my maize farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji cutworms ebote mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You will notice ragged holes eaten into the leaves at the top funnel of the plant, along with dark, sawdust-like waste left inside the central leaves by the caterpillars.
ga: Obaana buji ni ekpɔtɔ ni aye yɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ amli. Kɛfata jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmei ni ŋmeii lɛ shiɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and fall over easily when I plant the seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee ni egbɛɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, forcing them to grow tall, thin, and weak in an effort to reach the light.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛdara, amɛfee mlɛo, ni amɛgbɔjɔ yɛ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbɔɔ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he lɛ mli.

english: Is it better to plant my cassava cuttings immediately after the first rain of the season?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, planting right after the first rain ensures the soil has enough moisture for the stem cuttings to grow strong roots quickly before any short dry spell occurs.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku aba.

english: Why shouldn't I save hybrid maize seeds from my current harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ hybrid corn dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni yaa nɔ bianɛ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds only give their best yield in the first generation; if you replant seeds saved from that harvest, the new crops will grow unevenly and produce much smaller yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Nibii heei ni aduɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop without extra cost.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni awooo he nyɔmɔ kroko.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains alongside my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Plantain trees grow fast and have broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts on my land makes the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei ni adu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes, which means their roots naturally take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When you plant maize in that same field later, the maize uses that trapped nitrogen to grow greener and stronger.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ sɛɛ mli lɛ odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build green leaves. Applying fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure early in the plant's life prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my field as soon as I sow my seeds or wait until they sprout?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ loo mamɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃?

english: It is best to wait about two weeks after seeds sprout before applying fertilizer like NPK. Applying fertilizer too early can burn tender new roots, whereas waiting until shoots appear allows the roots to absorb the food safely.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsi enyɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK awo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi heei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ kɛyashi ŋmeii baaje kpo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ niyenii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young cassava shoots if cassava grows so easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava shwieɔ shi kɛji cassava kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo?

english: Even though cassava is tough, weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young cassava stems. Clearing weeds during the first three months helps the plant build large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei mli wa moŋ Shi jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmei tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji etɛ lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the damp ground toward full sunlight. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant, which leads to bigger yam tubers growing beneath the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Baai kɛ hulu la feɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Which type of plantain suckers should I dig up from an old farm to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: You should pick 'sword suckers', which have narrow, spear-like leaves and a heavy base. They grow faster and yield bigger plantain bunches than 'water suckers', which have broad leaves early on but weak stems.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala ‘Sword Bud’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli tseee ni tamɔ akpɔlɔ kɛ shishitoo ni tsii. Amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwui wuji fe ‘suckers’, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ. Shi eyɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves and leaves dark powder inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the leaf whorl. You can control them by spraying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the center funnel of the plant early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ahe ŋmeii lɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oooshwie tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the sap and passing along a plant virus. Spraying your pepper plants with a mild soapy water solution or neem oil helps keep these insects away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ Loo neem fɔ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eshwie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when temperatures get too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Giving your plants consistent water and light mulching helps keep soil moisture steady so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi daa bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do agricultural officers advise me to plant my crops using exact measurements like 10 by 10 instead of just estimating space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ mikɛ susumɔi pɔtɛɛ, tamɔ 10 x 10 atsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii, moŋ fe ni mabu he ni miyɔɔ lɛ he akɔntaa kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without competing with neighboring plants, leading to healthier growth and better yields.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ Enɛ haa amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How can I tell if my farm layout is correctly set up to give my crops the best chance to grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ koni eha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: A properly planned farm uses measured grid spacing recommended by extension officers, allowing equal growing space, easy weeding, and proper air movement between plants.
ga: Okwaafoi ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛ grid sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni ekstenshin onukpai lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ tsuɔ nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni anáa he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ajieɔ jwɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni sa tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ.

english: Is it safe for me to plant cassava, plantain, and cocoyam together on the same piece of land alongside my cocoa?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmei, plantain, kɛ kookoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ mikookoo lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, mixing these crops is a common practice, but you must space them carefully so fast-growing food crops do not choke or completely block sunlight from delicate trees like cocoa.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ. Shi esa akɛ okɛ ohe akabɔ he jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji koni niyenii ni aduɔ oya lɛ akatsi hulu la ni jɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ kookoo mli lɛ anaa loo akatsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Can I grow cocoyam under my plantain trees without harming either crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ dumɔwui ashishi ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, cocoyam naturally thrives in partial shade and cooler, moist soil, making it a great crop to grow underneath taller plants like plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains shishi.

english: Why do farmers around me plant food crops like plantain and cassava on new cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ miidu niyenii tamɔ plantains kɛ cassava yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Food crops provide quick food and income for your family while waiting several years for slow-maturing cocoa trees to start producing pods.
ga: Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ji niyenii kɛ shika jɛɛhe oya kɛha oweku lɛ. Beni amɛmɛɔ afii babaoo koni cacao tsei ni shwereɔ sɛɛ lɛ aje shishi amɛwo ŋmeii lɛ,.

english: How does planting plantain trees on my farm help my young cocoa trees survive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight, so fast-growing plantain trees act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade and cool soil it needs.
ga: Kokoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why is plantain preferred over cassava for shading my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihalaa plantain moŋ fe ŋmei koni mikɛwo mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe shade lɛ?

english: Plantains grow tall with high leafy canopies that shade cocoa without crowding it, whereas cassava grows bushy leaves low to the ground and heavy roots that can starve nearby seedlings.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa kɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛlɛ ni haa kookoo lɛ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kui amli ni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni baanyɛ aha hɔmɔ aye dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings need special shade management while cassava and plantain do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei kɛ plantain he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Cocoa seedlings are very delicate and sensitive to full heat early in life, whereas cassava and plantain are tough crops that love direct sunlight from the day they are planted.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ ahe waaa waa ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ he kwraa yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli mra. Yɛ be mli ni cassava kɛ plantain ji tsei ni wa ni sumɔɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ gbi ni adu amɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa plants small and hidden while the cassava plants around them are growing very wild?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni cassava tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ shwereɔ yɛ koo mli lɛ?

english: Cassava grows much faster than cocoa and can easily steal all the light and nutrients, hiding and weakening the cocoa if left unpruned or planted too close.
ga: Cassava daa oya kwraa fe kookoo. Ni ebaanyɛ eju la kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ oya. Ekɛ kookoo teeɔ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsɔ.

english: What happens if I plant too many different crop types too close together on one farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Overcrowding causes crops to fight over water and fertilizer in the soil, resulting in stunted plants, low harvests, and weaker crops being overgrown by aggressive ones.
ga: Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni egbɔjɔ lɛ baa. ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa shi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei yeɔ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees grow quickly and have broad leaves that shade delicate young cocoa seedlings from harsh sunlight while helping keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Do young cocoa trees still need manual watering if they are under shade trees like plantains?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ niji awo kookoo tsei bibii lɛ anɔ nu lolo kɛji amɛyɛ tsei tamɔ plantains shishi?

english: Yes, even under shade, young cocoa trees need direct watering around their bases during dry periods because the plantain trees also compete for water in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ hu biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ he yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui hu kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ.

english: How do plantain trees and cocoa plants share water when grown in the same field?
ga: Te cacao dumɔwui kɛ tsei lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjaa nu kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Both plants draw moisture from the soil, but plantains consume a lot of water due to their size. You must ensure extra water reaches the young cocoa roots so they do not dry out.
ga: Tsei enyɔ nɛɛ fɛɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shi plantains yeɔ nu babaoo yɛ bɔ ni amɛdara ha lɛ hewɔ. Obaasumɔ ni okwɛ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ayashɛ kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Can pests and diseases on my plantain trees spread to my cocoa plants?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mi kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, pests or diseases attacking plantains can spread to neighboring cocoa trees if the infestation is left untreated.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni tutuaa cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã cacao tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ni atsaaa lɛ

english: What signs show that my plantain trees are getting infested by pests?
ga: Mɛni ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai miihe mi plantains lɛ?

english: Common signs of pest infestation include yellowing or wilting leaves, holes in the leaves or stem, stunted growth, and visible insects on the leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba lɛ ahe ji baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni shwieɔ shi. bu ni yɔɔ baai loo tsei lɛ amli ni haa amɛdaraaa kɛ kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ

english: What should I do if the plantain trees protecting my cocoa start showing signs of sickness?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-cocoa shelter dumɔwui lɛ bɔi hela he okadii jiemɔ?

english: Inspect the sick plantain trees immediately, treat them with appropriate remedies, or trim infected leaves so the sickness does not transfer to your cocoa.
ga: Kwɛmɔ plantains ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ atsu nii kɛtsa hela lɛ. Aloo ŋmɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã kookoo lɛ nɔ.

english: How often should I inspect my farm for crop sickness and pests?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mana tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai?

english: It is best to set a regular weekly timetable to walk through every part of your farm so you catch any signs of disease before they spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooto gbɛjianɔ daa otsi ni okɛnyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ fãi fɛɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ona hela he okadi dani egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why is it bad to rush through inspecting my crops for pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oyaiyeli ni akɛkwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ lɛ?

english: Rushing through inspection makes it easy to miss early signs of disease or pest damage, allowing small problems to turn into big losses.
ga: Oya ni akwɛɔ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ hela loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe okadii mra. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, naagbai bibii tsɔɔ nibii ni laajeɔ wuji.

english: Why should I assign specific workers to water cocoa trees intercropped with plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha nitsulɔ pɔtɛɛ ko ni ekɛ nu awo cacao tsei ni akɛ plantains ewo mli lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Assigning dedicated workers ensures that every young cocoa tree gets proper, careful watering at its roots without any plants being overlooked.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni ejɔɔ amɛhe nɔ ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe nɔ lɛ haa akwɛɔ koni afɔ cacao tso bibioo fɛɛ tso bibioo nɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli ni akuuu hiɛ ashwieee tso ko nɔ.

english: Will maintaining a strict work schedule help me protect my crops better?
ga: Ani nitsumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa ni abaakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, a strict schedule ensures that essential care like watering, weeding, and pest checks happen at the right time rather than being delayed or rushed.
ga: Hɛɛ, gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli wa haa akwɛɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ nɔ. ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ baaba yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsi ohe loo ooofee oya

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow and dying after muddy water from a nearby river flooded my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi beni nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ eyi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Muddy river water contaminated by illegal mining carries heavy sediment and toxic chemicals. This chokes plant roots, blocks oxygen, and poisons the soil so crops cannot absorb nutrients.
ga: Faa lɛ mli nu ni mli ewo muji, ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ efite lɛ, mli eyi kɛ tsofai fɔji ni tsii. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anaa. ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ naa lɛ naa ni ekɛ tsofa fɔŋ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Can I still plant crops on land where people previously dug deep pits for galamsey?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni gbɔmɛi efo bu ni mli kwɔ kɛha galamsey lɛ nɔ lolo?

english: Topsoil containing natural plant nutrients is usually lost during mining. To farm there again, you must level the land and rebuild soil fertility with compost and manure, which takes time and effort.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ laajeɔ yɛ be mli ni akuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛji oosumɔ ni otsu okwaayeli yɛ jɛmɛ ekoŋŋ Esa akɛ Ofee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ biɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa take several years to give fruit, while crops like maize take only a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani tsei tamɔ kookoo woɔ yibii lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa heɔ nyɔji fioo pɛ?

english: Perennial trees invest their early years in building strong trunks and deep root systems so they can produce crops for decades, whereas short-season crops put all their energy into producing seeds quickly before dying.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ kɛ amɛshika woɔ shishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni afee tsei ashishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii afii nyɔŋmai abɔ. Yɛ kukufoo mli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo dumɔwui oya dani amɛgboi.

english: How do I know when my crops are fully ripe so I do not harvest them too early and waste my effort?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni wɔkakpa nii oya ni wɔfite mɔdɛŋbɔɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as pods changing color, leaves drying naturally, or fruit turning firm and sweet; picking too early leads to small yields and lower market value.
ga: Tsei lɛ baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ amɛfee klalo, tamɔ ŋmeii ni amɛhe su tsakeɔ kɛ baai ni egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Aloo aduawai lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni ŋɔɔ. Nihalamɔ mra tsɔ haa sɛɛnamɔi ni baa shi kɛ jara ni baa shi baa.

english: Why does my cassava crop stay green and healthy even when rain has not fallen for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassavas lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo ni eyɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko be kakadaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Cassava has thick underground roots that store water and nutrients, allowing the plant to survive severe drought far better than shallow-rooted crops.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt even when I water them regularly from a stream near a mining site?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa kɛjɛɔ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ he ni atsuɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If the water contains harmful chemicals or fine silt from upstream mining, it damages delicate root hairs, preventing the plant from drinking water properly.
ga: Kɛji tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo sũ bibii ni jɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai amli lɛ yɛ nu lɛ mli lɛ Ebaakpata shishifãi ahe yitsɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahiɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, tsei nyɛɛɛ anu nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops give smaller harvests every year if I plant the same crop on the same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season; rotating different crops helps rest the soil and restore balance.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ Haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my maize plants turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are a common sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil, meaning the plant lacks the main nutrient required to build strong, green leaves.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ aba.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind begins to blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tsei lɛ ahe baai babaoo fiteɔ kɛ́ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi etswa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees intentionally shed leaves during extreme dry weather to reduce water loss through their foliage, protecting the main stem and roots until rain returns.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa lɛ koni nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi. Buu tso titri lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, allowing them to overpower young crops if not cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa jwɛi yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii anɔ kunim kɛji ajieee amɛ mra.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a recommended nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and healthy.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are small worms eating the tender leaves inside the middle of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the heart of the maize plant during the hot afternoon and feeds at night. Catching them early and applying organic neem spray or recommended crop protection products protects the leaves so the crop can mature.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛtsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ organic neem spray loo tsofa ni abuɔ tso he ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe koni tso lɛ anyɛ eda.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to them acts like a living umbrella, protecting the seedlings from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoot suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajieɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many suckers attached to one plantain stem forces them to fight each other for food and water in the soil. Removing weaker suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main stem to produce a larger bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ plantain tso kome nɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi, ni no baaha ŋmeii titri lɛ afee ŋmeii agbo.

english: How do I know which part of a cassava stem is best to plant for a good yield?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ odu koni onine ashɛ yibii kpakpai anɔ?

english: The strong, mature middle portion of a healthy cassava stem makes the best planting material. Soft green tops dry out easily and very old bottom stems sprout slowly, while middle cuttings sprout quickly and produce strong roots.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni mli wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛduɔ nii. Tsofɔi eŋɔli bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni shishigbɛ tsei ni edara lɛ daa blɛoo. Yɛ be mli ni nine ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni ebaawo shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and produce food, which is sent down to swell the underground tuber. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and giving the plant maximum sunlight to grow bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛheɔ hulu la ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fitemɔ naa ni oha hulu la babaoo bɔ ni ooonyɛ koni eye ebua o-sweet potato tsei lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Tomato flowers often drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when soil nutrients are unbalanced. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ tsei amli loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa lɛ Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What causes the leaves of my pepper plants to curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites that attack young shoots. Inspecting under the leaves and spraying with neem oil or mild soap water early keeps these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni tutuaa ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni okɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ shwie nɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: Why is it better to leave cleared weeds on top of the ground instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni aaashã lɛ?

english: Leaving cut weeds on the farm covers the ground like a blanket, keeping the soil cool and moist during hot days. As the weeds rot, they feed the soil, whereas burning destroys nutrients and leaves the soil dry.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ ni edɔɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ egbo lɛ Amɛbaaye niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni la ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli gĩɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer on my field right before a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer off the field and into nearby gutters or streams before the crop roots can soak it up. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist or before a light shower so the nutrients sink into the root zone.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui loo faai ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo fioo dani nugbɔ anɛ koni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ abote shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food or a sign of water stress. When maize lacks nitrogen—a key nutrient it gets from soil or fertilizer—or when the soil is too wet, the plant cannot produce enough green chlorophyll to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii ni abiɔ loo nu he haomɔ he okadi. Beni nitrogen ni ji niyenii titri ni anáa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ bɛ ŋmãa mli loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee klorofil eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crop curl up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. When the sun is too hot, the plant rolls its leaves to protect itself from losing too much water through evaporation, keeping its moisture inside until the air cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu babaoo ni amɛbaafite kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ emli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the plant doesn't get enough water, or when tiny insects aren't moving pollen around. Without successful pollination or under stress, the plant drops the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tsiii pollen lɛ kɛyaa he fɛɛ he. Kɛji akɛ pollination lɛ yeee omanye loo oyɛ haomɔ shishi. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce so many tiny flowers, but only a few turn into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ fioo ko pɛ tsɔɔ cocoa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree naturally creates thousands of flowers, but only flowers visited by tiny flying insects called midges get pollinated to become pods. The tree also drops extra flowers it cannot support with water and nutrients.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi fɔfɔi ni kooloi bibii ni foɔ yɔɔ mli pɛ yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Mɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges ni baasara lɛ pɛ baanyɛ afee pollination ni amɛtsɔmɔ pods. Tso lɛ hu shwieɔ fɔfɔi krokomɛi ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with large leaves, but producing very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa kɛ baai wuji shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen and too little potassium, the plant puts all its strength into growing tall branches and big leaves above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium hu faaa tsɔ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo niji kakadaji kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato tuber ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are ready for harvest without digging up the mound?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Yams tell you they are mature through their foliage. When the leaves and vines stop growing green, turn yellow, and naturally dry up at the end of the season, it means the plant has finished sending food down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ bo bɔ ni amɛdara ha kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ kpa ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe niyenii ni ekɛmajeɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting in peppers is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves. Their feeding damages the leaf veins, causing new leaves to grow deformed and wrinkled.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ. Enɛ haa baai heei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during rainstorms even when they carry heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli kɛ́ jwɛi ni tsii po eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains fall when their root system is weakened underground. Tiny worms called nematodes or insect larvae chew through the roots, leaving the stem with no strong anchor in the soil to hold heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly during the dry Harmattan season even when I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops slow down in the Harmattan because the air is extremely dry and the nights are cold. Even with water at the roots, dry winds force the plant to work harder to stay alive rather than using energy to grow fast.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ Harmattan lɛ eba shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa kɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ Shi kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi hu haa tsei tsuɔ nii waa koni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii koni eda oya lɛ

english: Why do my okra seeds take much longer to sprout out of the ground than my maize seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okra dumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛjeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Okra seeds have a very tough, thick outer shell that takes several days to absorb water before the baby plant inside can break out, whereas maize seeds have softer coats that soak up water quickly.
ga: Roselle dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa waa ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eheɔ gbii babaoo dani ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tso bibioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ gbálaa. Shi ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ yɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shwieɔ nu oya.

english: Why is it important for me to keep my cocoa farm clean and free from bush?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ maha mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni jwɛi akafee nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Weeds and overgrown bushes steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Keeping your farm clean prevents pests and diseases from hiding in the brush, helping your trees build strong foundations and produce more pods.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ jwɛi lɛ amli. Ye obua otso lɛ ni etswa shishitoo ni wa ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Why must I leave enough space between my cocoa trees when planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for food and their foliage blocks sunlight from each other. Proper spacing ensures each tree develops a strong foundation, grows large, and yields healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋshii mli ni tsei ahe baai tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa shishitoo ni wa, edaa, ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need shade trees when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa tsei ni haa hulutsoo be mli ni ehe ehiaaa lɛ? Ani eji bibioo lolo?

english: Young crops have tender roots and leaves that easily dry out under hot, direct sunlight. Temporary shade crops protect the young plants until their root foundation is deep and strong enough to survive full sun exposure.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ba amɛnɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli lɛ baabu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi shishifã lɛ shishitoo lɛ mli kwɔ ni ewa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to cut away small branches and chupon shoots from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? Ni chappon ŋmeii ni jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cutting unwanted shoots lets air and sunlight flow through the tree canopy. This stops fungal diseases like black pod from taking hold and directs the tree's energy into developing larger, healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ akamɔ tso lɛ mli, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has lost its nutrients and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When soil becomes weak, leaves turn yellowish, trees stop growing vigorously, and crop yields drop. Applying organic manure or balanced fertilizer restores the soil's strength so the crops can feed properly.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ Tso lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ waa. ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ ba shi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye abua lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young cocoa pods turning black and rotting on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp, and dark conditions. Clearing weeds and trimming thick branches allows sunlight into the farm to dry out the air and protect your pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji black pod hela, ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ waa lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ agbi ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops drop their leaves and look weak during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry periods, plants shed leaves to save water and protect themselves from drying out completely. Once rains return, the crop uses stored energy in its roots to sprout fresh leaves and flower.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, Dumɔwui kɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei.

english: How does leaving dry leaves around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Te mi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tso lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground with dead leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt and cools the roots. Over time, these leaves decay and turn into rich soil food for the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai gboi haa nɔ Atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ shikpɔŋ niyenii ni baa nii kɛhaa tsei lɛ.

english: Why do Mirids or capsids attack my cocoa trees more when new leaves start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ myrids loo capsids lɛ tutuaa mi cacao tsei lɛ babaoo kɛ́ baai heei je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Mirid insects feed on soft, fresh bark and tender shoots. When your trees produce new leaves, pests are attracted to the soft food, so you must inspect your farm regularly to catch them early.
ga: Mirid ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni yɔɔ ehee kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛji otso lɛ jie baai heei lɛ, niyenii ni mli jɔ lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa koni onyɛ omɔ amɛ mra.

english: Why should I clear wild roots and stumps before planting new crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie shishifãi kɛ tsei akutsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ dani madu tsei heei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing old roots and hard stumps opens up the soil so young seedlings can easily push their roots deep into the earth. It creates a clean, strong foundation for your crops to grow without competition.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie shishifãi momoi kɛ tsei akutsei ni wa lɛ, ebaagbele shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ashɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya. Tsɔɔmɔ shishitoo ni he tse ni mli wa koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there is full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender, sensitive leaves that easily scorch under direct sun. Giving them shade using temporary nurse crops like plantain keeps the environment humid and cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ akɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shihilɛ lɛ mli feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my orange trees shed many of their small fruits long before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii lɛ? Bulk dani efee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Fruit drop usually happens when a tree is under stress from prolonged dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks. The tree sheds excess fruit it cannot support to save enough energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ shishi be kakadaŋŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Tso lɛ baawo yibii babaoo aahu akɛ enyɛŋ eye ebua hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and weak with small leaves when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ kɛlɛ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ baai bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing plants properly allows each crop enough space and sunlight to build strong stems.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb on instead of trailing on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to produce food for the tubers growing underground. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground by staking also prevents leaves from rotting and catches more light.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ tso ni akɛwoɔ amɛnɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛkafiteɔ, ni ehaa amɛnáa la babaoo.

english: Yellowing starting from the lowest leaves of maize usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green leaves. Feeding the soil with compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Sũ lɛ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava have massive leaves and thick stems but tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or receives excessive rain, the cassava plant directs all its food to leafy growth instead of underground root expansion. Balancing soil nutrients encourages tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ eniyenii lɛ fɛɛ woɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa.

english: How does placing dry grass around the roots of my pepper plants help them grow?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te pepper tso shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in hot weather, keeps soil cool, reduces weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich soil food.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ Ehaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows pests that feed on that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating crops keeps the soil balanced and healthier.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ daa be mli, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes small green worms to eat holes in the leaves inside the center funnel of my maize?
ga: Nɔ ni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms that hatch from moth eggs laid inside the young maize shoot. Applying recommended organic or chemical remedies early into the center funnel stops them from destroying the plant's growing tip.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ amli. Akɛ tsofai ni akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai tsuɔ nii mra lɛ he ŋaawoo haa. kɛtee ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli koni ekafite tso lɛ naagbee ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the blossom ends on the bottom of my tomatoes turn black and rot as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black, sunken spots on tomato bottoms are caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often triggered by uneven watering. Keeping soil moisture steady helps the plant move calcium into the fruit.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and die when I clear all the trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. Leaving taller trees or planting fast-growing plants like plantains gives cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ni eshiɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ Aloo, tsei ni daa oya lɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ baaha kookoo lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that pull nitrogen fertilizer straight from the air into the soil. The maize feeds on this natural fertilizer, helping it grow taller and greener without extra cost.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmɔshi nibii krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yeɔ ŋmãa. Ye obua ni eda ni ekɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ akafite ni nɔ ko nɔ ko fataaa he.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen in the soil. The maize plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves, turning the bottom ones yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi tsei juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baa bibii lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become watery and rot when left in the soil during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains soak the ground for too long without draining, the roots drown, absorb too much water, and begin to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni amɛmɔɔ nu babaoo. ni ebɔi fitemɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees give smaller bunches when I let many suckers grow around one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ?

english: All the shoots growing from the same plantain stem fight for the same food and water in the soil. If you remove the extra suckers and leave only one or two, the mother plant can send all its energy to making a large bunch.
ga: Tso kome mli tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛji ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni eshwɛ ekome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii agbo.

english: Why are my tomato flowers dropping off the stem instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they get too hot or dry. Under severe heat or water stress, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy so the whole plant doesn't dry up.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo edɔ. yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ shishi Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Koni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ akagbi

english: How can planting a ground cover crop help me stop weeding my farm so often?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makpa miŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwiemɔ shii abɔ lɛ?

english: Cover crops like Mucuna grow low and fast, spreading thick leaves over the ground like a carpet. This carpet blocks sunlight from reaching the dirt, preventing weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei tamɔ Mucuna lɛ daa shi shiŋŋ ni amɛdaraa oya. Amɛgbɛ amɛbaai ni mli tse lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti. Tade nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ muji he. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the floor?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tso ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make food that builds the big tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the dark, wet ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay safe from rot.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli nibii ni akɛfeɔ niyenii ni feɔ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛkafite.

english: Curled leaves are a sign that tiny insects like thrips or aphids are sucking the sap out of the young leaves, or that a plant virus has infected them. This damages the leaf structure and stunts growth.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids miimu nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. aloo tso mli hela ko ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ he ni ehaa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do crops grow so poorly on land where the top layer of soil has been cleared or dug away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie loo atsa lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: The dark topsoil contains almost all the food and organic matter crops need to grow. When heavy clearing or digging removes this top layer, you are left with hard subsoil that holds very little food or water for roots.
ga: Niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara lɛ ateŋ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni tsuɔ ediŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ ehe bahia ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo atsa shi waa koni ajie ŋwɛi fã nɛɛ, Shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni wa fioo ko pɛ ni toɔ niyenii loo nu kɛhaa shishifãi lɛ baashwɛ bo.

english: What happens if I leave ripe cocoa pods on the tree for too long without harvesting them?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni mikpaaa amɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree too long causes the beans inside to start germinating or rotting. Overripe pods also attract pests and encourage fungal diseases like black pod to spread across your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ pods diji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell when my cocoa pods are fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Cocoa pods change color when mature. Pods that started green turn yellow, while pods that started red or purple turn orange or yellow-orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, pods ni jeɔ shishi kɛ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ-ŋmɔŋ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods dry up and turn black while they are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Small pods drying up can be due to a natural thinning process called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops excess pods it cannot feed. However, if they turn black and soft, it is caused by black pod disease, which thrives in cool, damp conditions.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii bibii ni egbi lɛ jɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa tso lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, ni tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aha lɛ niyenii lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Shi, kɛji amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfee blɛoo lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ

english: Why do some cocoa pods turn soft and dark brown right on the tree before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in wet weather and shady fields. Removing these infected pods from the tree and carrying them off the farm helps protect your remaining harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔji ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ojie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are some parts of my cocoa farm growing thick with heavy leaves while other areas look thin and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fãi komɛi amli eyi kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? be mli ni hei krokomɛi Look ni egbɔjɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ?

english: Uneven growth happens when sunlight, water, or soil nutrients are spread unevenly across your farm. Overgrown areas usually have too much shade or crowded trees, while thin areas often suffer from poor soil, pest attack, or too much direct sunlight.
ga: Dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baa kɛji akɛ hulu la, nu, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlijaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni tsei ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo loo tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Yɛ be mli ni hei komɛi Bei pii lɛ, amɛkɛ naagbai ni kɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛhe, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo lɛ he lɛ kpeɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to prune overgrown branches on my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or excess branches so sunlight and air can circulate through the farm. Good airflow dries up wet leaves quickly, which stops black pod disease from growing and encourages the tree to produce more pods lower down.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ niji ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ. Bɔni afee ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ lɛ baaha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ haaa black pod hela lɛ aya hiɛ ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ pods babaoo awo shishigbɛ.

english: How does clearing heavy weeds from my farm help my cocoa trees yield better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni tsii ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mikoo tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients that your cocoa trees need to make pods. Keeping your farm floor clean gives your trees full access to plant food and keeps climbing weeds from suffocating young cocoa branches.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha ehe atse lɛ haa otsei lɛ náa tsei niyenii fɛɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɔɔ jwɛi lɛ koni kookoo niji bibii lɛ akagbɔjɔ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa trees growing very tall instead of spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mikoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees grow tall and thin when they are reaching for sunlight under heavy shade trees. Managing your shade trees and trimming the main stems early helps cocoa trees branch out wide so pods are easier to reach during harvest.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ yɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ashishi. Nibii ni haa hulutsoo tsei lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ ni afoɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ niji lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa babaoo koni enyɛ eshɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe oya yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to save water and protect themselves from heat. Planting permanent shade trees helps buffer your farm against harsh sun and dry harmattan winds so the cocoa trees stay green.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ he. Koni kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji

english: Does removing shade trees completely make cocoa trees grow more pods?
ga: Ani tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha cacao tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Full sunlight can increase pod production for a few years, but without shade, cocoa trees get stressed quickly, require much more fertilizer, and die much younger. Moderate shade keeps your farm healthy and productive over many years.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha pod lɛ afee nɔ ni yaa hiɛ afii fioo komɛi. Shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be bɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ haoɔ oya. Ehe miihia ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mli ni egbo yɛ gbekɛbiiashi kwraa. Shade ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewoɔ yibii afii babaoo.

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off due to environmental stress like dry weather, lack of shade, or damage from small insects. Providing proper shade and ensuring the trees get enough moisture helps the flowers develop into young pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha tso lɛ ni akwɛ koni ená ŋmɔtɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ bibii.

english: Why should I cut off some of the extra branches from my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes weak, dead, or overcrowded branches so air and sunlight can reach all parts of the tree. This stops fungal diseases from breeding in damp leaves and encourages the tree to direct its energy into producing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egboi, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã he. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekafɔ yɛ baai ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. ni ewoɔ tsei hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfee kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa seedlings very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak trees. Good spacing gives each tree room to spread its branches and produce maximum pods.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. He ni ato jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu mli gbɛɔ eshwaa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and dry up during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry Harmattan winds and hot sun strip moisture from the leaves faster than the roots can drink from the dry soil. Keeping shade trees on your farm and covering the ground around the tree trunk with dry leaves (mulch) helps retain moisture.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi kɛ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ, ni okɛ baai ni egbi (Mulch) ha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it important to leave some big trees standing when I clear land for a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mashi tsei wuji ni amɛdamɔ shi beni mijieɔ shikpɔŋ kɛha kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: Large forest trees act as natural umbrellas that protect young cocoa trees from being scorched by strong sun and damaged by heavy winds. Cocoa grows healthiest under moderate, filtered sunlight.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni mli tse, ni mli tse mli.

english: What causes my healthy green cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy, humid weather. You can control it by cutting off infected pods immediately, clearing thick bush around the tree, and keeping the farm well-aerated.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Obaanyɛ okudɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ brɔshi ni mli tse ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni oha kɔɔyɔɔ ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly help my cocoa trees grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital food, water, and sunlight that your cocoa trees need to grow strong. Removing weeds also clears away hiding spots for pests that eat young cocoa leaves and pods.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa koni kookoo tsei lɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ hei ni kooloi ni yeɔ kookoo baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe lɛ kɛyaa.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is at the start of the rainy season when the soil is damp. The rainwater dissolves the fertilizer so the cocoa roots can easily soak up the food.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bɔni afee ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ oya.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest a cocoa pod?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa pod is ready for harvest when its skin changes color completely—usually turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange. Harvesting at this stage ensures the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni amɛhiɛ su tsakeɔ kwraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. aloo kɛjɛ tsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans with plantain leaves for a few days after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baai haa kookoo yibii heei ahe gbii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Covering fresh beans with plantain leaves allows them to ferment properly. Fermentation is essential because it develops the rich brown color and deep chocolate flavor inside the cocoa bean that buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfee ŋmeii jogbaŋŋ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ejaakɛ ehaa kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa kɛ tsokolate ni mli wa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil has lost its strength to grow good crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crops grow slowly, leaves become pale or yellow, and harvests get smaller each year. Adding manure, compost, or the right fertilizer puts nutrients back into the soil so your plants can thrive.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa fiofio. Baai lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ. ni nɔ ni anáa lɛ baa shi daa afi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaku sɛɛ ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Ni midu yɛ nakai gbɛ nɔ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth every time they grow. If you keep planting without giving nutrients back to the ground, the soil becomes exhausted, causing your crop yields to drop over time.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji odu ni okɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuuu sɛɛ kɛyaaaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ, sũ lɛ mli baafee shoo, ni no baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it possible to revive old, tired soil so it feels like fresh land again?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atswa shikpɔŋ ni egbɔ ni efite lɛ ekoŋŋ koni enu he akɛ eji shikpɔŋ hee ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, adding organic materials like animal manure, decomposed crop waste, or balanced fertilizers restores nutrients and organic matter, effectively giving your old land the strength of fresh, untouched soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa he. Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Ehaa oshikpɔŋ momo lɛ mli waa tamɔ shikpɔŋ hee ni he tse jogbaŋŋ.

english: My plantain trees are growing slowly and look weak, what is happening to them?
ga: Midumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ. Mɛni ba dumɔwui nɛɛ anɔ?

english: Plantains are heavy feeders that need lots of nutrients from the earth. Weak growth usually means the soil lacks essential food like nitrogen and potassium, which can be fixed by applying manure or plantain fertilizer around the base.
ga: Plantains ji niyenii ni tsii ni biɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium. Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo plantain ŋmei ni akɛbaabɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do crops on some farms look dark green and shiny while mine look dry and dull?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii komɛi ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ekpɛɔ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Dark green, shiny plants are getting proper nutrition and moisture from fertile soil. Plants look dry and dull when they suffer from poor soil nutrients, heat stress, or pest damage.
ga: Tsei ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ naa niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbi ni amɛhe efee shoo kɛji amɛnáa shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. hulutsoo haomɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efiteɔ

english: Why do plantains require richer soil compared to crops like cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni jara wa fe tsei tamɔ ŋmei he hiaa plantains lɛ?

english: Plantains produce heavy bunches and large leaves very quickly, which demands a high amount of soil nutrients and water, whereas cassava can survive on poorer soil because its roots store energy differently.
ga: Plantains lɛ woɔ panicles agboi kɛ baai agboi oya. ni biɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Cassava baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ohiafoi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ toɔ hewalɛ srɔtoi babaoo.

english: What does spraying liquid food or medicine on my crops actually do for them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ?

english: Spraying crop treatments can feed plants directly through their leaves or protect them from insects and diseases, allowing the plant to recover fast and grow healthier leaves and fruits.
ga: Tsei ahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi kɛ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhe wa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: How long does it take to see changes in my crops after spraying them with fertilizer or treatment?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mana tsakemɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofafeemɔ eshwie nɔ sɛɛ?

english: Foliar treatments applied to leaves work quickly; you will often see greener leaves and fresher growth within a few days to two weeks if the plant is receiving what it lacks.
ga: Foliar tsofai ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ ahe lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Bei pii lɛ, obaana baai eŋɔli kɛ shweremɔ hee yɛ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsii enyɔ mli kɛji akɛ aha tso lɛ nɔ ko ni he ehiaaa.

english: What makes farm produce look big and appealing at the market?
ga: Mɛni haa okwaayeli nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe yɔɔ fɛo yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Produce grows big and bright when crops get enough nutrients, proper water, and protection from pests during their growth stage, which allows the plant to send maximum energy into the harvest.
ga: Produce lɛ daa ni ekpɛɔ kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. yɛ nu ni sa Ni hebuu yɛ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli.

english: Does feeding the soil actually improve the look and quality of the crop yield?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni akɛyeɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛ bɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?
