english: Yes, well-fed soil feeds the roots, which leads to stronger stems, lush leaves, and bigger, healthier produce that commands better prices at the market.
ga: Hɛɛ, sũ ni ayeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe wa waa. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ nibii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni fãa jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is this farm input called 'lisaa', and how does it help my corn grow?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔ mli saji nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘Lisa’ lɛ ni te eyeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Lisaa (fertilizer) acts like rich food for your crops, feeding the soil with essential nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus so your corn plants gain the energy and strength needed to grow tall and produce large cobs.
ga: Lisa (ŋmeii) tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha onibii. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus haa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni eha o-corn tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my maize so it gets the most vitality?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ awo ŋmãa mli koni ená hewalɛ babaoo?

english: Maize needs nutrients most during its early growth. Applying fertilizer about two to three weeks after germination gives the young roots early strength, and a second application around flowering ensures big, full cobs.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa abele fe fɛɛ yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli aaafee otsii 2-3 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi bibii lɛ aná hewalɛ oya. ni nɔ ni ji enyɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ Flower he lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ aba.

english: Why do my crops look weak and pale even though I planted them in good soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ moŋ? Te nɔ ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa nɔ?

english: Plants pull nutrients out of the soil every season. Over time, the soil loses its natural strength and vitality, so without adding fertilizer or organic manure, your crops will lack the essential food they need to grow strong.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ehewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young crops need so much constant attention and daily care?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ midumɔwu lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be, daa gbi lɛ?

english: Young crops are like human infants—they are delicate and easily choked by weeds or destroyed by pests. Giving them regular attention ensures they get enough water, shade, and nutrients during their most critical growing weeks.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. Amɛhe waaa ni jwɛi shwieɔ amɛ loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ fiteɔ amɛ oya. Kɛ́ akwɛ amɛ daa lɛ, ebaaha amɛná nu, hulutsoo, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛdalɛ otsii ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds prevent my corn from growing big even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi tsiɔ mi-abele lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbors; they steal the fertilizer nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the strength from the soil goes straight into your corn plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa hewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa o-abele tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How often should I visit my field to check on my crops after planting?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔji amli koni mayakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu lɛ agbe naa?

english: It is best to visit your field at least two to three times a week. Regular checks allow you to catch pests, diseases, or dry soil early before they drain the crop's vitality and ruin your yield.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ, kɛ́ hooo kwraa lɛ, obaayasara onitsumɔhe nine lɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ otsi mli. Nibii amlipɛimɔ ni ooofee daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaafite hewalɛ ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ ni amɛbaafite onibii lɛ.

english: What makes maize stalks grow thick and strong instead of falling over in the wind?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: A thick maize stalk comes from strong root development and adequate nitrogen and phosphorus early in life. When young plants get enough nutrients and space, they build sturdy trunks capable of supporting heavy corn ears.
ga: Abɛi tsei ni mli tse lɛ jɛɔ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ mli. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ná niyenii kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Amɛwoɔ tsei ni wa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmãa toi ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are some corn plants on my farm growing very tall while others next to them stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ waa yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu shwereɔ waa lɛ? Mɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ daraaa.

english: Soil nutrition is often unequal across a field. Plants in spots with less fertility, poor water retention, or early weed competition will stay small, while plants in rich, well-nourished soil thrive and grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo. nu ni ehiii Aloo jwɛi komɛi yɛ ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ shishijee mli ni amɛbaafee bibii. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni niyenii yɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baashwere ni amɛdara.

english: How does feeding my crops early in the season change the final size of my corn harvest?
ga: Te niyenii ni mikɛhaa mi tsei lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baatsake mi naagbee ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Early feeding builds a strong root network and thick leaves early on. This solid foundation allows the plant to absorb more sunlight and water later, resulting in bigger ears and heavier grains at harvest time.
ga: Niyenii ni ayeɔ mra lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ baai ni mli wa baa mra. Nɛkɛ shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hulu la kɛ nu babaoo baa sɛɛ mli. Enɛ haa toi lɛ daraa ni dumɔwui lɛ tsiiɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: Why do my plants stop growing and look stressed during dry spells even if I fertilize them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni haoɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ amɛmli moŋ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Without moisture in the soil, the plant cannot swallow the nutrients, causing its growth to slow down until water is available again.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛshwie shi bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ ami niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa edalɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby acts as a natural umbrella, keeping the young trees cool and preserving soil moisture until their roots grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Is it really necessary to put tall wooden stakes next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi?

english: Yes, yam plants are climbing vines. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to produce large underground tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato tso lɛ miikwɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow big leaves. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or planting leguminous crops like cowpeas helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ baai wuji Nitrogen ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same patch of soil every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer maize to multiply in the field. Rotating with legumes restores nitrogen and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems to cut and plant for a good yield?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ni adu ŋmei tsei koni aná yibii kpakpai?

english: Select thick, healthy stems from mature cassava plants that are 8 to 12 months old. Cut pieces from the middle portion of the stem that have active buds and show no signs of insect damage or disease spots.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni mli tse ni mli wa kɛjɛ ŋmei tsei ni eda ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 lɛ amli. Kpɔ̃ɔ fãi kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɔɔ lɛ. ni ejieee okadi ko ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi efite loo hela ko yɛ he.

english: What causes small caterpillars to hide inside the centers of my young corn leaves and destroy them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. They lay eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central whorl of the plant to feed, which can severely ruin your harvest if not controlled early.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm lɛ. Amɛwoɔ wɔji yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛyatao niyenii. Enɛ baanyɛ afite onibii lɛ waa kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ mra.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce less food even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds steal the valuable fertilizers, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Even with rain, the weeds crowd out crop roots and prevent them from getting enough food to yield well.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaaa amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often due to uneven watering or dry soil spells while the fruit is growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why does my maize produce very small ears if I plant immediately after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa woɔ toi bibii waa kɛji akɛ adu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rains are often followed by unexpected dry spells. If young plants suffer from water shortages right after germinating, their growth gets stunted and they cannot produce full-sized corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ ahum ni akpaaa gbɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji tsei bibii lɛ na nu he naagba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ Tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekɛ ŋmãa toi ni dalɛ fɛɛ aba.

english: Why does my harvested maize get covered in powdery dust and small holes inside my storeroom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyi kɛ sũ kɛ bu bibii lɛ? yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by grain weevils that bore into dried corn to feed and lay eggs. Ensuring your maize is thoroughly dried before storage and keeping it in sealed hermetic bags prevents weevils from surviving.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ egbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛto ni okɛto kotoku ko ni atsĩ naa mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akahi shi.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves toward direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases and helps the plant produce larger yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong leaves.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni eye ebua ni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abele lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ je lɛŋ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing very tall with big leaves but almost no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Baai wuji shi pods ko kwraa bɛ mli?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes okra plants to put all their energy into growing stems and leaves instead of flowering and setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa okra tsei lɛ yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii lɛ

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme heat or dry soil as a defense mechanism to save water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni amɛdaraa yɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle kɔɔpoi ni mli wa lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and damaging them as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ be mli ni oyeɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my crops while the crop seedlings are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your seedlings if not removed early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya kɛha odumɔwui lɛ kɛji ajieee amɛ oya.

english: Groundnut plants naturally bury their fertilized flower stems under the soil because the actual nuts grow and mature underground where it is dark and safe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei tsei fuɔ amɛ fɔfɔi ni awo amɛ fɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ejaakɛ eji nuts diɛŋtsɛ. Edaa ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Cassava is typically mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack as the tubers enlarge underneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do some of my planted maize seeds fail to come up out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep in the ground, if the soil lacks moisture after planting, or if soil insects eat the seeds before they can germinate.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly when the rain stops for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves into tight tubes to conserve water and protect themselves from heat loss during dry spells.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli amɛwoɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa shi yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani pods jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face heat stress, lack sufficient shade, experience prolonged dry weather, or suffer from insect attacks that weaken the plant.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Shade ni sa ni bɛ ni akɛwoɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ loo ni kooloi ni yeɔ tso lɛ ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ yeɔ amanehulu.

english: Will using chemical spray for weeds every season hurt my farm's soil over time?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa afi lɛ baaye shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ awui yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Overusing chemical sprays can kill beneficial soil insects and organisms like earthworms, which weakens soil structure and lowers natural fertility over time.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi bibii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni no haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni ehaa bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know if a weedkiller spray will destroy my growing crops along with the weeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ baafite miŋmɔshinii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Selective weedkillers target specific broadleaf weeds or grasses without harming your crop, while non-selective ones kill all green plants on contact, so checking the product type beforehand prevents crop damage.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni ahalaa lɛ tsuɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ baai babaoo lɛ ahe nii tɛ̃ɛ ni eyeee oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ baagbe tsei eŋɔli fɛɛ ni kɛ amɛ kpeɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okwɛ nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in poorly drained soil, creating wet conditions where underground fungi can easily infect and destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu shwie shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii baanyɛ atswa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfite amɛ oya.

english: Why do armyworms always hide inside the middle funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: The central funnel of a young maize plant contains soft, tender leaves that are easy for armyworms to eat while shielding them from sunlight and birds.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni ŋmeii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ yeɔ mlɛo ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I plant my cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmei?

english: Tired soil often looks pale, forms hard crusts when dry, produces pale yellow crop leaves, or only grows weak weeds, indicating that key plant nutrients are exhausted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efeɔ ŋshɔŋloo ni wa kɛji egbi. Ehaa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Aloo jwɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ pɛ yɔɔ? Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ mli niyenii titrii lɛ etã.

english: Why does my pepper plant grow very tall with bushy green leaves but no flowers or peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni ekɛ baai eŋɔlii ebɔle ehe lɛ? Shi fɔfɔii loo ŋmeii bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Giving a pepper plant too much nitrogen fertilizer causes it to spend all its energy growing leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen babaoo ha o-pepper tso lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛbaa kɛ eshishifãi akwɛ̃. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: How can using motorized spraying machines help my cocoa farm compared to my manual knapsack sprayer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto tsɔne ni akɛ niji tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ he?

english: Motorized spraying machines blow chemical mists higher and faster, covering large cocoa farms in a fraction of the time. This saves you days of hard labor and ensures pests hiding in high branches are reached effectively.
ga: Motor ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa nɔ lɛ fɔ̃ɔ tsofa mli afua lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi oya. Ha kookoo ŋmɔji wuji ahe yɛ sɛkɛndii fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa okɛ gbii babaoo tsuɔ nii waa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni anyɛ ana tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei niji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ amli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will using a motorized weed cutter harm my cocoa trees compared to clearing weeds with a cutlass?
ga: Ani tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi ni akɛ tsɔne tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye mi-kokoo tsei lɛ awui? Kɛ akɛto jwɛi ni akɛ dade jieɔ lɛ he

english: Motorized weed cutters clear land much faster without exhausting you, but you must keep the machine's blade away from the base of the cocoa trunk so you do not strip the bark or damage shallow roots.
ga: Motor ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ baanyɛ ajie he ko oya ni egbɔjɔɔɔ bo. Shi esa akɛ okɛ tsɔne lɛ ŋmeii lɛ akashɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ ji koni okajie tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo okafite shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does it take so many years for my traditional cocoa trees to start producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kusum cacao tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ lɛ?

english: Older cocoa varieties take 4 to 5 years to mature because they grow slowly. Modern hybrid cocoa varieties produce pods much faster—often within 2 to 3 years—when given proper fertilizer, shade, and regular care.
ga: Kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛshɛɔ shweremɔ he beni amɛdaraa fiofio lɛ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid cocoa henɔi lɛ woɔ ŋmeii oya (bei pii lɛ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli) kɛji akɛ aha amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, hulutsoo kɛ kwɛmɔ daa.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods when the branches grow too thick and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ be mli ni eniji lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: When cocoa branches become overly thick, sunlight cannot reach the trunk where flowers form, and moisture gets trapped inside the canopy. Pruning excess branches allows air and light in, encouraging more flowering and reducing disease.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo niji lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ Hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. ni ŋmɔtɔ baatsi ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la boteɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi babaoo baa ni ehaa helai baa shi.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my cocoa seedlings very close together to fit more trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu kookoo dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too close together causes them to compete for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. This results in tall, weak trees that bear very few pods compared to properly spaced trees.
ga: Kɛ́ adu kokoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu he. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli kɛ akɛto tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Black pod rot is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather. Removing infected pods immediately and pruning extra branches helps sunlight dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod rot baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya, ni afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akagbi ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ

english: Why do many small cocoa flowers drop off the trunk without ever turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrition, or insect attacks. Protecting the trees from pests like capsids and keeping soil moist helps more flowers successfully turn into pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ Tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids lɛ ahe kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: How do I know if modern cocoa farming practices will work better than the traditional ways I learned growing up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ fe blema gbɛi ni mikase yɛ be mli ni mida lɛ he lɛ?

english: Traditional methods helped establish farms, but modern scientific techniques—such as hybrid seeds, motorized tools, and proper pruning—are designed to give higher yields in fewer years while reducing physical strain.
ga: Kusum gbɛi baanyɛ aye abua ni ama ŋmɔ. Shi ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ jeŋ nilee gbɛi tamɔ hybrid seeds motorized tools kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa Afee lɛ koni ekɛ nibii babaoo aba yɛ be fioo mli, yɛ be mli ni ebaa gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔnyɛɛ shi.

english: What happens to the beans inside if I leave ripe yellow cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni baa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ? Ni kɛji akɛ mishi kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ hu?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to sprout or rot. Sprouted beans ruin the flavor profile and lower the grade of your cocoa, reducing the price buyers will pay for your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Bean sprouts lɛ baafite ŋmɔlɔ lɛ ni ebaafite o-cocoa lɛ. Enɛ haa jara ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baawo kɛha onibii lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your young cocoa plants are getting too much direct sunlight or are lacking nutrients like nitrogen. Providing temporary shade crops like plantains and applying fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-cacao tso bibioo lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tɛ̃ɛ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ mli. Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛwoɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: How long does it usually take to see new flowers after I apply a flower treatment to my crops?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani minaa fɔfɔi heei beni mikɛ fɔfɔi ewo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe sɛɛ?

english: After applying a flowering treatment, you should wait about two weeks to start seeing new flowers appear on your plants.
ga: Kɛ okɛ fɔfɔi ahe tsofa lɛ tsu nii ogbe naa lɛ Esa akɛ omɛ aaafee otsii enyɔ dani obɔi fɔfɔi heei ni jeɔ kpo yɛ otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ namɔ.

english: What sign should I look out for after treating my crops to know if the booster is working?
ga: Mɛɛ okadii esa akɛ makwɛ kɛji mikɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ etsu nii koni mana kɛji booster lɛ miitsu nii?

english: You should observe the plant after two weeks to see if new flowers are coming out on the branches.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ tso lɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ koni ona kɛji eyɛ fɔfɔi heei. Nitsumɔhe niji loo daabi?

english: What is the recommended first step when using a treatment to boost flowering on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ afee kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni haa fɔfɔii babaoo yaa hiɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsu nii?

english: Apply a initial dose first, wait for two weeks to see how the flowers develop, and then decide if your plant needs more.
ga: Kɛ shishijee tsofa lɛ atsu nii klɛŋklɛŋ. Mɛɛ otsii enyɔ ni okwɛ bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa. No sɛɛ lɛ, kpɛ oyiŋ kɛji akɛ saji krokomɛi he miihia otso lɛ.

english: How do I know if my crops need a second dose of flower treatment?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he miihia ni afee lɛ fɔfɔii ahe tsofa ni ji enyɔ?

english: Check your plants two weeks after the first application. If you are not satisfied with the number of flowers that have appeared, you can add another dose.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli otsii enyɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ tsofa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ayibɔ ni jeɔ kpo lɛ haaa otsui anyɔ omli lɛ Obaanyɛ okɛ tsofa kroko afata he.

english: Can I apply a flower treatment to my plants more than once in a season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ fɔfɔi tsofa atsu nii yɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ fe shikome yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, you can apply the treatment at least twice if needed. Adding another dose can help the plant produce even more flowers.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ tsofai enyɔ atsu nii kɛ ehe miihia. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa kroko fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo.

english: Will applying more of the flower treatment cause my crops to yield more flowers?
ga: Ani fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ babaoo ni mikɛaaha lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo fɔfɔii babaoo?

english: Generally, the more of the treatment you apply appropriately, the more flowers the plant will produce for you.
ga: Yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ lɛ, bɔ ni tsofafeemɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sa ha lɛ, nakai ehi jogbaŋŋ. Babaoo ni oduɔ fɔfɔii babaoo lɛ, babaoo ni fɔfɔii baakwɛ̃.

english: Is it safe to repeat a flowering treatment if I want a bigger harvest from my crop?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafo ekoŋŋ kɛji miitao yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Yes, repeating the application after observing the plant's response gives the crop an extra boost to produce more flowers and increase your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ okɛtsu nii shii abɔ yɛ be mli ni okwɛ bɔ ni tso lɛ tsuɔ nii eha lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo fɔfɔi babaoo ni eha onibii ni oooha lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Do I need to apply the flower booster multiple times during the major farming season?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tsofa ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ awo mihe shii abɔ yɛ okwaayeli be titri lɛ mli?

english: Depending on the season, a single application is often enough during the major season because weather conditions naturally favor flower growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofa kome pɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Edamɔ be lɛ nɔ Enɛ ji akɛ, adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ daa.

english: Why do my crops respond better to flower treatments during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ fɔfɔi ahe nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The major season provides favorable growing conditions, allowing plants to produce flowers easily even after just one treatment application.
ga: Bei ni he hiaa lɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa ni haa mɔ daa lɛ baa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi mlɛo yɛ be mli ni atsa amɛ shikome pɛ po sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I choose not to apply any flower treatment?
ga: Mɛni baa minibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mihala akɛ mikɛ fɔfɔi komɛi tsuuu nii?

english: If you do not apply the treatment, your plants will produce significantly fewer flowers, leading to a much lower harvest compared to treated crops.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofafeemɔ tsuuu nii Otsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi fioo ko kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmaa ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa kɛ akɛto tsei ni atsa amɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato stems turning soft and oozing watery juice?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni nu miiho lɛ?

english: This is a sign of bacterial soft rot. When heavy rain or over-watering leaves moisture on damaged parts of the plant, bacteria enter and break down the stem tissues into a watery, smelly liquid.
ga: Enɛ ji helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahe okadi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo nu ni awoɔ fe nine lɛ ha ŋmɔtɔ ba tso lɛ fãi ni efite lɛ anɔ lɛ. Muawai boteɔ mli ni amɛgbalaa fɔlɔ fãji lɛ amli ni amɛfeɔ nu ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni tamɔ nu.

english: Why are my cocoa pods showing wet brown spots that quickly spread and turn black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli efɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: That is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded farms. The wet spot is the early stage of the fungus eating into the pod tissue.
ga: No ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, edɔ, ni hɔɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Wet spot ji klɛŋklɛŋ gbɛ ni ŋmei lɛ yeɔ nii kɛboteɔ pod lɛ mli fãji lɛ amli.

english: How can I tell if holes on my pepper leaves are caused by insects or by a plant disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ amli lɛ ba?

english: Insects physically bite and leave clean holes or chewed edges. Sicknesses usually start as discolored yellow, brown, or watery spots that gradually dry up or rot, creating holes as the dead tissue falls away.
ga: Kplukai ŋmɔɔ ni amɛshiɔ bu loo ŋmeii ni he tse. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ shishi akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, loo nu ni su tsakeɔ ni fiofio lɛ egbiɔ loo egboɔ. Ehaa buji baa kɛji fãji ni egboi lɛ gbee shi.

english: How do I choose the right medicine to spray on my crops when the leaves get soft spots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa ni sa ni mikɛbaafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ beni baai lɛ bɛ hewalɛ?

english: Soft, watery spots usually mean a bacterial or fungal rot. You need a fungicide or copper-based spray specifically made for rot, because standard insect sprays will not kill plant diseases.
ga: Nu mli hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ helai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ. Ebaabi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii loo akɔɔble ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni afee pɔtɛɛ koni ekɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ ji akɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ egbeŋ helai ni yɔɔ tsei anɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to apply chemical medicine before I see plant sickness or after it appears?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii dani tso helai aba loo yɛ no sɛɛ?

english: Preventive medicines are sprayed before wet weather to stop disease from starting. Curative medicines are applied right when you notice early symptoms like spots to halt the spread.
ga: Akɛ tsofai ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa lɛ haa dani kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baa koni hela lɛ akaba. Akɛ tsofai tsuɔ nii kɛji ona hela lɛ he okadii lɛ mra pɛ, tamɔ koni akɛkpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves sometimes burn or wither after I spray them with farm medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ beni mikɛ tsofa shwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves burn when medicine is applied during the hot afternoon sun, or if the mixture is too strong. Spraying early in the morning or late evening lets the plant absorb the medicine safely.
ga: Baai lɛ baashã kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa lɛ wo shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nuɔ tsofa lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: How does a disease travel so fast from one end of my maize farm to the other?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ naagbee kɛyaa ekroko lɛ nɔ?

english: Disease germs travel through splashing rain water, wind, insects moving between plants, or on your hands and cutlasses when you work in wet fields.
ga: Muawai tsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ kooloi bibii ni nyiɛɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ amli. Aloo yɛ oniji kɛ dadei anɔ kɛ́ otsu nii yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some cassava plants rot easily in heavy rain while others in the same soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii henɔi komɛi fiteɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni kooloi srɔtoi komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ?

english: Different plant varieties have different levels of natural defense. Improved crop varieties are bred to resist root rot fungi, whereas older varieties may easily rot in soggy soil.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu srɔtofeemɔ. Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛte shi amɛwo shishifãi ni fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni etsɛ lɛ baanyɛ afite oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: What is that simple device you extension officers use to check my soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛduɔ nii?

english: It is a soil testing meter. It measures soil moisture, acidity, and nutrients to tell us if your land has the right conditions for crops to grow well before you invest in seed.
ga: Eji tsɔne ko ni akɛsusuɔ shikpɔŋ he. Esusuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ, acidity kɛ niyenii mli nibii ahe koni ekɛtsɔɔ wɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ ni sa ni baaha tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ shika awo dumɔwui amli.

english: How can I predict if rainy weather will cause my vegetables to develop leaf rot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baaha mi-aduawai lɛ agbo?

english: High humidity and continuous rain leave leaves wet for long periods. If leaves stay wet for more than a few hours in warm weather, conditions are ripe for rot fungi to grow.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni mli wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ mli edɔ fe ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Rot fungus baanyɛ ada.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down so easily when a heavy storm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum wuji amli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit at the top, making them top-heavy. Propping them up with sturdy wooden or bamboo poles supports the trunk and keeps them upright during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. make it top heavy Tso loo ŋmei tsei ni wa ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ni ehaa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants use to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the maize turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally feeds the soil and helps your maize grow better without wearing out the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper and tomato plants falling off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper kɛ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when small pests damage the blossoms before the fruit can form.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔɔ shigbeemɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ fɔfɔi lɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up into small, twisted shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe bibii ni etsɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or by a plant virus spread by those same insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nakai kooloi bibii lɛ nɔŋŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why is it necessary to put tall wooden stakes in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the growing tuber underground. Lifting the vines off the ground catches more sunlight and prevents diseases caused by leaves touching damp soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulu la babaoo, ni ebaatsi helai ni baai ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kpeɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the leaves of some of my cassava plants develop yellowish patches and look crumpled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ekpɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This is cassava mosaic disease, which is caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies or by using infected stem cuttings from a previous harvest.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni whiteflies bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ ni jɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather when there is too much shade or bad airflow around the cocoa trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii yɛ kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during dry periods?
ga: Te jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji edɔ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Can I plant cassava together on the same plot with my plantains?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi plantains lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop plantain and cassava because they draw nutrients from different soil depths and grow at different speeds. Plantains grow taller and provide light shade, while cassava grows below, allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui kɛ ŋmei ejaakɛ amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hei srɔtoi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛdaraa oya. Plantains baakwɛ̃ ni eha hulutsoo. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa lɛ yɛ shishi lɛ Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: How many young suckers should I leave growing around one main plantain tree?
ga: Bii enyiɛ esa akɛ mashi koni madu yɛ he fɛɛ he? Plantain tso titri kome

english: You should leave only one or two healthy suckers beside the main tree. If you let too many suckers grow, they will steal water and nutrients from the parent tree, resulting in small plantain bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ masɛi. Kɛ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji plantains bibii bibii.

english: What can I do to keep the soil moisture from drying up quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni abaanyɛ afee koni shikpɔŋ nɔ nu lɛ akagbi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop leftover stems—a practice called mulching—blocks the harsh heat of the sun, keeping the soil cool and retaining moisture much longer.
ga: Mulching around Okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ akpã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain tree turning yellow before the fruit is even fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plant is lacking essential plant food in the soil, such as nitrogen or potassium, or it is severely thirsty. Adding animal manure or rich compost around the tree base helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium. loo kumai ni naa wa Kooloo ŋmei loo ŋmei ni mli ewo muji ni akɛbaafata he lɛ he Tso lɛ shishi baaye abua ni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why do my plantain stems start rotting near the ground where they meet the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ he ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpeɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Stem rotting near the base is typically caused by insect pests like banana weevils burrowing inside, or fungal infections from wet, waterlogged soil. Clearing weeds around the base and keeping soil well-drained helps keep the stems strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ banana ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishi lɛ baa. loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ajiemɔ Shishitoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ koni nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli waa.

english: Is it helpful to cut off the dry, brown leaves hanging at the bottom of my plantain trees?
ga: Ani eyeɔ ebuaa akɛ aaafo baai ni egbi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmɛɔ plantain lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, trimming off old and dead leaves helps protect your farm because pests and diseases often hide in dry foliage. Cleaning the tree allows energy to go directly to the growing fruit bunch.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni egbɔ ni egboi lɛ ni ooofo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oŋmɔ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni egbi lɛ amli. Tso lɛ he saamɔ haa hewalɛ yaa aduawai akui ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tall plantain trees easily fall down when strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots near the surface of the soil, making them unstable when carrying a heavy bunch of fruit. You can protect them from falling by supporting the stems with strong, double-forked bamboo or wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Ehaa ehiɛɛɛ shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ ehiɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Obaanyɛ otsi enaa koni ekagbee shi kɛtsɔ ŋmei loo tso ni yɔɔ ŋmeii enyɔ ni okɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is my plantain tree taking more than a year and still hasn't produced any fruit bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ eye nɔ ni fe afi ni ewooo yibii lolo lɛ?

english: Delayed fruiting usually happens when the plant lacks enough nutrients or water, or when it is choked by heavy weeds and too many suckers. Clearing surrounding weeds and giving the plant room to feed will help it flower on time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni jwɛi eyi mli obɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ Jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ gbɛ ni akɛduɔ tsei lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi yɛ be naa.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay so small and thin instead of plump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ ji bibii ni eyɛ mlɛo moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Small bunches occur when the tree suffers from food shortage or drought while forming the fruit. Applying compost near the root zone and protecting the soil with organic matter ensures the fruits get enough nourishment to fill out fully.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii feɔ kɛji niyenii faaa loo hɔmɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli abu shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha aduawai lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my plantains for boiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains kɛha shãa?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest while still green when the individual fingers become plump and round, losing their sharp, angled edges. This shows the fruit inside is fully mature and suitable for boiling.
ga: Plantains efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lolo, be mli ni inchi fɛɛ inchi mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ laajeɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ahoo.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants need enough space to share nutrients, sunlight, and water from the soil. When planted too close together, they fight for food, leading to weak growth and yellow leaves from a lack of nitrogen.
ga: Abele tsei taoɔ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛja niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu ni jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni no haa amɛdaraa waa, ni amɛbaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nitrogen ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stems on mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei tsei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges loosens the soil around the roots, making it much easier for tubers to expand and yield bigger roots while reducing the heavy labor needed during harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni ehaa shishifãi wuji baa lɛ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nitsumɔ ni tsii ni he hiaa yɛ nikpamɔ be mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when the dry Harmattan wind starts blowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ?

english: Harmattan winds carry dry air that quickly sucks moisture out of cocoa leaves. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around young cocoa trees traps moisture and protects them from the harsh wind and direct heat.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ aba mli ni ebaabu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off without turning into fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive heat stresses the tomato plant and dries up the pollen before fertilization can happen. Supplying consistent water at the base and providing mild shade keeps the plants cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa amɛmli ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aba. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shishigbɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo fioo yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are ragged holes appearing in my maize leaves shortly after the seeds sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli buji ni etse ehe lɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the growing point. Early spraying with recommended organic or chemical insecticides protects the crop before severe yield loss occurs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce many green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to put all their energy into leafy foliage instead of flowers. Balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to stop growing extra leaves and start producing flowers and fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha o-pepper tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ awo baai lɛ amli moŋ fe fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpaa baai lɛ adalɛ babaoo. ni ebɔi fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai feemɔ

english: Why does my land produce smaller yam tubers every time I plant on the exact same field year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii be fɛɛ be ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ, afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Yams are heavy feeders that pull specific nutrients from the soil. Continuous planting without resting the field or rotating with legumes like cowpeas depletes the soil and allows tuber diseases to build up.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ ni aŋmɛɛɛ he lɛ hejɔɔmɔ loo adu ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afite ni ekɛ bulb hela aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting and developing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing cassava leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-free stem cuttings prevents this virus from destroying your harvest.
ga: Kasava baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji kasava mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ odu tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni ana he odaseyeli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite onibii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantains so they do not rot before reaching market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantain lɛ? Koni ekafite dani eshɛ jara nɔ?

english: Plantains are ready for harvest when the individual fingers become plump and the sharp ridges on the green peel begin to smooth out, but before the peel turns yellow. This gives them enough shelf life for transport.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni enine fɛɛ nine mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Shi dani ŋshɔŋloo lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ Enɛ haa ŋshɔŋloo lɛ shihilɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha gbɛfaa.

english: Why do my stored maize grains turn to powder and get infested with insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ batsɔ powder ni tsɛŋemɔ helai emɔ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Maize weevils multiply quickly if grain is stored with too much moisture inside. Sun-drying the maize until the kernels are hard and storing them in airtight, hermetic bags stops insects from damaging the grain.
ga: Abɛi mli ŋmeii lɛ faa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni mli ewo nu babaoo yɛ mli lɛ to. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ aahu kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or shade trees to block the heat, the sun dries out the soil and burns the leaves, turning them yellow and dry.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa ni baatsi dɔlɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa baai lɛ. Tsɔmɔmɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize is a sign that the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has to the newest upper leaves, causing the older lower leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛji nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nibii fioo kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi fe fɛɛ lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting in the ground before I am ready to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when too much water stays in the soil around them without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater flow away so the roots remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when heavy rains and winds come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have very shallow root systems and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top, making them unbalanced. Supporting the main trunk with strong wooden or bamboo poles keeps the tree upright until the fruit is ripe.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ nɔ. unbalance Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fĩ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet suddenly. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps protect the plant from heat stress so the flowers can form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ muji wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. koni fɔfɔii awo yibii

english: Why do my young corn plants have ragged holes in the leaves and green droppings in the center fold?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ ebaai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Ragged holes and green droppings in young corn are caused by fall armyworm caterpillars feeding inside the plant's growing center. Applying an approved control measure directly into the center funnel early in the morning destroys the pest before it ruins the crop.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ jɛ fall cutworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ hei lɛ amli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛtee ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaakpata tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ hiɛ dani ekpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers recommend planting groundnuts or cowpeas in a field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani adu ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas belong to a family of plants that capture natural nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When these plants finish growing, they leave rich nutrients in the soil that feed the maize planted after them.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas fata tsei ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ ahe. Kɛji tsei nɛɛ dara kwraa Ebaashi niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak if I wait too long before clearing weeds from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛji mimɛ be kakadaŋŋ dani mijie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the soil's nutrients and sunlight so they can grow thick and strong stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa otsei titrii lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ mli kwraa. Koni eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee shiŋŋ

english: Why do I need to give my yam vines long sticks to climb up instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji kakadaji he hiaa mi lɛ? Kɛ sweet potato wain tsei ni kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make the energy required to grow big tubers underground. Staking the vines keeps the leaves lifted into the light and away from damp soil diseases on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulbs wuji akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aba. Wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛyaa la lɛ he, ni helai kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops give smaller yields when I plant many seeds close together in one place?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete with each other for food and water in the soil while their leaves shade one another from the sun. Giving each seed proper space allows every plant to get enough light and food to produce larger harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe hulutsoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ he ko ni sa ha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong, direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that create living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa plants the shade and moist soil conditions they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ oya. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to produce energy for growth. Staking lifts the foliage off the hot ground, preventing heat damage and leaf diseases while encouraging larger tuber development under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ dɔlɛ ni fiteɔ nii kɛ foliar hela naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient needed for healthy green foliage. Adding compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizers helps restore green color and healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize heavy-feeds on nitrogen and leaves the soil weak. Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and return it to the dirt through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the leaf funnel to feed on tender growing leaves. Applying appropriate organic or chemical sprays directly into the plant funnel early in the morning kills the pest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli koni amɛye baai ni miida ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni egbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark, and cool weather. Pruning extra branches and clearing weeds around the base lets sunlight and air flow through the farm to keep the pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, duŋ, kɛ fɛ̃i. Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi krokomɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi ni ajie amɛ. Shishitoo ni baaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbi.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small plantain shoots grow around the main plant at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ ni amɛbɔleɔ tso wulu lɛ he shikome lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow forces them to fight with the main plant for nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra shoots to leave only two or three strong ones focuses energy on producing larger fruit.
ga: Ha ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃. Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ awuu koni amɛná niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la, ni no haa dumɔwui bibii baa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ koni ashi tsei 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaha ajwɛŋmɔ ahi yibii wuji ni abaawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do flowers fall off my tomato plants before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Balanced watering and protecting plants during heat spikes help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa tsei jogbaŋŋ kɛ amɛhebuu yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when there is continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ ni naa wa miinɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. In waterlogged ground where water cannot drain away, oxygen is cut off, causing fungus to attack and rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ hei ni nu damɔ shi yɛ ni nu nyɛɛɛ ajɛ mli lɛ. Afoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ji oxygen lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do farmers spread dry grass around the base of pepper plants during dry months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi shwereɔ jwɛi ni egbi amɛshwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around the base acts as mulch, keeping the hot sun off the dirt. This prevents moisture from evaporating quickly, keeps the roots cool, and reduces the frequency of manual watering.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛbaabɔle Shishitoo lɛ he lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akafite. Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nu ni akɛ niji shwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ lɛ baa shi

english: Young cocoa plants have very tender leaves and shallow roots. Direct sunlight scorches their leaves and dries out soil moisture rapidly, so they require taller nurse crops like plantains to provide shade and trap moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ agbi oya. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains koni amɛná hulutsoo ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually signals a lack of nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to the newest, top leaves to keep growing, leaving the older bottom leaves starved of nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmãa baa lɛ shishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni eya nɔ eda. Kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ ni niyenii bɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know my cassava tubers are ready to harvest if they are hidden under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji akɛ akɛtee shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. This usually happens between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep falling off before turning into actual fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani ebatsɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off without setting fruit when the air gets too hot, when the soil lacks steady water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ he ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with one another for soil nutrients, sunlight, and water. This results in weak, thin stems and very small crop yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, hulu la, kɛ nu mli lɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the soil.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Better sunlight exposure allows the plant to produce more energy, which feeds the underground tuber so it grows big and long.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei feɔ hewalɛ babaoo. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara ni amɛdara

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my farm soil richer for other crops later?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural food supply for the next crop you plant there.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii jɛɛhe kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl and droop their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun and prevent water loss. If the soil has moisture, they usually recover by evening.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu ni elaaje lɛ naa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Bei pii lɛ, ehaa ehe baa shi gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to stay small even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most cultivated crops. They steal the fertilizer and water out of the soil before your main crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ. Amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani onibii titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes rot so quickly after I pick them from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes are high-water perishable crops that continue to breathe and heat up after harvest. If exposed to hot sun, rough handling, or kept in tight bags without airflow, they decay very quickly.
ga: Tomato ji tsei ni fiteɔ oya ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛdɔɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kpe lɛ, akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Aloo akɛto kotoku ko ni mli wa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Nakai nibii lɛ fiteɔ oya waa.

english: Why do some of my fresh vegetables get soft and damaged on the way to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables heei lɛ bafee bɔdɔɔ ni efite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Perishable crops lose water rapidly in heat and bruise easily when stacked tightly during transport. Physical damage breaks the skin, allowing bacteria to enter and cause rapid softening and spoilage.
ga: Tsei ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ adɔ amɛ, ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ ato amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ haa hewolo lɛ fãa. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa hewolo lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do my plantains turn yellow and soft so fast after I cut the bunch from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya beni mifo tso lɛ nine ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cutting the bunch triggers the plantain to release a natural gas called ethylene. This gas signals the crop to rapidly convert its starches into sugars, accelerating the ripening and softening process.
ga: Kɛ́ afo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa ŋmei lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene. Nɛkɛ gas nɛɛ haa tsei leɔ koni amɛtsake starch oya kɛfee sugar. Koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ oya ni efee blɛoo.

english: Why does cassava start going bad within just a few days after I dig it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are living plant tissues with no natural outer bark to protect them once harvested. Being separated from the main plant triggers rapid internal oxidation, causing brown streaks and decay within 48 hours.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso mli fãji ni hiɛ ka ni bɛ adebɔɔ mli kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe kɛji akpa amɛ pɛ. Mligbalamɔ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ haa mligbɛ oksideshin baa oya. Ekɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 mli linei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What causes my harvested garden eggs to shrink and wrinkle when left in the sun?
ga: Mɛni haa mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Garden eggs contain high moisture levels. Once separated from the parent stem, they can no longer draw water from the soil, so solar heat rapidly evaporates their internal water, causing the skin to shrivel.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo. Kɛji ajie amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Amɛnyɛŋ amɛjie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ la oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hewolo lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do buyers sort through my crops and reject some of them when I bring them for sale?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ jieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ni amɛkpooɔ ekomɛi kɛ́ mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers separate damaged or spoiled items because decaying produce spreads rot to healthy crops very quickly through contact and trapped moisture, lowering the overall value of the batch.
ga: Mɔ ni heɔ nii lɛ gbalaa nibii ni efite loo nibii ni efite lɛ amli. Enɛ ji akɛ, nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛkpeɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afee lɛ fɛɛ jara baa shi.

english: Why does one rotten yam in my storage barn cause the healthy yams next to it to rot too?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔtɔ kome ni fiteɔ yɛ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ hu fiteɔ lɛ?

english: Rotting produce is actively infected with fungi and bacteria. These microorganisms produce spores and excess wetness that easily spread across surfaces to infect neighboring healthy tubers.
ga: Nibii ni egboi lɛ amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛhe waa. Nɛkɛ nibii bibii nɛɛ feɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya koni ekɛ hela aba tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize ears get moldy while they are still attached to the plant in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe lolo lɛ?

english: Heavy rains entering unsealed husks or damage caused by insects creates wet pockets on the cob, allowing naturally occurring mold spores to thrive before the crop is even harvested.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni boteɔ ŋmei ni atsĩko naa lɛ mli loo nɔ ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ lɛ haa kotokui ni mli efɔ baa ŋmei lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli lɛ daa dani akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ po.
