english: Why is it bad to pack my harvested cabbages in tightly sealed fertilizer sacks for long journeys?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ mi-cabbage ni akpa lɛ baato ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli kɛha gbɛfaa kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cabbages release heat and moisture after being cut. Sealed sacks trap this humidity, creating a hot environment that cooks the outer leaves and causes rapid wet rot during transport.
ga: Kaabaji jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji afo lɛ sɛɛ. Kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ baamɔmɔ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni hoɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baa. ni ekɛ fitemɔ baa oya yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: Why do pepper fruits drop off the stem or spoil early when exposed to sudden heavy rainfall before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ loo amɛgboiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa dani akpa lɛ?

english: Excess water floods the crop's root system and causes sudden pressure changes inside the fruit cells, making delicate pepper skins crack and allowing fungal diseases to attack before picking.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee nu. ni ekɛ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa yɛ nɔnyɛɛ mli yɛ aduawai lɛ amli wala yibii lɛ amli Gbalamɔ ŋmɔtɔ hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni oha ŋmɔtɔ helai atutua bo dani okɛto.

english: How do I know the exact right time to start planting on my farm when the rain season arrives?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: You can tell the main planting season has arrived when the early rains soak the soil deeply enough for seeds to germinate, and when local trees start putting out fresh leaves, showing that the soil has enough moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ be titri ni dumɔwui lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ eba beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ bɔi baai heei feemɔ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How does planting my crops at the wrong time of the year affect my total harvest?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli be ni ejaaa mli lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni miwoɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting too early or too late means your young crops won't get the right amount of rain, causing roots to dry up or rot, which leads to weak plants and much lower yields.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu mra loo sɛɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otsei bibii lɛ náaa nugbɔ ni sa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ loo amɛgboiɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why is it important for me to time my plantain planting with the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato mi-plantain dumɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that need consistent water to establish quickly. Planting at the beginning of the rains gives them enough moisture to build strong roots before any dry spell begins.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni biɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa koni amɛfee shishifãi oya. Nugbɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni mli wa aba dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: How can I tell when my plantain bunch is fully ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Plantains are ready to harvest when the top leaves start turning yellow and the individual fingers swell up and lose their sharp edges, becoming rounded.
ga: Plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛji ŋwɛi baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni nineshi nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fũuɔ ni eshishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Can the harvest time of my plantain crop show me that a farming year is coming to an end?
ga: Ani mi-plantain kpamɔ be lɛ baatsɔɔ mi akɛ okwaayeli afi lɛ miiba naagbee?

english: Yes, plantains take around 9 to 12 months to mature, so harvesting a full bunch usually marks the end of a full year's farming cycle before the dry season sets in.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni eyi obɔ ni akpaa lɛ kadiɔ okwaayeli be lɛ fɛɛ naagbee dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my plantain trees turn yellow and drop off towards the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally shed their lower, older leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss through evaporation and direct energy into feeding the main stalk and fruit.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ shi ni ekɛ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni akɛhaa tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ niyenii.

english: How can harvesting my plantain bunch help me plan for the next planting season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ plantain tsei akui ni akpaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mato gbɛjianɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ?

english: Harvesting mature plantains near the end of the year signals that the current growing cycle is complete, letting you know it is time to clear the land and gather seeds before the new year's rains come.
ga: Dumɔwui ni edara ni akpaa beni ebɛŋkɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ amrɔ nɛɛ egbe naa. No hewɔ lɛ ole akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni obua dumɔwui lɛ anaa dani afi hee nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: What crop signs should I look for on my farm to know that the dry season is near?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ matao yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni male akɛ ebɛŋkɛ hulutsoo be lɛ?

english: You will notice soil drying out faster, crop growth slowing down, and plants like plantain and cassava shedding their lower leaves to prepare for the drier months ahead.
ga: Obaayɔse akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei adalɛ baa shi. Ni tsei tamɔ plantains kɛ yucca miiho amɛshishi baai lɛ amli koni amɛkɛsaa amɛhe kɛha nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my farm crops seem to grow much slower during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daaa blɛoo kwraa yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: During dry months like the Harmattan, there is less water in the soil and air, so crops slow down their growth to save energy and survive until the rains return.
ga: Yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ tamɔ Harmattan lɛ amli lɛ, nu faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: What practical steps should I take on my farm when I notice the rainy season is coming to an end?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ́ mina akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ miiba naagbee?

english: When the rains slow down, you should harvest mature crops like plantains, cover the soil around remaining plants with dry leaves to keep moisture in, and clear fields for the next season.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ba shi lɛ Esa akɛ okpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara, tamɔ plantains, ni okɛ baai ni egbi awo tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite. ni ojie ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their young leaves burn easily and dry out. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or bananas nearby creates a protective canopy that keeps the cocoa cool and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo banana ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛitsu ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize plant usually show that the crop is lacking nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plant the food it needs to turn green and grow heavy ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ená toi ni mli tse.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up off the hot ground so they can catch plenty of sunlight to feed the tubers below. It also improves airflow around the leaves, preventing fungal diseases that thrive on damp ground.
ga: Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ hu yaa hiɛ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ anaa.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with my main crops help my land?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen gas from the air and stores it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil and feeds neighboring crops like maize or cassava.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts fata legume weku ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess shade branches lets sunlight and wind dry out the trees, making it hard for the fungus to spread.
ga: Fuŋ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ lɛ kɛ pods diji baa. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ agbi kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmei lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or straw, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly during hot dry spells. It keeps the soil cool, prevents weeds from growing, and decomposes into rich plant food over time.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to rot in the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe. be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or by stress from extreme heat and dry soil. Regular watering and using natural sprays like neem oil help protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tso lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by too much heat, dry soil, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Watering the plants regularly and providing light shade during very hot weather keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao tsei lɛ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Why do my crop harvests get smaller every season if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every year drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with beans, groundnuts, or cassava gives the soil time to rebuild its food reserves.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa amɛhe shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei tsake ŋmei lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa niyenii ni ekɛto lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and short roots that cannot handle intense heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a soft canopy that shelters the young cocoa trees from harsh sunlight and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa naa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my maize crop turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when water gets trapped around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ loo kɛji nu tsɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans alongside my maize help my farm grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny swellings on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural food for the soil. When grown with maize, they help feed the soil so the maize grows stronger without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni eha ŋmãa lɛ mli awa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ehe afɔ̃ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big green stems and leaves, but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together or given excessive nitrogen fertilizer, the plant uses all its energy to grow upper leaves and stems instead of storing energy in the roots to form large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo akɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ ŋwɛi tsei lɛ anɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ he wami ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Yam vines naturally spread out to catch sunlight. Guiding the vines up tall wooden stakes lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to maximum sunlight to produce energy while preventing leaf diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwãa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ agbɛ wain tsei lɛ ashwã yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ajie tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛhaa hulu la ni fa babaoo baa koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba, yɛ be mli ni yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, amɛtsiɔ foliar hela ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely high heat, a lack of regular water, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients like calcium in the soil during the flowering period.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli daa loo niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ ni bɛ, tamɔ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On very hot days, tomato leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can drink it up from the ground. The leaves temporarily wilt to protect the plant from losing too much moisture and usually recover by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ baagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves and small dirt-like powder inside the plant shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ amli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that burrows into the central shoot of young maize plants during the night to feed on soft new leaves.
ga: Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli gbɛkɛ koni eye baai heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops stay small and produce poor harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ afee bibioo ni ewooo yibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital resources—such as soil nutrients, water, and sunlight—directly from your main crops, leaving your plants starved of the food they need to produce a good yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Ha otsei lɛ hɔmɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their strength if stored in damp places where mould or tiny insects attack them. Additionally, seeds from hybrid crop varieties are designed for a single season and naturally grow poorly if reused for a second harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ. Kɛfata he lɛ, afee dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ aha be kome pɛ, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, kɛ́ akɛtsu nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ, edaaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do so many of the flowers on my cocoa trees fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need pollen moved onto them by tiny insects or by hand to get fertilized. If a flower isn't pollinated within a day or two, the tree naturally drops it because it cannot form a pod.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi biɔ pollen ni kooloi bibii loo pollen tsiɔ amɛhe koni amɛwo fɔfɔi. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ eshɛko fɔfɔi lɛ ahe yɛ gbi kome loo gbii enyɔ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baagbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ efee ŋmeii.

english: What actually happens to a crop's flower when hand pollination is done?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe fɔfɔi anɔ kɛji akɛ nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ egbe naa pɛ?

english: Hand pollination manually transfers pollen from the male part of a flower to the female part. This guarantees fertilization, helping the plant convert that flower into a healthy, growing fruit or pod.
ga: Nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ pollen lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ fã ni ji nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa yoo lɛ fã lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔmɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa nakai fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ aduawai loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Are all tiny insects crawling on my crop flowers bad pests that I should spray?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mitsei lɛ afɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ fɛɛ ji kooloi fɔji ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ashwie nɔ?

english: No, many tiny insects like midges and bees are natural pollinators. They carry pollen from flower to flower, which is necessary for crops like cocoa, squash, and tomatoes to form fruits.
ga: Dabi, kooloi bibii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa. Amɛwoɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Ehe hia koni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, squash, kɛ tomato afee aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer flowers during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During extreme heat and drought, plants conserve water to survive. A cocoa tree drops its flowers and stops making new ones until it receives enough moisture and shade.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei toɔ nu koni amɛhi shi. Cacao tsei lɛ baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi ni amɛbaakpa heei feemɔ kɛyashi amɛbaaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbi beni eji bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: This is often called cherelle wilt. It happens when the tree doesn't have enough water or soil nutrients to feed all its young pods, or when insects damage the young pods early in their growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii fiteɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli

english: How do I know if my crops are weak because of poor soil nutrient levels?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni falɛ faaa lɛ hewɔ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, leaves turn pale green or yellow, plant growth slows down, and the crop produces very few flowers and small fruits.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii bɛ lɛ Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Tsei adalɛ baa shi. ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Because each plant gets less nourishment, none of them have enough energy to make large fruits.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Akɛni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii fioo ko nɔ hewɔ lɛ, ebɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji.

english: How does cutting off extra branches help my crops produce better yield?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Pruning opens up the crop canopy to sunlight and fresh air. It redirects the plant's food and energy away from useless leaves and into growing bigger, healthier fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa baa tso lɛ nɔ. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds around my crops make the plants produce fewer flowers?
ga: No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi fioo lɛ.

english: Weeds steal water and fertilizers directly from the soil before your crops can reach them. Without those nutrients, your crops become too weak to form strong flowers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ bɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi ni mli wa.

english: Why does a new cocoa tree take several years before it starts producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei heei jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees must first spend energy building strong roots, branches, and leaves. Only after the tree is mature enough can it store enough energy to support flowering and growing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hewalɛ koni amɛshishifãi, amɛniji, kɛ amɛbai ni mli wa lɛ adara. Beni tso lɛ edara pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato koni eye ebua fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves standing water around the roots, preventing them from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haaa amɛná niyenii kpakpai.

english: What is causing small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving dark dirt inside the center stem?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa bibii lɛ anɔ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli.

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. These caterpillars hide in the funnel of the maize plant during the day, chewing on the young leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like coarse sawdust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei akutsei amli yɛ gbi mli. Okɛ baai bibii lɛ atsu nii ni oshi jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are like human babies—they burn easily under full sun. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantain or gliricidia around them to protect their delicate leaves from harsh heat and wind during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi lɛ Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains loo glicidia, ni ebɔle amɛhe. Bɔni afee ni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily just when the fruit bunches start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ jwɛi lɛ mli tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because tiny pests called nematodes or banana weevils eat away their underground roots, destroying their support structure. Without strong roots, the heavy weight of the fruit pulls the tree out of the wet soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbee shi yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ahewɔ. Ale amɛ akɛ nematodes loo banana ŋmeii, ni amɛyeɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kpatamɔ nibii ni fiɔ amɛsɛɛ lɛ ahiɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ Yibii ni tsii hu gbalaa tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers soft and rotten in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits in the soil for too long without draining away, especially in clay soil during heavy rains. The extra water suffocates the roots and allows soil fungi to invade and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Titri lɛ, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or when vines are left to crawl on the ground without stakes, the yam plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to build big tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli Aloo be mli ni ashiɔ wain tsei koni amɛkplekeshi shikpɔŋ ni tso bɛ he. Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa si konɛ e pee bulb nguahi.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air becomes too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when flowers are not shaken by wind or insects to spread pollen inside. The plant drops its blossoms to save water and energy when stressed.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu bɛ tsei amli loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii tswaaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛgbɛ pollen amɛshwã amɛmli lɛ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛji amɛmiifee nɔ ko ni haoɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck the liquid from the plant, they cause the leaves to twist, dry out, and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. beni amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ Amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I know if the first rain of the year is enough for me to safely plant my crop seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui shweshweeshwe?

english: The very first rain usually only wets the top layer of dry soil. You should dig down a hand's length; if the soil is wet deep down and rains continue steadily for a few days, it means the soil has enough moisture to germinate seeds safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ pɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ tso kome atsu nii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɔ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi nɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster on my land than the crop seeds I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native plants that have adapted to survive harsh local conditions over many years. Their roots spread aggressively to drink water and take food from the soil before your crop seeds even get a chance to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛnu nu ni amɛye niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛtswa amɛhe shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the large shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantain because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots can establish.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ, ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can climb high to catch sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which feeds the growth of big tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso koni baai lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my plantain suckers help them grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the soil, protects roots from extreme heat, and gradually rots into natural organic plant food.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni aduɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and build strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni amɛma amɛshishifãi ni wa.

english: Planting the same crop continuously exhausts the soil of specific nutrients and allows pests and diseases that feed on that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer only when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in soil moisture for roots to absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money.
ga: Esa akɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or a lack of phosphorus, which prevents the plant from setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. be kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛgbiɔ loo fɔsfɔs ni faaa ni haa tso lɛ wooo yibii

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up and look twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Curled leaves are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which drain sap from the leaves and can spread stunt viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ akrobatik hela lɛ eshwa.

english: Excessive rain in poorly drained soil blocks oxygen from reaching cassava roots, causing waterlogging that allows rotting fungi to attack the tubers.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa lɛ ayashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do store-bought seeds produce a better harvest than seeds I save from my own maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mibuaa naa kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mi ŋmãa mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought hybrid seeds are specially bred for uniform growth and high yield in their first generation, whereas saved seeds lose these improved qualities in the next generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni eha amɛdara yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baafite amɛhe ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and fragile root systems that burn under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby provides a natural umbrella that keeps the soil cool and moist while protecting the young cocoa trees.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hulutsoo ni baaye abua ni eha edɔ ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a key food plants need to stay healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the soil the nutrients needed to bring back the green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛbaa eŋɔlii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to apply fertilizer on my farm right before a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ wulu ko aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away fertilizer from the topsoil before plant roots have time to soak it in. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist, but not during heavy downpours, ensures the nutrients stay in the soil where the crop can use them.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaaŋɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests to build up. Swapping crops, especially with groundnuts or beans, helps rebuild soil nutrients and breaks the cycle of crop diseases.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ buaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ anaa Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ahe. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ. ni ekpa tsei ahe helai ni yaa nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin when I plant the stem cuttings very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ, be mli ni adu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are too close together, their underground roots compete fiercely for water, space, and food. Giving stems proper spacing allows each plant enough soil room to swell into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, he ko, kɛ niyenii he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ bulb agbo.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to grow so slowly and give a poor harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni amɛkpaaa nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential light, water, and soil nutrients directly from your main crops. Clearing weeds early ensures all the food and water in the soil goes straight into growing your crop.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni oyɔɔ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ haa niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ yaa nibii ni odu lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why are there small holes appearing on my young maize leaves, and why do the tops look chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii ni mɛni hewɔ amɛyitsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛye amɛhe lɛ?

english: Small holes and chewed edges on young maize leaves are typically caused by destructive pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts helps stop them before they destroy the crop center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli mra. Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔhei lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pest killer on my flowering pepper plants during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-pepper tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Spraying during the hot afternoon can burn crop leaves with chemical heat and kills good insects like bees when they are actively visiting flowers. Bees are needed to pollinate flowers so they can turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ashã tso lɛ baai lɛ. ni egbeɔ kooloi kpakpai tamɔ ŋmeii kɛji amɛtee fɔfɔii amli Ehe miihia ni ŋmeii lɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen koni amɛtsɔmɔ peppery.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetables with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass acts as mulch, which shades the dirt from the scorching sun, slows down water evaporation, and keeps the soil damp longer for plant roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ naa Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha tsei shishifãi

english: Why is it helpful to cut off some of the extra small branches near the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ tsei aniji bibii lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ nibii krokomɛi ni fata he ni bɛŋkɛ tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Pruning extra low branches removes useless foliage that consumes water and nutrients. This directs the plant's energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes and improves airflow to prevent leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ babaoo jieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa ni biɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni tsɛŋemɔ hela akabote baai lɛ amli.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dying when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle full direct sunlight during their first few years. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective cover that shelters the young cocoa leaves from scorching heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and white powder inside the central growing shoot?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that feeds inside the maize shoot. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemical sprays directly into the plant funnel can save your maize crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ehere o-ŋmã lɛ yiwala.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling upwards and getting crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips. Controlling these insects with insecticidal soap or neem oil and removing heavily infected plants keeps the virus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi nɛɛ ye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ, ni ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil starves the underground cassava roots of oxygen, allowing fungal and bacterial rots to break down the tubers. Harvesting mature cassava before prolonged heavy rains prevents tuber loss.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni egbɔ lɛ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa be kakadaŋŋ anɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiiho lɛ? Ni mikɛ nu haa daa gbi?

english: Sudden wilting in green tomato plants is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne organism that blocks water flow inside the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-susceptible crops like maize helps reduce bacterial levels in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato tsei ni eŋɔli lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. ni ji nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni shikpɔŋ woɔ lɛ Enɛ tsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɛɛ atswa, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ tsake tomato lɛ, ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I remove extra suckers from my plantain shoots instead of letting them all grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ plantains mli moŋ fe ni mahã amɛfee ekome kɛkwɛ̃?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow on one plantain stool creates heavy competition for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Keeping only one main bearing stalk and one or two young suckers ensures large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi ŋmeii babaoo yɛ plantain ŋmeii kome nɔ lɛ, ekɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa baa kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa tso titri kome pɛ ni woɔ yibii kɛ tso bibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha plantain lɛ afee agbo ni etsii.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has run out of nutrients for growing maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛha ŋmãa?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crops grow slowly, leaves look light green or pale yellow instead of deep green, and yields drop significantly. Adding animal manure, compost, or balanced fertilizers restores essential plant food to the soil.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ fo lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Baai lɛ baafee eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help improve my land for the next farming season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly soil bacteria attached to their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally enriching the ground for future nitrogen-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ amɛshishifãi ahe. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ nitrogen tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why is clearing weeds within the first month of planting maize so important for my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ he hiaa mikpamɔ lɛ?

english: Young maize plants are easily overpowered by fast-growing weeds that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil. Removing weeds early gives the maize seedlings strong root growth and leads to bigger yields.
ga: Jwɛi ni shwereɔ oya ni juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ kunim oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni mli wa. ni eha ewo yibii babaoo

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a dry spell before regular rains establish. Planting too early can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up and die due to a lack of continuous moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ ehiɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants are missing nitrogen, which is their main food, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure helps restore the green color and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko bɛ tso lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh sunlight and can easily burn and die. Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛshã ni amɛgboi oya. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo tsei bibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are signs of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant stem varieties from the agriculture office is the best way to keep your farm safe.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tso lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ni ooodu lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha oŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it better to plant cassava stems slanting into the soil or flat on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmei tso lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ loo akɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slanted angle encourages roots to grow deeper into the soil where moisture stays during dry spells. Planting them flat creates shallow roots that are easier for heavy rain to expose or dry out.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, he ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nugbɔ ni naa wa loo egbiɔ lɛ waaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the soil gets too dry or when the air gets extremely hot. Watering the plants regularly during the flowering stage and covering the soil with dry grass helps keep the moisture in so flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Nu ni afɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai.

english: Should I place fertilizer right against the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: No, fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem in a circle or small hole. Placing strong fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant tissue and damage the roots, while putting it a short distance away lets the roots safely feed.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo 2-3 inches kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ kooyigbɛ loo bu bibioo ko mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ esha tso lɛ fãji ni efite shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii to he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aye nii shweshweeshwe.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in tall, thin, weak stalks that produce very small cobs or no cobs at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa loo amɛwooo kwraa.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the vine has stopped growing and has stored all its energy down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ amɛdalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito eyitso mli.

english: Why are my bean seeds failing to sprout after planting them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need water to soften their outer shell and start growing. If bean seeds remain in completely dry soil without rain or watering, they stay asleep or rot when high heat burns them under the soil.
ga: Nu he miihia dumɔwui koni amɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ afee blɛoo ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tee nɔ amɛhi shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa nɔ ni nugbɔ loo nu bɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ wɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo ni naa wa lɛ shãa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it important to cut off extra wild branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ koo mli tsei niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mi cacao tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Trimming extra or dead branches lets sunlight and fresh air pass through the tree canopy. This keeps the tree dry, preventing fungal problems like black pod disease while helping the tree direct its energy into growing big pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni egbiɔ Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ black pod hela lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants need to build strong green leaves, or that waterlogged soil is preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Aloo sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛye nii.

english: Why is it good to plant groundnuts or beans on the field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, naturally restoring nutrients for the next crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and twisted instead of long and thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Hard or shallow soil stops yam tubers from pushing downward freely. Making high, soft mounds or ridges with loose topsoil allows the yams to grow straight and expand easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baatsi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi amɛhe kɛya shi yɛ heyeli mli. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ loo ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi sũ ni mli ejɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa jaŋŋ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa mlɛo.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them close together to get more yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving them enough space allows each plant to grow bigger, stay healthier, and produce more harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa. Na hewalɛ kpakpa ni okpa nibii babaoo

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the juices out of young leaves, or by viruses carried by those insects. Clearing weeds around the farm helps reduce these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Okwaafoi baanyɛ aye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no bees and insects around to move pollen within the flower so it can form a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi bɛ he fɛɛ he. Koni ekɛ pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ aya koni ewo yibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When heavy rain leaves standing water in the field for too long, the roots drown and fungi in the soil cause them to decay.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why should I water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Midday heat causes most water to evaporate into the air before reaching plant roots. Morning watering lets the water soak deep into the cool soil so plants stay hydrated throughout the hot day.
ga: Gbi teŋ dɔlɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani eshɛɔ tsei ashishifãi ahe. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi lɛ haa nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbi lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when they start bearing heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ ebɔi jwɛi mli ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that cannot support the weight of a full fruit bunch during strong winds. Support poles made of bamboo or wood are needed to hold up the stems until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akuu ni eyi obɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Tsoi ni akɛ ŋmei loo tso fee ni fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ he miihia koni akɛmɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why must I clear weeds away while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa kwraa lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and easily lose the fight against fast-growing weeds for water, fertilizer, and sunlight. Early weeding ensures your crops get all the field's resources.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ oya koni amɛná nu, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ náa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits stay so small instead of growing big like the ones sold in the major markets?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ ji bibioo moŋ fe ni eeetsɔ agbo tamɔ tomato ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ jarayeli hei wuji lɛ?

english: Tomato size depends heavily on the specific seed variety you plant, as well as getting enough water and plant food. Varieties like 'sala' naturally stay smaller, while improved hybrid varieties grow much larger when given proper soil nutrients.
ga: Bɔ ni o-tomato lɛ da ha lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ waa. Kɛ nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni anáa lɛ fata he lɛ, srɔtoi tamɔ ‘Sala’ lɛ baafee bibioo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafee wuji babaoo kɛji akɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: I hear there are new high-yielding crop seeds available in Ghana, how do I know if they are worth the extra cost to buy?
ga: Minu akɛ tso dumɔwu hee ko ni woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji amɛhe jara ni akɛfata he lɛ?

english: New improved seeds cost more up front, but they are bred to resist local pests, tolerate dry weather, and produce higher yields, which usually brings in more profit at harvest time compared to traditional saved seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jara wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Shi atsɔse amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ni ehaa yibii babaoo Bei pii lɛ, enɛ he baa sɛɛnamɔ babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly on the way to the market compared to other varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛ akɛto henɔi krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Different tomato varieties have different skin thickness and shelf life. Harvesting tomatoes when they are just starting to turn color rather than fully ripe also helps them withstand long transport without spoiling.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni tomato henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɔɔ lɛ hewolo nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ be ni ekɛhiɔ shi. Tomato ni ajieɔ yɛ be mli ni ebɔi su tsakemɔ kɛkɛ moŋ fe ni ekwɛ̃ kwraa lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdamɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ naa ni amɛfiteee.

english: How do I choose which variety of vegetables to plant so local traders will easily buy them from me?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala aduawai ni esa akɛ madu koni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi lɛ anyɛ ahe yɛ midɛŋ mlɛo?

english: Before buying seeds, talk to local market traders to find out what their customers prefer. Traders know which specific shapes, firmness, and sizes sell fastest in local markets during different seasons.
ga: Dani obaahe dumɔwui Wiemɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni ona nɔ ni amɛ jarayelɔi lɛ sumɔɔ. Jarayelɔi le bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ha, bɔ ni amɛhe yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni amɛdalɛ ji lɛ, ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ oya yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli hei yɛ bei srɔtoi amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and dropping off before producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the plant is stressed from a lack of nutrients in the soil, overwatering, or tiny pests feeding under the leaves. Adding manure or balanced fertilizer and checking for insects will help.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo loo kooloi bibii ni baaye nii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he ni okwɛ kɛji kooloi yɛ mli lɛ baaye abua.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ?

english: During intense afternoon heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it. As long as the soil remains moist and the plants revive by evening, this is a normal temporary protective reaction to heat.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ. Abuɔ enɛ akɛ eji be kukuoo mli latsaa hebuu nifeemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: My tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making fruits. Why is this happening?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ gbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Mɛni he je nɛ e baa jã a?

english: Flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. Consistent watering and balanced plant food help flowers stay on to form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsei aniyenii ni ja yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: If I plant my maize crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ mihe waa lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in weak plants and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant room to produce larger, healthier yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni da, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer right at the base of my crop stem or scatter it across the soil?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo tso lɛ shishi loo akɛbaagbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away from the stem in a small ring or hole, not directly against the stem. Touching the stem directly can burn the plant, while scattering it everywhere feeds weeds.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta bibioo ko loo bu ko mli. ni akɛkpɛtɛɛɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ. Beni egbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he lɛ ebaafee niyenii kɛha jwɛi.

english: Why is my crop yield getting smaller every year even though I plant the same crop in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ miiba shi daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the soil. Rotating your crop with beans or cowpeas restores nutrients to the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves need direct sunlight every day to make the cob grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa mi ŋmãa baa lɛ daa gbi koni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Leaves act like tiny kitchens for the plant. They use sunlight to turn water from the soil and air into sweet food starch, which is then moved down to fill up the maize grains on the cob.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tso lɛ ŋtayaa bibioo lɛ. Amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛtsakeɔ nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ amɛfeɔ niyenii ni ŋɔɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, efãa kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ ŋmãa afata ŋmãa lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die if I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are like human babies—they burn easily in heavy heat. Tall shade trees act like large umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving moisture in the ground so the young cocoa can survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii. ni shãa oya kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo la ni mli edɔ waa mli Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai wuji. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are bees and small insects always crawling inside the flowers of my watermelon crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii shwieɔ mi-watermelon fɔfɔi lɛ amli be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Bees carry tiny yellow dust called pollen from male flowers to female flowers. Without insects doing this work to mix the pollen, the flowers will simply drop off and no watermelon fruits will form.
ga: Wuobii hiɛɔ sũ bibii ni ji ŋmɔŋ. Atsɛɔ no akɛ pollen ni jɛɔ fɔfɔi nuu lɛ mli kɛyaa fɔfɔi yoo lɛ mli. Kɛji kooloi ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni watermelon yibii ko bɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without forming fruit during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot and the soil is dry, the plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save water. Keeping the soil moist helps the flowers stay healthy and turn into tomatoes.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ Tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ tomatoi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and dropping to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil lacks nutrients like nitrogen, the plant sacrifices its older bottom leaves to feed the young green leaves at the top. Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is hungry or water-stressed.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, tsei kɛ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ loo nu efo emli.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or beans on my field make my next season's maize grow so much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa mi-be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans have special roots that grab plant food (nitrogen) directly out of the air and trap it in the dirt. When you plant maize afterward, it feeds on that natural fertilizer left behind.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa tsei aniyenii (nitrogen) kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why must I heap up high soil mounds before I plant my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Soft, loose soil mounds give the yam room to stretch and expand into large tubers. Hard ground squeezes the tuber, keeping it small, and holds standing water which causes root rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hegbɛ ni amɛgbala amɛhe ni amɛdara amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ miimiɔ yitso lɛ. feɔ bibioo ni ehiɛɔ nu ni haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ

english: Why should I cover the soil around my plantain stems with dry grass and cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ kookoo ŋmeii awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the dirt acts like a blanket that stops the hot sun from drying out the soil. It keeps moisture near the plant roots for longer and slowly rots into rich compost food.
ga: Mulching tamɔ blanket ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ ni fiofio lɛ Egboɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jara wa.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants twisting and curling into tiny tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni abɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bɔɔlu bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves mean tiny unseen pests like aphids are hiding underneath, sucking out the plant's juices. This stops food from moving freely through the plant and stunts its growth.
ga: Baai ni abɔle amɛhe lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Nibii ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shishi. Koni ajie nu kɛjɛ tsei amli Enɛ haaa niyenii lɛ aya tso lɛ mli oya ni ehaaa eda.

english: Will pruning off some of the extra side branches on my tomato plants help me harvest bigger tomatoes?
ga: Ani tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua mi ni makpa tomato agboi?

english: Yes, removing extra branches keeps the plant from wasting food on unnecessary leaves. Instead, all the food created by the leaves moves directly into swelling the remaining fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ. Shi niyenii fɛɛ ni baai lɛ feɔ lɛ tsiɔ ehe tɛ̃ɛ koni eha aduawai ni eshwɛ lɛ afu.

english: Why are my young fruits falling off the plants onto the ground before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii bibii lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ dani amɛmiikpa nii lɛ?

english: Crops often drop immature fruit when they are stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or pest attacks, as the plant tries to save energy to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii laajeɔ amɛyibii ni eshɛko lɛ kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atutuaa Enɛ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛto hewalɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my seedlings look weak and dropped before they suddenly start growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ feɔ tamɔ mɛi ni bɛ hewalɛ trukaa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Plants frequently experience transplant shock or early leaf shedding while their root systems adjust to the soil, after which they recover and grow rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei naa shoofeemɔ ni baa kɛji akɛ amɛtsake amɛhe loo amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ mra be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛhe waaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Is it bad to leave fruits that have fallen off the plant lying on the farm floor?
ga: Ani ehiii akɛ aaashi aduawai ni egbee shi kɛjɛ tsei anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fallen fruits attract harmful insects and breed fungal diseases on the ground, which can easily spread back up into your healthy standing crops.
ga: Yibii ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã otsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ amli oya.

english: What is the main difference between local pawpaw varieties and the newer varieties available?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔi titrii ni yɔɔ pawpaw henɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ henɔi heei ni yɔɔ lɛ ateŋ?

english: Local varieties usually start growing quickly and suit local weather, while newer varieties come in different fruit shapes like round or small segmented types that can produce higher market yields.
ga: Kuu lɛ mli tsei srɔtoi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya ni amɛhi jogbaŋŋ kɛha he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ. Yɛ be mli ni henɔi heei Ayɛ aduawai ahe mfonirii srɔtoi, tamɔ ŋwɛi loo bibii ni mli eja. ni baanyɛ aha yibii babaoo aba yɛ jara nɔ

english: How do I decide whether to plant round-shaped pawpaw or the small-piece varieties on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ akɛ makwɛ papaya ni yɔɔ kokroo loo bibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Round varieties are usually firmer and easier to transport to distant markets without bruising, while smaller varieties often ripen faster for quick local sales.
ga: Henɔi ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni eyɛ mlɛo akɛ akɛbaaya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he. yɛ be mli ni henɔi bibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya koni amɛja yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why does my local seed start growing faster in the beginning than the hybrid seed I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mimaŋ dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa oya fe hybrid dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ?

english: Local seeds are adapted to sprout rapidly in native soil conditions, whereas hybrid seeds often take extra time developing deep roots first before producing heavier yields.
ga: Atsakeɔ akutsoŋ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ heɔ be kroko dani shishifãi ni mli kwɔ baa dani amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why do some fruits grow into smooth round shapes while others break into smaller uneven shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai komɛi yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? yɛ be mli ni ajara henɔi komɛi amli awo bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee lɛ mli?

english: Fruit shape is determined by the plant's variety and how well bees pollinate the flowers; complete pollination leads to full, round fruit development.
ga: Bɔ ni aduawai lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ damɔ tso lɛ henɔi lɛ kɛ bɔ ni wuobii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ pollination ni yeɔ emuu mli baa ji aduawai ni eda, ni yɔɔ kokroo.

english: Why do my crop stems break and fall over just when heavy fruits start to form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ amli fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii je shishi amɛba lɛ?

english: Stems break under heavy fruit loads if the plant lacks calcium for strong stems, or if you do not support the branches with wooden stakes early enough.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baafo kɛji amɛná aduawai babaoo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ calcium ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsei ni akɛtswaa tsei lɛ fiii tsei lɛ aniji lɛ asɛɛ oya bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do leaves turn yellow and drop off right when the crop begins to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ bɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: Plants naturally shift food and water from older leaves into the growing fruit, but excessive leaf loss means the soil needs additional fertilizer and water.
ga: Tsei tsakeɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa aduawai amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi baai babaoo ni laajeɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu krokomɛi.

english: Why do some of my crops mature quickly while others take a much longer time before producing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi daa oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ nii lɛ?

english: Short-duration crops are bred to finish producing before dry seasons begin, while long-duration varieties grow slowly to produce food steadily over many months.
