ga: Akwɛɔ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ koni amɛgbe nitsumɔ naa dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aje shishi. yɛ be mli ni srɔtoi ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ daraa blɛoo fe tsutsu lɛ. koni ekɛ niyenii aba be fɛɛ be nyɔji babaoo

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on the same land where I just planted my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu kookoo tsei bibii amrɔ nɛɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight and can easily dry up. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and cool soil they need during their first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa, ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close together to try to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in weak, thin plants with small harvests, and creates a damp environment where diseases can spread easily.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. ni efee shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni helai Baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mli oya

english: Why should I alternate planting maize with beans or cowpeas on the same field instead of planting maize every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ atsake ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu ŋmãa daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and wears out the land over time. Beans and cowpeas put vital nutrients like nitrogen back into the soil naturally, which restores land fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abele yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Beans kɛ cowpeas kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my crops with dry grass or fallen leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii ni jwɛi gboi loo baai ni egbee shi yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry plant material, called mulching, keeps moisture in the ground during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots to feed the soil with rich natural fertilizer.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efite fiofio koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo aha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When rain saturates the ground and creates standing water, the roots drown and begin to decay, which is why planting on raised soil mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu ni damɔ shi baa. Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛje shishi amɛgboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum exposure to sunlight to capture energy and grow large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp ground where they can catch light and stay safe from rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ akashɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛmɔmɔ la ni amɛyɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ fitemɔ he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for green foliage. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does swamp rice grow well in flooded fields while my other crops die if covered in water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli shi mi tsei krokomɛi lɛ gboiɔ kɛji nu eyi amɛmli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air passages inside their stems that send oxygen down to their roots underwater. Most other crops do not have these passages, so their roots drown when submerged for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo bɛ nɛkɛ gbɛjegbɛi nɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects. Sprinkling soapy water or neem leaf extract on the leaves can help clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Nu ni akɛ saamɔ loo neem baa mli nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the flowers. Giving them steady water and planting flower-attracting herbs nearby helps fruit set properly.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu daa ni odu tsofai ni gbalaa fɔfɔii ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akpɛtɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because harsh sun scorches their delicate leaves. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade umbrellas that protect the cocoa trees until they grow stronger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ cacao tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ naa hewalɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that hides in the heart of maize plants and chews through leaves. Early detection and spraying with recommended neem extracts or insecticides can control them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ ni ekɛyeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ ana mra ni akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite nibii ni afee lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava leaves to curl up and get light yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni haa cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies or spread through infected planting sticks. You can prevent this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by your extension service.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ loo amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛtsɔɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. Obaanyɛ otsi enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni o-extension service lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Bacterial Wilt, a soil disease that blocks the plant's internal tubes so water cannot reach the leaves. Once present in the soil, it is best to plant non-susceptible crops like maize in that space for a few seasons.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Wilt muawai, hela ko ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli paipii lɛ anaa, ni ehaa nu shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe. Be ni eje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Esa akɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɛɛ atswa, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ jɛmɛ be fioo komɛi.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my growing crop turn yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants use to stay green and build leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-decomposed manure will restore healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii tso titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines grow plenty of big leaves but produce very tiny tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baa lɛ dara waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: If soil has too much nitrogen, the yam puts all its energy into leaf growth instead of building tubers underground. Yams need balanced soil nutrients and loose, well-mounded soil so the tubers can expand properly.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Sweet potatoes kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ, Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same farm patch every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores natural fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ baa ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nibii amli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from intense sun and conserve moisture. It reduces the leaf surface area exposed to heat, preventing the plant from losing too much water during dry hours.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni hulutsoo baa lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when plants face extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Maintaining steady soil moisture through mulching helps the plant hold onto its flowers so they mature into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: Why do weeds harm my young crops so much more than when the crops are tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe be mli ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young crop roots and leaves are small, making them too weak to compete with fast-growing weeds for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds during the first month allows your crop to establish strong roots.
ga: Tsei bibii ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ daraaa. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ abɔ akaŋ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen or when heavy rain washes nutrients away from the roots, preventing the plant from making food.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with many leaves but produces very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava puts its energy into growing leaves instead of roots when there is too much nitrogen in the soil or when planted in shaded areas without enough direct sun.
ga: Cassava kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai amli yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ kɛ́ nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and dry up when the dry season sun comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ je kpo yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and thin leaves that lose water rapidly under direct sunlight, requiring temporary shade crops like plantain to shield them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ mlɛo, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Esa akɛ akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ atsu nii kɛbu he.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when heat gets too extreme, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no beneficial insects visiting to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and getting small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ bibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites feeding under the leaves, or by viruses transmitted when these insects bite the plant.
ga: Nibii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ŋmɔ tsei lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down easily right when the fruit bunch is starting to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains fall over because microscopic worms called nematodes destroy their root base underground, leaving the stem unable to hold the heavy fruit weight.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli.

english: Cowpeas trap natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, leaving natural plant food in the ground for whatever crop you plant after them.
ga: Cowpea mɔ̃ɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shi adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn before the next planting season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that rest after harvest; once ambient temperature and humidity rise in the barn, the tuber naturally senses it is time to start growing again.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni jɔɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Beni hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, bulb lɛ baanu he yɛ adebɔɔ naa akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ ebɔi dalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to sow my seeds right after the very first small rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by dry heat; if seeds germinate in shallow moisture, the hot ground will scorch and kill the young tender shoots before regular rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ni ekpata ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my crops even when I give the farm plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ fioo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa ŋmɔ lɛ moŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal root space, soil nutrients, and sunlight, effectively starving your crops of essential growth materials.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ shishifãi ahe gbɛ. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni hulu lɛ mli wa waa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli yɛ gbɛ ni mɔɔ shi nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong, or that heavy rains have waterlogged the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni esa akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ada waa Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry spells to save water and keep the underground tubers alive. Once the rains start again, the plant will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ ŋmeii heei ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper bushes curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni baai ni yɔɔ mi chili tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices, or by a virus they carry. Controlling these small pests keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni amɛhiɛ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii nɛɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my leafy vegetable plants wilt in the afternoon sun but look fresh again every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-green lɛ shwieɔ shi shwane mli shi ebaa ehee daa leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through leaves faster than the roots can take it from the soil. They wilt temporarily to protect themselves, but rest and absorb moisture overnight. Placing dried grass around the stems holds water in the soil longer.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe. Mohu ɔ, e ma jɔɔ e he nɛ e ma ngɔ nu nɛ e ngɛ mi nyɔ kɛ nyɔ kake. Hay ni akɛbaabɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni nu ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the daytime air gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly soaked. Shade nets and regular, light watering help keep the flowers on the plant so they can form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Shade netting kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fioo Daa yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees stop producing pods when their upper branches get too thick and dark?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii feemɔ beni eniji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni efeɔ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cocoa branches need sunlight and air movement to produce healthy flowers and pods. When the canopy gets too thick, it creates damp shade that encourages diseases like black pod and prevents flowers from growing. Pruning extra branches lets in sunlight.
ga: Cocoa niji he miihia hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛji ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Ehaa hulutsoo ni mli edɔ ni woɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ahe hewalɛ ni ehaa fɔfɔii lɛ shwereɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he koni hulu la aba

english: Why are my plantain bunches getting very small when many young shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small shoots—called suckers—compete with the mother plant for food and water in the soil. Cutting away extra suckers and leaving only two or three allows the main plant to yield big plantain bunches.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Ekɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni ena niyenii kɛ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yam vines naturally climb toward sunlight, which allows the leaves to make plenty of food for the tubers underneath. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, protecting them from rot and disease.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ niyenii babaoo. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa

english: Excess water makes cowpea plants grow lots of leaves but very few pods. Heavy rain also causes the ripe pods to rot easily on the ground, so cowpeas prefer drier, sunnier conditions.
ga: Nu babaoo haa cowpea tsei lɛ náa baai babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu haa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, cowpea sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ hulu la babaoo.

english: Why do my rice seeds fail to come up when I plant them deep in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Rice seeds are small and carry only a tiny bit of stored energy. If planted too deep, the young shoot exhausts its strength before reaching the surface, so planting them near the top layer helps them sprout easily.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa lɛ ji bibii, ni hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ ni ato he lɛ yɔɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewalɛ baaje mli dani amɛshɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ odu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ oya.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees on my new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive under strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa plants during their first few years.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do extension officers recommend planting tall trees along the boundaries of my crop field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsei kakadaji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ?

english: Tall trees act as windbreaks that shield fragile crops like cassava and plantains from strong winds, preventing stems from snapping and stopping heavy rains from blowing topsoil away.
ga: Tsei ni kɛlɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɔjɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi fãa, ni ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: How does planting beans alongside my maize help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and pull it down into the soil through their roots. Maize needs nitrogen to grow strong, so the beans naturally feed the maize without requiring as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi Egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni egbalaa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃, no hewɔ lɛ ŋmãa haa ŋmãa niyenii ni tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why do some farmers plant cover crops like Mucuna before planting their main food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ Mucuna dani amɛduɔ niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ?

english: Cover crops grow fast and form a thick leafy layer over the ground. This smothers weeds, prevents rain from washing away soil nutrients, and turns into rich natural fertilizer when chopped down into the dirt.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ baai ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi lɛ. Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa waa kɛ́ afolɔ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers plant Gliricidia trees inside their crop fields and cut the leaves off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ glicidia tsei yɛ amɛŋmɔji amli ni amɛfoɔ baai lɛ?

english: Gliricidia trees pull nutrients deep from the ground and fix nitrogen into the soil. When farmers trim the leaves and bury them in the dirt, the leaves break down and act as a free, green manure for nearby food crops.
ga: Gliricidia tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni amɛfiɔ nitrogen lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ okwaafoi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛfu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ fãa ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa niyenii tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ.

english: How does planting pigeon peas help improve hard or dry soil on my land?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni pigeon peas ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni egbi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Pigeon peas have deep, strong roots that punch holes into hard, compacted soil. This loosens the earth so rainwater and air can sink deeper, making the land softer and better for future crops.
ga: Pigeon beans yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa ni shwieɔ bu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tseɔ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ abote mli shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehi kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can planting marigold flowers around my vegetable bed really protect my crops from bugs?
ga: Marigolds ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, marigold flowers release a strong scent that repels harmful insects and tiny underground worms. Planting them around vegetables creates a natural barrier that keeps pests away without chemical sprays.
ga: Hɛɛ, marigold tsei lɛ jieɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma ko ni naa wa ni shwieɔ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ Aduawai ahe lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni haaa ŋmeii akabote mli ni akɛ tsofai shwieee nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously allows specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil. Changing the crop every season breaks the life cycle of these pests and keeps the soil healthy.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni ayaa nɔ akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa be lɛ fiteɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ashihilɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes or tree branches to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso loo nine ni mikɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants create energy in their leaves using sunlight. When the vine climbs high on a stake, its leaves spread out to catch maximum sunlight, giving the plant the power to produce large, heavy yams underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ hewalɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Beni wain tsei lɛ kwɔ kɛtee akulashiŋi kakadaji lɛ anɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my cassava grow slowly during the first few months when I plant it together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize grows faster than cassava and consumes most of the early sunlight and soil nutrients. Once the maize matures and is harvested, full sunlight reaches the cassava, allowing it to speed up its growth.
ga: Abele daa oya fe ŋmei ni eyeɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni akpa lɛ Hulu la ni yeɔ emuu lɛ shɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ he. Ye obua ni eda oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and dry up during the sunny weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and sensitive to direct sunlight. Planting them under shade crops like plantain or shade trees protects them from scorching heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛ nuɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ he. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli tamɔ plantains loo shia tsei ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants dropping their flowers instead of forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifɔlɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is irregular, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Consistent watering and mulching around the roots help keep the plant stable.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines need long wooden sticks to climb up as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ lɛ? Koni okwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛ́ oda?

english: Yam vines produce yield based on sunlight exposure. Staking holds the leaves up off the ground so they catch maximum sunlight and stay away from wet soil that causes leaf rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ hulu la naa. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ he.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my maize immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a hot dry period. Seeds planted too early will sprout and then dry up and die before the main rainy season truly begins.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ be ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni adu mra tsɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava crop is ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-cassava tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months when the lower leaves yellow and shed, and cracks begin to appear in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ, be mli ni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ fãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen. Applying poultry manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer gives the plant the nutrient it needs to grow green leaves and big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi ashishifã loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli kɛ toi wuji.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts on the same plot where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes nitrogen out of the soil, but groundnuts are legumes that naturally trap nitrogen from the air and feed it back into the soil, restoring field fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli nitrogen ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ

english: Why do weeds lower my crop yield even when my crops are bigger than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ da fe jwɛi lɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that secretly steal water, plant food, and sunlight away from your crops, leaving your crops hungry and less productive.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli yɛ teemɔŋ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes inside the funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, which hatch from moth eggs inside the plant's growing center. Spraying early with approved organic solutions like neem oil or recommended pesticides keeps them from destroying the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli yɛ tso lɛ he ni edaa lɛ mli. Akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ tamɔ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite tso lɛ.

english: Why does my dry harvested maize develop tiny holes and turn into white powder in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa ni egbi lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ebafeɔ powda yɛŋ yɛ nitoohe.

english: Grain weevils bore into dry corn kernels to lay eggs and feed inside. Properly drying your corn and storing it in airtight bags or treated containers prevents these insects from entering.
ga: Dumɔwui ŋmeii shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni amɛye nii yɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo nibii ni akɛ tsofa ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up and fail so quickly when the rain stops for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya beni nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Maize has shallow roots and needs constant water, especially when forming ears. Without enough rain during these critical weeks, the roots cannot pull moisture from deep ground, causing the plant to dry out and die.
ga: Abɛi shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ehe hiaa nu daa. titri lɛ beni afee toii Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa yɛ otsii ni he hiaa nɛɛ amli Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei agbi ni amɛgboi.

english: What kind of seeds should I buy if the rainy season in my area is getting shorter every year?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi?

english: Look for early-maturing crop seeds. These special varieties grow and produce full harvests in 60 to 90 days instead of four months, allowing you to harvest before the rains stop early.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ daa ni amɛshɛɔ yibiiwoo he yɛ gbii 60 kɛyashi 90 mli yɛ nyɔji ejwɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ mra.

english: What crops can I grow to feed my farm animals when maize is hard to find or too expensive?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu koni mikɛha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ niyenii be mli ni ŋmãa namɔ wa tsɔ loo ejara wa tsɔ?

english: You can grow cassava, sorghum, or millet. Sorghum survives dry weather much better than maize, and cassava tubers can be processed into feed for poultry and livestock.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmãa, ŋmãa, loo ŋmãa. Sorghum hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmãa. Ni abaanyɛ afee ŋmei shishifãi lɛ niyenii aha kooloi kɛ kooloi.

english: Why does cassava stay green and alive during long dry spells while maize dies off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa gboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water deep underground in its thick tuber roots and drops its outer leaves to conserve moisture, allowing it to survive months without rain.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ tuber shishifãi ni mli tse amli ni ekɛshwieɔ kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Ha eho nyɔji babaoo ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: What can I put on my field soil to keep it from drying out so fast under the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mikɛwo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi?

english: You can cover the ground with dry grass, leaves, or straw, which is called mulching. This layer acts like a shade blanket, blocking sunlight and keeping moisture trapped in the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching. Nɛkɛ fã nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo. Etsiɔ hulu la naa ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers always tell me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi be fɛɛ be akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the dirt, acting as a natural food supply that helps neighboring maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni edara waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, preventing water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize plants so much faster than other grass crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms gbeɔ mi-corn tsei lɛ oya fe jwɛi tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer maize because they feed directly on the tender central leaf funnel where new growth happens, stopping the plant from producing new leaves or ears.
ga: Fall cutworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmãa heei miiya nɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ewo baai loo toi heei.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my maize seeds when the rain starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until you receive two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the dirt. Planting in dry soil after just one light shower will cause seeds to burn and die before roots form.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã ni amɛgboi dani shishifãi lɛ aba.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains rot or get eaten by insects so fast in my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya loo kooloi ni yɔɔ mi-nitoohe lɛ yeɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains hidden water. If you do not dry the grains thoroughly under the sun before storehouses are closed, the trapped moisture creates mold and attracts destructive weevils.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ogbiiaa ŋmaa lɛ kwraa dani ogbeɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Trapped moisture lɛ haa ŋmeii baa ni egbalaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: What will happen if I plant my plantain suckers too close to each other on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition leads to thin, weak stems and much smaller bunches of plantains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ plantains bibii waa baa.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in my field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. This naturally restores soil fertility so your next crop of maize can grow strong without relying entirely on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ adara waa ni okɛ ohe afɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ anɔ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant is hungry for nitrogen in the soil, or when heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Abɛi baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper leaves curl upward in intense heat to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ latsaa mli koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Eji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to water my vegetable garden in the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane mli lɛ?

english: Watering under the scorching afternoon sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can absorb it. Morning or evening watering allows the soil to hold moisture longer.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔ nu lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the plant without ever producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high, when watering is inconsistent, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which makes the plant grow big leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa baai wuji yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yams grow twisted when the soil underneath is too hard, stony, or compacted. Making high, soft mounds gives the tubers loose soil so they can expand straight downwards.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ yitso lɛ afee mlɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa shi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves dry up and fall off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Can I save seeds from market tomatoes to plant on my farm next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ jara nɔ tomatoi amli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Market tomatoes are often hybrids, meaning seeds saved from them will not grow into the exact same quality of plant. They usually produce weaker crops with smaller fruits compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛfee nɔ ko. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ edaŋ ni amɛfee tsei ni hiɛ su kome pɛpɛɛpɛ. Amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibii bibii yɔɔ mli kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a vital food in the soil, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava bushes curl up and show yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies that pass the virus from infected plants to healthy ones, reducing tuber growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso dalɛ ni baa shi.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, overly shaded, and very wet weather with poor air movement through the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and thin, but producing small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete for limited sunlight and soil food, spending all their energy growing tall instead of making big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee bɔɔlu agbo ko ni ji cob.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during storms even when carrying fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ ahum be mli eyɛ mli akɛ eewo yibii moŋ lɛ?

english: Tiny underground worms called nematodes or insect grubs eat away the root system, leaving the plantain tree without a strong anchor in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Extremely hot weather, dry soil, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes heat stress, forcing the plant to drop its flowers to survive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomatoes turning soft and black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why should I clear weeds early from my yam farm instead of waiting until the vines get big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi lɛ mra? Kɛjɛ sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooomɛ kɛyashi wain tso lɛ baakwɛ̃?

english: Yam vines grow slowly at first, so aggressive weeds will easily steal soil water, light, and fertilizer before the yam plant can build tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei lɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Dani sweet potato tso lɛ baawo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ,.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant maize on the same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baa ŋmãa nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do the tips of my lowland rice leaves turn reddish-brown as if they were burned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi lowland rice grits lɛ miitsɔ red-brown tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ lɛ?

english: This is often caused by iron toxicity in flooded lowlands, where too much iron damages the roots and prevents the rice plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni yɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Dade babaoo fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ni ehaaa ŋmãa tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees around my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ he lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo koni ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to leave proper space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi he ko ni sa yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak plants with small ears. Giving each plant proper spacing allows it to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnáa toi bibii. Kɛ́ okɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená hewalɛ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants turning yellow even when rain is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize often mean the plant is lacking key soil food like nitrogen, or weeds are stealing its nutrients. Applying a small amount of nitrogen fertilizer or practicing crop rotation helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii titri ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ jwɛi miiju niyenii lɛ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ni akɛwoɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ he nitsumɔ baaye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your garden bed.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha nu lɛ akatsɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaha obɔɔ mli saatsoi lɛ anɔ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my cassava stem cuttings?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted at the early start of the rainy season when the ground is moist. This allows the stems to establish deep roots before any dry spell begins.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi.

english: Fertilizer works best when applied into moist soil shortly after rain, but not during heavy downpours that wash the nutrients away. Applying it a few weeks after germination and again during flowering gives plants maximum benefit.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Shi jeee yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii amli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tso lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ, ni akɛwo mli ekoŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves with tiny dirt left inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni muji bibii komɛi eshwɛ yɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the growing center of the plant. Spraying recommended treatments directly into the plant funnel early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ shwie tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Tomato leaf curling is usually caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. Protecting young tomato plants from insects and removing infected plants prevents the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ obu tomato tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe, ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do groundnut flowers bloom above the ground, but the nuts mature inside the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔii fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant grows long stems that bend downward and push themselves into the soil. The actual nuts grow and ripen underground to stay protected from heat and birds.
ga: Beni ekɛ ŋmeii fɔfɔi lɛ ewo ŋmeii amli sɛɛ lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kakadaji ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beans lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ kɛ okpoi ahe.

english: Why does my stored harvested maize turn to powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpa lɛ tsɔɔ powda yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize turns to powder because tiny insects called weevils bore inside the dry grains to feed and reproduce. Drying your grains thoroughly before storage and using airtight containers or protective storage powders prevents this insect damage.
ga: Abɛi tsɔɔ sũ yɛ kooloi bibii ahewɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi mli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛfɔ bii. Nibii ni agbiɔ yɛ ŋmaa mli dani akɛtoɔ Ni akɛ tsɛnsi ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo powda ni akɛtoɔ nii ahe lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite.

english: Why do my maize plants curl up their leaves during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up like small tubes during intense heat to reduce their surface area, which helps trap moisture and prevents water from evaporating too quickly from the plant.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe tamɔ paipii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ koni akɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya tsɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli.

english: Will using a water pump to irrigate my tomatoes daily make them produce better fruit during the dry season?
ga: Ani nu pɔmp ni akɛbaatsu nii ni akɛfɔ tomato nɔ daa gbi lɛ baaha ewo yibii kpakpai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, steady watering with an irrigation pump keeps soil moisture levels stable, preventing dry stress which causes tomato flowers to fall off and fruits to crack.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛ nu pɔmp shwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. Buu he kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduawai lɛ fãa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants start turning yellow and dropping when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns the soil and deprives cassava roots of air, causing root rot which makes the plant shed its leaves to survive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai koni ehi wala mli.

english: Why do my watermelon vines look wilted in the afternoon heat even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli edɔ po

english: On hot days, water leaves the watermelon leaves faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil; the leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves and will recover by evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Nu jeɔ watermelon baa mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ baagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he, ni amɛbaatsa amɛhe gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant blossoms drop off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high temperature stress or lack of water, saving their energy to stay alive rather than producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛhiɔ wala mli lɛ baa shi moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees growing tall and thin instead of strong and bushy under my tree canopy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miida ni amɛmiifee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When shade is too heavy, young cocoa trees stretch upward trying to reach daylight, resulting in weak, thin stems instead of sturdy branches.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei akutsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ feɔ tsei niji ni he wa najiaŋ.

english: How does installing a borehole for clean water help my vegetables grow better than using stagnant pond water?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mli tse ni akɛwoɔ nubu mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nubu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Borehole water provides a reliable supply of water free from diseases and chemicals that can stunt vegetable root growth and damage soil health.
ga: Nu ni jɛɔ nubui amli lɛ ji nu jɛɛhe ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni helai kɛ tsofai bɛ mli. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ aduawai shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my corn turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishi baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign of nitrogen deficiency; the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the fresh growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam tubers end up very small when I plant them close together on the same mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii waa beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ gɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams planted too closely fight each other for soil nutrients, sunshine, and water, leaving less food for each individual vine to expand its tuber.
ga: Atomɔ ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ baawu tsɔ kɛha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, hulu la kɛ nu, ni niyenii fioo pɛ baaha wain tsei aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ akwɛ bulbs.

english: Why do dark spots appear on my tomato leaves after I splash water directly on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-tomato baai lɛ anɔ beni mikɛ nu shwie tomato baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Water splashed onto leaves carries fungi from the soil up to the plant, and the wet leaf surface gives diseases the moisture they need to infect the crop.
ga: Nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso lɛ nɔ. Ni baai ni efɔ lɛ haa helai srɔtoi náa ŋmɔtɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii amli

english: Why are the pest chemicals I sprayed on my maize not killing the insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwie ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ egbeee kooloi lɛ?

english: Agrochemicals fail mostly because of improper application—such as using the wrong dose, spraying at the hottest time of the day when heat breaks down the chemical, or spraying just before rain washes it off.
ga: Agrochemicals lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Ni akɛshwieɔ tsofai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli beni dɔlɛ kpataaa tsofai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ. loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ ahoɔ lɛ.

english: Can I mix two different crop medicines together to save time when spraying my field?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ afutu mli koni mikɛ be akafite yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli tsofai lɛ ahe?

english: Mixing different farm chemicals without expert guidance can spoil the medicine, cause harmful chemical reactions, or even burn your crop leaves instead of protecting them.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔji srɔtoi amli Kɛ́ ŋaawolɔ ko ni he esa waa bɛ lɛ, tsofa lɛ baanyɛ afite. Ekɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara baa Aloo eshãa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai po yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebu amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops burn after I apply fertilizer to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shãa beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer burns plants when it touches wet leaves directly or when too much is placed too close to the stem. Fertilizer should be placed in the soil a short distance away from the plant stem so the roots can safely drink it.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baashã tso lɛ kɛ́ ekɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo koni shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning or late in the evening because the air is cool, wind is calm, and the medicine stays on the plant long enough to work before the hot sun dries it up.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ, ni tsofa lɛ baanyɛ ahi tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni etsu nii dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ aha egbi.

english: What does it mean when experienced farmers say I should help my maize first when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ kɛɛ akɛ esa akɛ maye mabua ŋmãa klɛŋklɛŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni etsɔɔ?

english: Helping your maize first means giving the seeds good soil preparation and applying starter fertilizer or compost at planting so the young roots grow fast and strong before weeds take over the field.
ga: Ni aye abua ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ asaa dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni eye ebua shishifãi bibii lɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe awa dani jwɛi lɛ aŋɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to come up out of the dirt after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the soil is too dry, or if soil insects and birds destroy the seeds before they sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpata dumɔwui lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds while my young crop is still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and cannot fight aggressive weeds for nutrients, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the food in the soil so it can grow strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi jwɛi ni baa amɛŋɔɔ ni kɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen food in the soil, or heavy rains have washed the nutrients away from the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi amli.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up to protect themselves from intense heat and reduce water loss. It is the plant's natural way of surviving dry spells and strong sunlight.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi hulutsoo naa fe nine ni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall and thin with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight and soil space, causing them to grow tall and weak instead of producing big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ he ko he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ daraa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains no longer start at the usual time?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ yɛ be ni afeɔ daa lɛ mli dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil stays moist for at least three consecutive days after a heavy rain. Planting too early during false rains causes seeds to burn in dry dirt, while waiting too long leaves crops without enough water during their growth period.
ga: Mɛɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hoo lɛ gbii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have small root systems that cannot pull up enough water when hot winds evaporate moisture from their leaves. Planting plantain or shade trees alongside cocoa creates natural protection that keeps the air humid and blocks direct sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii. No nyɛŋ agbala nu ni fa bɔ ni sa beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Plantains loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli hebuu baa ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Why is my cassava crop growing tall with many green leaves but giving me very small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ehaa shishifãi bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: When soil contains too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, the cassava plant spends all its energy producing leaves instead of feeding the roots. Avoid applying high-nitrogen fertilizer right before root formation to encourage big cassava tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani shishifãi lɛ aje kpo koni ewo ŋmei wuji lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have ragged holes in them and look like tiny worms are eating the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni etamɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Ni oooye baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are a key sign of Fall Armyworm attack. These caterpillars hide deep inside the central funnel of the plant, so spraying targeted organic mixtures or recommended control products directly into the funnels early stops them before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Buji ni etse yɛ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ ji okadi titri ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm tutua mɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ loo nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔ lɛ awo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha amɛkpa dani amɛbaakpãtã tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, that natural food stays in the dirt, making the soil richer for your maize without costing extra money for chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Adebɔɔ mli niyenii hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha o-ŋmãa lɛ ni ofiteee shika babaoo yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomatoes turn black and rot before the fruit can ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot pull up calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the fruit from developing this dark rot.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ aduawai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do strong winds easily push over my plantain trees right when the fruits start growing heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa mi-plantains lɛ nɔ mlɛo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi shwiili lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches against strong wind. Supporting the main stem with sturdy bamboo poles and planting them in clusters helps distribute the weight and block wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fi tso wulu lɛ sɛɛ ni adu amɛ kui amli lɛ, ebaaja muji lɛ mli ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and yellow even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer from the soil. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks after planting gives your crops full access to nutrients so they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high heat, dry soil, or standing water. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my plants with dry grass or cocoa pod husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic material, called mulching, acts like a shade cover that stops the hot sun from baking the soil dry. It holds water in the ground longer and slowly rots into natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow if I plant them in dry soil before the main rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ waa?

english: Maize seeds require steady moisture in the topsoil to soften their outer coat and sprout. If you plant in dry soil before continuous rains begin, the seeds will either dry out and die under the heat or get eaten by insects and birds.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui he miihia ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni eha kponɔgbɛ ŋmei lɛ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee blɛoo. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ latsaa be lɛ shishi loo kooloi bibii kɛ okpoi yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified hybrid seeds instead of planting seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred to produce high yields and resist common local diseases. Saved seeds from previous harvests lose these strong traits, which leads to uneven plant growth and much smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛha yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli helai. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight and dry winds. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that provide essential shade and retain soil moisture, protecting the cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, overly damp, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches and clearing weeds around the base of the trees improves sunlight and airflow, which helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo Kpãa niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Tsei ashishi haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for building green stems and leaves. Applying well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-based fertilizer will help restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni akɛfee tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas in the same field with my maize crop?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize improves your soil. Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which pulls nitrogen from the air and puts it back into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for your maize.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo. Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa o-corn lɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the central leaves of my young maize plants and leaving holes behind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni amɛshiɔ bu yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the funnel of the plant to feed on tender growth. Checking your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract directly into the central funnel will stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli koni amɛye tsei ni shwereɔ waa lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ awo gbɛ ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to set up tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tso kakadaŋŋ ko koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants rely on their leaves reaching sunlight to produce energy for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing the plant to get full sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulbs agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ tsei lɛ ahe helai anaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa hulu la ni fa babaoo.
