english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves dry up and drop off, and the stem base hardens. You can confirm by gently digging up the soil around one plant stem to check if the tubers have swollen to a good size before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi. ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli wa Obaanyɛ oma enɛ nɔ mi kɛtsɔ ŋtayaa ni ooofo kɛbɔle he lɛ nɔ. A light trunk Koni akɛkwɛ kɛji ŋmeii lɛ edara kɛyashɛ bɔ ni sa loo amɛdarako dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without developing into fruits when the weather is very dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress cause tomato plants to drop their blossoms to conserve energy. Covering the soil around the base with dry grass mulch keeps the soil cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on the stem and form fruits.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa tomato tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Mulching around Shishitoo ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ tsei kɛ aduawai anɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the soil around them dries out too fast. Leaving some tall shade trees or planting plantains around them acts as a shelter to keep the air humid and protect the young plants until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni sũ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hu shãa. egbiɔ oya tsɔ ni ejieɔ tsei kakadaji Haa hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui ebɔle ehe. Etsuɔ nii akɛ he ko ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa.

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape, it usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to build healthy green leaves. The plant moves the little nitrogen it has left from the older bottom leaves to feed the young top leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, eŋɔli. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: If cassava cuttings are planted too close together, their underground roots compete aggressively for soil space, water, and food. Instead of getting large, heavy tubers, you will harvest many thin, woody roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ niyenii he akaŋshii mli waa. Yɛ yitso agbo ni tsii najiaŋ lɛ Obaakpa shishifãi babaoo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni abaanyɛ adu.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up into tight curls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves roll up during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant hold onto its water. However, if the leaves stay curled even in the cool morning, it may be a sign of tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpã yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ mli lɛ, Ebaanyɛ efee okadi hu ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii komɛi, tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ eba.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly very wet. Heat stress stops the flower from pollinating itself properly, so the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Heat haomɔ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow crooked and split instead of growing straight and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ebɔle ehe ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow sideways or bend when they hit hard, compacted soil or heavy stones underground. Making high, soft soil mounds free of rocks allows the yam to expand downward easily and grow straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa afã loo amɛkotoɔ kɛji amɛtswa shikpɔŋ ni wa loo ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ ni afee lɛ haa sweet potato lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛyaa shi mlɛo ni edaa shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why did the stems of my crops turn black and wither after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Placing dry fertilizer directly against a plant stem burns the tissue because the salts in the fertilizer pull moisture straight out of the plant. Fertilizer should always be placed in a ring a small distance away from the stem when the soil is moist.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã fãji lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baagbala ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ring mli ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves showing light green and yellow patches with twisted edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ji eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshishigbɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is a sickness spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease stops the leaf from making food properly, leading to smaller harvests.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ baafee bibioo.

english: Why does my plantain bunch remain small and thin even when the tree looks tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains akui lɛ ji bibii lolo ni amɛhe ejɔ eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛkwɔ moŋ?

english: A plantain tree needs a large amount of water and soil nutrients like potassium right at the time the bunch emerges. If the plant lacks water or good soil food during bunch formation, the individual plantain fingers cannot swell up.
ga: Nu kɛ niyenii babaoo he miihia plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ potassium, kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai yɛ be mli ni afeɔ kuu lɛ Nine fɛɛ nine nyɛŋ atsɔ.

english: Weed seeds naturally sleep in the soil and are adapted to sprout instantly at the first drop of rain. Because your crop plants take longer to establish their roots, clearing weeds early prevents them from stealing all the water and nutrients meant for your crop.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ni ebaatsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛfeɔ shishifãi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaju nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave my wet animal manure sitting directly on top of my wooden worktable?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii ni efɔ yɛ mi tso okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving wet manure on a flat surface like a table traps moisture underneath, which damages the surface over time and creates an unhygienic environment where bacteria and flies can multiply.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ, tamɔ okpɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shishi. Enɛ baafite ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ehaa shihilɛ ko ni he tseee ni bacteria kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ afɔ yɛ mli lɛ baa

english: Why do extension officers recommend hanging sacks of wet compost off the ground to dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ awo kotokui amli koni egbi lɛ?

english: Hanging a permeable sack allows gravity to draw out excess water evenly through the bag, preventing the organic material from sitting in trapped liquid and rotting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ kotoku ko ni nu tsɔɔ mli lɛ fɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛtsɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkafite.

english: Is the liquid dripping from my stored manure bags safe to touch with my bare hands?
ga: Ani nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-manure kotoku lɛ mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ niji ni bɛ nɔ ko ataa he?

english: No, because while the liquid is packed with plant nutrients, those same nutrients make it a prime breeding ground for bacteria, making it unhygienic to touch without protection.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ yɛ be mli ni nu lɛ mli eyi kɛ tsei amli niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ, Nakai niyenii mli hewalɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ haa he ko ni he hiaa waa ni bacteria fɔɔ yɛ. Enɛ haaa efee nɔ ni he tseee kɛji akɛ ata he ni abuuu he.

english: What will happen to my organic plant mixtures if I do not let the excess water drain out during storage?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-organic tso nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ? Kɛji mihaaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: If excess water cannot escape, the organic mixture will become sour and unhygienic, which can ruin nearby farm tools and reduce the overall quality of your fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ ajie nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe tseee. Enɛ baanyɛ afite okwaayeli he nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ. ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi

english: How can I safely dry wet poultry manure without creating a dirty mess on my farm floor?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ magbi kooloi ashishifã ni efɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ muji ko akafee miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Place the wet manure inside a breathable bag and suspend it somewhere outdoors so the excess water drains off naturally into the soil below, keeping your storage surfaces clean.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efɔ lɛ awo kotoku ko mli ni okɛwo kpo nɔ koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he atse

english: Why does my stored organic fertilizer start to smell bad and attract flies so quickly when it stays wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-organic fertilizer ni mikɛto lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ oya ni egbalaa ŋmeii kɛji etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: High nutrient content combined with stagnant water creates perfect conditions for germs and flies, so draining the excess water is key to maintaining farm hygiene.
ga: Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni akɛfataa nu ni ekã shi lɛ he lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ ji nɔ titri ni haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ.

english: Why does hanging a bag of wet farm inputs dry it out better than laying the bag flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kotoku ni mli efɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛaawo mli lɛ haa egbiɔ jogbaŋŋ fe kotoku lɛ ni akɛaama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hanging the bag allows air to circulate all around it and lets water drip freely out of the bottom, whereas laying it flat traps liquid at the base.
ga: Baagi lɛ ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ ehe. ni oha nu lɛ ajɛ shishigbɛ atsɔ oya Kɛtsɔ kotoku lɛ ni oookɛfɔ̃ shi koni ekɛmɔ nu lɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Will my organic fertilizer lose all its food for crops if water drains out of the bag?
ga: Ani mi-organic fertilizer lɛ baafite niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji nu ho kɛjɛ kotoku lɛ mli?

english: No, allowing excess water to drain out removes unnecessary moisture to prevent spoilage, while leaving the rich organic solids and vital nutrients trapped safely inside the bag for your crops.
ga: Dabi, nu ni fa fe nine ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ mli lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni ekafite. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, eshiɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it important to remove standing water from green crop waste before using it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie nu ni damɔ shi kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ amli dani akɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water in organic waste leads to foul rotting conditions that are unhygienic, whereas properly drained material decomposes cleanly into safe nutrients.
ga: Nu ni eshwɛ yɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ haa fitemɔ shihilɛi ni he tseee baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni ajieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baafite yɛ gbɛ ni he tse nɔ ni etsɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is the best way to handle wet nutrient-rich materials so they don't spoil my farm shed?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nibii ni efɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe nii koni ekafite mi ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Wrap the materials securely inside a bag and hang it up so the water leaks out into a controlled area, keeping your shed floors and tables free from water damage and contamination.
ga: Okɛ nibii lɛ awo kotoku mli jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo mli koni nu lɛ ajɛ mli kɛya he ko ni akudɔɔ. Ha oshĩa lɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ okpɔlɔi lɛ akafite ni nu akafite amɛ.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Ekɛ ehe ewo baa lɛ mli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. They feed on young maize leaves, which reduces crop growth. You can manage them by checking your farm early, applying recommended control treatments, or putting clean sand mixed with ash directly into the leaf center.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, amɛyeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Kɛ nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii Aloo okɛ ŋã ni he tse ni akɛ sũ efutu mli lɛ awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and shade. Pruning overhead tree branches to let sunlight reach the crop and removing infected pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni shwereɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo fe nine mli kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe, ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn pale yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tseee lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential plant nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding compost, animal manure, or appropriate fertilizers helps restore nutrients so the plant can grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. titri lɛ nitrogen Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba koni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why should I leave space between cassava sticks when planting instead of placing them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ oshi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ oodu amɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ amɛ ama amɛhe lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room under the soil to grow into thick tubers. Planting them too close forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin and small roots.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ tsɔ lɛ, ejieɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa.

english: How does planting beans or cowpeas in the same field as my maize help the soil?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds the surrounding maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ niyenii.

english: The first rain is often followed by a dry spell. If seeds germinate and the soil dries out completely, the young seedlings will wither and die before the continuous rainy season officially establishes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Tsei bibii lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni maŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ gbɛ lɛ aya nɔ.

english: Why is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning instead of under the afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ nu awo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha nu yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ani ehi fe no?

english: Watering under hot afternoon sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots absorb it. Morning watering allows water to sink deep into the soil where roots can draw moisture throughout the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted directly in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under intense heat. They require shade crops, like plantains or canopy trees, to filter the direct sunlight and keep the soil surrounding them cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi. Koni ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ atsu nii ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures the main plant produces large, heavy bunches of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops so much during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and consume the water, light, and soil food meant for your crops, which weakens the seedlings before they can establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛyeɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ dani amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa.

english: How does the size of my farmland affect the money I will make at harvest time?
ga: Te bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dara ha lɛ saa shika ni mana yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Larger land gives you space to harvest more crops, which can increase your earnings if well maintained. However, a small plot can still yield high profits if you use good farming methods, rich soil, and proper care rather than just relying on land size.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni da lɛ haa onáa hegbɛ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo, ni baanyɛ aha onine ashɛ shika nɔ kɛji okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Shi kɛlɛ, hei bibii baanyɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo lolo kɛji akɛ okɛ okwaayeli gbɛi kpakpai tsu nii. shikpɔŋ ni baa nii kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ he aaafɔ̃ shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ pɛ nɔ

english: Can I just plant any crop I want on my farm land, or do different crops need specific types of land?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. ni misumɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Aloo ani ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ henɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi?

english: Not all crops grow well on every piece of land. Some crops like cassava thrive in sandy soil, while crops like cocoa or maize require deep, fertile soil with good water drainage to produce well.
ga: Jeee ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei fɛɛ. Tsei komɛi, tamɔ ŋã, yeɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni tsei tamɔ kookoo loo ŋmãa he hiaa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai lɛ.

english: If I am lucky enough to get a bigger piece of land to farm, what extra things do I need to prepare for?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ hegbɛ ni minine shɛ shikpɔŋ agbo ko nɔ ni mikɛbaatsu okwaayeli he nii. Mɛɛ hesaamɔi krokomɛi ehe miihia ni mafee?

english: A bigger farm requires more labor for clearing and weeding, more seeds, and higher costs for fertilizers or pest control. Expanding your land only brings better returns if you have enough hands or funds to manage the full area.
ga: Okwaafoi wuji biɔ nitsumɔ babaoo koni akɛjie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. tsei dumɔwui babaoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo. Oshikpɔŋ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ baaha oná sɛɛnamɔi kpakpai kɛji oyɛ niji loo shika ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛbaakwɛ kpokpaa muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad if I pack my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my small farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes weak, thin plants that produce smaller fruits or grains compared to properly spaced plants.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ, ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui bibii kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do crops grow very tall and green on one section of my land but stay short and yellowish on another section?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ kuku ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ he kroko.

english: Soil fertility varies even across the same field. Spots where crops grow green and tall usually have richer topsoil or better moisture, while poor spots may lack essential plant food like nitrogen or suffer from hard, stony ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he kome po mli. Bei pii lɛ, hei ni tsei lɛ daa yɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛkwɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ loo nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ekolɛ hei ni ohiafoi yɔɔ lɛ bɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baaná he amanehulu.

english: Is it better for me to plant only one crop on my land, or should I mix different crops together?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kome yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu mli?

english: Mixing crops, such as planting legumes like beans alongside maize, protects your income if one crop fails. Certain crops also add nutrients back into the soil, helping neighboring crops grow stronger.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni akɛfutuɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshika he kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kome fite. Tsei komɛi hu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How do I know the exact time to sow my seeds when the rains start coming?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is safest to plant after the rains become steady and regular, not after the very first light rain. Planting too early during unpredictable rains can cause young seedlings to dry up and die in the hot sun.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ aaadu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa, ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ. Jeee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ fioo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if the soil on my farm is tired and needs a rest or extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni mafo mli loo akɛ tsei niyenii krokomɛi afata he?

english: Tired soil often becomes hard, turns light in color, and yields smaller harvests each year even when weather is good. You can restore it by adding animal manure, compost, or letting it rest (fallowing) for a season.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ fɔɔ shiwoo ni wa, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ewooo yibii babaoo daa afi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ hi po. Obaanyɛ okɛwo mli ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ni oooha ejɔɔ ehe (oshi lɛ) be kome lɛ nɔ.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from choking your young crops and reducing your yield.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafo ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes the leaves of my food crops to curl up and turn yellow before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually warning signs that your plants are under stress. This can be caused by sap-sucking insects, viral diseases, or a lack of water and key nutrients in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ miihe afee shoo. Kooloi ni nuɔ nu, helai ni jɛɔ muawai amli baa, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni he hia ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛba.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and showing holes in the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves with holes usually mean fall armyworm caterpillars are feeding on your maize. Applying the right bio-pesticide early in the morning or late evening when the caterpillars are active will stop them from damaging the growing point of the plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bu yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmeii miiye o-corn lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and shrinking instead of growing broad and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem oil spray or insecticidal soap helps the plant produce normal, healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ baai ni sa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before any fruit grows on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and using balanced nutrients helps the plant set strong fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be, ni akɛ niyenii ni sa tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full, direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and lose water too fast. Growing temporary shade crops like plantain beside them creates a cool environment that protects young cocoa during its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni nu lɛ hu sɛɛ foɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high into the air to catch maximum sunlight for leaf growth, which feeds the tuber underground. Without stakes, the leaves rot on the damp soil, resulting in very small yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awó amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo koni baa lɛ adara. Enɛ baaye shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ lɛ, baai lɛ baagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast through evaporation under the hot sun. Covering the ground with dried leaves or crop residue (mulch) shades the dirt, retains moisture longer, and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo tsei amli nibii ni etse (Mulch) ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ muji naa. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ

english: Why should I avoid applying my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes loose fertilizer off the topsoil into nearby gutters before the plant roots can drink it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the ground is moist but heavy downpours are not expected.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse ehe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa nubui ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ nuɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi akpaaa nugbɔ ni naa wa gbɛ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest yield much less than certified seeds bought from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specially bred for maximum strength and yield in their first planting. Saving seeds from that harvest causes them to lose those special high-yield traits in the next generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo kɛ yibiiwoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Dumɔwui ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ haa amɛsui ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ jeɔ amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: How do I decide which small suckers to cut off from my main plantain stem?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ kɛji mafolɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mi-plantain tso titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A plantain stem gives away too much energy if it supports too many shoots at once. Keeping only one main plant, one medium sucker, and one tiny shoot ensures all soil nutrients focus on building one large, heavy fruit bunch.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo tsɔ kɛji amɛfiɔ tsei babaoo asɛɛ shikome. Tso titri kome pɛ, tso bibioo kome, kɛ tso bibioo kome ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso yibii agbo kome ni tsii ni afeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy or flat soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why should I buy packaged certified seeds from seed producers instead of just using seeds saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe nitsulɔ ko dɛŋ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i he kɛ je ye nyagbe kpami ɔ mi ɔ pɛ tsu ní.

english: Packaged certified seeds are specially tested and bred to grow fast, resist common crop diseases, and produce much higher yields. Seeds saved from past harvests often carry hidden diseases and lose their strength, leading to uneven growth and smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ paketi lɛ mli ni awo he odase lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ amɛ koni amɛdara oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo babaoo Bei pii lɛ Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee kɛ yibiiwoo ni faaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear away all the tall trees on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani miduɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight and heat. Tall shade trees act like living umbrellas that protect young cocoa from direct sun and keep the soil moist until the cocoa plants are old enough to handle full sunlight.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu kɛ dɔlɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ shade mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he tɛ̃ɛ. Ni ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ agbo bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green food. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen out of the soil, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni ji eŋɔli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same nutrients out of the soil every season and lets maize pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil naturally and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ shii abɔ He kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha ŋmãa mli ŋmeii abua amɛhe naa ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers under the ground are small and thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or too much shade, it spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of food below. Giving plants proper spacing and full sunlight encourages energy to move down into swelling the roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo loo hulutsoo babaoo nɔ. Ebaafite hewalɛ fɛɛ ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo lɛ, ewoɔ hewalɛ hewalɛ koni eya shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce small fruit bunches when I let many shoots grow around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii bibii lɛ? Akɛni miŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he hewɔ lɛ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water, light, and nutrients from the main plantain tree. Pruning excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main tree to direct all its food into forming large, heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsoji bibii lɛ, juɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ashi niji kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee aduawai ni tsii ni dara.

english: Why do I need to clear the ground and stake my yam vines with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie he ko ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground and away from wet soil diseases, helping the plant photosynthesize better and build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee amɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efeɔ fotosintɛsis ni efeɔ bulbs agboi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly when the plants suffer from severe heat stress or dry soil. When it gets too hot or water is scarce, the plant intentionally sheds its blossoms to conserve water and protect itself from dying.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi titri kɛ́ tso lɛ naa dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Kɛ́ edɔ tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ Tsei baajɛ amɛtsuiŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do the roots of my crops rot and decay during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When water sits on a farm for too long without draining, it fills all the tiny air pockets in the soil, preventing roots from breathing oxygen. Without oxygen, plant roots suffocate, die, and begin to rot underground.
ga: Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Nu lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ amu kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies. Controlling these insects early with appropriate sprays protects the foliage and keeps the plant producing peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for growth, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or manure and improving soil drainage will help your crop regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is healthy enough for planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ tomato nɔ?

english: Healthy tomato soil is dark, crumbly, holds moisture without staying soaked, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter. If weeds grow vigorously and the earth breaks easily in your hand, the soil has good nutrients for vegetables.
ga: Tomato shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwieee nɔ. ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni miifite lɛ ahe nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ Kɛji jwɛi lɛ dara waa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fãa oya yɛ oniji amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baaná niyenii kpakpai kɛha aduawai.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable crop early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because the soil absorbs the moisture before the sun gets too hot. Afternoon sun quickly evaporates water before roots can drink it, and can stress hot leaves.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baaŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu lɛ adɔ tsɔ. Gbi gbɛkɛ hulu lɛ haa nu lɛ feɔ la oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ haomɔ aba baai ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa yield decrease when I plant the trees very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: Overcrowded cocoa trees fight with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Dense planting also traps heat and moisture between trees, making it easy for diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Dumɔ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa helai tamɔ black pods lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot when I plant them in swampy land during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen in the soil to stay alive. Excess standing water suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungi to multiply, causing the tubers to decay before harvest.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping soil consistently moist and mulched helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni awo nɔ ŋmɔtɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my yam leaves during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ diji yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are typically caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which thrives in warm, wet conditions. Clearing infected leaves early and spacing plants properly helps slow down the infection.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ nu mli. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa baaye abua ni hela lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get full of small holes after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: The holes are made by tiny insects called weevils that lay eggs inside dry seeds. Drying your cowpeas thoroughly under the sun and storing them in airtight containers starves insects of air and stops damage.
ga: Kooloo bibioo ko ji mɔ ni fee bu nɛɛ. Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmei. ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ dumɔwui ni egbi mli Kɛ́ agbi tsina ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye kɔɔyɔŋ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni amɛkpa nɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my food crops after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants adapted to absorb water and soil nutrients instantly. Removing weeds early in the season stops them from stealing light and nutrients away from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni agbeɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haaa amɛju la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize in the exact same spot on my farm every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in one spot drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows maize-loving pests to build up in the soil. Rotating with legumes like groundnuts recharges soil nitrogen naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the leaves of my cocoa trees turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their leaves during the dry Harmattan season to prevent water loss through evaporation. Providing shade trees and keeping organic mulch around the base helps the soil retain moisture so the trees stay green.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haaa nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ la ni hoɔ lɛ hewɔ lɛ akafite. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and makes the edges look chewed?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ anɔ ni eha eshishigbɛi lɛ afee tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre?

english: Tiny holes and ragged edges on young maize leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the crop. Applying recommended control methods early in the morning directly into the central leaf whorl prevents major crop loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ nii lɛ tsu nii leebi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress or irregular watering. Maintaining a steady watering routine at the base of the plant helps the flowers convert into healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu daa yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and naturally put it into the soil through their roots, which feeds the maize and improves soil fertility without costly chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: Why should I remove the extra young suckers growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra suckers steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the parent plantain stem. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Suckers krɛdɛɛi juɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground using energy captured by sunlight on their leaves. Staking keeps the leaves spread out toward the sun and prevents wet ground contact, which reduces leaf fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni anáa kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaaa amɛyashɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa shi

english: How can I tell if my cassava field is ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves begin to turn yellow and drop, and the soil at the base of the stem cracks open slightly due to the expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai lɛ je shishi amɛfee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli egbɛ eshwa fioo yɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ hewɔ.

english: The first rain of the season often only wets the top layer of soil while the deep soil remains dry and hot, which can heat up and kill newly germinated seeds. Waiting for consecutive rainfall ensures enough moisture underground for seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he egbi ni edɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ adɔ ni egbe dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Watering early in the morning allows plant roots to soak up water before the hot afternoon sun causes quick evaporation, ensuring the plant stays hydrated through the day.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ haa amɛshwieɔ shi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard and woody to cook if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava tubers stay in the ground past their ideal harvest time, the plant turns its tender soft starch into tough plant fibers to survive dry conditions, making the roots hard and woody.
ga: Be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi kpamɔ be ni sa lɛ eho. Tsei tsakeɔ starch ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ewoɔ tso mli fibers ni mli wa mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tso

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential soil food that helps plants stay green and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does covering the soil around my cabbage roots with dry grass help them grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi wo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle kaabe shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass acts as a blanket that traps moisture in the ground, keeps roots cool in the hot sun, and stops weeds from stealing plant food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ. ni ehaaa jwɛi akaju niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli

english: Why do my cassava plants drop almost all their leaves when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to conserve water inside its stem and roots, allowing it to survive heat until the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi koni nu ahi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Ha eŋmɛ etsui shi yɛ latsaa lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Extreme heat and lack of water cause severe stress to tomato plants, making their flowers drop before they can form fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my corn stalks grow very thin with small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the corn plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving little energy to grow large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, Abele tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná koni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches if I leave all the young shoots growing at the base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ daa bibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Extra shoots suck away valuable water and soil nutrients from the main plantain stem, leaving less energy for the main stem to grow big fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ nu ni jara wa kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ plantain tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aha tso titri lɛ koni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why does my yam vine need to climb up a wooden stake to give me large yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni enyɛ ená sweet potato agbo ko aha mi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make energy, so staking the vine helps the leaves catch light and send nutrients down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ wain tso lɛ wo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaa lɛ naa la ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers push themselves down into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are unique because after the flower opens, it bends down and buries itself in the soil where the actual peanut pods grow underground.
ga: Peanuts yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ kɛ́ amɛfɔ lɛ, amɛkotoɔ ni amɛfuɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to grow when I plant them straight into the main field soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds have delicate roots that need soft, moist nursery soil to germinate before they are strong enough to handle full sun in the main field.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ dani amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye hulu muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Continuous rain and damp air create perfect conditions for a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly across cocoa pods when foliage stays wet.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod baa. Enɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli fɛɛ beni baai lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into thin tubes when the midday sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during hot hours to protect themselves from losing too much water. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite amɛ. Eji tso lɛ adebɔɔ naa gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its lower leaves during dry periods to conserve water and send remaining nutrients to the growing tips and root tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ koni ekɛ nu ahi shi ni ekɛ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aya shishi kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plant flowers fall off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or water is inconsistent, because extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents pollen from fertilizing the blossom.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ, ni ehaaa pollen lɛ awo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow fast and have large leaves that provide the necessary shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hia. Ehe miihia ni kookoo bibioo lɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight to make food, while keeping delicate leaves off the hot ground where heat and wet soil can cause rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ahe. Dɔlɛ kɛ sũ ni efɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha egbo.

english: Why do groundnut plant stems bend down into the soil after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: After groundnut flowers are pollinated, the plant forms stems called pegs that grow downward to push the seed pods into the soil where the nuts can safely develop underground.
ga: Beni tso lɛ efo ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollen sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs. Enɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛya shi koni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifã lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ adara shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster on my land than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild plants adapted to survive tough conditions, allowing their roots to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves shrinking and curling upward at the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ekɛmiibɔle ehe yɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Upward leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the plant's sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains stay for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out air, suffocating the roots and creating a wet environment where soil fungi can easily attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atutua oya ni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why does planting maize on the exact same plot every year make the harvest smaller each time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa ŋmãa bibioo baa be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Growing maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover, while allowing maize-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shii abɔ. ni ahaaa be ni akɛsaa jɛmɛ yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ ko ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young rice leaves start turning yellow at the tips during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-rice baai bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaf tips usually mean your rice crop is lacking nitrogen or water. When soil nutrients are low, the plant takes food from its older leaves to feed new growth, causing the leaf tips to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ o-rice tso lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs end up with missing kernels instead of full rows of grain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii ni elaaje yɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when hot sun or dry weather ruins the silks during flowering. Every kernel needs pollen to land on its individual silk; if the weather is too dry or hot, pollination fails and those kernels never form.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi fite siliki lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu he miihia pollen koni enyɛ eshɛ esiliki lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo edɔ lɛ Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii ni nakai dumɔwui lɛ efeee.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my paddy rice so the grains do not break during milling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Koni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ akakumɔ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Harvest your rice when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains on the stalk turn golden yellow while the main stem is still slightly green. If you leave it too long in the field, the grains become too dry and brittle, causing them to shatter inside the milling machine.
ga: Kpaa ŋmãa be mli ni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa titri lɛ ji ŋmãa fioo lolo lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Ŋmaa lɛ baagbi tsɔ ni ebaagbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fãa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy branches instead of food roots. Cassava needs soil rich in potassium to send food down to expand the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji amli moŋ fe ni ekɛ shishifãi baatsu nii kɛye niyenii. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia Cassava koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ aha.

english: Why does my crop yield improve when I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in my field before planting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani midu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have small root nodules that take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. When the legumes finish, they leave behind rich, natural food that helps your next crop grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ etee Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii babaoo ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper crops grow stunted and struggle when planted in hard red clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛnaa naagbai kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ tsuru ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil packs tightly together, making it hard for delicate roots to spread out and find air or water. Mixing organic compost or decomposed manure into clay soil loosens it up so roots can easily grow and absorb plant food.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛna kɔɔyɔɔ loo nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo futu shikpɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni amɛŋɔ tsei aniyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before they develop into young pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛbatsɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or attacks from insects like mirids. Keeping shade trees in your field protects the delicate flowers from harsh sunshine and retains moisture so pods can form.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatu ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ wo ŋmɔji amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni ekwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni pods lɛ afee.

english: Why do fall armyworms cause so much damage to my maize field during short dry spells in the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall worms lɛ fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be kuku lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry spells allow armyworm eggs to hatch quickly without heavy rains washing the tiny caterpillars off the leaves. The dry heat also slows down the plant's growth, making it easier for caterpillars to eat through tender leaves.
ga: Be ni nugbɔ egbi lɛ haa cutworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ oya ni nugbɔ ni naa wa he ehiaaa koni ekɛfɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli. Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi lɛ hu haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii akɛ amɛyeɔ baai bibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and collapse even when the soil around them is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛkuɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli edɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot disease in the soil. The harmful bacteria block the plant's inner tubes, stopping water from traveling up from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsiɔ tsei amli tsɔnei lɛ anaa. Kaaha nu miiho kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛtee baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop dark mold and spoil quickly inside the storage sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ nii ni efiteɔ oya yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Maize rots inside sacks when it is bagged before being dried thoroughly under the sun. Excess moisture trapped inside warm, closed bags creates the perfect home for fungus and mold to spread through the grain.
ga: Abele baagbo yɛ kotokui lɛ amli kɛ́ akɛwo kotoku mli dani agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kotoku ni mli edɔ ni aŋã mli lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow from the bottom up before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi dani abele lɛ afee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize crop lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for crop growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and produce full corn cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no ji niyenii titri ni haa tsei lɛ daraa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Is it true that planting cowpeas together with my maize will help my soil stay fertile?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa du tsina ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ewo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds the soil, helping your maize grow better while reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need to buy.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli ni esa akɛ ohe lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry like a brick just a few days after rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi tamɔ brikii yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter like compost, dried leaves, or animal manure. Mixing organic matter into your field acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold water much longer so your crops don't dry out quickly during sunny days.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai ni egboi, loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ egbiɛɛ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the leaves and central stems of my young maize crops?
ga: Mɛni ji bu ni bɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that hides inside the funnel of the maize plant. Early monitoring and applying recommended botanical or biological sprays can control them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe ewoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ agbɛjegbɛi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra ni akɛ tsofai loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Abaanyɛ akudɔ lɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing leaves or fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa baai loo aduawai lɛ adalɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral disease they transmit. Removing affected leaves early and spraying with an organic neem oil solution helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Baai ni ena hela lɛ ajiemɔ mra Ni akɛ organic neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi nɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants keep falling over in the wind before the bunches mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are easily damaged by microscopic soil pests called nematodes. Propping heavy plants with sturdy wooden poles and mulching around the base keeps root systems cool and firmly anchored.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ oya. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots suffocate and rot when water sits trapped in flat, heavy soil. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots receive enough oxygen.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu mɔmɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsii lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. koni shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Why are my soybean plants growing tall with lots of leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ miiya hiɛ ni ebaa babaoo shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes soybeans focus all their energy on growing leafy foliage rather than flowers. Adding phosphorus fertilizer encourages the crop to bloom heavily and develop abundant seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa soybean lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tsei ahe tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Fosfɔs ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnáa dumɔwui babaoo.

english: How is certified maize seed from agricultural officers better than saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Abele dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ema nɔ mi lɛ Te ehi fe bo diɛŋtsɛ odumɔwui ni obaabua naa lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Certified seed is specially bred to resist local diseases, tolerate dry spells, and give high yields. Saved seeds lose their vigor over generations, resulting in smaller harvests and weaker plants.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli. Enɛ haa yibii bibii kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop seeds fail to sprout even when I plant them right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ po?

english: Planting seeds too deep in soil that is either too dry or completely waterlogged prevents them from getting the air and gentle warmth needed to break open. Planting seeds at the correct shallow depth ensures uniform germination.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ tsɔ lɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtswa lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni mli kwɔɔɔ lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ daa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa trees need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Will planting groundnuts together with my maize harm the growth of my maize?
ga: Ani ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaye ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ awui?

english: Groundnuts actually help maize because groundnut roots take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, serving as a natural fertilizer that feeds the maize crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ ebuaa abele diɛŋtsɛ ejaakɛ abele shishifãi lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmãa niyenii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cassava plants turning yellow and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava naturally sheds its leaves during long dry spells to save water and stay alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout new leaves and continue growing normally.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi wala mli. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eda bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I know if my maize crop desperately needs water or if it is just reacting to normal afternoon heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia mi-ŋmã lɛ diɛŋtsɛ loo eefee nɔ ko kɛkɛ yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he?

english: If maize leaves roll up like pencils during the hot afternoon but open flat again by early morning, the plant is managing normal heat. If the leaves stay tightly rolled up early in the morning, the soil is too dry and needs water immediately.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baa ko shwie shi tamɔ pensil yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli shi ekã shi ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miikwɛ dɔlɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni ehe miihia ni aná nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Purple leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking phosphorus or the ground is too cold and waterlogged for the plant's roots to draw up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: My tomato plants have many green leaves, so why are the flowers dropping off without making tomatoes?
ga: Mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔlii babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi shi jeee tomatoi lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, water is inconsistent, or when too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. Aloo beni nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open in the field before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they receive a sudden heavy watering or rain after a dry period. The inside of the head absorbs water and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei lɛ baajara kɛji amɛná nu babaoo loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ. Bulb lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking the sap from under the leaves and spreading plant viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni shwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over at the root even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when pests like banana root borers or microscopic worms called nematodes destroy the underground roots, leaving the tall, heavy plant without a firm anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kooloi tamɔ banana shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ba. Aloo ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni etsii ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my harvested yam tubers to turn soft and rot while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miifee blɛoo ni egbo beni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam rot happens when rot-causing fungi or bacteria enter the tuber through tiny cuts made by farm tools during harvest, especially if the storage area is warm and lacks fresh airflow.
