ga: Sweet potato fitemɔ baa kɛji ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ bote ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afo lɛ anɔ. ni ŋmɔ mli nibii feɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri kɛji akɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ jɛmɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and grow strong. Rain can wash this nutrient deep into the soil where roots cannot reach it, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Stretching up to reach light makes them tall and thin, but leaves them too weak to produce a good harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni shwieɔ shi kɛyaa la mli lɛ haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛhe waaa. Shi ehaa amɛgbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpa nikpamɔ kpakpa.

english: Why does my farmland dry out so fast even after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries out quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or dried plant leaves. Adding decomposed manure or leaving crop residues on top of the soil acts like a sponge, helping the ground trap water for your crops during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tso baai ni egbi. Nibii ni efite ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ nu toɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ hɔmɔ be mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die if I plant them in an open field without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast with big leaves that provide natural shade and cooler air, acting like protective umbrellas while the young cocoa trees build strength.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ mɔ he yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ maa hewalɛ

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need to lift their leaves off the ground to get as much sunlight as possible. When the vines climb up stakes, their leaves can make more food to send down into the ground, forming bigger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ tso lɛ nɔ Amɛbaai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ebafeɔ sweet potato tuber ni da fe no.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off without making any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or sudden dry soil. When the temperature gets too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and protect itself until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are small worms eating holes right inside the center leaf whorl of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, growing heart of the maize plant where it is easiest to eat. Checking your farm early in the morning allows you to catch and treat them before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tsɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni miida lɛ atsuii yɛ he ni amɛyeɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ ni otsa amɛ dani amɛfite hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and show yellow patches during warm weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled leaves with light yellow patches are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using resistant stems for planting helps protect your crop from getting damaged by this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dumɔwui amli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe kɛjɛ hela nɛɛ ni baafite lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my seeds when the rains first start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: It is safest to wait until there are three or four steady rains that soak deep into the soil rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting in soil that is wet deep down ensures seeds germinate fully without drying out.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii etɛ loo ejwɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kwraa ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to dig up when they grow underground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: You can tell cassava is getting mature when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem with leaves only at the top. You can also carefully dig around one plant to check the size of the tuber before harvesting the whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona akɛ ŋmei ko miida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ yitso ni bɛ nɔ ko ni baai yɔɔ nɔ lɛ pɛ eshwɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli hu. Akwɛ tso kome mli jogbaŋŋ koni ana bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees failing to grow well on some parts of my land in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-ghana lɛ ekomɛi anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees require deep, well-drained soil rich in organic matter. If the soil is too rocky, sandy, or holds too much water, the roots cannot grow properly, causing the crop to struggle or die.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ he miihia cacao tsei. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛi, ŋã, loo nu babaoo yɛ mli lɛ, Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ adara jogbaŋŋ. ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ

english: Is coffee a good crop to start with if my land is not suitable for cocoa?
ga: Ani kɔfe ji ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ esaaa kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, coffee is a strong alternative because it can tolerate slightly tougher soil conditions, lower nutrients, and drier weather better than sensitive cocoa trees.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɔfe ji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa fioo, niyenii ni mli wa fioo, kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa jogbaŋŋ fe cacao tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland is better suited for coffee than for cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ sa kɛha kɔfe fe kookoo?

english: Cocoa thrives in shaded, deeply fertile, moist soil, whereas coffee can handle more direct sunlight and slightly poorer or rocky soils where cocoa normally refuses to grow.
ga: Cocoa shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni shade yɔɔ nɔ. Deep rich Coffee lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ohia emɔ lɛ fioo loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, kookoo lɛ kwɛŋ.

english: Why do some crops refuse to grow on land where other crops grow easily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi kpooɔ akɛ aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei krokomɛi baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ oya lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops have unique needs for nutrients, water depth, and soil acidity. Land that lacks the specific nutrients cocoa needs might still have everything necessary for coffee or cassava to thrive.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiamɔ nii. nu lɛ mlibotemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ acidity lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa Shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha kookoo lɛ bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa koni kɔfi loo ŋmei akwɛ̃ lolo.

english: What kind of care does a young cocoa tree need when I first plant it in the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ kwɛmɔ nɛkɛ he hiaa kookoo tso bibioo ko beni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade cover from companion plants like plantains, clear ground around their base to prevent weed competition, and consistent moisture to survive their early months.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni bɔle amɛshishigbɛ lɛ he koni jwɛi akaye akaŋ. kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli.

english: Does the region where my farm is located in Ghana affect whether my cocoa crop will succeed?
ga: Ani kpokpaa ni miŋmɔ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ saa omanye ni miyeɔ yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ he?

english: Yes, cocoa requires high humidity and evenly distributed rainfall. Regions with long dry seasons or very shallow soil make cocoa farming much more difficult compared to high-rainfall forest zones.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo biɔ hulutsoo babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kpokpai ni hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ waa lɛ haa kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ nɔ ni wa waa kɛ akɛto hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop off during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry periods to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out completely. Adding shade trees helps reduce this water stress.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛtsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbi kwraa. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni akɛfataa he lɛ haa nu he haomɔ baa shi.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted coffee tree to start producing beans?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kɔfe tso hee ni adu lɛ jeɔ kɔfe ŋmeii afeemɔ shishi?

english: Coffee trees usually begin producing their first harvest about 3 to 4 years after planting, reaching full berry production capacity around 5 to 7 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔfi tsei jeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shishi aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ. Ni ebaaná berry feemɔ he hewalɛ ni fa yɛ aaafee afii 5 kɛyashi 7 mli.

english: Can I plant cocoa and coffee together on the same piece of farmland?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu kookoo kɛ kɔfe yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, you can intercrop them, but you must space them far enough apart so their roots and branches do not compete heavily for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okwɛ tsei yɛ amɛteŋ. Shi esa akɛ oshi he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ akashi akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What key steps should I take to prepare my land before planting coffee for the first time?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii ni he hiaa ni esa akɛ afee koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu kɔfe klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa?

english: Clear heavy weeds, dig wide and deep planting holes, and mix organic manure or compost into the soil to help the young coffee seedlings establish strong roots quickly.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua kɔfi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛtswa shishifãi ni wa oya.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow and dying?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure near the roots will help the leaves stay green and produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Officer, why are my okra plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but giving me very few pods?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi pods lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and big green leaves instead of making flowers and fruits. Using balanced fertilizer with more phosphorus will encourage the plant to produce more okra pods.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nitrogen babaoo Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo okra ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Officer, why do my cassava stems drop almost all their leaves during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Amralofoi Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out in the sun. Once the rains start again, the stem will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing big roots underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe koni hulu lɛ akagbi. Kɛ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Officer, why do my cowpea leaves fold up tightly during the middle of the afternoon when the sun is hot?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants fold their leaves to shade themselves and cut down on water evaporation when temperatures rise. It is a natural defense mechanism that helps the plant survive high heat until the weather cools down in the evening.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo aba ni amɛha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aba shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ. Eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli kɛyashiɔ gbɛkɛ mli fɛ̃i baa.

english: Officer, why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any peppers can form?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ afee?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when the weather gets too hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or if insects damage the flowers. Giving the plants steady water and protecting them from pests will help the flowers turn into pepper fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi fiteɔ fɔfɔii Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa ni obuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Officer, why are my tomato fruits developing black, rotten patches at the bottom end while growing?
ga: Officer Mɛni hewɔ mi tomatoi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ naagbee lɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium and uneven soil moisture. Keeping the soil consistently moist through mulching and adding organic compost or lime helps the plant take up calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shiŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua otsei lɛ ni amɛná calcium ni sa.

english: Officer, why are my cocoa pods turning black and wet while hanging on the trees?
ga: Agent Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni amɛkpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during cold, rainy periods. Pruning dense branches to let sunlight and air into the farm, along with removing spoiled pods, helps stop the rot from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fɛ̃i ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Dense pruning koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Kɛfata ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Officer, why are the leaves on my plantain suckers turning brown and dry around the edges?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Browning leaf edges are often caused by lack of water, heat stress, or leaf diseases like Sigatoka. Removing heavily damaged leaves and piling organic mulch around the base of the plantain will hold moisture in the soil and protect new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo tso helai tamɔ Sigatoka. Baai ni efite waa kɛ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ. Plantain shishifãi yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebuɔ baai heei ahe.

english: Officer, why do my yam shoots need to climb tall sticks instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Official Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to manufacture food for building big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the light and off damp soil, where fungal diseases can easily attack the leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ la ni tsoɔ waa mli, shi jeee yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atutua baai lɛ mlɛo lɛ

english: Officer, why do my maize plants easily fall over when a heavy wind blows through the farm?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa kɛfo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over if their roots are weak or if they are planted too close together, making their stems thin and soft. Spacing plants properly allows sunlight to build thick stems, and earthing up soil around the base gives roots extra support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ loo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ mli afee mlɛo ni efee bɔdɔɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ feɔ tsei akutsei ni mli tse. Ni shikpɔŋ ni akɛfataa shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ babaoo.

english: How do I properly prepare my land before planting maize so the crops grow strong?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu ŋmãa koni tso lɛ awa?

english: Preparing land well involves clearing weeds, loosening the soil so roots can push deep, and adding organic manure or compost before sowing. This creates a solid foundation for seeds to easily access water and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jɛmɛ. ni ajieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ akumɔ mli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli awo mli dani adu. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa shishitoo ni ma shi shiŋŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai mlɛo.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm field before sowing any crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with young crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Clearing them before planting ensures your seeds get all the resources they need to establish quickly without stress.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie mli dani odu lɛ, ehaa odumɔwui lɛ naa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛto amɛhe gbɛjianɔ oya ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why is it important for me to plan my crop planting schedule around the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mato midumɔ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting right at the start of the rains ensures your young crops receive natural, steady water during their critical early growth stages, saving you money on irrigation and setting up a good harvest timeline.
ga: Dumɔ mra yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii bibii lɛ aná adebɔɔ mli nu ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ amɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ shika toɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he ni otoɔ kpamɔ kpakpa he gbɛjianɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava plants are lacking nutrients in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy cassava has bright green leaves and steady stem growth. If the leaves turn yellow, show dark spots, or if growth stalls completely, the soil is low on essential nutrients like nitrogen or potassium.
ga: Kasava ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ diji, loo kɛji amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants shed their flowers before producing any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, sudden dry spells, or a lack of water and nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and mulched helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, ŋmɔlɔ trukaa, loo nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my pepper plants to stop growing when the weather gets very hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tsei lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa?

english: Extreme heat forces plants to lose moisture quickly through their leaves, so they enter a survival mode and pause growth. Watering early in the morning and placing mulch around the stems protects the roots from heat.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ boteɔ wala shihilɛ mli ni ekpaa dalɛ be kukuoo ko. Nu leebi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii abɔle he. Tso lɛ buɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and die back. This signals that the plant has finished transferring its energy underground to fully mature the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekɛ hewalɛ etee shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛha bulb lɛ adara.

english: Why do my watermelons split open in the field before I can pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ tswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani minyɛ mifo lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when they receive a heavy burst of water or rain after a dry period. The inside grows faster than the outer skin can stretch, so maintaining regular, balanced watering prevents splitting.
ga: Watermelon baatswa kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wo nu loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli yɛ be ko sɛɛ. Mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa ni ja lɛ baaye abua ni akagbala.

english: What is the best way to dry and store my harvested maize so it doesn't spoil before I find buyers?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ magbi mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ ni mikɛto koni ekafite dani mana mɔ ni baahe?

english: Drying maize thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard reduces moisture that causes mold. Storing the dried grains in airtight bags or clean silos protects them from moisture and weevils while you wait for buyers.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, ehaa nu ni kɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ wo vacuum bags loo silo ni mli tse mli lɛ, ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he be mli ni omɛɛɔ mɔ ko ni baahe lɛ.

english: How does sorting my harvested tomatoes by size and quality help me get a better price at the market?
ga: Te mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ mli ni mijaraa yɛ elɛɛmɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ naa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Sorting removes damaged or diseased produce that could ruin the rest of your harvest. Traders pay higher prices for uniform, clean, undamaged crops because they look better and last longer during transport.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ jieɔ nibii ni efite loo helai ni baanyɛ afite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ. Jarayelɔi woɔ jara ni nɔ kwɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa, ni he tse, ni efiteee. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ baafee fɛo ni amɛbaahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my NPK fertilizer as soon as I plant my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ pɛ?

english: If you apply chemical fertilizer right next to seeds, it can burn them before they germinate. Waiting until the young plants grow early roots ensures they can actually absorb the nutrients safely without damage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fata dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ashã dani amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ amɛmɛ kɛyashi tsei bibii lɛ baawo shishifãi oya lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: What does NPK fertilizer actually do for my crops?
ga: Te NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium. Nitrogen helps build strong green leaves, Phosphorus builds strong roots and flowers, and Potassium helps the plant fight off diseases and produce good fruits.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji feɔ. Fosfɔs haa shishifãi kɛ fɔfɔi ni mli wa baa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: How do I know the exact right time to put fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: The best time to apply top-dressing fertilizer is usually right when the crop enters its fast-growth stage or just before flowering, so the plant gets extra strength when it needs it most.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo mli ji be mli ni tso lɛ miibote edalɛ oyaiyeli mli loo dani ebaawo fɔfɔi. Koni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ kroko yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ

english: Can applying too much NPK fertilizer ruin my harvest?
ga: Ani NPK ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer adds too much salt to the soil, which pulls water away from the plant roots and causes the crops to wither and dry up as if burned.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei babaoo ahi sũ lɛ mli. ni baajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi amli ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbo ni amɛgbi tamɔ nɔ ni ashã.

english: Should I apply fertilizer when the soil is dry or wait for rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi loo esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: You should wait until the soil is moist after a rain. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it, and applying it to bone-dry soil can burn your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Ni shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ashã.

english: My crops are growing many leaves but no flowers yet, should I be worried?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi bɛ lolo. Ani esa akɛ mahao?

english: No, a crop must first build strong stems and leaves to gather energy before it can support flowers. As long as the leaves look healthy, flowering will happen naturally when the crop matures.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ama tsei kɛ baai ni wa klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛbua hewalɛ naa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua fɔfɔii. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ, fɔfɔi baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa be mli ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Is it normal for my crops to stop growing taller once flowers appear?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mitsei lɛ baakpa shweremɔ kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je kpo pɛ?

english: Yes, once a plant flowers, it shifts its energy away from growing leaves and stems to focus entirely on producing flowers, seeds, and fruits.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ tso lɛ fɔfɔi Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai kɛ tsei ni miida lɛ ahe koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ fɛɛ ama fɔfɔi, dumɔwui, kɛ aduawai ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my crops falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers can fall off if the crop is stressed by extreme heat, long dry spells, or a lack of key nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil moist and well-fed helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Fɔfɔi baanyɛ agbo kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa ha tso lɛ hao. Nuu be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. loo niyenii mli nibii titrii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How long after planting does maize usually start to produce flowers?
ga: Be enyiɛ beni adu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi?

english: Most maize varieties in Ghana begin to flower or show tassels around 50 to 60 days after planting, depending on water availability and soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo jeɔ fɔfɔi loo ŋmeii shishi aaafee gbii 50 kɛyashi 60 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ni enɛ damɔ nu ni yɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn slightly light green just before flowering starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ fioo dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Plants use up a huge amount of nutrients to prepare for flowering, which can briefly drain the leaves. Applying fertilizer around this stage helps the plant recover its deep green color and produce healthy yields.
ga: Tsei kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii kɛsaa amɛhe kɛha fɔfɔi. ni baanyɛ ajie baai lɛ amli nu yɛ be kukuoo mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa amɛhe su ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will help bring the healthy green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans helps my soil grow better crops next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When you harvest them, that trapped food stays in the soil to feed whatever crop you plant there next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. kɛji okpa lɛ Niyenii ni ekã lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass—known as mulching—keeps the soil cool, stops water from drying up quickly in the hot sun, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil before I even dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ po shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly when the soil holds too much water for long periods or if there is a fungal disease in the ground. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo be kakadaŋŋ loo ŋmeii hela ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that attacks the tender inner leaves of maize. Applying recommended control measures early into the center funnel of the plant can protect your crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling up and turning dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbi lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heat stress, irregular watering, or tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus. Keeping the soil evenly moist and controlling pests early prevents this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni ejaaa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and thin when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. Giving each seed proper spacing allows roots and stems room to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni sa yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground so leaves catch maximum sunlight and avoid rotting on the wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. koni baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ, ni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry weather, insect attacks, or lack of soil food. Providing shade trees and keeping soil moist helps the flowers stay on the tree to turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli, kooloi bibii tutua amɛ, loo niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers and tiny peppers before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi kɛ pepper bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Peppers drop flowers and young fruit when temperatures get too high, when water supply is irregular, or if the soil lacks key nutrients like potassium. Regular watering during dry spells helps hold the fruit.
ga: Peppers baajie fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa Aloo kɛji akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What key steps should I take to prepare my farm land in Nsawam before putting seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni he hiaa esa akɛ mafee koni mikɛsaa mi-swamp dumɔhe lɛ dani madu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Before planting, you need to clear old weeds and debris, then loosen the topsoil so root seeds can easily spread. Adding well-rotted manure or compost during land clearing gives the soil nutrients so your crops get off to a strong start.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie jwɛi momo kɛ sũ ni efite lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, gbálamɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya hiɛ koni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛje shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize after the first rains fall?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the soil is thoroughly wet deep down after a few steady rains. Planting right after the very first light rain is risky because the soil can quickly dry up, causing young sprouting seeds to die before the next rain comes.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni ehaa dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ gboiɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but the tubers underground remain very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ daraaa kwraa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, cassava puts all its energy into growing thick stems and leaves instead of storing food in the roots. Giving plants enough space and balanced nutrients helps the plant focus on expanding tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛhaa eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ He ni akɛaaha tso lɛ kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa eshishifãi lɛ amlilɛɛmɔ nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing starting from the bottom leaves usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen. Maize uses nitrogen to stay green and grow, and heavy rains can wash this food away deeper into the soil where young roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen tsuɔ nii koni ekɛha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ niyenii nɛɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into fresh tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato hee lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the ground around your plants moist and encouraging beneficial insects like bees helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ehiii. He ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei ni aaaha amɛfee fɛ̃i kɛ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni awoɔ he hewalɛ lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do people recommend that I plant plantain stems alongside my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create shade and trap soil moisture, protecting the young cocoa until it is big enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo ni haa sũ lɛ mli nu shwieɔ shi. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests when I plant many seeds close together in one small area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ he bibioo kome lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, their roots fight each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each crop enough room to stretch its roots and leaves to produce bigger fruits and stems.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe akaŋ kɛha nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ hulu la He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaagbala eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ amli kɛha aduawai kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking plant juices, or by viruses they spread. Checking under leaves regularly and using proper organic or recommended sprays can stop insects from damaging the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo tsei amli nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa kɛ tsofai ni sa loo ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛ tsofai fɔji tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha kooloi bibii akafite baai lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my crop seedlings and ruin my farm if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ ni efiteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji mijieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that suck up fertilizer and water faster than young crops can. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients and sunlight without fighting for survival.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ hulu la fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛwuu koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass or dead leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Tsoi ni jwɛi ni egbi loo baai ni egboi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from drying out moisture from the soil. It keeps the ground cool around plant roots and also prevents new weeds from popping up.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akashã ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ye obua shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ. Tse lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ejɔ ni amɛtsiɔ jwɛi heei anaa koni amɛkaje kpo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning around the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiishã yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves are very tender. When exposed to full sun without shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them, the leaves overheat and scorch, which slows down the tree's growth.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa. Kɛji akɛ onine shɛ hulu la ni fa ni hulutsoo bɛ nɔ lɛ tsei tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa baai lɛ hulutsoo. Baai lɛ baadɔ fe nine ni amɛbaashã. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ daamɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks in my farm for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Okɛwo ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni sweet potato tsei lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam plants are vines that naturally seek light to grow strong leaves. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread easily, and allows maximum leaves to catch sunlight, which feeds the growing yam tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni taoɔ la ni tsoɔ waa koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ ni ji sweet potato tubers ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii.

english: When too many young suckers grow around one plantain stem, they steal water, plant food, and sunlight from the main mother plant. Removing excess suckers leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring the main plant yields big, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Amɛjuɔ nu, tso niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri ko ni da ni tsii aba.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize plants and caterpillar dirt inside the center leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai lɛ yɛ bu ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmeii muji yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep central funnel of young maize plants to feed on tender leaves. Identifying these early symptoms helps you spray targeted remedies directly into the leaf funnel before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Kɛ́ oyɔse nɛkɛ mra be mli okadii nɛɛ, ebaaha okɛ tsofa ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ afɔ tso lɛ baa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani efite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up tightly and getting yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from infected plants to healthy ones by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Once infected, the plant cannot manufacture enough food, leading to stunted stems and very small tubers.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Ejɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni foɔ lɛ anɔ. atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Kɛji hela lɛ emɔ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛyitsei lɛ feɔ bibii waa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves rolling up like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the juices from the undersides of young leaves, or by intense heat and water stress. The leaf curls upward as a defense mechanism to reduce moisture loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ mli. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛba ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ shi.

english: The first rain of the season is often a false start, followed by hot, dry weather. If you plant too quickly, the soil will dry out before seeds establish strong roots, causing seeds to wither, rot, or fail to germinate altogether.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi dani dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ, amɛgboɔ, loo amɛkwɛ̃ɛɛ kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant beans or groundnuts on land where we previously harvested maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wɔkpaa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ tsutsu lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, while legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for future crops.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get extremely hot or when water supply drops suddenly. The heat stress causes the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy and water for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ba shi trukaa. Dɔlɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my young crop plants wilt and die when I pour chemical fertilizer directly against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ wo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of the plant stems and roots when placed too close. Fertilizer should be placed a few inches away from the stem in a ring so the roots can safely drink the nutrients without getting burned.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo amɛhe tsɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa.

english: Can I use water from a river where illegal mining takes place to water my vegetable farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ awo mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Water from rivers affected by illegal mining often contains dangerous heavy metals and chemical pollutants. Using this water can poison your plants, harm the soil, and make your harvested vegetables dangerous for people to eat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsofai ni fiteɔ nu lɛ yɛ faai ni shika tsuru ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ saa amɛhe lɛ amli. Nu nɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ awo tsei amli tsofa, efite shikpɔŋ, ni eha aduawai ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ oshara kɛha gbɔmɛi ni amɛyeɔ.

english: Why don't I see earthworms in my soil anymore after watering my farm with stream water from mining areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mana shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dɔŋŋ beni mikɛ faai ni jɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Earthworms are very sensitive to toxic chemicals and heavy metals. When polluted stream water enters your soil, it creates a toxic environment that kills earthworms and other helpful organisms that naturally keep your soil healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ dade ni tsii ahe waa. Kɛji faa mli nu ni mli ewo muji bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni gbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii krokomɛi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Will heavy metals in polluted soil actually get inside the cassava and yams that I harvest?
ga: Ani dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ baabote ŋmei kɛ ŋmei ni mikpaa lɛ mli diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, crop roots absorb minerals and water directly from the ground. If the soil contains heavy metals from polluted water or mining, the plant will take up those toxins and store them inside the roots and leaves, making the food unsafe to consume.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ashishifãi gbalaa mineral kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ dade ni tsii ni jɛɔ nu ni mli ewo muji mli loo kɛjɛɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nakai tsofai fɔji lɛ ni amɛbuaa amɛnaa yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ amli. Enɛ haaa niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha niyeli.

english: Why do the roots of my crops stay short and weak when planted near old mining lands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔ momo ko lɛ?

english: Heavy metals and harsh chemicals left in the ground burn the delicate growing tips of plant roots. This stops the roots from growing deep into the soil to find the nutrients and water the plant needs to grow strong.
ga: Dade ni tsii kɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shãa tsei shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa tso lɛ koni enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and stunted even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can happen when toxic substances in polluted soil damage the roots, preventing the plant from taking up essential nutrients like nitrogen, even if water is available.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ aba kɛji tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ sũ ni mli ewo muji lɛ mli lɛ fite shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, kɛji nu yɛ po.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off before they can produce any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani manyɛ mawo tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they experience extreme stress, such as intense heat, nutrient imbalances, or exposure to dirty water, saving energy to survive rather than producing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ ni naa wa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ejaaa lɛ he. loo nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛaakpe Eji hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ koni anyɛ ahi shi moŋ fe ni aaawo yibii.

english: Cassava drops its leaves as a natural way to save water during dry periods. The plant remains alive underground and will quickly sprout fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava baai ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ nu toɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Tso lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, ni kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaawo baai heei oya.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow tall and thin with very few peppers when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ pepper fioo ko pɛ beni midu lɛ yɛ tso agbo ko ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need full sunlight to bloom and produce fruit. When planted in thick shade, they stretch upward to search for light instead of putting energy into producing peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ he miihia hulu babaoo koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii. Kɛ́ eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ekpãa kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ena la, moŋ lɛ, efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over and wilting even though the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ efɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Excess water or poor drainage can rot the roots of plantain trees. Without healthy roots to breathe and anchor the tree, the plant cannot absorb water properly and will wilt and fall over.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha odumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ agbo. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni amɛkɛmuɔ ni amɛmɔɔ tso lɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaagbi ni ebaagbee shi.

english: Why should I avoid planting yams in the exact same patch of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop on the same land every year drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that target yams to build up, resulting in smaller harvests over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ sweet potato nɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa nibii ni afeɔ lɛ faaa yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How often should I water my crops once they start bearing fruit?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: When crops enter the fruiting stage, they require controlled watering—often just once or twice at critical development points—to help the fruit fill out properly without causing root rot or fruit splitting.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ bote yibiiwoo be lɛ mli lɛ Amɛbiɔ ni akudɔ amɛ nu—bei pii lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ pɛ yɛ hei ni he hiaa waa yɛ yibiiwoo lɛ mli lɛ—koni eye ebua yibii lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo yibii lɛ mligbalamɔ baaa.

english: Why do my crop seeds need extra water immediately after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu kroko he hiaa midumɔwui lɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Once a seed sprouts and starts growing, its young roots are weak and sensitive. Giving it adequate moisture right at the start helps it establish strong roots in the soil.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni amɛbɔi dalɛ Eshishifãi bibii lɛ baafee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha kɛjɛ shishijee lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi ni wa ama shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my crops if they do not get enough water during the flowering and fruiting stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo be mli?

english: If crops lack water when fruits are forming, the plant gets stressed and may drop its flowers or produce small, poor-quality fruits.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ Tsei lɛ naa haomɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite fɔfɔi loo amɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I keep watering my crops all the time until I harvest them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mawo minibii lɛ anɔ nu be fɛɛ be kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: No, you should reduce or stop watering at the right stage of crop maturity. Overwatering close to harvest can rot the crop or reduce the quality of the harvest.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ otsi nu ni okɛhaa lɛ nɔ loo okpa kɛji tso lɛ dalɛ he ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ shɛ. Nu ni fa babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ kpamɔ be lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my young crops need water right away?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu he miihia midumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: When young crops begin to sprout, wilting or curling leaves early in the day show that the soil has dried out and the plant needs immediate watering to survive.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ Baai ni egbo loo ebɔle amɛhe leebi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni ehe miihia ni awo tso lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ehi shi.

english: How do I know if I should plant my crops within one week or wait up to a month after preparing the land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ madu tsei yɛ otsi kome mli loo mamɛ kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome beni misaa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting timing depends on soil moisture and rains. Planting within a week of land preparation ensures the seeds catch early moisture before the soil dries out or weeds take over.
ga: Be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ damɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ otsi kome mli kɛjɛ be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ mra. Dani shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi loo jwɛi lɛ baaye nɔ

english: Is it bad to wait a whole month before planting after clearing my land?
ga: Ani ejaaa akɛ ooomɛ nyɔŋ muu fɛɛ dani odu nii beni ajie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Waiting too long like a month can cause the prepared soil to harden, lose essential moisture, and grow weeds, which weakens your new crop's chances of germinating well.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ be kakadaŋŋ, kɛyashi nyɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ ni asaa he lɛ mli awa. Fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ ni laajeɔ kɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ Enɛ haa hegbɛ ni yɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii heei baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it important to follow strict timing when planting and watering crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akwɛ be ni mli wa nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ?

english: Crops grow in specific stages; doing farm activities like planting or watering at the correct time ensures the crop gets what it needs precisely when it is growing most actively.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Okwaafoi anitsumɔi tamɔ dumɔwui loo nu ni awoɔ yɛ bei ni sa mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa waa lɛ.

english: Do crops need the same amount of water when they are young compared to when they mature?
ga: Ani nu ni he hiaa tsei beni amɛji bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdara kwraa lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, crops need lighter, consistent water when starting out, increased moisture during flowering and fruiting, and very little to no water as they mature for harvest.
ga: Dabi, nu ni mli waaa, ni fa babaoo po he miihia tsei kɛji amɛje shishi. Ha hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo be mli. Ni amɛkɛ nu fioo ko pɛ tsuɔ nii loo amɛkɛtsuuu nii kwraa kɛji amɛdara kwraa kɛha nikpamɔ.

english: Why does my crop suddenly require more care and water after staying small for a while?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛfee bibii be fioo ko lɛ?

english: When a crop transitions from early leaf growth to producing fruit, its internal energy demands increase, requiring extra water to support the new growth.
ga: Kɛ tsei tsake kɛjɛ baai ni daa oya kɛtee aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ehewalɛ ni he hiaa yɛ emli lɛ baaya hiɛ. Enɛ biɔ nu kroko ni akɛyeɔ abuaa dalɛ hee.

english: Why shouldn't I spray my crops with pest medicine during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying in the hot afternoon causes the liquid chemical to evaporate quickly into the air before it can work properly. The intense heat combined with the chemical can also scorch or burn your crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni ji nu lɛ atsɔ oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛ tsofai fata he lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo eshã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why do my cassava plants need so much space between them when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ aná gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ kɛ́ adu lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers grow large underground and need plenty of soft soil to expand. Leaving enough distance ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting with its neighbors.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ daraa wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ babaoo dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the cocoa seedlings shade and moisture until they are mature enough to stand the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i kɛyashi amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why do the flowers drop off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil moist and protecting young plants from harsh weather helps flowers turn into full tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni esaaa lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni abuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛfeɔ tomato fɔfɔii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I replant the maize seeds I harvest from my previous crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikpa kɛjɛ ŋmãa ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation, producing weaker plants and smaller harvests. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees strong plants and high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa afi lɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ naa nɔmimaa.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: Early morning is best because it gives plants water to survive the hot sun, and leaves dry quickly in the daylight, which prevents fungal diseases from growing on wet leaves overnight.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tsei lɛ nu koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ni baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ baai ni efɔ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow smaller and yield less food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients away from your main crops. When weeds are left in the field, your crops starve and cannot grow to their full size.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii titrii lɛ amli. Beni ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why should I cut off the small extra shoots growing on my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: Removing extra shoots forces the plant to direct all its energy and food into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than growing unnecessary extra leaves and branches.
ga: Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii fɛɛ koni ekɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe ni eeetsɔ baai kɛ niji krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, traps water in the ground so it doesn't dry out in the hot sun. It also keeps the soil cool, stops weeds from growing, and eventually breaks down into rich organic food for your soil.
ga: Mulching, ni atsɛɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ, haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akagbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni ji niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and dropping off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat without shade. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving larger trees protects young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps soil retain moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ amɛhe lɛ naa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei ni eda ni ashiɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have small holes in them and look like someone sprinkled sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Yɛ mli lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko kɛ ŋmeii efɔ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant, chewing tender leaves and leaving behind waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli, ni amɛyeɔ baai ni mli tse ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up tightly and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, whiteflies, or mites. These pests feed on plant sap and transmit viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, whiteflies loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground mainly due to waterlogged soil from poor drainage, or fungal infections spread by using diseased stem cuttings during planting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi babaoo ejaakɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. aloo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko yɛ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afoɔ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines need to climb up stakes to spread their leaves to sunlight. More sunlight allows the leaves to produce more food, which goes down into the soil to build bigger tubers.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tso ko nɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ he. Hulu la babaoo haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni baaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee bulbs wuji

english: Why are my tomato plants producing many flowers, but the flowers fall off without growing into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomatoi?

english: Tomato flowers drop off mainly due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor pollination. When soil dries out or temperatures get too high, the plant sheds flowers to survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ateŋ babaoo baa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni ejaaa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi loo hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi bɔni afee ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches when I leave many suckers growing around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many suckers compete with the main tree for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Pruning extra suckers ensures that nutrients go directly into growing a single, large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ, ebaakudɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmei agbo kome.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for light, space, and soil nutrients, leading to slender plants that give very low yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ la, he ko kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Why is it bad to place chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer right against the stem can burn the plant roots and stem tissue due to high salt concentration. Fertilizer should be placed a few centimeters away in a ring or side-hole.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ashã yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo sɛntimitai fioo komɛi kɛjɛ ŋwɛi ŋta loo bu ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ he.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for maize in the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, acting as natural fertilizer that improves soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Can I chop up raw plantain stems and leaves to feed my goats and chickens when commercial feed is too expensive?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafolɔ plantain tsei kɛ baai ni afeee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni mikɛha mitooi kɛ mikooloi lɛ niyenii? Be mli ni niyenii ni akɛheɔ jara lɛ jara wa tsɔ

english: Yes, plantain stems and fruits are safe energy and moisture sources for animals like goats and poultry, though they should ideally be combined with other feeds containing protein for complete animal nutrition.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantain tsei kɛ amɛyibii ji hewalɛ kɛ fɛ̃i jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe kɛha kooloi tamɔ tooi kɛ kooloi. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ akɛ niyenii krokomɛi afata he moŋ. ni protein yɔɔ mli koni ekɛha kooloi niyenii ni yeɔ emuu

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same farm with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moist soil environment cocoa seedlings need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ shihilɛ. Ehe miihia ni kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I remove the extra small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Extra side shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients and water. Trimming them away allows the plant to send all its energy into growing a larger, healthier bunch of fruit.
ga: Lateral loo extra shoots lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛtsɔ amɛfomɔ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do the large leaves on my plantain tree tear into thin strips after heavy winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves tear naturally along their side veins as a protection mechanism. This allows strong winds to pass through the leaves without snapping the trunk or pulling the entire tree out of the ground.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ gbálaa yɛ fãji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ahe akɛ gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ he. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ baai lɛ amli ni ekuuu tso lɛ shishi loo egbalaaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔnei yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward during extreme heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the crop save water and survive hot dry spells.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa ni nu egbi mli.

english: How can I tell when a bunch of plantains is ready to be harvested from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni plantains lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ mli?

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the individual fingers lose their sharp, angular edges and become plump and rounded, and the dried flower tips at the ends break off easily.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo beni nineshi nine fɛɛ nineshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni fɔfɔii ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fãa oya yɛ naagbee.

english: Is it helpful to leave dry plantain leaves and crop trash lying on top of the soil around my crops?
ga: Plantain baai ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ?

english: Yes, leaving organic materials on top of the soil creates a protective layer called mulch. Mulch reduces soil moisture loss from the sun, prevents weeds from sprouting, and slowly turns into natural manure.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Mulching haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hulu la lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ehaa jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ, ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during light rain even when the trunk is not broken?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ eshishifã lɛ efoŋ moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over easily when root pests, such as soil weevils or roundworms, attack and destroy the root system underground, leaving the heavy plant without a firm anchor.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi tamɔ sũ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ amɛhe oya. Etutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tsiiɔ ni ebɛ he ko ni ekɛbaamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava tubers when I plant cassava on the exact same spot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs large amounts of specific nutrients from the soil to form its roots. Planting it continuously on the same plot drains those nutrients, causing yields to drop unless you rotate crops or add fertilizer.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee shishifãi. Kɛ́ oya nɔ adu nii yɛ saatso kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli.

english: Why are the leaves at the top of my plantain tree turning yellow and clustering tightly together instead of spreading out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain lɛ yiteŋ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã lɛ?

english: Tight clustering and yellowing of top leaves is a common sign of a plant virus like Bunchy Top, which stunts the plant's growth and stops it from producing healthy fruit bunches.
ga: Kpoji ni mli wa kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ tso mli helai tamɔ banshee yiteŋ, ni haa tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaaa ewo aduawai akui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning brown and dying during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?
