english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh heat and hold soil moisture, the sun scorches their tender leaves and dries out their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ ni baatsi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, Hulu lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when the plant does not get enough water. When the plant is stressed by heat, it shuts down fruit production to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa mli lɛ Nitsumɔhe lɛ kpaa aduawai afeemɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: What causes these small caterpillars to hide inside the central leaves of my maize and eat them?
ga: Mɛni haa nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms. They hide deep inside the central whorl of the maize plant where it is safe and moist, eating the tender new leaves before they even unfold.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Asraafoi. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhe ejɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ po.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight cups and stop the plant from growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe yɛ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa mli ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the juices from the leaves and spread viruses, causing the leaves to twist and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the whole farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Look at the plant above ground: when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and you see cracks forming in the soil around the base of the stem, it usually means the tubers are mature and ready.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni obaanyɛ ona ŋmeii ni miifee yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo.

english: Why do my yam plants need tall wooden poles to climb up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need as much sunlight as possible to produce food for the heavy tuber underground. Climbing up stakes lifts the leaves into the sun and keeps them off the damp ground, which prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli, ni ebaaha amɛkashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baa helai anaa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant my maize seeds right after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The first rain is often a false start followed by weeks of dry weather. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then wither and die in the dry soil before the main rainy season truly begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: If too many shoots grow at once, they fight with the main mother plant for nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to produce big, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo miida shikome Ekɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ baawu koni ená niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efeɔ ŋmeii agbo ni tsii.

english: Why does my maize grow tall and green but only produce tiny, empty cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli pɛ lɛ?

english: This happens when the soil has plenty of nitrogen (which builds leaves) but lacks phosphorus and potassium, which the crop needs to develop strong cobs and fill the grains.
ga: Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo. (ni woɔ baai) shi ebɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmeii ni mli wa ni amɛwo dumɔwui amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops even if I put fertilizer on the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mitsei bibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔji lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ?

english: Weeds have stronger, faster-growing roots than young crops. They will quickly suck up the water, sunlight, and fertilizer you applied before your crops ever get a chance to use them.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdaraa oya fe tsei bibii. Amɛmuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ oya dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops starting to dry and shrivel after I spray them with chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbiɔ ni egboɔ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: When chemical sprays are applied during hot weather or direct sunlight, they can burn tender crop leaves, causing them to dry up quickly and shrivel.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ Ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashã. Egbiɔ oya ni egboɔ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my farm crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning before the sun comes out, as cool morning temperatures allow the spray to work without harming the plant.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔse nii ji leebi maŋkpa dani hulu lɛ aje kpo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, leebi hulutsoo be lɛ haa tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni eyeee tsei lɛ awui.

english: Why is it harmful to spray chemicals on my plants when the afternoon sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji oshara lɛ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes chemical sprays to react harshly on tender leaves, scorching the leaf tissues and making it hard for the leaves to survive.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii waa yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ. Eshãa baa lɛ mli fãji ni ehaa ewaa ahaa baa lɛ akɛ eeehi shi.

english: Will spraying my delicate crops in the cool morning hurt them?
ga: Ani kɛ́ mikɛ tsofa shwie mitsei bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ leebi ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: No, spraying early in the morning before the sun hits does no harm to tender plants because cool temperatures prevent chemical scorching.
ga: Dabi, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi dani hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ yeee tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ awui. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsofai ni shãa mɔ lɛ naa.

english: Why do my tender plant leaves dry up so fast right after spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ afɔ amɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tender crop leaves are very delicate, so applying chemical sprays under a hot sun rapidly strips moisture from the leaves and burns them.
ga: Tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ waaa kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ baai lɛ amli oya ni ekɛ shãa aba.

english: How can I tell if strong sunlight is interacting badly with my crop spray?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ miiná miŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: You will notice that the leaves quickly turn dry, curl up, and shrivel shortly after chemical application if the sun is out and hot.
ga: Obaana akɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ tsofa lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ kɛji amɛyɛ hulutsoo be mli ni edɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings seem so delicate and easily damaged?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛfiteɔ oya lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are very tender, making their leaves soft and sensitive to environmental heat, harsh chemical sprays, and pest damage.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛnuɔ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ shihilɛ mli lɛ he. tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni mli wa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii

english: Why are insects constantly attacking and bothering my young seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi dumɔwui lɛ be fɛɛ be ni amɛgbaa amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Insects target seedlings because the young, tender leaves are soft, easy to feed on, and full of moisture compared to older plants.
ga: Kplukai kwɛɔ dumɔwui anɔ ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛkwɛ̃mɔ waaa, ni amɛhe eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ akɛto tsei ni edara lɛ ahe.

english: How can I safely spray chemicals to kill insects on my delicate seedlings without destroying the plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ midumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: To protect fragile seedlings while treating for insects, always spray early in the morning before the heat of the sun sets in.
ga: Koni abu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ kooloi bibii kɛyaa. Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ leebi, dani hulu lɛ ashɛ.

english: Can applying chemicals at the wrong time permanently destroy my nursery seedlings?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ be ni esaaa mli lɛ baanyɛ akpata dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahiɛ kwraa?

english: Yes, spraying tender seedlings during hot, sunny weather can severely burn their leaves, making it impossible for the young plants to survive.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui bibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ Yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, enɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã waa. Enɛ haa tso bibioo lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under hot, direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow very quickly and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and shade-moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Staking lifts the yam leaves up toward sunlight and away from damp soil. This extra sunlight helps the plant make more energy to build bigger tubers underneath, while keeping leaves off the wet ground protects them from rot.
ga: Staking baaha sweet potato baai lɛ akwɛ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ akabɔ he. Nɛkɛ hulu la ni fa nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo feɔ tsɔnei wuji ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he.

english: Why should I cut off most of the small shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ Midumɔwu titri lɛ shishi lɛ ateŋ babaoo ajieɔ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow at once, they steal food and water from the main tree. Removing extra shoots leaves only two or three strong ones, ensuring your main tree produces a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ he kome Ebaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ gbɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha niji 2-3 pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha otso titri lɛ awo plantains akui wuji ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if the worms eating my maize leaves are fall armyworms?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi?

english: Fall armyworms leave ragged, torn holes in maize leaves and leave behind dark, sawdust-like dirt inside the central funnel of the plant. If you look closely at their heads, you will often see a white inverted 'Y' mark.
ga: Cutworms ni egbee shi lɛ shĩɔ bu ni etsilɛ, ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ ŋmãa baai amli. ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmei yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛ okwɛ amɛyitsei lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, obaana ‘Y’ okadi yɛŋ ni tsɔɔ shishi.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turn black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It usually happens when the plant experiences irregular watering or cannot absorb enough calcium from the soil while the fruit is growing rapidly.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Bei pii lɛ, ebaa kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ tso lɛ nu be fɛɛ be loo enyɛɛɛ ejie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during hot dry spells to save water and protect itself from drying out. Once the rainy season returns, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and resume growing.
ga: Yucca shwieɔ baai lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi ehe koni ekagbi. Kɛji akɛ ebote nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi-ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, leguminous plants like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves natural fertilizer behind that helps cereal crops like maize grow stronger afterwards.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I wait for the soil to be moist before putting chemical fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer on completely dry soil can burn your crop's roots or cause the fertilizer to blow away in the wind without helping the plant.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ loo eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni eyeee ebuaaa tso lɛ.

english: Is it better for my pepper plants if I water them early in the morning instead of hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi aha mi-pepper tso lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ leebi moŋ fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning allows the plants to drink water before the day gets hot. It also gives excess water on the leaves time to dry off in the sun, which stops fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ nu dani hulu lɛ mli woɔ la tsɔ. Ehaa nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ hu náa be ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akaya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni mikɛfo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers do not have a thick protective skin like yams, so once cut or dug up, they react rapidly with air and lose moisture, causing them to rot within two to three days unless processed into products like gari or flour.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afo loo atsa Cassava shishifãi lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja afee nibii tamɔ gari loo ashikishaŋ.

english: What actually happens to the soil when I cultivate my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ mikɛ mihe wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani mikɛtsu nii?

english: Cultivating or tilling loosens hard soil so crop roots can easily grow deep, breathe air, and absorb water and nutrients needed for healthy growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ loo akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ, amɛmu kɔɔyɔɔ, ni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my land is fully ready for planting after clearing it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii beni ajie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Land is ready for planting when cleared weeds are removed or tilled into the soil, hard dirt is loosened with a hoe, and early rains have soaked the ground enough to keep seeds moist.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji ajie jwɛi ni ajie lɛ loo atsu nii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Akɛ shɔvel shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ bɔ ni sa ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Why do my maize crops grow rapidly in the first two months but seem to stop growing taller after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli shi etamɔ nɔ ni ekpaa shweremɔ beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: In the first two months, maize focuses its energy on growing leaves and tall stalks. Once flowering happens, the plant stops growing taller and redirects all its energy into developing corn cobs.
ga: Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Abɛi maa baai kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ lɛ adalɛ nɔ mi. Kɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ lɛ Tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa ŋmãa ni miida lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantain stems take almost a year before they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi dani plantain tsei lɛ jeɔ yibii woɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains need many months to build strong underground root systems and thick stems to store enough energy before they can push out and support heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Plantains he miihia nyɔji babaoo koni amɛma shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ tsei ni mli tse koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ato dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsi amɛhe ni amɛye amɛbua aduawai akui ni tsii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster than my planted crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to local soils, so they capture water and sunlight much faster than newly planted crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo jɛmɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ hulu la oya fe dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, this is called intercropping. Maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving space for the slower-growing cassava to expand and mature later.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ intercropping. Abele daa oya ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli, ni ehaa gbɛ haa ŋmei ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer for surrounding crops.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow after continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes away key soil nutrients like nitrogen and fills soil air spaces with water, which prevents roots from breathing and absorbing food properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen lɛ, ni ekɛ nu fataa sũ lɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer near the roots of my crop instead of spreading it across the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishitoo lɛ moŋ fe ni magbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the roots ensures your crop absorbs the food directly before rain washes it away or weeds consume it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛ loo jwɛi lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots underground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready for harvest after 9 to 12 months when the bottom leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks appear on the soil surface near the stem base.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ, efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa. ni ŋmeii je kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants full of holes with caterpillar droppings inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plants lɛ baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii afɔfɔi yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaves of maize. They eat the tender growing parts of the plant, which weakens the maize and reduces your grain yield if you do not control them early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛyeɔ tsei ahe nibii ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ baa shi kɛji okuuu lɛ mra.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow big. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea helps the leaves regain their strength and color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ kɛ su ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field without tall crops around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot survive harsh, direct sunlight or strong heat. They need shade crops like plantains or temporary trees to protect them from burning and to keep the soil moist until they grow stronger.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. loo latsaa ni naa wa waa Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛhe wa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme hot weather, irregular watering, or too much fertilizer. Keeping the moisture level in the soil steady and avoiding excessive high-nitrogen fertilizer will help the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛfataa he Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Does it make any difference if I plant my cassava cuttings slanting instead of pushing them straight down?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ mi-cassava niji lɛ du yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaa shi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant (about 45 degrees) allows the plant to form roots closer to the soil surface where nutrients are, resulting in better tuber formation and making it easier to harvest later.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ (aaafee digrii 45) lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ shishifãi bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa sɛɛ mli

english: Why do my vegetables wilt so quickly during hot days even if I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: In hot weather, water rapidly evaporates from bare soil and from plant leaves. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil shaded, traps moisture longer, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nu lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ kɛ tsei ahe baai amli. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aduɔ (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and sits around the roots without draining away, especially in heavy clay soils. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain off and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he. shishifãi ni nu ejeee kpo titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni mli edɔ nɔ Shishitoo ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my crops looking small and weak even though I applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: If weeds are growing close to your crops, they steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients intended for your plants. Clearing weeds before applying fertilizer ensures your crops get all the food.
ga: Kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ onibii lɛ Nakai jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa otsei lɛ shwereɔ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ dani awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii kwraa.

english: Why do small green pods on my cocoa tree turn shriveled and black while they are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ gboi ni amɛtsɔ ediŋŋ beni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: This is often 'cherelle wilt,' which happens naturally when a cocoa tree has produced more pods than it has water or nutrients to feed. However, it can also be triggered by severe dry weather or insect attacks.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘cherelle wilt’ lɛ baa yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo fe nu loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ayeɔ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo kooloi ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha eje shishi.

english: If I harvest maize from high-yielding store-bought seeds, why do those saved grains yield very poorly when I replant them next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni ahe yɛ shwapo mli lɛ amli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ nakai dumɔwui ni ato lɛ woɔ yibii gbonyo waa beni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Store-bought high-yielding seeds are usually hybrids created from special parent plants. The grains you harvest from them lose their special strength in the second generation, so buying fresh certified seed each season gives you the best yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ shwapoi amli lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee tso krɛdɛɛ ko ni ji nyɛ lɛ. Nibii ni nyɛkpaa lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ahe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: How long does it usually take for tree crops like cocoa or oil palm to start bearing fruit after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsei tamɔ kookoo loo mu tso lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most tree crops need about 3 to 4 years after planting to grow strong roots and trunks before they start producing their first fruits. During these early years, the tree is focusing its strength on growing rather than making fruit.
ga: Tsei babaoo he miihia aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ be mli ni adu amɛ lɛ sɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa dani amɛje amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ feemɔ shishi. Yɛ shishijee afii nɛɛ amli lɛ, nɔ ni tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa nɔ ji dalɛ moŋ fe yibii ni ewoɔ.

english: How many years can a tree crop keep giving me harvest once it starts producing fruit?
ga: Kɛ́ tso ko bɔi yibiiwoo lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ ebaanyɛ ekɛha mi?

english: Many tree crops, such as cocoa, can continue yielding fruit for 20 years or more if they are properly weeded, pruned, and protected from pests and diseases.
ga: Tsei pii, tamɔ kookoo baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii kɛyashi afii 20 loo nɔ ni fe nakai. Kɛji akɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ jogbaŋŋ, afolɔ tsei lɛ, ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe lɛ,.

english: Why do my young fruit trees drop their flowers without producing any fruit in their early years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young trees often produce flowers before their stems and roots are strong enough to support heavy fruit. As the tree matures over 3 to 4 years, it will hold onto its flowers and turn them into full fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua aduawai ni tsii. Beni tso lɛ daa yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli lɛ, ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni ebafeɔ aduawai ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better for me to farm a large land like 20 acres all at once or start with a smaller portion?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ matsu ŋmɔ agbo ko ni dalɛ ji aaafee acre 20 yɛ be kome mli loo mabɔi kɛ fã bibioo ko?

english: Starting with a size you can manage easily allows you to care for the young plants properly. Managing a large plot like 20 acres takes a lot of strength, labor, and money for clearing and weeding before you get any returns.
ga: Kɛ́ oje shishi kɛ dalɛ ni obaanyɛ otsu he nii oya lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ wulu ko tamɔ acre 20 nɔkwɛmɔ biɔ hewalɛ, nitsumɔ, kɛ shika babaoo ni okɛjie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi dani obaanyɛ okpa nyɔmɔwoo lɛ.

english: Why is it hard for one person's strength to maintain a big farm during the first few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewaa kɛhaa gbɔmɛi akɛ Te mɔ ko baakwɛ ŋmɔ agbo ko nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Young crops require frequent weeding, pest control, and watering before they grow tall enough to shade out weeds. A large farm requires more labor than one person can handle to keep plants healthy until harvest time.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni ajie jwɛi shii abɔ. tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ dani eda bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okwaafoi wuji biɔ nitsulɔi ni fa fe ekome koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: How can I make money to feed my family while waiting three years for my main tree crops to yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná shika ni mikɛkwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ afii etɛ dani mitso titri lɛ awo yibii lɛ?

english: You can plant quick-yielding crops like maize, cassava, or plantain between the young trees. These short-term crops give you food and income during the first few years while your main crops grow.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa loo plantains yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kukuoo nɛɛ haa onáa niyenii kɛ shika yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Will planting cash crops between my young trees take away nutrients from the main trees?
ga: Ani shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baahe niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli?

english: If you leave proper space between the main trees and the quick crops, they can grow safely together. Fast crops like plantains also provide helpful shade to young tree seedlings while giving you early income.
ga: Kɛji oshi gbɛ ni sa yɛ tso titri lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ mra lɛ Nakai tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee ekome kɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe. Nibii ni aduɔ mra tamɔ plantains hu haa tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni ehaa amɛnáa shika oya hu.

english: Why do crops grow well in one part of my farmlands but perform poorly in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi okwaayeli fã lɛ mli lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ ehiii yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil depth, water holding capacity, and plant nutrients vary across large fields. Adding organic manure or fertilizer to poor spots helps equalize plant growth across your entire farm.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ hei wuji. Kɛ́ okɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata hei ni ehiii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What happens if I do not weed my farm regularly during the first three years after planting?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ jwɛi tsuuu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii etɛ ni mikɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from young crop roots. Severe weed competition delays the time it takes for young crops to start yielding fruit.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Jwɛi ahe akaŋshii ni naa wa lɛ haa be ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do old tree crops produce less fruit after many years of harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni egbɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ afii babaoo ni akɛkpaa amɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As tree crops age past 20 to 25 years, their branches weaken and soil nutrients around their roots get depleted. Gradually replanting with fresh seedlings restores your farm's productivity over time.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei ye afii 20 kɛyashi 25 lɛ, amɛniji lɛ gbɔjɔɔ, ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Dumɔwui heei ni ooodu fiofio lɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees during their first few years to protect their leaves from burning and to keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ akashã, ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees when they are already growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ be mli ni eda momo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so that sunlight and air can reach all parts of the tree. This reduces humidity inside the canopy, which prevents black pod disease and directs the tree's energy into producing more cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ejieɔ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ anyɛ ashɛ tso lɛ fãi fɛɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ black pod hela lɛ naa, ni ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their dark green color and growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ekwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cowpeas or beans on the same plot where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and beans have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When grown with or after maize, they naturally feed the soil and make it richer for future crops without buying extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa loo yɛ esɛɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛha efee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers drop off the plant without forming any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When pepper plants experience excessive heat and dry weather, they drop their flowers as a survival trick to save water. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching keeps the plant cool enough to hold its flowers and set fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ, Amɛbaashɛre fɔfɔi amɛshwie shi akɛ wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa ni amɛkɛbuɔ nu he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ mli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni ewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and rot underground when there is heavy rainfall for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water collects and stagnates in the ground due to poor drainage, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungus to cause root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛha shishifãi lɛ afite.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them grow during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ mi tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli?

english: Spreading dry grass or leaves around plants is called mulching. It acts as a blanket that blocks the harsh Harmattan sun from drying out the soil, helping the roots retain moisture much longer after watering.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa Tsei ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni tsiɔ Harmattan hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni awo amɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle of my young maize stalks, and how does it harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, which feed on the growing center (the funnel) of the maize plant. If they damage the growing point, the stalk cannot form healthy ears of corn, drastically reducing your total yield.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ he (channel) lɛ. Kɛji efite he ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmãa toi ni mli wa. Enɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller fruits when I plant the seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When plants grow too close together, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited soil nutrients, water, and sunlight. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and food to produce large, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from last year's maize harvest produce smaller yields than certified seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred in laboratories for high yield and disease resistance. The seeds saved from those crops lose their special strengths in the next generation, resulting in smaller plants and lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ amɛye amɛnɔ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baafite amɛhewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei bibii kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or rich compost will help the leaves turn dark green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my pepper plants with dried grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi aha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like an umbrella for the soil. It keeps the hot sun from drying out the moisture, stops weeds from growing, and cools down the plant roots so they grow better.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa ŋmɔtɔ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce many more flowers than they can support. They drop excess flowers to save energy for the pods they can feed, but heavy flower drop can also be caused by dry weather or lack of pollinating insects.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato amɛ ŋmeii ni ayeɔ lɛ ahe. Shi kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi loo fɔfɔi ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi lɛ afite waa.

english: Why do I need to put stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy to grow big tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get enough light and stay away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ aná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce very small fruits when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii bibii waa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight like children sharing a small bowl of food. They compete for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow big fruits.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baawuu tamɔ gbekɛbii. Jaa niyenii tsɛnsi mli Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Why are the bottoms of my garden eggs and tomatoes turning black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This black spot is caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit while it is forming, often because the soil dried out completely between waterings. Keeping the soil evenly damp helps the plant draw up calcium.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli beni efeɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ kwraa yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ teŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhe calcium.

english: Why is it risky to plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest instead of buying fresh certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from modern hybrid crops often lose their strength in the next generation, producing uneven plants with lower yields. Fresh certified seeds guarantee strong growth and maximum yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni yeɔ wala kɛjɛɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. Dumɔwui heei ni ana he odaseyeli haa dalɛ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Why do my stored cowpea seeds get full of tiny holes after keeping them in bags for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui stash lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Beni ekɛwo kotoku mli nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ

english: Tiny insects called weevils lay invisible eggs on the beans before or right after harvest. Inside the bag, the eggs hatch into tiny worms that eat their way out of the seed, leaving holes behind.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani akpaa loo yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, wɔji lɛ fɔɔ kɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. No yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ buji eshwɛɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the soil when the rainy season becomes too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. Excess water fills up all the air spaces in heavy soil, drowning the roots and encouraging rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ ni tsii mli lɛ amli, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my crops during the first few weeks after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛdu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already adapted to the soil and jump at the first rain. Because crop seedlings start small and grow slowly, weeds steal the sunlight, water, and food before your crop can establish itself.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ etsɔ amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo ni amɛtuɔ amɛhe kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi bibioo ni amɛdaraa blɛoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii dani ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ama shi.

english: What is causing the lower leaves of my corn plants to turn yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli?

english: Yellowing lower leaves in a V-shape is a sign that your soil is low in nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure will give the plants the nutrients they need to stay green and grow strong ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ V lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛha toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help make my soil better for next season's crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha be ni baa lɛ mli dumɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When you plant maize after harvesting these crops, the maize uses that stored nitrogen to grow strong without needing as much bought fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni oduɔ ŋmãa beni okpa ŋmãa nɛɛ sɛɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why are there small worms eating the center of my maize plants before the corn even comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Those worms are called Fall Armyworms. They lay eggs on young maize leaves and eat the growing center, but you can control them by spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or late evening when the worms come out to feed.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii lɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms. Amɛ woɔ amɛ wuji lɛ yɛ abele baa bibii anɔ ni amɛ yeɔ he ni amɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Shi obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ beni kooloi lɛ jeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes the leaves on my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips that suck juice from the plant and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem leaf extract or insecticidal sprays keeps the leaves flat and growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛtsɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, baa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaada.

english: Why do the bottom parts of my growing tomatoes turn black and soft while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni miida lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This condition is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the tomato roots absorb calcium continuously to build firm fruit bottoms.
ga: Shihilɛ nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tomato shishifãi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛŋɔɔ calcium koni amɛfee aduawai lɛ ashishi ni ma shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and turn brown when I cut down all the big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mifoɔ tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Leaving some large trees or planting plantains next to young cocoa gives them the shelter and moisture they need to survive.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli gĩɔ. Tsei wuji ni ashiɔ loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Cacao tsei lɛ baaha amɛná he ko ni amɛhi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to put tall sticks for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makɛ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ ama shi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up to catch sunshine and keeps them away from pests and damp soil on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ hiɔ shi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe ni eha amɛhe akafee tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off most of the small shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɔleɔ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ ateŋ babaoo jie

english: When too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they all fight for the same food and water, leading to tiny bunches. Leaving only two or three strong shoots allows the main plant to put its energy into producing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ Plantain kome Plantain muu lɛ fɛɛ baatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: How come my cassava tubers start rotting just two days after I dig them out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spoil quickly once harvested because exposure to air and minor scratches trigger rapid decay. Processing them into gari or flour right away, or keeping undamaged roots buried in moist sawdust, preserves them much longer.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwo mli kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo ko lɛ haa egboɔ oya. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni afeɔ lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ. Aloo fumɔ shishifãi ni efite lɛ yɛ tsei ni mli efɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up and die when I plant right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egboɔ kɛ́ midu yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a hot dry spell before the main rains actually start. Waiting until the rainy season fully establishes ensures there is enough continuous moisture in the soil for the seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni mli egbi sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: If I dig a well on my farm, can I water my cocoa trees during the dry season to get more pods?
ga: Kɛji mifo nubu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani manyɛ mawo mi-kookoo tso lɛ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni maná ŋmeii babaoo?

english: Cocoa trees need constant moisture to keep their leaves green and retain pods during the dry season. Watering them from a well during dry spells prevents pods from shriveling and helps the tree produce flowers continuously.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛbaai lɛ afee eŋɔli, ni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ nu bu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Harvest cocoa pods when they turn fully yellow or orange. Harvesting pods while they are still green means the beans inside are under-developed, while leaving them overripe on the tree makes the beans sprout or rot.
ga: Kpãa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔji lolo lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ eshɛko lolo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ tsɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi.

english: Why is it necessary to cover cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni aha kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi dani agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the beans under leaves creates heat for fermentation, which develops the chocolate flavor and deep brown color buyers look for. Without fermentation, the beans stay bitter, purple, and sell for a much lower price.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɛ baai ashishi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo baa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɛ lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baaná ŋmɔtɔ lolo, ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ, ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ jara ni baa shi kwraa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning when there are no big shade trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block harsh sun, the young leaves scorch and cannot make food for the tree to grow.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii bɛ he ni ebɔle lɛ Koni ekɛtsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa Baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛha tso lɛ niyenii koni ekwɛ̃.

english: My cocoa trees produce plenty of small flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into pods. What causes this?
ga: Mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they do not get enough water, nutrients, or light. High heat and dry winds during the dry season also cause the tree to shed flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛnáaa nu, niyenii, loo la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ hu haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, cool, and damp weather. Opening up the farm canopy to let sunlight in and removing black pods immediately keeps the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ, fɛ̃i, kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Agbeleɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋwɛitsu lɛ koni hulu la abote mli ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why does cutting off the small side shoots and suckers help my cocoa trees yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Efãi lɛ eje kpo, no hewɔ lɛ eyeɔ ebuaa mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Water sprouts and unnecessary branches suck away water and food that the main tree needs to produce pods. Cutting them off lets energy flow directly into pod formation and improves air circulation to stop diseases.
ga: Nu mli dumɔwui kɛ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie lɛ lɛ, ehaa hewalɛ hoɔ kɛboteɔ pod lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni helai akpa

english: Is it helpful to plant leguminous crops like groundnuts or beans near my young crops?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ madu ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe?

english: Yes, leguminous plants take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts as a free natural fertilizer that feeds your young crops and keeps the soil rich.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: When is the best time to put fertilizer on my crop trees so the heavy rain doesn't wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo tsei amli ŋmɔshi nii koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie amɛ?

english: Apply fertilizer at the beginning of the rainy season when the ground is moist but not flooded. This allows the roots to absorb the nutrients immediately while the tree is actively growing new leaves and flowers.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbalaa niyenii amrɔ nɔŋŋ be mli ni tso lɛ miikwɛ̃ baai kɛ fɔfɔi heei.

english: What will happen if I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other on the land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Trees planted too close together fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, growing tall and skinny with fewer pods. The overcrowded leaves also create a dark, humid environment where pests and rot spread quickly.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la yeɔ akaŋ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli. Baai ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu haa shihilɛ feɔ duŋ, ni edɔ. Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ ŋmeii gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: How far apart should I plant my cashew trees so they have enough room to grow well?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cashew tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cashew trees develop wide branches as they mature. Planting them 7 to 10 meters apart gives each tree enough sunlight, air movement, and soil space to produce healthy branches and high nut yields.
ga: Cashew tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ niji babaoo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 7 kɛyashi 10 lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la. kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa Koni afee niji ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii ni fa babaoo.

english: Can I grow food crops like maize or groundnuts between my young cashew trees?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Mi cashew tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Yes, you can plant short crops between young cashew trees for the first 2 to 3 years. This practice, called intercropping, helps you maximize land use and get food while your cashew trees are still growing.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kukuji yɛ cashew tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli. Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni onáa niyenii yɛ be mli ni o-cashew tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cashew seedlings turning brown and dropping during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cashew roots are still shallow and cannot reach deep underground water during long dry spells. Placing dry grass mulch around the base of the plant helps trap soil moisture and protect the roots from high heat.
ga: Cashew shishifãi bibii lɛ hu mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain before I plant my maize seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the ground receives two or three steady, deep rains so the soil is thoroughly moist. Planting too early after a light first rain can cause seeds to dry up if a hot spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ be fɛɛ be koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why are there tiny holes and small green droppings inside the center leaves of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Mi-ŋmei tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the central growing point of the plant to feed, which weakens the stalk and reduces corn formation if not controlled early.
ga: Enɛ ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe teeɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ koni amɛye nii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa lɛ shweremɔ baa shi kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: How do I know when my cassava stems are mature enough to harvest from the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties are ready for harvest between 8 to 12 months after planting. You can test maturity by carefully digging around the base of one stem to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Cassava henɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo efee klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ oka kɛji eshɛ emuu kɛtsɔ tso kome shishigbɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni ona kɛji tso lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ shiŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom ends of my ripening tomato fruits turn soft and black?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ lɛ?

english: This problem is blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by inconsistent watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull nutrients up into the fruit.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Why is it harmful to burn all the cleared bush on my land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mashã tsei ni ajie yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and kills helpful earthworms and soil organisms. Clearing without burning leaves plant residue to decay naturally, which acts as free soil fertilizer and holds water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jara wa lɛ. ni egbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ afite yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa nu jeɔ kpo ni ehiɛɔ mli.

english: Why do my crop leaves stay pale green or yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves often mean the soil is low in nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen out of the root zone, so adding organic manure or fertilizer helps restore plant vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Why is it good practice to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a plot before planting other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Legume plants like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they leave this natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite Eshiɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: How do I know if my farmland has a good soil foundation before I start planting cassava?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishitoo kpakpa dani mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ?

english: Good soil for cassava breaks apart easily in your hands, holds moisture without becoming waterlogged, and is deep enough for root tubers to expand without hitting hard rock or dense clay.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha ŋmei baakumɔ oya yɛ oniji amli. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni nu shwieee mli. ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni tɛi ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ etswaaa amɛ.

english: What happens to my maize crop if I plant directly into hard ground without plowing the field first?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛtsuuu nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Hard soil prevents delicate roots from penetrating deep into the earth to find water and nutrients, resulting in weak, stunted plants that easily fall over in strong wind.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbɔjɔ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi oya.

english: If I channel water from a local dam to my vegetable beds, how do I keep the crops from drowning?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ nu jɛ maŋ lɛ mli faa ko mli kɛtee mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tsei anaa koni amɛkabote nu mli?

english: Vegetables need moist soil rather than standing water. Creating raised soil beds and small drainage channels allows excess water to flow away while keeping root systems damp and healthy.
ga: Aduawai sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nu ni ekã shi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saatsoi ni awó nɔ kɛ nu homɔ gbɛi bibii ni afee lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants turn yellow and lose leaves when the soil stays flooded after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaaji lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa sɛɛ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi lolo lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to breathe. When land stays flooded, roots suffocate, rot, and lose the ability to feed the plant, causing leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua tso lɛ dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Is it worth taking a loan to buy commercial fertilizer and high-quality seeds for my crop farm?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ mafa shika koni mikɛhe jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Improved seeds and correct fertilizer give crops a stronger start against dry weather and pests, yielding much higher harvests that can cover the investment cost if water and management are reliable.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo ni baanyɛ awo shika ni akɛwoɔ nitsumɔ mli lɛ he nyɔmɔ kɛji akɛ anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nu kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt so easily during the afternoon heat even when the ground feels damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their small roots can pull water up from the ground. Providing shade plants like plantains protects them until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe shishifãi bibii. ni baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi Tsei tamɔ plantains ni akɛhaa hulutsoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ baa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce plenty of leafy branches during the rainy season but very few flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ aniji kɛ baai babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli shi fɔfɔi fioo pɛ amɛyɔɔ lɛ?

english: When soil receives too much water and rich nitrogen, the plant puts all its energy into growing big leaves and stems instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ náa nu kɛ nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai agboi kɛ tsei ahe nii ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: If I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year, why does my harvest keep dropping?
ga: Kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without giving the earth a chance to recover or balance itself.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaaa je lɛ hegbɛ ni ekɛ ehe awo mli loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ

english: Why do spots appear on my plant leaves after a sudden rain break following a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii jeɔ kpo yɛ mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rapid changes in temperature and high humidity create ideal conditions for fungal spores to bloom on warm, damp leaves, showing up as brown or black spots.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa oya yɛ dɔlɛ mli kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fungal spores lɛ koni amɛfɔ yɛ baai ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ. Amɛjeɔ kpo tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ediŋŋ.

english: Can I safely plant my crops right next to the bank of a water source or dam?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhe loo faa?

english: Planting too close to the water edge risks heavy rains washing away topsoil and young crops. It is safer to plant a short distance away on elevated ground and guide the water through small furrows.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ naa tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni baaha sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aya. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu yɛ he ko ni kɛ jɛmɛ jɛkɛmɔ kuku. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ ni ahaa nu hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ gbɛjegbɛi bibii anɔ.

english: Why do you advise us to look underneath the leaves and small fruits when inspecting our crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ wɔkwɛ baai kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ? Beni wɔkwɛɔ wɔŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ

english: Tiny pests and disease germs like to hide away from direct sunlight and rain under leaves and small fruits. Checking underneath helps you catch diseases early before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he yɛ baai kɛ aduawai bibii ashishi. Kɛ́ okwɛ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona hela mra. dani ebaakpata tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: Why do my small coconut fruits turn dark or fall off the tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ani minɔ lɛ mli ewo duŋ loo ejɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: Young fruits are delicate, and small pests or fungal germs often attack them from underneath, weakening the connection to the stem and causing them to drop early.
ga: Yibii bibii lɛ waaa. Ni bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ tutuaa amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi. Enɛ haa tsakpaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ kɛ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa amɛshwieɔ shi oya.

english: What actually causes my crops to get sick or diseased on the farm?
ga: Mɛni miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiye hela loo hela miiba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crop diseases are caused by microscopic organisms called germs, fungi, bacteria, or viruses that infect the plant tissue and stop the crop from growing normally.
ga: Tso helai jɛɔ nibii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pathogens, fungi, bacteria, loo virus ni gbeɔ tso fãji ni tsiɔ tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Where do these crop germs and diseases come from in the first place?
ga: Nɛgbɛ nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai nɛɛ jɛ shishijee?

english: Disease germs can travel through the wind, infected seeds, contaminated soil, water splashes during rains, or on insects moving between farms.
ga: Muawai baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. dumɔwui ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji Nu ni shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli loo kooloi ni nyiɛɔ ŋmɔji ateŋ

english: How can I tell if my crops are sick from a disease or just stressed by dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji helai miipiŋ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miihao amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Germ diseases usually cause specific signs like leaf spots, rotting, powdery dust, or unusual colors, whereas weather stress usually affects all plants evenly without causing leaf rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ helai kɛ okadii pɔtɛɛ baa, tamɔ baa he muji, fitemɔ, sũ, loo su ni ejaaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ fɔɔ tsei fɛɛ anɔ hewalɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ekɛ baai lɛ fiteee.

english: How can I know the exact disease that is damaging my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male hela ni miifite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Every crop disease leaves specific clues or symptoms—such as the shape and color of leaf spots, rotting roots, or wilting stems—which help us identify the exact germ responsible.
ga: Tsei ahe helai fɛɛ shĩɔ okadi loo okadii pɔtɛɛ komɛi, tamɔ bɔ ni baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ kɛ amɛhe su. shishifãi ni egbo loo tso lɛ shishi lɛ egbo Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa wɔ ni wɔyɔseɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa lɛ.

english: How do I know if a problem on my farm is caused by insects or by a disease germ?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ naagba ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko loo hela ko mli?

english: Insect damage usually leaves visible bite marks, holes, or chewed leaves, while germs usually cause discoloration, spots, rotting, or wilting without physical chewing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ shĩɔ okadii ni anaa, bu, loo baai ni amɛye. Shi bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ haa tsɔne lɛ su tsakeɔ, ehaa ehe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egboɔ, loo egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ ŋmɔɔ.

english: What is the best way to handle a crop disease when it starts spreading in our community?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsu tsei ahe helai ahe nii kɛji amɛbɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ wɔ akutsei lɛ amli pɛ?

english: The best approach is to inspect your farm regularly, clear weeds, remove infected plants immediately, and avoid moving dirty tools or infected crops between farms.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa, ojie jwɛi, ni ojie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni he tseee loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni oootsi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji ateŋ lɛ he.

english: Can I spread sickness from a diseased plant to a healthy one using my cutlass or farm tools?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsɔ dade loo ŋmɔ mli nibii anɔ magbɛ hela ashwã tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, when you cut an infected plant, disease germs stick to your tool blade and can easily transfer to healthy plants when you cut them next.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ofo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baakpɛtɛ odɛŋdadei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe. Ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛya tso ko ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ be kroko ni obaafo lɛ.

english: If I find a plant that is clearly ruined by a disease, should I leave it or destroy it?
ga: Kɛji ana tsei ni helai efite amɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ Ani esa akɛ mashɛrɛ ashwie loo makpãtã amɛhiɛ?

english: You should carefully remove and destroy heavily infected plants away from your field so the germs do not spread to the rest of your healthy crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ ajie tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ kɛjɛ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe ni okpãtã amɛhiɛ. Enɛ ji koni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli.
