english: Yellowing from the bottom leaves upward usually means your maize is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore leaf health and improves crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ ayibii aya hiɛ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast because hot sunlight and wind evaporate the water directly. Covering the ground around your plants with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket to lock moisture in the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa tɛ̃ɛ ni haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hewɔ. Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ atade koni ekɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when planted in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and cannot handle harsh sunlight directly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary canopy protection until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ baaha ŋwɛi ŋtayaai lɛ abu amɛhe yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and using shade netting during extreme hot days helps plants hold onto their flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo latsaa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ shade netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Planting seeds too closely causes crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients, resulting in thin plants and small yields. Giving crops proper space allows each plant to grow large and produce a fuller harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no baaha tsei lɛ afee mlɛo ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi. He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa ni ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing small green worms to chew holes into the leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ bu yɛ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ amli?

english: These worms are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hatches from eggs laid by moths on crop leaves. Catching them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem leaf extracts protects your leaves from being destroyed.
ga: Ekolɛ ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii kɛwoɔ tsei ahe baa lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni ji bio-insecticide loo neem tso lɛ mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ tsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otso lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or a viral disease spread by these pests. Spraying neem oil or insecticidal soap helps control the pests and stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye kooloi lɛ anɔ ni etsi curling naa.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to quickly steal nutrients, light, and water from the soil faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the first few weeks gives your crops the advantage to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛbaanyɛ amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, la, kɛ nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ ni ji dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: It is best to wait until the ground has received two or three deep, steady rains that thoroughly wet the soil before planting. Sowing too early in dry soil causes seeds to dry out and fail to sprout.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nuɔ jogbaŋŋ dani oduɔ nii. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ mra yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agbi ni amɛkwɛ̃ŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants produce only a small harvest during the first week compared to later weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsi lɛ mli kɛ akɛto otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Vegetable crops like peppers and tomatoes mature in stages. The initial harvest only comes from the earliest flowers that set fruit, but as the rest of the plant fully matures, fruit production builds up and peaks over the following weeks.
ga: Aduawai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tomato kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli. Klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔ lɛ jɛɔ fɔfɔi ni woɔ yibii mra fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. Shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ afãi krokomɛi dara kwraa lɛ, Yibii ni ajieɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ ni ebaashɛ he ni fe fɛɛ yɛ otsii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some crops like chili peppers keep producing fruit every week while maize is harvested all at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi, tamɔ chili peppers, woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii daa otsi yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmãa fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Crops have different reproductive behaviors. Tomato and pepper plants produce flowers continuously as long as they stay healthy, giving you weekly harvests, whereas maize produces all its grain at one time and finishes its life cycle.
ga: Tsei yɛ fɔmɔ sui srɔtoi. Tomato kɛ pepper tsei lɛ baaya nɔ awo fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be ni amɛhiɛ kã shi lɛ. Kɛtsɔ yibiiwoo ni akɛhaa daa otsi yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa feɔ eshishifãi fɛɛ shikome ni egbeɔ ewala shihilɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Does picking ripe fruits regularly encourage my plants to produce more new fruits?
ga: Ani aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni mikpaa daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitso lɛ ni ewoɔ aduawai heei babaoo?

english: Yes, harvesting mature fruits regularly signals the plant to direct its energy into developing young flowers and new fruits rather than keeping already mature fruits on the stem.
ga: Hɛɛ, aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ ni akpaa daa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo fɔfɔi bibii kɛ aduawai heei. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ yiblii nɛ e wa ngɛ tso ɔ tso ɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce heavily for a few weeks and then suddenly stop producing new fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ ekpa yibii heei feemɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Heavy fruit production uses up a vast amount of energy and soil nutrients. Without additional fertilizer or compost after the main harvest begins, the plant runs out of energy to sustain new growth.
ga: Yibii babaoo ni anáa lɛ heɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi bɛ ni akɛfataa he yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ shishijee sɛɛ. Hewalɛ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ koni ekɛkwɛ dalɛ hee nɔ lɛ baaho.

english: How can I figure out how many kilograms of vegetables I am producing if I only collect them in crates or boxes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male aduawai kilogram enyiɛ ni mafee kɛji akɛ mikɛwo adekai loo adekai amli pɛ?

english: You can determine the weight by weighing one typical filled box on a scale to find its average weight in kilograms, then multiplying that weight by the total number of boxes harvested.
ga: Obaanyɛ ole shwiili lɛ shwiili kɛtsɔ jarayeli nibii ni akɛwoɔ adeka mli lɛ ni ooosusu yɛ sɛkɛl nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ona shwiili lɛ shwiili mlijaa yɛ kilogram mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai muji lɛ ato adekai ni akpa lɛ fɛɛ ayibɔ he.

english: Why are my harvested fruits smaller and lighter in weight towards the end of the harvest season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ feɔ bibioo ni amɛhe waaa yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: As the plant grows older, its roots absorb nutrients less efficiently and its energy reserves drop, resulting in smaller fruit sizes and lower total weight per harvest.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ daraaa bibii ni amɛtsiimɔ fɛɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ kome mli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ anɔkwa yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers drop when plants experience stress from high heat, lack of water, or insufficient soil nutrients like phosphorus. Without proper pollination and care, the flower cannot form fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs lɛ mli. Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops produce fewer fruits during hot dry periods even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Extreme daytime heat causes plant stress that damages pollen, preventing fertilization. Even with watering, high heat slows down fruit development until temperatures cool.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa yɛ gbi mli lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei lɛ anɔ, ni no fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa kɛji akɛ awo nu po Dɔlɛ ni naa wa baaha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: If I plant my crop seeds very close together, will I harvest more total crop weight from my field?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni tsiimɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli?

english: Overcrowding crops causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This produces weak, thin plants with very low yields per plant, often resulting in a smaller total harvest overall.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ tso kome mli lɛ baa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa ŋmaa fɛɛ ni akpaa lɛ feɔ bibioo.

english: How can I tell when my tomatoes are ready to be harvested so they don't spoil on the way to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-tomato lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa? Koni tomatoi lɛ akafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pick tomatoes at the 'breaker' stage when the green color just starts showing a blush of yellow or pink at the bottom. They will finish ripening off the plant while remaining firm enough for transport.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ tomato yɛ ‘breaker’ stage lɛ mli beni ŋmɔji lɛ jeɔ shishi ejieɔ red loo pink kpo yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Amɛbaaha tsei lɛ ashwere kwraa bɔ ni sa ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ lɛlɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn and dry out quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby creates a living umbrella that gives young cocoa the cool shade and soil moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpee hulu la tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Efeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips, it means the plant is starving for nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is what keeps leaves green and strong, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growing season prevents this yellowing.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, ni efee V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting under the ground when there is heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive rain creates waterlogged soil, which cuts off oxygen to the cassava roots and suffocates them. Sitting in soggy, wet dirt allows fungal diseases to easily enter and rot the tubers before harvest time.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni ooota lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai abote mli ni eha bulb lɛ afee nɔ ni fiteɔ oya dani akpaa.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants dropping off instead of turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress or erratic watering. When it gets too hot or dry, the plant drops its blossoms to conserve energy and survive, preventing successful pollination and fruit formation.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa. Beni edɔ loo edɔ tsɔ Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Aye omanye ni atsĩ pollination kɛ aduawai afeemɔ naa.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the centers of my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu kɛ muji ni tsuɔ yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which crawls inside the growing tip of the maize plant to eat tender leaves. The dark dirt left behind is the caterpillar's waste, and catching it early with safe treatments protects the growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishi koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Muji ni tsuɔ waa ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji ŋmei lɛ jwɛi. kɛ emɔmɔ mra Kɛji akɛ atsa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, abaabu he ni edaa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to put strong wooden sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso ni wa awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need to lift their leaves up toward sunlight to make food efficiently. Staking keeps leaves off the wet soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases while maximizing sun exposure to produce larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni esa akɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛhoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Staking baaye abua ni abu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ he. Tsi fungal baa helai anaa yɛ be mli ni ohaa hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ koni ekɛ sweet potato tsei wuji aba.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and looking small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ bibii ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Upward curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant's sap and transmitting viruses. Controlling these sucking insects early prevents leaf distortion and allows normal fruit growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ asɛɛkuu naa ni eye ebua aduawai lɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily right when the fruit bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ aduawai akui lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have very shallow root systems rather than deep taproots. When heavy fruit bunches form at the top, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for winds to pull the shallow roots out of wet soil unless supported by wooden props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa moŋ fe shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Kɛji aduawai akuu ni tsii ba yɛ ŋwɛi Tso lɛ baaná ŋwɛi tsiimɔ. ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ oya Ja nɔ ko ni akɛ tso fee ni akɛfiɔ he lɛ yɛ.

english: Why should I avoid watering my garden vegetables in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ mibɔɔ mli aduawai lɛ anɔ nu ni mikɛhaa yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Watering under hot sunlight causes water to evaporate before roots can absorb it, wasting effort. Water droplets on leaves can also act like magnifying glasses in strong heat, burning leaves and creating damp conditions that favor fungal leaf spots.
ga: Nu ni oooha yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji hewalɛ ni afiteɔ Nu ni shwieɔ baai anɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ atsu nii tamɔ glase ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli, ni eshãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ ni haa fungal leaf spot hela lɛ baa.

english: Why does my field produce smaller harvests if I plant maize on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season without rest. It also allows specific pests and soil diseases that feed on maize to build up over time; rotating with crops like beans restores soil health.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli ni ekpaaa. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the maize seeds I bought from the open market produce weak and sickly crops compared to seeds from certified dealers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ni bɛ hewalɛ ni helai yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni jɛɔ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Market grain is often meant for eating, not planting. It carries unknown genetic history and hidden diseases from previous harvests, whereas certified seeds are specially bred and treated to resist pests and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ ayeɔ, shi jeee ni adu, ni aleee bɔ ni amɛfɔmɔ nii yɔɔ ha kɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni jɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How can I check if the cassava stem cuttings I am buying from another farmer are healthy before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmei niji ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi adɛŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu?

english: Look closely at the stems and inner wood; healthy cuttings should be firm, free of dark spots or holes made by pests, and cut from plants that showed no leaf yellowing or stunted growth during their harvest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebɛ ŋmeii diji loo bu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ he. ni afolɔ tsei ni bɛ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo amɛdaramɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ amli.

english: If my pepper farm gets sick, how do I find out whether the disease came from the soil or from the seeds I planted?
ga: Kɛji mi pepper ŋmɔ lɛ hela mɔ lɛ Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela lɛ jɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo dumɔwui ni midu lɛ amli?

english: You can investigate by checking the roots and stem base. If the roots are rotted or black, the disease likely lived in the soil; if the leaves and upper stem show spots first while roots look healthy, the seed or airborne pests are usually to blame.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ enɛ kɛtsɔ shishifãi kɛ tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ mlipɛimɔ nɔ. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ egbo loo amɛji ediŋŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ekolɛ hela nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋwɛi baai kɛ tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa lɛ, bei pii lɛ, Dumɔwui loo kɔɔyɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔ baa.

english: Can my new crop catch a disease from what I planted in the same soil last season?
ga: Ani nɔ ko ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atswa miŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ hela?

english: Yes, many plant diseases and fungal spores stay alive in the soil or in leftover crop stems for months, waiting to infect the next batch of crops if you do not rotate with a different crop type.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tsei ashishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ nyɔji babaoo. Koni omɛ ni tsei akuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛji okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsakeee.

english: Maize plants roll their leaves to protect themselves from heat and reduce water loss through evaporation; it is the plant's natural way of saving moisture until the air cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he, ni amɛha nu ni amɛlaaje kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Eji tsei adebɔɔ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings wilting and dying after I cleared all the shade trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their root systems are tender. Without shade trees like plantains to block intense sun, the leaves burn and the soil dries out too fast.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ tso bibioo lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahewɔ. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni tsiɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Baai lɛ shãa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya tsɔ.

english: How can I tell if my tomato plants are turning yellow because of a disease or because they lack fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-tomato tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: If nutrient deficiency is the problem, whole leaves usually turn a smooth, even yellow across the field. If it is a disease, you will notice brown spots, curled edges, or patchy yellow patterns that spread from plant to plant.
ga: Kɛji niyenii ni esaaa ni ayeɔ lɛ ji naagba lɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ bo lɛ, obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmeii ni ebɔle, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that inject a virus into the plant while feeding, which disrupts the crop's normal growth and fruiting process.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni kɛ helai woɔ tsei lɛ amli beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ tomato mli lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Enɛ gbalaa ŋmɔshi nibii adalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa lɛ mli.

english: If only one plant in my farm shows dark spots on its leaves, why does the whole farm get sick a few days later?
ga: Kɛji tso kome pɛ yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ diji yɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ hela mɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fungal spots produce microscopic seeds called spores. Rain drops splashing on the infected plant or wind blowing through the field easily transfer these spores to healthy neighbor crops.
ga: Fungi woɔ dumɔwui bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ spores. Nugbɔ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛya tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: Why does a disease attack crops in one specific corner of my field while the rest of the farm looks green and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hela ko tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koŋ kome mli yɛ be mli ni eyɔɔ ekroko mli lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ.

english: That corner might have wetter soil, poorer drainage, or less sunlight, creating a perfect environment for soil germs to multiply and attack weak plants first before moving to the rest of the field.
ga: Ekolɛ nakai koŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ. nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ loo hulu la fioo pɛ yɔɔ Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ babaoo ni amɛtutuaa tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hela lɛ dani amɛyaa ŋmɔ lɛ fã kroko lɛ mli.

english: Can big trees growing on my land cause my young cocoa plants to wither and die?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha mikokoo tsei bibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi?

english: Yes. While cocoa trees need some shade, certain large trees steal too much sunlight and soil moisture, or create too much dense canopy, which causes cocoa plants underneath them to wither and dry up.
ga: Hɛɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ hulutsoo he miihia kokoo tsei moŋ, shi tsei wuji komɛi juɔ hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. aloo afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ tsɔ Enɛ haa cacao tsei ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How do I know if I should cut down a shade tree on my cocoa farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If a shade tree blocks too much sunlight, drizzles toxic sap, or causes the cocoa plants beneath it to look yellow, weak, and withered, you should remove or trim that tree to let air and light reach your cocoa.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa lɛ Ehaa latɛs ni hoɔ lɛ feɔ poison. aloo eha kookoo tso ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ, egbɔjɔ, ni egbo lɛ, esa akɛ ojie tso lɛ loo ofolɔ tso lɛ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la ashɛ okookoo tso lɛ he.

english: What can I do if the leaves on my cocoa trees are constantly drying up under heavy shade?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi?

english: You should clear or prune heavy, non-beneficial shade trees on your farm. Removing trees that cause your cocoa to wither allows the crops to get enough balanced light and stay fresh and healthy.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie loo ofo tsei ni tsii ni he ehiaaa ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tsei ni haa kookoo lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná la ni sa jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ ehee ni eyɛ hewalɛ lolo

english: Do cocoa trees yield pods every month like vegetables do?
ga: Ani cacao tsei woɔ yibii tamɔ aduawai daa nyɔŋ nɔ?

english: No, cocoa trees do not produce a harvest every single month. Instead, they go through specific flowering and pod development cycles that lead to major harvesting periods during certain times of the year.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei wooo ŋmɔshi nibii daa nyɔŋ nɔ, shi moŋ amɛtsɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa kpamɔ bei ni he hiaa waa baa yɛ afi lɛ mli bei komɛi amli.

english: Will I only be able to harvest my cocoa pods once a year?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa kookoo ŋmeii shikome pɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: No, cocoa farming is not limited to just one single harvest a year. In Ghana, cocoa trees typically produce two harvest periods each year: the main crop season and a smaller light crop season.
ga: Dabi, jeee ŋmaa shikome pɛ ni akpaa yɛ afi mli lɛ ji kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii. Yɛ Ghana lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei lɛ yɛ kpamɔ bei enyɔ yɛ afi mli: be titri ni amɛdaraa kɛ kpamɔ bibioo.

english: Why do I see flowers, small pods, and mature pods on my cocoa tree at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa fɔfɔii, ŋmeii bibii, kɛ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally cycle through growth stages continuously. Because pods develop over several months, a single tree will often carry young pods and ripe pods simultaneously while new flowers are opening.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni edara ha lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji babaoo mli. Bei pii lɛ, tso kome woɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni eda yɛ be kome mli. amɛfeɔ ekome yɛ be mli ni fɔfɔi heei lɛ miikwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How can I make sure the pods on my cocoa trees stay clean and free from pests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe tse ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli?

english: Regularly clearing weeds, pruning overcrowded branches, and removing damaged or sick pods prevents insects and diseases from breeding, keeping your cocoa pods healthy and pest-free.
ga: weeding Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi waa Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni efite loo hela mɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii kɛ helai akafɔ. Ha o-cocoa pods lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are the cocoa pods on my neighbor's farm looking healthy while mine get destroyed by insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni kooloi fiteɔ mikookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Pests attack cocoa farms that lack proper maintenance or canopy ventilation. Keeping your farm tidy, managing shade levels, and protecting trees early helps keep pods safe from insects.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa kookoo ŋmɔji ni bɛ saamɔ kpakpa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli lɛ. Oŋmɔ lɛ ni oooha ehi shi yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛ tsei ahebuu mra Enɛ baaye abua ni pod lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: How can I keep my cocoa plants looking green and fresh throughout the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-cacao tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee ehee afi muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Cocoa stays fresh and healthy when it receives the right balance of shade, sufficient moisture, healthy soil, and regular protection from pests and diseases that damage the stems and leaves.
ga: Cocoa lɛ hiɔ shi ehee ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ kɛji akɛ aha lɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni sa. hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ hebuu daa kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Is cocoa a good crop for me to start farming in my community?
ga: Ani kookoo ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi koni maje ŋmɔ shishi yɛ mi akutso lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cocoa is a strong long-term crop in regions with suitable forest soils and climate. Once established and properly cared for, cocoa trees yield reliable harvests over many years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa, ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ hei ni shikpɔji, kooi, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sa yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, Cacao tso lɛ baawo yibii ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ afii babaoo mli.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves of maize usually means the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from older leaves at the bottom to support new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛ baai heei ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ atsu nii.

english: Why should I plant beans in the same field where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ mli?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but bean plants actually put nitrogen back into the soil through their roots. Rotating with beans natural restores soil fertility for your next crops without buying expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, shi yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, ŋmeii tsei kɛ nitrogen kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmeii ni jara wa.

english: Why does my crop field dry up so quickly even when it rained just a few days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii fioo komɛi ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil dries quickly when it lacks organic matter like decayed leaves or manure, which work like sponges to hold moisture. Adding compost or leaving crop residues on the farm helps the soil retain water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa nu hiɔ shi Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet weather, especially when cocoa trees are crowded and air cannot move freely through the branches.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and getting wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of the leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies that distorts how the plant grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa ni fiteɔ bɔ ni tsei daraa amɛhaa lɛ nɔ

english: Why are my plantain trees falling over by themselves before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain tso lɛ shwieɔ shi dani eyibii lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because their roots are shallow and can be destroyed underground by pests like banana weevils or microscopic worms, leaving the heavy plant without support against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii tamɔ banana ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ afite amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi tsei ni tsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ enaaa amɛnɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or water is irregular. Extremely hot weather prevents the flower from pollinating itself, causing the plant to shed the flower to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu lɛ ejaaa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haaa fɔfɔii lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yam tubers become twisted when the soil beneath them is too hard, stony, or compacted for the tuber to push through easily as it expands underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, eyɛ tɛi, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ mli oya beni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Does planting my crops in straight lines really help them grow better than planting them randomly?
ga: Ani tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ fe ni aduɔ amɛ trukaa?

english: Planting in straight lines gives each plant equal space, light, and water to grow strong. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and detecting disease much easier.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni edaa yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko, la, kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ helai akasemɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready to be dug up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the main stem grows tall, the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil right around the base of the plant begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ efee klalo kɛji tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ eda. Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. ni sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning brown and curling up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkpãa amɛhe yɛ hulu la lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight. Without shade from companion plants like plantains, the harsh sun burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil around their tender roots.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni hiɔ shi ekome lɛ bɛ hulutsoo be lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa ebaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ ni bɔle eshishifãi bibii lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ.

english: Why are my maize plants turning yellow even though it has been raining regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains provide water, but they can also wash nutrients deeper into the ground away from the roots, meaning the crop still needs fertilizer or manure.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ nu baa Shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lolo.

english: How can I tell which end of a cassava stem stick should point upward when I am planting it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei tso lɛ fã ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf nodes or buds along the stem. The tiny growth buds should always point upward toward the sky so the shoots can grow properly above ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai bibii ni ebɔle ehe loo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to make food for the growing underground tubers. Staking lifts the foliage off the ground, maximizing sunlight and preventing rotting diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha hulu la lɛ aya hiɛ ni otsi fitemɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: This condition, known as blossom-end rot, is caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by dry spells or irregular watering that prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo nu ni akɛhaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to grow foliage instead of fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ laajeɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ewo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small suckers grow around my main plantain stem at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso wulu lɛ he yɛ be kome too mli lɛ?

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to compete with the main plant for soil nutrients and water, which results in smaller plantain bunches and longer harvest times.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo akwɛ̃ lɛ, ehaa amɛ kɛ tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Enɛ haa plantains lɛ feɔ bibii, ni kpamɔ be lɛ hu sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why should I cover the dirt around my crops with dried leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry plant material, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground during hot days, suppresses weed growth, and enriches the soil as the organic matter decomposes.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts help improve my soil for the next farming season?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds the crops planted in that soil later.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ mli lɛ ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the field over time.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ helai babaoo buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and grow, or that the ground is holding too much trapped water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: What causes tiny holes in my maize leaves when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ ŋmãa baai amli beni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Those holes are usually caused by young armyworms or caterpillars eating the leaves. Spraying early with recommended treatments stops them before they ruin the entire maize crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii mra lɛ shwieɔ nɔ Kpaa amɛ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmãa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas planted nearby to protect them from heat during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo banana ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I harvest more corn?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani makpa ŋmãa babaoo?

english: No, planting them too close makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off mainly because of extreme heat, irregular watering when flowering starts, or a lack of essential soil nutrients like calcium.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛji fɔfɔi lɛ je shishi loo niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium.

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal the water, light, and soil fertilizer that your main plants need to build strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otso titri lɛ koni shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why does my yam vine start drying up and turning brown before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: When the yam vine dries up naturally at the end of the season, it shows that the plant has finished sending all its energy into the tuber beneath the ground and the yam is fully mature.
ga: Beni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gĩɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potato tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ naa. Ni yams lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: Hybrid seeds only give high yields in their first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest will grow unevenly and produce much smaller, weaker yields in the second season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ni egbɔjɔ kwraa yɛ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plant roots can drink before the heat sets in. Afternoon watering causes most of the water to evaporate quickly in the sun.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu nu dani latsaa lɛ aba. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli shwane mli lɛ baaha nu lɛ mli babaoo atsɔ oya yɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell that my cocoa pods are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color. Pods that start as green turn bright yellow, and pods that start as red or purple turn orange, showing the beans inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛsu Nibii ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse. Ni pods ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ etsuru loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa.

english: How often should I walk through my farm to check on my crops rather than just visiting occasionally?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooyasara yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ?

english: Walking through your field two to three times a week allows you to catch hidden pests or early symptoms of disease on the undersides of leaves before an outbreak destroys your entire harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔji amli shii fioo yɛ otsi mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ loo helai okadii ni jeɔ kpo mra yɛ baai lɛ ashishi dani tsɛŋemɔ hela ko baafite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Where do fall armyworms suddenly come from in my young maize field when the land was clean when I planted?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jɛ trukaa yɛ mi-baby corn ŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mitsuɔ shikpɔŋ ni he tse nɔ nii lɛ?

english: Adult moths fly in at night from neighboring fields and lay hundreds of tiny eggs under leaves, which hatch rapidly into worms that seem to appear out of nowhere.
ga: Akpɔlɔi ni eda lɛ fãa kɛbaa gbɛkɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. ni ekɛ ŋmeii bibii woɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi Ni shwere oya ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ nɔ ni ejɛ he ko he ko.

english: Why do I see green leafy bushes growing directly on top of my cocoa branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa baai eŋɔli ko ni miida yɛ mi-kookoo nine lɛ yiteŋ lɛ?

english: Those are mistletoe plants, which are parasites brought by bird droppings; their roots tap into your tree's branches to steal water and food, slowly weakening the tree if you do not prune them off.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji mistletoe tsei, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ okpoi afɔfɔi amli. Eshishifãi lɛ boteɔ tsei aniji amli koni amɛyaju nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ fiofio. Kɛji okɛkpaaa lɛ

english: Weed seeds stay asleep in the soil for years and are naturally hardier; as soon as you clear the land and rain falls, they sprout instantly to steal light and fertilizer from your slower-growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo ni amɛhe wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Kɛji ojie he ni oyɔɔ lɛ pɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ Amɛbaakwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛbaaju la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ otsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ amli.

english: If I plant sweet cassava right next to bitter cassava, will the bitter one make my sweet cassava taste bitter?
ga: Kɛji odu ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ ŋmei ni mli edɔ Ani ŋmei baaha ŋmei ni ŋɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmei?

english: No, planting them next to each other does not change the flavor of the roots, because the taste is determined purely by each individual plant's own genetics.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ, etsakeee shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmɔlɔ. Ejaakɛ tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli wala yibii lɛ ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ kwraa.

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry soil, or lack of insect pollinators, causing the plant to drop its blooms to save water and survival energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ bɛ. Enɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when my farm stays too dark and wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ be mli ni miŋmɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Too much shade and stagnant moisture create the perfect home for the Black Pod fungus to live and spread rapidly from pod to pod across your farm.
ga: Shade babaoo kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ haa shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha blackpod fungus lɛ koni eshwere ni egbɛ eshwa oya kɛjɛ pod mli kɛya pod mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra shoots from my plantain stool instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ plantain ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ moŋ fe ni mahã ekwɛ̃ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: If too many shoots grow from one plantain mat, they compete with each other for water and soil nutrients, leaving you with thin stems and small bunches instead of one large harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ plantain kome mli lɛ, Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni fãa kɛfeɔ kui bibii. Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ agbo kome najiaŋ

english: If I save seeds from my best harvested maize to plant next season, why do I end up with a poor crop?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ mináa yibii gbohii?

english: Hybrid seeds are specifically bred for one high-yielding generation; saving and planting their seeds results in offspring that lose that vigor and produce smaller, uneven cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛha henɔi ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa seshibii lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight; fast-growing plantain trees act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping soil moisture while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when planted in open sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very delicate and cannot handle full, direct sunlight. They need shade from larger plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their soft leaves and keep the soil moist while their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni amɛbu baai bibii ahe ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ.

english: How does a long dry season affect my cocoa trees?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During dry months, a cocoa tree conserves water by shedding its leaves and stopping new growth. If the dry period is too long without soil moisture, young trees can wither and tiny pods will stop growing and fall off.
ga: yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ buɔ nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ hee lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ ni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei bibii baanyɛ agbo, ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akpa dalɛ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: How can I know if the land I have is good for growing cocoa?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni miyɔɔ lɛ hi kɛha kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Good cocoa soil is rich, dark, soft, and deep enough for roots to push down easily. It should retain moisture during dry periods but allow water to drain well so it does not become waterlogged after heavy rains.
ga: Kokoo shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ, eyɛ ediŋ, eyɛ bɔdɔɔ, ni eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ shi mlɛo. Esa akɛ akwɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ shi esa akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akatsɔ nu.

english: If cocoa trees are planted too close, their roots fight for food and water in the soil, and their upper branches block sunlight and fresh air. This dark, airless environment encourages plant diseases like black pod to spread quickly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo tso lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Ni niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baatsi hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa naa. Shihilɛ ni mli ewo duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli lɛ haa tsei ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do I need to cut off the small shoots growing on the trunk of my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? No ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso shishi lɛ?

english: Those extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and food that the main tree needs to grow strong and make fruit. Removing them forces the tree's energy into producing a healthy canopy and more pods.
ga: Nakai tsei krokomɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tso titri lɛ koni enyɛ eda ni ewo yibii. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli wa kɛ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How many years does a new cocoa tree usually take before it starts giving fruit?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take 3 to 5 years to start producing pods, but newer hybrid varieties can start producing fruit in about 2 to 3 years if properly cared for.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni afɔɔ feemɔ yɛ blema lɛ heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii. Shi hybrid henɔi heei Ebaabɔi yibiiwoo yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji akwɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do so many small flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Tsei enyiɛ ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces thousands of flowers, but it naturally drops most of them because it can only nourish a small number into full pods. Dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or poor insect pollination can also cause flowers to drop.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔii akpei abɔ. Shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ fioo pɛ ji nɔ ni abaanyɛ aha amɛ niyenii ni amɛkɛwo pod lɛ mli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni ehiii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔii lɛ agbo.

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod on the tree is ripe and ready to pick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ ajie?

english: A pod is ripe when its skin color changes completely, usually from green or red to a bright yellow or orange, and it makes a hollow sound when you tap it lightly with your knuckles.
ga: Pods lɛ egbɔ kɛji amɛhewolo nɔ su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru nɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse nɔ. Ni ebaafee gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ onine tswa lɛ fioo.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa tree to turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pod is a disease caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, cold, and dark conditions. Rain splashes the fungus from the soil or infected trees onto healthy pods, especially when the farm is overgrown.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo, fɛ̃i, kɛ duŋ yɔɔ. Nugbɔ haa ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ anɔ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse fe nine.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa trees turning pale green or yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree is hungry because the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen. Even if there is plenty of rain, a tree needs proper soil nutrients to keep its leaves dark green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ ejaakɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ waa moŋ Tsei hu he miihia niyenii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛbaai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: What is a net house, and how does it help my vegetables grow better than in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji trellis ŋmɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua mi-vegetables lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A net house is a simple frame covered with fine mesh that shields crops from harsh sunlight, heavy pounding rain, and destructive insects, allowing delicate vegetables like tomatoes and sweet peppers to stay healthy and produce higher yields.
ga: Trellis greenhouse ji tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ tsɔne bibioo ko ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo tamɔ tomato kɛ bell peppers. Ha oná hewalɛ ni owo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit during the heat of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to tomato plants, drying up the pollen and preventing fertilization, which forces the plant to shed its flowers before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa fɔmɔ baa. Enɛ nyɛɔ tomato tsei anɔ koni amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants turning yellow and getting dry brown spots in the sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Intense direct sunlight and heat can sunburn sensitive plant leaves and dry out moisture too quickly, causing the green pigment to fade and leaves to scorch unless shaded or watered adequately.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ni hulu lɛ nuɔ he waa lɛ ahe baai lɛ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebaa lɛ shãa. ja akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni sa ewo mli

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are suffering from heat stress or lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ hewɔ?

english: When maize lacks moisture and suffers from heat, its leaves roll inward like narrow tubes during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss, and the plants turn dull or pale green.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ miipiŋ lɛ, ebaai lɛ shwieɔ mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko. yɛ gbi lɛ mli la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni nu ni elaaje lɛ aba shi ni tso lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eŋɔli fioo

english: Why do small white flies make my garden egg leaves roll up and get sticky?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ haa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Whiteflies suck essential juice out of plant leaves, which weakens the plant and spreads plant viruses that cause leaf curling, while leaving behind a sweet liquid that attracts black mold.
ga: Whiteflies lɛ nuɔ nu ni he hiaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɛɔ hela ko eshwaa tso lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eshiɔ nu ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii diji kɛbaa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots turn black and rot when water stays on my land for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu hi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the soil to breathe; standing water drowns the roots by blocking air, causing them to suffocate and decay due to root-rot fungi.
ga: Tso shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛnaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ehaa mɔ shwieɔ shi yɛ fungal root rot lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my cabbage leaves getting full of tiny holes even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Watering helps the plant grow, but small caterpillars hatching from moth eggs on the undersides of leaves actively feed on the green leaf tissue, creating holes.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa. Shi ŋmeii bibii ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ni no haa ŋmeii baa.

english: Why is my cassava producing huge stems and bushy leaves, but very tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ tsei wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil pushes the cassava plant to spend its energy growing top foliage instead of storing starches and swelling its roots into tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaa lɛ baa. Mohu ɔ, e kɛ starch toɔ, nɛ e haa nɛ e sisije ɔmɛ fuɔ kɛ peeɔ tubers.

english: Why are my cucumber plants producing plenty of flowers but no cucumbers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kukumba tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi kukumba ko bɛ lɛ?

english: Cucumbers have separate male and female flowers, and if bees or other insects are missing to transfer pollen between them, the female flowers will wither without growing into fruit.
ga: Kukumba yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Ni kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo kooloi krokomɛi Pollination bɛ amɛteŋ. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my green pepper plants stop making new flowers after I leave ripe fruits on them for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔi heei feemɔ beni mishi aduawai lɛ ni ekwɛɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving mature fruits on the plant sends a signal to the crop that its seed production is complete, causing it to stop spending energy on new flowers until the old fruit is harvested.
ga: Yibii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ashiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ egbe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, akpaa hewalɛ yɛ fɔfɔi heei anɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa momo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen nutrients or the field has too much standing water. Adding the right fertilizer and improving drainage helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo tsɔ. Nibii ni sa ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by a fungal condition called Black Pod disease, which spreads in damp and shaded fields. Pruning excess branches to allow sunlight and clearing affected pods early protects the remaining harvest.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ enɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la aba mli kɛ ŋmeii ni ena naagbai lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Ebaaye ebua ni abu nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava tubers rot when the ground stays soaked in water for too long. Planting on raised soil mounds helps water drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu lɛ atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants lack steady water. Regular watering and shielding plants during dry heat helps save the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu ni abu amɛhe daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when they have fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ eyɛ yibii moŋ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow and can be weakened by underground pests like nematodes. Adding organic mulch around the base and keeping roots healthy helps the tree anchor firmly in the soil.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Okɛ organic mulch abɔle amɛhe. Shishitoo kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my yam vines drying up early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shwieɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam vines is often caused by leaf spot diseases or stem borers. Planting clean seed yams and managing pests early keeps the foliage green longer so the tubers grow larger.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa hela loo stem borers ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbimɔ oya baa. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni he tse ni aduɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni eha baai lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. koni eha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Why should I space my crops widely instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mabɛŋkɛ he kroko lɛ?

english: When plants are too close, they fight for nutrients, water, and sunlight, leading to weak plants and small harvests. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough food and air to produce well.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does growing the same crop on the same farm every year reduce my yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly growing one crop drains specific soil nutrients and lets plant-specific pests build up in the soil. Rotating different crops keeps the soil rich and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. kɛ gbɛ ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer so it doesn't wash away and waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafo ni efite shika?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist after a moderate rain while plants are actively growing. Avoid applying right before heavy downpours, which wash it away, or during dry spells, which can burn plant roots.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nitsumɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa ni shwieɔ nu lɛ baa. loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli, ni baanyɛ aha tsei shishifãi ashã

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the shade trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees protect the young seedlings from burning and drying out, keeping the soil moist until the cocoa canopy grows thick enough to protect itself.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkashã ni amɛkagbi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ abu ehe.

english: Which suckers should I cut away from my plantain stem if I want the main plant to produce big bunches?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmeii esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ plantain tso lɛ he kɛji miisumɔ ni tso titri lɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji?

english: You should remove 'water suckers' which have broad leaves early on because they consume water and nutrients without growing strong. Keep only one or two 'sword suckers' with narrow leaves, as they grow into strong stems that produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie ‘suckers’ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ mra. Amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛdaraaa hewalɛ. Ha ‘klante tso’ kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni baai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi beni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni wa ni woɔ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is key food for the plant. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can grow full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso lɛ niyenii titri lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam plants make food in their leaves using sunlight. Lifting the vines on stakes allows leaves to catch more sunlight and fresh air while keeping them off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and growing bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ ehe akabɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ahe. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How do I choose the best cassava stem cuttings to plant for a good yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaadu koni ewo yibii kpakpai?

english: Choose cuttings from the middle section of a healthy, mature plant that is at least eight months old. Avoid soft green tops or hard woody bases, and ensure each cutting has 4 to 6 healthy growth nodes.
ga: Halamɔ tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ hoo lɛ eye nyɔji kpaanyɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsei ni wa shishitoo he. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nitsumɔhe nine lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni edaa yɛ mli lɛ 4 kɛyashi 6.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same patch of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply. Rotating with leguminous crops like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abaajie niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa abele lɛ babaoo. Legume ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry winds, or irregular watering. Giving the plants consistent moisture and keeping the soil cool helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ shɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ mli fũɔ be fɛɛ be, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu mli jɔɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites feeding under the leaves. Neem oil spray or simple soap solutions can help control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, thrips, loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo samla ni yɔɔ mlɛo baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil richer for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ, kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have small nodules on their roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the plant roots decay, that stored nitrogen remains behind to feed the next crop naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ koni emɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ sɛɛ koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why is it beneficial to spread dry grass or leaves around the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mitso lɛ shishitoo lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun, keeps moisture in the soil longer, and suppresses weed growth so your crops get all the food and water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the vital shade and cool moisture young cocoa needs during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign that the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient maize uses to stay green. The plant moves whatever nitrogen is left to its top leaves, so adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help green up the whole plant.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni ŋmãa kɛtsuɔ nii koni ehi shi eŋɔli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why is my cassava bush growing very tall with bushy leaves, but only producing tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of sending food down to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ ebaa kɛ eshishifãi ni edaa yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niye ní kɛ yaa si konɛ a ya ma tsɔwi nɛ mi wa ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a small fungus that multiplies rapidly when the farm is too wet and shaded. Trimming excess branches to let in sunlight and air helps dry out the farm and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni shwereɔ oya kɛji ŋmɔ ko mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hulutsoo. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and hang down during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains lose water very fast through their broad leaves in hot, dry winds. The plant naturally sacrifices its older leaves to conserve water in its main stem until the rains return.
ga: Plantains lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ baai momoi shaa afɔle koni amɛkɛto nu yɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off before any peppers start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper lɛ jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or dry soil. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy so it can survive extreme weather until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ye amɛnɔ. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa amli kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my maize field so aggressively right after the first heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms lɛ tutuaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay their eggs on tender green leaves as soon as new shoots emerge after the rains. The caterpillars hatch quickly and feed on the soft young leaves because they are easy to eat and full of water.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmeii heei je kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ pɛ. Kplukai lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛyemɔ waaa ni nu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of loose soil before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji agbo ko dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to grow deep and wide without hitting hard soil. Raising the soil into mounds also keeps roots cool and protects the growing tubers from direct sun exposure.
