ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛshwere ni shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ebuɔ bulb ni miida lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni mi-ŋmei srɔtoi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots work with natural soil microbes to trap nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the cowpea plant decays, it leaves behind free plant food for the next maize crop.
ga: Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii tsuɔ nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwo sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji cowpea tso lɛ fite Ebaashi tso niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By rolling its leaves inward, the tomato plant reduces the surface area exposed to strong sunlight, which stops water from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie mli lɛ, ebaaha tomato tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ baashɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ oya tsɔ.

english: If I add more fertilizer to my maize, will it grow faster and let me harvest earlier?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ, ani ŋmãa lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya ni abaakpa mra?

english: Fertilizer gives crops essential nutrients that speed up growth, but applying too much can burn the roots or create excess leaves instead of grain. Applying the right amount at the right crop stage ensures maximum growth speed and early harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa amɛdaraa oya. Shi kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ loo eha baai ni fa fe nine aba yɛ dumɔwui lɛ najiaŋ. Kɛ akɛ yibɔ ni sa tsu nii yɛ dumɔ be ni sa mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ daa oya fe fɛɛ ni ekpaa mra.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops grow much faster than mine even though we planted on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ daa oya fe mi nɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ wɔdu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops grow faster when they receive good soil nutrients, proper plant spacing, timely weeding, and sufficient moisture. Just like well-fed animals grow quickly, well-cared-for crops absorb nutrients easily and reach maturity much faster.
ga: Tsei daa oya kɛji amɛyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai. Tsei ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa Taakɛ koolooi ni ayeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ŋmɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa oya kwraa.

english: Is there a way I can get my cassava ready for market in eight months instead of waiting a full year?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ afee ŋmei klalo kɛha jara nɔ yɛ nyɔji 8 mli moŋ fe ni abaamɛ afi muu fɛɛ?

english: Using early-maturing improved cassava varieties, along with proper weed control and soil fertilization, can significantly reduce growth time, allowing you to harvest healthy tubers months earlier than traditional varieties.
ga: Kɛ akɛ cassava henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii koni ekwɛ̃ oya kɛ jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ eba shweremɔ be lɛ shi waa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa bulbs ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ nyɔji babaoo mra fe blema ŋmeii srɔtoi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my pepper plants are delayed in growing or if they are on normal schedule?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-pepper tso lɛ miida blɛoo loo yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Healthy pepper plants should show new leaf shoots every week and start flowering within two to three months. If stem growth stalls or flowering takes longer, the plants are likely stressed by poor soil, lack of water, or pest attack.
ga: Esa akɛ pepper tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná ŋmeii heei daa otsi. ni ejeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi yɛ nyɔji enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ edaaa shi loo fɔfɔii lɛ heɔ be babaoo lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, nu ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha Tsei lɛ aná haomɔ.

english: Does removing weeds really help crops yield faster, or does it just keep the farm looking neat?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya diɛŋtsɛ loo ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛkɛ?

english: Weeds actively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops. Removing them early stops this competition, allowing your crops to use all available resources to grow rapidly and produce fruit much earlier.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ni ajieɔ mra lɛ baaha akaŋshii nɛɛ akpa Ha oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ lɛ atsu nii koni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo oya.

english: What happens to my tomato plants if I leave the farm unattended for two weeks?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi ŋmɔ lɛ mli otsii enyɔ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ nɔ?

english: Neglecting tomato plants even briefly allows weeds to choke them, diseases like blight to spread unchecked, and pests to attack vulnerable flowers, which delays fruit production and severely lowers your final yield.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ agbe jwɛi lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa helai tamɔ late blight gbɛɔ eshwaa ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ. ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa fɔfɔi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai ni anáa lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ, ni ehaa naagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Will watering my vegetables every day during the dry season make them produce fruit continuously?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai anɔ daa gbi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha amɛya nɔ amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, consistent irrigation keeps crop roots active and prevents heat stress, allowing crops to grow, flower, and produce yield continuously throughout the dry season when market prices are high.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi daa lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii daa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ beni jara nɔ jara wa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops slow down their growth during minor dry spells even when there is plenty of sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ fioo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ

english: Plants need water to transport nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. Without water, crops shut down their growth processes to conserve energy and avoid drying out, regardless of how bright the sun is.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛdalɛ gbɛ lɛ naa koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkagbi lɛ naa. Bɔ fɛɛ bɔ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa ha

english: Will cutting off extra suckers from my plantain trees help the main plant grow faster?
ga: Ani mi-plantain lɛ nɔ tsei krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso titri lɛ ada oya?

english: Yes, extra suckers consume nutrients and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers directs all soil nutrients to the main plant, helping it flower and produce bigger bunches faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa lɛ yeɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni jɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii lɛ fɛɛ aya tso titri lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ewoɔ fɔfɔii wuji oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my okra plants turn yellow and drop when I stop giving them attention?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi gumbo lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ mikpa amɛjwɛŋmɔ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal nutrient deficiency, water stress, or disease attack caused by neglect. Regular farm visits help you spot these early warning signs and apply fertilizer or treatment before crop growth halts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. nu mli haomɔ loo hela ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hiɛ ni akuɔ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli baa Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii nɛɛ mra. ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofa awo mli dani tsei lɛ akpa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling up and becoming very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibioo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap from tender shoots. As they feed, they transfer plant viruses that cause the leaves to distort and stop growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛjieɔ tsei amli helai ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when heat gets too high or when soil moisture changes drastically. Intense heat dries up the pollen inside the flower, preventing pollination, so the plant sheds the flower.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ gbiɔ. Tsi pollination naa No sɛɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why are there small holes in my young maize leaves and dirt inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ani muji yɛ baa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This is typical damage from Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars hide inside the growing center (funnel) of the plant to feed, leaving behind holes in the unfolding leaves and dark waste that looks like sawdust.
ga: Enɛ ji nɔ ni Fall Armyworm fɔɔ fitemɔ. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (cones) lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Eshiɔ bu yɛ baai ni ajieee lɛ amli kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow from the middle out to the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ kɛyaa naagbee lɛ?

english: Yellowing that starts at the tips of older leaves indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen down past the roots, leaving the plant hungry for nutrients needed to keep leaves green.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ anaagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen ni hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni eha ebaa lɛ afee eŋɔli.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have microscopic organisms in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This naturally fertilizes the soil so next season's maize crop grows better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots compete heavily with each other for space, soil water, and nutrients. Without enough space, the plant puts its energy into growing tall for sunlight rather than expanding its roots into big tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ He ko ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa kɛha he ko, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara koni amɛná hulu la. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ lɛɛɔ nɛ a peeɔ bulb nguahi.

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to sunlight to create food for the plant. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out, allowing maximum sunlight to fuel the growth of large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa. Koni ekɛ hulu la babaoo aba bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekanya ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the rainy season is too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air pockets in the soil to stay alive. When the ground remains soaked for long periods, water fills those air pockets, drowning the roots and encouraging rot fungi to multiply.
ga: Tso shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ Nu lɛ yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ amli, ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why does putting dried grass on the ground around my garden help my vegetables stay healthy in hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mibɔɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-aduawai lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a sunshade for the soil. It keeps the earth cool, stops water from evaporating quickly into the air, and prevents weed seeds from sprouting.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Ye obua ni je lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when planted in an open field without plantains nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni plantains ko bɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living canopy shade and retain moisture, creating a cool climate that allows young cocoa trees to establish safely.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ haa ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmaa shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know when my beetroot crops are ready to be harvested from under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-beetroot tsei lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Root crops like beetroot show signs above ground when they reach maturity. The top shoulder of the red root will start pushing slightly out of the soil, and the leaves will look lush and fully grown. You can also gently clear away a bit of topsoil around the base to check if the bulb has reached a good size.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ shishifãi, tamɔ beetroot lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ nɔ okadii akpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Shishifãi tsuru lɛ ŋwɛi tsitsi lɛ baabɔi shwiemɔ fioo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni baai lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Obaanyɛ Ojie sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni ebɔle ohe lɛ hu fiofio. Gbalamɔ shishigbɛ lɛ fioo koni ona kɛji bɔl lɛ dalɛ sa.

english: Why do my beetroot plants stay very small even though I water them every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi beetroot tso lɛ ji bibioo nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Beetroot seeds often sprout very close together, causing crowded roots that fight for space and nutrients. If you do not thin out the extra seedlings while they are small so each plant has space, the underground roots cannot expand and grow large.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, beetroot dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa. Enɛ haa shishifãi ni ebɔle amɛhe ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko kɛ niyenii kpakpai amli lɛ baa. Kɛji akɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieee shi be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ koni oha tso fɛɛ tso hegbɛ. Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛdara.

english: Why do I need to break up and loosen the soil deeply before planting root vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni mafee lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani madu shishifãi?

english: Root crops grow directly downward into the earth. If the soil is hard or compacted, the roots cannot easily push through the dirt, causing the vegetable to grow twisted, split, or remain tiny.
ga: Tse shishifãi kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛmli gbalaa, loo amɛhiɔ shi bibii.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn yellow during the heavy rainy season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ Ghana lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during heavy rains usually mean the soil is waterlogged, which smothers the roots and prevents them from breathing and taking up nutrients. Intense rain can also wash away nitrogen from the topsoil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my weak young crop seedlings bend and lean towards one side instead of growing straight up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikwɛ he kome yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ̃ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Plants naturally lean toward light to make their food. If your seedlings are under heavy tree shade or receiving light from only one angle, the stems stretch out toward the sun, making them long, thin, and crooked.
ga: Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ la nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shishi loo amɛnáa la pɛ kɛjɛɔ he kome lɛ, Tso lɛ shishi lɛ yaa hulu lɛ he, ni ehaa efeɔ kakadaŋŋ, eyɛ mlɛo, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress, such as intense heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing big leaves instead of keeping its blossoms to form fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kpe. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeŋmɛ fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt in the middle of the day even when the soil around them is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi mli lɛ? Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ edɔ po?

english: On hot days, water leaves the plant's leaves through evaporation faster than the roots can pull water up from the ground. It can also happen if underground pests or diseases have damaged the root system.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa nɔ lɛ Nu shĩɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi loo helai fite shishifãi lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my vegetable garden early in the morning or during the hot afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha aduawai abɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can drink before the scorching sun heats the ground. Watering in the hot afternoon leads to rapid evaporation, wasting water before the plant can take it up.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha tsei lɛ nu leebi koni amɛnu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ adɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha etsɔ la oya. Enɛ haa nu lɛ laajeɔ dani tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ.

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stems and small harvests. It also reduces airflow between plants, allowing crop diseases to spread very fast.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa, ni akpaa nii fioo. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ hu baa shi. Enɛ haa tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya waa.

english: Why do my freshly sprouted seedlings suddenly collapse and rot at ground level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ miifite ni amɛmiifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by a soil fungal disease called damping-off, which attacks delicate stems when the soil stays overly wet and cold right around the base of tiny young plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ dampening off, ni tutuaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi bibioo lɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my papaya trees are male or female before they start bearing fruit?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mipapaya tso lɛ ji nuu loo yoo dani ebɔi yibiiwoo?

english: Papaya trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male trees produce long branches with many small hanging flowers that do not yield fruit, while female flowers grow close to the main trunk and swell at the base to form the fruit after pollination.
ga: Papaya tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei ni ji hii lɛ woɔ niji kakadaji ni fɔfɔi bibii ni fĩɔ amɛhe lɛ yɔɔ mli. babaoo ni wooo yibii Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, fɔfɔi yei lɛ daa ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ pollination sɛɛ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants grow plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without making any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo yɔɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Flowers drop when there are not enough insects like bees to pollinate them, or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet. Ensuring good air flow and keeping soil moisture steady helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni aná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How do I choose the right suckers from a mother plantain tree to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmeii ni sa kɛjɛ dumɔwui amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Always look for 'sword suckers' growing from the mother plant. These have a thick, heavy base and narrow, spear-like leaves, which grow much faster and produce stronger plantain bunches than suckers with broad leaves.
ga: Taomɔ ‘klante ŋmeii’ ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ nyɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be. Eyɛ shishi ni mli tse, ni tsii kɛ baai ni mli tse ni tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Amɛdaraa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ plantain panicles ni mli wa fe nɔ ni baai lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ.

english: Does the thickness of a cassava stem cutting affect how big the tubers will grow?
ga: Ani bɔ ni ŋmei tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ ha lɛ saa ŋmei lɛ dalɛ he?

english: Yes, thicker cuttings taken from the middle part of a mature plant hold more stored food and water. This helps the young plant grow strong roots quickly, leading to bigger cassava tubers at harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ajie kɛjɛ tso ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ baaha niyenii kɛ nu babaoo ahi mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa oya. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ akpa ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ daraa.

english: Should I wash or soak my pepper seeds in water before I sow them in the nursery bed?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafɔ pepper dumɔwui lɛ ahe loo mawo nu mli dani madu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji akwɛmɔhe?

english: Soaking pepper seeds in clean water overnight softens their tough outer coat and helps them sprout faster and more evenly once you plant them in the moist nursery soil.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ pepper dumɔwui wo nu ni mli tse mli nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ, ebaaha amɛ yitsɔi ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot on the ground if I do not support them with wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei fiii amɛsɛɛ?

english: When tomato vines rest directly on damp soil, soil-borne diseases and pests easily attack the leaves and fruits. Using wooden stakes lifts the plant into the air and sunlight, keeping the leaves dry and the fruits clean.
ga: Kɛ akɛ tomato wain tsei wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ oya. Tsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ woɔ tsei anɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la mli. Ha baai lɛ agbi ni aduawai lɛ hu ahe atse.

english: What is the best way to construct a wooden shade frame for my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ ama tso ŋta kɛha mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ?

english: You can build a simple wooden post frame about two meters high and cover the top with palm fronds. This filters harsh sunlight, giving young cocoa seedlings the partial shade they need so their leaves do not burn.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma tso ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni kɛlɛ ji aaafee mitai enyɔ ni okɛ ŋmei baai aha nɔ. Enɛ baajie hulu la ni naa wa lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Ha kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ hulutsoo fã ko ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. koni akashã baai lɛ

english: Why is it important to guide my yam vines up tall wooden poles as soon as they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ aya tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ kɛji amɛje kpo pɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch full sunlight. The more sunlight the leaves capture, the more food the plant makes to build large tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso kakadaŋŋ ko ni baaha amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Babaoo ni hulu la ni baa lɛ naa lɛ, Babaoo ni tsei lɛ daa lɛ, babaoo ni bulbs wuji ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fa.

english: Why are the stalks of my maize plants very thin and falling over when wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Thin maize stalks happen when seeds are planted too close together or when the soil lacks nutrients. Thinning your farm so each plant has space helps the stalks grow thick and strong enough to withstand wind.
ga: Abele tsei ni mli tseee lɛ baa kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ooofee bibioo koni eha tso fɛɛ tso aná hegbɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ naa.

english: How can I look at a bunch of plantains on the tree and know it is ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ plantains ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni male kɛji amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: A plantain bunch is mature when the individual fruits lose their sharp, flat sides and become full and rounded, and when the dark dried flowers at the tips easily rub off with your fingers.
ga: Plantains kuu ko shɛɔ dalɛ he beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ebafeɔ nɔ ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Ni kɛ́ fɔfɔi lɛ egbi lɛ, amɛhe su lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ amɛnaagbee lɛ, okɛ oniji shwie nɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my cash crops look burnt after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Cash crops can be very sensitive to agrochemicals. If you spray them too heavily or too often—even just twice without proper care—the chemical concentration can scorch and burn the leaves, even if you have not added any fertilizer.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ okwaayeli tsofai ahe waa. Kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ waa loo okɛshwie shi shii abɔ tsɔ—shii enyɔ pɛ po ni okwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ—tsofa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni eshã amɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko fataaa he kwraa po.

english: Can spraying my crops too many times cause them to burn even if I haven't added any fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛshã kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he po?

english: Yes, plant leaves can burn directly from chemical contact. Fertilizer affects root nutrition, but strong chemical sprays land directly on the leaves and can cause burning on their own if applied incorrectly.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Fertilizer lɛ saa shishifãi lɛ amli niyenii he. Shi tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baagbee baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa ni baa trukaa lɛ aba kɛji akɛ akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ

english: What causes my plants to turn brown and dry up after chemical spraying?
ga: Mɛni haa mitsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: When agrochemicals are applied too frequently or at high strengths, they cause chemical stress on the plant tissue, leading to leaf burning and drying up.
ga: Kɛ akɛ agrochemicals tsu nii shii abɔ loo kɛ hewalɛ babaoo Ekɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli baa tsei ahe fãji anɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Can I care for my cash crops the exact same way I care for my low-yielding subsistence crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ mishika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tamɔ bɔ ni mikwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛyeɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: No, high-yielding cash crops and basic low-yielding crops respond differently to inputs. Cash crops require more precise care and cannot handle rough or uniform chemical treatments without suffering damage.
ga: Dabi Shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo kɛ nɔ ni woɔ yibii fioo lɛ haa nibii srɔtoi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahetoo. Shikayeli tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ ni ja fe tsutsu lɛ. ni enyɛŋ etsu tsofai ni mli wa loo ni yɔɔ ekome lɛ ahe nii ni efiteee.

english: Why do my cash crops seem more sensitive to spraying than my local food crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nuɔ he waa kɛha shwiemɔ fe mimaŋ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: High-yielding cash crops are often more delicate and sensitive to chemical exposure. Treating them with the same heavy hand as hardier, low-yielding crops can burn them and reduce your harvest.
ga: Shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ nuɔ he waa. Nine ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii, taakɛ eji yɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii fioo, ni wa lɛ ahe lɛ, baanyɛ ashã amɛ ni eha ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Is it safe for me to spray my cash crops a second time right away if I want better results?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafɔ shika ni ji enyɔ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji miitao nɔ ni hi fe tsutsu lɛ?

english: No, spraying cash crops repeatedly in a short period can overload the leaves with chemicals, causing them to burn and damaging the overall health of the plant.
ga: Dabi, shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ shii abɔ Yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa lɛ ahi baai lɛ amli babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shãa ni efiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if I am over-spraying my cash crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mikɛ tsofa babaoo eshwie mishika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ?

english: A clear sign of over-spraying is leaf scorching or burning shortly after application, which happens when chemicals build up on the plant beyond what it can tolerate.
ga: Okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ ashwie tsofa lɛ nɔ fe nine ji baai ni ashã loo ashã yɛ be mli ni akɛwo mli lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsofai bua amɛhe naa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ.

english: Are there specific farming tasks that I should not do on cash crops the same way I do on other crops?
ga: Ani okwaayeli nitsumɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni esaaa akɛ mikɛ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ yɛ gbɛ ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi tsuɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, tasks like chemical spraying and fertilization must be tailored specifically to cash crops because improper management practices can easily ruin high-value yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ nitsumɔi tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni sa shika helɛtemɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite nibii ni jara wa waa lɛ oya.

english: If I do not give my cash crops fertilizer, does that mean they won't burn when I spray them?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ mi shika ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo mli Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ eshãŋ kɛji mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ?

english: No, withholding fertilizer will not prevent spray burn. Spraying chemicals directly onto cash crop leaves can still burn them regardless of whether fertilizer was applied to the soil.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsiŋ shãa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ naa. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha shãa aba lolo, kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛwooo mli.

english: Does chemical spraying take the place of fertilizer for cash crops?
ga: Ani tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shika helɛtemɔ mli lɛ najiaŋ?

english: No, chemical sprays protect against pests or diseases while fertilizers feed the plant. Spraying alone without proper soil feeding does not replace nutrient care and can still cause leaf burn if done improperly.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ buɔ he kɛjɛɔ kooloi loo helai ahe yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ ni akɛ niyenii haaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeee nɔ ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ najiaŋ, ni ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã po kɛji akɛ afeee lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the main cocoa harvest season in Ghana usually start around September or November?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ, be titri ni akɛkpaa kookoo yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ September loo November mli lɛ?

english: The main cocoa season starts around September or November because the trees rely on the heavy rains from the earlier months of the year to grow pods, which take about five to six months to fully mature and ripen.
ga: Kookoo be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ September loo November mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛjɛɔ shishijee nyɔji lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. afi lɛ mli kɛha pods dumɔ Eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani edaa kwraa ni ekwɛɔ.

english: Can my cocoa trees grow well if I rely only on natural rainfall instead of manual watering?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ miniji baawo amɛ nu?

english: Yes, mature cocoa trees in Ghana are naturally adapted to rain-fed agriculture, meaning they grow successfully on the natural seasonal rainfall pattern without needing daily manual watering.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo tsei ni edara ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu okwaayeli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ mli lɛ he nii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ niji awo amɛ nu daa gbi.

english: Does rain across different regions in Ghana affect cocoa trees in the exact same way?
ga: Nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kpokpai srɔtoi anɔ Yɛ Ghana lɛ, ani enaa kookoo tsei anɔ hewalɛ yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ?

english: While it rains across all cocoa regions in Ghana, localized factors like soil type, temperature, and shade level mean trees in different areas may absorb moisture and produce fruit at slightly different rates.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ kookoo kpokpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ anɔ moŋ, shi nibii pɔtɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ henɔ, latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hei srɔtoi lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo nɔ.

english: How does heavy rainfall affect the way my cocoa trees produce pods?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ saa bɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Adequate rainfall gives cocoa trees the water they need to form healthy pods, but continuous heavy rain without enough sunlight can encourage fungal diseases like black pod and reduce overall yield.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ náa nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛfee ŋmeii ni wa. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ awo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ hewalɛ ni eha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers when a sudden heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain can physically knock delicate blossoms off the branches or flood the roots, causing stress to the tree which leads it to drop its flowers before they turn into small pods.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbo kɛjɛ tsei aniji anɔ loo eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot during the wet rainy months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Excessive wetness and high humidity during rainy periods create ideal conditions for the Black Pod fungus to spread across pods, destroying the crop if not properly managed.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli nugbɔshiimɔ ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baaha blackpod fungus lɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii lɛ amli fɛɛ. Efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens to cocoa trees after the main harvest season ends in the dry period?
ga: Mɛni baa kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ beni kpamɔ be titri lɛ eba naagbee yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: After the main harvest, cocoa trees enter a rest period where they conserve energy and water during the drier months before starting a new cycle of flowering for the next season.
ga: Yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ boteɔ hejɔɔmɔ be mli ni amɛbuɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu he yɛ nyɔji ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ amli. dani ebɔi fɔmɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why do older cocoa trees produce fewer pods even when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees age, their branches become less efficient at transporting nutrients and water, meaning even good rainfall will not yield as many pods as when the tree was young.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛniji lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛkɛ niyenii kɛ nu aya. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ kpakpa po wooo yibii babaoo tamɔ beni kookoo tsei lɛ darako lɛ.

english: Why do shade trees help my cocoa farm handle erratic rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ ni enyɛɔ ekpeeɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa from direct sun heat, help the soil retain rainwater longer, and break the force of heavy rains so fragile cocoa flowers and pods are not damaged.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. ni eye ebua ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ aba shi bɔni afee ni ekafite kookoo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni waaa lɛ.

english: Why is it difficult to harvest and dry my cocoa when the rain comes unexpectedly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ abaakpa kookoo ni agbi lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ trukaa lɛ?

english: Unexpected rain slows down field harvesting work and prevents cocoa beans from drying properly in the sun, which can spoil the quality of the harvested beans.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa nikpamɔ nitsumɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli. ni ehaaa kookoo yibii lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ baanyɛ afite kɔfi yibii ni akpa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when there are no big plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi be mli ni cacao tsei wuji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and burn easily under harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree canopies to lower the field temperature and hold moisture in the air while the young roots settle.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ahe tsɔi. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi bibii lɛ miifee lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain stems produce tiny bunches when I leave many shoots growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ mli fãa bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo ni bɔleɔ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: When too many suckers grow around a mother plant, they all fight for the same soil food and water. Cutting excess shoots allows the mother plant to focus all its nutrients into growing a single, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ he lɛ, amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ buaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ kuu kome ni tsii.

english: Why am I finding small caterpillars eating inside the center funnel of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni miiye nii yɛ mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, which like to hide in the soft, dark center of maize plants where leaves are forming. They chew the tender growing tip, which damages the leaves before they can fully open.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ he ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ duŋ lɛ mli he ni baai lɛ feɔ lɛ. Amɛyeɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ blɛoo. Enɛ baafite baai lɛ dani amɛgbele kwraa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe ejɔ ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops block light from each other and compete for root space. The plants stretch upward to search for sunlight instead of growing thick stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe tɛ̃ɛ koni etao hulu la, moŋ lɛ, edaa ni efeɔ tso ni mli tse ni ŋmeii eyi mli obɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots become soft and rot underground during heavy rainy periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess rain causes water to collect around the roots if the soil drainage is poor. Without air pockets in the soggy soil, roots suffocate and natural fungi move in to decay the tuber.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha nu abua naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii baabote mli ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: Why do my yam plants produce larger tubers when I lift the vines off the ground using tall wooden poles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct exposure to light to convert sunlight into food for the roots. Staking lifts leaves off the ground, maximizing sunlight capture and keeping leaves away from ground diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia la tɛ̃ɛ koni etsake hulu la lɛ ewo niyenii kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ yaa hiɛ babaoo. ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off the plant before turning into fruit during hot afternoon weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ aduawai yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High afternoon temperatures dry up the moisture needed inside tomato flowers for pollination. When pollination fails, the plant drops the flower to save its water and energy.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa nu ni he hiaa yɛ tomato fɔfɔi amli koni ekɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ agbiɔ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛhere nu kɛ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap and spread plant viruses, causing the leaves to twist up and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa amɛdaraaa.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for growing maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in little root nodules. When the plant roots decay after harvest, this nitrogen stays behind as free plant food for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Beni tso shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Nitrogen nɛɛ hiɔ shi akɛ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my fertilizer seem to do nothing when I apply it to my field during a heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nɔ ko nɔ ko kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔji amli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer off the soil surface or flushes it deep into the ground past the root zone before the plant roots have a chance to absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eshiɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ asɛɛ, dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔɔ.

english: How many years does it take for a new cocoa tree to start giving me pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa trees usually start bearing pods in about 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties take up to 5 years to start fruiting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo tsei ni akɛ tsofai sɔrɔtoi ebɔ he lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni adu amɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo tsei ni etsɛ fe tsutsu lɛ heɔ afii enumɔ dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: My cocoa farm is over 30 years old and doesn't produce well; is it better to cut them down or try to fix them?
ga: Mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ eye fe afii 30 ni ewooo yibii jogbaŋŋ. Ani ehi akɛ ooofo mli loo ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni osaa?

english: Very old or severely diseased cocoa trees yield very little fruit even with care. It is usually best to cut them down and rehabilitate the farm by replanting with fast-yielding hybrid varieties.
ga: Kokoo tsei ni egbɔ waa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baawo yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ po. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaafolɔ amɛ ni aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii mra ni akɛduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: People talk about pruning cocoa trees, but how does cutting the branches help my farm produce more?
ga: Mɛi wieɔ kookoo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ he. Shi mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead, weak, or overcrowded branches. This allows sunlight and air to reach the inner tree, reducing diseases like Black Pod and encouraging the tree to produce more healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni egbɔjɔ, loo ni eyi obɔ lɛ ajieɔ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ tso lɛ mligbɛ fãi lɛ ahe, ehaa helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo.

english: How many times in a year am I supposed to prune my cocoa farm?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ afi mli?

english: It is generally recommended to prune cocoa trees twice a year: a major pruning before the main rainy season (around April/May) and a lighter touching-up after the main harvest season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsɔɔ akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli: afolɔ tsei wuji dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba. (Aaafee April/May) ni afolɔ mli fioo yɛ kpamɔɔ be titri lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What is the best method to trim tall cocoa trees so they are easier to take care of?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ cacao tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ koni amɛkwɛmɔ afee mlɛo?

english: Height reduction involves cutting back the central main trunk top (chupons) to keep the tree at a manageable height of 3 to 4 meters, making it easier to spray, prune, and harvest pods.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋwɛi ŋta ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ yiteŋ (chupons) lɛ ni aaafo lɛ he ji ni akɛ tsei lɛ aya ŋwɛi ŋta ni ji mitai 3 kɛyashi 4 ni anyɛɔ akwɛɔ nɔ, ni eha efee mlɛo akɛ aaafɔse, afolɔ ni akpa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die during the hot sun season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees to shield them until they grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa yɛ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛha hebuu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Can I plant cassava together with my young cocoa trees to save space?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ kookoo tsei bibii koni mikɛ he akafite?

english: It is not advisable to plant cassava with young cocoa because cassava has aggressive tuber roots that steal water and soil nutrients, and its heavy foliage blocks too much sunlight.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ akɛ kookoo ni mli jɔ adu ŋmei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ebaai ni mli tse lɛ tsiɔ hulu la babaoo naa.

english: How many times a year should I clear weeds from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi yɛ mikoo tsei lɛ ashishi yɛ afi mli?

english: For young farms, weeding should be done 3 to 4 times a year to prevent weeds from choking seedlings. For full-grown farms, 2 to 3 weedings per year are usually sufficient.
ga: kɛha ŋmɔji bibii Esa akɛ ajie jwɛi shii 3 kɛyashi 4 yɛ afi mli koni jwɛi lɛ akatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa. Kɛha ŋmɔji ni eda lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ shii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ afi mli lɛ fa.

english: What makes my green cocoa pods turn black and rot before they are ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, overly shady conditions. Regular pruning to let in sunlight, clearing weeds, and applying recommended copper-based fungicides will control it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli daa koni hulu la babaoo aba, jwɛi lɛ akudɔ, kɛ tsofai ni akɛ akɔɔble fee ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I easily tell that a cocoa pod is mature enough to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Look at the color change on the pod skin: unripe green pods turn bright yellow when mature, while red or purple varieties change to an orange-yellow color.
ga: Kwɛmɔ bɔ ni pod lɛ hiɛ su tsakeɔ ehaa: Pod ni ji eŋɔli ni eshɛko lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse beni amɛdaraa lɛ. yɛ be mli ni henɔi ni tsuɔ loo purple lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct heat from the sun. Tall trees provide shade that protects the seedlings from leaf burn and keeps the surrounding soil moist while the cocoa establishes its roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ baai ni shãa lɛ ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are there small holes in my maize leaves with tiny green worms hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ hu yɛ. Ani akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central whorl of the maize plant to eat tender leaves, so applying recommended treatments directly into the plant whorl early in the morning or evening helps protect your crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli koni amɛye baai bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stems straight upright or lying flat in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu mi-cassava tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ loo ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Planting cassava stems at a slant or upright encourages roots to grow deeper into the ground, producing bigger tubers, whereas planting them completely flat near the surface usually yields smaller tubers that can rot easily.
ga: Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ loo he ni ja lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ amɛ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii bibii ni baanyɛ afite oya lɛ baa.

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs maximum sunlight to make food for its underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, which prevents fungal diseases and gives the plant the energy it needs to build large yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Staking baajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa ni ehaa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni ekɛduɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai wuji.

english: Can I safely plant maize and cassava together on the same field without them competing for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shweshweeshwe ni mikɛ niyenii he akaŋ akaŋ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested within three to four months, leaving plenty of space and soil nutrients for the cassava to mature later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmei lɛ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I spread dry leaves and grass around the roots of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi mabɔle he lɛ? pepper tso shishifãi

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter acts as a protective blanket. It blocks the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps moisture around the roots longer, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants drop off to the ground instead of growing into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they suffer from severe heat stress, prolonged dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering and partial shade during very hot weeks help flowers stay on the vine.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ hulutsoo fã ko yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Black pod is a fungal disease caused by excessive humidity and damp conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight and air circulate through your farm helps keep the pods dry and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni hulutsoo ni fa fe nine kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi kɛbaa. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ekpa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: How do I know which plantain sucker is the best one to dig up and plant on my new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mafo ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ hee lɛ mli?

english: Look for sword suckers, which have spear-shaped leaves and a broad base. These suckers grow faster and produce stronger roots than water suckers that have wide, broad leaves from an early age.
ga: Taomɔ klante ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishi ni mli kwɔ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni mli wa fe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni mli kwɔ yɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my maize so it doesn't go to waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmãa mli ŋmãa koni ekafite?

english: Apply the first round of fertilizer about two weeks after the seeds sprout when the roots are ready to absorb food, and apply a second round when the plant reaches knee-height right before it develops tassels.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ sɛɛ beni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ niyenii lɛ. Ni okɛ kpokpaa ni ji enyɔ lɛ atsu nii beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe, dani ŋmeii lɛ baaje kpo.

english: Why did my farm give a huge harvest in the first year, but now the yield keeps dropping every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ? Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, ani nibii ni afeɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ebaa shi daa be?

english: When you plant crops on fresh land, they use up the easy nutrients stored in the soil. If you do not put nutrients back into the ground using compost, animal manure, or the right fertilizers, the soil gets exhausted and cannot support a good harvest in the following years.
ga: Beni oduɔ tsei yɛ sũ nɔ Nakai tsei lɛ baafite niyenii ni ato yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua nikpamɔ kpakpa yɛ wɔsɛɛ afii amli.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same patch every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the land time to recover. It also lets crop-specific pests and diseases live in the soil permanently, which lowers your harvest each year.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛsaa ehe. Ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa. Enɛ baaha nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ aba shi daa afi.

english: I spent a lot of money buying chemical fertilizers this year, so why did my crops still fail to produce?
ga: Afi nɛɛ mikɛ shika babaoo he tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii lolo lɛ?

english: Fertilizers only work if there is enough moisture in the soil and if they are applied at the correct stage of crop growth. Applying fertilizer during severe heat or drought can actually burn the roots and ruin your crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii pɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ, ni akɛwo mli yɛ be ni sa mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are the maize seeds I saved from last year's harvest growing into weaker plants with smaller cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ da ni etsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ŋmãa bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Many modern high-yielding seeds are hybrids, meaning their strong traits only last for one planting season. When you plant seeds collected from a hybrid crop, the new plants lose that strength, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ ji dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, dumɔwui nɛɛ ahe sui ni wa lɛ baahi shi be kome pɛ ni amɛdaraa. Kɛji odu dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ Tsei heei lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ fioo.

english: Why are my maize plants growing very tall with dark green leaves, but the cobs remain small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ waa lɛ? Shi ŋmei lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil makes crops grow plenty of leaves, but crops also need phosphorus and potassium to form big cobs and seeds. Too much of one nutrient without a balance stops the plant from producing proper fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa baai babaoo. Shi tsei hu he miihia phosphorus kɛ potassium koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji kɛ dumɔwui. Niyenii mli hewalɛ kome ni fa fe nine ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee lɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekawo yibii ni sa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves turn yellow and start curling up even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually signs of a plant virus carried by tiny insects like whiteflies, or a lack of plant nutrients in the soil, rather than a lack of water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso mli hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa loo tso mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nu ni baa shi lɛ najiaŋ

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that thrives in dark, wet, and cool conditions. If shade trees are too dense or infected pods are left on the ground, rain splashes will spread the fungus to healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ, ni efɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ kɛji tso lɛ mli ewo hulutsoo waa loo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashi shikpɔŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ baagbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize farm so fast within just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms hatch in huge numbers from eggs laid by flying moths. The young caterpillars hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant where rain cannot wash them away, eating the growing points rapidly.
ga: Fall cutworms lɛ fɔɔ babaoo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kplukai bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli yɛ he ni nugbɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe yɛ lɛ. ni eyeɔ hei ni shwereɔ oya lɛ

english: Why does planting my crops very close together cause me to get smaller vegetables at harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitsei lɛ ni miduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ haa mináa aduawai bibii yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin, weak plants that yield small produce.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do my crops wilt and dry up during short dry spells while my neighbor's crops stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli lɛ? yɛ be mli ni akutsoŋnyo lɛ tsei lɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lolo lɛ.

english: Your neighbor may have soil with high organic matter or may use mulching (covering bare soil with dry grass or leaves), which holds water in the soil longer and protects crop roots from heat.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli loo ekolɛ eefee ŋmɔtɔ. (Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ), ni haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ebuɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight all day. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted beside them to block the intense sun and keep the soil moist while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ tsei bibii loo hulutsoo tsei ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cocoa trees too close to each other on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting cocoa trees too closely causes their roots and branches to fight for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Crowded trees grow weak, produce fewer pods, and trap humidity that leads to disease outbreaks.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛniji lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu he akaŋ. Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ baagbɔjɔ, amɛnáa ŋmeii fioo, ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli, ni no haa helai baa.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees if I want them to yield more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata mi-kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes dead or unnecessary branches so the tree doesn't waste food on them. It allows light and air to pass through the tree, which prevents disease and directs energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ. koni tsei lɛ akafite niyenii Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa mɔ nɔ, ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ kookoo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why is it bad to let weeds grow thick around the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mahã jwɛi akwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your cocoa trees for water and nutrients in the soil. Thick bush around the trunk also creates a wet shelter where pests and fungal diseases can hide and multiply.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsoi bibii ni ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe lɛ hu feɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: This black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that spreads quickly in damp, wet weather. Clearing weeds, pruning branches for better airflow, and applying recommended treatments help protect the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ Ni tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the young shoots and leaves of my cocoa trees dry up and look burned after insect attacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tso lɛ tsei bibii kɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ shi kɛji kooloi ŋmɔɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by pests like mirids (capsids) that suck the sap out of soft stems and leaves, injecting poisons into the plant. Spraying approved treatments during peak pest seasons helps save the new growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji kooloi tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei bibii kɛ baai amli lɛ. kɛ tsofai fɔji ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli Tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai heei lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers but only a few of them turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shi fioo pɛ tsɔɔ fɔfɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: A tree naturally drops flowers it cannot feed, but low pod counts are often due to a lack of tiny insects called midges that pollinate the flowers. Keeping leaf litter on the soil helps these beneficial insects survive and pollinate more flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni anyɛɛɛ aye niyenii. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ayibɔ faaa lɛ. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni afo lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi babaoo amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer to help my crops grow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: If your trees grow slowly, have pale yellow leaves instead of deep green ones, or give lower yields each season, the soil is likely missing nutrients like nitrogen or potassium that fertilizer can restore.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ miida blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ. loo ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be fɛɛ mli Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen loo potassium ni ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ aku sɛɛ aba lɛ.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my cocoa pods from the trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa kookoo ŋmeii kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods are ready to pick when their outer color changes completely, usually turning from green to yellow, or from dark red to bright orange. Picking unripe pods results in low-quality beans, while leaving pods too long makes beans sprout inside.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji amɛ kponɔgbɛ su tsake kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ mli. loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ nɔ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse nɔ. Pods ni eshɛko lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni ehiii aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kpo nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why must I cover and ferment my harvested cocoa beans under plantain leaves before drying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mihaa kookoo ni akpa lɛ nɔ ni mikɛwoɔ plantain baai lɛ ashishi dani migbiɔ kookoo lɛ?

english: Fermentation heats up the wet beans, killing the bitter seed germ and creating the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyer's look for. Covering them with fresh plantain leaves traps the heat and moisture needed for this process.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Nibii ni gbeɔ helai ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ ni ehaa tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ plantain baai heei ha nɔ lɛ, ebaamɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa kɛha nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and getting yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava leaves curl and turn yellow because of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava varieties from the agricultural office prevents this problem.
ga: Yucca baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ cassava mosaic hela, ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ hewɔ. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by tiny black bugs inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miifite mi ŋmãa lɛ? yɛ mi nitoohe kotoku lɛ mli

english: Those bugs are maize weevils that hatch from eggs laid in the grain. Drying your maize thoroughly until it is hard and storing it in airtight (hermetic) bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Kplukai lɛ ji ŋmãa ŋmeii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa waa ni okɛto kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkajo foi ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep falling off without turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or lack of pollination by tiny insects called midges. Keeping shade trees in your farm helps maintain the moisture cocoa trees need to hold their flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni bɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Atsɛɔ lɛ Midge. Kɛ́ okwɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛhiɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are my plantain trees producing very small bunches even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: When too many young suckers grow around the main plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Cutting away extra suckers so only 2 or 3 remain gives the main plant enough strength to grow large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ he lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ koni eshwɛ 2 loo 3 pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my yam plants grow long leaves and thick vines but produce very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ baa kakadaŋŋ kɛ wain tsei ni mli tse lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam plants put all their energy into leafy vines if the soil has too much nitrogen or if the soil mounds are too hard. Loose soil mounds and balanced fertilizer encourage the plant to send energy downward to grow big tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo kɛji gɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tseee ni ato kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ yaa shi koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the young leaves on my maize farm turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less crop yield every year even when I use the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the soil every season, leaving the soil tired and empty over time. Rotating different crops, like planting beans before maize, or adding animal manure puts vital food back into the earth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, be ni be hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ ŋmãa. Aloo, ŋmei ni akɛaawo mli lɛ baaha niyenii ni he hiaa aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it bad to sow my maize seeds immediately after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch that dries up the soil. If seeds germinate right away, the hot dry ground will burn the tender young sprouts before the steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ amrɔ nɔŋŋ He ni edɔ ni egbi lɛ baashã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and choke my crops when I clear the land and plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni midu nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are already wild in the soil and sprout faster than farm crops to steal water and sunlight. Clearing weeds early within the first three weeks gives your young crops space and light to grow stronger than the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli momo ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛju nu kɛ hulu la. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ lɛ mli lɛ enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ la ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa fe jwɛi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers and leaves when the weather gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers and leaves during excessive heat to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Covering the soil around the plant base with dry grass (mulching) keeps the root area cool and moist.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Koni okɛ nu akafite ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni egbi lɛ he. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ shishi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why do my young maize leaves turn yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main nutrient for green growth. This happens when the soil is poor, washed out by rain, or when fertilizer has not been applied.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii, nugbɔ eho, loo kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ko ewo mli.

english: Why shouldn't I spread my fertilizer right before heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer away off the top of the soil before the roots can swallow it. Apply fertilizer when the ground is moist or during light rains so it melts into the soil where the roots live.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmiɔ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli koni etsɔ shikpɔŋ ni shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does leaving cut weeds on top of the soil help my crops during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni afolɔ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Leaving dead weeds on the soil acts like a grass blanket (mulch). It stops the hot sun from evaporating water from the soil, keeping the root area cool and wet for much longer.
ga: Jwɛi ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. (Mulch) tsiɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekafee nu ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why is my pepper farm growing tall with big leaves but giving me very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper ŋmɔji lɛ kɛlɛ waa ni amɛbaai wuji yɔɔ mli shi amɛwoɔ chili fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to put all its strength into growing leaves instead of fruits. Plants need different nutrients, like phosphorus, to produce flowers and grow pepper fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Tsei taoɔ niyenii srɔtoi, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛkwɛ̃ pepper aduawai.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop leaves and small pods during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Yɛ Harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ mli

english: During dry seasons, cocoa trees drop leaves and young pods to save water and keep their main trunk alive. Planting shade trees nearby helps protect them from direct heat and water loss.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai kɛ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ahi shi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ kɛ nu ni laajeɔ tɛ̃ɛ baa.
